meanings.note: Abandonner un projet.
Abandonner un projet.

examples.text: Je ne t'abandonnerai pas.
examples.trans: I won't abandon you.

examples.text: Il abandonne le projet.
examples.trans: He's giving up the project.

examples.text: Il m'abandonne.
examples.trans: He's abandoning me.

meanings.note: Compound masculine noun (literally 'turns down the daylight'); invariable in traditional spelling (des abat-jour), though abat-jours also appears in modern usage.

examples.text: L'abat-jour en verre diffuse une lumière chaude dans le salon.
examples.trans: The glass lampshade spreads a warm light in the lounge.

examples.text: Henri nettoie doucement l'abat-jour avec un chiffon sec.
examples.trans: Henri gently cleans the lampshade with a dry cloth.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le abattoir', plural 'les abattoirs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'slaughterhouse'.

examples.text: Les animaux vont à l'abattoir.
examples.trans: The animals go to the slaughterhouse.

examples.text: Elle combat la cruauté des abattoirs.
examples.trans: She fights slaughterhouse cruelty.

meanings.en: vider l'abcès = to clear the air, lance the boil
meanings.note: Vider l'abcès. Masculine noun ('le abcès', plural 'les abcès') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'abscess'.

examples.text: Au moins, nous avons vidé l'abcès ensemble.
examples.trans: At least, we cleared the air together.

examples.text: Il fallait crever l'abcès rapidement.
examples.trans: It was necessary to lance the boil quickly.

meanings.note: Honeybee; 'cire d'abeille' = beeswax.

examples.text: Les abeilles butinent les fleurs du tilleul tout l'été.
examples.trans: The bees forage on the linden blossoms all summer.

examples.text: Ce meuble ancien est nourri à la cire d'abeille.
examples.trans: This antique piece of furniture is conditioned with beeswax.

meanings.note: Common idiom. Masculine noun ('le abord', plural 'les abords') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'approach'.
Common idiom. Masculine noun ('le abord', plural 'les abords') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'approach'.

examples.text: D'abord, parlons travail.
examples.trans: First of all, let's talk about work.

examples.text: Non, je ne crois pas que je vais l'épouser. D'abord, parce qu'elle préfère les femmes.
examples.trans: No, I don't think that I'm going to marry her. First, because she prefers women.

examples.text: Pense d'abord à ta santé, Andréa.
examples.trans: Think first of your health, Andrea.

meanings.note: Often in à l'abri de ('sheltered from').

examples.text: Bonsoir! Entrez vite à l'abri de la pluie, monsieur.
examples.trans: Good evening! Come quickly inside out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: Voici l'abri sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the shelter on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la absence', plural 'les absences') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'absence'.

examples.text: Son absence remarquée.
examples.trans: His noticed absence.

examples.text: Voilà le flyer. Ça s'appelle Absence.
examples.trans: Here's the flyer. It's called Absence.

examples.text: Ça s'appelle Absence.
examples.trans: It's called Absence.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'absent'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Notre directeur est absent du bureau toute la semaine.
examples.trans: Our director is absent from the office all week.

examples.text: Il avait l'air complètement absent pendant la réunion.
examples.trans: He looked completely spaced out during the meeting.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'absolute'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: L'horreur absolue!
examples.trans: Total horror!

examples.text: Un silence absolu.
examples.trans: Complete silence.

examples.text: L'horreur absolue! C'était comme si elle avait treize ans.
examples.trans: Total horror! It was as if she were thirteen.

meanings.note: Pas absolument.
Pas absolument.

examples.text: Absolument. Vous aimez le cinéma?
examples.trans: Absolutely. Do you like films?

examples.text: C'est absolument vrai.
examples.trans: It's absolutely true.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'abstract'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est encore abstrait.
examples.trans: It is still abstract.

examples.text: C'est encore très abstrait pour moi.
examples.trans: It is still very abstract for me.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'absurd'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est complètement absurde!
examples.trans: It is completely absurd!

examples.text: Une idée absurde.
examples.trans: An absurd idea.

examples.text: Quoi? Pourquoi pas? C'est complètement absurde!
examples.trans: What? Why not? It is completely absurd!

abîmer.gloss: to damage, spoil (s'abîmer = get damaged, chip)

meanings.en: to damage, wear out; (reflexive s'abîmer) to get damaged, chip, spoil
meanings.note: Very common in reflexive s'abîmer for everyday objects that scratch, chip, or wear out.

examples.text: Cette vaisselle épaisse ne s'abîme pas au lavage.
examples.trans: This thick crockery does not get damaged in the wash.

examples.text: Mettez une nappe pour ne pas abîmer le bois de la table.
examples.trans: Put a tablecloth on so as not to damage the wood of the table.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to monopolize'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'accaparé').

examples.text: Tout le monde va t'accaparer.
examples.trans: Everyone will monopolize you.

examples.text: Tout le monde va t'accaparer là-bas.
examples.trans: Everyone will monopolize you over there.

accent.gloss: accent, tone of voice; written accent mark

meanings.note: avoir un accent = to have an accent
Un accent aigu = an acute accent.

examples.text: Vous avez entendu son accent?
examples.trans: Did you hear her accent?

examples.text: Il parle français avec un petit accent.
examples.trans: He speaks French with a slight accent.

meanings.note: Accepts either a direct noun (accepter une offre) or de + infinitive (accepter d'aider).

examples.text: Odette a tout de suite accepté de jouer vendredi soir.
examples.trans: Odette immediately agreed to play on Friday evening.

examples.text: Ce petit stand n'accepte pas les cartes bancaires.
examples.trans: This small stall does not take bank cards.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le accessoiriste', plural 'les accessoiristes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'prop master'.

examples.text: Il est accessoiriste pour le cinéma.
examples.trans: He is a prop master for the cinema.

examples.text: Je suis accessoiriste pour le cinéma.
examples.trans: I am a prop master for cinema.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le accident', plural 'les accidents') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mishap'.

examples.text: C'était un accident.
examples.trans: It was an accident.

examples.text: Complètement par accident! Chez mon cousin, je l'ai ouverte et j'ai vu des partitions et un ruban rouge.
examples.trans: By complete accident! At my cousin's flat, I opened it and saw sheet music and a red ribbon.

meanings.note: Formed from feminine adjective accidentelle + -ment; par erreur is equally natural in speech.

examples.text: Quelqu'un a pris ma valise bleue accidentellement sur le quai.
examples.trans: Someone accidentally took my blue suitcase on the platform.

examples.text: Pardon, j'ai appuyé accidentellement sur la sonnette de la chambre quatre.
examples.trans: Sorry, I accidentally pressed the buzzer for Room 4.

meanings.note: Accompagner quelqu'un au violon = accompany someone on the violin.

examples.text: Le voisin accompagne la pianiste au violon.
examples.trans: The neighbor accompanies the pianist on the violin.

examples.text: Je vous accompagne jusqu'au portail.
examples.trans: I will walk you to the gate.

meanings.note: mission accomplie = mission accomplished
Accomplir un devoir. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to accomplish, carry out'.

examples.text: Mission accomplie, Andréa!
examples.trans: Mission accomplished, Andrea!

examples.text: Il a accompli un grand travail.
examples.trans: He accomplished a great task.

examples.text: Mission accomplie, Andréa.
examples.trans: Mission accomplished, Andrea.

examples.text: Nous avons un accord.
examples.trans: We have a deal.

examples.text: Bonjour Thibault, merci d'être venu. D'accord, je peux retenir ça.
examples.trans: Hello Thibault, thank you for coming. Okay, I can remember that.

meanings.en: to tune (a musical instrument); to grant
meanings.note: Used for tuning string or keyboard instruments (*accorder un piano*, *accorder une guitare*) as well as granting a request.

examples.text: Le technicien vient accorder le piano avant le concert.
examples.trans: The technician is coming to tune the piano before the concert.

examples.text: Il faut accorder chaque corde avec patience.
examples.trans: You have to tune each string patiently.

related.gloss: string (of a piano or violin); rope

accoucher.gloss: to give birth, be in labor

meanings.en: to give birth, deliver a baby; to be in labor
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to give birth'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'accouché').

examples.text: Elle est en train d'accoucher.
examples.trans: She is in labor / giving birth.

examples.text: L'actrice va bientôt accoucher.
examples.trans: The actress will give birth soon.

examples.text: Elle accouche! Tu as besoin d'un médecin!
examples.trans: She is in labor! You need a doctor!

meanings.note: The final c is silent. Masculine noun ('le accroc', plural 'les accrocs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hitch'.
Masculine noun ('le accroc', plural 'les accrocs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hitch'.

examples.text: Un petit accroc.
examples.trans: A little hitch.

examples.text: Tout s'est passé sans accroc.
examples.trans: Everything went without a hitch.

examples.text: Une crise ou un accroc?
examples.trans: A crisis or a hitch?

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Où est-ce que j'accroche ce miroir rond? À gauche de la fenêtre ou à droite?
examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?

examples.text: C'est facile à accrocher ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to hang up, hook together.

meanings.note: À l'accueil = at reception. Masculine noun ('le accueil', plural 'les accueils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'reception'.
Un accueil chaleureux. Masculine noun ('le accueil', plural 'les accueils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'reception'.

examples.text: Claire, vous avez le sens de l'accueil! Vous me sauvez la vie!
examples.trans: Claire, you have a gift for hospitality! You are saving my life!

examples.text: Les décibels? Alors neuf sur dix, ce n'était pas une note pour mon accueil?
examples.trans: Decibels? So nine out of ten was not a score for my welcome?

examples.text: Votre accueil mérite dix sur dix! Mais en réalité, je suis architecte acousticien.
examples.trans: Your welcome deserves ten out of ten! In reality, though, I am an acoustic architect.

meanings.note: Des gens accueillants. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'welcoming'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ils ne sont pas très accueillants.
examples.trans: They are not very welcoming.

examples.text: Un endroit très accueillant.
examples.trans: A very welcoming place.

meanings.note: Accueillir un invité. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to welcome, to receive'.

examples.text: Accueillir notre nouveau junior.
examples.trans: To welcome our new junior.

examples.text: Elle nous accueille chaleureusement.
examples.trans: She welcomes us warmly.

examples.text: Faites-moi confiance. Descendons l'accueillir.
examples.trans: Trust me. Let us go down and welcome him.

meanings.note: Takes direct object for the person or thing blamed (*accuser le vent*, *accuser quelqu'un de quelque chose*).

examples.text: Enfant, il accusait toujours le chat quand un verre tombait.
examples.trans: As a child, he always blamed the cat when a glass fell.

examples.text: N'accusez pas la pluie si vous avez oublié votre parapluie.
examples.trans: Don't blame the rain if you forgot your umbrella.

meanings.note: Un accès ouvert à la cour = open access to the courtyard. Same spelling in singular and plural.

examples.text: L'accès au jardin est libre l'après-midi.
examples.trans: Access to the garden is open in the afternoon.

examples.text: Ce couloir donne accès à la cour.
examples.trans: This hallway gives access to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to access'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'accédé').

examples.text: Accéder aux profondeurs.
examples.trans: To access the depths.

examples.text: Accéder au dossier.
examples.trans: To access the file.

examples.text: Avec Mathias, c'est difficile d'accéder aux profondeurs.
examples.trans: With Mathias, it is difficult to reach the depths.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'accelerator pedal, throttle'.

examples.text: Appuie sur l'accélérateur.
examples.trans: Press on the accelerator.

examples.text: N'appuie pas sur le frein et l'accélérateur.
examples.trans: Do not press on the brake and the accelerator.

acharner.gloss: to pursue relentlessly; s'acharner = to persist fiercely

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to pursue fiercely'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'acharné').

examples.text: Ils s'acharnent à réussir.
examples.trans: They persist relentlessly in succeeding.

examples.text: Pourtant, Mathias adore cette lutte acharnée.
examples.trans: Yet, Mathias loves this fierce struggle.

meanings.note: stem changes to achèt- when the ending is silent

examples.text: Les Allemands achètent l'agence.
examples.trans: The Germans are buying the agency.

examples.text: J'achète du pain.
examples.trans: I'm buying bread.

examples.text: Avec les Allemands qui achètent l'agence, qu'est-ce qu'on va faire?
examples.trans: With the Germans buying the agency, what are we going to do?

meanings.note: feminine: acheteuse; from 'acheter'

examples.text: L'acheteur est allemand.
examples.trans: The buyer is German.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé un acheteur pour l'agence. C'est une offre sérieuse.
examples.trans: I've found a buyer for the agency. It's a serious offer.

examples.text: Ils nous donnent trente jours avant la visite des nouveaux acheteurs!
examples.trans: They give us thirty days before the new buyers inspect it!

meanings.note: Masculine material noun; combined with *en* or *d'* (*en acier*, *fil d'acier*).

examples.text: Les cordes graves et aiguës sont en fil d'acier.
examples.trans: The low and high strings are made of steel wire.

examples.text: Cette petite clé en acier est très solide.
examples.trans: This small steel wrench is very sturdy.

meanings.note: Feminine: acousticienne.

examples.text: Votre accueil mérite dix sur dix! Mais en réalité, je suis architecte acousticien.
examples.trans: Your welcome deserves ten out of ten! In reality, though, I am an acoustic architect.

examples.text: Architecte acousticien! Vous dessinez des salles de concert?
examples.trans: An acoustic architect! Do you design concert halls?

meanings.note: Same form in masculine and feminine singular because it already ends in -e. (As a feminine noun, l'acoustique means 'the acoustics' of a room.)

examples.text: Antoine étudie le confort acoustique du jardin d'hiver.
examples.trans: Antoine studies the acoustic comfort of the winter garden.

examples.text: Un plafond en bois offre une qualité acoustique remarquable.
examples.trans: A wooden ceiling provides remarkable acoustic quality.

meanings.note: Takes ç before a/o: nous acquiesçons.

examples.text: Article quatorze de la loi sur le vieux quartier de {CITY} — et mon frère ici vient de faire oui de la tête!
examples.trans: Clause fourteen of the {CITY} Old Quarter Act—and my brother here just nodded!

examples.text: C'est facile à acquiescer ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to nod in agreement, assent together.

meanings.note: Acte quatre = act four.

examples.text: Tchekhov, La Mouette, acte quatre.
examples.trans: Chekhov, The Seagull, act four.

examples.text: Le premier acte.
examples.trans: The first act.

meanings.note: Feminine: actrice.

examples.text: Deux de nos acteurs.
examples.trans: Two of our actors.

examples.text: C'est un acteur célèbre.
examples.trans: He's a famous actor.

meanings.note: Il faut être actif. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.
La population active. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Pour séduire, il faut être très actif!
examples.trans: To seduce, one must be very active!

examples.text: Elle mène une vie très active.
examples.trans: She leads a very active life.

meanings.note: Activity and events; an action film has energetic or dramatic events.

examples.text: Je veux de l'action!
examples.trans: I want action!

examples.text: C'est un film d'action.
examples.trans: It's an action film.

examples.text: Je veux du mouvement, de l'action, de l'énergie!
examples.trans: I want movement, action, energy!

meanings.note: l'actionnaire majoritaire = the majority shareholder

examples.text: L'actionnaire majoritaire de l'agence.
examples.trans: The majority shareholder of the agency.

examples.text: Monsieur Janowski, vous êtes actionnaire majoritaire d'ASK avec soixante pour cent.
examples.trans: Mr. Janowski, you are majority shareholder of ASK with sixty percent.

examples.text: Je suis l'actionnaire majoritaire.
examples.trans: I am the majority shareholder.

meanings.note: Masculine: acteur.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas actrice.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress.

examples.text: C'est une grande actrice.
examples.trans: She's a great actress.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Mon travail actuel.
examples.trans: My current job.

examples.text: La situation actuelle.
examples.trans: The current situation.

examples.text: Mais j'adore mon travail actuel.
examples.trans: But I love my current work.

meanings.note: faux ami: means currently, not actually

examples.text: Il n'est pas en couple actuellement.
examples.trans: He is not currently in a relationship.

examples.text: Actuellement en vacances.
examples.trans: Currently on vacation.

examples.text: Nous faisons actuellement une thérapie de couple.
examples.trans: We are currently doing couples therapy.

meanings.note: A practitioner of acupuncture.

examples.text: Je connais un excellent acupuncteur.
examples.trans: I know an excellent acupuncturist.

examples.text: Tu connais un acupuncteur pour ça?
examples.trans: Do you know an acupuncturist for that?

meanings.note: The total amount to pay in a restaurant: demander l’addition.
Addition or sum in arithmetic.

examples.text: L'addition, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: The bill, please.

examples.text: L'addition est chère.
examples.trans: The bill is expensive.

examples.text: Prends ton temps, je règle l'addition.
examples.trans: Take your time, I am settling the bill.

meanings.note: For a final parting. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'farewell', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Adieu, mon ami.
examples.trans: Farewell, my friend.

examples.text: Il a dit adieu.
examples.trans: He said goodbye.

examples.text: Adieu, Samuel.
examples.trans: Farewell, Samuel.

examples.text: J'ai peur de l'administration.
examples.trans: I'm scared of the tax office.

examples.text: L'administration est fermée.
examples.trans: The office is closed.

examples.text: Tu peux leur dire? J'ai peur de l'administration.
examples.trans: Can you tell them? I'm scared of the tax office.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Votre travail ici est vraiment admirable, Ulrika.
examples.trans: Your work here is truly admirable, Ulrika.

examples.text: Un dévouement admirable pour la cause.
examples.trans: An admirable dedication to the cause.

examples.text: Votre honnêteté est tout à fait admirable.
examples.trans: Your honesty is entirely admirable.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le admirateur', plural 'les admirateurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'admirer'.

examples.text: Elle a beaucoup d'admirateurs.
examples.trans: She has many admirers.

examples.text: Une star comme toi a beaucoup d'admirateurs!
examples.trans: A star like you has many admirers!

examples.text: Viens, tes admirateurs attendent aux loges.
examples.trans: Come, your fans are waiting at the dressing rooms.

meanings.note: Avoir de l'admiration pour means admire; grande strengthens that respect.

examples.text: J'ai une grande admiration pour vous.
examples.trans: I have great admiration for you.

examples.text: Avec admiration.
examples.trans: With admiration.

meanings.note: To admire, gaze at with wonder or appreciation.

examples.text: Les voyageurs s'arrêtent pour admirer la façade en pierre.
examples.trans: Travelers stop to admire the stone facade.

examples.text: J'admire beaucoup la patience des artisans.
examples.trans: I greatly admire the patience of craftspeople.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la adoption', plural 'les adoptions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'legal adoption of a child'.

examples.text: L'adoption plénière de l'enfant.
examples.trans: The full adoption of the child.

examples.text: L'adoption plénière ne sera plus possible.
examples.trans: Full adoption will no longer be possible.

examples.text: Tu pourras faire une adoption simple.
examples.trans: You can still do a simple adoption.

examples.text: Ils sont adorables.
examples.trans: They're lovely.

examples.text: Quel chien adorable!
examples.trans: What an adorable dog!

meanings.note: Stronger than aimer for things.

examples.text: J'adore Paris!
examples.trans: I love Paris!

examples.text: Ni l'un ni l'autre! Il a adoré les poutres calmes et nous a remerciés.
examples.trans: Neither! He loved the quiet beams and thanked us.

meanings.note: Regular -ir (-issant) verb built from doux.

examples.text: Parce que les volets en bois mouillés adoucissent l'écho des pavés...
examples.trans: Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the cobblestones...

examples.text: C'est facile à adoucir ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to soften, mellow together.

meanings.note: Une nouvelle adresse. Feminine noun ('la adresse', plural 'les adresses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'address'.

examples.text: Quelle est ton adresse?
examples.trans: What is your address?

examples.text: Pas encore? Prenez le numéro et l'adresse de notre hôtel, s'il vous plaît. Merci!
examples.trans: Not yet? Please take our guesthouse number and address. Thank you!

meanings.note: adresser qch à qqn = to send/address sth to sb
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to speak to'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'adressé').

examples.text: Elle est adressée au juge.
examples.trans: It is addressed to the judge.

examples.text: Elle est adressée au juge familial.
examples.trans: It is addressed to the family judge.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le adultère', plural 'les adultères') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'adultery'.

examples.text: Cette histoire d'adultère fait la une des journaux.
examples.trans: This story of adultery is making the front page of the newspapers.

examples.text: Le film raconte un adultère compliqué à Paris.
examples.trans: The film tells the story of a complicated affair in Paris.

meanings.note: Plural: mes affaires.

examples.text: Prends tes affaires.
examples.trans: Get your things.

examples.text: C'est une bonne affaire.
examples.trans: It's a good deal.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'starving'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Les animaux affamés attendent leur repas.
examples.trans: The starving animals wait for their meal.

examples.text: Huit clients affamés descendent à sept heures et demie!
examples.trans: Eight hungry guests come down at half past seven!

meanings.note: affecter quelque chose = to have an effect on something
Administrative assignment.

examples.text: Ça n'affectera pas leur intention de racheter mes parts?
examples.trans: Won't that affect their intention to buy my shares?

examples.text: Cela affecte notre travail.
examples.trans: That affects our work.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la affection', plural 'les affections') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'warmth'.

examples.text: C'est une marque d'affection.
examples.trans: It is a sign of affection.

examples.text: C'est la preuve de ton affection.
examples.trans: It is proof of your affection.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un au revoir très affectueux.
examples.trans: A very affectionate goodbye.

examples.text: Un geste affectueux.
examples.trans: An affectionate gesture.

examples.text: C'était rien, juste un au revoir très affectueux.
examples.trans: It was nothing, just a very affectionate goodbye.

meanings.note: en tête d'affiche = top-billed, starring

examples.text: Guy Marchand est en tête d'affiche.
examples.trans: Guy Marchand has top billing.

examples.text: Une belle affiche de cinéma.
examples.trans: A beautiful movie poster.

examples.text: C'est la nouvelle affiche de mon film.
examples.trans: It is the new poster for my movie.

meanings.note: Afficher complet = to have no vacancies.

examples.text: Oh... sous cette pluie? Tous les hôtels près de la gare affichaient complet.
examples.trans: Oh... in this rain? Every hotel near the station had a full sign.

examples.text: C'est facile à afficher ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to display, post together.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'panicked'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Voilà Arlette qui arrive affolée.
examples.trans: Here comes Arlette in a panic.

examples.text: Regarde, voilà Arlette qui arrive affolée.
examples.trans: Look, here comes Arlette in a panic.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un drame affreux.
examples.trans: An awful drama.

examples.text: Une nouvelle affreuse.
examples.trans: Dreadful news.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas un drame affreux.
examples.trans: That is not an awful drama.

examples.text: Tu m'agaces!
examples.trans: You're annoying me!

examples.text: Ce bruit agace Andréa.
examples.trans: That noise annoys Andréa.

meanings.note: From 'agacer' (to annoy).

examples.text: C'est agaçant.
examples.trans: It's annoying.

examples.text: Il a une voix très agaçante.
examples.trans: He has a very annoying voice.

meanings.note: une agence artistique = a talent agency

examples.text: Bienvenue à l'agence!
examples.trans: Welcome to the agency!

examples.text: Le facteur vient de me faire signer un recommandé. Il y a un tampon rouge d'agence immobilière.
examples.trans: The postman just had me sign for registered mail. There is a red property-agency stamp.

meanings.note: An appointment diary or planner; an agenda for a meeting is usually un ordre du jour.

examples.text: Elle est dans mon agenda?
examples.trans: Is she in my diary?

examples.text: Mon agenda est plein.
examples.trans: My diary is full.

examples.text: Est-ce que Rebecca Vialle est dans mon agenda aujourd'hui?
examples.trans: Is Rebecca Vialle in my diary today?

meanings.note: Commonly used in France for civil servants and municipal staff (*un agent de la mairie*).

examples.text: L'agent de la mairie vérifie les documents à l'accueil.
examples.trans: The municipal clerk checks the documents at reception.

examples.text: Un agent du service culturel visite la salle demain.
examples.trans: An officer from the cultural department is visiting the hall tomorrow.

meanings.note: Feminine form of agent. Feminine noun ('la agente', plural 'les agentes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'agent'.

examples.text: Ma nouvelle agente.
examples.trans: My new agent.

examples.text: Elle ferait une excellente agente.
examples.trans: She would make an excellent agent.

examples.text: Prenez soin de vous... Ma Nouvelle Agente.
examples.trans: Take care of yourself... My New Agent.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to worsen'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aggravé').

examples.text: Tu ne fais qu'aggraver les choses.
examples.trans: You are only making things worse.

examples.text: Tu ne fais qu'aggraver ta tristesse.
examples.trans: You are only making your sadness worse.

meanings.en: to act; to take effect, work
meanings.note: *Laisser agir* ('to let work / soak in') is standard for oil, soap, or remedies.

examples.text: Laissez agir le produit cinq minutes avant de rincer.
examples.trans: Let the product work for five minutes before rinsing.

examples.text: En cas d'orage, il faut agir vite et calmement.
examples.trans: In a storm, you have to act quickly and calmly.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'agitation, restlessness'.

examples.text: Calmer son agitation.
examples.trans: To calm one's agitation.

examples.text: L'agitation du plateau.
examples.trans: The bustle of the set.

examples.text: Désolé pour mon agitation tout à l'heure.
examples.trans: Sorry for my agitation earlier.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le agneau', plural 'les agneaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lamb'.

examples.text: Il prépare un rôti d'agneau.
examples.trans: He is preparing a roast lamb.

examples.text: Regarde, cet agneau est vraiment parfait.
examples.trans: Look, this lamb is truly perfect.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la agonie', plural 'les agonies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'death throes'.
Feminine noun ('la agonie', plural 'les agonies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'death scene'.

examples.text: J'en suis à ma septième agonie!
examples.trans: I am on my seventh death scene!

examples.text: L'agonie d'un personnage tragique.
examples.trans: The death scene of a tragic character.

examples.text: Oh non, j'en suis à ma septième agonie!
examples.trans: Oh no, I am already on my seventh death scene!

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Cette eau est trop agressive.
examples.trans: This water is too harsh.

examples.text: Oui, elle est beaucoup trop agressive pour moi.
examples.trans: Yes, it is much too harsh for me.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Un moment très agréable.
examples.trans: A very pleasant moment.

examples.text: C'est agréable.
examples.trans: It is pleasant.

examples.text: Calme et agréable, merci, mais cette valise semble très lourde aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Quiet and pleasant, thank you, though this suitcase feels very heavy today.

meanings.note: Understanding or surprise.

examples.text: Ah, d'accord!
examples.trans: Ah, I see!

examples.text: Ah bon? Il y a un problème avec ma réservation?
examples.trans: Oh really? Is there a problem with my booking?

meanings.note: Playful exclamation of discovery.

examples.text: Aha! Vous aviez peur qu'en signant votre nom, le grand frère têtu reste chez lui!
examples.trans: Aha! You feared that if you signed your name, the stubborn big brother would stay home!

examples.text: Aha! Voilà la clé du grenier!
examples.trans: Aha! There's the attic key!

examples.text: Merci pour ton aide.
examples.trans: Thanks for your help.

examples.text: Tu as besoin d'aide?
examples.trans: Do you need help?

meanings.note: Aider quelqu'un, no preposition.

examples.text: Après avoir gardé sa valise bleue toute la semaine? Il voudra sûrement nous aider!
examples.trans: After guarding his blue suitcase all week? He will surely want to help us!

examples.text: Tu peux m'aider avec cette valise?
examples.trans: Can you help me with this suitcase?

meanings.note: Les aigus = the high notes. Masculine noun ('le aigu', plural 'les aigus') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'high note'.

examples.text: Des aigus comme le feuillage.
examples.trans: High notes like foliage.

examples.text: Monter dans les aigus.
examples.trans: To reach the high notes.

examples.text: Et des aigus comme le feuillage.
examples.trans: And highs like foliage.

meanings.note: Sewing or compass needle; clock or watch hand ('les aiguilles d'une horloge').

examples.text: L'aiguille de la boussole indique toujours le nord.
examples.trans: The compass needle always points north.

examples.text: La grande aiguille approche de midi.
examples.trans: The minute hand is nearing noon.

meanings.note: D'ailleurs = besides, moreover.

examples.text: On peut se retrouver ailleurs?
examples.trans: Can we meet up somewhere else?

examples.text: Je préfère aller ailleurs.
examples.trans: I prefer to go elsewhere.

examples.text: Nous pouvons trouver un autre financement ailleurs.
examples.trans: We can find another financing elsewhere.

meanings.note: Comme c'est aimable = how kind of you.

examples.text: Oh, comme c'est aimable, monsieur. Juste un demi-verre.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind, sir. Just half a glass.

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment aimable.
examples.trans: This place is really kind, pleasant, gracious.

meanings.note: attiré comme un aimant = drawn like a magnet

examples.text: Je suis attiré par elle comme un aimant.
examples.trans: I'm drawn to her like a magnet.

examples.text: C'est un aimant très fort.
examples.trans: It's a very strong magnet.

meanings.note: With things and places.
With people.

examples.text: Tu n'aimais pas Mandelieu?
examples.trans: Didn't you like Mandelieu?

examples.text: J'aime le cinéma.
examples.trans: I like films.

meanings.note: In this way, like that; therefore, thus.

examples.text: Pliez la carte ainsi pour ne pas abîmer les coins.
examples.trans: Fold the map like this so you don't damage the corners.

examples.text: Ainsi, chacun repart avec un souvenir du jardin.
examples.trans: Thus, everyone leaves with a keepsake from the garden.

meanings.note: avoir l'air + adjective = to look, to seem
The air we breathe.
Un air de musique.

examples.text: Tu as l'air fatigué.
examples.trans: You look tired.

examples.text: Elle a l'air contente.
examples.trans: She looks happy.

meanings.note: être à l'aise = to be comfortable, at ease

examples.text: Je ne suis pas très à l'aise.
examples.trans: I am not very comfortable.

examples.text: Mettez-vous à l'aise.
examples.trans: Make yourself comfortable.

examples.text: Il n'est pas très à l'aise avec les filles...
examples.trans: He is not very comfortable with girls...

meanings.note: Ajouter une pincée de sel = add a pinch of salt.

examples.text: Ajoutez un peu de beurre doux à la fin.
examples.trans: Add a little unsalted butter at the end.

examples.text: J'ajoute deux chaises autour de la table.
examples.trans: I am adding two chairs around the table.

examples.text: Avez-vous un problème avec l'alcool?
examples.trans: Do you have a problem with alcohol?

examples.text: Je ne bois pas d'alcool.
examples.trans: I don't drink alcohol.

examples.text: Avez-vous un problème avec l'alcool, le Coca-Cola, les bonbons?
examples.trans: Do you have a problem with alcohol, Coca-Cola, sweets?

meanings.note: Capitalised as a noun.

meanings.en: un Allemand / une Allemande = a German (person)
meanings.note: Capitalised as a noun.

examples.text: Un acheteur allemand.
examples.trans: A German buyer.

examples.text: Les Allemands achètent l'agence.
examples.trans: The Germans are buying the agency.

examples.text: Avec les Allemands qui achètent l'agence, qu'est-ce qu'on va faire?
examples.trans: With the Germans buying the agency, what are we going to do?

meanings.note: aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
Je vais déjeuner.
Imperative used to encourage.

examples.text: Allez, au travail!
examples.trans: Come on, to work!

examples.text: Madame Odette, tout va bien? Vous avez sonné!
examples.trans: Madam Odette, is everything alright? You rang the bell!

meanings.note: faire l'aller-retour = to make the round trip

examples.text: Je voulais faire l'aller-retour.
examples.trans: I wanted to make the round trip.

examples.text: Un billet aller-retour.
examples.trans: A round-trip ticket.

examples.text: Vous pouvez faire l'aller-retour en dix minutes?
examples.trans: Can you run there and back in ten minutes?

meanings.note: Allergique à = allergic to.

examples.text: Je suis allergique!
examples.trans: I'm allergic!

examples.text: Il est allergique aux chats.
examples.trans: He's allergic to cats.

meanings.note: Idiomatic French interj expression meaning 'come on', frequent in natural conversational dialogue.

examples.text: Allez, viens avec nous!
examples.trans: Come on, come with us!

examples.text: Allez, on y va maintenant!
examples.trans: Come on, let's go now!

examples.text: Allez, calme-toi et respire un peu.
examples.trans: Come on, calm down and breathe a bit.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to ally'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allié').

examples.text: Nous devrions nous allier contre nos rivaux.
examples.trans: We should ally against our rivals.

examples.text: Il allie talent et détermination.
examples.trans: He combines talent and determination.

examples.text: Nous devrions nous allier contre Mathias.
examples.trans: We should ally ourselves against Mathias.

meanings.note: A female ally is une alliée.

examples.text: C'est notre seul allié.
examples.trans: He is our only ally.

examples.text: Nous avons un allié.
examples.trans: We have an ally.

meanings.en: to light (a lantern, candle, fire) or turn on (a lamp)
meanings.note: Allumer les lanternes = light the lanterns; opposite of éteindre.

examples.text: Nous allumons les lanternes de la cour à six heures.
examples.trans: We light the courtyard lanterns at six o'clock.

examples.text: Tu peux allumer la petite lampe du bureau?
examples.trans: Can you turn on the little desk lamp?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la allure', plural 'les allures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'look'.
Feminine noun ('la allure', plural 'les allures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'speed'.

examples.text: Elle a une belle allure.
examples.trans: She has a fine look.

examples.text: Elle vous donnera une allure inoubliable.
examples.trans: It will give you an unforgettable look.

meanings.note: Only on the telephone.

examples.text: Je compose le numéro... Allô? Quelqu'un a signalé une valise bleue échangée?
examples.trans: I am dialling the number... Hello? Did anyone report a swapped blue suitcase?

examples.text: Oui, allô?
examples.trans: Yes, hello?

meanings.note: Jeudi, alors.

examples.text: Alors, tu viens?
examples.trans: So, are you coming?

examples.text: Alors pourquoi on ne la loue jamais aux clients?
examples.trans: Then why do we never rent it to guests?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le alzheimer', plural 'les alzheimers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'Alzheimer's disease'.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas Alzheimer.
examples.trans: It is not Alzheimer's.

examples.text: Regardez les examens, ce n'est pas Alzheimer.
examples.trans: Look at the tests, it is not Alzheimer's.

meanings.note: In French pastry, *aux amandes* (plural) describes dishes made with ground or sliced almonds (*biscuits aux amandes*, *pâte aux amandes*).

examples.text: Elle prépare des biscuits dorés aux amandes pour le thé.
examples.trans: She bakes golden almond biscuits for tea.

examples.text: Un peu de poudre d'amande rend la pâte plus fondante.
examples.trans: A little almond flour makes the crust more tender.

meanings.note: Feminine: une amante.

examples.text: Parce que toi, tu es l'amant idéal, c'est ça?
examples.trans: Because you're the ideal lover, is that it?

examples.text: Elle a un amant.
examples.trans: She has a lover.

meanings.note: ambassadrice de marque = brand ambassador

examples.text: L'ambassadrice parfaite de la marque.
examples.trans: The perfect brand ambassador.

examples.text: Un ambassadeur culturel.
examples.trans: A cultural ambassador.

examples.text: Ils te voient comme l'ambassadrice parfaite.
examples.trans: They see you as the perfect ambassador.

meanings.note: une bonne ambiance = a great atmosphere

examples.text: Une ambiance sexy au bord de la piscine.
examples.trans: A sexy atmosphere by the pool.

examples.text: Il y a une bonne ambiance ici.
examples.trans: There's a good atmosphere here.

examples.text: Une ambiance sexy, des maillots de bain... La petite Mathurine est superbe!
examples.trans: A sexy atmosphere, swimsuits... Little Mathurine is gorgeous!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'ambient'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: De l'eau à température ambiante.
examples.trans: Room-temperature water.

examples.text: Je voudrais de l'eau à température ambiante.
examples.trans: I would like room-temperature water.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un projet ambitieux.
examples.trans: An ambitious project.

examples.text: Elle est très ambitieuse.
examples.trans: She is very ambitious.

examples.text: C'est un projet très original et ambitieux.
examples.trans: It is a very original and ambitious project.

meanings.note: Payer une amende = to pay a fine.

examples.text: Il y aura une amende à payer.
examples.trans: There will be a fine to pay.

examples.text: Il y aura une amende à payer, et vous irez au tribunal de commerce.
examples.trans: There will be a fine to pay, and you will go to commercial court.

examples.text: Béatrice, les amendes vont retomber sur ASK.
examples.trans: Beatrice, the fines will fall back on ASK.

meanings.en: to bring (person or pet), to take along
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to bring'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'amené').

examples.text: Amène-le chez moi ce soir.
examples.trans: Bring him to my place tonight.

examples.text: Nous amènerons la moitié de la mairie aux tables de Nadia la semaine prochaine, promis.
examples.trans: We will bring half of City Hall to Nadia's tables next week, I promise.

meanings.note: A female friend is une amie.

examples.text: C'est un ami très cher.
examples.trans: He is a very dear friend.

examples.text: Mon ami est là.
examples.trans: My friend is here.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'friendly'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: J'offre simplement un conseil amical.
examples.trans: I am simply offering friendly advice.

examples.text: Une discussion amicale et chaleureuse.
examples.trans: A friendly and warm discussion.

examples.text: J'offre simplement un conseil amical à Nathalie.
examples.trans: I am simply offering friendly advice to Nathalie.

meanings.en: in a friendly way, warmly, cordially
meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Discuter amicalement.
examples.trans: To chat in a friendly way.

examples.text: Bien amicalement.
examples.trans: Best regards.

examples.text: Je voulais seulement discuter amicalement.
examples.trans: I only wanted to chat in a friendly way.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la amitié', plural 'les amitiés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'friendship'.

examples.text: Transmets-lui mes amitiés.
examples.trans: Pass along my regards to her.

examples.text: Une longue amitié.
examples.trans: A long friendship.

examples.text: J'en suis ravi. Transmets-lui mes amitiés.
examples.trans: I am delighted. Pass along my warm regards to her.

meanings.en: to cushion, to absorb a shock
meanings.note: Amortir le choc.
Finance.

examples.text: Le coussin a amorti le choc.
examples.trans: The cushion absorbed the shock.

examples.text: Tes jolies petites fesses ont amorti le choc.
examples.trans: Your pretty little backside cushioned the shock.

meanings.note: Love or affection; scène d’amour means love scene.

examples.text: C'est une histoire d'amour.
examples.trans: It's a love story.

examples.text: Mon amour!
examples.trans: My love!

examples.text: Quand vous regardez des films, des scènes d'amour...
examples.trans: When you watch films, love scenes...

meanings.note: mon amour-propre ne me le permet pas = my pride won't allow it

examples.text: Mon amour-propre ne me le permet pas.
examples.trans: My pride will not allow it.

examples.text: C'est une question d'amour-propre.
examples.trans: It is a matter of pride.

meanings.note: A sweetheart or boyfriend; feminine amoureuse.
As an adjective, amoureux de means in love with someone.

examples.text: Elle a un amoureux.
examples.trans: She has a boyfriend.

examples.text: On est amoureux!
examples.trans: We're in love!

examples.text: Françoise avait un amoureux. Devine qui!
examples.trans: Françoise had a boyfriend. Guess who!

meanings.note: Avoir des ampoules aux mains.

examples.text: Regardez mes ampoules!
examples.trans: Look at my blisters!

examples.text: J'ai des ampoules aux pieds.
examples.trans: I have blisters on my feet.

examples.text: Regardez mes ampoules! Touchez mes mains.
examples.trans: Look at my blisters! Touch my hands.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'fun'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est amusant pour les enfants.
examples.trans: It is fun for children.

examples.text: Une histoire amusante.
examples.trans: A funny story.

examples.text: C'est amusant pour des enfants de dix ans.
examples.trans: It's fun for ten-year-old children.

meanings.note: Ça m'amuse = that amuses me.
On s'amuse bien.

examples.text: Je suis content que ça t'amuse.
examples.trans: I'm glad that amuses you.

examples.text: Très bien. Très drôle. Je suis content que ça t'amuse.
examples.trans: Very good. Very funny. I'm glad that amuses you.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas t'empêcher de t'amuser.
examples.trans: I do not want to stop you from having fun.

meanings.note: Améliorer la communication. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to improve'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'amélioré').

examples.text: Qu'allez-vous améliorer chez ASK?
examples.trans: What will you improve at ASK?

examples.text: Nous voulons améliorer nos résultats.
examples.trans: We want to improve our results.

examples.text: Oui, cela va s'améliorer avec le temps.
examples.trans: Yes, that will improve with time.

meanings.note: lowercase as an adjective; Américain(e) with a capital for a person

examples.text: Les actrices américaines.
examples.trans: American actresses.

examples.text: Un film américain.
examples.trans: An American film.

meanings.note: for counting: vingt ans; for age: j'ai vingt ans

examples.text: Ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: His twenty years of career.

examples.text: Elle a quarante ans.
examples.trans: She's forty.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la analyse', plural 'les analyses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'analysis'.

examples.text: Je suis impressionné par ton analyse.
examples.trans: I am impressed by your analysis.

examples.text: Je suis très impressionné par ton analyse.
examples.trans: I am very impressed by your analysis.

meanings.note: une ancienne amie = an old / former friend
Un immeuble ancien.

examples.text: Une de ses anciennes amies.
examples.trans: One of his old friends.

examples.text: Mon ancien bureau.
examples.trans: My former office.

meanings.note: always masculine, even for a woman: elle est un ange
Affectionate: mon ange.

examples.text: Tu es un ange!
examples.trans: You're an angel!

examples.text: Mon ange gardien.
examples.trans: My guardian angel.

meanings.note: Parler anglais = to speak English. Masculine noun ('le anglais', plural 'les anglais') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'English language'.
Un Anglais / une Anglaise. Masculine noun ('le anglais', plural 'les anglais') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'English language'.

examples.text: Elle parle parfaitement anglais.
examples.trans: She speaks English perfectly.

examples.text: J'apprends l'anglais.
examples.trans: I am learning English.

examples.text: Passez-moi la grosse clé anglaise à votre gauche.
examples.trans: Pass me the heavy wrench on your left.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le angle', plural 'les angles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'corner'.
Masculine noun ('le angle', plural 'les angles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'angle'.

examples.text: Je t'attends à l'angle de la rue.
examples.trans: I am waiting for you on the street corner.

examples.text: Un angle droit.
examples.trans: A right angle.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la angoisse', plural 'les angoisses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'anxiety'.

examples.text: Les pleurs expriment son angoisse.
examples.trans: The crying expresses its anxiety.

examples.text: Bien au contraire, c'est de l'angoisse.
examples.trans: Quite the opposite, it is anxiety.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'anxious'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Vous êtes angoissés?
examples.trans: Are you anxious?

examples.text: Bonne chance pour le film! Vous êtes angoissés?
examples.trans: Good luck with the film! Are you anxious?

examples.text: Je me sens tellement angoissé, Gabriel.
examples.trans: I feel so anxious, Gabriel.

meanings.note: Des animaux dans les bois.

examples.text: Des animaux qui gambadent dans les bois?
examples.trans: Animals frolicking in the woods?

examples.text: Tu es un animal, Didier.
examples.trans: You are an animal, Didier.

meanings.note: une métaphore animalière = an animal metaphor

examples.text: Un documentaire animalier.
examples.trans: A wildlife documentary.

examples.text: Le monde animalier.
examples.trans: The animal world.

examples.text: Il est très métaphore animalière, non?
examples.trans: He is very into animal metaphors, isn't he?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la animation', plural 'les animations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'animation'.

examples.text: C'est un film d'animation.
examples.trans: It is an animated movie.

examples.text: Je prépare maintenant un beau film d'animation.
examples.trans: I am preparing a beautiful animated film now.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'animated'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est un dessin animé.
examples.trans: It is a cartoon.

examples.text: Mais cela n'arrive que dans les dessins animés!
examples.trans: But that only happens in cartoons!

meanings.note: L'anis étoilé = star anise.

examples.text: Prends du thé à l'anis étoilé.
examples.trans: Have some star-anise tea.

examples.text: Ça sent l'anis.
examples.trans: It smells of aniseed.

examples.text: Tu as mal au ventre? Prends du thé à l'anis étoilé.
examples.trans: Does your stomach hurt? Have some star-anise tea.

meanings.note: Birthday ('bon anniversaire!'); anniversary of an event.

examples.text: Nous fêtons le trentième anniversaire de l'ouverture de l'hôtel.
examples.trans: We are celebrating the thirtieth anniversary of the hotel's opening.

examples.text: Pour son anniversaire, elle a préparé un gâteau aux amandes.
examples.trans: For her birthday, she baked an almond cake.

meanings.note: Takes ç before a/o: nous annonçons. Annoncer une bonne nouvelle = share good news.

examples.text: Il a une bonne nouvelle à nous annoncer.
examples.trans: He has good news to tell us.

examples.text: Le panneau annonce l'ouverture du salon de thé.
examples.trans: The sign announces the opening of the tearoom.

meanings.note: Feminine: annuelle.

examples.text: Sauf s'il écrit pour le Guide annuel de Lyon!
examples.trans: Unless he writes for the annual Lyon Guide!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment annuel.
examples.trans: This place is really annual, yearly.

meanings.note: Le train est annulé = the train is canceled.

examples.text: Heureusement, notre train du matin n'est pas annulé.
examples.trans: Thankfully, our morning train is not canceled.

examples.text: Le client a appelé pour annuler sa réservation.
examples.trans: The guest called to cancel his reservation.

meanings.note: Chaque année, une bonne année.

examples.text: Chaque année.
examples.trans: Every year.

examples.text: Bonne année!
examples.trans: Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Describes someone whose identity is not known, or something sent without a name.

examples.text: Un donneur anonyme.
examples.trans: An anonymous donor.

examples.text: Une lettre anonyme.
examples.trans: An anonymous letter.

examples.text: Entre un donneur anonyme et un ami, je choisis l'ami.
examples.trans: Between an anonymous donor and a friend, I choose the friend.

anse.gloss: handle (of a cup, jug, or basket)

meanings.en: curved handle (of a cup, mug, pot, or basket)
meanings.note: Used for curved loop handles on cups, pitchers, and baskets; contrast poignée (door handle) and manche (straight tool/pan handle).

examples.text: Prenez la tasse par l'anse: le thé est brûlant.
examples.trans: Hold the cup by the handle: the tea is piping hot.

examples.text: L'anse du panier en osier est très solide.
examples.trans: The handle of the wicker basket is very sturdy.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le antispasme', plural 'les antispasmes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'antispasmodic'.

examples.text: Acheter des antispasmes.
examples.trans: Buy antispasmodics.

examples.text: Achète des antispasmes, s'il te plaît.
examples.trans: Buy some antispasmodics, please.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le antiterrorisme', plural 'les antiterrorismes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'counter-terrorism'.

examples.text: La lutte contre l'antiterrorisme.
examples.trans: The anti-terrorism fight.

examples.text: Une unité d'antiterrorisme.
examples.trans: A counter-terrorism unit.

examples.text: Quoi, alors? Antiterrorisme?
examples.trans: What then? Counter-terrorism?

meanings.note: qui est à l'appareil? = who's calling?
Appareil photo = camera.

examples.text: Qui est à l'appareil?
examples.trans: Who is speaking?

examples.text: Hôtel du Tilleul, bonjour! Claire à l'appareil.
examples.trans: Hotel du Tilleul, good morning! Claire speaking.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Apparemment, c'est vrai.
examples.trans: Apparently, it is true.

examples.text: Le moment venu. Aujourd'hui, apparemment.
examples.trans: When the time came. Today, apparently.

examples.text: Vous parlez un anglais remarquable, apparemment.
examples.trans: You speak remarkable English, apparently.

meanings.note: Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'flat, residence, apartment'.

examples.text: Mon appartement est calme.
examples.trans: My apartment is quiet.

examples.text: Mon appartement est en plein travaux.
examples.trans: My apartment is under renovation.

examples.text: Vendre notre appartement dans mon dos?
examples.trans: Selling our apartment behind my back?

meanings.note: Appartenir à quelqu'un. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to belong'.

examples.text: Ton corps t'appartient.
examples.trans: Your body belongs to you.

examples.text: Ce livre m'appartient.
examples.trans: This book belongs to me.

examples.text: appartient à
examples.trans: belongs to

meanings.note: Un appel de Rio = a call from Rio.

examples.text: On attend l'appel.
examples.trans: We're waiting for the call.

examples.text: J'ai un appel.
examples.trans: I've got a call.

meanings.note: je peux t'appeler? = can I call you?

examples.text: Claire, appelez tout de suite le bureau des objets trouvés de la gare.
examples.trans: Claire, call the station lost-and-found office right away.

examples.text: Attendez... bonjour, monsieur! Vous appelez pour la valise bleu foncé?
examples.trans: Wait... hello, sir! Are you calling about the dark-blue suitcase?

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb (-iss- in plural and imperfect: nous applaudissons).

examples.text: Toute la cour applaudit à la fin du morceau.
examples.trans: The whole courtyard applauds at the end of the piece.

examples.text: Les voisins ont applaudi pendant deux minutes.
examples.trans: The neighbors applauded for two minutes.

meanings.en: to apply, to put into practice
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to apply'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'appliqué').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to enforce'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'appliqué').

examples.text: Oui, nous appliquons le règlement.
examples.trans: Yes, we enforce the regulations.

examples.text: Il faut appliquer la loi avec rigueur.
examples.trans: The law must be applied with rigor.

meanings.note: For people use 'amener'.

examples.text: Tu apportes le dessert?
examples.trans: Are you bringing dessert?

examples.text: J'apporte des draps blancs propres de l'armoire à linge!
examples.trans: I will bring clean white sheets from the linen cupboard!

meanings.note: Apprendre le français.
apprendre quelque chose à quelqu'un

examples.text: Attendez qu'Étienne apprenne qu'il a paniqué toute la nuit pour des décibels!
examples.trans: Wait until Etienne learns he panicked all night over decibels!

examples.text: J'apprends le français.
examples.trans: I'm learning French.

meanings.note: Feminine form: une apprentie.

examples.text: Les deux apprentis préparent la pâte dès six heures.
examples.trans: The two apprentices prepare the dough starting at six o'clock.

examples.text: Chaque boulanger a commencé comme apprenti.
examples.trans: Every baker started out as an apprentice.

meanings.en: to bring closer, move closer; to approach
meanings.note: Transitive (*approchez la lampe*, 'bring the lamp closer') or reflexive (*s'approcher de*, 'to come closer to').

examples.text: Approchez votre chaise de la table pour mieux voir.
examples.trans: Pull your chair closer to the table to see better.

examples.text: J'approche la lampe pour éclairer le fond du tiroir.
examples.trans: I bring the lamp closer to light the back of the drawer.

related.gloss: to back up, retreat, shrink back

meanings.note: Approuvé! on a certificate = Approved!

examples.text: La mairie a officiellement approuvé notre projet.
examples.trans: City Hall officially approved our project.

examples.text: Tout le quartier approuve la réouverture du café.
examples.trans: The whole neighborhood approves of reopening the café.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to appreciate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'apprécié').

examples.text: J'apprécie beaucoup ce geste généreux.
examples.trans: I appreciate this generous gesture very much.

examples.text: Tout le monde apprécie son travail.
examples.trans: Everyone appreciates his work.

examples.text: Merci Andréa, j'apprécie beaucoup ce geste.
examples.trans: Thank you Andrea, I really appreciate this gesture.

meanings.en: to press, push down (appuyer sur un bouton / un interrupteur)
meanings.note: Stem changes -y- -> -i- before a silent ending (j'appuie, ils appuient, j'appuierai), while keeping -y- in nous appuyons / vous appuyez.

examples.text: Appuyez doucement sur le loquet pour débloquer le siège.
examples.trans: Press gently on the catch to release the seat.

examples.text: Claire appuie sur l'interrupteur en laiton et la pièce s'éclaire.
examples.trans: Claire presses the brass switch and the room lights up.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le appétit', plural 'les appétits') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hunger'.

examples.text: Couper l'appétit de quelqu'un.
examples.trans: To ruin someone's appetite.

examples.text: Stop! Vous m'avez coupé l'appétit.
examples.trans: Stop! You ruined my appetite.

examples.text: Être avec toi m'ouvre l'appétit.
examples.trans: Being with you whets my appetite.

meanings.note: Après le déjeuner.

examples.text: Après, elles ne peuvent plus s'arrêter.
examples.trans: Then they can't stop anymore.

examples.text: On mange, et après on part.
examples.trans: We eat, and afterwards we leave.

meanings.note: Masculine or feminine. This lesson uses masculine cet après-midi. Both après-midi and après-midis are accepted plural spellings.

examples.text: Je travaille cet après-midi.
examples.trans: I'm working this afternoon.

examples.text: Je vous en prie, madame. Lundi après-midi, l'entrée était sombre.
examples.trans: Go right ahead, madam. Monday afternoon, the lobby was dark.

meanings.note: Watercolor paint or painting ('peindre à l'aquarelle').

examples.text: Elle a peint les toits du village à l'aquarelle.
examples.trans: She painted the village rooftops in watercolor.

examples.text: Une petite aquarelle encadrée décore le couloir.
examples.trans: A small framed watercolor decorates the hallway.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (*un grand arbre*), despite ending in *-e*.

examples.text: Un grand arbre donne de l'ombre à toute la cour.
examples.trans: A tall tree shades the whole courtyard.

examples.text: Les oiseaux chantent dans les arbres dès le matin.
examples.trans: Birds sing in the trees first thing in the morning.

meanings.note: Une fenêtre en arc is an arched window. Notice the final -c is pronounced /k/.

examples.text: Les fenêtres en arc donnent sur le jardin intérieur.
examples.trans: The arched windows overlook the inner garden.

examples.text: La pierre forme un bel arc au-dessus de la porte.
examples.trans: The stone forms a lovely arch above the door.

meanings.note: Architectural arch over a passage.

examples.text: Juste sous cette arche. Je vais monter la valise bleue pour vous.
examples.trans: Right under this archway. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

examples.text: Voici l'arche sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the arch, archway on the table.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine (un/une architecte).

examples.text: Votre accueil mérite dix sur dix! Mais en réalité, je suis architecte acousticien.
examples.trans: Your welcome deserves ten out of ten! In reality, though, I am an acoustic architect.

examples.text: Architecte acousticien! Vous dessinez des salles de concert?
examples.trans: An acoustic architect! Do you design concert halls?

examples.text: Un architecte qui travaille sur les vieilles cours historiques dans tout Lyon!
examples.trans: An architect who works on historic old courtyards all over Lyon!

meanings.note: Un atelier d'architecture = an architecture studio.

examples.text: Il ouvre un petit atelier d'architecture dans la rue.
examples.trans: He is opening a small architecture studio on the street.

examples.text: L'architecture ancienne de l'hôtel est très lumineuse.
examples.trans: The old architecture of the hotel is very bright.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la ardeur', plural 'les ardeurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ardor'.

examples.text: Elle défend le projet avec ardeur.
examples.trans: She defends the project with passion.

examples.text: Tu défends ce projet avec beaucoup d'ardeur.
examples.trans: You defend this project with great passion.

meanings.note: Normally uncountable when referring to money.
The metal silver, also normally uncountable.

examples.text: Je n'ai pas d'argent.
examples.trans: I have no money.

examples.text: Alors tu n'as pas besoin d'argent, finalement.
examples.trans: So you don't need money, after all.

examples.text: Donnez-moi un sac et de l'argent!
examples.trans: Give me a bag and some cash!

meanings.note: Feminine noun; en argile describes pottery or tiles made of clay.

examples.text: Ce pot en argile garde l'eau fraîche tout l'été.
examples.trans: This clay pot keeps water cool all summer.

examples.text: L'artisan travaille l'argile humide sur son tour.
examples.trans: The potter shapes the damp clay on his wheel.

meanings.note: Une aristocrate for a woman, un aristocrate for a man; the noun itself has the same spelling.

examples.text: Je suis une aristocrate.
examples.trans: I am an aristocrat.

examples.text: Cette aristocrate est ici.
examples.trans: This aristocrat is here.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la arme', plural 'les armes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'weapon'.

examples.text: Ils prennent les armes.
examples.trans: They take up arms.

examples.text: Les personnages prennent les armes sans hésiter.
examples.trans: The characters take up arms without hesitating.

examples.text: Je ne te donnerai pas plus d'armes.
examples.trans: I will not give you more weapons.

meanings.note: Armoire à linge = linen cupboard.

examples.text: J'apporte des draps blancs propres de l'armoire à linge!
examples.trans: I will bring clean white sheets from the linen cupboard!

examples.text: Voici l'armoire sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the wardrobe, tall cupboard on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la armure', plural 'les armures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'armor'.

examples.text: Une armure brillante.
examples.trans: Shining armor.

examples.text: On pourrait même l'appeler le chevalier en armure brillante d'ASK!
examples.trans: We could even call him ASK's knight in shining armor!

meanings.note: Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'arrangement, deal'.

examples.text: Un arrangement temporaire.
examples.trans: A temporary arrangement.

examples.text: Nous avons trouvé un arrangement.
examples.trans: We found an arrangement.

examples.text: Un arrangement temporaire, juste une façade.
examples.trans: A temporary arrangement, just a facade.

meanings.note: on va arranger ça = we'll sort this out
Arranger des fleurs.
Ça m'arrange = that suits me.

examples.text: On va arranger ça.
examples.trans: We're going to fix this.

examples.text: Ça m'arrange.
examples.trans: That suits me.

meanings.note: je viens d'arriver = I've just arrived
Qu'est-ce qui arrive?.

examples.text: Je viens d'arriver à Paris.
examples.trans: I've just arrived in Paris.

examples.text: Le train arrive.
examples.trans: The train is arriving.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la arrivée', plural 'les arrivées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'arrival'.

examples.text: Compris! Vous avez déjà coupé l'arrivée d'eau principale?
examples.trans: Got it! Did you turn off the main water supply already?

examples.text: L'arrivée du train est à huit heures.
examples.trans: The train arrives at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Adverbial phrase. Invariable French adverb meaning 'back'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Masculine noun. Invariable French adverb meaning 'back'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Un pas en arrière vers l'avant!
examples.trans: A step backward toward the future!

examples.text: Regarder en arrière.
examples.trans: To look backward.

examples.text: Je reviens un peu en arrière.
examples.trans: I am going back a little.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'arrogant'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Deux types particulièrement arrogants.
examples.trans: Two particularly arrogant guys.

examples.text: Deux types arrogants sont arrivés.
examples.trans: Two arrogant guys showed up.

meanings.note: le vingtième arrondissement = the twentieth district

examples.text: J'habite dans le vingtième arrondissement.
examples.trans: I live in the twentieth arrondissement.

examples.text: Les arrondissements de Paris.
examples.trans: The districts of Paris.

examples.text: Pourquoi refuses-tu d'aller dans cet arrondissement?
examples.trans: Why do you refuse to go to that arrondissement?

meanings.note: arroser les plantes = to water the plants

examples.text: Il faut arroser le bonsaï.
examples.trans: You have to water the bonsai.

examples.text: Arroser le jardin.
examples.trans: To water the garden.

examples.text: Je vais l'arroser tous les jours.
examples.trans: I am going to water it every day.

meanings.en: stop, halt; stop on a route
meanings.note: Final -t is silent (/aʁɛ/). Prochain arrêt means 'next stop', and sans arrêt means 'non-stop'.

examples.text: L'arrêt de bus est juste au coin de la place.
examples.trans: The bus stop is right at the corner of the square.

examples.text: Prochain arrêt: la boulangerie pour le pain chaud!
examples.trans: Next stop: the bakery for warm bread!

meanings.note: Arrête! / arrêtez!.
Arrête! / arrêtez!.

examples.text: Des petites bibliothèques et des cours, surtout. Je mesure comment les vieux murs arrêtent le bruit.
examples.trans: Small libraries and courtyards, mostly. I measure how old walls block noise.

examples.text: Seulement des petits chiffres gris! Mon cœur s'est arrêté à la page un!
examples.trans: Only small grey numbers! My heart stopped at page one!

examples.text: Il arrête de travailler à six heures.
examples.trans: He stops working at six.

meanings.note: Un art dramatique = dramatic art. Masculine noun ('le art', plural 'les arts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'art'.
L'art de la comédie. Masculine noun ('le art', plural 'les arts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'art'.

examples.text: C'est un art dramatique puissant.
examples.trans: It is powerful dramatic art.

examples.text: L'art du cinéma français.
examples.trans: The art of French cinema.

examples.text: Sans totale liberté, l'art est inutile.
examples.trans: Without total freedom, art is useless.

meanings.note: Used for legal clauses, newspaper pieces, and shop items.

examples.text: Article quatorze de la loi sur le vieux quartier de {CITY} — et mon frère ici vient de faire oui de la tête!
examples.trans: Clause fourteen of the {CITY} Old Quarter Act—and my brother here just nodded!

examples.text: En mots simples, je vous en prie! Que dit l'article quatorze?
examples.trans: In plain words, please! What does clause fourteen say?

examples.text: Articulez, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Articulate, please.

examples.text: Il n'articule pas assez.
examples.trans: He doesn't enunciate enough.

meanings.note: Skilled craftsperson who makes bread, furniture, pottery, or metalwork by hand.
Feminine form: une artisane.

examples.text: De la musique, de la pâtisserie, des tables d'artisans et une plaque d'or pour la cour la plus chaleureuse!
examples.trans: Music, baking, craft tables, and a golden plaque for the warmest courtyard!

examples.text: Les artisans du quartier exposent leurs créations dans la rue des Tilleuls.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood craftspeople display their creations on Rue des Tilleuls.

meanings.note: Un grand artiste = a great artist. Masculine noun ('le artiste', plural 'les artistes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'artist'.

examples.text: Il s'agit de vrais artistes.
examples.trans: It is about real artists.

examples.text: Une agence pour les artistes.
examples.trans: An agency for artists.

examples.text: Je travaille avec des artistes photographes.
examples.trans: I work with photographic artists.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un nouvel élan artistique.
examples.trans: A new artistic impetus.

examples.text: Une création artistique.
examples.trans: An artistic creation.

examples.text: Je propose un nouvel élan artistique.
examples.trans: I offer a new artistic impetus.

meanings.note: prendre l'ascenseur = to take the elevator

examples.text: Les portes de l'ascenseur se ferment.
examples.trans: The elevator doors are closing.

examples.text: L'ascenseur est en panne.
examples.trans: The elevator is out of order.

examples.text: Les portes de l'ascenseur se ferment enfin.
examples.trans: The elevator doors are finally closing.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sanitized'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un monde tellement aseptisé.
examples.trans: Such a sanitized world.

examples.text: Une pièce aseptisée.
examples.trans: A sterile room.

examples.text: Vous vivez dans un monde tellement aseptisé!
examples.trans: You live in such a sanitized world!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to murder'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'assassiné').

examples.text: L'autre a été assassiné.
examples.trans: The other was murdered.

examples.text: Il a été assassiné hier.
examples.trans: He was murdered yesterday.

examples.text: L'un battait sa femme, l'autre a été assassiné.
examples.trans: One beat his wife, the other was murdered.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la assemblée', plural 'les assemblées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'assembly'.

examples.text: Votre discours touche l'assemblée.
examples.trans: Your speech touches the assembly.

examples.text: L'assemblée applaudit le discours.
examples.trans: The assembly applauds the speech.

examples.text: Votre discours va énormément toucher l'assemblée.
examples.trans: Your speech will touch the audience enormously.

meanings.note: S'asseoir sur une chaise.
Transitive.

examples.text: Un coussin pour t'asseoir.
examples.trans: A cushion to sit down on.

examples.text: Tu dois te balader avec un coussin pour t'asseoir.
examples.trans: You have to walk around with a cushion to sit on.

meanings.note: j'en ai assez = I've had enough, I'm fed up
Assez bien.

examples.text: J'en ai assez!
examples.trans: I've had enough!

examples.text: C'est assez difficile.
examples.trans: It's quite difficult.

meanings.note: Une assiette blanche = a white plate.

examples.text: Posez chaque part de tarte sur une petite assiette.
examples.trans: Set each slice of tart on a small plate.

examples.text: Les assiettes propres sont empilées près du comptoir.
examples.trans: The clean plates are stacked near the counter.

meanings.note: Past participle of *asseoir* used as an adjective (*rester assis / assise*, 'to stay seated'); final *-s* is silent in masculine, pronounced `/z/` in feminine *assise*.

examples.text: Restez assise quelques minutes avec un verre d'eau.
examples.trans: Stay seated for a few minutes with a glass of water.

examples.text: Les clients sont assis sous les arbres du jardin.
examples.trans: The guests are sitting under the garden trees.

meanings.note: Feminine: assistante.

examples.text: Voici l'assistant sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the assistant, helper on the table.

examples.text: Tout est prêt dans la cour.
examples.trans: Everything is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Masculine: assistant. Feminine noun ('la assistante', plural 'les assistantes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'assistant'.

examples.text: Je suis la nouvelle assistante.
examples.trans: I'm the new assistant.

examples.text: Andréa cherche une assistante.
examples.trans: Andréa is looking for an assistant.

examples.text: Je trouve une assistante qui me plaît.
examples.trans: I find an assistant I like.

meanings.note: Une association de défense. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'association, society'.
Travailler en association. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'association, society'.

examples.text: Une association cherche à faire interdire votre film.
examples.trans: An association is trying to ban your film.

examples.text: Une association culturelle.
examples.trans: A cultural association.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to associate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'associé').

examples.text: Il s'associe avec des réalisateurs.
examples.trans: He partners with directors.

examples.text: Nous nous associons pour ce projet.
examples.trans: We team up for this project.

examples.text: Il s'associe directement avec les réalisateurs.
examples.trans: He partners directly with directors.

meanings.note: Feminine form is *une associée* (`/asɔsje/`).

examples.text: Mon associé s'occupe des plans au bureau cette semaine.
examples.trans: My partner is handling the blueprints at the office this week.

examples.text: Les deux associés ont ouvert leur atelier à Lyon.
examples.trans: The two partners opened their studio in Lyon.
