meanings.note: Une associée de l'agence. Feminine noun ('la associée', plural 'les associées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'partner'.

examples.text: Je suis associée de l'agence.
examples.trans: I am a partner in the agency.

examples.text: Elle est associée depuis cinq ans.
examples.trans: She has been a partner for five years.

meanings.en: matching, in a matching style or colour
meanings.note: Placed after the noun; assorti à quelque chose means 'matching something'.

examples.text: Claire achète douze tasses et un pot à lait blanc assorti.
examples.trans: Claire buys twelve cups and a matching white milk jug.

examples.text: Les nappes sont assorties aux rideaux du salon.
examples.trans: The tablecloths match the curtains in the lounge.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'assume'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'assumé').

examples.text: J'assume mes actes.
examples.trans: I take responsibility for my actions.

examples.text: J'assume l'entière responsabilité.
examples.trans: I take full responsibility.

examples.text: Appelle ta fille maintenant et assume ton rôle.
examples.trans: Call your daughter now and take on your role.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la assurance', plural 'les assurances') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'insurance policy or company'.

examples.text: L'assurance prend en charge le tournage.
examples.trans: The insurance covers the filming.

examples.text: Les assurances remboursent généralement ces frais imprévus.
examples.trans: Insurances generally reimburse these unforeseen costs.

examples.text: Les assurances feront simplement leur travail normal.
examples.trans: The insurances will simply do their normal work.

meanings.note: A life-insurance or life-insurance savings contract; the French term can refer to accumulated savings, as in Arlette's offer here.

examples.text: J'ai mon assurance-vie.
examples.trans: I have my life insurance.

examples.text: Ton assurance-vie?
examples.trans: Your life insurance?

examples.text: Ton assurance-vie? Tu es sûre?
examples.trans: Your life insurance? Are you sure?

assurer.gloss: to secure, to assure, to insure

meanings.en: to secure, to assure, to guarantee

examples.text: L'avenir d'ASK est assuré.
examples.trans: ASK's future is secure.

examples.text: Je vous assure que c'est vrai.
examples.trans: I assure you that it's true.

meanings.note: un atelier de théâtre = a theater workshop

examples.text: L'atelier de scène.
examples.trans: The stage workshop.

examples.text: Travailler dans son atelier.
examples.trans: To work in one's workshop.

examples.text: Il y a une lampe de lecture en laiton dans mon atelier en bas.
examples.trans: There is a brass reading lamp in my workshop downstairs.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la atmosphère', plural 'les atmosphères') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'atmosphere'.
Feminine noun ('la atmosphère', plural 'les atmosphères') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'atmosphere'.

examples.text: L'atmosphère est déjà très claire.
examples.trans: The atmosphere is already very clear.

examples.text: Il y a une bonne atmosphère dans l'équipe.
examples.trans: There is a good atmosphere in the team.

meanings.note: Un atout majeur. Masculine noun ('le atout', plural 'les atouts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'asset'.

examples.text: Est-il un atout ou un véritable handicap?
examples.trans: Is he an asset or a real handicap?

examples.text: Son expérience est un précieux atout.
examples.trans: His experience is a valuable asset.

meanings.note: attacher sa ceinture = fasten one's seat belt

examples.text: Il attache ses lacets.
examples.trans: He ties his shoelaces.

examples.text: Il y a une petite carte en papier attachée à la poignée.
examples.trans: There is a small paper card tied to the handle.

examples.text: Tout à l'heure, j'ai vu une deuxième page attachée derrière le courrier.
examples.trans: Earlier, I spotted a second page clipped behind the letter.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la attaque', plural 'les attaques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'attack'.

meanings.en: passer à l'attaque = to go on the offensive
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la attaque', plural 'les attaques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'attack'.

examples.text: On passe à l'attaque avec Luchini.
examples.trans: We're going on the attack with Luchini.

examples.text: Une attaque surprise.
examples.trans: A surprise attack.

examples.text: Comment réagissez-vous à ces attaques?
examples.trans: How do you react to these attacks?

meanings.note: attaquer en justice = to take legal action

examples.text: On va attaquer en justice.
examples.trans: We will sue in court.

examples.text: L'avocat attaque le magazine.
examples.trans: The lawyer is suing the magazine.

examples.text: Mais quand elle est attaquée, je la défends. On va attaquer en justice, et soyez sûrs qu'on gagnera.
examples.trans: But when it is attacked, I defend it. We will sue in court, and be sure we will win.

meanings.note: Conjugated like *peindre* and *éteindre* (*j'atteins, nous atteignons, j'ai atteint*).

examples.text: Avec l'échelle, on atteint facilement le haut de la fenêtre.
examples.trans: With the ladder, we easily reach the top of the window.

examples.text: Je suis trop petit pour atteindre la dernière étagère.
examples.trans: I am too short to reach the top shelf.

meanings.note: No preposition: attendre quelqu'un.
Il vous attend?.

examples.text: Attendez, elle est bleu foncé, exactement comme la vôtre!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

examples.text: Attendez, cette rue est juste ici dans notre quartier, à cinq minutes!
examples.trans: Wait, that street is right here in our neighbourhood, five minutes away!

examples.text: Attendez. Regardez en bas sur la marche en pierre.
examples.trans: Wait. Look down on the stone step.

meanings.note: Salle d'attente = waiting room. Feminine noun ('la attente', plural 'les attentes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'wait'.

examples.text: Deux mois d'attente.
examples.trans: Two months of waiting.

examples.text: Contre toute attente.
examples.trans: Against all expectations.

examples.text: Deux mois d'attente, c'est une catastrophe.
examples.trans: Two months of waiting, it is a disaster.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Sois très attentif au travail.
examples.trans: Be very attentive at work.

examples.text: Sois très attentif et très convaincant.
examples.trans: Be very attentive and very convincing.

meanings.note: As a warning shout: attention!.
Faire attention = to be careful.

examples.text: Attention, la route!
examples.trans: Careful, the road!

examples.text: Fais attention!
examples.trans: Be careful!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'caring'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un homme attentionné et doux.
examples.trans: A caring and gentle man.

examples.text: Un homme simple, travailleur et attentionné.
examples.trans: A simple, hardworking, and caring man.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Je vous écoute attentivement.
examples.trans: I am listening to you attentively.

examples.text: D'accord, je vous écoute attentivement.
examples.trans: Agreed, I am listening to you closely.

examples.text: Je t'écoute attentivement, Mathias.
examples.trans: I am listening attentively, Mathias.

meanings.note: atterrir comme une héroïne = to land like a heroine

examples.text: Vous me voyez atterrir comme une héroïne?
examples.trans: Do you see me landing like a heroine?

examples.text: L'avion va atterrir.
examples.trans: The plane is going to land.

examples.text: C'est attirant.
examples.trans: It is attractive.

examples.text: Elle est très attirante.
examples.trans: She is very attractive.

meanings.note: attirer le public = to draw audiences

examples.text: Elle attire le public.
examples.trans: She draws the public.

examples.text: Ce film attire beaucoup de monde.
examples.trans: This film attracts a lot of people.

examples.text: Elle attire le public, et elle aime vos vidéos.
examples.trans: She draws the public, and she likes your videos.

meanings.en: to grab, catch, get hold of
meanings.note: Everyday verb for grabbing an object or catching a ball/train (*attrape mon bras!*, *attraper un bol en haut*).

examples.text: Attrape ma main avant de descendre la marche.
examples.trans: Grab my hand before stepping down the stair.

examples.text: Peux-tu attraper les bols sur l'étagère du haut?
examples.trans: Can you grab the bowls on the top shelf?

meanings.note: atténuer la douleur = to ease the pain

examples.text: Ça n'atténue pas la douleur.
examples.trans: It doesn't ease the pain.

examples.text: Pour atténuer le choc.
examples.trans: To soften the blow.

examples.text: Ça n'atténuera pas mon humiliation publique.
examples.trans: That will not diminish my public humiliation.

meanings.note: à + le contracted: au boulot, au téléphone

examples.text: Je suis au boulot.
examples.trans: I'm at work.

examples.text: Elle est au téléphone.
examples.trans: She's on the phone.

meanings.note: Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'by the way', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Au fait, tu as appelé Dominique?
examples.trans: By the way, did you call Dominique?

examples.text: Au fait, où est-elle?
examples.trans: By the way, where is she?

examples.text: Au fait, tu as appelé Dominique Besnehard?
examples.trans: By the way, did you call Dominique Besnehard?

meanings.en: être au point = to have got it right, to be ready
meanings.note: Of a skill or a plan. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'ready', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Je suis presque au point.
examples.trans: I've almost got it.

examples.text: Le projet est au point.
examples.trans: The plan is ready.

examples.text: Oui. Je suis presque au point. Je vous rappelle.
examples.trans: Yes. I've almost got it. I'll call you back.

meanings.note: Neutral, polite.

examples.text: Merci, au revoir!
examples.trans: Thank you, goodbye!

examples.text: Au revoir, madame.
examples.trans: Goodbye, madam.

examples.text: Au revoir, Andréa!
examples.trans: Goodbye, Andréa!

meanings.note: Beyond, past ('au-delà de' = beyond, past).

examples.text: Le sentier continue au-delà du vieux pont.
examples.trans: The path continues past the old bridge.

examples.text: On aperçoit les collines bleues juste au-delà.
examples.trans: You can glimpse the blue hills just beyond.

meanings.note: Au-dessus de = above, over.

examples.text: Sur la cour, juste au-dessus du vieux tilleul. C'est très calme.
examples.trans: The courtyard, right above the old linden tree. It is very quiet.

examples.text: Seulement une clé dorée peinte au-dessus de la porte. Montrez cette vanne au vendeur.
examples.trans: Only a painted golden key above the door. Show this valve to the clerk.

meanings.note: *À l'aube* ('at dawn') is the standard idiomatic time phrase.

examples.text: La boulangère allume son four dès l'aube.
examples.trans: The baker lights her oven at dawn.

examples.text: Le ciel devient rose à l'aube au-dessus des toits.
examples.trans: The sky turns pink at dawn above the rooftops.

meanings.note: Aucune before a feminine noun. Normally singular; plural forms occur with nouns used only in the plural or with a special plural meaning.

examples.text: Aucune nouvelle.
examples.trans: No news.

examples.text: Je n'ai aucun problème.
examples.trans: I have no problem.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: C'est un film d'auteur très audacieux.
examples.trans: It is a very bold art film.

examples.text: Elle a pris une décision audacieuse.
examples.trans: She made a daring decision.

examples.text: Voici un modèle flashy et audacieux.
examples.trans: Here is a flashy and daring design.

meanings.note: Final t is pronounced.

examples.text: Bonne chance pour l'audit.
examples.trans: Good luck with the audit.

examples.text: L'audit commence demain.
examples.trans: The audit starts tomorrow.

meanings.note: Passer une audition = to audition.

examples.text: Personne ne me propose d'auditions!
examples.trans: Nobody offers me auditions!

examples.text: Tu as volé cette audition!
examples.trans: You stole this audition!

meanings.en: to audition, try out (for a role)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to audition'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'auditionné').

examples.text: Sofia a auditionné pour beaucoup de rôles.
examples.trans: Sofia auditioned for many roles.

examples.text: Elle auditionne demain.
examples.trans: She is auditioning tomorrow.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la augmentation', plural 'les augmentations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'raise'.

examples.text: Il espère une augmentation de salaire.
examples.trans: He hopes for a salary raise.

examples.text: Une vraie augmentation de salaire enfin?
examples.trans: A real salary raise at last?

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to increase'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'augmenté').

examples.text: Il veut augmenter les salaires.
examples.trans: He wants to increase salaries.

examples.text: Je peux aussi augmenter vos salaires fixes.
examples.trans: I can also increase your fixed salaries.

meanings.note: The film director in this episode.

examples.text: Augustin est réalisateur.
examples.trans: Augustin is a director.

examples.text: Je parle avec Augustin.
examples.trans: I am talking with Augustin.

examples.text: C'est non-stop aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: It's non-stop today.

examples.text: Aujourd'hui, je travaille.
examples.trans: Today I'm working.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'previously'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Je ne l'ai jamais vue auparavant.
examples.trans: I have never seen her beforehand.

examples.text: Non, je ne l'ai jamais vue auparavant.
examples.trans: No, I have never seen her before.

examples.text: Il n'a jamais rien fait auparavant.
examples.trans: He has never done anything before.

meanings.en: auprès de = with, in the presence of, to
meanings.note: Auprès de son père. Core French preposition meaning 'with', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Pas auprès de ton père?
examples.trans: Not to your father?

examples.text: Intervenir auprès de la direction.
examples.trans: To intervene with management.

meanings.note: Moi aussi = me too.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes aussi avec Dany Boon.
examples.trans: You're also having lunch with Dany Boon.

examples.text: Moi aussi.
examples.trans: Me too.

meanings.note: autant + infinitive at the start of a sentence
Autant que.
Degree or quantity without an explicit comparison: manger autant, eat so much.

examples.text: Pourquoi tu manges autant?
examples.trans: Why do you eat so much?

examples.text: Je travaille autant que toi.
examples.trans: I work as much as you.

meanings.note: An author or creator; context can refer to a filmmaker.
For films shaped by a director's personal creative style.

examples.text: C'est un film d'auteur.
examples.trans: It's an art-house film.

examples.text: L'auteur est là.
examples.trans: The author is here.

examples.text: Line est devenue une star, et Françoise a fait du cinéma d'auteur.
examples.trans: Line became a star, and Françoise made art-house films.

meanings.note: a filmmaker who writes and directs their own films

examples.text: Un pôle auteurs-réalisateurs.
examples.trans: A writer-directors department.

examples.text: Tu sais ce que j'aimerais? Un pôle auteurs-réalisateurs.
examples.trans: Do you know what I'd like? A writers-directors department.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Ton jeu était tellement authentique.
examples.trans: Your acting was so authentic.

examples.text: Une émotion authentique.
examples.trans: An authentic emotion.

examples.text: Ton jeu était tellement authentique aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Your acting was so authentic today.

examples.text: Un autographe, s'il vous plaît!
examples.trans: An autograph, please!

examples.text: J'ai un autographe de Cécile.
examples.trans: I have Cécile's autograph.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; the -m- is silent (/otɔn/). Takes en without an article: en automne ('in autumn').

examples.text: Les feuilles du tilleul deviennent dorées en automne.
examples.trans: The linden tree's leaves turn golden in autumn.

examples.text: Nous préparons de la soupe chaude chaque soir d'automne.
examples.trans: We make hot soup every autumn evening.

meanings.note: often plural: les autorisations de tournage
often plural: les autorisations de tournage

examples.text: Il faut une autorisation.
examples.trans: You need a permit.

examples.text: Nous avons les autorisations.
examples.trans: We have the permits.

meanings.note: Used alone (*regarde autour*) or followed by *de* (*autour de la table*, *autour de toi*).

examples.text: Les voisins discutent autour d'une grande théière chaude.
examples.trans: The neighbors chat around a big hot teapot.

examples.text: Regardez autour de vous: tout est propre et rangé.
examples.trans: Look around you: everything is clean and tidy.

meanings.note: Une autre = another (one).
Also a pronoun.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

examples.text: Qui est-ce? Une autre réservation pour ce week-end?
examples.trans: Who is it? Another booking for this weekend?

meanings.note: Autrefois à Paris.

examples.text: Les nobles vivaient autrement autrefois.
examples.trans: Nobles lived differently in the past.

examples.text: Autrefois, elle habitait ici.
examples.trans: She used to live here.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.
Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Je veux faire ce métier autrement.
examples.trans: I want to do this job differently.

examples.text: Fais attention, autrement tu vas tomber.
examples.trans: Be careful, otherwise you will fall.

aux.gloss: to the; at the; in the (plural)

meanings.en: to the; at the; in the (plural)
meanings.note: Contraction of à + les; the following noun phrase is plural.

examples.text: Je parle aux agents.
examples.trans: I am talking to the agents.

examples.text: Le film est tourné aux États-Unis.
examples.trans: The film is shot in the United States.

examples.text: Je ne peux pas avaler ce café, il est trop chaud!
examples.trans: I can't swallow this coffee, it's too hot!

examples.text: Avale ton croissant, le bus arrive!
examples.trans: Swallow your croissant, the bus is coming!

meanings.en: advance; en avance = early, ahead of time
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la avance', plural 'les avances') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'advance'.

examples.text: Vous êtes en avance.
examples.trans: You are early.

examples.text: Prendre de l'avance.
examples.trans: To get ahead.

examples.text: Moi, c'est Henri. Vous êtes en avance de dix minutes.
examples.trans: I am Henri. You are ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to move forward'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'avancé').

examples.text: J'avance... oh, je vois la clé dorée et la porte bleue!
examples.trans: I am walking forward... oh, I see the golden key and the blue door!

examples.text: Le travail avance bien.
examples.trans: The work is progressing well.

meanings.note: Time: avant mon départ.

examples.text: Dernière réunion avant mon départ.
examples.trans: Last meeting before I leave.

examples.text: Viens avant midi.
examples.trans: Come before noon.

meanings.note: Avoir l'avantage de. Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'advantage, benefit'.

examples.text: Tu as l'avantage de travailler ici.
examples.trans: You have the advantage of working here.

examples.text: C'est un grand avantage.
examples.trans: It is a big advantage.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Une offre avantageuse.
examples.trans: An advantageous offer.

examples.text: Un contrat avantageux.
examples.trans: A favorable contract.

examples.text: J'ai reçu une offre très avantageuse.
examples.trans: I received a very advantageous offer.

meanings.note: acronym for accident vasculaire cérébral

examples.text: Vous avez eu un petit AVC.
examples.trans: You had a minor stroke.

examples.text: Vous avez simplement eu un petit AVC.
examples.trans: You simply had a minor stroke.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: You're having lunch with Audiard.

examples.text: Avec plaisir!
examples.trans: With pleasure!

meanings.note: À l'avenir = in the future.

examples.text: Il s'inquiète pour ton avenir professionnel.
examples.trans: He's worried about your professional future.

examples.text: Vraiment? Qu'est-ce qui ne va pas avec mon avenir professionnel?
examples.trans: Really? What's wrong with my professional future?

examples.text: Quelle aventure!
examples.trans: What an adventure!

examples.text: Un film d'aventure.
examples.trans: An adventure film.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la avenue', plural 'les avenues') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'avenue'.

examples.text: Notre agence se trouve sur une grande avenue parisienne.
examples.trans: Our agency is located on a grand Parisian avenue.

examples.text: Nous avons marché tout le long de l'avenue.
examples.trans: We walked all the way down the avenue.

meanings.note: Specifically describes a brisk, heavy burst of rain (*une grosse averse*), heavier than a light *pluie*.

examples.text: Nous avons rentré les chaises juste avant l'averse.
examples.trans: We brought the chairs inside right before the downpour.

examples.text: Après l'averse d'été, les pierres sèchent très vite.
examples.trans: After the summer shower, the stones dry very fast.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le avertissement', plural 'les avertissements') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'warning'.

examples.text: Merci pour cet avertissement.
examples.trans: Thank you for this warning.

examples.text: Merci pour cet avertissement précieux, Charles.
examples.trans: Thank you for this valuable warning, Charles.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sightless'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Elle devient aveugle.
examples.trans: She becomes blind.

examples.text: Ensuite, la petite femme devient aveugle.
examples.trans: Then, the small woman becomes blind.

meanings.note: prendre l'avion = to catch a plane / fly

examples.text: Elle veut les voir avant de prendre son avion.
examples.trans: She wants to see them before catching her flight.

examples.text: Je vais à Rome en avion.
examples.trans: I'm going to Rome by plane.

meanings.note: un avis de décès = a death notice / obituary
À mon avis = in my opinion.

examples.text: Comme un avis de décès?
examples.trans: Like a death notice?

examples.text: À mon avis, c'est une bonne idée.
examples.trans: In my opinion, it's a good idea.

meanings.note: Feminine: avocate. Masculine noun ('le avocat', plural 'les avocats') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lawyer'.
The fruit. Masculine noun ('le avocat', plural 'les avocats') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lawyer'.

examples.text: On attend l'avocat.
examples.trans: We're waiting for the lawyer.

examples.text: C'est mon avocat.
examples.trans: He's my lawyer.

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. On attend l'avocat.
examples.trans: I don't know. We're waiting for the lawyer.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression.

examples.text: J'ai un petit loft.
examples.trans: I've got a little loft.

examples.text: Tu as une réunion.
examples.trans: You have a meeting.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to confess'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'avoué').

examples.text: J'avoue tout.
examples.trans: I confess everything.

examples.text: J'avoue que j'ai un trac terrible.
examples.trans: I confess that I have terrible stage fright.

examples.text: Hervé, je dois tout t'avouer.
examples.trans: Herve, I must confess everything.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le avril', plural 'les avrils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fourth month'.

examples.text: Rien de disponible pour avril.
examples.trans: Nothing available for April.

examples.text: Il n'y a rien de disponible pour avril.
examples.trans: There is nothing available for April.

meanings.note: In mechanics and instrument making, *un axe* is the small metal pin around which a hinge or piano hammer pivots.

examples.text: Ce minuscule axe en laiton tient le marteau bien droit.
examples.trans: This tiny brass pin holds the hammer straight.

examples.text: Mettez une goutte d'huile sur l'axe de la roue.
examples.trans: Put a drop of oil on the wheel axle.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le aéroport', plural 'les aéroports') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'airport'.

examples.text: Je vais à l'aéroport.
examples.trans: I'm going to the airport.

examples.text: À l'aéroport de Dole.
examples.trans: To Dole airport.

examples.text: Je vais chercher Charlotte à l'aéroport.
examples.trans: I am picking up Charlotte at the airport.

meanings.note: Feminine: aînée.

examples.text: Un menuisier vivait là avec ses deux petits-fils: l'aîné jouait du piano, et le petit adorait les trains!
examples.trans: A carpenter lived there with his two grandsons: the older boy played piano, and the little one loved trains!

examples.text: Voici l'aîné sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the eldest child, older brother on the table.

meanings.note: The trema on ï shows a + i are pronounced separately as /aj/ rather than /ɛ/. Used both for sudden physical pain and for comic dismay ('Uh-oh!').

examples.text: Aïe! La plaque du four est encore très chaude.
examples.trans: Ouch! The baking tray is still very hot.

examples.text: Aïe, j'ai oublié mon parapluie sur le comptoir!
examples.trans: Uh-oh, I forgot my umbrella on the counter!

meanings.note: Un or une baby-sitter.

examples.text: Tu n'as pas trouvé de baby-sitter?
examples.trans: Didn't you find a babysitter?

examples.text: La baby-sitter arrive à huit heures.
examples.trans: The babysitter arrives at eight.

examples.text: Bonjour, Audrey. Tu n'as pas trouvé de baby-sitter?
examples.trans: Hello, Audrey. Didn't you find a babysitter?

meanings.note: To brush pastry with glaze, melted butter, or egg wash; to whitewash.

examples.text: Badigeonnez le gâteau tiède de deux cuillères de miel chaud.
examples.trans: Brush the warm cake with two spoons of warm honey.

examples.text: Elle utilise un pinceau doux pour badigeonner la brioche.
examples.trans: She uses a soft brush to glaze the brioche.

meanings.note: Usually plural: les bagages.

examples.text: J'ai enfermé l'autre valise bleue à clé dans notre placard à bagages.
examples.trans: I locked the other blue suitcase in our luggage closet.

examples.text: Voici le bagage sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the piece of luggage on the table.

meanings.note: chercher la bagarre = look for a fight

examples.text: Ils cherchent la bagarre.
examples.trans: They are looking for a fight.

examples.text: Une bagarre dans la rue.
examples.trans: A fight in the street.

meanings.note: Both a finger ring and a pipe ring/collar.

examples.text: Vérifiez bien que la bague à l'intérieur fait vingt millimètres.
examples.trans: Make sure the ring inside is twenty millimetres.

examples.text: Voici la bague sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the ring on the table.

meanings.note: Irregular plural: les baux.

examples.text: Alors le bail de votre hôtel est protégé pour dix ans par la ville!
examples.trans: Then your hotel lease is protected for ten years by the city!

examples.text: Lundi vous avez ouvert notre porte capricieuse, et depuis vous avez sauvé les chambres, les tuyaux, le petit-déjeuner et notre bail.
examples.trans: Monday you opened our tricky door, and since then you saved the rooms, pipes, breakfast, and our lease.

meanings.note: maillot de bain = swimsuit; prendre un bain = to take a bath

examples.text: Elle met son maillot de bain.
examples.trans: She puts on her swimsuit.

examples.text: Je prends un bon bain chaud.
examples.trans: I'm taking a nice hot bath.

examples.text: Et la petite salle de bain à côté? La lumière marche?
examples.trans: What about the small bathroom next door? Does the light work?

related.gloss: swimsuit; prendre un bain = to take a bath

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le baiser', plural 'les baisers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'kiss'.

examples.text: C'est un baiser de respect mutuel.
examples.trans: It is a kiss of mutual respect.

examples.text: Un doux baiser sur la joue.
examples.trans: A gentle kiss on the cheek.

examples.text: C'est un baiser d'adieu?
examples.trans: Is this a goodbye kiss?

meanings.note: en baisse = on the decline, falling

examples.text: Nos bénéfices sont en baisse.
examples.trans: Our profits are down.

examples.text: Une baisse des prix.
examples.trans: A price drop.

examples.text: Sans compter le nouveau cadre sur les salaires, nos bénéfices sont en baisse.
examples.trans: Not to mention the new rules on salaries, our profits are down.

baisser.gloss: to lower, to turn down; to go down

meanings.en: to lower, to drop (eyes, head, voice)
meanings.note: baisser les yeux = to lower one's eyes
les prix baissent = prices are falling

examples.text: Baisse un peu la musique.
examples.trans: Turn the music down a bit.

examples.text: Laissez-moi baisser mes lunettes de mon front... Chambre neuf?!
examples.trans: Let me pull my glasses down from my forehead... Room nine?!

meanings.en: to walk around, to stroll (reflexive se balader)
meanings.note: Informal everyday verb.
Reflexive form for walking around oneself.

examples.text: Tu dois te balader avec un coussin.
examples.trans: You have to walk around with a cushion.

examples.text: Tu dois te balader avec un coussin pour t'asseoir.
examples.trans: You have to walk around with a cushion to sit on.

meanings.note: To swing or rock; 'se balancer' = to sway gently back and forth.

examples.text: Les lanternes en papier se balancent doucement dans la brise du soir.
examples.trans: The paper lanterns sway gently in the evening breeze.

examples.text: Il balance ses jambes, assis sur le vieux mur du jardin.
examples.trans: He swings his legs while sitting on the old garden wall.

meanings.note: Stem alternates balaie / balayons.

examples.text: Je pose cette valise bleue ici cinq minutes pendant que je balaie le placard.
examples.trans: Let me set this blue suitcase here for five minutes while I sweep the closet.

examples.text: C'est facile à balayer ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to sweep together.

meanings.note: Balcony overlooking a street, courtyard, or theater.

examples.text: Nous prenons le café du matin sur le balcon.
examples.trans: We have morning coffee out on the balcony.

examples.text: Des géraniums rouges fleurissent le long du balcon.
examples.trans: Red geraniums bloom along the balcony.

meanings.note: se tirer une balle dans le pied = to shoot oneself in the foot
Balle de tennis.

examples.text: Elle s'est tiré une balle dans le pied.
examples.trans: She shot herself in the foot.

examples.text: Attrape la balle!
examples.trans: Catch the ball!

related.word: se tirer une balle dans le pied
related.gloss: to shoot oneself in the foot

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'banal'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une histoire très banale.
examples.trans: A very ordinary story.

examples.text: Ces actrices sont trop banales.
examples.trans: These actresses are too plain.

examples.text: Elle les trouve beaucoup trop banales.
examples.trans: She finds them much too plain.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la banane', plural 'les bananes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'banana'.

examples.text: J'ai glissé sur une peau de banane.
examples.trans: I slipped on a banana peel.

examples.text: J'ai glissé sur une peau de banane!
examples.trans: I slipped on a banana peel!

examples.text: Une vraie plaie, ces peaux de banane!
examples.trans: A real nuisance, these banana peels!

meanings.note: Park, courtyard, or stone bench.

examples.text: Asseyons-nous un instant sur le banc à l'ombre.
examples.trans: Let's sit for a moment on the bench in the shade.

examples.text: Un vieux banc en pierre fait face à la fontaine.
examples.trans: An old stone bench faces the fountain.

meanings.note: Narrow strip or ribbon of paper, cloth, or paint; group of friends.

examples.text: Une bande de papier entoure le paquet de lettres.
examples.trans: A paper band wraps around the bundle of letters.

examples.text: Il a découpé une fine bande de tissu en lin.
examples.trans: He cut a narrow strip of linen cloth.

meanings.note: En banlieue = in the suburbs.

examples.text: Ce sera dans un hangar en banlieue.
examples.trans: It will be in a warehouse in the suburbs.

examples.text: Elle habite en banlieue.
examples.trans: She lives in the suburbs.

examples.text: Sauf que ce sera dans un hangar en banlieue.
examples.trans: Except it will be in a warehouse in the suburbs.

meanings.note: A financial bank; a feminine noun.

examples.text: Le site de ma banque.
examples.trans: My bank's website.

examples.text: Je vais à la banque.
examples.trans: I'm going to the bank.

examples.text: J'ai passé la nuit sur le site de ma banque.
examples.trans: I spent the night on my bank's website.

meanings.note: Feminine: banquière.

examples.text: Mon banquier n'est pas content.
examples.trans: My bank manager isn't happy.

examples.text: Il est banquier.
examples.trans: He's a banker.

meanings.note: Au bar = at the bar.

examples.text: Va chercher du champagne au bar.
examples.trans: Go and get some champagne at the bar.

examples.text: On prend un verre au bar?
examples.trans: Shall we have a drink at the bar?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le barbare', plural 'les barbares') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'barbarian'.

examples.text: Qui sont les vrais barbares?
examples.trans: Who are the real barbarians?

examples.text: On les traite pourtant de barbares.
examples.trans: Yet they are treated as barbarians.

examples.text: Qui sont les vrais barbares aujourd'hui?
examples.trans: Who are the real barbarians today?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le barbecue', plural 'les barbecues') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'barbecue'.

examples.text: Cuire sur un barbecue.
examples.trans: To cook on a barbecue.

examples.text: Faire un barbecue.
examples.trans: To have a barbecue.

examples.text: Elle fait cuire le morceau sur un barbecue.
examples.trans: She cooks the piece on a barbecue.

meanings.note: servir de baromètre = to serve as a barometer

examples.text: C'est un vrai baromètre.
examples.trans: It is a real barometer.

examples.text: Le baromètre de l'opinion.
examples.trans: The barometer of public opinion.

examples.text: La séance du mercredi matin est un vrai baromètre.
examples.trans: The Wednesday morning screening is a real barometer.

meanings.note: Metal or wooden bar, rod, railing, or pry bar; helm.

examples.text: Il utilise une barre en fer pour soulever la dalle.
examples.trans: He uses an iron pry bar to lift the flagstone.

examples.text: Tenez-vous à la barre dans le bus.
examples.trans: Hold on to the pole on the bus.

barreau.gloss: rung (of a stool or ladder); bar

meanings.en: rung (of a stool, chair, or ladder); bar
meanings.note: Plural in *-x*: *des barreaux* (`/baʁo/`).

examples.text: Posez bien le pied sur le barreau du milieu.
examples.trans: Place your foot firmly on the middle rung.

examples.text: Le barreau en bois de cette vieille chaise est solide.
examples.trans: The wooden rung of this old chair is sturdy.

barrer.gloss: cross out, block; take off, leave

meanings.en: to cross out, bar; to take off, split, leave (se barrer)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to cross out'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'barré').

examples.text: Si on se barrait?
examples.trans: What if we took off?

examples.text: Et si on se barrait?
examples.trans: What if we took off?

meanings.note: Can describe physical height or morally low behaviour.
As an adverb, parler bas means speak quietly.

examples.text: C'est vraiment bas.
examples.trans: That's really low.

examples.text: La table est basse.
examples.trans: The table is low.

examples.text: Attendez. Regardez en bas sur la marche en pierre.
examples.trans: Wait. Look down on the stone step.

meanings.en: to tip over, flip, shift abruptly
meanings.note: Tout a basculé. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to tip over'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'basculé').

examples.text: Tout a basculé en une fraction de seconde!
examples.trans: Everything flipped in a fraction of a second!

examples.text: Le destin de la société a basculé.
examples.trans: The destiny of the company shifted abruptly.

meanings.en: les bases = the basics, the fundamentals
meanings.note: Connaître les bases.

examples.text: Je connais les bases.
examples.trans: I know the basics.

examples.text: C'est la base du métier.
examples.trans: It's the foundation of the job.

examples.text: Oui. Je connais les bases.
examples.trans: Yes. I know the basics.

meanings.note: Ornamental fountain basin or garden pool; river basin.

examples.text: L'eau claire brille au fond du bassin en pierre.
examples.trans: Clear water gleams at the bottom of the stone basin.

examples.text: Les enfants regardent les poissons rouges dans le bassin.
examples.trans: The children watch the goldfish in the garden pool.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la bataille', plural 'les batailles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'battle'.

examples.text: Il faut accepter de perdre des batailles.
examples.trans: One must accept losing battles.

examples.text: Diriger implique de perdre certaines batailles.
examples.trans: Leading implies losing certain battles.

examples.text: Nous verrons qui gagne cette bataille.
examples.trans: We will see who wins this battle.

meanings.note: Plural in -x: les bateaux.

examples.text: Trois mois sur un bateau!
examples.trans: Three months on a boat!

examples.text: On prend le bateau.
examples.trans: We're taking the boat.

meanings.note: Feminine: battante. Masculine noun ('le battant', plural 'les battants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fighter'.

examples.text: C'est un battant.
examples.trans: He is a fighter.

examples.text: Tu es un battant, un gagnant!
examples.trans: You are a fighter, a winner!

meanings.en: se battre = to fight, to brawl
meanings.note: se battre avec quelqu'un = to fight with someone
Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to beat; to fight'.

examples.text: On va se battre.
examples.trans: We are going to fight.

examples.text: Mon cœur bat très vite!
examples.trans: My heart is beating fast!

examples.text: Mon cœur bat très vite! Claire, expliquez-lui, vous avez l'air calme et sincère!
examples.trans: My heart is beating fast! Claire, explain it to him, you sound calm and sincere!

meanings.note: The straps that secure a climber to the rope. Also a shoulder belt in other contexts.

examples.text: Le baudrier fait mal.
examples.trans: The harness hurts.

examples.text: Elle met son baudrier.
examples.trans: She puts on her climbing harness.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas bavarde.
examples.trans: I'm not a chatterbox.

examples.text: Hervé est très bavard.
examples.trans: Hervé is very talkative.

meanings.note: Éviter les bavardages. Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'chatter, gossip'.

examples.text: Nous voulions éviter les bavardages inutiles.
examples.trans: We wanted to avoid unnecessary gossip.

examples.text: Arrêtez vos bavardages en classe.
examples.trans: Stop your chattering in class.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le bazar', plural 'les bazars') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mess'.
Masculine noun ('le bazar', plural 'les bazars') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bazaar'.

examples.text: C'est quoi ce bazar?
examples.trans: What is this mess?

examples.text: Range ta chambre, c'est le bazar!
examples.trans: Tidy up your room, it is a mess!

meanings.note: before the noun; bel before a vowel: un bel endroit

examples.text: C'est un bel endroit.
examples.trans: It's a lovely place.

examples.text: Il fait beau.
examples.trans: The weather is nice.

meanings.note: Le père de son conjoint.
Le mari de sa mère.

examples.text: Le beau-père a des biens à Paris.
examples.trans: The father-in-law owns property in Paris.

examples.text: Son beau-père est très riche.
examples.trans: Her father-in-law is very wealthy.

examples.text: Si! Le beau-père a des biens immobiliers à Paris.
examples.trans: Yes he would! The father-in-law owns real estate in Paris.

meanings.note: beaucoup de + noun, with no article: beaucoup de travail

meanings.en: beaucoup de = a lot of, many

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde.
examples.trans: You know a lot of people.

examples.text: Faites beaucoup de parts du coin, ma chère!
examples.trans: Make plenty of corner pieces, my dear!

meanings.note: pejorative slang; originally short for beau-frère

examples.text: Tu es comme un vieux beauf!
examples.trans: You are like an old redneck!

examples.text: C'est un vrai beauf.
examples.trans: He is a real redneck.

examples.text: Tu es raide, tu es comme un vieux beauf!
examples.trans: You are stiff, you are like an old redneck!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la beauté', plural 'les beautés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'beauty'.

examples.text: Une grande beauté.
examples.trans: A great beauty.

examples.text: La beauté du paysage.
examples.trans: The beauty of the landscape.

examples.text: Il écrit que ma beauté féline le hante.
examples.trans: He writes that my feline beauty haunts him.

meanings.note: Le bec de la carafe = the pitcher spout.

examples.text: Attention, Étienne, le bec de la carafe est large!
examples.trans: Careful, Etienne, the pitcher spout is wide!

examples.text: Voici le bec sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the spout on the table.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le berceau', plural 'les berceaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'crib'.

examples.text: Le berceau du bébé.
examples.trans: The baby's crib.

examples.text: Acheter un berceau.
examples.trans: To buy a crib.

examples.text: Regarde ce grand berceau magnifique!
examples.trans: Look at this magnificent big crib!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to rock'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'bercé').

examples.text: Elle berce l'enfant doucement.
examples.trans: She rocks the child gently.

examples.text: Je peux la bercer doucement.
examples.trans: I can rock her gently.

meanings.note: Avoir besoin de = to need.

examples.text: J'ai besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: I need a little lesson.

examples.text: Tu as besoin d'aide?
examples.trans: Do you need help?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le beurre', plural 'les beurres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'butter'.

examples.text: Un tout petit peu de lait, deux œufs, et plus de beurre du tout!
examples.trans: A tiny splash of milk, two eggs, and no butter at all!

examples.text: Trois bouteilles de lait, vingt œufs, du beurre, du fromage et des pommes rouges!
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

examples.text: Attends une seconde, Claire... tu as pris quelle plaquette de beurre?
examples.trans: Wait a second, Claire... which packet of butter did you grab?

meanings.note: Means both a public library and a bookshelf.

examples.text: Des petites bibliothèques et des cours, surtout. Je mesure comment les vieux murs arrêtent le bruit.
examples.trans: Small libraries and courtyards, mostly. I measure how old walls block noise.

examples.text: Voici la bibliothèque sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the library on the table.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'phony'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Cette histoire est du bidon.
examples.trans: This story is total nonsense.

examples.text: L'histoire du film Bond était du bidon!
examples.trans: The Bond film story was total nonsense!

meanings.note: Très bien = very well, fine.
C'est bien.

examples.text: Très bien.
examples.trans: Very well.

examples.text: Elle est bien.
examples.trans: She's nice.

meanings.note: bien sûr que + sentence = of course...

examples.text: Bien sûr que tu es fatiguée.
examples.trans: Of course you're tired.

examples.text: Bien sûr!
examples.trans: Of course!

examples.text: Bien sûr. Interflora, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Of course. Interflora, please.

meanings.note: À bientôt = see you soon.

examples.text: À bientôt!
examples.trans: See you soon!

examples.text: Il arrive bientôt.
examples.trans: He's arriving soon.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la bienveillance', plural 'les bienveillances') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'benevolence'.

examples.text: Je te remercie de ta bienveillance.
examples.trans: I thank you for your benevolence.

examples.text: Traiter les gens avec bienveillance.
examples.trans: To treat people with kindness.

examples.text: Oui, je te remercie de ta bienveillance.
examples.trans: Yes, I thank you for your benevolence.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'welcome'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Soyez les bienvenus ce soir.
examples.trans: Be welcome tonight.

examples.text: Votre aide est la bienvenue.
examples.trans: Your help is welcome.

examples.text: Bonsoir tout le monde, soyez les bienvenus!
examples.trans: Good evening everyone, be welcome!

meanings.note: la bienvenue = the welcome; also used as greeting

examples.text: Bonjour à tous! Bienvenue, Claire. Tout est prêt?
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Claire. Is everything ready?

examples.text: Bienvenue! Bonjour, madame.
examples.trans: Welcome! Good morning, madam.

examples.text: Bienvenue à l'Hôtel du Tilleul, Claire. Votre deuxième jour ne sera pas ennuyeux.
examples.trans: Welcome to the Hotel du Tilleul, Claire. Your second day will not be boring.

meanings.note: Plural in -x. Masculine noun ('le bijou', plural 'les bijoux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'jewel'.

examples.text: Les bijoux de la star.
examples.trans: The star's jewels.

examples.text: Un bijou magnifique.
examples.trans: A magnificent jewel.

examples.text: J'en déduis que les bijoux Chopard sont arrivés. Bonjour.
examples.trans: I deduce that the Chopard jewelry has arrived. Hello.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le bilan', plural 'les bilans') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'annual review'.

examples.text: Le bilan de fin d'année.
examples.trans: The year-end review.

examples.text: Le bilan de fin d'année approche rapidement.
examples.trans: The year-end review is approaching quickly.

examples.text: Notre agence a déposé le bilan.
examples.trans: Our agency has filed for bankruptcy.

meanings.note: In France, *un billet de train* is a long-distance train ticket (whereas metro/bus tickets are often *un ticket*).

examples.text: J'ai échangé mon billet de train pour partir samedi matin.
examples.trans: I exchanged my train ticket to leave Saturday morning.

examples.text: Gardez votre billet dans la poche de votre manteau.
examples.trans: Keep your ticket in your coat pocket.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Je suis son père biologique.
examples.trans: I am her biological father.

examples.text: Elle achète des fruits biologiques.
examples.trans: She buys organic fruit.

examples.text: Mais je suis le père biologique!
examples.trans: But I am the biological father!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le biopic', plural 'les biopics') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'biographical film'.

examples.text: C'est un biopic historique.
examples.trans: It is a historical biopic.

examples.text: C'est le biopic sur la Comtesse.
examples.trans: It is the biopic on the Countess.

meanings.note: Après le bip sonore. Masculine noun ('le bip', plural 'les bips') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'beep'.

examples.text: Laissez un message après le bip.
examples.trans: Leave a message after the beep.

examples.text: Attendez le bip.
examples.trans: Wait for the beep.

meanings.en: to beep, emit an electronic beeping sound
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to beep'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'bipé').

examples.text: L'appareil bipe.
examples.trans: The device is beeping.

examples.text: Je ne bipe pas pour tout le monde.
examples.trans: I don't beep for everyone.

meanings.note: Final *-t* is silent (`/biskɥi/`); literally 'twice-cooked' (*bis-cuit*).

examples.text: Ces petits biscuits secs accompagnent très bien le thé.
examples.trans: These crisp little cookies go very well with tea.

examples.text: La boîte en fer est pleine de biscuits au beurre.
examples.trans: The tin box is full of butter cookies.

meanings.en: kiss (on the cheek, between family and friends)
meanings.note: At the end of a call or visit.
At the end of a call or visit.

examples.text: Bisous, Maman!
examples.trans: Kisses, Mum!

examples.text: Fais un bisou à ton père.
examples.trans: Give your dad a kiss.

meanings.note: reduplicated form of 'bisou' (little kiss)

examples.text: Merci! Bisou-bisou!
examples.trans: Thank you! Kiss-kiss!

examples.text: Vous dites bisou-bisou à une star?
examples.trans: Do you say kiss-kiss to a star?

examples.text: Allô? Oui, merci! Bisou-bisou!
examples.trans: Hello? Yes, thank you! Kiss-kiss!

meanings.note: Strange or unusual; singular spelling does not change with gender.

examples.text: C'est bizarre.
examples.trans: It's weird.

examples.text: Une idée bizarre.
examples.trans: A strange idea.

examples.text: Nerveux pour un petit train en bois? Cette histoire devient bizarre.
examples.trans: Nervous about a little wooden train? This story is getting strange.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Il me regarde bizarrement.
examples.trans: He looks at me strangely.

examples.text: En plus, son copain me regarde bizarrement.
examples.trans: Plus, her boyfriend looks at me strangely.

examples.text: Une bière fraîche.
examples.trans: A cold beer.

examples.text: Jus d'orange ou bière?
examples.trans: Orange juice or beer?

meanings.note: faire une blague = to tell or play a joke

examples.text: La vie, c'est une grande blague pour toi?
examples.trans: Is life a big joke to you?

examples.text: C'est une blague!
examples.trans: It's a joke!

related.gloss: to tell or play a joke

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le blaireau', plural 'les blaireaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'badger'.
Masculine noun ('le blaireau', plural 'les blaireaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shaving brush'.

examples.text: Le blaireau sort de son terrier pendant la nuit.
examples.trans: The badger comes out of its burrow during the night.

examples.text: Nous avons vu un blaireau dans la forêt.
examples.trans: We saw a badger in the forest.

meanings.note: en noir et blanc = in black and white; feminine: blanche

examples.text: Une chemise blanche.
examples.trans: A white shirt.

examples.text: Elle est trop blanche?
examples.trans: She's too white?

examples.text: Voici une nappe blanche propre et deux tasses bleues.
examples.trans: Here is a clean white tablecloth and two blue cups.

related.gloss: in black and white; feminine: blanche

meanings.note: se blesser = to get hurt / to injure oneself
Figurative.

examples.text: Andréa? Tu es blessée?
examples.trans: Andréa? Are you hurt?

examples.text: Il s'est blessé.
examples.trans: He got hurt.

examples.text: Arrête, Hervé! Je ne voulais pas te blesser.
examples.trans: Stop, Herve! I did not want to hurt you.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la blessure', plural 'les blessures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'wound'.

examples.text: C'est une blessure qui ne guérira jamais.
examples.trans: It is a wound that will never heal.

examples.text: Soigner une blessure.
examples.trans: To treat a wound.

examples.text: Cette blessure est douloureuse.
examples.trans: This injury is painful.

meanings.note: Un homme blessé. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'injured'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Elle sait que je suis un homme blessé.
examples.trans: She knows that I am a wounded man.

examples.text: Il n'est pas blessé.
examples.trans: He is not hurt.

examples.text: C'est l'histoire d'un brave soldat blessé.
examples.trans: It is the story of a brave wounded soldier.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'blue'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Elle porte une belle robe bleue pour la soirée.
examples.trans: She is wearing a beautiful blue dress for the evening.

examples.text: Je voudrais un steak cuit bleu, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: I would like a steak cooked very rare, please.

meanings.note: Tempered to a deep blue sheen ('acier bleui' = blued steel); tinged with blue.

examples.text: L'aiguille en acier bleui pivote doucement vers le nord.
examples.trans: The blued-steel needle pivots gently northward.

examples.text: Le soir, les collines lointaines semblent bleuies par la brume.
examples.trans: In the evening, the distant hills look tinged blue with mist.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'bluish'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une lueur bleutée.
examples.trans: A bluish glow.

examples.text: Une peau rose bleutée.
examples.trans: Bluish-pink skin.

examples.text: La peau devient plutôt rose bleutée.
examples.trans: The skin turns rather bluish pink.

meanings.note: Solid block of stone or wood; notepad ('bloc-notes').

examples.text: La fontaine est taillée dans un seul bloc de calcaire.
examples.trans: The fountain is carved from a single block of limestone.

examples.text: Elle garde toujours un petit bloc de papier dans son sac.
examples.trans: She always keeps a small pad of paper in her bag.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le blocage', plural 'les blocages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'deadlock'.

examples.text: Ce blocage me rend fou!
examples.trans: This stalemate is driving me crazy!

examples.text: Ce blocage me rend complètement fou!
examples.trans: This stalemate makes me completely crazy!

examples.text: Elle est blonde, elle est normale!
examples.trans: She's blonde, she's normal!

examples.text: Il a les cheveux blonds.
examples.trans: He has blond hair.

meanings.en: to block, stop, keep out; to jam
meanings.note: Spelling keeps -qu- before all endings (/blɔk/).

examples.text: Les volets en bois bloquent le vent froid de l'hiver.
examples.trans: The wooden shutters block out the cold winter wind.

examples.text: Toutes ces chaises empilées bloquent le passage vers la cour.
examples.trans: All these stacked chairs are blocking the way to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Informal, from English.

examples.text: Vous bluffez!
examples.trans: You're bluffing!

examples.text: Il ne bluffe pas.
examples.trans: He isn't bluffing.

examples.text: Ne bois pas trop!
examples.trans: Don't drink too much!

examples.text: Vous voulez boire quelque chose?
examples.trans: Would you like something to drink?

examples.text: Les animaux sont dans les bois.
examples.trans: The animals are in the woods.

examples.text: La table est en bois.
examples.trans: The table is made of wood.

meanings.note: Used for soup or morning hot chocolate/coffee.

examples.text: Voici une serviette sèche pour votre manteau et un bol de soupe chaude, monsieur.
examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat and a bowl of hot soup, sir.

examples.text: Vous l'avez laissé près du bol de soupe sur le comptoir.
examples.trans: You left it near the soup bowl on the counter.

meanings.note: une bombe à retardement = a time bomb

meanings.en: c'est une bombe! = it's dynamite! / it's a sensation!
meanings.note: Informal.

examples.text: Je te jure, c'est une bombe!
examples.trans: I swear, it's dynamite!

examples.text: Ce scénario est une bombe.
examples.trans: This script is dynamite.

meanings.note: as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day

examples.text: Bon. Alors, je vais attendre.
examples.trans: Fine. Then I'll wait.

examples.text: Ah bon? Il y a un problème avec ma réservation?
examples.trans: Oh really? Is there a problem with my booking?

meanings.note: Usually plural: les bonbons.

examples.text: Les enfants adorent les bonbons.
examples.trans: Children love sweets.

examples.text: Tu veux un bonbon?
examples.trans: Do you want a sweet?

examples.text: Avez-vous un problème avec l'alcool, le Coca-Cola, les bonbons?
examples.trans: Do you have a problem with alcohol, Coca-Cola, sweets?

meanings.note: Masculine. Que du bonheur is the actual French series title in this scene; Happy Ever After is the English working-subtitle localization.

examples.text: Quel bonheur de te voir!
examples.trans: What a joy to see you!

examples.text: Je te souhaite beaucoup de bonheur.
examples.trans: I wish you much happiness.

meanings.note: the standard greeting until evening

examples.text: Bonjour! Excusez-moi, la porte est fermée à clé?
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: Bonjour. Non, soulevez d'abord la poignée, puis poussez.
examples.trans: Good morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.

examples.text: Alors la maison dit bonjour toute seule?
examples.trans: So the house says hello on its own?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le bonsaï', plural 'les bonsaïs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bonsai tree'.

examples.text: J'ai mis le bonsaï sur ton bureau.
examples.trans: I put the bonsai on your desk.

examples.text: Prendre soin d'un bonsaï.
examples.trans: To take care of a bonsai.

examples.text: Hervé, j'ai mis le bonsaï sur ton bureau.
examples.trans: Herve, I put the bonsai on your desk.

meanings.note: Evening greeting.

meanings.en: good night (when leaving in the evening)
meanings.note: Can also be used when leaving someone in the evening.

examples.text: Allô? Bonsoir! Il n'y a personne au portail!
examples.trans: Hello? Good evening! Nobody is standing at the gate!

examples.text: Bonsoir! Entrez vite à l'abri de la pluie, monsieur.
examples.trans: Good evening! Come quickly inside out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: Bonsoir. Pardon pour l'eau sur votre sol propre.
examples.trans: Good evening. Sorry for the water on your clean floor.

meanings.note: Kindness, goodness of heart; 'bonté divine!' = goodness gracious!

examples.text: Je n'oublierai jamais la bonté de nos voisins.
examples.trans: I will never forget our neighbors' kindness.

examples.text: Bonté divine, comme le jardin a grandi!
examples.trans: Goodness gracious, how the garden has grown!

bord.gloss: board, side; maître à bord = in charge

meanings.en: board, edge, shipboard; maître à bord = master on board
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le bord', plural 'les bords') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'board'.

examples.text: Vous serez maître à bord ici.
examples.trans: You will be in charge here.

examples.text: Ne bougez plus, tous les deux. Vous entendez ce moteur s'arrêter au bord du trottoir?
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Do you hear that engine stopping at the kerb?

meanings.note: Border un lit / un drap = to tuck in a sheet.

examples.text: Borde bien le coin du drap, Claire! Et voilà les deux oreillers doux.
examples.trans: Tuck the sheet corner tight, Claire! Here go the two soft pillows.

examples.text: C'est facile à border ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to tuck in together.

meanings.note: Decorative border on a card or page; garden edging or curb.

examples.text: Une fine bordure dorée entoure le menu.
examples.trans: A delicate gold border frames the menu.

examples.text: De la lavande pousse en bordure de l'allée.
examples.trans: Lavender grows along the edge of the path.

meanings.note: idiom: to cross the line, go too far

examples.text: Tu dépasses les bornes!
examples.trans: You're crossing the line!

examples.text: Pardon? Tu dépasses les bornes!
examples.trans: Excuse me? You're crossing the line!

examples.text: J'ai vraiment dépassé les bornes.
examples.trans: I really crossed the line.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to work hard'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'bossé').

examples.text: On a bossé comme des fous.
examples.trans: We worked like crazy.

examples.text: Je dois bosser ce soir.
examples.trans: I have to work tonight.

examples.text: Oui, on a bossé comme des fous, tu vois.
examples.trans: Yes, we worked like crazy, you see.

meanings.note: brand name, usually written with a capital: le Botox

examples.text: Un peu de Botox?
examples.trans: A bit of Botox?

examples.text: Elle ne veut pas de Botox.
examples.trans: She doesn't want any Botox.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la botte', plural 'les bottes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'boot'.

examples.text: C'est une fausse botte.
examples.trans: It is a fake boot.

examples.text: C'est parfait, enfilons cette fausse botte!
examples.trans: It is perfect, let us slip on this fake boot!

meanings.note: Mouth; 'motus et bouche cousue' = mum's the word, my lips are sealed.

examples.text: Ce gâteau fond littéralement dans la bouche.
examples.trans: This cake literally melts in your mouth.

examples.text: C'est une surprise: motus et bouche cousue!
examples.trans: It's a surprise: mum's the word, lips sealed!

meanings.note: Invariable in plural. Masculine noun ('le bouche-à-bouche', plural 'les bouche-à-bouche') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mouth-to-mouth resuscitation'.

examples.text: Faire du bouche-à-bouche.
examples.trans: To do mouth-to-mouth.

examples.text: Essayez le bouche-à-bouche!
examples.trans: Try mouth-to-mouth!

meanings.en: to block, to clog; se boucher = become blocked
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to clog'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'bouché').

examples.text: Un vaisseau sanguin s'est bouché.
examples.trans: A blood vessel got blocked.

examples.text: Un petit vaisseau sanguin s'est bouché.
examples.trans: A small blood vessel got blocked.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la boucherie', plural 'les boucheries') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'meat shop'.

examples.text: Une boucherie du quartier.
examples.trans: A butcher shop in the neighborhood.

examples.text: Draguer son patron dans une boucherie?
examples.trans: Hitting on her boss in a butcher shop?

meanings.note: Built from bouche ('mouth').

examples.text: Une bouchée... {M3}, ferme les yeux! Ça a exactement le même goût que le gâteau de grand-père!
examples.trans: One bite... {M3}, close your eyes! That tastes exactly like Grandfather's cake!

examples.text: Voici la bouchée sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the bite, mouthful on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for sulking quietly.

examples.text: Bien sûr! Chaque vendredi, quand il ratait une note au piano, il boudait devant le mur.
examples.trans: Of course! Every Friday, when he missed a piano note, he sulked at the wall.

examples.text: C'est facile à bouder ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to sulk, pout together.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to move'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'bougé').

examples.text: Le bébé bouge beaucoup.
examples.trans: The baby is moving a lot.

examples.text: Ne bougez plus, tous les deux.
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you.

examples.text: Stop, plus personne ne bouge! Quelle heure est-il? Neuf heures trente-cinq!
examples.trans: Hold everything, nobody move! What time is it? Nine thirty-five!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la bougie', plural 'les bougies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'wax candle'.

examples.text: Allumer une bougie tous les soirs.
examples.trans: To light a candle every evening.

examples.text: J'allume ta belle bougie tous les soirs.
examples.trans: I light your lovely candle every evening.

meanings.note: Faire bouillir de l'eau = boil water; laisser bouillir = let boil.

examples.text: L'eau bout déjà dans la grande bouilloire.
examples.trans: The water is already boiling in the big kettle.

examples.text: Ne laissez jamais bouillir la crème au citron.
examples.trans: Never let the lemon curd boil.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la bouilloire', plural 'les bouilloires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'kettle'.

examples.text: La bouilloire électrique.
examples.trans: The electric kettle.

examples.text: J'ouvre le couvercle de la bouilloire.
examples.trans: I open the lid of the kettle.

meanings.note: Un bouillon de légumes chaud = hot vegetable broth.

examples.text: Versez le bouillon chaud sur les carottes et les lentilles.
examples.trans: Pour the hot broth over the carrots and lentils.

examples.text: Ce bouillon parfumé réchauffe toute la maison.
examples.trans: This fragrant broth warms the whole house.

meanings.note: Masculine boulanger /bulɑ̃ʒe/ drops the final -r sound; feminine boulangère /bulɑ̃ʒɛʁ/ pronounces the -r and opens the vowel.

examples.text: La boulangère ouvre sa boutique à six heures du matin.
examples.trans: The baker opens her shop at six in the morning.

examples.text: Notre boulanger prépare d'excellentes tartes aux pommes.
examples.trans: Our baker makes excellent apple tarts.

meanings.note: From boulanger ('baker').

examples.text: La boulangerie du coin ouvre dès l'aube.
examples.trans: The corner bakery opens at dawn.

examples.text: On sent le pain chaud devant la boulangerie.
examples.trans: You can smell warm bread outside the bakery.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la boule', plural 'les boules') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ball'.

examples.text: Une boule de neige.
examples.trans: A snowball.

examples.text: Se mettre en boule.
examples.trans: To curl up into a ball.

examples.text: J'étais comme un hérisson en boule!
examples.trans: I was like a curled-up hedgehog!

meanings.note: Birch tree or its pale, smooth wood ('bois de bouleau').

examples.text: Ces pinces à linge sont taillées dans du bois de bouleau bien lisse.
examples.trans: These clothespins are carved from smooth birchwood.

examples.text: L'écorce blanche du bouleau brille au soleil d'automne.
examples.trans: The white bark of the birch tree gleams in the autumn sun.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to deeply shake'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'bouleversé').

examples.text: Le film m'a complètement bouleversé.
examples.trans: The film completely shook me.

examples.text: Cette annonce a bouleversé toute l'agence.
examples.trans: This announcement shook the whole agency.

examples.text: Votre émotion a bouleversé la salle!
examples.trans: Your emotion moved the entire room!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'deeply shaken'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ma sœur est bouleversée.
examples.trans: My sister is distraught.

examples.text: Ma sœur est complètement bouleversée.
examples.trans: My sister is completely overwhelmed.

examples.text: Pourtant, je me sens complètement bouleversé.
examples.trans: Yet, I feel completely overwhelmed.

meanings.note: Informal word for travail.

examples.text: Je cherche du boulot.
examples.trans: I'm looking for work.

examples.text: Tu avais un bon boulot.
examples.trans: You had a good job.

meanings.note: un bouquet de fleurs = a bouquet of flowers

examples.text: Je vais recevoir un autre bouquet?
examples.trans: Will I receive another bouquet?

examples.text: Un beau bouquet de fleurs.
examples.trans: A lovely bouquet of flowers.

meanings.note: faire une bourde = to make a blunder

examples.text: C'est la pire bourde de ma carrière.
examples.trans: It is the worst blunder of my career.

examples.text: Une grosse bourde.
examples.trans: A big blunder.

meanings.note: Magnetic pocket compass; figurative guiding compass ('perdre la boussole' = lose one's bearings).

examples.text: Il pose la boussole en laiton bien à plat sur la carte.
examples.trans: He sets the brass compass flat on the map.

examples.text: Avec une bonne boussole, impossible de se perdre en forêt.
examples.trans: With a good compass, it's impossible to get lost in the woods.

meanings.note: à bout = at the end of one's tether, exhausted

examples.text: Je suis complètement à bout.
examples.trans: I am completely exhausted.

examples.text: Au bout de la rue.
examples.trans: At the end of the street.

examples.text: Écoutez... le clocher au bout de la rue commence à sonner les douze coups de midi!
examples.trans: Listen... the church bell tower down the street is starting to strike the twelve chimes of noon!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la bouteille', plural 'les bouteilles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bottle'.

examples.text: Regarde cette bouteille de champagne!
examples.trans: Look at this bottle of champagne!

examples.text: Une bouteille d'eau fraîche.
examples.trans: A bottle of fresh water.

examples.text: Trois bouteilles de lait, vingt œufs, du beurre, du fromage et des pommes rouges!
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

meanings.note: nickname for the press room full of free gifts
nickname for the press room full of free gifts

examples.text: La boutique est fermée.
examples.trans: The shop is closed.

examples.text: La boutique a une grande enseigne dehors?
examples.trans: Does the shop have a big sign outside?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le bouton', plural 'les boutons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'button'.

examples.text: Et j'allume le bouton.
examples.trans: And I turn on the switch.

examples.text: Appuie sur le bouton pour descendre.
examples.trans: Press the button to go down.

meanings.note: To fasten a shirt, jacket, or coat with buttons.
Past participle boutonné(e) is often used as an adjective ('veste boutonnée' = buttoned jacket).

examples.text: Vérification rapide avant trois heures: veste boutonnée, chaussures propres... où sont mes lunettes?!
examples.trans: Quick check before three strikes: jacket buttoned, clean shoes... where are my glasses?!

examples.text: Il boutonne son manteau avant de sortir dans la cour fraîche.
examples.trans: He buttons up his coat before stepping out into the cool courtyard.

meanings.note: c'est une belle boîte = it's a great company

examples.text: C'est une belle boîte.
examples.trans: It's a great company.

examples.text: La vérité, c'est que mon agence... C'est une belle boîte. Un joyau, envié de tous.
examples.trans: The truth is that my agency... It's a great company. A jewel, envied by all.

examples.text: Je n'ai jamais vu cette boîte en quinze ans!
examples.trans: I have never seen that box in fifteen years!

meanings.note: Built from boîte ('box') + -ier; used for fuse boxes, switch casings, watch cases, and camera bodies.

examples.text: Henri referme le boîtier électrique dans le couloir.
examples.trans: Henri closes the electrical box in the corridor back up.

examples.text: Tous les fils neufs sont bien rangés dans le boîtier.
examples.trans: All the new wires are neatly arranged inside the casing.

meanings.en: branch (of a tree or climbing plant)
meanings.note: Feminine noun (*une branche verte*).

examples.text: Une longue branche de lierre court sur le mur en pierre.
examples.trans: A long branch of ivy runs along the stone wall.

examples.text: Le vent fait bouger les branches du tilleul.
examples.trans: The wind stirs the branches of the linden tree.

related.gloss: stem, stalk (of a plant); thin rod

meanings.note: Opposite: débrancher.

examples.text: Branche la lampe en laiton d'Henri... oh, regarde cette belle lumière jaune!
examples.trans: Plug in Henri's brass lamp... oh, look at that lovely yellow light!

examples.text: C'est facile à brancher ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to plug in, connect together.

meanings.note: An armed robbery or hold-up; not the English sense of an ordinary delay.

examples.text: Ils font des braquages.
examples.trans: They do hold-ups.

examples.text: Un braquage de banque.
examples.trans: A bank robbery.

examples.text: C'est l'histoire d'un vieux couple qui fait des braquages.
examples.trans: It's the story of an old couple who do hold-ups.

meanings.note: Le bras droit = the right arm.
être le bras droit de quelqu'un = to be someone's right hand

examples.text: Je deviendrai son bras droit.
examples.trans: I will become his right hand.

examples.text: Il lève le bras.
examples.trans: He raises his arm.

examples.text: Ne baissez pas les bras!
examples.trans: Do not give up!

examples.text: Brave garçon!
examples.trans: Good boy!

examples.text: C'est une brave personne.
examples.trans: She is a kind person.

meanings.note: Invariable exclamation of praise—or gentle teasing when someone makes a comical blunder (Bravo, patron!).

examples.text: Bravo, Henri! La vieille lampe fonctionne comme au premier jour.
examples.trans: Well done, Henri! The old lamp works like day one.

examples.text: Toute la salle a dit bravo après la dernière note du piano.
examples.trans: The whole room said bravo after the final note on the piano.

examples.text: C'était bref.
examples.trans: It was short.

examples.text: Une réunion brève.
examples.trans: A short meeting.

meanings.note: Everyday French word for home repairs.

examples.text: Écoutez Monsieur Bricolage! Hier tu réparais la chaudière, aujourd'hui tu répares deux frères!
examples.trans: Listen to Mr Handyman! Yesterday you fixed the boiler, today you fix two brothers!

examples.text: Voici le bricolage sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the DIY, handyman repairs on the table.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le brief', plural 'les briefs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'brief'.

examples.text: Pascal attend notre brief tout de suite.
examples.trans: Pascal expects our briefing right away.

examples.text: Préparer un brief complet.
examples.trans: To prepare a complete brief.

examples.text: D'accord pour un brief rapide de dix minutes.
examples.trans: Agreed for a quick ten-minute briefing.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to brief'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'briefé').

examples.text: Je dois briefer Pascal d'abord.
examples.trans: I must brief Pascal first.

examples.text: Briefer l'équipe avant le tournage.
examples.trans: To brief the team before filming.

examples.text: Mais laisse-moi te briefer avant de partir.
examples.trans: But let me brief you before leaving.

meanings.en: kitchen staff, kitchen brigade (in a restaurant)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la brigade', plural 'les brigades') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'kitchen staff'.
Feminine noun ('la brigade', plural 'les brigades') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'brigade'.

examples.text: Tu dois juste crier sur ta brigade.
examples.trans: You must just shout at your brigade.

examples.text: Le chef dirige toute la brigade en cuisine.
examples.trans: The chef leads the entire brigade in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Masculine /bʁijɑ̃/ has a silent -t; feminine brillante (/bʁijɑ̃t/) pronounces the -t.

examples.text: Sous le drap, le bois du piano est encore lisse et brillant.
examples.trans: Under the dust sheet, the wood of the piano is still smooth and shiny.

examples.text: Claire a eu une idée brillante pour ranger les chaises.
