examples.trans: Claire had a brilliant idea for storing the chairs.

meanings.note: Double -ll- after i is pronounced /j/ (/bʁije/, il brille /bʁij/).

examples.text: Le parquet ciré brille sous le soleil du matin.
examples.trans: The waxed floor gleams in the morning sunlight.

examples.text: Après le nettoyage, toutes les vitres brillent.
examples.trans: After the cleaning, all the windowpanes sparkle.

meanings.note: Un brin de thym / de persil = a sprig of thyme / parsley.

examples.text: Ajoutez deux brins de thym frais dans la marmite.
examples.trans: Add two sprigs of fresh thyme to the pot.

examples.text: Elle attache les brins de persil avec une ficelle.
examples.trans: She ties the sprigs of parsley with kitchen twine.

meanings.note: Classic French breakfast pastry.

examples.text: Bonjour, Madame Odette! Mes brioches à la cannelle sortent tout juste du four.
examples.trans: Good morning, Madam Odette! My cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Prenez d'abord une tasse de thé chaud et une brioche pendant dix minutes!
examples.trans: Have a hot cup of tea and a roll for ten minutes first!

examples.text: Ma foi, personne ne refuse une brioche chaude à la cannelle à sept heures du matin.
examples.trans: Well now, nobody turns down a warm cinnamon roll at seven in the morning.

meanings.note: En brique = made of brick.

examples.text: Les chambres resteront chaudes jusqu'au matin, Claire, grâce aux murs en brique.
examples.trans: The rooms will stay warm until morning, Claire, thanks to the brick walls.

examples.text: Dans les vieux immeubles en brique, l'eau met souvent longtemps à monter tout en haut.
examples.trans: In old brick buildings, water often takes a long time to reach the very top.

examples.text: Parce qu'une maison, c'est de la brique et du bois, Thibault, mais la famille, on la garde.
examples.trans: Because a house is brick and wood, Thibault, while family is what we keep.

meanings.note: Une brise douce = a gentle breeze.

examples.text: Une brise fraîche entre par les fenêtres ouvertes.
examples.trans: A cool breeze comes in through the open windows.

examples.text: La brise du soir fait bouger les feuilles du tilleul.
examples.trans: The evening breeze stirs the leaves of the linden tree.

meanings.en: briser le cœur à quelqu'un = to break someone's heart

examples.text: Ça va lui briser le cœur.
examples.trans: It's going to break her heart.

examples.text: Le verre s'est brisé.
examples.trans: The glass shattered.

meanings.note: Smooth heavy card stock; note card, recipe card, or calling card ('fiche bristol').

examples.text: Elle recopie ses meilleures recettes sur des fiches en bristol.
examples.trans: She copies her best recipes onto heavy index cards.

examples.text: Un bristol écrit à la main était glissé dans l'enveloppe.
examples.trans: A handwritten note card was tucked inside the envelope.

meanings.note: prendre du bromazépam = to take bromazepam

examples.text: Le bromazépam est son ami.
examples.trans: Bromazepam is her friend.

examples.text: Un comprimé de bromazépam.
examples.trans: A tablet of bromazepam.

examples.text: Le bromazépam est devenu son meilleur ami.
examples.trans: Bromazepam has become her best friend.

meanings.note: Bronze alloy or bronze sculpture/plaque.

examples.text: Une plaque en bronze indique l'année de construction du pont.
examples.trans: A bronze plaque marks the year the bridge was built.

examples.text: La cloche en bronze résonne dans toute la vallée.
examples.trans: The bronze bell rings out across the whole valley.

brouiller.gloss: to mix up, fall out (se brouiller)

meanings.note: se brouiller avec qqn = to fall out with someone

meanings.en: to fall out, quarrel (se brouiller avec)
meanings.note: se brouiller avec qqn = to fall out with someone

examples.text: Attendez: le beurre salé est mauvais pour la confiture, mais génial pour les œufs brouillés!
examples.trans: Wait: salted butter is bad for jam, but amazing for scrambled eggs!

examples.text: Claire a acheté du beurre salé, alors ce matin on fait de bons œufs brouillés!
examples.trans: Claire bought salted butter, so this morning we are making good scrambled eggs!

examples.text: Les œufs brouillés sont délicieux, {F1}. Fais mes compliments à {F2}!
examples.trans: The scrambled eggs are delicious, {F1}. Tell {F2} my compliments!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le brouillon', plural 'les brouillons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'draft'.

examples.text: C'est un premier brouillon.
examples.trans: It is a first draft.

examples.text: Écrire un brouillon.
examples.trans: To write a draft.

examples.text: Non, pas du tout, c'était juste un premier brouillon.
examples.trans: No, not at all, it was just a first draft.

meanings.note: Faire du bruit = to make noise.

examples.text: Avec tout ce bruit.
examples.trans: With all this noise.

examples.text: Il y a beaucoup de bruit.
examples.trans: There's a lot of noise.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la brume', plural 'les brumes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mist'.

examples.text: La brume recouvre le plateau.
examples.trans: The mist covers the set.

examples.text: Regarde cette silhouette dans la brume.
examples.trans: Look at this silhouette in the mist.

meanings.note: *Du papier brun* refers to heavy brown kraft paper used to protect floors when painting or wrapping parcels.

examples.text: Étalez du papier brun sur le sol avant d'ouvrir le pot de peinture.
examples.trans: Spread brown paper on the floor before opening the paint tin.

examples.text: Il porte un carnet à couverture brune sous le bras.
examples.trans: He carries a brown-covered notebook under his arm.

meanings.note: Un talent brut = raw talent. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'raw'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est un talent brut.
examples.trans: It is raw talent.

examples.text: Du pétrole brut.
examples.trans: Crude oil.

examples.text: C'est un talent brut magnifique.
examples.trans: She is a magnificent raw talent.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'harsh'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est un milieu brutal.
examples.trans: It is a brutal environment.

examples.text: C'est un milieu artistique trop brutal.
examples.trans: It is too brutal an artistic milieu.

examples.text: Pourquoi prend-il une telle décision brutale?
examples.trans: Why does he make such a brutal decision?

meanings.note: Feminine: bruyante.

examples.text: Exactement. Sur l'avenue dehors, c'est bruyant, mais dans cette cour on entend les feuilles et les oiseaux.
examples.trans: Exactly. Out on the avenue it is noisy, yet in this courtyard you hear leaves and birds.

examples.text: Le grand frère était vif et bruyant, toujours pressé de finir ses gammes.
examples.trans: The older brother was lively and loud, always in a hurry to finish his scales.

meanings.note: Piping hot, glowing hot, or scorching (of an oven, grill, or teacup).

examples.text: Attention aux doigts: le moule sort tout juste du four brûlant!
examples.trans: Watch your fingers: the baking tin just came out of the scorching-hot oven!

examples.text: Le sucre caramélise en une minute sous le gril brûlant.
examples.trans: The sugar caramelizes in one minute under the blazing grill.

examples.text: Attention, tu vas te brûler.
examples.trans: Be careful, you are going to burn yourself.

examples.text: Le film a brûlé la pellicule.
examples.trans: The film burned the reel.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le budget', plural 'les budgets') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'budget'.

examples.text: Le budget du film.
examples.trans: The movie budget.

examples.text: Gérer un budget.
examples.trans: To manage a budget.

examples.text: Gillières peut bloquer le budget de ton film.
examples.trans: Gillières can block the budget of your movie.

examples.text: Il la pousse dans les buissons.
examples.trans: He pushes her into the bushes.

examples.text: Un petit buisson.
examples.trans: A small bush.

meanings.note: Une bulle d'air = an air bubble.

examples.text: Oh! Parfois les vieux tuyaux ont une petite bulle d'air la nuit.
examples.trans: Oh! Sometimes old pipes have a little air bubble at night.

examples.text: Dites-moi que c'était juste une petite bulle d'air, Henri! Je vous en prie!
examples.trans: Tell me it was just a tiny air bubble, Henri! Please!

examples.text: À droite, près du bureau, là où la lumière est bonne.
examples.trans: On the right, near the desk, where the light is good.

examples.text: Le vieux bureau clair sous les toits... suivez-moi, vite!
examples.trans: The old bright attic study... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: City or intercity bus ('prendre le bus' = take the bus).

examples.text: Le bus numéro quatre s'arrête juste devant le square.
examples.trans: The number four bus stops right outside the park square.

examples.text: Nous avons pris le premier bus du matin pour venir.
examples.trans: We took the first morning bus to get here.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la buse', plural 'les buses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'buzzard'.

examples.text: Regarde là-haut, c'est une buse.
examples.trans: Look up there, that is a buzzard.

examples.text: Une buse tourne dans le ciel.
examples.trans: A buzzard circles in the sky.

meanings.note: Informal, from English.

examples.text: C'est le business.
examples.trans: That's business.

examples.text: Le cinéma est un business.
examples.trans: Cinema is a business.

meanings.en: goal, aim, purpose (près du but = close to the goal)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le but', plural 'les buts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'goal'.

examples.text: Si près du but.
examples.trans: So close to the goal.

examples.text: C'est dur si près du but.
examples.trans: It is hard so close to the goal.

meanings.note: faire le buzz = to create a buzz, to go viral

examples.text: Ça va faire le buzz.
examples.trans: It will create a buzz.

examples.text: Un buzz sur les réseaux sociaux.
examples.trans: A buzz on social media.

examples.text: Au contraire, ça va faire le buzz! C'est pimenté!
examples.trans: On the contrary, it will create buzz! It is spicy!

related.gloss: to create a buzz, to go viral

meanings.en: fogging, mist, condensation (on glass or spectacles)
meanings.note: Avoir de la buée sur ses lunettes = have misted-up glasses.

examples.text: La vapeur du thé met de la buée sur mes lunettes.
examples.trans: The steam from the tea fogs up my glasses.

examples.text: Essuie la buée sur la vitre pour voir la cour.
examples.trans: Wipe the condensation off the windowpane to see the courtyard.

meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire') meaning 'to build'; essential in everyday spoken and professional French.

meanings.en: bâtir des compromis: to forge compromises
meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire') meaning 'batir des compromis: to forge compromises'; essential in everyday spoken and professional French.

examples.text: Mathias sait bâtir des compromis.
examples.trans: Mathias knows how to forge compromises.

examples.text: Bâtir une agence solide.
examples.trans: To build a solid agency.

examples.text: Moi, j'ai bâti ma fortune rapidement.
examples.trans: I built my fortune quickly.

meanings.note: une famille de bâtisseurs = a family of builders

examples.text: Je viens d'une famille de bâtisseurs!
examples.trans: I come from a family of builders!

examples.text: Un grand bâtisseur de cathédrales.
examples.trans: A great builder of cathedrals.

examples.text: Le castor! Oui, Mathias, je viens d'une famille de bâtisseurs!
examples.trans: The beaver! Yes, Mathias, I come from a family of builders!

meanings.note: Always masculine, even for a girl.

examples.text: Le bébé dort.
examples.trans: The baby is sleeping.

examples.text: Elle a une tête de bébé.
examples.trans: She has a baby face.

meanings.note: Money remaining after costs, often plural in company accounts.
A benefit or advantage gained from something.

examples.text: L'agence fait des bénéfices.
examples.trans: The agency makes a profit.

examples.text: Les bénéfices sont bons.
examples.trans: The profits are good.

examples.text: Vous touchez simplement les bénéfices.
examples.trans: You simply collect the profits.

meanings.note: Silly or foolish; can be affectionate in a friendly exchange.

meanings.en: une bête = an animal, a beast (noun)
meanings.note: As a feminine noun, une bête is an animal.

examples.text: Oh, Gabriel! Tu es bête!
examples.trans: Oh, Gabriel! You're silly!

examples.text: C'est bête.
examples.trans: That's a shame / That's silly.

examples.text: Ce sont juste des bêtes de foire.
examples.trans: They are just fairground animals.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: J'ai bêtement oublié mes clés sur la table.
examples.trans: I foolishly forgot my keys on the table.

examples.text: Il a répondu bêtement sans réfléchir.
examples.trans: He answered foolishly without thinking.

meanings.note: dire des bêtises = to talk nonsense / say rude things
Faire une bêtise.

examples.text: Mais c'est quoi ces bêtises?
examples.trans: Hey, what is this nonsense?

examples.text: Arrête de dire des bêtises.
examples.trans: Stop talking nonsense.

examples.text: Dis bonjour à Mathias. Mais c'est quoi ces bêtises?
examples.trans: Say hello to Mathias. Hey, what is this nonsense?

related.gloss: to talk nonsense / say rude things

meanings.note: Introduces a clarification or restatement.
Used on its own as a question.

examples.text: C'est-à-dire?
examples.trans: Meaning?

examples.text: Demain, c'est-à-dire lundi.
examples.trans: Tomorrow, that is to say Monday.

meanings.note: Used for legal, medical, or property offices.

examples.text: Du cabinet du propriétaire de l'immeuble? Étrange, notre loyer est payé jusqu'à l'été prochain.
examples.trans: From the building landlord's office? Strange, our rent is paid until next summer.

examples.text: Voici le cabinet sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the office, practice, firm on the table.

meanings.note: cacher quelque chose à quelqu'un = hide something from someone

examples.text: Il cache un secret.
examples.trans: He's hiding a secret.

examples.text: Ne cache pas la vérité.
examples.trans: Don't hide the truth.

meanings.note: Here the payment for an actor’s work on a production.

examples.text: Il faut payer deux cachets.
examples.trans: We have to pay two performers’ fees.

examples.text: Son cachet est élevé.
examples.trans: Her fee is high.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cachette', plural 'les cachettes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hiding place'.

examples.text: Il a négocié cet accord en cachette.
examples.trans: He negotiated this agreement secretly.

examples.text: Les enfants ont trouvé une bonne cachette.
examples.trans: The children found a good hiding place.

examples.text: Mathias a négocié ce départ en cachette?
examples.trans: Did Mathias negotiate this departure in secret?

meanings.en: corpse, dead body; skeleton in closet
meanings.note: un cadavre dans le placard = a skeleton in the closet

examples.text: Un cadavre dans le placard.
examples.trans: A skeleton in the closet.

examples.text: Découvrir un cadavre.
examples.trans: To discover a corpse.

examples.text: On a tous un cadavre dans le placard!
examples.trans: We all have a skeleton in the closet!

meanings.note: la pâleur cadavérique = deathly paleness

examples.text: Une pâleur cadavérique.
examples.trans: A cadaverous pallor.

examples.text: La lividité cadavérique.
examples.trans: Post-mortem lividity.

examples.text: La lividité cadavérique n'est pas blanche.
examples.trans: Post-mortem lividity is not white.

meanings.note: En cadeau = as a gift; plural in -x: des cadeaux.

examples.text: Elle apporte deux brioches chaudes en cadeau.
examples.trans: She brings two warm brioches as a gift.

examples.text: Ce vieux livre est un cadeau de ma tante.
examples.trans: This old book is a gift from my aunt.

related.gloss: to give (as a present), to offer

meanings.note: le cadre légal = the legal framework

examples.text: Le nouveau cadre des salaires.
examples.trans: The new salary framework.

examples.text: Dans ce cadre particulier.
examples.trans: In this particular framework.

examples.text: Sans compter le nouveau cadre sur les salaires, nos bénéfices sont en baisse.
examples.trans: Not to mention the new rules on salaries, our profits are down.

meanings.note: Un café = an espresso.
The place.

examples.text: comme un café du matin ouvert au quartier?!
examples.trans: like a morning cafe open to the neighbourhood?!

examples.text: Donne-moi le lait d'abord pour la machine à café.
examples.trans: Give me the milk first for the coffee machine.

meanings.note: Larger bound notebook.

examples.text: Dans le tiroir. Ici, on utilise ce grand cahier en papier et un crayon.
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper notebook and a pencil.

examples.text: Un cahier en papier? Vraiment?
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

examples.text: Je dois lire le cahier de réservations, mais je ne trouve pas mes lunettes!
examples.trans: I need to read the reservation book, but I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Caisse à outils = toolbox; la caisse = the till.

examples.text: Voici cinquante euros de la caisse. Rapportez le ticket!
examples.trans: Here is fifty euros from the cash box. Bring back the receipt!

examples.text: Vous avez une vanne de rechange dans votre caisse à outils?
examples.trans: Do you have a spare valve in your toolbox?

meanings.en: to wedge steady (a wobbly table or door)
meanings.note: Caler une table = stop a table from wobbling with a wedge or shim.

examples.text: J'ai calé le pied de la table sur les pierres.
examples.trans: I steadied the table leg on the stones.

examples.text: Calez la porte ouverte avec ce petit bloc de bois.
examples.trans: Prop the door open with this small block of wood.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le call-back', plural 'les call-backs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'callback'.

examples.text: Le réalisateur m'a rappelé pour un call-back demain!
examples.trans: The director called me back for a second audition tomorrow!

examples.text: Dix acteurs ont été retenus pour le call-back final.
examples.trans: Ten actors were kept for the final callback.

meanings.note: Decorative handwriting or calligraphy written with a nib or fountain pen.

examples.text: Sa calligraphie au stylo-plume donne un air royal au plan de table.
examples.trans: His fountain-pen calligraphy gives the seating chart a royal air.

examples.text: Elle a inscrit le nom de chaque invité avec une belle calligraphie.
examples.trans: She wrote each guest's name in lovely calligraphy.

meanings.note: Rester calme = to stay calm.
Une rue calme = a quiet street.

examples.text: Reste calme, Julie.
examples.trans: Stay calm, Julie.

examples.text: C'est un quartier très calme.
examples.trans: It's a very quiet neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Je respire très calmement.
examples.trans: I am breathing very calmly.

examples.text: D'accord, je respire calmement.
examples.trans: All right, I am breathing calmly.

examples.text: Respire calmement et détends-toi.
examples.trans: Breathe calmly and relax.

meanings.note: imperative: calme-toi! / calmez-vous!
imperative: calme-toi! / calmez-vous!

examples.text: Calmez-vous, Étienne. La chambre est propre et les serviettes sont fraîches.
examples.trans: Relax, Etienne. The room is clean and the towels are fresh.

examples.text: Tout va se calmer.
examples.trans: Everything will calm down.

meanings.note: figurative: un vrai calvaire = a real ordeal

examples.text: Un calvaire, tu veux dire.
examples.trans: An ordeal, you mean.

examples.text: C'était un calvaire.
examples.trans: It was an ordeal.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le camarade', plural 'les camarades') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'classmate'.

examples.text: Nous sommes de vieux camarades.
examples.trans: We are old schoolmates.

examples.text: Nous sommes de vieux camarades d'école.
examples.trans: We are old schoolmates.

examples.text: Non, c'était juste une camarade d'école!
examples.trans: No, she was just a school classmate!

meanings.note: Everyday word for trucks and vans.

examples.text: Le camion du laitier est en panne. Regardez dans le frigo!
examples.trans: The milkman's van has broken down. Look in the fridge!

examples.text: Voici le camion sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the lorry, truck, delivery van on the table.

meanings.note: Diminutive of camion ('lorry/truck') formed with -ette, making it feminine.

examples.text: La camionnette du fleuriste est garée devant la grille.
examples.trans: The florist's van is parked in front of the gate.

examples.text: Ils déchargent vingt caisses de pommes de la camionnette.
examples.trans: They are unloading twenty crates of apples from the van.

meanings.note: Usually paired with *à la* (*une tisane à la camomille*) or used directly for a cup of chamomile infusion (*boire une camomille*).

examples.text: Une tisane chaude à la camomille aide à bien dormir.
examples.trans: A hot cup of chamomile herbal tea helps you sleep well.

examples.text: Les petites fleurs de camomille sèchent dans un panier.
examples.trans: The little chamomile flowers are drying in a basket.

meanings.note: à la campagne / en pleine campagne = in the countryside
Une campagne électorale.

examples.text: Je suis toute seule en pleine campagne!
examples.trans: I'm all alone in the middle of the countryside!

examples.text: On habite à la campagne.
examples.trans: We live in the countryside.

meanings.note: Idiom: refuse to budge. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to camp'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'campé').

meanings.en: to stick firmly, dig in one's heels (camper sur ses positions)
meanings.note: Idiom: refuse to budge. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to camp'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'campé').

examples.text: Il a campé sur ses positions.
examples.trans: He dug his heels in.

examples.text: Ils campent dans la forêt.
examples.trans: They are camping in the forest.

meanings.note: devant la caméra = in front of the camera

examples.text: Manger devant la caméra.
examples.trans: To eat in front of the camera.

examples.text: Tourner avec deux caméras.
examples.trans: To shoot with two cameras.

examples.text: Il mange un animal cru devant la caméra?
examples.trans: He eats a raw animal in front of the camera?

meanings.note: lowercase as an adjective; capitalized as a noun: un Canadien

examples.text: On va tourner d'abord la partie canadienne.
examples.trans: We're going to shoot the Canadian part first.

examples.text: Ma mère est canadienne.
examples.trans: My mother is Canadian.

examples.text: Quelle partie canadienne?
examples.trans: What Canadian part?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le canapé', plural 'les canapés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sofa'.

examples.text: Dormir sur le canapé.
examples.trans: To sleep on the couch.

examples.text: Un grand canapé.
examples.trans: A large sofa.

examples.text: Ils restent assis sur le canapé toute la soirée.
examples.trans: They stay seated on the sofa the whole evening.

meanings.note: un canard gonflable = an inflatable duck
Canard en plastique.

examples.text: Le canard est dans l'eau.
examples.trans: The duck is in the water.

examples.text: Mais je ne saute pas sur le canard!
examples.trans: But I'm not jumping on the duck!

examples.text: Je ne saute pas sur le canard, c'est clair?
examples.trans: I'm not jumping on the duck, is that clear?

meanings.note: Pronounced with a final -r.

examples.text: Il va mourir d'un cancer terrible.
examples.trans: He is going to die of a terrible cancer.

examples.text: La recherche contre le cancer.
examples.trans: Cancer research.

meanings.note: le meilleur candidat = the best candidate

examples.text: Nous avons dix candidats au total.
examples.trans: We have ten candidates in total.

examples.text: Un candidat sérieux.
examples.trans: A serious candidate.

examples.text: On choisira ensemble le meilleur candidat.
examples.trans: We will choose the best candidate together.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la candidate', plural 'les candidates') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'female candidate'.

examples.text: Elle était la seule candidate.
examples.trans: She was the only candidate.

examples.text: Ils disent que d'autres candidates voulaient le poste.
examples.trans: They say other candidates wanted the position.

meanings.note: Walking stick or cane, as well as a reed or fishing rod (canne à pêche).

examples.text: Et marchant à côté d'Antoine avec une élégante canne à pommeau d'argent et un chapeau clair...
examples.trans: And walking beside Antoine with an elegant silver-topped walking stick and a light hat...

examples.text: Le voyageur a posé sa canne en bois contre le banc du jardin.
examples.trans: The traveller rested his wooden walking stick against the garden bench.

meanings.note: À la cannelle = cinnamon-flavoured.

examples.text: Bonjour! Ça sent la cannelle chaude jusqu'en haut de l'escalier!
examples.trans: Good morning! It smells like warm cinnamon all the way up the stairs!

examples.text: Bonjour, Madame Odette! Mes brioches à la cannelle sortent tout juste du four.
examples.trans: Good morning, Madam Odette! My cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Ma foi, personne ne refuse une brioche chaude à la cannelle à sept heures du matin.
examples.trans: Well now, nobody turns down a warm cinnamon roll at seven in the morning.

meanings.note: Followed by de and a noun or infinitive; en can replace that de-complement.

examples.text: J'en suis capable.
examples.trans: I can do it.

examples.text: Elle est capable de tout.
examples.trans: She's capable of anything.

examples.text: Je vais la convaincre de revenir. J'en suis capable.
examples.trans: I'm going to persuade her to come back. I can do it.

meanings.note: Ship, team, or expedition captain (used for any gender: 'le/la capitaine').

examples.text: Le capitaine étudie la carte avant de lever l'ancre.
examples.trans: The captain studies the chart before weighing anchor.

examples.text: C'est toi le capitaine de notre petite expédition!
examples.trans: You're the captain of our little expedition!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'vital'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est une question capitale.
examples.trans: It is a vital question.

examples.text: Nous devons sauver ce contrat capital.
examples.trans: We must save this crucial contract.

examples.text: Mais d'abord, j'ai un rendez-vous capital.
examples.trans: But first, I have a vital appointment.

meanings.note: Idiomatic French interj expression meaning 'got it', frequent in natural conversational dialogue.

examples.text: On se retrouve devant le théâtre à huit heures, capito?
examples.trans: We meet in front of the theatre at eight o'clock, got it?

examples.text: Pas un mot à la presse, capito?
examples.trans: Not a word to the press, understood?

meanings.note: Of a child.
Of a child.

examples.text: Un nouveau caprice?
examples.trans: Another whim?

examples.text: Ce n'est pas un caprice.
examples.trans: It's not a whim.

examples.text: Tu deviens capricieuse.
examples.trans: You become capricious.

examples.text: Un acteur capricieux.
examples.trans: A temperamental actor.

meanings.note: Une capsule temporelle = a time capsule.

examples.text: Ils ont caché une capsule temporelle sous l'arbre.
examples.trans: They hid a time capsule under the tree.

examples.text: La petite capsule en métal protège la lettre de la pluie.
examples.trans: The small metal capsule protects the letter from the rain.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction introducing a reason or explanation ('for, because').

examples.text: Rentrons vite, car la pluie commence à tomber.
examples.trans: Let's head inside quickly, for the rain is starting to fall.

examples.text: J'aime cette librairie, car on y trouve des livres rares.
examples.trans: I love this bookshop, because you find rare books there.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le caractère', plural 'les caractères') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'personality'.

examples.text: Elle a un fort caractère.
examples.trans: She has a strong personality.

examples.text: Elle a déjà un fort caractère!
examples.trans: She already has a strong personality!

meanings.note: Une carafe d'eau is free at French tables.

examples.text: Attention, Étienne, le bec de la carafe est large!
examples.trans: Careful, Etienne, the pitcher spout is wide!

examples.text: Voici la carafe sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the carafe, water pitcher on the table.

meanings.en: cardiac, related to the heart or heart conditions
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'cardiac'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il a eu une crise cardiaque.
examples.trans: He had a heart attack.

examples.text: Il a eu une crise cardiaque!
examples.trans: He had a heart attack!

examples.text: Oui, pour surveiller mon rythme cardiaque.
examples.trans: Yes, to monitor my heart rate.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le carnage', plural 'les carnages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'carnage'.

examples.text: La critique a fait un vrai carnage après la première.
examples.trans: The critics made a total carnage after the premiere.

examples.text: Si le réalisateur voit ça, ce sera un carnage.
examples.trans: If the director sees that, it will be a bloodbath.

meanings.note: Smaller than un cahier.

examples.text: Attendez: à qui est ce petit carnet en cuir marron sur le comptoir?
examples.trans: Wait: whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?

examples.text: Oh, mon carnet en cuir! Merci! Je le cherchais justement.
examples.trans: Oh, my leather notebook! Thank you! I was just looking for it.

examples.text: Quand votre carnet s'est ouvert sur le comptoir hier soir, on a vu écrit neuf sur dix...
examples.trans: When your notebook fell open on the counter last night, we saw nine out of ten written...

meanings.note: Feminine noun (*une carotte fraîche*, *des carottes râpées*).

examples.text: Coupez trois carottes en petits dés pour la soupe.
examples.trans: Chop three carrots into small cubes for the soup.

examples.text: Ces carottes du marché sont douces et croquantes.
examples.trans: These market carrots are sweet and crisp.

meanings.note: Plural *des carreaux*; *laver les carreaux* is idiomatic everyday French for washing windowpanes.

examples.text: Le soleil brille à travers chaque carreau fraîchement lavé.
examples.trans: The sun shines through each freshly washed windowpane.

examples.text: Les carreaux de la cuisine sont propres et secs.
examples.trans: The kitchen tiles are clean and dry.

examples.text: Vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Twenty years of career.

examples.text: Elle a une belle carrière.
examples.trans: She has a fine career.

examples.text: On commence par le carrousel?
examples.trans: Do we start with the carousel?

examples.text: Les enfants aiment le carrousel.
examples.trans: The children like the merry-go-round.

examples.text: On commence par le carrousel? Oh, c'est rapide!
examples.trans: Do we start with the carousel? Oh, that's fast!

meanings.note: Écriture carrée = neat block handwriting.

examples.text: J'ai reconnu ton écriture carrée sur cette carte postale en deux secondes.
examples.trans: I recognized your neat block handwriting on that postcard in two seconds.

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment carré.
examples.trans: This place is really square, neat block.

meanings.note: Carte de visite.
Carte bancaire.

examples.text: Vous avez la carte, s'il vous plaît?
examples.trans: Do you have the menu, please?

examples.text: Il y a une petite carte en papier attachée à la poignée.
examples.trans: There is a small paper card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Same form in masculine and feminine: un / une cartographe.

examples.text: Le jeune cartographe dessinait les collines de la région.
examples.trans: The young mapmaker was drawing the hills of the region.

examples.text: Ce cartographe garde toutes ses cartes dans un étui sec.
examples.trans: This cartographer keeps all his maps in a dry case.

meanings.note: The art and science of drawing maps.

examples.text: Cet atlas ancien est un chef-d'œuvre de cartographie.
examples.trans: This antique atlas is a masterpiece of cartography.

examples.text: Il s'est passionné pour la cartographie dès l'université.
examples.trans: He fell in love with mapmaking back at university.

meanings.en: cardboard box, carton (for moving or storage)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le carton', plural 'les cartons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cardboard box'.

examples.text: Tu prépares tes cartons pour déménager?
examples.trans: Are you packing your boxes to move?

examples.text: Remplir un grand carton.
examples.trans: To fill a large cardboard box.

examples.text: Seulement trois petits cartons! Peut-être quatre!
examples.trans: Only three small boxes! Maybe four!

cartonner.gloss: to rock, to be a massive hit

meanings.en: to be wildly successful, hit big
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to be wildly successful'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'cartonné').

examples.text: Le jeune acteur a cartonné aux essais.
examples.trans: The young actor was a massive hit at auditions.

examples.text: Samy a totalement cartonné aujourd'hui!
examples.trans: Samy totally rocked the audition today!

meanings.note: Au cas où = just in case; en tout cas = in any case. Silent final -s.

examples.text: Prenez un parapluie dans l'entrée au cas où.
examples.trans: Take an umbrella from the entryway just in case.

examples.text: Dans ce cas, nous ouvrons les deux portes du jardin.
examples.trans: In that case, we open both garden doors.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cascade', plural 'les cascades') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'stunt'.
Feminine noun ('la cascade', plural 'les cascades') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'waterfall'.

examples.text: Il fait ses cascades lui-même.
examples.trans: He does his stunts himself.

examples.text: Une belle cascade en montagne.
examples.trans: A beautiful mountain waterfall.

examples.text: Il peut faire ses cascades lui-même.
examples.trans: He can do his own stunts.

meanings.note: Mettre un casque. Masculine noun ('le casque', plural 'les casques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'headphones'.

examples.text: Voici votre casque.
examples.trans: Here are your headphones.

examples.text: Écouter de la musique au casque.
examples.trans: To listen to music with headphones.

examples.text: Tu n'as même pas de casque!
examples.trans: You do not even have a helmet!

meanings.note: envoyer à la casse = to discard, put out to pasture

examples.text: La peur d'être envoyé à la casse.
examples.trans: The fear of being sent to the scrap heap.

examples.text: La voiture est partie à la casse.
examples.trans: The car went to the scrapyard.

meanings.note: Non-reflexive completed past forms use avoir: j'ai cassé.

meanings.en: se casser + body part = to break one's (arm, leg, ankle)
meanings.note: Reflexive se casser uses être. In elle s'est cassé la cheville, the following direct object means cassé stays unchanged.

examples.text: Elle s'est cassé la cheville.
examples.trans: She broke her ankle.

examples.text: Attention, tu vas tout casser!
examples.trans: Careful, you're going to break everything!

meanings.en: to cast (an actor for a role)
meanings.note: Borrowed from English to cast. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'cast'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'casté').

examples.text: Il l'a casté pour ce rôle.
examples.trans: He cast him for this role.

examples.text: Arrête, il t'a casté, tu l'as convaincu.
examples.trans: Stop it, he cast you, you convinced him.

examples.text: Pas du tout. Vous avez été casté dans un film d'Audiard.
examples.trans: Not at all. You were cast in an Audiard movie.

meanings.en: casting, audition process (for a film or play)
meanings.note: Borrowed from English.

examples.text: Elle me veut pour le casting!
examples.trans: She wants me for the casting!

examples.text: Je passe un casting demain.
examples.trans: I have a casting tomorrow.

meanings.note: un barrage de castor = a beaver dam

examples.text: Mon animal totem est le castor.
examples.trans: My totem animal is the beaver.

examples.text: Les castors vivent près des rivières.
examples.trans: Beavers live near rivers.

examples.text: Le castor! Oui, Mathias, je viens d'une famille de bâtisseurs!
examples.trans: The beaver! Yes, Mathias, I come from a family of builders!

examples.text: Quelle catastrophe! Hier, j'ai noté une réservation sur la tablette sans mes lunettes!
examples.trans: What a disaster! Yesterday I wrote a booking on the tablet without my glasses!

examples.text: Même une catastrophe, c'est juste un accroc!
examples.trans: Even a disaster is just a hitch!

examples.text: Quelle catastrophe!
examples.trans: What a disaster!

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Les chiffres du film sont catastrophiques.
examples.trans: The film's numbers are catastrophic.

examples.text: Attends, Mathias, ma robe est catastrophique!
examples.trans: Wait, Mathias, my dress is a disaster!

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Refuser catégoriquement.
examples.trans: To refuse categorically.

examples.text: Il a nié catégoriquement.
examples.trans: He flatly denied.

examples.text: Non, elle refuse catégoriquement d'y aller.
examples.trans: No, she categorically refuses to go there.

meanings.note: Faire un cauchemar. Masculine noun ('le cauchemar', plural 'les cauchemars') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nightmare'.

examples.text: Je ne dors plus et je fais des cauchemars.
examples.trans: I no longer sleep and I have nightmares.

examples.text: Toute cette histoire ressemble à un cauchemar.
examples.trans: This whole affair resembles a nightmare.

examples.text: C'est un véritable cauchemar!
examples.trans: It is a true nightmare!

examples.text: Quelle est la cause?
examples.trans: What is the cause?

examples.text: La cause est claire.
examples.trans: The cause is clear.

causer.gloss: to cause, bring about; to chat

meanings.en: to cause, bring about, produce; to chat, talk
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to cause'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'causé').

examples.text: Cela a causé des ennuis.
examples.trans: That caused trouble.

examples.text: On doit causer tous les deux.
examples.trans: We need to talk, the two of us.

examples.text: Je t'ai causé beaucoup d'ennuis.
examples.trans: I caused you a lot of trouble.

meanings.note: Underground storage or wine cellar.

examples.text: Merci pour votre patience! Henri va vérifier la cave tout de suite.
examples.trans: Thank you for your patience! Henri is going to check the cellar right away.

examples.text: Voici la cave sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the cellar, basement on the table.

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: I can't come tonight.

examples.text: Il y a vingt-cinq ans? Dans cette même maison?
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago? In that same house?

meanings.note: Points forward to something being shown or introduced.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé les chaises... et derrière une vieille cloison en brique, j'ai trouvé ceci.
examples.trans: I found the chairs... and behind an old brick partition, I found this.

examples.text: et derrière une vieille cloison en brique, j'ai trouvé ceci.
examples.trans: and behind an old brick partition, I found this.

meanings.note: attacher sa ceinture = to fasten one's seatbelt

examples.text: Serre un peu ta ceinture.
examples.trans: Tighten your belt a bit.

examples.text: Une ceinture noire.
examples.trans: A black belt.

meanings.note: A demonstrative pronoun; ça is the common everyday form.

examples.text: Je comprends cela.
examples.trans: I understand that.

examples.text: Cela arrive.
examples.trans: That happens.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cellule', plural 'les cellules') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cell'.

examples.text: Il est en cellule.
examples.trans: He is in a cell.

examples.text: Par ici. Il est en cellule de dégrisement.
examples.trans: This way. He is in the sobering-up cell.

meanings.note: celle = feminine: celle de la semaine dernière

examples.text: Celle de la semaine dernière?
examples.trans: The one from last week?

examples.text: Je prends celui-là.
examples.trans: I'll take that one.

meanings.note: masculine singular; refers to a near object

examples.text: Celui-ci est celui de Tonie Marshall.
examples.trans: This one is Tonie Marshall's.

examples.text: Je préfère celui-ci.
examples.trans: I prefer this one.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun pointing out a specific person or thing ('that one there').

examples.text: Parmi tous les cahiers, je préfère celui-là.
examples.trans: Among all the notebooks, I prefer that one.

examples.text: Cette clé ouvre la cave, et celle-là ouvre le jardin.
examples.trans: This key opens the cellar, and that one opens the garden.

meanings.note: Être censé faire quelque chose.

examples.text: On est censés être soulagés?
examples.trans: We're supposed to be relieved?

examples.text: Il est censé arriver à midi.
examples.trans: He is supposed to arrive at noon.

meanings.note: Trois cents, but trois cent mille.

examples.text: Trois cent mille.
examples.trans: Three hundred thousand.

examples.text: Cent euros.
examples.trans: A hundred euros.

meanings.note: An approximate group of one hundred ('une centaine de' = about a hundred; 'des centaines de' = hundreds of).

examples.text: Attendez: des centaines de visiteurs dans la rue des Tilleuls pour notre piano et le pain de Nadia?!
examples.trans: Wait: hundreds of visitors walking down Rue des Tilleuls for our piano and the bread from Nadia?!

examples.text: Il y a une centaine de livres anciens sur cette étagère.
examples.trans: There are about a hundred old books on this shelf.

meanings.note: Au centime près = down to the last cent.

examples.text: Dix, onze, douze. Le compte est bon au centime près, merci!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last cent, thank you!

examples.text: Voici le centime sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the cent on the table.

meanings.note: Masculine unit of length (*un centimètre*, 1/100 of a meter).

examples.text: Laissez deux centimètres d'espace entre le meuble et le mur.
examples.trans: Leave two centimeters of space between the cabinet and the wall.

examples.text: La planche mesure quarante centimètres de large.
examples.trans: The board measures forty centimeters wide.

meanings.note: Located in the middle or serving as the main hub of a city ('la gare centrale' = the central station).
Masculine plural takes -aux: centraux.

examples.text: Deux heures vingt-huit! Mon frère et moi devons partir à pied vers la gare centrale maintenant!
examples.trans: Twenty-eight minutes past two! My brother and I must walk to the central station now!

examples.text: Le vieux tilleul se dresse sur la place centrale du quartier.
examples.trans: The old linden tree stands on the central square of the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Middle point ('au centre de'); town center ('centre-ville') or cultural center.

examples.text: La fontaine se dresse exactement au centre de la place.
examples.trans: The fountain stands right in the center of the square.

examples.text: On peut tout faire à pied dans le centre du village.
examples.trans: You can do everything on foot in the village center.

meanings.note: Geometric circle or ring ('en cercle' = in a circle); social circle.

examples.text: Les chaises sont disposées en cercle sous le tilleul.
examples.trans: The chairs are arranged in a circle under the linden tree.

examples.text: Il trace un cercle parfait sur la feuille blanche.
examples.trans: He draws a perfect circle on the blank sheet.

related.gloss: round; in circles (in tourner en rond)

meanings.note: used as pronoun in plural: certains

examples.text: Certains ont même acheté des chaussettes.
examples.trans: Some people even bought socks.

examples.text: Certains ont même acheté des chaussettes avec l'argent de la société!
examples.trans: Some people even bought socks with the company's money!

examples.text: Certaines surprises sont indésirables.
examples.trans: Some surprises are unwelcome.

meanings.note: Built from certain + -ment.

examples.text: Je ne chausse certainement pas du quarante-quatre!
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four shoes!

examples.text: Vous restez pour le dîner? Certainement!
examples.trans: Are you staying for dinner? Certainly!

meanings.note: Plural in -x: les cerveaux.

examples.text: C'est mauvais pour les jeunes cerveaux.
examples.trans: It's bad for young brains.

examples.text: Le cerveau humain.
examples.trans: The human brain.

examples.text: J'ai peut-être le cerveau mal câblé.
examples.trans: Maybe my brain is wired wrong.

meanings.en: ceasing, stopping; used chiefly in "sans cesse" = non-stop, endlessly
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cesse', plural 'les cesses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ceasing'.

examples.text: Sans cesse.
examples.trans: Endlessly.

examples.text: Parler sans cesse.
examples.trans: To speak without stopping.

examples.text: Cette histoire me tourmente sans cesse.
examples.trans: This story torments me endlessly.

meanings.note: Formal property/legal term.

examples.text: Avis de cession immobilière: l'immeuble du numéro huit est mis en vente pour des bureaux commerciaux.
examples.trans: Notice of property transfer: the building at number eight is up for sale for commercial offices.

examples.text: Voici la cession sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the transfer, sale on the table.

meanings.note: Chacune de ces chaises = each one of these chairs (agrees in gender with the noun it represents, always singular).

examples.text: Chacun des invités reçoit une tasse de thé chaud.
examples.trans: Each of the guests receives a cup of hot tea.

examples.text: Chacune de ces fenêtres donne sur le vieux tilleul.
examples.trans: Each one of these windows overlooks the old linden tree.

meanings.note: Sorrow or grief caused by loss.
A cause of sadness or distress.

examples.text: Elle a du chagrin.
examples.trans: She's sad.

examples.text: Un gros chagrin.
examples.trans: A great sorrow.

examples.text: Oui, il faut se battre contre le chagrin.
examples.trans: Yes, we must fight against sorrow.

meanings.note: A chair; an armchair is un fauteuil.

examples.text: Prends une chaise.
examples.trans: Grab a chair.

examples.text: Quatre tables, huit chaises, tout est en place!
examples.trans: Four tables, eight chairs, everything is in place!

examples.text: Oh... oh non. Où est ma chaise? J'ai les jambes qui tremblent.
examples.trans: Oh... oh no. Where is my chair? My legs are shaking.

meanings.note: Feminine noun, both physical (garder la chaleur = retain heat) and figurative (human warmth).

examples.text: Une théière en fonte garde longtemps la chaleur.
examples.trans: A cast-iron teapot keeps the heat in for a long time.

examples.text: On sent la douce chaleur du four dès l'entrée.
examples.trans: You can feel the gentle warmth of the oven right from the entrance.

meanings.note: In a warm, cordial, and welcoming manner.
Formed from the feminine adjective chaleureuse + -ment.

examples.text: Trente étés entre deux chansons, et la cour résonne plus chaleureusement que jamais.
examples.trans: Thirty summers between two songs, and the courtyard sounds warmer than ever.

examples.text: Les voisins ont accueilli le cartographe très chaleureusement.
examples.trans: The neighbours welcomed the mapmaker very warmly.

meanings.note: Un accueil chaleureux. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un accueil très chaleureux.
examples.trans: A very warm welcome.

examples.text: Des applaudissements chaleureux.
examples.trans: Warm applause.

examples.text: Écoutez la pluie sur le toit, c'est tellement chaleureux ici!
examples.trans: Listen to the rain on the roof, it feels so cosy up here!

meanings.note: consulter un chaman = to consult a shaman

examples.text: Je connais un chaman extraordinaire.
examples.trans: I know an extraordinary shaman.

examples.text: Le chaman du village.
examples.trans: The village shaman.

examples.text: Je sais que vous êtes sceptique, mais je connais un chaman extraordinaire.
examples.trans: I know you are skeptical, but I know an extraordinary shaman.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le chamane', plural 'les chamanes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shaman'.

examples.text: Réveillez le chamane qui est en vous.
examples.trans: Awaken the shaman within you.

examples.text: Oui, j'essaie de réveiller mon chamane.
examples.trans: Yes, I am trying to awaken my shaman.

meanings.note: pratiquer le chamanisme = to practice shamanism

examples.text: Vous connaissez le chamanisme?
examples.trans: Do you know about shamanism?

examples.text: Le chamanisme traditionnel.
examples.trans: Traditional shamanism.

examples.text: Vous lisez un livre sur le chamanisme?
examples.trans: Are you reading a book about shamanism?

meanings.note: Une chambre d'hôtel.
Une chambre d'hôtel.

examples.text: Une chambre au Carlton.
examples.trans: A room at the Carlton.

examples.text: Elle est dans sa chambre.
examples.trans: She's in her room.

meanings.note: the region is la Champagne (feminine)

examples.text: Apportez deux coupes de champagne pour fêter le contrat!
examples.trans: Bring two glasses of champagne to celebrate the contract!

examples.text: On a ouvert une bouteille de champagne à l'agence.
examples.trans: We opened a bottle of champagne at the agency.

examples.text: Tu es capable de faire cette scène, champion!
examples.trans: You can do this scene, champ!

examples.text: C'est un grand champion.
examples.trans: He is a great champion.

meanings.note: Bonne chance! means 'Good luck!', and avoir de la chance means 'to be lucky'.

examples.text: Souhaitez-moi bonne chance avant la visite du maire!
examples.trans: Wish me good luck before the mayor's visit!

examples.text: Nous avons de la chance: il fait grand soleil ce matin.
examples.trans: We are lucky: it is bright and sunny this morning.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le change', plural 'les changes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'diaper change'.
Masculine noun ('le change', plural 'les changes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'foreign exchange'.

examples.text: S'occuper des repas et des changes.
examples.trans: Taking care of meals and diaper changes.

examples.text: Faire le change du bébé.
examples.trans: To change the baby's diaper.

examples.text: S'occuper des repas et des changes?
examples.trans: Taking care of meals and changes?

meanings.note: From changer. Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'change'.

examples.text: Un léger changement de programme.
examples.trans: A slight change of schedule.

examples.text: Le changement est nécessaire.
examples.trans: Change is necessary.

examples.text: Attendez: quelle réduction est-ce qu'on lui offre pour le changement de chambre?
examples.trans: Wait: what discount do we offer him for the room change?

meanings.note: Changer quelque chose.
changer de + noun without article: changer d'agent

examples.text: Il a changé de travail.
examples.trans: He changed jobs.

examples.text: Regardez là-haut à la fenêtre du grenier: Antoine a déjà changé trois fois de chemise!
examples.trans: Look up at the attic window: Antoine has already changed his shirt three times!

meanings.note: Feminine noun from chanter ('to sing'), typically for a song with lyrics or a short lyrical melody.

examples.text: Odette joue une vieille chanson française au piano.
examples.trans: Odette plays an old French song on the piano.

examples.text: Tout le quartier connaît le refrain de cette chanson.
examples.trans: The whole neighbourhood knows the chorus of this song.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le chant', plural 'les chants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'vocal music'.

examples.text: Elle prend des cours de chant.
examples.trans: She takes singing lessons.

examples.text: De la danse, du chant, de la comédie!
examples.trans: Dance, singing, comedy!

meanings.en: blackmail, extortion (faire du chantage = to blackmail)
meanings.note: Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'blackmail'.

examples.text: C'est du chantage.
examples.trans: That is blackmail.

examples.text: Un chantage inacceptable.
examples.trans: An unacceptable blackmail.

examples.text: C'est un chantage inacceptable, Hicham.
examples.trans: That is unacceptable blackmail, Hicham.

meanings.note: Participial adjective from chanter; describes a lyrical melody (une mélodie chantante) or a musical regional accent (un accent chantant).

examples.text: Cette valse a une ligne très douce et chantante.
examples.trans: This waltz has a very gentle, singing line.

examples.text: La marchande de miel a une voix chaude et chantante.
examples.trans: The honey vendor has a warm, lilting voice.

meanings.en: to sing; (of an instrument or piano key) to ring out clearly
meanings.note: Used literally for singing and poetically in French music talk when piano keys or strings 'sing' (les touches chantent).

examples.text: Les oiseaux chantent dans le tilleul dès six heures.
examples.trans: The birds sing in the linden tree from six o'clock on.

examples.text: Sous les doigts d'Odette, le vieux piano chante à nouveau.
examples.trans: Beneath Odette's fingers, the old piano sings again.

meanings.note: A singer; masculine chanteur, feminine chanteuse.

examples.text: Line est chanteuse.
examples.trans: Line is a singer.

examples.text: Le chanteur arrive.
examples.trans: The singer is arriving.

examples.text: Line était une chanteuse connue. Françoise était une jeune actrice.
examples.trans: Line was a well-known singer. Françoise was a young actress.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'singer (female)'.

examples.text: Julien cherche une chanteuse.
examples.trans: Julien is looking for a singer.

examples.text: Une chanteuse d'opéra.
examples.trans: An opera singer.

examples.text: Il cherche une chanteuse pour son film.
examples.trans: He is looking for a singer for his film.

meanings.note: Enlever son chapeau = take off one's hat. Plural chapeaux.

examples.text: Le monsieur enlève son chapeau gris en entrant.
examples.trans: The gentleman takes off his grey hat as he comes in.

examples.text: Accrochez votre chapeau près de la porte.
examples.trans: Hang your hat near the door.

meanings.note: Invariable, singular noun.

examples.text: Du Botox chaque année.
examples.trans: Botox every year.

examples.text: Je travaille chaque jour.
examples.trans: I work every day.

charge.gloss: duty, care; se charger de = to take charge of

meanings.en: load, responsibility; s'en charger = take charge of it
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la charge', plural 'les charges') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'duty'.

examples.text: Je m'en charge.
examples.trans: I will take care of it.

examples.text: Non, c'est ma cliente, je m'en charge.
examples.trans: No, that is my client, I will handle it.

meanings.note: un emploi du temps chargé = a busy schedule

examples.text: Mon emploi du temps est très chargé.
examples.trans: My schedule is very busy.

examples.text: Charger la voiture.
examples.trans: To load the car.

examples.text: Mon emploi du temps est trop chargé.
examples.trans: My schedule is much too tight.

meanings.note: Wheeled book cart, serving trolley, or luggage cart.

examples.text: La bibliothécaire pousse un chariot chargé de dictionnaires.
examples.trans: The librarian pushes a book cart loaded with dictionaries.

examples.text: Posez les valises lourdes sur le chariot de l'entrée.
examples.trans: Set the heavy suitcases on the lobby luggage cart.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le charisme', plural 'les charismes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'charisma'.

examples.text: Il a un charisme naturel impressionnant.
examples.trans: He has an impressive natural charisma.

examples.text: Le charisme de cet acteur crève l'écran.
examples.trans: The charisma of this actor lights up the screen.

examples.text: J'ai beaucoup de charisme naturel.
examples.trans: I have a lot of natural charisma.

meanings.note: Delightful, pleasant, full of charm.

examples.text: Ils habitent une charmante maison aux volets bleus.
examples.trans: They live in a charming house with blue shutters.

examples.text: Votre accueil est toujours aussi charmant.
examples.trans: Your welcome is as lovely as ever.

meanings.note: Quel charme! = how charming!. Masculine noun ('le charme', plural 'les charmes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'charm'.

examples.text: Il a beaucoup de charme.
examples.trans: He has a lot of charm.

examples.text: Quel charme!
examples.trans: Such charm!

examples.text: Oh oui, une grande actrice. Quel charme!
examples.trans: Oh yes, a great actress. Such charm!

meanings.note: Metal hinge on a box or door.

examples.text: Regardez le vieux plan plié coincé dans la charnière: il y a une porte cachée dessinée à cet étage!
examples.trans: Look at the folded old blueprint tucked in the hinge: there is a hidden door drawn on this floor!

examples.text: Voici la charnière sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the hinge on the table.

meanings.note: un charognard en affaires = a corporate scavenger

examples.text: Bréhier est un charognard.
examples.trans: Brehier is a scavenger.

examples.text: Les charognards tournent dans le ciel.
examples.trans: The scavengers circle in the sky.

examples.text: Bréhier est un charognard. Il ferait n'importe quoi pour nous couler.
examples.trans: Brehier is a scavenger. He would do anything to sink us.

meanings.note: Wooden structural beams under a roof.

examples.text: Oh... regardez les proportions de cette charpente en bois!
examples.trans: Oh... look at the proportions of this timber frame!

examples.text: Voici la charpente sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the roof timber frame on the table.

meanings.en: hunt, hunting (chien de chasse = hunting dog)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la chasse', plural 'les chasses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hunt'.

examples.text: C'est un chien de chasse.
examples.trans: It's a hunting dog.

examples.text: Mathias, c'est le chien de chasse.
examples.trans: Mathias, he is the hunting dog.

meanings.en: to chase away, drive out, expel
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to chase away'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'chassé').

examples.text: Elle nous a chassées.
examples.trans: She drove us away.

examples.text: Elle nous a chassées de là!
examples.trans: She kicked us out of there!

meanings.note: Hunter ('chasseur de trésor' = treasure hunter); bellhop in classic grand hotels.

examples.text: Les enfants jouent aux chasseurs de trésor dans le parc.
examples.trans: The children are playing treasure hunters in the park.

examples.text: C'est un grand chasseur de livres anciens sur les quais.
examples.trans: He is an avid hunter of old books along the riverbanks.

meanings.note: Un petit chat = a little cat.

examples.text: Je me sens comme un petit chat timide.
examples.trans: I feel like a shy little cat.

examples.text: J'ai un chat noir.
examples.trans: I have a black cat.

meanings.en: mon chaton = sweetheart, little one (to a child)

examples.text: Merci, mon chaton.
examples.trans: Thank you, my little kitten.

examples.text: Un petit chaton blanc.
examples.trans: A little white kitten.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'hot'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'hot'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il fait chaud.
examples.trans: It's hot.

examples.text: Un café chaud.
examples.trans: A hot coffee.

examples.text: Il fait chaud. Vous faites quoi?
examples.trans: It's hot. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Built from chaud ('hot').

examples.text: Mauvaise nouvelle. La vanne en laiton de la vieille chaudière vient de lâcher.
examples.trans: Bad news. The brass valve on the old boiler just gave out.

examples.text: Vingt millimètres, en laiton, vanne de chaudière: je vais répéter ça tout le long!
examples.trans: Twenty millimetres, brass, boiler valve: I am going to repeat that all the way!

examples.text: Pas une seule goutte! On peut rallumer la chaudière maintenant?
examples.trans: Not a single drop! Can we relight the boiler now?

meanings.note: Central heating in a building.

examples.text: Oui! On dirait que ça vient du tuyau de chauffage dans le coin.
examples.trans: Yes! It sounds like it comes from the heating pipe in the corner.

examples.text: Ça veut dire pas de chauffage cette nuit, ou pas d'eau chaude non plus?
examples.trans: Does that mean no heating tonight, or no hot water either?

meanings.note: Used both transitively and intransitively.

examples.text: Touchez le tuyau en cuivre! Il chauffe déjà!
examples.trans: Touch the copper pipe! It is warming up already!

examples.text: C'est facile à chauffer ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to heat, warm up together.

meanings.note: Basement room housing the boiler.

examples.text: Vous avez trouvé les trois chaises pliantes derrière la chaufferie, Henri?
examples.trans: Did you find the three folding chairs behind the boiler room, Henri?

examples.text: Voici la chaufferie sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the boiler room on the table.

meanings.en: driver (of a van, bus, taxi, or delivery vehicle)
meanings.note: Refers to a professional driver; an everyday motorist driving their own car is un conducteur / une conductrice.

examples.text: Le chauffeur appelle dix minutes avant la livraison.
examples.trans: The delivery driver calls ten minutes before the delivery.

examples.text: J'ai signé le bon et remercié le chauffeur.
examples.trans: I signed the slip and thanked the driver.

chausser.gloss: to wear (a shoe size); put shoes on

meanings.en: to wear (a shoe size); put shoes on
meanings.note: Chausser du 42 = to take size 42 shoes.

examples.text: Je ne chausse certainement pas du quarante-quatre!
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four shoes!

examples.text: C'est facile à chausser ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to wear together.

examples.text: J'ai acheté des chaussettes.
examples.trans: I bought socks.

examples.text: Certains ont même acheté des chaussettes avec l'argent de la société!
examples.trans: Some people even bought socks with the company's money!

meanings.note: Une paire de chaussures. Feminine noun ('la chaussure', plural 'les chaussures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shoe'.

examples.text: Elle achète de nouvelles chaussures.
examples.trans: She buys new shoes.

examples.text: Deux paires de grandes chaussures marron pour homme et des pulls gris.
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes and grey sweaters.

examples.text: Pourquoi laisser ses chaussures et son train en bois chez des inconnus jusqu'à vendredi?
examples.trans: Why leave one's shoes and wooden train with strangers until Friday?

meanings.note: chef scénariste = head screenwriter

examples.text: Voici Marie-Sophie Garnier, chef scénariste.
examples.trans: This is Marie-Sophie Garnier, head screenwriter.

examples.text: C'est le chef du projet.
examples.trans: He's the head of the project.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le chef-d'œuvre', plural 'les chefs-d'œuvre') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'masterpiece'.

examples.text: Ce nouveau film est un véritable chef-d'œuvre.
examples.trans: This new film is a true masterpiece.

examples.text: Tout le monde admire ce chef-d'œuvre du cinéma français.
examples.trans: Everyone admires this masterpiece of French cinema.

meanings.note: Modern feminine spelling alongside *une chef*, widely used in French kitchens and bakeries (*la cheffe de cuisine*).

examples.text: La cheffe goûte chaque soupe avant le service de midi.
examples.trans: The chef tastes every soup before lunch service.

examples.text: Toute l'équipe écoute les consignes de la cheffe.
examples.trans: The whole team listens to the chef's instructions.

meanings.note: Sur le chemin du retour means 'on the way back'; en chemin means 'along the way'.

examples.text: Nous prenons du pain frais sur le chemin du retour.
examples.trans: We pick up fresh bread on the way back.

examples.text: Le petit chemin en pierre traverse tout le jardin.
examples.trans: The little stone path crosses the whole garden.

meanings.note: le rôle d'un cheminot = the role of a railway worker

examples.text: Tu es Dario, le cheminot.
examples.trans: You are Dario, the railway worker.

examples.text: Les cheminots sont en grève.
examples.trans: The railway workers are on strike.

examples.text: Tu es Dario, le cheminot et second rôle.
examples.trans: You are Dario, the railway worker and supporting role.

meanings.note: Changer de chemise = to change one's shirt.

examples.text: Regardez là-haut à la fenêtre du grenier: Antoine a déjà changé trois fois de chemise!
examples.trans: Look up at the attic window: Antoine has already changed his shirt three times!

examples.text: Voici la chemise sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the shirt on the table.

examples.text: J'ai réparé son chemisier préféré.
examples.trans: I fixed her favourite blouse.

examples.text: Un chemisier en soie.
examples.trans: A silk blouse.

meanings.note: Before a person noun it commonly means dear; after a thing it can mean expensive.

examples.text: C'est un ami cher.
examples.trans: He is a dear friend.

examples.text: Ce film est cher.
examples.trans: This film is expensive.

meanings.note: no preposition: chercher du travail

meanings.en: aller chercher = to go and get, fetch

examples.text: Je cherche du boulot.
examples.trans: I'm looking for work.

examples.text: Tu cherches quoi?
examples.trans: What are you looking for?

examples.text: C'est une vraie tête chercheuse.
examples.trans: She is like a heat-seeking missile.

examples.text: Elle travaille comme chercheuse.
examples.trans: She works as a researcher.

meanings.note: irregular plural in -aux: un cheval -> des chevaux

examples.text: Il y a des chevaux et tout!
examples.trans: There are horses and everything!

examples.text: Elle monte à cheval.
examples.trans: She rides a horse.

meanings.en: knight (chevalier en armure = knight in armor)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le chevalier', plural 'les chevaliers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'knight'.

examples.text: Un chevalier en armure.
examples.trans: A knight in armor.

examples.text: On pourrait même l'appeler le chevalier en armure brillante d'ASK!
examples.trans: We could even call him ASK's knight in shining armor!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le chevauchement', plural 'les chevauchements') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'overlap'.

examples.text: C'est un léger chevauchement d'horaires.
examples.trans: It is a slight schedule overlap.

examples.text: C'est juste un léger chevauchement d'horaires.
examples.trans: It is just a slight schedule overlap.

meanings.note: Lampe / table de chevet = bedside lamp / table.

examples.text: Alors: il y a un lit, une table et une chaise, mais pas de lampe de chevet.
examples.trans: Okay: there is a bed, a table, and a chair, but no bedside lamp.

examples.text: Voici le chevet sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the bedside on the table.

meanings.note: singular 'un cheveu' = a single strand of hair

examples.text: Isabelle Adjani a un problème de cheveux très urgent.
examples.trans: Isabelle Adjani has a very urgent hair problem.

examples.text: Elle a les cheveux longs.
examples.trans: She has long hair.

meanings.en: ankle; wooden peg or tuning pin
meanings.note: Means both the human ankle (*se tordre la cheville*) and a wooden or metal peg.

examples.text: Posez de la glace sur votre cheville pendant vingt minutes.
examples.trans: Put ice on your ankle for twenty minutes.

examples.text: Elle marche lentement pour ménager sa cheville droite.
examples.trans: She walks slowly to spare her right ankle.

related.gloss: foot; leg (of a table or chair)

meanings.note: At or to someone's home: chez moi, at my place.
At a professional's premises, such as chez le médecin.

examples.text: On est rentrés chez moi.
examples.trans: We went back to my place.

examples.text: Viens chez nous!
examples.trans: Come to our place!

examples.text: Exactement! Tu es déjà chez toi ici.
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in here.

meanings.note: Invariable or with regular plural. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'stylish'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: L'endroit est plutôt chic.
examples.trans: The place is quite fancy.

examples.text: Un restaurant très chic.
examples.trans: A very chic restaurant.

examples.text: L'endroit est plutôt chic. Ils ont sûrement tout.
examples.trans: The place is quite fancy. They surely have everything.

meanings.note: Feminine: chienne. Masculine noun ('le chien', plural 'les chiens') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'dog'.

examples.text: Jean Gabin est un chien.
examples.trans: Jean Gabin is a dog.

examples.text: Je promène mon chien.
examples.trans: I am walking my dog.

examples.text: Ton chien Jean Gabin est vraiment gentil.
examples.trans: Your dog Jean Gabin is really nice.

meanings.note: Ta chienne = your dog. Feminine noun ('la chienne', plural 'les chiennes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'dog'.

examples.text: Je crois que ta chienne m'aime bien, Michel!
examples.trans: I think your dog likes me, Michel!

examples.text: C'est une très gentille chienne.
examples.trans: She is a very nice dog.

meanings.note: Soft cloth for wiping or polishing.

examples.text: Voici un chiffon propre et de l'eau froide, Étienne.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Etienne.

examples.text: Voici le chiffon sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the cleaning cloth, duster on the table.

examples.text: J'ai les chiffres.
examples.trans: I have the figures.

examples.text: Donnez-moi les chiffres.
examples.trans: Give me the figures.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'Chinese'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: L'actrice chinoise Gong Li.
examples.trans: The Chinese actress Gong Li.

examples.text: La cuisine chinoise.
examples.trans: Chinese cuisine.

examples.text: L'actrice chinoise Gong Li en porte un pour la cérémonie d'ouverture.
examples.trans: The Chinese actress Gong Li is wearing one for the opening ceremony.

meanings.note: Feminine: chirurgienne.

examples.text: Elle a un bon chirurgien?
examples.trans: Does she have a good surgeon?

examples.text: Le chirurgien est là.
examples.trans: The surgeon is here.

meanings.note: Amortir le choc.
Être sous le choc.

examples.text: Tes fesses ont amorti le choc.
examples.trans: Your backside cushioned the shock.

examples.text: J'avais les mains froides sous le choc!
examples.trans: My hands were cold from the shock!

meanings.note: une boîte de chocolats = a box of chocolates

examples.text: Elle a apporté des chocolats.
examples.trans: She brought chocolates.

examples.text: Manger du chocolat.
examples.trans: To eat chocolate.

examples.text: Et en plus, tu as apporté des chocolats!
examples.trans: And what is more, you brought chocolates!

meanings.note: Regular second-group verb: nous choisissons; past participle choisi.

examples.text: Je choisis l'ami.
examples.trans: I choose the friend.

examples.text: Tu choisis quel film?
examples.trans: Which film are you choosing?

examples.text: À vrai dire, j'ai aussi choisi ce quartier pour une vieille histoire de famille.
examples.trans: Truthfully, I also chose this neighbourhood for an old family matter.

meanings.note: Same form in the plural.

examples.text: C'est son choix.
examples.trans: It's her choice.

examples.text: Tu as le choix.
examples.trans: You have the choice.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'shocking'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un document choquant.
examples.trans: A shocking document.

examples.text: Cette nouvelle est choquante.
examples.trans: This news is shocking.

examples.text: Regardez ce document choquant sur mon bureau!
examples.trans: Look at this shocking document on my desk!

meanings.note: La chorégraphie du film.

examples.text: D'abord la chorégraphie.
examples.trans: First the choreography.

examples.text: La chorégraphie est difficile.
examples.trans: The choreography is difficult.

examples.text: D'abord la chorégraphie, ensuite votre scène, d'accord?
examples.trans: First the choreography, then your scene, okay?

examples.text: Je veux quelque chose.
examples.trans: I want something.

examples.text: C'est une bonne chose.
examples.trans: It's a good thing.

meanings.note: un chouchou du public = a fan favorite

examples.text: Ryan est un chouchou du public.
examples.trans: Ryan is a darling of the public.

examples.text: C'est le chouchou du réalisateur.
examples.trans: He's the director's favorite.

meanings.note: To speak very softly under one's breath, whisper.

examples.text: Dans la salle de lecture, tout le monde chuchote.
examples.trans: In the reading room, everyone whispers.

examples.text: Elle lui a chuchoté le secret à l'oreille.
examples.trans: She whispered the secret in his ear.

meanings.note: Spoken French interj expression meaning 'hush', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Chut, ne fais pas de bruit pendant le tournage!
examples.trans: Shh, don't make any noise during the shoot!

examples.text: Chut, écoutez bien ce que dit le réalisateur!
examples.trans: Hush, listen carefully to what the director is saying!

examples.text: Chut! Parle doucement, s'il te plaît.
examples.trans: Hush! Speak softly, please.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la chute', plural 'les chutes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fall'.

examples.text: Ils attendent notre chute.
examples.trans: They expect our downfall.

examples.text: Tout le monde attend notre chute.
examples.trans: Everyone expects our downfall.

meanings.note: A wrap worn around the shoulders; a masculine noun despite its final e.

examples.text: Un châle en cachemire.
examples.trans: A cashmere shawl.

examples.text: Elle porte un châle vert.
examples.trans: She's wearing a green shawl.

examples.text: Vous avez eu le châle pour Françoise Fabian?
examples.trans: Did you get the shawl for Françoise Fabian?

meanings.note: Plural takes -x: les châteaux.

examples.text: On veut les esclaves derrière le château, d'accord?
examples.trans: We want the slaves behind the chateau, okay?

examples.text: La duchesse habite dans un château.
examples.trans: The duchess lives in a castle.

meanings.note: faire un chèque = to write a cheque

examples.text: J'attends votre chèque cette semaine.
examples.trans: I expect your cheque this week.

examples.text: Il paie par chèque.
examples.trans: He pays by cheque.

examples.text: J'attends votre chèque cette semaine, avec dix pour cent de plus.
examples.trans: I expect your cheque this week, with ten percent extra.

meanings.note: An affectionate form of address; chérie for a woman.
For a beloved person or thing.

examples.text: Ça va, chérie?
examples.trans: All right, darling?

examples.text: Mon chéri, tu viens?
examples.trans: Darling, are you coming?

examples.text: Ça va, chérie? Tu es en retard.
examples.trans: All right, darling? You're late.

meanings.note: Ma chérie = my dear, darling. Feminine noun ('la chérie', plural 'les chéries') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'darling'.

examples.text: Oui, ma chérie?
examples.trans: Yes, my dear?

examples.text: Bonjour, ma petite chérie.
examples.trans: Hello, my darling.

examples.text: Oui, ma chérie? Qu'est-ce qui ne va pas?
examples.trans: Yes, my dear? What is wrong?

meanings.note: Chêne massif = solid oak.

examples.text: Du chêne massif, quatre-vingts ans d'âge. Pas une seule fuite.
examples.trans: Solid oak, eighty years old. Not a single leak.

examples.text: Voici le chêne sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the oak, oakwood on the table.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le ciel', plural 'les cieux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'firmament'.

examples.text: Le ciel est tout bleu.
examples.trans: The sky is completely blue.

examples.text: Regardez ces lanternes dorées sous le ciel du soir, comme c'est paisible!
