examples.trans: Look at those golden lanterns against the evening sky, how peaceful!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cigarette', plural 'les cigarettes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cigarette'.

examples.text: Tu fumes une cigarette maintenant?
examples.trans: Do you smoke a cigarette now?

examples.text: Elle allume une cigarette.
examples.trans: She lights a cigarette.

examples.text: Tu fumes une cigarette maintenant, Sofia?
examples.trans: Are you smoking a cigarette now, Sofia?

meanings.note: A cemetery or burial ground.

examples.text: J'ai couru dans le cimetière.
examples.trans: I ran in the cemetery.

examples.text: Le cimetière est grand.
examples.trans: The cemetery is big.

examples.text: Oui, j'ai couru dans le cimetière.
examples.trans: Yes, I ran in the cemetery.

meanings.note: The final q is pronounced: sɛ̃k.

examples.text: Je peux enlever cinq ans.
examples.trans: I can take off five years.

examples.text: Cinq minutes.
examples.trans: Five minutes.

examples.text: Regardez l'horloge: il est midi moins cinq!
examples.trans: Look at the clock: it is five to twelve!

meanings.note: Cinquante et un = fifty-one.

examples.text: Cinquante euros.
examples.trans: Fifty euros.

examples.text: Voici cinquante euros de la caisse. Rapportez le ticket!
examples.trans: Here is fifty euros from the cash box. Bring back the receipt!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'fifth'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: La cinquième vitesse.
examples.trans: The fifth gear.

examples.text: Attention, c'est la cinquième vitesse!
examples.trans: Watch out, that is fifth gear!

meanings.note: un cintre en bois = a wooden hanger

examples.text: Tu es une vraie actrice, pas un cintre.
examples.trans: You are a real actress, not a coat hanger.

examples.text: Accrocher un manteau sur un cintre.
examples.trans: To hang a coat on a hanger.

examples.text: J'ai toujours adoré le cinéma.
examples.trans: I've always loved films.

examples.text: On va au cinéma?
examples.trans: Shall we go to the cinema?

meanings.note: Road traffic in town.

examples.text: Laissez-lui quelques minutes, Monsieur Antoine. La circulation en ville à midi est toujours lente.
examples.trans: Give him a few minutes, Mr Antoine. City traffic at noon is always slow.

examples.text: Voici la circulation sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the traffic on the table.

meanings.note: *Faire circuler l'air* ('to keep the air moving / create airflow') is the standard expression for ventilating a room.

examples.text: Ouvrez deux fenêtres pour faire circuler l'air frais.
examples.trans: Open two windows to let fresh air circulate.

examples.text: On circule facilement entre les quatre petites tables.
examples.trans: People can move easily between the four small tables.

meanings.note: Beeswax, sealing wax ('sceau de cire'), or furniture polish.

examples.text: L'escalier en chêne sent bon la cire d'abeille.
examples.trans: The oak staircase smells wonderfully of beeswax.

examples.text: Un cachet de cire rouge ferme encore l'enveloppe.
examples.trans: A red wax seal still closes the envelope.

meanings.note: Past participle *ciré(e)* describes gleaming polished shoes (*des chaussures cirées*) or waxed parquet.

examples.text: Il cire ses chaussures noires tous les dimanches soir.
examples.trans: He polishes his black shoes every Sunday evening.

examples.text: L'escalier en bois ciré brille sous la lampe.
examples.trans: The waxed wooden staircase gleams under the lamp.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le cirque', plural 'les cirques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'circus'.

examples.text: Un spectacle de cirque.
examples.trans: A circus show.

examples.text: Aller au cirque.
examples.trans: To go to the circus.

examples.text: J'ai organisé des spectacles de cirque.
examples.trans: I organized circus performances.

meanings.note: Je cite = I quote.

examples.text: Je cite: pas de petites filles comme vous.
examples.trans: I quote: no little girls like you.

examples.text: Il cite un grand auteur.
examples.trans: He quotes a great author.

meanings.note: Au citron = made with lemon.

examples.text: Son grand-père coupait du gâteau tiède au citron avec du sucre glace dessus!
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with icing sugar on top!

examples.text: Oh! Le glaçage jaune au citron! On se battait pour la part du coin chaque vendredi!
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze! We fought over the corner piece every Friday!

examples.text: Six citrons jaunes attendent dans mon panier en ce moment: ma cuisine attendait ce vendredi!
examples.trans: Six yellow lemons are waiting in my basket right now: my kitchen was waiting for this Friday!

meanings.note: French forms most fruit-tree names by adding masculine -ier to the fruit: citron -> citronnier, pomme -> pommier, cerise -> cerisier.

examples.text: Le citronnier en pot passe l'hiver à l'abri du gel.
examples.trans: The potted lemon tree spends the winter sheltered from frost.

examples.text: Nous avons placé le citronnier près de la fontaine.
examples.trans: We put the lemon tree near the fountain.

meanings.en: civil, relating to citizens or civil law
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'civil'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: La déclaration à l'état civil.
examples.trans: The registration with the civil registry.

examples.text: Il porte des vêtements civils.
examples.trans: He wears civilian clothes.

examples.text: L'officier d'état civil vient d'arriver.
examples.trans: The civil registrar has just arrived.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'civilized'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Nous sommes civilisés.
examples.trans: We are civilized.

examples.text: Un comportement civilisé.
examples.trans: Civilized behavior.

examples.text: Pas du tout, nous sommes civilisés.
examples.trans: Not at all, we are civilized.

meanings.note: Une couleur plus claire. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'clear'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est clair.
examples.trans: It's clear.

examples.text: Cette couleur est plus claire.
examples.trans: This colour is lighter.

examples.text: Le vieux bureau clair sous les toits... suivez-moi, vite!
examples.trans: The old bright attic study... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Distinctly, plainly, without ambiguity.

examples.text: On voit clairement le clocher depuis la fenêtre du haut.
examples.trans: You can clearly see the bell tower from the upstairs window.

examples.text: Expliquez-moi clairement par où nous devons passer.
examples.trans: Explain clearly to me which way we should go.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to snap'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'claqué').

examples.text: On ne meurt pas en claquant des doigts.
examples.trans: One does not die at the snap of a finger.

examples.text: La porte a claqué violemment.
examples.trans: The door slammed violently.

meanings.en: to clarify, to clear up, to explain
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to clarify'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'clarifié').

examples.text: Clarifier les choses.
examples.trans: To clarify things.

examples.text: Clarifier une situation.
examples.trans: To clear up a situation.

examples.text: Tu devrais peut-être clarifier les choses avec lui.
examples.trans: You should maybe clarify things with him.

meanings.note: Avec classe = with style.
Informal invariable adjective use.

examples.text: Elle a beaucoup de classe.
examples.trans: She has a lot of class.

examples.text: La classe est finie.
examples.trans: Class is over.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le classement', plural 'les classements') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ranking'.

examples.text: On est au premier rang du classement.
examples.trans: We are in first place in the ranking.

examples.text: Consulter le classement annuel.
examples.trans: To consult the annual ranking.

examples.text: Pardon? Qui a décidé ce classement?
examples.trans: Excuse me? Who decided this ranking?

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: C'est une robe classique.
examples.trans: It is a classic dress.

examples.text: Cette robe classique est plutôt ennuyeuse.
examples.trans: This classic dress is rather boring.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'claustrophobic'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je suis extrêmement claustrophobe!
examples.trans: I am extremely claustrophobic!

examples.text: Il se sent claustrophobe dans les petits espaces.
examples.trans: He feels claustrophobic in small spaces.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeic masculine noun; faire clic means 'to click' (of a lock, latch, or light switch).

examples.text: Tournez la clé jusqu'au petit clic de la serrure.
examples.trans: Turn the key until the lock gives a little click.

examples.text: Un seul clic suffit pour allumer la lampe du salon.
examples.trans: A single click is enough to turn on the lounge lamp.

examples.text: Ce sont seulement des clichés.
examples.trans: Those are only clichés.

examples.text: Éviter les clichés.
examples.trans: To avoid clichés.

examples.text: Ce sont seulement des clichés qui m'énervent.
examples.trans: Those are only cliches that annoy me.

meanings.note: Feminine: cliente.

examples.text: Avec moi, toujours! Garde le vous poli pour les clients.
examples.trans: With me, always! Save the polite 'you' for the guests.

examples.text: La cliente de la chambre quatre reste toute la semaine. Tout doit être parfait!
examples.trans: The guest in room four is staying all week. Everything must be perfect!

examples.text: Huit clients affamés descendent à sept heures et demie!
examples.trans: Eight hungry guests come down at half past seven!

examples.text: Elle ne perd pas de clientèle.
examples.trans: She doesn't lose any customers.

examples.text: Le salon a une bonne clientèle.
examples.trans: The salon has a good clientele.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le clignotant', plural 'les clignotants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'turn signal'.

examples.text: Mettre le clignotant.
examples.trans: To put the turn signal on.

examples.text: N'oubliez pas le clignotant.
examples.trans: Do not forget the turn signal.

examples.text: N'oubliez pas le clignotant!
examples.trans: Do not forget the turn signal!

meanings.en: to blink, flash intermittently (of an indicator light or lamp)
meanings.note: Used for indicator lights on phones, dashboards, and street signs (le voyant clignote).

examples.text: Le petit voyant rouge du téléphone clignote sur le comptoir.
examples.trans: The phone's little red indicator light is blinking on the counter.

examples.text: Une ampoule fatiguée commence souvent par clignoter.
examples.trans: A worn-out bulb often starts by flickering.

examples.text: La clinique est à Paris.
examples.trans: The clinic is in Paris.

examples.text: Je vais à la clinique demain.
examples.trans: I'm going to the clinic tomorrow.

meanings.note: Gate bell or church bell.

examples.text: C'était quoi, cette cloche? Quelqu'un a sonné deux fois!
examples.trans: What was that bell? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: Ne dites rien à personne! Maintenant, un grand sourire quand la cloche sonne.
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Now, a big smile when the bell rings.

examples.text: Très généreux! Vous avez entendu la cloche du portail en bas?
examples.trans: Very generous! Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?

meanings.note: Church tower that rings the hours.

examples.text: Écoutez... le clocher au bout de la rue commence à sonner les douze coups de midi!
examples.trans: Listen... the church bell tower down the street is starting to strike the twelve chimes of noon!

examples.text: Voici le clocher sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the bell tower, steeple on the table.

meanings.en: small bell (on a shop door or courtyard gate)
meanings.note: Diminutive of cloche ('bell').

examples.text: La clochette de la porte tinte à chaque visiteur.
examples.trans: The door bell tinkles for every visitor.

examples.text: J'entends la clochette du portail depuis la cuisine.
examples.trans: I can hear the gate bell from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Interior dividing wall.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé les chaises... et derrière une vieille cloison en brique, j'ai trouvé ceci.
examples.trans: I found the chairs... and behind an old brick partition, I found this.

examples.text: Voici la cloison sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the partition wall on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la clope', plural 'les clopes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cigarette'.

examples.text: J'ai taxé une clope à l'entrée.
examples.trans: I bummed a smoke at the entrance.

examples.text: Tu as une clope pour moi?
examples.trans: Do you have a cigarette for me?

examples.text: J'ai taxé une clope pour déstresser.
examples.trans: I bummed a smoke to de-stress.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le clown', plural 'les clowns') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'clown'.

examples.text: Quel clown, j'y ai cru!
examples.trans: What a clown, I believed it!

examples.text: Quel clown, j'y ai presque cru!
examples.trans: What a clown, I almost believed it!

meanings.note: Un club de jazz.

examples.text: Au club de jazz où il jouait.
examples.trans: At the jazz club where he was playing.

examples.text: Un club de sport.
examples.trans: A sports club.

examples.text: C'était à New York, au club de jazz où il jouait.
examples.trans: It was in New York, at the jazz club where he was playing.

meanings.en: fermer à clé = to lock (with a key)

examples.text: Il n'y a pas de clé.
examples.trans: There is no key.

examples.text: J'ai perdu mes clés.
examples.trans: I lost my keys.

examples.text: Bonjour! Excusez-moi, la porte est fermée à clé?
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

meanings.note: Garden fence or enclosure wall; formal closing of an event or account.

examples.text: Un rosier grimpant couvre toute la clôture en bois.
examples.trans: A climbing rosebush covers the entire wooden fence.

examples.text: Le chat a sauté par-dessus la clôture du jardin.
examples.trans: The cat jumped right over the garden fence.

meanings.note: Describes something amusing because of its oddness or incongruity.

examples.text: C'est cocasse, quand même!
examples.trans: It's funny, all the same!

examples.text: Une situation cocasse.
examples.trans: An oddly funny situation.

meanings.note: Final x is pronounced s.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas le coccyx.
examples.trans: It isn't the tailbone.

examples.text: Tu as de la chance que ce ne soit pas le coccyx. C'est horrible.
examples.trans: You're lucky it isn't the tailbone. That's horrible.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le cocktail', plural 'les cocktails') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cocktail'.

examples.text: Elle commande un cocktail.
examples.trans: She orders a cocktail.

examples.text: Veuillez annuler ce bar à cocktails.
examples.trans: Please cancel this cocktail bar.

meanings.note: Often in compound phrase. Feminine noun ('la coco', plural 'les cocos') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'coconut'.

examples.text: Il est allergique à la noix de coco.
examples.trans: He is allergic to coconut.

examples.text: Du lait de coco.
examples.trans: Coconut milk.

examples.text: Et il est allergique à la noix de coco.
examples.trans: And he is allergic to coconut.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le code', plural 'les codes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'access code'.

examples.text: Quel est le code de l'immeuble?
examples.trans: What is the building door code?

examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu veux dire par mon code?
examples.trans: What do you mean by my door code?

examples.text: Ce sont des codes très différents.
examples.trans: These are very different codes.

meanings.note: Wooden chest or safe.

examples.text: Un petit coffre en bois de cèdre? Je n'ai jamais vu cette boîte en quinze ans!
examples.trans: A small cedarwood chest? I have never seen that box in fifteen years!

examples.text: Écoutez quand je penche le coffre: un objet en métal vient de glisser dedans.
examples.trans: Listen when I tilt the chest: a metal object just slid inside.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Attention dans le virage, ne cognez pas le mur!
examples.trans: Careful on the turn, do not bump the wall!

examples.text: C'est facile à cogner ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to bump, knock, bang together.

coiffer.gloss: to style hair, to dress hair

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to style hair'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'coiffé').

examples.text: La maquilleuse finit de coiffer l'actrice avant la scène.
examples.trans: The make-up artist finishes styling the actress's hair before the scene.

examples.text: Il prend toujours dix minutes pour se coiffer le matin.
examples.trans: He always takes ten minutes to do his hair in the morning.

examples.text: Qui coiffe cette pauvre actrice?
examples.trans: Who styles this poor actress's hair?

meanings.note: feminine: coiffeuse; aller chez le coiffeur

examples.text: Toujours un coiffeur différent.
examples.trans: Always a different hairdresser.

examples.text: Je vais chez le coiffeur.
examples.trans: I'm going to the hairdresser's.

examples.text: Si. Toujours un coiffeur différent.
examples.trans: Yes, you do. Always a different hairdresser.

meanings.note: un salon de coiffure = a hair salon
Une jolie coiffure. Feminine noun ('la coiffure', plural 'les coiffures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hairstyle'.

examples.text: Ça va faire du bruit dans le salon de coiffure de ma mère!
examples.trans: That's going to cause a stir in my mother's hair salon!

examples.text: Elle a changé de coiffure.
examples.trans: She changed her hairstyle.

examples.text: Les agents ne s'occupent pas des coiffures.
examples.trans: Agents do not deal with hairstyles.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le coin', plural 'les coins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'corner'.

examples.text: J'ai besoin d'un coin tranquille.
examples.trans: I need a quiet corner.

examples.text: Faites beaucoup de parts du coin, ma chère!
examples.trans: Make plenty of corner pieces, my dear!

coincer.gloss: to jam, to catch, to trap

meanings.en: to jam, to catch, to get stuck
meanings.note: Takes ç before a/o: nous coinçons. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to jam'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'coincé').

examples.text: J'ai coincé la portière.
examples.trans: I jammed the car door.

examples.text: La porte est coincée.
examples.trans: The door is stuck.

examples.text: Quand je suis arrivée au centre d'examen, j'ai coincé la portière sur la main de l'examinateur.
examples.trans: When I arrived at the test center, I caught the car door on the examiner's hand.

meanings.note: Invariable in the plural: un colis, des colis (the final -s is silent).

examples.text: Le facteur a déposé un petit colis pour la chambre quatre.
examples.trans: The postman dropped off a small parcel for Room 4.

examples.text: Votre colis vous attend derrière le comptoir de la réception.
examples.trans: Your package is waiting for you behind the front desk.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le collaborateur', plural 'les collaborateurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'colleague'.

examples.text: Des collaborateurs préparent leur départ.
examples.trans: Associates are preparing their departure.

examples.text: Des collaborateurs préparent un départ secret.
examples.trans: Collaborators are preparing a secret departure.

meanings.note: From *coller* ('to stick'); describes wet paint, honey, or dough that still sticks to the fingers.

examples.text: Ne touchez pas le volet: la peinture est encore collante.
examples.trans: Don't touch the shutter: the paint is still tacky.

examples.text: Si la pâte est trop collante, ajoutez un peu de farine.
examples.trans: If the dough is too sticky, add a little flour.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (*de la colle à bois*, 'wood glue').

examples.text: Une goutte de colle à bois suffit pour fixer la pièce.
examples.trans: A drop of wood glue is enough to secure the piece.

examples.text: Attendez une heure que la colle soit bien sèche.
examples.trans: Wait an hour until the glue is completely dry.

meanings.note: un suicide collectif = a collective suicide

examples.text: Un suicide collectif.
examples.trans: A collective suicide.

examples.text: D'abord, on a pensé à un suicide collectif... Enfin, moi. Un suicide collectif tout seul.
examples.trans: First, we thought about a collective suicide... Well, I did. A collective suicide all by myself.

examples.text: La réussite chez ASK est toujours collective.
examples.trans: Success at ASK is always collective.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Il y a une petite serrure devant, et regardez collée en dessous: une vieille clé en laiton!
examples.trans: There is a tiny lock on the front, and look taped underneath: an old brass key!

examples.text: C'est facile à coller ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to stick, tape, glue together.

meanings.note: Smaller and gentler than *une montagne* ('mountain'); Lyon itself is famous for its two hills (*Fourvière* and *la Croix-Rousse*).

examples.text: On voit les toits rouges depuis le haut de la colline.
examples.trans: You can see the red roofs from the top of the hill.

examples.text: Le sentier monte doucement sur la petite colline verte.
examples.trans: The path climbs gently up the small green hill.

meanings.note: Can refer to a man or a woman: un collègue, une collègue.

examples.text: C'est ma collègue.
examples.trans: She's my colleague.

examples.text: Mon collègue est ici.
examples.trans: My colleague is here.

colonne.gloss: column (of a table, page, or building)

meanings.en: column (in a table, ledger, newspaper, or architecture)
meanings.note: Used both for architectural pillars and for vertical columns of figures or dates on a page.

examples.text: Écrivez le total en bas de la deuxième colonne.
examples.trans: Write the total at the bottom of the second column.

examples.text: Sans ses lunettes, il a lu la mauvaise colonne du tarif.
examples.trans: Without his glasses, he read the wrong column of the price list.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'colossal'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une somme absolument colossale.
examples.trans: An absolutely colossal sum.

examples.text: Un travail colossal.
examples.trans: A colossal amount of work.

examples.text: C'est une somme absolument colossale, Hicham!
examples.trans: That is an absolutely colossal sum, Hicham!

meanings.note: Être en colère = to be angry.

examples.text: Il est très en colère.
examples.trans: He's very angry.

examples.text: Parce que j'avais peur que tu sois encore en colère.
examples.trans: Because I was afraid you were still angry.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le combat', plural 'les combats') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fight'.

examples.text: Le combat commence.
examples.trans: The battle begins.

examples.text: C'est parti pour le combat!
examples.trans: Here we go for the fight!

examples.text: Je ne lâcherai pas le combat!
examples.trans: I will not give up the fight!

meanings.note: Irregular third-group French verb inherited from core Latin roots, used across registers for 'to fight'.

examples.text: Nous devons combattre cette injustice.
examples.trans: We must fight this injustice.

examples.text: Je refuse de céder sans combattre.
examples.trans: I refuse to give up without fighting.

examples.text: Elle combat la cruauté des abattoirs.
examples.trans: She fights slaughterhouse cruelty.

meanings.note: Tu sais combien.
Tu sais combien.

examples.text: C'est combien?
examples.trans: How much is it?

examples.text: Nadia, combien de brioches à la cannelle et de gâteaux au citron votre four peut cuire chaque matin?
examples.trans: Nadia, how many cinnamon rolls and lemon cakes can your oven bake each morning?

meanings.en: coming (used in the loan expression coming-out)
meanings.note: borrowed from English

examples.text: Il a fait son coming out.
examples.trans: He came out publicly.

examples.text: C'est un coming out médiatique.
examples.trans: It is a public coming-out.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.text: C'est une scène comique.
examples.trans: It is a comedic scene.

examples.text: Allons plutôt dans un club comique.
examples.trans: Let us go instead to a comedy club.

examples.text: J'ai complètement raté ma carrière comique!
examples.trans: I have completely missed out on my comedic career!

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'committee, board'.

examples.text: Le comité de sélection.
examples.trans: The selection committee.

examples.text: Réunion du comité.
examples.trans: Committee meeting.

examples.text: Avez-vous envoyé une version édulcorée au comité?
examples.trans: Did you send a toned-down version to the committee?

meanings.note: Customer order in a café, bakery, or bookshop; control lever or command.

examples.text: La libraire a mis ma commande de côté près de la caisse.
examples.trans: The bookseller set my order aside near the register.

examples.text: La commande de farine fraîche arrive chaque mardi matin.
examples.trans: The fresh flour order arrives every Tuesday morning.

meanings.note: Authority or leadership ('prendre le commandement' = take command); precept.

examples.text: Elle prend le commandement des opérations avec le sourire.
examples.trans: She takes command of the operation with a smile.

examples.text: Sous son commandement, l'équipe travaille dans le calme.
examples.trans: Under her leadership, the team works calmly.

meanings.en: to order (from a shop, supplier, or café menu)
meanings.note: Everyday verb for placing an order: commander par téléphone ('order by phone'), commander un café.

examples.text: Étienne a commandé des chaises pliantes pour la terrasse.
examples.trans: Étienne ordered folding chairs for the terrace.

examples.text: Nous commandons toujours notre farine au moulin voisin.
examples.trans: We always order our flour from the neighbouring mill.

meanings.note: Comparison: comme un rêve.
Conjunction.

examples.text: C'est comme un rêve.
examples.trans: It's like a dream.

examples.text: Comme tu veux.
examples.trans: As you like.

meanings.note: commencer + noun, or commencer à + infinitive

examples.text: Tu peux commencer maintenant?
examples.trans: Can you start now?

examples.text: Le film commence.
examples.trans: The film is starting.

meanings.note: Comment ça va?.
Informal.

examples.text: Comment tu t'appelles?
examples.trans: What's your name?

examples.text: Comment était votre voyage en train?
examples.trans: How was your train trip?

meanings.note: Pas de commentaire = no comment.

examples.text: Pas de commentaire.
examples.trans: No comment.

examples.text: Merci pour ton commentaire.
examples.trans: Thanks for your comment.

meanings.note: Les petits commerces.
Les petits commerces.

examples.text: On n'est pas dans le commerce!
examples.trans: We're not in trade!

examples.text: Elle travaille dans le commerce.
examples.trans: She works in business.

examples.text: On n'est pas dans le commerce, Gabriel! Pas question, on doit trouver une solution.
examples.trans: We're not in trade, Gabriel! No way, we have to find a solution.

meanings.note: Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.text: Un échec commercial.
examples.trans: A commercial failure.

examples.text: Des bureaux commerciaux?! Transformer notre hôtel et ma cuisine en bureaux gris?!
examples.trans: Commercial offices?! Turn our hotel and my kitchen into grey offices?!

meanings.en: to commit, to make (a serious error)
meanings.note: Commettre une erreur. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Core French verb meaning 'to commit, to make (a mistake)'.

examples.text: J'ai commis une grave erreur il y a vingt-quatre ans.
examples.trans: I made a serious mistake twenty-four years ago.

examples.text: Il ne faut pas commettre d'erreur.
examples.trans: One must not make a mistake.

examples.text: Tu as commis une grave erreur.
examples.trans: You made a serious mistake.

meanings.note: Commission de financement. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'committee, commission'.

examples.text: La commission se réunit demain.
examples.trans: The committee meets tomorrow.

examples.text: Une commission d'experts.
examples.trans: A commission of experts.

meanings.note: Shared; en commun means in common.

examples.trans: We have friends in common.

examples.trans: It's a common name.

examples.trans: It's Gabor's idea. You and Line have nothing in common.

meanings.note: La communication interne. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'communication, messaging'.

examples.text: La communication, sans aucune hésitation.
examples.trans: Communication, without any hesitation.

examples.text: La communication est très importante.
examples.trans: Communication is very important.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la compagne', plural 'les compagnes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'female companion'.

examples.trans: Is everything going well with your partner?

examples.trans: His partner is charming.

examples.trans: It is noted. Is everything going well with your partner?

examples.trans: The insurance companies are investigating.

meanings.note: comparer avec / à = to compare with / to

examples.trans: We were supposed to compare our lists of first names.

meanings.note: Hôtel complet, vol complet. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.trans: Everything is fully booked today.

examples.text: C'est complet.
examples.trans: It is full.

meanings.note: Une situation complexe. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.trans: The situation is complex.

examples.trans: It is a complex problem.

examples.trans: Give Léa my compliments on her warm brioches!

examples.trans: A compliment like that first thing in the morning always brightens the day.

meanings.note: Complimenter quelqu'un pour / sur quelque chose.

examples.text: Tous les voisins complimentent la boulangère pour ses tartes.
examples.trans: All the neighbors compliment the baker on her tarts.

examples.text: Il a même complimenté le nouveau menu clair.
examples.trans: He even praised the clear new menu.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to make difficult'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'compliqué').

examples.trans: Do not complicate things.

examples.trans: Sofia, do not complicate things.

examples.trans: The contract is complicated.

examples.trans: Is it a conspiracy or what?

examples.trans: There is a plot against him.

examples.trans: That is a fine conspiracy theory.

examples.text: Tu as complètement perdu la tête!
examples.trans: You've completely lost your mind!

examples.trans: It's completely crazy.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le comportement', plural 'les comportements') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'behavior'.

examples.trans: A strange behavior.

examples.trans: To watch one's behavior.

examples.trans: Your behavior yesterday was very embarrassing.

meanings.en: se comporter = to behave, to act
meanings.note: Se comporter bien / mal.
Non-reflexive.

examples.trans: When they want a part, they behave badly.

examples.text: Il se comporte bien.
examples.trans: He behaves well.

meanings.en: to compose (music, text); to dial (phone number)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to compose'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'composé').

examples.text: Elle compose la musique.
examples.trans: She composes the music.

examples.text: Composer un numéro.

examples.trans: I am dialling the number... Hello?

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of *un compositeur* (`-teur` -> `-trice`).

examples.trans: I make compost.

meanings.en: compote, stewed fruit purée (common snack for children in France)

examples.trans: Really? Sweetheart, do you want a fruit compote?

examples.text: Vous comprenez le français?
examples.trans: Do you understand French?

meanings.note: In a company.
In a company.

examples.trans: I work in accounts.

meanings.note: An account, including a bank account.

meanings.note: Faire ses comptes means work out one's finances.

examples.trans: I did my accounts.

examples.trans: My account is empty.

examples.text: Dix, onze, douze. Le compte est bon au centime près, merci!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last cent, thank you!

meanings.note: Compter sur quelqu'un.

meanings.en: compter sur = to count on, to rely on

examples.trans: People are counting on this film.

examples.text: Tu peux compter sur moi.
examples.trans: You can count on me.

meanings.note: Front counter in a hotel or café.

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the counter, boss.

meanings.note: Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.text: Il est bien moins compétent que vous.
examples.trans: He is much less competent than you.

examples.text: Il est surtout bien moins compétent.
examples.trans: He is above all much less competent.

meanings.note: En compétition = in competition. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'competition, contest'.

examples.text: La compétition officielle.
examples.trans: The official competition.

examples.trans: Is that Turkish film in the official competition?

meanings.note: Masculine: le comte.

examples.trans: But I can send you Sofia Leprince to play the role of the countess.

meanings.note: Un film comique / humoristique. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'comedy'.
faire la comédie = to put on a show / play up

examples.trans: It is a comedy.

examples.trans: Comedy is not necessarily funny.

examples.trans: The story was good. It is a comedy.

meanings.note: stage and screen; feminine: comédienne
Informal, figurative.

examples.text: Je suis comédienne.
examples.trans: I'm an actress.

examples.text: C'est un grand comédien.
examples.trans: He's a great actor.

meanings.en: se concentrer = to concentrate, to focus
meanings.note: Reflexive in everyday use. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to concentrate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'concentré').

examples.trans: I really have to focus.

examples.trans: Focus on your work.

examples.text: J'ai une scène avec JoeyStarr, je dois vraiment me concentrer.
examples.trans: I have a scene with JoeyStarr, I really have to focus.

meanings.note: Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard masculine noun meaning 'concept, idea'.

examples.text: Un concept moderne.
examples.trans: A modern concept.

examples.trans: Regarding Virginie, I would prefer that you take her back.

examples.text: Concernant ce dossier, tout est prêt.
examples.trans: Concerning this file, everything is ready.

examples.trans: It concerns Samuel and it's important.

examples.text: Cette question me concerne.

examples.trans: One last thing. It concerns Samuel and it's important.

examples.trans: We're going to the concert tonight.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'concession, compromise'.

examples.trans: I always refused to make concessions.

examples.trans: But she did not take any. In conclusion...

meanings.note: Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le confort', plural 'les conforts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'comfort'.

examples.trans: You are afraid to leave your comfort zone!

examples.trans: What kind of tip?

examples.text: Le consulat est fermé.
examples.trans: The consulate is closed.

examples.text: J'appelle du consulat.
examples.trans: I'm calling from the consulate.

meanings.note: Consulter quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to consult'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'consulté').

examples.text: Vous auriez dû nous consulter.
examples.trans: You should have consulted us.

examples.text: Consulter un médecin.
examples.trans: To consult a doctor.

examples.text: Vous auriez dû nous consulter avant.
examples.trans: You should have consulted us beforehand.

meanings.note: Prendre contact = to make contact. Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard masculine noun meaning 'contact, touch'.

examples.text: Je n'aime pas trop le contact.
examples.trans: I don't really like contact.

examples.text: Garder le contact.
examples.trans: To stay in touch.

examples.text: Je pourrais vous mettre en contact avec lui...
examples.trans: I could put you in touch with him...

contacter.gloss: to contact, to get in touch with

meanings.en: to contact, to reach out to, to get in touch with
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to contact'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'contacté').

examples.text: Il m'a contactée.
examples.trans: He contacted me.

examples.text: Contacter un client.
examples.trans: To contact a client.

examples.text: Un chasseur de têtes m'a contactée.
examples.trans: A headhunter contacted me.

meanings.en: to contaminate, to corrupt, to infect
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to contaminate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'contaminé').

examples.text: Ils t'ont contaminée.
examples.trans: They have contaminated you.

examples.text: Contaminer l'eau.
examples.trans: To contaminate the water.

examples.text: Ils t'ont contaminée avec ce régime!
examples.trans: They contaminated you with this diet!

meanings.note: Content de = pleased with / to.

examples.text: Je suis vraiment contente.
examples.trans: I'm really happy.

examples.text: Il est content de te voir.
examples.trans: He's glad to see you.

meanings.note: En continu = continuously, non-stop.

examples.text: Les deux pages forment une seule mélodie continue.
examples.trans: The two pages form a single continuous melody.

examples.text: On entend le murmure continu de la fontaine.
examples.trans: You can hear the continuous murmur of the fountain.

examples.text: Continuez comme ça, la scène est vraiment parfaite!
examples.trans: Keep going like that, the scene is truly perfect!

examples.text: Nous allons continuer la répétition après le déjeuner.
examples.trans: We will continue the rehearsal after lunch.

meanings.en: to contract, tighten; undergo labor contractions
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to contract'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'contracté').

examples.text: Ça contracte très fort.
examples.trans: It is contracting very strongly.

examples.text: Disons que ça contracte très fort!
examples.trans: Let us say the contractions are getting intense!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la contraction', plural 'les contractions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'uterine contraction'.

examples.text: J'ai une petite contraction.
examples.trans: I have a minor contraction.

examples.text: Aïe, j'ai une contraction assez douloureuse!
examples.trans: Ouch, I have a rather painful contraction!

examples.text: C'est juste une petite contraction passagère.
examples.trans: It is just a minor passing contraction.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la contradiction', plural 'les contradictions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'contradiction'.

examples.text: Elle assume ses contradictions.
examples.trans: She embraces her contradictions.

examples.text: Une femme doit assumer ses contradictions.
examples.trans: A woman must embrace her contradictions.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la contrainte', plural 'les contraintes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'constraint'.

examples.text: Ils souffrent des contraintes.
examples.trans: They suffer from restrictions.

examples.text: Ils réagissent aux contraintes de la société.
examples.trans: They react to society's constraints.

examples.text: Non, au contraire.
examples.trans: No, quite the opposite.

examples.text: C'est le contraire.
examples.trans: It's the opposite.

meanings.note: The difference between light and dark areas in an image, or more generally between two things.

examples.text: Le contraste est vraiment bon.
examples.trans: The contrast is really good.

examples.text: Quel contraste!
examples.trans: What a contrast!

examples.text: Vous avez peur du contraste d'âge?
examples.trans: Are you afraid of the age contrast?

meanings.note: signer un contrat = to sign a contract

examples.text: Je lis le contrat.
examples.trans: I'm reading the contract.

examples.text: Il signe un contrat.
examples.trans: He's signing a contract.

meanings.note: Against someone or something; se battre contre, fight against.

examples.text: Je suis contre.
examples.trans: I'm against it.

examples.text: Se battre contre le chagrin.
examples.trans: To fight against sorrow.

examples.text: Réglez votre réveil, Henri. Demain matin, on gagne contre l'eau froide!
examples.trans: Set your alarm, Henri. Tomorrow morning, we beat the cold water!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to counter'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'contré').

examples.text: Il faut contrer leur attaque.
examples.trans: We must counter their attack.

examples.text: Nous devons contrer les Américains avant lui.
examples.trans: We must counter the Americans before him.

meanings.note: Une liste de contrôle = a checklist (note false friend: contrôler usually means 'to check/inspect', not 'to control').

examples.text: Nous relisons la liste de contrôle avant la visite.
examples.trans: We reread the checklist before the inspection.

examples.text: Le contrôle des lampes et des sorties est terminé.
examples.trans: The check of the lamps and exits is finished.

meanings.note: Contrôler ses émotions. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to control'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'contrôlé').

examples.text: J'ai appris à contrôler mes émotions.
examples.trans: I learned to control my emotions.

examples.text: Contrôler la situation.
examples.trans: To control the situation.

examples.text: C'est comme ça que j'ai appris à contrôler mes émotions.
examples.trans: That is how I learned to control my emotions.

meanings.note: Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.text: Sois très convaincant au téléphone.
examples.trans: Be very convincing on the phone.

examples.text: Sois très attentif et très convaincant.
examples.trans: Be very attentive and very convincing.

examples.text: Espérons que le résultat soit convaincant.
examples.trans: Let us hope the result is convincing.

meanings.note: Convaincre quelqu'un de faire quelque chose means persuade someone to do something.

examples.text: Je vais la convaincre de revenir.
examples.trans: I'm going to persuade her to come back.

examples.text: Tu m'as convaincu.
examples.trans: You've convinced me.

examples.text: Je vais la convaincre de revenir. J'en suis capable.
examples.trans: I'm going to persuade her to come back. I can do it.

meanings.note: Une tenue convenable. Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.text: Je n'ai rien de convenable à me mettre.
examples.trans: I have nothing suitable to wear.

examples.text: C'est une proposition tout à fait convenable.
examples.trans: It is a perfectly suitable proposal.

meanings.note: convenir à quelqu'un = to suit someone

examples.text: Elle conviendrait bien pour ta comédie musicale.
examples.trans: She would suit your musical well.

examples.text: Cette heure me convient.
examples.trans: This time suits me.

examples.text: Il pense que les chansons ne conviennent pas.
examples.trans: He thinks that the songs are not suitable.

meanings.note: Comme convenu = as agreed. Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.text: Neuf heures pile, comme convenu.
examples.trans: Nine o'clock sharp, as agreed.

examples.text: C'est la date convenue.
examples.trans: It is the agreed date.

meanings.note: All French nouns ending in *-tion* are feminine.

examples.text: Une douce conversation anime le salon de thé l'après-midi.
examples.trans: Gentle conversation livens up the tearoom in the afternoon.

examples.text: Nous reprenons notre conversation autour d'un café chaud.
examples.trans: We pick up our conversation over a hot coffee.

meanings.note: A firm belief or principle; avoir des convictions means have principles.

examples.text: J'ai des convictions.
examples.trans: I have convictions.

examples.text: Elle parle avec conviction.
examples.trans: She speaks with conviction.

examples.text: J'ai des convictions, c'est tout.
examples.trans: I have convictions, that's all.

meanings.note: C'est très cool. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'cool'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: De toute façon, c'est très cool.
examples.trans: Anyway, it is very cool.

examples.text: Il est très cool.
examples.trans: He is very cool.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la coopération', plural 'les coopérations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cooperation'.

examples.text: Cette crèche parentale demande beaucoup de coopération.
examples.trans: This parent daycare requires a lot of cooperation.

examples.text: Travailler en étroite coopération.
examples.trans: To work in close cooperation.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le copain', plural 'les copains') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'boyfriend'.

examples.text: Son copain est là.
examples.trans: Her boyfriend is there.

examples.text: En plus, son copain me regarde bizarrement.
examples.trans: Plus, her boyfriend looks at me strangely.

meanings.note: Curled wood shaving ('copeaux de cèdre') or chocolate curl.

examples.text: L'atelier du menuisier est jonché de copeaux de bois blond.
examples.trans: The carpenter's workshop is strewn with pale wood shavings.

examples.text: Des copeaux de cèdre parfument le coffret ancien.
examples.trans: Cedar shavings scent the antique box.

meanings.en: copy (of a text, script, or film)

examples.text: On était les seuls à avoir une copie!
examples.trans: We were the only ones to have a copy!

examples.text: Une copie du scénario.
examples.trans: A copy of the script.

meanings.note: Une bonne copine = a good friend. Feminine noun ('la copine', plural 'les copines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'friend'.

examples.text: C'est ma copine.
examples.trans: She is my friend.

examples.text: Sortir avec des copines.
examples.trans: To go out with girlfriends.

examples.text: Je passe beaucoup de temps chez ma copine.
examples.trans: I spend a lot of time at my girlfriend's place.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la coproduction', plural 'les coproductions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'co-production'.

examples.text: Le deal de coproduction est fait.
examples.trans: The co-production deal is done.

examples.text: Oui, le deal de coproduction est fait.
examples.trans: Yes, the co-production deal is done.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'playful'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Des promenades coquines à Paris.
examples.trans: Playful walks in Paris.

examples.text: Ce livre propose des promenades très coquines!
examples.trans: This book suggests very playful strolls!

meanings.en: coral; coral-red (invariable as a color/variety modifier)
meanings.note: Les lentilles corail = split red lentils (corail stays invariable here).

examples.text: Les lentilles corail cuisent en quinze minutes.
examples.trans: Red lentils cook in fifteen minutes.

examples.text: Elle garde un bracelet couleur corail dans un tiroir.
examples.trans: She keeps a coral-colored bracelet in a drawer.

corde.gloss: string (of a piano or violin); rope

meanings.note: On a piano, most middle and high notes strike three steel *cordes* at once for a rich tone.

examples.text: Le petit marteau en feutre frappe trois cordes à la fois.
examples.trans: The small felt hammer strikes three strings at once.

examples.text: Il tend une corde dans le jardin pour faire sécher le linge.
examples.trans: He stretches a line in the garden to dry the laundry.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'cordial'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Oui, avec un mot très cordial.
examples.trans: Yes, with a very cordial note.

examples.text: Un accueil cordial de la part des voisins.
examples.trans: A cordial welcome from the neighbors.

meanings.en: cordially, warmly; formal sign-off in correspondence
meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Cordialement, Andréa.
examples.trans: Best regards, Andrea.

examples.text: Saluer cordialement.
examples.trans: To greet cordially.

examples.text: Cordialement, Hicham.
examples.trans: Cordially, Hicham.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le cordon', plural 'les cordons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'umbilical cord'.

examples.text: Clamper le cordon.
examples.trans: Clamping the cord.

examples.text: Donnez vos lacets pour le cordon!
examples.trans: Give your shoelaces for the cord!

meanings.note: le langage corporel = body language

examples.text: Le langage corporel est très important.
examples.trans: Body language is very important.

examples.text: L'expression corporelle.
examples.trans: Physical expression.

examples.text: Je vais lui parler de la PNL et du langage corporel.
examples.trans: I will talk to her about NLP and body language.

meanings.note: The final s is silent; singular and plural are written the same.

examples.text: Il protège son corps.
examples.trans: He protects his body.

examples.text: Le corps a besoin de repos.
examples.trans: The body needs rest.

meanings.en: corral, enclosure, cattle pen (figuratively: crowded bullpen)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le corral', plural 'les corrals') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'corral'.

examples.text: On dirait plutôt un corral d'avocats!
examples.trans: It looks more like a lawyers' corral!

examples.text: Les chevaux attendent dans le corral.
examples.trans: The horses wait in the corral.

meanings.note: g becomes ge before a and o: nous corrigeons

examples.text: Corrige l'âge, tout simplement.
examples.trans: Just correct the age.

examples.text: Elle corrige une erreur.
examples.trans: She corrects a mistake.

examples.text: Je n'ai pas pu la corriger.
examples.trans: I was not able to correct her.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le corset', plural 'les corsets') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'medical brace'.
Masculine noun ('le corset', plural 'les corsets') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'corset'.

examples.text: Elle doit porter un corset médical.
examples.trans: She must wear a medical brace.

examples.text: Ce corset maintient bien le dos.
examples.trans: This brace supports the back well.

examples.text: Elle porte un corset depuis quinze jours.
examples.trans: She has been wearing a brace for two weeks.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cortisone', plural 'les cortisones') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cortisone'.

examples.text: La cortisone n'a fait aucun effet.
examples.trans: The cortisone had no effect.

examples.text: Le médecin lui a prescrit de la cortisone.
examples.trans: The doctor prescribed her cortisone.

examples.text: La cortisone n'a donc fait aucun effet?
examples.trans: Did the cortisone have no effect then?

meanings.note: un film en costume = a costume drama / period film
Un film en costumes.

examples.text: Pour vérifier mes costumes.
examples.trans: To check my suits.

examples.text: Il porte un costume gris.
examples.trans: He's wearing a grey suit.

examples.text: Pour vérifier mes costumes et mes notes de frais. Bonne chance!
examples.trans: To check my suits and my expense claims. Good luck!

meanings.note: Cotton fiber, fabric, or rag paper ('papier coton').

examples.text: Les draps en coton blanc sèchent au soleil dans la cour.
examples.trans: The white cotton sheets are drying in the sun in the courtyard.

examples.text: L'aquarelle demande un papier coton bien épais.
examples.trans: Watercolor calls for nice thick cotton paper.

meanings.note: *Une première couche / une deuxième couche* is the standard term when painting wood or walls.

examples.text: Passez deux couches fines plutôt qu'une seule couche épaisse.
examples.trans: Apply two thin coats rather than one thick coat.

examples.text: La première couche de peinture verte sèche en trois heures.
examples.trans: The first coat of green paint dries in three hours.

coucher.gloss: to go to bed, to put to bed

meanings.en: to go to bed (reflexive se coucher)
meanings.note: Aller se coucher.
Coucher les enfants.

examples.text: Je vais aller me coucher.
examples.trans: I'm going to go to bed.

examples.text: Je crois que je vais aller me coucher. Bonne nuit.
examples.trans: I think I'm going to go to bed. Good night.

meanings.en: friendly wave, peekaboo ('faire coucou'); hi there
meanings.note: *Faire coucou (de la main)* means to wave hello to someone, especially through a window or from afar.

examples.text: Les enfants nous font coucou par la fenêtre du train.
examples.trans: The children wave at us through the train window.

examples.text: Elle fait un petit coucou au voisin depuis le balcon.
examples.trans: She gives a friendly wave to the neighbor from the balcony.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le coude', plural 'les coudes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'anatomical elbow'.

examples.text: Elle a mal au coude droit.
examples.trans: Her right elbow hurts.

examples.text: Regarde, je n'ai même plus de coudes!
examples.trans: Look, I do not even have elbows anymore!

examples.text: C'est rare qu'on te regarde les coudes.
examples.trans: People rarely look at your elbows.

meanings.note: In this scene the sound suggests abruptly finishing the character off.

examples.text: Couic! Plus un bruit.
examples.trans: Eek! Not another sound.

examples.text: Il n'a pas eu le temps de dire couic.
examples.trans: He did not even have time to squeak.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb conjugated with *avoir* (*l'eau a coulé sur le sol*, 'water dripped/ran onto the floor').

examples.text: De l'eau de pluie a coulé le long de la vieille vitre.
examples.trans: Rainwater trickled down the old windowpane.

examples.text: Laissez couler l'eau froide quelques secondes.
examples.trans: Let the cold water run for a few seconds.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (*une belle couleur*, *la couleur des volets*), unlike English/Latin gender guesses.

examples.text: Cette couleur douce s'accorde très bien avec la pierre ancienne.
examples.trans: This soft color goes very well with the old stone.

examples.text: La lumière du jour montre la vraie couleur de la peinture.
examples.trans: Daylight shows the true color of the paint.

meanings.note: Standard French word for an indoor hallway connecting rooms.

examples.text: La chambre six se trouve tout au bout du couloir.
examples.trans: Room six is right at the far end of the corridor.

examples.text: Merci de parler bas dans le couloir le soir.
examples.trans: Please speak quietly in the hallway in the evening.

meanings.en: un coup dur = a hard blow, bad news

examples.text: Un coup de téléphone.
examples.trans: A phone call.

examples.text: Et voilà la cloche du portail. Un coup franc.
examples.trans: There goes the gate bell. One firm ring.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').
Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Je me sens toujours très coupable.
examples.trans: I still feel very guilty.

examples.text: Il n'est pas coupable de cette erreur.
examples.trans: He is not guilty of this mistake.

examples.text: Faire le ménage, c'est un geste coupable.
examples.trans: Cleaning up, it is a guilty move.

meanings.note: Une coupe de champagne. Feminine noun ('la coupe', plural 'les coupes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'champagne flute'.
Feminine noun ('la coupe', plural 'les coupes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'champagne flute'.

examples.text: Tu veux une coupe?
examples.trans: Do you want a glass?

examples.text: Elle boit une coupe de champagne.
examples.trans: She drinks a glass of champagne.

examples.text: Il était en mode silencieux. Tu veux une coupe? On a sorti le champagne.
examples.trans: It was on silent mode. Do you want a glass? We brought out the champagne.

meanings.note: Slender blade used to slit envelopes or uncut book pages.

examples.text: Il ouvre son courrier du matin avec un coupe-papier en laiton.
examples.trans: He opens his morning mail with a brass letter opener.

examples.text: Le coupe-papier repose à côté de l'encrier sur le bureau.
examples.trans: The letter opener rests beside the inkwell on the desk.

examples.text: Coupez!
examples.trans: Cut!

examples.text: Je coupe le pain.
examples.trans: I am cutting the bread.

meanings.note: A couple or pair, grammatically singular even though it consists of two people.

examples.text: Un vieux couple.
examples.trans: An old couple.

examples.text: C'est un beau couple.
examples.trans: They're a lovely couple.

examples.text: Non, Étienne, le couple du sud est arrivé dans la chambre six il y a une heure.
examples.trans: No, Etienne, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la coupure', plural 'les coupures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'banknote'.
Feminine noun ('la coupure', plural 'les coupures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cut'.

examples.text: En petites coupures, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: In small bills, please.

examples.text: Une coupure de courant dans le quartier.
examples.trans: A power outage in the neighborhood.

examples.text: En petites coupures.
examples.trans: In small bills.

examples.text: Dans la cour.
examples.trans: In the courtyard.

examples.text: Seulement le tilleul de la cour et la pluie.
examples.trans: Only the linden tree in the courtyard and the rain.

meanings.note: Said to encourage someone.

meanings.en: bon courage!: good luck!, hang in there!

examples.text: Courage, c'est seulement ta première semaine!
examples.trans: Chin up, it's only your first week!

examples.text: Il faut du courage pour parler à son frère.
examples.trans: It takes courage to talk to your brother.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Il est très courageux.
examples.trans: He is very brave.

examples.text: Une décision courageuse.
examples.trans: A courageous decision.

examples.text: Tu es courageux, tu vas surmonter cette épreuve.
examples.trans: You are brave, you will overcome this trial.

meanings.en: être au courant = to know about it, to be in the loop

examples.text: Tout le bureau est au courant?
examples.trans: Does the whole office know?

examples.text: Tiens-moi au courant.
examples.trans: Keep me posted.

meanings.note: Run; past participle couru.

examples.text: J'ai couru dans le cimetière.
examples.trans: I ran in the cemetery.

examples.text: Il court vite.
examples.trans: He runs fast.

examples.text: Oh non! Tous les paquets se ressemblaient quand je courais!
examples.trans: Oh no! All the packets looked alike when I was running!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le courriel', plural 'les courriels') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'email'.

examples.text: Consultez vos courriels.
examples.trans: Check your emails.

examples.text: Consultez vos courriels pour notre négociation.
examples.trans: Check your emails for our negotiation.

examples.text: Je viens de lire tes courriels.
examples.trans: I have just read your emails.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le courrier', plural 'les courriers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mail'.

examples.text: Envoyer du courrier pour elle.
examples.trans: To send mail for her.

examples.text: Tout à l'heure, j'ai vu une deuxième page attachée derrière le courrier.
examples.trans: Earlier, I spotted a second page clipped behind the letter.

examples.text: Oui! Tout à l'heure, j'ai vu une deuxième page attachée derrière le courrier.
examples.trans: Yes! Earlier, I spotted a second page clipped behind the letter.

meanings.note: un cours d'équitation = a riding lesson

examples.text: J'ai besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: I need a little lesson.

examples.text: Dites-moi que je n'ai pas vingt-cinq ans de retard à mon cours!
examples.trans: Tell me I am not twenty-five years late for my lesson!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la course', plural 'les courses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'running'.
Feminine noun ('la course', plural 'les courses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'errand'.

examples.text: Elle court sur un tapis de course.
examples.trans: She runs on a treadmill.

examples.text: Belle course ce matin, coéquipière.
examples.trans: Good run this morning, partner.

examples.text: Trois minutes pour monter au troisième étage. Belle course ce matin, coéquipière.
examples.trans: Three minutes to reach the third floor. Good run this morning, partner.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le coursier', plural 'les coursiers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'courier'.

examples.text: Appeler un coursier.
examples.trans: Call a courier.

examples.text: Oui, je téléphone au coursier maintenant.
examples.trans: Yes, I am phoning the courier now.

examples.text: Bonsoir, je voudrais un coursier.
examples.trans: Good evening, I would like a courier.

meanings.en: short, brief in duration or length
meanings.note: Une courte pause. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'short'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Le voyage a été très court.
examples.trans: The trip was very short.

examples.text: Commencez par trois phrases courtes. Un: Bonjour Thibault, merci d'être venu.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences. One: Hello Thibault, thank you for coming.

meanings.note: Un court-métrage. Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'short film'.

examples.text: C'est un court-métrage sans argent.
examples.trans: It is a short film without money.

examples.text: Elle a joué dans un court-métrage.
examples.trans: She acted in a short film.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la courtisane', plural 'les courtisanes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'courtesan'.

examples.text: Une courtisane célèbre.
examples.trans: A famous courtesan.

examples.text: Les courtisanes d'autrefois.
examples.trans: The courtesans of the past.

examples.text: Les actrices ne sont pas des courtisanes!
examples.trans: Actresses are not courtesans!

meanings.note: Feminine: cousine. Masculine noun ('le cousin', plural 'les cousins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cousin'.

examples.text: Mon cousin Saïd.
examples.trans: My cousin Saïd.

examples.text: J'ai une idée. Mon cousin Saïd, c'est lui qui conduit dans le film.
examples.trans: I have an idea. My cousin Saïd, he's the one who drives in the film.

examples.text: Chez mon cousin, je l'ai ouverte et j'ai vu des partitions et un ruban rouge.
examples.trans: At my cousin's flat, I opened it and saw sheet music and a red ribbon.

meanings.note: Distinguished from *un oreiller* (bed pillow for sleeping), though both can prop up a sore foot.

examples.text: J'ai posé deux coussins verts sur le banc en bois.
examples.trans: I put two green cushions on the wooden bench.

examples.text: Ce coussin épais rend la chaise beaucoup plus confortable.
examples.trans: This thick cushion makes the chair much more comfortable.

meanings.note: Hand-sewn or stitched ('cousu main'); 'bouche cousue' = lips sealed.

examples.text: Ce vieux registre a un dos cousu très solide.
examples.trans: This old ledger has a very sturdy sewn spine.

examples.text: Promis, je ne dirai rien: bouche cousue!
examples.trans: I promise I won't say a word: my lips are sealed!

meanings.note: grandir dans un couvent = to grow up in a convent (final t is silent)

examples.text: Elle a grandi dans un couvent!
examples.trans: She grew up in a convent!

examples.text: Un vieux couvent au calme.
examples.trans: An old convent in a quiet spot.

related.gloss: to grow up in a convent (final t is silent)

meanings.note: Figurative.

meanings.en: to brood, to sit on eggs
meanings.note: Literal.

examples.text: On couve trop nos acteurs.
examples.trans: We coddle our actors too much.

examples.text: On couve trop nos acteurs en oubliant de vivre pour nous-mêmes.
examples.trans: We coddle our actors too much while forgetting to live for ourselves.

meanings.en: lid (of a pot, jar, chest, or piano)
meanings.note: Masculine noun covering pot lids, box lids, chest covers, and the hinged lid of a piano.

examples.text: Mettez le couvercle sur la casserole pour garder la vapeur.
examples.trans: Put the lid on the saucepan to keep the steam in.

examples.text: Henri relève doucement le couvercle en bois du piano.
examples.trans: Henri gently lifts the wooden lid of the piano.

couverture.gloss: cover (of a magazine or book); blanket

meanings.note: faire la couverture de = to be on the cover of

examples.text: La couverture du livre.
examples.trans: The cover of the book.

examples.text: J'ai une bonne couverture chaude, alors je suis très bien ce soir.
examples.trans: I have a good warm blanket, so I am very comfortable tonight.

meanings.en: to cover, protect; meet financial liability
meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire') meaning 'to cover'; essential in everyday spoken and professional French.

examples.text: L'assurance va couvrir les frais.
examples.trans: The insurance will cover the costs.

examples.text: L'assurance va couvrir l'interruption?
examples.trans: Will the insurance cover the shutdown?

examples.text: Leur assurance ne couvre pas ces frais?
examples.trans: Does their insurance not cover these costs?

meanings.note: Feminine: coéquipière.

examples.text: Trois minutes pour monter au troisième étage. Belle course ce matin, coéquipière.
examples.trans: Three minutes to reach the third floor. Good run this morning, partner.

examples.text: Voici le coéquipier sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the teammate, partner on the table.

meanings.note: coûter cher = to be expensive; coûter la vie à quelqu'un = to cost someone their life

examples.text: Elle peut vous coûter la vie!
examples.trans: She could cost you your life!

examples.text: Combien ça coûte?
examples.trans: How much does it cost?

meanings.note: À la craie means 'written in chalk', especially on café menu boards (un panneau / une ardoise à la craie).

examples.text: Nadia écrit le menu du jour à la craie sur l'ardoise.
examples.trans: Nadia writes today's menu in chalk on the slate board.

examples.text: Il reste un morceau de craie blanche près du comptoir.
examples.trans: There is a piece of white chalk left near the counter.

meanings.en: to fear, to be afraid of
meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to fear, to dread'.

examples.text: Ne craignez rien.
examples.trans: Fear nothing.

examples.text: Il craint le pire.
examples.trans: He fears the worst.

examples.text: Vous ne craignez pas une interdiction aux mineurs?
examples.trans: Are you not afraid of an age restriction?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la crainte', plural 'les craintes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fear'.
Feminine noun ('la crainte', plural 'les craintes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sans crainte: without fear'.

examples.text: Soyez sans crainte, tout va bien.
examples.trans: Have no fear, everything is fine.

examples.text: Dissiper ses craintes.
examples.trans: To dispel one's fears.

examples.text: Non, madame, soyez sans crainte.
examples.trans: No, madam, have no fear.

meanings.en: notch, courage; à cran = on edge
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le cran', plural 'les crans') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'notch'.

examples.text: Il est à cran aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: He is on edge today.

examples.text: C'est pour mon film À cran.
examples.trans: It is for my film A cran.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le craquement', plural 'les craquements') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'creaking'.

examples.text: Le craquement des feuilles perturbe la prise.
examples.trans: The crunching of leaves disrupts the take.

examples.text: Ce craquement gâche toute l'émotion.
examples.trans: This crunching ruins all the emotion.

craquer.gloss: to snap, to lose it; to crack

meanings.note: Informal.

meanings.en: craquer pour quelqu'un = to fall for someone
meanings.note: Informal.

examples.text: J'ai complètement craqué.
examples.trans: I completely lost it.

examples.text: La branche a craqué.
examples.trans: The branch cracked.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cravate', plural 'les cravates') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tie'.

examples.text: Une cravate en soie.
examples.trans: A silk tie.

examples.text: Mon Dieu! Pas une goutte sur la table, heureusement... tout est sur ma cravate!
examples.trans: Oh dear! Not a drop on the table, thankfully... all of it is on my tie!

meanings.note: Au crayon = in pencil (false friend: not 'crayon').

examples.text: Dans le tiroir. Ici, on utilise ce grand cahier en papier et un crayon.
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper notebook and a pencil.

examples.text: Regarde sous les roues: ton prénom et le mien sont toujours écrits au crayon.
examples.trans: Look underneath the wheels: your first name and mine are still written in pencil.

examples.text: Regardez où Antoine pointe son crayon, Étienne!
examples.trans: Look where Antoine is pointing his pencil, Etienne!

examples.text: Je fais creuser une piscine.
examples.trans: I am having a pool dug.

examples.text: Le chien creuse un trou.
examples.trans: The dog is digging a hole.

meanings.note: Adverbially invariable in sonner creux ('ring/sound hollow').

examples.text: Cette vieille pierre du jardin sonne creux sous le pied.
examples.trans: This old garden stone sounds hollow underfoot.

examples.text: Servez la soupe chaude dans les assiettes creuses.
examples.trans: Serve the hot soup in the soup bowls.

meanings.note: crever de faim = to starve to death

examples.text: Si vous réduisez mon salaire, je vais crever de faim!
examples.trans: If you reduce my salary, I'll starve!

examples.text: Le pneu a crevé.
examples.trans: The tire burst.

examples.text: Hors de question, si vous réduisez le mien, je vais crever de faim!
examples.trans: Out of the question, if you reduce mine, I will starve!

meanings.note: Very common informal adjective.
Un pneu crevé.

examples.text: Je suis crevée ce soir.
examples.trans: I'm exhausted tonight.

examples.text: Oui, tu as raison. Je suis crevée.
examples.trans: Yes, you're right. I'm exhausted.

examples.text: J'ai entendu crier à propos de beurre depuis le fond de la cour.
examples.trans: I heard shouting about butter from the back of the courtyard.

examples.text: Alors? Il a crié? Il a demandé un remboursement?
examples.trans: Well? Did he shout? Did he ask for a refund?

examples.text: Ne crie pas.
examples.trans: Don't shout.

meanings.note: Crise évitée! = Crisis averted!

examples.text: Grâce à ton étiquette rouge, la crise est évitée.
examples.trans: Thanks to your red label, the crisis is averted.

examples.text: Il garde son calme même en pleine crise.
examples.trans: He keeps his cool even in the middle of a crisis.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la critique', plural 'les critiques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'criticism'.

examples.text: La Semaine de la Critique.
examples.trans: The Critics' Week.

examples.text: Une bonne critique.
examples.trans: A good review.

examples.text: Non, ça c'est la Semaine de la Critique.
examples.trans: No, that is the Critics' Week.

meanings.note: Critiquer mon agent. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to criticize'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'critiqué').

examples.text: Si tu veux critiquer mon agent, laisse tomber.
examples.trans: If you want to criticize my agent, drop it.

examples.text: Il critique tout le monde.
examples.trans: He criticizes everyone.

examples.text: Il prétend que je le critique.
examples.trans: He claims that I criticize him.

meanings.note: From *croc* ('fang/hook'); on traditional French wooden shutters, *un crochet en fer* holds the open shutter flat against the wall.

examples.text: Fixez le crochet en fer pour que le volet ne claque pas au vent.
examples.trans: Fasten the iron hook so the shutter doesn't bang in the wind.

examples.text: Mettez votre tablier sur le crochet derrière la porte.
examples.trans: Hang your apron on the hook behind the door.

meanings.note: Je ne crois pas = I don't think so.
Je ne crois pas = I don't think so.

examples.text: Je crois que oui.
examples.trans: I think so.

examples.text: Tu me crois?
examples.trans: Do you believe me?

croiser.gloss: to cross paths with; to fold

meanings.en: to cross paths with; to fold
meanings.note: To pass or run into someone on the street; to cross or fold ('croiser les bras').

examples.text: J'ai croisé le boulanger sur la place ce matin.
examples.trans: I ran into the baker on the square this morning.

examples.text: Deux ruelles anciennes se croisent derrière l'église.
examples.trans: Two old lanes intersect behind the church.

meanings.note: Croissant de lune = crescent moon. Masculine noun ('le croissant', plural 'les croissants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'croissant'.

examples.text: Apporter des croissants.
examples.trans: To bring croissants.

examples.text: Un café et un croissant.
examples.trans: A coffee and a croissant.

examples.text: Je peux lui apporter des croissants!
examples.trans: I can bring him croissants!

meanings.note: Quick freehand drawing or rough sketch ('carnet de croquis' = sketchbook).

examples.text: Il a fait un croquis rapide du porche en pierre.
examples.trans: He made a quick sketch of the stone archway.

examples.text: Son carnet est rempli de croquis au fusain.
examples.trans: His notebook is filled with charcoal sketches.

meanings.note: The quintessential praise for fresh French bread (*du pain chaud et croustillant*).

examples.text: La croûte du pain est bien dorée et croustillante.
examples.trans: The bread crust is nicely golden and crusty.

examples.text: Servez la soupe chaude avec deux tranches de pain croustillant.
examples.trans: Serve the hot soup with two slices of crusty bread.

meanings.en: believable, credible (often negative: pas croyable = unbelievable)
meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Ce n'est pas croyable.
examples.trans: It is unbelievable.

examples.text: Ce n'est vraiment pas croyable!
examples.trans: That is truly unbelievable!

meanings.note: Golden crust on bread or cake.

examples.text: Il refroidit sur la grille en ce moment: croûte dorée et bon parfum de citron!
examples.trans: It is cooling on the rack right now: golden crust and lovely lemon scent!

examples.text: Voici la croûte sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the crust on the table.

meanings.note: manger de la viande crue = to eat raw meat

examples.text: Il mange un animal cru.
examples.trans: He eats a raw animal.

examples.text: Des légumes crus.
examples.trans: Raw vegetables.

examples.text: Il mange un animal cru devant la caméra?
