examples.trans: He eats a raw animal in front of the camera?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cruauté', plural 'les cruautés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cruelty'.

examples.text: Elle refuse toute cruauté envers les animaux.
examples.trans: She rejects all cruelty toward animals.

examples.text: Elle combat la cruauté des abattoirs.
examples.trans: She fights slaughterhouse cruelty.

examples.text: Pourquoi montrer une telle cruauté à l'écran?
examples.trans: Why show such cruelty on screen?

examples.text: C'est un métier cruel.
examples.trans: It's a cruel profession.

examples.text: La vie est parfois cruelle.
examples.trans: Life is sometimes cruel.

examples.text: Les médias peuvent être cruels.
examples.trans: The media can be cruel.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Je manquais cruellement de temps.
examples.trans: I was desperately short on time.

examples.text: Mais je manquais cruellement de temps.
examples.trans: But I was desperately short on time.

meanings.en: daycare center, day nursery (for young children)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la crèche', plural 'les crèches') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'daycare center'.

examples.text: Inscrire son enfant à la crèche.
examples.trans: To enroll one's child in daycare.

examples.text: Cette crèche parentale est très conviviale.
examples.trans: This parent-run daycare is very friendly.

examples.text: Cette crèche parentale demande beaucoup de coopération.
examples.trans: This parent daycare requires a lot of cooperation.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (la crème fraîche); note un café crème (masculine, short for un café à la crème).
When used as a colour modifier (du grès blanc crème, des rideaux crème), crème stays invariable.

examples.text: J'aime les tasses en céramique d'un joli ton blanc crème.
examples.trans: I like ceramic cups in a pretty creamy off-white shade.

examples.text: Nadia fouette la crème fraîche pour la tarte au citron.
examples.trans: Nadia whips the cream for the lemon tart.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le crève-cœur', plural 'les crève-cœurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'heartbreak'.

examples.text: Pour moi, c'est un véritable crève-cœur.
examples.trans: For me, it is a real heartbreak.

examples.text: Ce départ est un crève-cœur.
examples.trans: This departure is heartbreaking.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'designer, creator'.

examples.text: Un autre créateur de mode.
examples.trans: Another fashion designer.

examples.text: La robe du créateur.
examples.trans: The designer's dress.

examples.text: Non, un autre créateur. Mais c'est quand même un smoking.
examples.trans: No, another designer. But it is still a tuxedo.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Elle gère le développement créatif.
examples.trans: She manages creative development.

examples.text: Tu diriges maintenant tout le développement créatif.
examples.trans: You now direct all creative development.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Transpirez ou ça ne sera pas crédible.
examples.trans: Sweat or it will not look credible.

examples.text: Une histoire crédible.
examples.trans: A credible story.

examples.text: Oscar, ce n'est vraiment pas crédible.
examples.trans: Oscar, that is truly not believable.

meanings.note: Prendre un crédit: take out a loan.
Credit provided by a lender or a seller.

examples.text: J'ai pris un crédit.
examples.trans: I took out a loan.

examples.text: Un crédit sur vingt ans.
examples.trans: A twenty-year loan.

examples.text: Andréa a pris un crédit sur vingt ans.
examples.trans: Andréa has taken out a twenty-year loan.

examples.text: Ça peut créer quelque chose d'intense.
examples.trans: It can create something intense.

examples.text: Elle a créé son agence.
examples.trans: She created her own agency.

meanings.en: chimney hook; housewarming party (in pendaison de crémaillère)

examples.text: On fête la pendaison de crémaillère ce soir.
examples.trans: We are celebrating the housewarming party tonight.

examples.text: Tu viens à ma crémaillère ?
examples.trans: Are you coming to my housewarming?

meanings.note: Masculine: crémier. Feminine noun ('la crémière', plural 'les crémières') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'dairywoman'.

examples.text: Séduire la crémière.
examples.trans: To charm the dairywoman.

examples.text: Acheter à la crémière.
examples.trans: To buy from the dairywoman.

examples.text: C'est une vieille habitude pour séduire la crémière.
examples.trans: It is an old habit to charm the dairywoman.

meanings.note: Petite cuillère = teaspoon.

examples.text: Où vont les petites cuillères et les serviettes?
examples.trans: Where do the small spoons and napkins go?

examples.text: Mets une serviette et une petite cuillère à côté de chaque tasse bleue.
examples.trans: Put one napkin and one teaspoon beside every blue cup.

meanings.note: En cuir = made of leather.

examples.text: Pas étonnant qu'elle soit si lourde. Du bois et du cuir!
examples.trans: No wonder it is so heavy. Wood and leather!

examples.text: Attendez: à qui est ce petit carnet en cuir marron sur le comptoir?
examples.trans: Wait: whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?

examples.text: Oh, mon carnet en cuir! Merci! Je le cherchais justement.
examples.trans: Oh, my leather notebook! Thank you! I was just looking for it.

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to cook, to bake'.

examples.text: Faire cuire au four.
examples.trans: To bake in the oven.

examples.text: Laisser cuire à feu doux.
examples.trans: Let simmer on low heat.

examples.text: Nadia, combien de brioches à la cannelle et de gâteaux au citron votre four peut cuire chaque matin?
examples.trans: Nadia, how many cinnamon rolls and lemon cakes can your oven bake each morning?

meanings.note: Dans la cuisine.
Faire la cuisine = to cook.

examples.text: Salut! Tu dois être Claire. Moi, c'est Nadia, de la cuisine.
examples.trans: Hi! You must be Claire. I am Nadia, from the kitchen.

examples.text: Oh non! Étienne, Claire, on a une urgence en cuisine!
examples.trans: Oh no! Etienne, Claire, we have a kitchen emergency!

examples.text: Six citrons jaunes attendent dans mon panier en ce moment: ma cuisine attendait ce vendredi!
examples.trans: Six yellow lemons are waiting in my basket right now: my kitchen was waiting for this Friday!

meanings.note: Process, time, or doneness of baking or cooking ('temps de cuisson').

examples.text: Surveillez bien la cuisson des brioches pendant les dernières minutes.
examples.trans: Watch the baking of the brioches closely during the final minutes.

examples.text: Une cuisson douce garde les fruits bien fondants.
examples.trans: Gentle baking keeps the fruit nice and tender.

meanings.en: drunken state, binge (prendre une cuite = get hammered)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cuite', plural 'les cuites') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'drunken state'.

examples.text: Il s'est pris une cuite.
examples.trans: He got hammered.

examples.text: Où Depardieu a pris une cuite?
examples.trans: Where Depardieu got totally drunk?

meanings.note: En cuivre = copper (pipes).

examples.text: Touchez le tuyau en cuivre! Il chauffe déjà!
examples.trans: Touch the copper pipe! It is warming up already!

examples.text: Voici le cuivre sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the copper on the table.

meanings.note: Informal. Masculine noun ('le culot', plural 'les culots') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'audacity'.

examples.text: Cette inconnue a beaucoup de culot.
examples.trans: This stranger has a lot of nerve.

examples.text: Gabriel, cette inconnue a beaucoup de culot.
examples.trans: Gabriel, this stranger has a lot of nerve.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'cult'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ce vieux film des années quatre-vingt est devenu culte.
examples.trans: That old film from the eighties has become a cult classic.

examples.text: Les fans connaissent chaque réplique de cette scène culte.
examples.trans: Fans know every line of this cult scene.

meanings.note: Used for garden herbs, vegetables, or skills.

examples.text: C'est vous qui cultivez ces herbes, Henri?
examples.trans: Do you grow these herbs yourself, Henri?

examples.text: C'est facile à cultiver ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to grow, cultivate together.

meanings.note: la ministre de la Culture = the Minister of Culture

examples.text: J'aime la culture française.
examples.trans: I like French culture.

examples.text: C'est le ministère de la Culture.
examples.trans: It's the Ministry of Culture.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'combined'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Nos chiffres cumulés restent sous la limite.
examples.trans: Our combined figures stay under the limit.

examples.text: Nos chiffres cumulés restent sous cinquante pour cent.
examples.trans: Our combined figures remain under fifty percent.

meanings.note: C'est curieux. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.
C'est curieux. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Restons curieux.
examples.trans: Let us stay curious.

examples.text: Un regard curieux.
examples.trans: A curious look.

examples.text: Alors restons curieux, intelligents, ouverts.
examples.trans: So let us stay curious, intelligent, open.

meanings.note: written CV, pronounced as two letters

examples.text: Laissez votre CV ici.
examples.trans: Leave your CV here.

examples.text: J'envoie mon CV.
examples.trans: I'm sending my CV.

meanings.note: avoir le cerveau mal câblé = to be wired wrong

examples.text: J'ai peut-être le cerveau mal câblé.
examples.trans: Maybe my brain is wired wrong.

examples.text: Ils ont câblé tout le studio.
examples.trans: They wired the entire studio.

meanings.note: Bois de cèdre = aromatic cedarwood.

examples.text: Un petit coffre en bois de cèdre? Je n'ai jamais vu cette boîte en quinze ans!
examples.trans: A small cedarwood chest? I have never seen that box in fifteen years!

examples.text: Voici le cèdre sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the cedar, cedarwood on the table.

meanings.en: to yield, to give in, to cede
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to yield'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'cédé').

examples.text: Céder à la panique.
examples.trans: To give in to panic.

examples.text: Ne cédez pas.
examples.trans: Do not give in.

examples.text: Je refuse de céder à ses caprices ridicules.
examples.trans: I refuse to give in to his ridiculous whims.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le célibat', plural 'les célibats') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'single life'.

examples.text: Je suis nulle en célibat.
examples.trans: I am terrible at being single.

examples.text: Je suis super nulle en célibat.
examples.trans: I am super terrible at being single.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le célibataire', plural 'les célibataires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'single person'.

examples.text: Des guides pour les célibataires.
examples.trans: Guides for singles.

examples.text: Ils ont des guides pour les célibataires.
examples.trans: They have guides for singles.

examples.text: Il y a beaucoup de célibataires.
examples.trans: There are many single people.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'renowned'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: La célèbre série télévisée.
examples.trans: The famous television series.

examples.text: C'est la célèbre série Game of Thrones.
examples.trans: It is the famous series Game of Thrones.

examples.text: Ils fabriquent la célèbre Palme d'or.
examples.trans: They manufacture the famous Palme d'Or.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to celebrate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'célébré').

examples.text: Nous célébrons le trentième anniversaire.
examples.trans: We celebrate the thirtieth anniversary.

examples.text: Ils célèbrent cet événement avec joie.
examples.trans: They celebrate this event with joy.

examples.text: Ce soir, célébrons le talent des agents.
examples.trans: Tonight, let us celebrate the talent of agents.

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'celebrity, star'.

examples.text: De grandes célébrités.
examples.trans: Big celebrities.

examples.text: La célébrité ne l'intéresse pas.
examples.trans: Fame does not interest him.

examples.text: Toute l'agence et de grandes célébrités!
examples.trans: The whole agency and big celebrities!

meanings.note: Used with *en* to indicate material (*un pot en céramique blanche*).

examples.text: Le sel se garde au sec dans un pot en céramique.
examples.trans: Salt stays dry in a ceramic jar.

examples.text: Elle peint de petites tasses en céramique à la main.
examples.trans: She paints small ceramic cups by hand.

meanings.note: Cérébralement, si. Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Cérébralement, si, mais pas au fond de moi.
examples.trans: Intellectually, yes, but not deep down.

examples.text: Analyser une émotion cérébralement.
examples.trans: To analyze an emotion intellectually.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la cérémonie', plural 'les cérémonies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ceremony'.

examples.text: La cérémonie d'ouverture.
examples.trans: The opening ceremony.

examples.text: Bonjour Andréa, nous parlions de la cérémonie.
examples.trans: Hello Andrea, we were talking about the ceremony.

examples.text: Juliette sera une maîtresse de cérémonie parfaite.
examples.trans: Juliette will be a perfect mistress of ceremonies.

meanings.en: César award, French national film award
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le césar', plural 'les césars') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'Cesar award'.

examples.text: Elle a gagné un César.
examples.trans: She won a César.

examples.text: Mais ça peut te valoir un César! Au minimum!
examples.trans: But that could win you a Cesar! At least!

examples.text: Pense au César, Julie!
examples.trans: Think about the Cesar, Julie!

meanings.note: Uphill slope; seacoast; rib ('côte à côte' = side by side).

examples.text: Ils marchent côte à côte le long des arbres.
examples.trans: They walk side by side along the trees.

examples.text: La petite rue monte en côte jusqu'à la tour.
examples.trans: The narrow street climbs uphill to the tower.

meanings.note: Un côté positif: a bright side.
Un côté positif: a bright side.

examples.text: Il y a un côté positif.
examples.trans: There's a bright side.

examples.text: Le café est à côté.
examples.trans: The café is next door.

meanings.en: briser le cœur = to break someone's heart

examples.text: De tout mon cœur.
examples.trans: With all my heart.

examples.text: Mon cœur s'est arrêté à la page un!
examples.trans: My heart stopped at page one!

examples.text: Bonjour. Non, soulevez d'abord la poignée, puis poussez.
examples.trans: Good morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.

examples.text: Règle numéro un: buvez d'abord du thé chaud, puis répondez à la sonnette.
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then answer the bell.

examples.text: Tu es une héroïne, Claire! Donne-moi le lait d'abord pour la machine à café.
examples.trans: You are a hero, Claire! Give me the milk first for the coffee machine.

meanings.note: Agreement.

examples.text: D'accord, je monte la valise tout de suite.
examples.trans: OK, I'll take the suitcase up right away.

examples.text: Tu es d'accord pour vendredi midi?
examples.trans: Are you OK with Friday at noon?

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'besides'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: D'ailleurs, c'est vrai.
examples.trans: Besides, that is true.

examples.text: Je ne sais pas, d'ailleurs.
examples.trans: I do not know, for that matter.

examples.text: Merci Hicham, toi aussi d'ailleurs.
examples.trans: Thank you Hicham, you too by the way.

meanings.note: Flat stone paving slab in a courtyard, church floor, or garden path.

examples.text: La pluie fait briller les vieilles dalles de la cour.
examples.trans: The rain makes the old courtyard flagstones gleam.

examples.text: Une dalle un peu mobile sonne creux sous le pied.
examples.trans: A slightly loose flagstone sounds hollow underfoot.

meanings.note: Polite everyday word when referring to a woman one doesn't know yet (*une dame à l'entrée*).

examples.text: Une dame en manteau bleu attend devant la réception.
examples.trans: A woman in a blue coat is waiting at the front desk.

examples.text: Cette vieille dame habite en face du marché depuis quarante ans.
examples.trans: This elderly lady has lived across from the market for forty years.

meanings.note: Final -r is silent (/dɑ̃ʒe/). Sans danger means 'safe, harmless'.

examples.text: Le nouveau câble est installé: on peut allumer sans danger.
examples.trans: The new cable is installed: we can switch it on safely.

examples.text: Attention, cette marche mouillée présente un vrai danger.
examples.trans: Careful, this wet step is a real hazard.

meanings.note: vivre dangereusement = to live dangerously

examples.text: Vivre dangereusement!
examples.trans: Living dangerously!

examples.text: Il conduit dangereusement.
examples.trans: He drives dangerously.

examples.text: Vivre dangereusement! Respect, monsieur Barneville!
examples.trans: Living dangerously! Respect, Mr Barneville!

examples.text: C'est dangereux.
examples.trans: It's dangerous.

examples.text: Elle est dangereuse.
examples.trans: She's dangerous.

meanings.note: J'étais dans les sous-vêtements.
Dans une heure = in an hour.

examples.text: Dans le cinéma.
examples.trans: In the film business.

examples.text: Il y a vingt-cinq ans? Dans cette même maison?
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago? In that same house?

meanings.en: dancing, lilting, lively (of music or rhythm)
meanings.note: Verbal adjective from *danser* describing a buoyant melody (*un air dansant*, *un rythme dansant*).

examples.text: Cette petite valse a un rythme léger et dansant.
examples.trans: This little waltz has a light, dancing rhythm.

examples.text: Sa démarche vive et dansante fait sourire tout le monde.
examples.trans: Her brisk, buoyant step makes everyone smile.

meanings.note: La danse à la barre = pole dancing.

examples.text: Elle fait de la danse.
examples.trans: She does dancing.

examples.text: C'est une danse difficile.
examples.trans: It's a difficult dance.

examples.text: Pour la danse à la barre, je sais que vous faites du tango.
examples.trans: For the pole dancing, I know that you do the tango.

meanings.note: danser le hip-hop = to dance hip-hop

examples.text: Tu danses le hip-hop?
examples.trans: Do you dance hip-hop?

examples.text: Elle adore danser.
examples.trans: She loves dancing.

examples.text: Tu danses?
examples.trans: Do you dance?

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a calendar date; for a social appointment or romantic date, French uses un rendez-vous.

examples.text: Quelle est la date inscrite en haut de la lettre?
examples.trans: What is the date written at the top of the letter?

examples.text: Claire vérifie la date d'arrivée sur le registre.
examples.trans: Claire checks the arrival date in the register.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel.
Also 'some': du sucre.

examples.text: Le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: The Kechiche film.

examples.text: C'est du sucre.
examples.trans: It's sugar.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le deal', plural 'les deals') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'business deal'.

examples.text: Le deal est signé.
examples.trans: The deal is signed.

examples.text: Oui, le deal de coproduction est fait.
examples.trans: Yes, the co-production deal is done.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le dealer', plural 'les dealers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'drug dealer'.

examples.text: C'est un dealer.
examples.trans: He is a drug dealer.

examples.text: Tu ramènes ton dealer sur le tournage?
examples.trans: Are you bringing your dealer on set?

examples.text: C'était son orthophoniste, pas un dealer.
examples.trans: It was his speech therapist, not a dealer.

meanings.note: Invariable adverb used like an adjective after *être* or *rester* (*rester debout*, 'to stay on one's feet').

examples.text: Ne restez pas debout si votre cheville vous fait mal.
examples.trans: Don't stand up if your ankle hurts.

examples.text: Toute la cuisine est déjà debout à six heures du matin.
examples.trans: The whole kitchen is already up at six in the morning.

related.gloss: foot; leg (of a table or chair)

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'inside'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Ouvre la boîte et regarde ce qu'il y a dedans.
examples.trans: Open the box and look at what is inside.

examples.text: Il fait froid dehors, rentrons vite dedans.
examples.trans: It is cold outside, let's go back inside quickly.

meanings.note: Angular or temperature degree ('au degré près' = to the exact degree); level or step.

examples.text: Le four est préchauffé à cent quatre-vingts degrés.
examples.trans: The oven is preheated to one hundred eighty degrees.

examples.text: La boussole donne l'angle au degré près.
examples.trans: The compass gives the angle to the exact degree.

meanings.note: On se retrouve dehors. Invariable French adverb meaning 'outside'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: La boutique a une grande enseigne dehors?
examples.trans: Does the shop have a big sign outside?

examples.text: Gardez la maison, je suis déjà dehors!
examples.trans: Hold the fort, I am already outside!

examples.text: Pas un mot dehors pour l'instant!
examples.trans: Not a word outside for now!

meanings.note: À demain = see you tomorrow.

examples.text: Et demain?
examples.trans: And tomorrow?

examples.text: À demain!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la demande', plural 'les demandes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'request'.

examples.text: Une demande typique de star.
examples.trans: A typical star request.

examples.text: Voilà une demande typique de grande star!
examples.trans: There is a typical request of a big star!

examples.text: Agence ASK, bonjour, j'écoute votre demande.
examples.trans: ASK agency, hello, I am listening to your request.

meanings.note: Demander quelque chose à quelqu'un.

examples.text: Et il n'a pas demandé sa propre valise avec le train en bois?
examples.trans: And he did not ask for his own suitcase with the wooden train?

examples.text: Il a laissé un petit mot pour nous demander de la garder jusqu'à vendredi.
examples.trans: He left a short note asking us to keep it until Friday.

examples.text: Demandez-lui son nom! Notez-le!
examples.trans: Ask him his name! Write it down!

meanings.note: Agrees after heure: sept heures et demie.

examples.text: Huit clients affamés descendent à sept heures et demie!
examples.trans: Eight hungry guests come down at half past seven!

examples.text: Dormez bien, monsieur. Le petit-déjeuner commence à sept heures et demie en bas.
examples.trans: Sleep well, sir. Breakfast starts at seven thirty downstairs.

meanings.note: *Demi-* stays invariable before a hyphenated noun; only *centimètres* takes plural *-s*.

examples.text: Soulevez le cadre d'un demi-centimètre sur la gauche.
examples.trans: Lift the frame half a centimeter on the left.

examples.text: La pâte à tarte doit faire un demi-centimètre d'épaisseur.
examples.trans: The tart dough should be half a centimeter thick.

meanings.note: Une demi-journée de travail.

examples.text: Il nous reste une demi-journée.
examples.trans: We have half a day left.

examples.text: Je travaille une demi-journée.
examples.trans: I work half a day.

meanings.note: Invariable adjective: du beurre demi-sel.

examples.text: C'est du beurre demi-sel! Mes petits pains sucrés ont besoin de beurre doux!
examples.trans: That is salted butter! My sweet rolls need unsalted butter!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment demi-sel.
examples.trans: This place is really lightly salted.

meanings.note: Faire demi-tour = to turn back.

examples.text: Oui, Nadia. Même s'il fait demi-tour et repart tout droit par le portail.
examples.trans: Yes, Nadia. Even if he turns around and walks straight back out the gate.

examples.text: Voici le demi-tour sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the half-turn, U-turn on the table.

meanings.note: Un demi-verre d'eau = half a glass of water.

examples.text: Oh, comme c'est aimable, monsieur. Juste un demi-verre.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind, sir. Just half a glass.

examples.text: Voici le demi-verre sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the half-glass on the table.

meanings.note: serrer les dents = to grit one's teeth

meanings.en: faire ses dents = to be teething (for a baby)

examples.text: Il fait ses dents.
examples.trans: He's teething.

examples.text: Elle a de belles dents.
examples.trans: She has nice teeth.

examples.text: Il n'a pas dormi de la nuit. Il fait ses dents.
examples.trans: He didn't sleep all night. He's teething.

meanings.note: Rideau en dentelle = lace curtain.

examples.text: Dit l'homme qui regarde derrière le rideau en dentelle toutes les trente secondes!
examples.trans: Says the man peeking behind the lace curtain every thirty seconds!

examples.text: Voici la dentelle sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the lace on the table.

meanings.en: for (a length of time, still going on)
meanings.note: With an ongoing state, French normally uses the present: je suis ici depuis lundi.
A starting point: depuis lundi, since Monday.

examples.text: Depuis quand?
examples.trans: Since when?

examples.text: J'ai entendu crier à propos de beurre depuis le fond de la cour.
examples.trans: I heard shouting about butter from the back of the courtyard.

examples.text: C'est pour ça que vous écoutiez la rue depuis le grenier hier soir!
examples.trans: That is why you were listening to the street from the attic last night!

meanings.note: after the noun: la semaine dernière = last week
Before the noun: le dernier jour.

examples.text: Celle de la semaine dernière?
examples.trans: The one from last week?

examples.text: C'est le dernier café.
examples.trans: It's the last coffee.

meanings.note: Opposite of 'devant' (in front of).

examples.text: Il est derrière la porte.
examples.trans: He's behind the door.

examples.text: Regardez dans le miroir derrière le comptoir, patron.
examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the counter, boss.

descendre.gloss: to go down, to travel down

meanings.en: to go down, to come down (stairs, or out of a vehicle)
to travel south / down from Paris for a visit

examples.text: Je descends tout de suite.
examples.trans: I'm coming right down.

examples.text: Faites-moi confiance. Descendons l'accueillir.
examples.trans: Trust me. Let us go down and welcome him.

meanings.note: Built from prefix *dé-* + *serrer* ('to tighten').

examples.text: L'humidité a légèrement desserré la petite vis du panneau.
examples.trans: Dampness slightly loosened the small panel screw.

examples.text: Desserrez le couvercle avec un torchon sec.
examples.trans: Loosen the lid with a dry kitchen towel.

related.gloss: to screw back on, tighten screws

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le dessin', plural 'les dessins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'drawing'.

examples.text: C'est un beau dessin.
examples.trans: It is a beautiful drawing.

examples.text: Pourquoi il y a des dessins précis de trois hôtels de notre rue?
examples.trans: Why are there neat drawings of three hotels on our street?

examples.text: Architecte acousticien! Vous dessinez des salles de concert?
examples.trans: An acoustic architect! Do you design concert halls?

examples.text: Regardez le vieux plan plié coincé dans la charnière: il y a une porte cachée dessinée à cet étage!
examples.trans: Look at the folded old blueprint tucked in the hinge: there is a hidden door drawn on this floor!

examples.text: L'enfant dessine une maison.
examples.trans: The child draws a house.

meanings.en: below, underneath (en dessous de = beneath, below)
meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'below'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Ton dossier est caché juste dessous.
examples.trans: Your file is hidden right underneath.

examples.text: Regarde la note écrite tout en dessous.
examples.trans: Look at the note written right at the bottom.

meanings.en: on it, at it (direction or position)
meanings.note: Tirer dessus = to shoot at. Invariable French adverb meaning 'on it'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Il y a un nom ou un numéro de téléphone dessus?
examples.trans: Is there a name or a phone number on it?

examples.text: Bien. Mets ces herbes vertes fraîches dessus avant de servir.
examples.trans: Good. Put these fresh green herbs on top before serving.

examples.text: Son grand-père coupait du gâteau tiède au citron avec du sucre glace dessus!
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with icing sugar on top!

meanings.note: Le destin frappe à la porte. Masculine noun ('le destin', plural 'les destins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'destiny'.

examples.text: C'est le destin qui frappe à ta porte.
examples.trans: It is destiny knocking at your door.

examples.text: Accomplir son destin.
examples.trans: To fulfill one's destiny.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to destine'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'destiné').

examples.text: On était destinés à passer cette soirée ensemble.
examples.trans: We were destined to spend this evening together.

examples.text: Ce projet est destiné aux jeunes.
examples.trans: This project is intended for young people.

examples.text: On était destinés à cette soirée.
examples.trans: We were destined for this evening.

meanings.note: The x sounds like z before a vowel.

examples.text: Deux places.
examples.trans: Two tickets.

examples.text: Deux fois.
examples.trans: Twice.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'second'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Oui, la chambre quatre au deuxième étage! Comment était votre voyage en train?
examples.trans: Yes, room four on the second floor! How was your train trip?

examples.text: Bienvenue à l'Hôtel du Tilleul, Claire. Votre deuxième jour ne sera pas ennuyeux.
examples.trans: Welcome to the Hotel du Tilleul, Claire. Your second day will not be boring.

examples.text: Pas mal pour un deuxième jour, la nouvelle.
examples.trans: Not bad for a second day, rookie.

meanings.en: in front of, before (a place or person)
meanings.note: devant la porte = in front of the door

examples.text: Je t'attends devant le cinéma.
examples.trans: I'll wait for you in front of the cinema.

examples.text: Voilà un taxi devant le portail à l'instant.
examples.trans: Here comes a taxi in front of the gate right now.

meanings.note: past forms use être: elle est devenue

examples.text: Elle est devenue une star.
examples.trans: She became a star.

examples.text: Il veut devenir acteur.
examples.trans: He wants to become an actor.

meanings.note: Work out a guess; devine qui or devinez qui invites the listener to guess someone's identity.

examples.text: Laissez-moi deviner. Vous avez promis une chambre qu'on n'a pas?
examples.trans: Let me guess. You promised a room we do not have?

examples.text: Devine qui est là!
examples.trans: Guess who's here!

examples.text: Je ne peux pas deviner.
examples.trans: I can't guess.

meanings.note: + infinitive.

examples.text: Salut! Tu dois être Claire. Moi, c'est Nadia, de la cuisine.
examples.trans: Hi! You must be Claire. I am Nadia, from the kitchen.

examples.text: La cliente de la chambre quatre reste toute la semaine. Tout doit être parfait!
examples.trans: The guest in room four is staying all week. Everything must be perfect!

examples.text: Je dois lire le cahier de réservations, mais je ne trouve pas mes lunettes!
examples.trans: I need to read the reservation book, but I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le diamant', plural 'les diamants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'diamond'.

examples.text: Elle porte une belle bague avec un diamant.
examples.trans: She is wearing a beautiful ring with a diamond.

examples.text: Ce collier de diamants coûte une fortune.
examples.trans: This diamond necklace costs a fortune.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la diction', plural 'les dictions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'diction'.

examples.text: Cet acteur de théâtre a une diction parfaite.
examples.trans: This stage actor has perfect diction.

examples.text: Elle prend des cours pour travailler sa diction.
examples.trans: She is taking lessons to work on her diction.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le dieu', plural 'les dieux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'supreme deity'.

examples.text: Oh mon Dieu!
examples.trans: Oh my goodness!

examples.text: Mon Dieu! Elles sont ensemble! Non, non...
examples.trans: My God! They're together! No, no...

examples.text: Dieu merci! Et les douches du matin?
examples.trans: Thank goodness! And the morning showers?

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'slander, defamation'.

examples.text: L'acteur menace d'attaquer le journal pour diffamation.
examples.trans: The actor threatens to sue the newspaper for defamation.

examples.text: Cet article est une vraie diffamation contre notre client.
examples.trans: This article is pure defamation against our client.

examples.text: C'est de la diffamation!
examples.trans: That's slander!

meanings.note: C'est difficile de + infinitive.

examples.text: Journée difficile?
examples.trans: Tough day?

examples.text: Le français n'est pas difficile.
examples.trans: French isn't difficult.

meanings.note: Formed from 'différent' + -ment.

examples.text: Après, tu vas voir les choses différemment.
examples.trans: Afterwards, you'll see things differently.

examples.text: Il pense différemment.
examples.trans: He thinks differently.

meanings.note: la différence entre = the difference between

examples.text: C'est la grande différence entre toi et moi.
examples.trans: That is the big difference between you and me.

examples.text: Faire la différence.
examples.trans: To make the difference.

examples.text: C'est totalement différent.
examples.trans: It's totally different.

examples.text: Elle est différente.
examples.trans: She's different.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'worthy'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est une issue digne.
examples.trans: It is a dignified outcome.

examples.text: C'est poétique et digne de Cocteau.
examples.trans: It is poetic and worthy of Cocteau.

examples.text: Je veux être digne de toi.
examples.trans: I want to be worthy of you.

meanings.en: with dignity, in a dignified or proper manner
meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Nous allons fêter ça dignement toutes les deux.
examples.trans: We are going to celebrate this properly, both of us.

examples.text: Accepter la décision dignement.
examples.trans: To accept the decision with dignity.

examples.text: Je parle de dignité et de loyauté.
examples.trans: I'm talking about dignity and loyalty.

examples.text: Il garde sa dignité.
examples.trans: He keeps his dignity.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la digue', plural 'les digues') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'dike'.

examples.text: L'eau passe au-dessus des digues.
examples.trans: Water passes over the dikes.

examples.text: Comme un fleuve brisant ses digues.
examples.trans: Like a river breaking its dikes.

meanings.en: to digest food; figuratively to process or accept difficult news
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to digest food'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'digéré').

examples.text: J'ai besoin de temps pour digérer cela.
examples.trans: I need time to process that.

examples.text: Il a du mal à digérer la nouvelle.
examples.trans: He has trouble digesting the news.

meanings.note: le dimanche = on Sundays; dimanche = this Sunday

examples.text: Tu travailles le dimanche?
examples.trans: Do you work on Sundays?

examples.text: À dimanche!
examples.trans: See you Sunday!

meanings.note: le dindon de la farce = the fall guy / laughing stock

examples.text: Le dindon de la farce.
examples.trans: The fall guy of the whole thing.

examples.text: Élever des dindons.
examples.trans: To raise turkeys.

examples.text: Et aussi de dindon de la farce!
examples.trans: And also of a fall guy!

meanings.note: An informal description, also used for being crazy about someone with de.
Can express enthusiastic surprise, depending on tone.

examples.text: C'est dingue.
examples.trans: It's crazy.

examples.text: Il est dingue de toi.
examples.trans: He's crazy about you.

examples.text: Je travaille tous les jours jusqu'à vingt-deux heures. C'est dingue.
examples.trans: I work until ten at night every day. It's crazy.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Des talents diplomatiques.
examples.trans: Diplomatic skills.

examples.text: Une mission diplomatique.
examples.trans: A diplomatic mission.

examples.text: Tu dois utiliser tes talents diplomatiques.
examples.trans: You must use your diplomatic skills.

meanings.note: Avoir un diplôme.

examples.text: Merci, mais il faut un diplôme pour ça!
examples.trans: Thank you, but you need a degree for this!

examples.text: Elle a un diplôme d'histoire.
examples.trans: She has a history degree.

meanings.note: une infirmière diplômée = a certified nurse

examples.text: Un professionnel diplômé.
examples.trans: A qualified professional.

examples.text: Une actrice diplômée.
examples.trans: A trained actress.

examples.text: Faites confiance à une infirmière diplômée!
examples.trans: Trust a certified nurse!

meanings.note: dire la vérité à quelqu'un = to tell someone the truth
dire à quelqu'un; dis-lui = tell her/him

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.
examples.trans: Tell her I can't come.

examples.text: Trop tard! Il a dit merci et il a raccroché!
examples.trans: Too late! He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.en: direct; live (en direct = live on air)
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'direct'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Nous sommes en direct.
examples.trans: We are live on air.

examples.text: On est en direct...
examples.trans: We are live on air...

examples.text: Elle m'attend en direct à la radio.
examples.trans: She is waiting for me live on the radio.

examples.text: Pourquoi il ne m'appelle pas directement?
examples.trans: Why doesn't he call me directly?

examples.text: Va directement chez lui.
examples.trans: Go straight to his place.

examples.text: Alors pourquoi il ne m'appelle pas directement?
examples.trans: Then why doesn't he call me directly?

meanings.note: Feminine: une directrice.

examples.text: On était là pour voir le directeur.
examples.trans: We were there to see the manager.

examples.text: C'est le directeur de l'hôtel.
examples.trans: He's the manager of the hotel.

examples.text: Bon, on faisait semblant. On était là pour voir le directeur.
examples.trans: All right, we were pretending. We were there to see the manager.

meanings.note: Way toward a place ('en direction de'); management of a hotel or school.

examples.text: Marchons en direction de la vieille tour d'horloge.
examples.trans: Let's walk in the direction of the old clock tower.

examples.text: La flèche gravée indique la bonne direction.
examples.trans: The carved arrow points in the right direction.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'female manager, director'.

examples.text: La directrice de casting est là.
examples.trans: The casting director is here.

examples.text: Ce n'était pas la vraie directrice de casting.
examples.trans: It was not the real casting director.

examples.text: Je cherche une nouvelle directrice.
examples.trans: I am looking for a new director.

meanings.en: to run, direct, lead (a kitchen, team, orchestra)
meanings.note: Takes -ge- before a/o: nous dirigeons, il dirigeait.

examples.text: Elle dirige toute sa cuisine avec calme et précision.
examples.trans: She runs her whole kitchen with calm and precision.

examples.text: Son oncle a dirigé cet hôtel pendant trente ans.
examples.trans: His uncle ran this hotel for thirty years.

meanings.note: Prononcer un discours. Masculine noun ('le discours', plural 'les discours') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'speech'.

examples.text: Elle répète son discours.
examples.trans: She is rehearsing her speech.

examples.text: Un discours émouvant.
examples.trans: A moving speech.

examples.text: Un discours de cinq minutes avec dix-neuf raisons pour lesquelles nous avions tort tous les deux.
examples.trans: A five-minute speech with nineteen reasons why we were both wrong.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'discreet'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Restons très discrets.
examples.trans: Let us stay very discreet.

examples.text: Une personne discrète.
examples.trans: A discreet person.

examples.text: Discret comme une souris!
examples.trans: Quiet as a mouse!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la discrimination', plural 'les discriminations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'discrimination'.

examples.text: C'est une discrimination à l'embauche.
examples.trans: It is hiring discrimination.

examples.text: C'est une vraie discrimination à l'embauche.
examples.trans: That is real hiring discrimination.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Ou m'aider discrètement?
examples.trans: Or help me discreetly?

examples.text: Elle sort discrètement.
examples.trans: She slips out discreetly.

examples.text: On prépare toutes les démarches discrètement.
examples.trans: We prepare all the paperwork discreetly.

meanings.note: Harm the reputation of someone. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to discredit'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'discrédité').

examples.text: Il faut discréditer son agent.
examples.trans: We must discredit his agent.

examples.text: Cette rumeur va le discréditer.
examples.trans: This rumor will discredit him.

examples.text: Il faut discréditer son agent Bréhier.
examples.trans: We must discredit his agent Bréhier.

meanings.note: à la discrétion de = at the discretion of

examples.text: C'est à la discrétion du réalisateur.
examples.trans: It is at the director's discretion.

examples.text: Il travaille avec une grande discrétion.
examples.trans: He works with great discretion.

examples.text: Aujourd'hui notre cour accueille des retrouvailles: discrétion absolue!
examples.trans: Today our courtyard hosts a reunion: complete discretion!

meanings.note: En discuter = talk about it.

examples.text: On peut en discuter?
examples.trans: Can we talk about it?

examples.text: Ils discutent au café.
examples.trans: They're chatting at the café.

meanings.en: to disappear, vanish (or be snapped up fast at market)
meanings.note: Conjugated like connaître (ils disparaissent /dispaʁɛs/, past participle disparu with avoir).

examples.text: Au marché, les tartes chaudes disparaissent avant dix heures.
examples.trans: At the market, the warm tarts sell out before ten o'clock.

examples.text: La poussière disparaît vite avec un bon chiffon humide.
examples.trans: The dust disappears quickly with a good damp cloth.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Une date disponible en avril.
examples.trans: An available date in April.

examples.text: Il n'y a rien de disponible pour avril.
examples.trans: There is nothing available for April.

examples.text: Non, je ne suis pas disponible.
examples.trans: No, I am not available.

examples.text: Je reste à votre entière disposition.
examples.trans: I remain completely at your disposal.

examples.text: Une voiture est à votre disposition.
examples.trans: A car is at your disposal.

meanings.note: From se disputer ('to argue').

examples.text: Les maisons de famille et les vieux souvenirs, ces disputes-là font mal.
examples.trans: Family houses and old memories, arguments like those hurt deeply.

examples.text: Voici la dispute sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the argument, quarrel on the table.

meanings.en: se disputer (avec) = to argue, to quarrel (with)
meanings.note: Reflexive verb.

meanings.en: disputer quelqu'un = to tell someone off
meanings.note: Informal.

examples.text: Les deux frères se sont disputés il y a trois ans.
examples.trans: The two brothers argued three years ago.

examples.text: On ne se dispute pas devant les clients!
examples.trans: We don't argue in front of the guests!

meanings.note: faire un disque = to record an album

examples.text: Nous allons faire un disque formidable.
examples.trans: We are going to make a wonderful record.

examples.text: Son nouveau disque sort demain.
examples.trans: Her new album comes out tomorrow.

meanings.note: garder ses distances = to keep one's distance

examples.text: Garder ses distances.
examples.trans: To keep one's distance.

examples.text: Une longue distance.
examples.trans: A long distance.

examples.text: Je garde mes distances avec lui.
examples.trans: I keep my distance from him.

meanings.note: Having an elegant, dignified, and refined air or manner.

examples.text: Hé! Ce monsieur distingué près du portail est remarquablement élégant, merci beaucoup!
examples.trans: Hey! That distinguished gentleman near the gate is remarkably handsome, thank you very much!

examples.text: Une dame très distinguée a réservé la chambre quatre pour la semaine.
examples.trans: A very distinguished lady booked Room Four for the week.

meanings.en: to hand out, pass around, distribute
meanings.note: Distribuer le courrier / les menus = hand out the mail / the menus.

examples.text: Il distribue les menus imprimés à chaque table.
examples.trans: He hands out the printed menus to every table.

examples.text: Le facteur distribue le courrier dans notre rue à midi.
examples.trans: The mail carrier delivers mail on our street at noon.

meanings.note: le distributeur du film = the film distributor

examples.text: Parler au distributeur.
examples.trans: To speak to the distributor.

examples.text: Un grand distributeur de cinéma.
examples.trans: A major movie distributor.

examples.text: J'ai enfin parlé au distributeur ce matin.
examples.trans: I finally spoke to the distributor this morning.

meanings.note: Godly, divine; colloquially delicious or wonderful ('bonté divine!' = goodness gracious!).

examples.text: Ce parfum de tarte chaude est absolument divin.
examples.trans: That scent of warm tart is absolutely heavenly.

examples.text: Bonté divine, vous avez retrouvé la boîte intacte!
examples.trans: Goodness gracious, you found the box intact!

meanings.en: to divide, break down into parts
meanings.note: *Diviser X en Y* ('to divide X into Y') is useful for splitting tasks, space, or numbers.

examples.text: Divisons le grand travail en trois petites étapes claires.
examples.trans: Let's divide the big job into three clear little steps.

examples.text: Elle divise la pâte à pain en quatre boules égales.
examples.trans: She divides the bread dough into four equal balls.

meanings.note: demander le divorce = to file for divorce

examples.text: Ça ressemble à un divorce.
examples.trans: That sounds like a divorce.

examples.text: Ils ont signé le divorce.
examples.trans: They signed the divorce.

examples.text: Et Mathias est très occupé par son divorce.
examples.trans: And Mathias is very busy with his divorce.

meanings.note: On divorce. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to divorce'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'divorcé').

examples.text: Il divorce.
examples.trans: He's getting divorced.

examples.text: Sa mère m'a dit qu'il divorce.
examples.trans: His mother told me that he is getting divorced.

examples.text: On divorce.
examples.trans: We are getting a divorce.

meanings.note: pronounced dis alone, di before a consonant, diz before a vowel

examples.text: Moi, c'est Henri. Vous êtes en avance de dix minutes.
examples.trans: I am Henri. You are ten minutes early.

examples.text: Voici votre clé, numéro quatre. Le petit-déjeuner est de sept heures trente à dix heures.
examples.trans: Here is your key, number four. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: Vous pouvez faire l'aller-retour en dix minutes?
examples.trans: Can you run there and back in ten minutes?

meanings.note: Cardinal number 18.

examples.text: Comptez dix-huit pas depuis le banc du square.
examples.trans: Count eighteen paces from the park bench.

examples.text: L'hôtel compte dix-huit chambres donnant sur le jardin.
examples.trans: The hotel has eighteen rooms overlooking the garden.

meanings.note: au dix-huitième siècle = in the eighteenth century

examples.text: Elle vit encore au dix-huitième siècle!
examples.trans: She's still living in the eighteenth century!

examples.text: Elle habite dans le dix-huitième arrondissement.
examples.trans: She lives in the eighteenth arrondissement.

meanings.note: Compound number 10 + 9.

examples.text: Un discours de cinq minutes avec dix-neuf raisons pour lesquelles nous avions tort tous les deux.
examples.trans: A five-minute speech with nineteen reasons why we were both wrong.

examples.text: Dix-neuf raisons?! Vous accueillez votre frère ou vous lisez un horaire de train?
examples.trans: Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a train timetable?

meanings.note: Seventeen; joined with a hyphen.

examples.text: Dix-sept pour cent.
examples.trans: Seventeen percent.

examples.text: J'ai dix-sept ans.
examples.trans: I'm seventeen.

examples.text: Donc je garde dix-sept pour cent des parts?
examples.trans: So I keep seventeen percent of the shares?

meanings.en: about ten, ten or so; tens (des dizaines de = dozens/scores of)
meanings.note: Formed from dix + -aine (feminine). Une dizaine de minutes = about ten minutes; des dizaines d'années = decades.

examples.text: Ce meuble était caché là depuis des dizaines d'années.
examples.trans: That piece of furniture had been hidden there for decades.

examples.text: Il reste une dizaine de places libres pour le concert.
examples.trans: There are about ten seats left for the concert.

meanings.en: C (the first note of the C-major scale)
meanings.note: Invariable in the plural (*des do*); French solfège names the notes *do, ré, mi, fa, sol, la, si*.

examples.text: Trouvez d'abord le do du milieu sur le clavier.
examples.trans: First find middle C on the keyboard.

examples.text: Le do sonne clair dès qu'on effleure la touche.
examples.trans: The C rings clear as soon as you brush the key.

related.gloss: D (second musical note: do, ré, mi)

meanings.note: as a title before a name: le docteur Lubek; written Dr

examples.text: Le docteur arrive.
examples.trans: The doctor is coming.

examples.text: J'ai rendez-vous chez le docteur.
examples.trans: I have a doctor's appointment.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le document', plural 'les documents') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'document'.

examples.text: Vérifier chaque document.
examples.trans: Check each document.

examples.text: Tu as vérifié chaque document important?
examples.trans: Did you verify each important document?

examples.text: Regardez ce document choquant sur mon bureau!
examples.trans: Look at this shocking document on my desk!

examples.text: Il tourne un documentaire.
examples.trans: He's filming a documentary.

examples.text: J'ai vu un bon documentaire.
examples.trans: I watched a good documentary.

examples.text: Il tourne un documentaire sur les paysans sans terre au Honduras.
examples.trans: He's filming a documentary about landless farmers in Honduras.

meanings.note: Both the -g- and the -t are silent in singular and plural (/dwa/).

examples.text: Tenez la feuille du bout des doigts pour ne pas la salir.
examples.trans: Hold the sheet by your fingertips so as not to smudge it.

examples.text: Étienne compte les tables sur ses doigts.
examples.trans: Étienne counts the tables on his fingers.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le dollar', plural 'les dollars') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'dollar'.

examples.text: Des millions de dollars.
examples.trans: Millions of dollars.

examples.text: Un dollar américain.
examples.trans: An American dollar.

examples.text: Une interruption coûte des millions de dollars.
examples.trans: A shutdown costs millions of dollars.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le domaine', plural 'les domaines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'area of expertise'.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas mon domaine.
examples.trans: That is not my field.

examples.text: Vous vous occupez des acteurs, c'est votre domaine.
examples.trans: You take care of the actors, that is your field.

related.gloss: a area of expertise / area of expertises

meanings.note: les aristocrates et les domestiques

examples.text: Les aristocrates et les domestiques.
examples.trans: The aristocrats and the servants.

examples.text: Il joue le rôle d'un domestique.
examples.trans: He plays the role of a servant.

examples.text: Écoute, je ne sais même pas comment les aristocrates et les domestiques faisaient à l'époque.
examples.trans: Listen, I do not even know how aristocrats and servants did things back then.

meanings.en: to dominate, to overlook, to master, to overpower
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to dominate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dominé').

examples.text: Dominer la situation.
examples.trans: To master the situation.

examples.text: Vouloir dominer.
examples.trans: To want to dominate.

examples.text: Je voulais absolument le dominer.
examples.trans: I absolutely wanted to dominate him.

meanings.en: c'est dommage = it's a shame, what a pity
meanings.note: Very common.
Formal.

examples.text: C'est dommage!
examples.trans: What a shame!

examples.text: Dommage pour toi.
examples.trans: Too bad for you.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le don', plural 'les dons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'talent'.

examples.text: Tu as un vrai don pour le drame.
examples.trans: You have a real gift for drama.

examples.text: Fais du vélo! Ça donne des forces.
examples.trans: Ride a bike! It gives you energy.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le donateur', plural 'les donateurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'donor'.

examples.text: Nous cherchons de nouveaux donateurs très généreux.
examples.trans: We look for very generous new donors.

examples.text: Un donateur anonyme a financé le refuge.
examples.trans: An anonymous donor financed the shelter.

examples.text: Donc, en fait...
examples.trans: So, actually...

examples.text: Il est tard, donc je pars.
examples.trans: It's late, so I'm leaving.

meanings.note: changer la donne = to change the game, change the situation

examples.text: Cette nouvelle change toute la donne.
examples.trans: This news changes the whole game.

examples.text: La donne a changé depuis hier.
examples.trans: The situation has changed since yesterday.

examples.text: Cette trahison change absolument toute la donne.
examples.trans: This betrayal changes the game completely.

meanings.note: Donner quelque chose à quelqu'un.

examples.text: Ça donne des forces.
examples.trans: It gives you energy.

examples.text: Je te donne mon numéro.
examples.trans: I'll give you my number.

meanings.note: Someone who gives or donates; feminine donneuse. Here, a sperm donor.

examples.text: Un donneur anonyme.
examples.trans: An anonymous donor.

examples.text: Il est donneur de sang.
examples.trans: He's a blood donor.

examples.text: Entre un donneur anonyme et un ami, je choisis l'ami.
examples.trans: Between an anonymous donor and a friend, I choose the friend.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'sleepyhead, sleeping woman'.

examples.text: La dormeuse se lève.
examples.trans: The sleepyhead gets up.

examples.text: Ah, la dormeuse est enfin réveillée!
examples.trans: Ah, the sleepyhead is finally awake!

meanings.note: Past participle dormi; compound tenses use avoir.

examples.text: Il dort.
examples.trans: He is sleeping.

examples.text: Nous avons bien dormi.
examples.trans: We slept well.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'golden'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Elle préfère la tour dorée.
examples.trans: She prefers the golden tower.

examples.text: Le papier doré sur l'étagère du haut. Pourquoi?
examples.trans: The gold wrapper on the top shelf. Why?

examples.text: J'avance... oh, je vois la clé dorée et la porte bleue!
examples.trans: I am walking forward... oh, I see the golden key and the blue door!

meanings.note: avoir mal au dos = to have backache; final s is silent

examples.text: J'ai mal au dos.
examples.trans: My back hurts.

examples.text: Il tourne le dos.
examples.trans: He turns his back.

examples.text: Oui, un médicament. J'ai mal au dos.
examples.trans: Yes, some medicine. My back hurts.

related.gloss: to have backache; final s is silent

examples.text: Le dossier est sur le bureau.
examples.trans: The file is on the desk.

examples.text: C'est un gros dossier.
examples.trans: It's a big case.

meanings.note: Un agent double = a double agent. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'double'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Tu es un agent double!
examples.trans: You are a double agent!

examples.text: Une double ration.
examples.trans: A double portion.

examples.text: Le double d'aujourd'hui! On ouvre vraiment le café de la cour aux gens de la rue?
examples.trans: Double what I make today! Are we really opening the courtyard cafe to the street?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la doublure', plural 'les doublures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'stand-in'.

examples.text: Une doublure pour créer un fantôme.
examples.trans: A stand-in to create a ghost.

examples.text: Le public va reconnaître la doublure.
examples.trans: The audience will recognize the stand-in.

meanings.note: Parler doucement.
Vas-y doucement = take it easy.

examples.text: Marche doucement.
examples.trans: Walk slowly.

examples.text: Je tourne doucement... écoutez! L'eau remplit le tuyau!
examples.trans: Turning slowly... listen! Water is filling the pipe!

examples.text: Tournez le volant bleu doucement vers la gauche, pas trop vite.
examples.trans: Turn the blue wheel slowly to the left, not too fast.

meanings.note: prendre une douche = to take a shower

examples.text: Une douche chaude.
examples.trans: A hot shower.

examples.text: Dieu merci! Et les douches du matin?
examples.trans: Thank goodness! And the morning showers?

meanings.note: Sans douleur / aucune douleur = pain-free, no pain.

examples.text: Après deux jours de repos, je n'ai plus aucune douleur.
examples.trans: After two days of rest, I have no pain at all anymore.

examples.text: La glace calme vite la douleur à la cheville.
examples.trans: Ice quickly soothes the pain in the ankle.

examples.text: Un souvenir douloureux.
examples.trans: A painful memory.

examples.text: Une expérience douloureuse.
examples.trans: A painful experience.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le doute', plural 'les doutes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'doubt'.

examples.text: Sans aucun doute.
examples.trans: Without any doubt.

examples.text: Au moindre doute, elle dégage.
examples.trans: At the slightest doubt, she is out.

examples.text: J'avais un doute sur ce projet.
examples.trans: I had a doubt about this project.

meanings.note: J'en doute: I doubt it.

examples.text: J'en doute.
examples.trans: I doubt it.

examples.text: Je doute de lui.
examples.trans: I have doubts about him.

meanings.note: Sois douce = be gentle. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sweet'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une voix douce.
examples.trans: A soft voice.

examples.text: Et regardez, ce gilet doux en laine est propre et neuf. Essayez-le.
examples.trans: And look, this soft wool cardigan is clean and new. Try it on.

examples.text: Et j'ai deux oreillers doux et un tapis bleu tissé dans la réserve!
examples.trans: And I have two soft pillows and a woven blue rug in the storeroom!

meanings.note: Feminine noun followed by de before a noun: une douzaine d'œufs, deux douzaines de chaises.

examples.text: Au marché, la douzaine d'œufs coûte moins cher.
examples.trans: At the market, a dozen eggs costs less.

examples.text: Nous avons commandé une douzaine de tasses assorties.
examples.trans: We ordered a dozen matching cups.

meanings.note: douze heures = twelve o'clock / twelve hours

examples.text: Juste ici! Tout a coûté trente-huit euros, alors voici douze euros de monnaie.
examples.trans: Right here! Everything cost thirty-eight euros, so here is twelve euros in change.

examples.text: Dix, onze, douze. Le compte est bon au centime près, merci!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last cent, thank you!

examples.text: Attendez une minute... Numéro douze, {STREET}, et deux initiales d'enfance écrites dans le coin!
examples.trans: Wait a moment... Number twelve, {STREET}, and two childhood initials written in the corner!

meanings.note: Doué pour = good at.

examples.text: Tu es douée!
examples.trans: You're gifted!

examples.text: Il est doué pour le piano.
examples.trans: He's good at the piano.

meanings.en: the most senior member of a group
meanings.note: Feminine: doyenne.
Of a university faculty.

examples.text: Arlette est la doyenne des agents.
examples.trans: Arlette is the most senior of the agents.

examples.text: C'est le doyen de l'équipe.
examples.trans: He's the oldest member of the team.

draguer.gloss: to flirt with, to hit on

meanings.en: to hit on, to flirt with
meanings.note: Draguer quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to flirt with'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dragué').

examples.text: Draguer son patron au bureau.
examples.trans: To hit on one's boss at the office.

examples.text: Draguer son patron dans une boucherie?
examples.trans: Hitting on her boss in a butcher shop?

examples.text: On ne drague jamais les clients.
examples.trans: We never flirt with clients.

meanings.note: Un film dramatique. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un vrai rôle dans un film dramatique.
examples.trans: A real role in a dramatic film.

examples.text: Une pièce dramatique.
examples.trans: A dramatic play.

examples.text: C'est un art dramatique puissant.
examples.trans: It is powerful dramatic art.

meanings.en: faire un drame = to make a big fuss

meanings.note: An everyday dramatic word for a problem, as well as a drama in theatre or cinema.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas un drame.
examples.trans: It's not a big drama.

examples.text: Il y a eu un drame sur le tournage.
examples.trans: There was a crisis on the shoot.

meanings.note: Final p is silent: /dʁa/.

examples.text: J'apporte des draps blancs propres de l'armoire à linge!
examples.trans: I will bring clean white sheets from the linen cupboard!

examples.text: Borde bien le coin du drap, Claire! Et voilà les deux oreillers doux.
examples.trans: Tuck the sheet corner tight, Claire! Here go the two soft pillows.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la drogue', plural 'les drogues') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'drug'.

examples.text: Ma seule drogue, c'est les fruits secs.
examples.trans: My only drug is dried fruit.

examples.text: Ma seule drogue, ce sont les fruits secs!
examples.trans: My only drug is dried fruit!

meanings.note: se tenir droit(e) = to stand up straight
À droite = on the right.

examples.text: Tournez à droite.
examples.trans: Turn right.

examples.text: À droite, près du bureau, là où la lumière est bonne.
examples.trans: On the right, near the desk, where the light is good.

meanings.en: right, right-hand side (à droite = to the right, on the right)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la droite', plural 'les droites') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'right'.

examples.text: Tournez à droite.
examples.trans: Turn right.

examples.text: Prendre à droite.
examples.trans: To take the right.

examples.text: Ici, on tourne à droite.
examples.trans: Here, we turn right.

meanings.note: After the noun: un film très drôle.
Before the noun: une drôle d'idée.

examples.text: Très drôle, très moderne.
examples.trans: Very funny, very modern.

examples.text: Cette histoire est drôle.
examples.trans: This story is funny.

examples.text: Très paisible! Mais vous avez entendu un drôle de choc métallique à l'instant?
examples.trans: Very peaceful! Though did you hear a funny metallic knock just now?

meanings.note: Contraction of de + le. In la cause du décès it connects the cause with the death being discussed.
for things you can't count; de la (feminine)

examples.text: C'est du compost.
examples.trans: It's compost.

examples.text: Je veux du pain.
examples.trans: I want some bread.

meanings.note: Masculine: le duc.

examples.text: Oui, elle fait le ménage pour la duchesse.
examples.trans: Yes, she does the cleaning for the duchess.

examples.text: La duchesse habite dans un château.
examples.trans: The duchess lives in a castle.

examples.text: Baissez les yeux devant la duchesse!
examples.trans: Lower your eyes before the duchess!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le duo', plural 'les duos') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'duo'.

examples.text: Les deux acteurs forment un duo comique parfait.
examples.trans: The two actors form a perfect comic duo.

examples.text: Ils chantent un beau duo sur scène.
examples.trans: They sing a beautiful duet on stage.

meanings.note: Physically hard, or hard to bear.
C'est dur = it's tough.

examples.text: La vie est dure.
examples.trans: Life is hard.

examples.text: Il faisait toujours le dur pendant cinq secondes, puis il souriait.
examples.trans: He always acted tough for five seconds, then smiled.

examples.text: Ça n'a pas duré un mois!
examples.trans: It didn't last a month!

examples.text: Le film dure deux heures.
examples.trans: The film lasts two hours.

examples.text: C'est ridicule. Ça n'a pas duré un mois!
examples.trans: That's ridiculous. It didn't last a month!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la dureté', plural 'les duretés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hardness'.

examples.text: Les affaires demandent de la dureté.
examples.trans: Business demands toughness.

examples.text: Elle montre la dureté de cette époque.
examples.trans: It shows the harshness of that era.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Le réalisateur veut une scène dynamique.
examples.trans: The director wants a dynamic scene.

examples.text: C'est une équipe très dynamique.
examples.trans: It is a very dynamic team.

examples.text: Le réalisateur Gary veut une scène plus dynamique.
examples.trans: Director Gary wants a more dynamic scene.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le dynamisme', plural 'les dynamismes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'dynamism'.

examples.text: Le dynamisme de cette scène est essentiel.
examples.trans: The dynamism of this scene is essential.

examples.text: Elle a un grand dynamisme.
examples.trans: She has great dynamism.

examples.text: Isabelle, le dynamisme est très important aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Isabelle, dynamism is very important today.

meanings.en: from, starting from, as soon as
meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'from', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Rappelle-moi dès que possible.
examples.trans: Call me back as soon as possible.

examples.text: Dès demain matin à huit heures!
examples.trans: Starting tomorrow morning at eight!

examples.text: Dès demain matin à huit heures! Quatre tables dedans, trois tables sous le tilleul!
examples.trans: Starting tomorrow morning at eight! Four tables inside, three tables under the linden tree!

dé.gloss: small cube ('en dés' = diced); die; thimble

meanings.en: small cube (in cooking: *couper en dés* = to dice); die
meanings.note: From dice cubes: *un dé de carotte / couper en petits dés* means cutting vegetables or cheese into neat little cubes.

examples.text: Coupez les carottes et les pommes de terre en petits dés.
examples.trans: Cut the carrots and potatoes into small cubes.

examples.text: Ajoutez quelques dés de fromage frais sur la soupe chaude.
examples.trans: Add a few cubes of fresh cheese on top of the hot soup.

meanings.note: dé-talquer le visage = to wipe talc from the face

examples.text: Dé-talquer la peau.
examples.trans: To remove talc from the skin.

examples.text: Je la dé-talque tout de suite.
examples.trans: I will remove the talc right away.

examples.text: Je dois la dé-talquer complètement?
examples.trans: Should I completely de-talc her?

débarquer.gloss: to turn up, show up, disembark

meanings.note: débarquer quelque part = to show up uninvited
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to turn up'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'débarqué').

examples.text: Débarquer dans une salle de sport.
examples.trans: Turning up in a gym.

examples.text: Il a débarqué sans prévenir.
examples.trans: He turned up without warning.

examples.text: Débarquer dans une salle de sport pour me parler!
examples.trans: Turning up in a gym to speak to me!

meanings.note: To clear a table or clear away clutter ('se débarrasser de' = get rid of).

examples.text: J'ai débarrassé la grande table pour déplier les plans.
examples.trans: I cleared off the big table to unfold the plans.

examples.text: Voulez-vous que je vous débarrasse de votre manteau?
examples.trans: Would you like me to take your coat for you?

related.gloss: to put away, tidy up, store neatly

meanings.note: le haut débit = high-speed broadband

examples.text: Une ligne à très haut débit.
examples.trans: A very high-speed broadband line.

examples.text: Un débit rapide.
examples.trans: A fast flow rate.

examples.text: C'est du très haut débit pour vous.
examples.trans: It is high-speed broadband for you.

meanings.note: To free something stuck or jammed; to unlock funds or a situation.

examples.text: Une goutte d'huile suffit à débloquer la vieille serrure.
examples.trans: A drop of oil is enough to free the old lock.

examples.text: Doucement, le levier débloque la pierre sans la casser.
examples.trans: Gently, the lever loosens the stone without breaking it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Grâce à ton énergie débordante.
examples.trans: Thanks to your overflowing energy.

examples.text: Un enthousiasme débordant sur le plateau.
examples.trans: An overflowing enthusiasm on the set.

examples.text: Grâce à ton énergie débordante, Andréa.
examples.trans: Thanks to your overflowing energy, Andrea.

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Elle est débordée, ne l'embêtons pas.
examples.trans: She is swamped, let's not bother her.

examples.text: Je sais, tu es débordée.
examples.trans: I know, you're swamped.

meanings.note: Transitive use: débrouiller quelque chose.
Reflexive use: se débrouiller. The scene uses the command débrouille-toi.

examples.text: François, débrouille-toi!
examples.trans: François, manage on your own!

examples.text: Elle se débrouille très bien.
examples.trans: She gets by very well.

examples.text: François, débrouille-toi! Tu es comédien, fais quelque chose!
examples.trans: François, manage on your own! You are an actor, do something!

meanings.note: débusquer des talents = to track down talent

examples.text: Il faut les observer et les débusquer.
examples.trans: You have to observe and track them down.

examples.text: Débusquer un acteur prometteur.
examples.trans: To flush out a promising actor.

examples.text: Il faut observer et les débusquer!
examples.trans: You have to observe and track them down!

meanings.note: au début = at first, at the beginning

examples.text: Au début, c'était difficile.
examples.trans: At first it was hard.

examples.text: C'est le début du film.
examples.trans: It's the start of the film.

meanings.note: False friend: not 'deception'.

examples.text: Je comprends ta déception.
examples.trans: I understand your disappointment.

examples.text: Quelle déception!
examples.trans: What a disappointment!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la décharge', plural 'les décharges') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'release'.

examples.text: Écrire dans un journal permet une vraie décharge d'émotion.
examples.trans: Writing in a diary allows a real release of emotion.

examples.text: Le médecin lui a fait signer une décharge.
examples.trans: The doctor had him sign a release form.

meanings.en: to unload (a van, cart, or crate)
meanings.note: Takes an -e- after -g- before a/o to keep the soft /ʒ/ sound: nous déchargeons, il déchargeait.

examples.text: Les livreurs déchargent les caisses devant le portail.
examples.trans: The deliverymen are unloading the crates in front of the gate.

examples.text: Aidez-moi à décharger le coffre avant l'averse!
examples.trans: Help me unload the boot before the rain shower!

meanings.note: Pour ne pas déchirer le papier = 'so as not to tear the paper'.

examples.text: Ouvrez l'enveloppe doucement pour ne pas déchirer la carte.
examples.trans: Open the envelope gently so you don't tear the card.

examples.text: Le vieux papier sec se déchire au moindre geste brusque.
examples.trans: Dry old paper tears at the slightest sudden movement.

meanings.note: Unit of sound level.

examples.text: Regardez bien cette page: elle mesure les décibels et le calme, pas les étoiles d'hôtel!
examples.trans: Look closely at this page: it measures decibels and quietness, not hotel stars!

examples.text: Les décibels? Alors neuf sur dix, ce n'était pas une note pour mon accueil?
examples.trans: Decibels? So nine out of ten was not a score for my welcome?

examples.text: Attendez qu'Étienne apprenne qu'il a paniqué toute la nuit pour des décibels!
examples.trans: Wait until Etienne learns he panicked all night over decibels!

meanings.note: C'est décidé = it's decided.

examples.text: C'est décidé.
examples.trans: It's decided.

examples.text: Je décide demain.
examples.trans: I'll decide tomorrow.

meanings.note: Common collocation: *prendre une décision* ('to make a decision', literally 'take') and *sage décision* ('wise decision').

examples.text: Rentrer les meubles avant la pluie était une sage décision.
examples.trans: Bringing the furniture inside before the rain was a wise decision.

examples.text: Nous prenons chaque décision importante tous ensemble.
examples.trans: We make every important decision all together.

meanings.note: déclaration de naissance = birth declaration

examples.text: La déclaration de naissance de l'enfant.
examples.trans: The birth declaration of the child.

examples.text: Une déclaration officielle à la mairie.
examples.trans: An official declaration at town hall.

examples.text: Il vient pour la déclaration de naissance?
examples.trans: Is he coming for the birth declaration?

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to declare'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'déclaré').

examples.text: Je déclare la fête ouverte.
examples.trans: I declare the celebration open.

examples.text: Il déclare son amour.
examples.trans: He declares his love.

examples.text: Je déclare ouvert ce grand festival!
examples.trans: I declare open this great festival!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to decline'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'décliné').

examples.text: Je décline votre offre.
examples.trans: I decline your offer.

examples.text: Ça sonne bien, mais je décline.
examples.trans: It sounds good, but I decline.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to unwind'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'décompressé').

examples.text: Nous allons enfin pouvoir décompresser.
