examples.trans: We are finally going to be able to unwind.

examples.text: Prends le temps de décompresser ce week-end.
examples.trans: Take time to unwind this weekend.

examples.text: Nous allons enfin pouvoir décompresser ensemble.
examples.trans: We are finally going to be able to unwind together.

meanings.en: set, scenery, decor (sur le décor = on set)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le décor', plural 'les décors') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'set'.

examples.text: On t'attend sur le décor.
examples.trans: We are waiting for you on set.

examples.text: On t'attend sur le décor maintenant.
examples.trans: We are waiting for you on set now.

meanings.en: to discourage; se décourager = to lose heart

examples.text: Ne te décourage pas.
examples.trans: Don't lose heart.

examples.text: Il ne faut pas se décourager.
examples.trans: You must not get discouraged.

meanings.note: La découverte de talents. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Standard feminine noun meaning 'discovery, find'.

examples.text: J'aime l'excitation de la découverte.
examples.trans: I like the excitement of discovery.

examples.text: C'est une belle découverte pour nous.
examples.trans: It is a fine discovery for us.

examples.text: Enchanté, Camille, bravo pour cette découverte!
examples.trans: Delighted, Camille, congratulations on this discovery!

meanings.note: Conjugated like 'ouvrir'.

examples.text: Colette Brancillon va le découvrir.
examples.trans: Colette Brancillon is going to find out.

examples.text: On a découvert la vérité.
examples.trans: We found out the truth.

examples.text: Colette Brancillon va le découvrir. Je voulais juste vous prévenir.
examples.trans: Colette Brancillon is going to find out. I just wanted to warn you.

meanings.note: décrocher une audition = to land an audition

examples.text: Elle t'a décroché l'audition.
examples.trans: She landed you the audition.

examples.text: Décrocher le téléphone.
examples.trans: To pick up the phone.

examples.text: Noémie s'est battue pour te décrocher l'audition.
examples.trans: Noemie fought hard to land you the audition.

meanings.note: The singular and plural have the same written form.

examples.text: La cause du décès est inconnue.
examples.trans: The cause of death is unknown.

examples.text: Le décès est confirmé.
examples.trans: The death is confirmed.

meanings.note: formal, official: used by doctors, officials, in letters

examples.text: Il est décédé hier.
examples.trans: He passed away yesterday.

examples.text: Sa mère est décédée.
examples.trans: Her mother has passed away.

examples.text: Non. La dédicace suffit.
examples.trans: No. The dedication is enough.

examples.text: Une belle dédicace.
examples.trans: A nice dedication.

examples.text: Juste la dédicace?
examples.trans: Just the dedication?

meanings.en: to dedicate, to autograph, to sign (a book/record)

examples.text: Je vais le dédicacer.
examples.trans: I am going to sign it.

examples.text: L'auteur dédicace son roman.
examples.trans: The author signs his novel.

examples.text: Ils veulent seulement des photos dédicacées!
examples.trans: They only want autographed photos!

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Core French verb meaning 'to deduce, infer'.

examples.text: J'en déduis que tout va bien.
examples.trans: I deduce from it that all is well.

examples.text: On peut en déduire une règle.
examples.trans: One can deduce a rule from it.

examples.text: J'en déduis que les bijoux Chopard sont arrivés. Bonjour.
examples.trans: I deduce that the Chopard jewelry has arrived. Hello.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le défaut', plural 'les défauts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'flaw'.

examples.text: Un grand défaut.
examples.trans: A major flaw.

examples.text: Chacun a ses défauts.
examples.trans: Everyone has their flaws.

examples.text: Je sens venir un grand défaut!
examples.trans: I feel a big flaw coming!

meanings.en: to defend, to stand up for
meanings.note: Défendre quelqu'un.
Défendre de + infinitive, formal.

examples.text: Tu ne me défends pas.
examples.trans: You don't stand up for me.

examples.text: Un agent défend ses clients.
examples.trans: An agent defends his clients.

meanings.en: to challenge, to dare, to defy
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to challenge'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'défié').

examples.text: Tu m'as défié au jeu.
examples.trans: You challenged me to the game.

examples.text: Il défie les lois.
examples.trans: He defies the laws.

examples.text: Tu m'as défié au jeu?
examples.trans: You challenged me to the game?

meanings.note: Être défiguré = to be disfigured. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to disfigure'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'défiguré').

examples.text: Je suis complètement défigurée!
examples.trans: I am completely disfigured!

examples.text: La blessure lui défigure le visage.
examples.trans: The wound disfigures her face.

examples.text: Vous plaisantez! Je suis complètement défigurée!
examples.trans: Are you joking! I am completely disfigured!

meanings.note: Un défilé de mode = a fashion show. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Standard masculine noun meaning 'fashion show, parade'.

examples.text: Je ne fais pas de défilés.
examples.trans: I do not do fashion shows.

examples.text: Assister à un défilé.
examples.trans: To attend a fashion show.

examples.text: Elle a un défilé et des essayages.
examples.trans: She has a fashion show and costume fittings.

meanings.note: Définir quelqu'un.

examples.text: Il faut d'abord bien définir les termes du contrat.
examples.trans: First we need to clearly define the terms of the contract.

examples.text: Comment peut-on définir son nouveau rôle?
examples.trans: How can we define her new role?

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Une décision définitive.
examples.trans: A final decision.

examples.text: Le résultat définitif.
examples.trans: The final result.

examples.text: Pour moi, ma vie personnelle est définitive.
examples.trans: For me, my personal life is definitive.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Elle est partie définitivement.
examples.trans: She left for good.

examples.text: Elle m'a définitivement quitté.
examples.trans: She definitely left me.

examples.text: Perdre Dany fermerait définitivement notre agence.
examples.trans: Losing Dany would permanently close our agency.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to smash'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'défoncé').

examples.text: J'ai défoncé la porte.
examples.trans: I smashed the door.

examples.text: J'ai défoncé cette porte vingt-sept fois!
examples.trans: I smashed through that door twenty-seven times!

dégager.gloss: to clear out, to get out

meanings.en: to get out, to clear off (colloquial)

examples.text: Tu t'excuses et tu dégages!
examples.trans: You apologize and you get out!

examples.text: Dégage d'ici!
examples.trans: Get out of here!

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: La route est bien dégagée.
examples.trans: The road is very clear.

examples.text: Le ciel est dégagé.
examples.trans: The sky is clear.

examples.text: La route est totalement dégagée.
examples.trans: The road is completely clear.

meanings.note: La cheville a dégonflé = the swelling in the ankle has gone down.

examples.text: Avec le coussin et le repos, ma cheville a bien dégonflé.
examples.trans: With the cushion and rest, the swelling in my ankle has really gone down.

examples.text: Laisse la pâte lever doucement sans la dégonfler.
examples.trans: Let the dough rise gently without deflating it.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to disgust'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dégoûté').

examples.text: Tu me dégoûtes.
examples.trans: You disgust me.

examples.text: Mathias, tu me dégoûtes vraiment!
examples.trans: Mathias, you really disgust me!

meanings.en: sobering up (cellule de dégrisement = drunk tank)
meanings.note: Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum'). Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Standard masculine noun meaning 'sobering up'.

examples.text: En cellule de dégrisement.
examples.trans: In the sobering-up cell.

examples.text: Par ici. Il est en cellule de dégrisement.
examples.trans: This way. He is in the sobering-up cell.

meanings.note: Se déguiser en. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to disguise'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'déguisé').

examples.text: Se déguiser et se faire tirer dessus, ce n'est pas mon truc.
examples.trans: Dressing up and being shot at is not my thing.

examples.text: Les enfants se déguisent pour la fête.
examples.trans: The children dress up for the party.

dégénérer.gloss: to degenerate, escalate, get out of hand

meanings.note: La situation dégénère. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to degenerate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dégénéré').

examples.text: Si Sacha les voit, ça va dégénérer.
examples.trans: If Sacha sees them, things will escalate.

examples.text: Le débat a dégénéré.
examples.trans: The debate degenerated.

examples.text: Tout a dégénéré avec Ben Stiller.
examples.trans: Everything fell apart with Ben Stiller.

meanings.note: Le déjeuner = lunch (noun).
Also a noun.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes avec Dany Boon.
examples.trans: You're having lunch with Dany Boon.

examples.text: On déjeune à midi?
examples.trans: Shall we have lunch at noon?

meanings.note: For something already done.
In a question, can ask about previous experience: tu es déjà venu?

examples.text: Déjà midi!
examples.trans: Midday already!

examples.text: Touchez le tuyau en cuivre! Il chauffe déjà!
examples.trans: Touch the copper pipe! It is warming up already!

examples.text: Gardez la maison, je suis déjà dehors!
examples.trans: Hold the fort, I am already outside!

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: C'est une affaire délicate.
examples.trans: It is a delicate matter.

examples.text: Il est très délicat.
examples.trans: He is very tactful.

examples.text: Camille m'a beaucoup aidé sur une affaire délicate cette semaine. Et on fête ça.
examples.trans: Camille helped me a lot on a delicate matter this week. And we're celebrating that.

examples.text: On pourrait avoir un peu de délicatesse?
examples.trans: Could we have a little delicacy?

examples.text: Avec beaucoup de délicatesse.
examples.trans: With great gentleness.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: L'eau est délicieuse.
examples.trans: The water is lovely.

examples.text: L'eau est délicieuse, tu peux essayer.
examples.trans: The water is lovely, you can try.

examples.text: Les œufs brouillés sont délicieux, {F1}. Fais mes compliments à {F2}!
examples.trans: The scrambled eggs are delicious, {F1}. Tell {F2} my compliments!

meanings.note: c'est un délit = it's a crime / offense

examples.text: C'est un délit.
examples.trans: It's an offense.

examples.text: C'est un délit. Désolée. Au revoir.
examples.trans: It's an offense. Sorry. Goodbye.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le démantèlement', plural 'les démantèlements') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'dismantling'.

examples.text: Il faut éviter le démantèlement de l'agence.
examples.trans: We must avoid dismantling the agency.

examples.text: Il faut éviter le démantèlement d'ASK.
examples.trans: We must avoid asset stripping ASK.

meanings.note: Une démarche artistique. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Standard feminine noun meaning 'approach, process'.
Faire des démarches. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Standard feminine noun meaning 'approach, process'.

examples.text: Bien sûr, nous respectons votre démarche.
examples.trans: Of course, we respect your approach.

examples.text: C'est une démarche très originale.
examples.trans: It is a very original approach.

examples.text: On prépare toutes les démarches discrètement.
examples.trans: We prepare all the paperwork discreetly.

meanings.note: For a vehicle or engine to start and pull away; to get a project underway.

examples.text: Le bus démarre doucement après le coup de sifflet.
examples.trans: The bus pulls away gently after the whistle.

examples.text: La journée démarre toujours par un café bien chaud.
examples.trans: The day always starts with a piping hot coffee.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to resign'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'démissionné').

examples.text: Il a décidé de démissionner.
examples.trans: He decided to resign.

examples.text: Nous devrions tous démissionner ensemble.
examples.trans: We should all resign together.

meanings.note: Démolir la rivale. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Core French verb meaning 'to demolish, to crush'.

examples.text: Allez, Noémie, démolis la rivale!
examples.trans: Go on, Noémie, crush the rival!

examples.text: Démolir un mur.
examples.trans: To demolish a wall.

examples.text: Elle va démolir Brancillon!
examples.trans: She's going to destroy Brancillon!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le démon', plural 'les démons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'demon'.

examples.text: Il est comme un démon.
examples.trans: He is like a demon.

examples.text: Chasser ses démons.
examples.trans: To banish one's demons.

examples.text: Il est comme un vrai démon sauvage!
examples.trans: He is like a true wild demon!

démonter.gloss: to take down, take off hinges, disassemble

meanings.en: to take down, unhinge, take apart
meanings.note: Opposite of *monter / remonter*; used for taking shutters off their hinges or disassembling furniture.

examples.text: Nous avons démonté les vieux volets pour les poncer à plat.
examples.trans: We took the old shutters off their hinges to sand them flat.

examples.text: Il démonte la serrure avec un petit tournevis.
examples.trans: He takes the lock apart with a small screwdriver.

examples.text: Si je n'avais pas déménagé à Paris.
examples.trans: If I hadn't moved to Paris.

examples.text: Ils ont déménagé hier.
examples.trans: They moved yesterday.

examples.text: Si je n'avais pas déménagé à Paris...
examples.trans: If I had not moved to Paris,

meanings.note: From déménager ('to move house').

examples.text: Avant que les déménageurs ne vident la maison, j'ai sauvé cette boîte de l'étagère du grenier.
examples.trans: Before the movers cleared the house, I saved this box from the attic shelf.

examples.text: Voici le déménageur sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the mover, removal worker on the table.

meanings.note: To untie a ribbon, knot, or shoelace; figuratively to unravel a mystery.

examples.text: Dénouez le ruban avec précaution pour le garder intact.
examples.trans: Untie the ribbon carefully to keep it intact.

examples.text: Le dernier indice finit par dénouer toute l'énigme.
examples.trans: The final clue ends up unraveling the whole riddle.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to strip'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dénudé').

examples.text: L'actrice refuse de se dénuder.
examples.trans: The actress refuses to appear nude.

examples.text: Cette scène oblige à se dénuder.
examples.trans: This scene requires undressing.

examples.text: L'actrice accepte de se dénuder au tournage.
examples.trans: The actress agrees to appear nude during shooting.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le dépannage', plural 'les dépannages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'help'.
Masculine noun ('le dépannage', plural 'les dépannages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'towing service'.

examples.text: C'était un simple dépannage.
examples.trans: It was just a favor.

examples.text: Pas du tout, c'était un dépannage.
examples.trans: Not at all, it was a favor.

meanings.note: Avant mon départ = before I leave.

examples.text: Avant mon départ, une réunion.
examples.trans: Before I leave, a meeting.

examples.text: Le départ est à midi.
examples.trans: Departure is at noon.

meanings.note: dépasser les bornes = to cross the line
Sur la route.

examples.text: Tu dépasses les bornes avec lui.
examples.trans: You're crossing the line with him.

examples.text: Henri, vous m'entendez? Je viens de dépasser la pharmacie verte!
examples.trans: Henri, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: ça dépend = it depends; dépendre de = to depend on

examples.text: Ça dépend.
examples.trans: It depends.

examples.text: Ça dépend du jour.
examples.trans: It depends on the day.

meanings.note: Notice French distinguishes spending money (dépenser de l'argent) from spending time (passer du temps).

examples.text: Nous avons dépensé moins que prévu au marché ce matin.
examples.trans: We spent less than planned at the market this morning.

examples.text: Inutile de dépenser beaucoup quand on répare soi-même.
examples.trans: There is no need to spend a lot when you repair things yourself.

meanings.en: to move, displace; (se déplacer) to travel, go to a place
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to move'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'déplacé').

examples.text: Se déplacer en ville.
examples.trans: To move around town.

examples.text: On peut déplacer quatre cartons en cinq minutes. Allons voir tout de suite!
examples.trans: We can move four boxes in five minutes. Let us go look right now!

meanings.en: to unfold (chairs, a tablecloth, a map)
meanings.note: Opposite of plier ('to fold').

examples.text: Déplions six chaises supplémentaires sous l'arbre.
examples.trans: Let's unfold six extra chairs under the tree.

examples.text: Elle déplie une grande nappe blanche sur la table.
examples.trans: She unfolds a big white tablecloth over the table.

meanings.en: frosted, etched, matte (du verre dépoli = frosted glass)
meanings.note: Literally 'un-polished' (dé- + poli): glass whose surface has been dulled so it softens bright glare into an even glow.

examples.text: Le globe en verre dépoli adoucit la lumière de l'ampoule.
examples.trans: The frosted-glass globe softens the light from the bulb.

examples.text: Une porte vitrée dépolie sépare la cuisine du couloir.
examples.trans: A frosted-glass door separates the kitchen from the hallway.

meanings.en: to drop off (someone), set down, deposit
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to drop off'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'déposé').

examples.text: Tu peux me déposer?
examples.trans: Can you drop me off?

examples.text: Tu peux me déposer au tournage? C'est sur la route.
examples.trans: Can you drop me off at the shoot? It's on the way.

examples.text: Qui a déposé ces affaires ici?
examples.trans: Who dropped off these things here?

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to depress'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'déprimé').

examples.text: La maison me déprime.
examples.trans: The house depresses me.

examples.text: Ce temps me déprime.
examples.trans: This weather depresses me.

examples.text: La maison de mes parents me déprime. Re-réserve un billet!
examples.trans: My parents' house depresses me. Rebook a ticket!

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Je suis plutôt déprimé.
examples.trans: I am rather depressed.

examples.text: Il se sent déprimé aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: He feels down today.

examples.text: Moi, je suis plutôt déprimé. J'ai raté un film de James Bond.
examples.trans: Me, I'm pretty depressed. I missed out on a James Bond movie.

meanings.en: to hurry, to rush; se dépêcher = to hurry up
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to hurry'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dépêché').

examples.text: Il faut se dépêcher, c'est loin.
examples.trans: We must hurry, it is far.

examples.text: Par ici, dépêchons-nous un peu!
examples.trans: This way, let us hurry up a bit!

examples.text: Dépêche-toi, le casting commence maintenant.
examples.trans: Hurry up, the casting is starting now.

meanings.note: Pardon pour le dérangement = sorry for the trouble.

examples.text: Pardon pour tout ce dérangement, Henri. Merci d'avoir gardé ce sac toute la semaine.
examples.trans: Sorry for all this trouble, Henri. Thank you for guarding this bag all week.

examples.text: Voici le dérangement sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the trouble, inconvenience, bother on the table.

meanings.note: désolé(e) de vous déranger = sorry to bother you

examples.text: Je ne veux pas te déranger.
examples.trans: I don't want to disturb you.

examples.text: Vraiment? Les étages en plus ne vous dérangent pas?
examples.trans: Really? The extra floors do not bother you?

meanings.note: un désastre financier = a financial disaster

examples.text: C'est un véritable désastre.
examples.trans: It is a real disaster.

examples.text: Éviter le désastre.
examples.trans: To avoid disaster.

examples.text: Des acteurs qui se séparent, c'est un désastre. Le film va faire un bide.
examples.trans: Actors splitting up is a disaster. The movie is going to flop.

meanings.note: déserter pendant la guerre = to desert during the war

examples.text: Le soldat a déserté.
examples.trans: The soldier deserted.

examples.text: Déserter les salles de cinéma.
examples.trans: To desert movie theaters.

examples.text: Ce pauvre homme déserte pendant la guerre.
examples.trans: This poor man deserts during the war.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le déserteur', plural 'les déserteurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'deserter'.

examples.text: C'était le début du Déserteur.
examples.trans: It was the beginning of The Deserter.

examples.text: Le déserteur a fui son régiment.
examples.trans: The deserter fled his regiment.

examples.text: La fin du Déserteur, ça se fête!
examples.trans: The end of The Deserter calls for a celebration!

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Il cherchait désespérément.
examples.trans: He was searching desperately.

examples.text: Oui, je cherche désespérément Sofia.
examples.trans: Yes, I am desperately looking for Sofia.

meanings.en: to undress, to strip; se déshabiller = undress oneself
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to strip'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'déshabillé').

examples.text: Elle me demande de me déshabiller.
examples.trans: She asks me to undress.

examples.text: Cette femme me demande de me déshabiller!
examples.trans: This woman is asking me to strip!

examples.text: Trouve une autre idée sans me déshabiller!
examples.trans: Find another idea without undressing me!

meanings.note: Avoir le désir de = to desire to.

examples.text: Sa peur de la mort, le désir, le plaisir!
examples.trans: His fear of death, desire, pleasure!

examples.text: C'est mon plus grand désir.
examples.trans: It is my greatest desire.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas son désir qui l'empêche d'être fidèle.
examples.trans: It isn't his desire that stops him being faithful.

meanings.en: to desire, to want, to wish for
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to wish for'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'désiré').

examples.text: Les réalisateurs aiment se sentir désirés.
examples.trans: Directors like to feel desired.

examples.text: Les réalisateurs aiment aussi se sentir désirés.
examples.trans: Directors also like to feel wanted.

examples.text: Oui madame, que désirez-vous?
examples.trans: Yes madam, what would you like?

meanings.note: je suis désolé(e) = I'm sorry; désolé! alone also works

examples.text: Désolé, c'est tout.
examples.trans: Sorry, that's all. (a man speaking)

examples.text: Ils n'ont rien pour l'instant, madame, je suis vraiment désolé.
examples.trans: They have nothing for now, madam, I am truly sorry.

examples.text: Excusez le désordre dans le bureau.
examples.trans: Excuse the mess in the office.

examples.text: Tout est en désordre ici.
examples.trans: Everything is in a mess here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Tout change désormais.
examples.trans: Everything changes from now on.

examples.text: Nos petites erreurs semblent insignifiantes désormais.
examples.trans: Our little mistakes seem insignificant now.

examples.text: Tu joues, c'est ton métier désormais.
examples.trans: You act, it is your job from now on.

meanings.en: to destabilize, throw off balance, unnerve
meanings.note: Déstabiliser un adversaire. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to destabilize'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'déstabilisé').

examples.text: Je peux la déstabiliser si tu veux.
examples.trans: I can destabilize her if you want.

examples.text: La question l'a déstabilisé.
examples.trans: The question threw him off balance.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to relieve stress'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'déstressé').

examples.text: J'ai besoin de fumer pour déstresser.
examples.trans: I need to smoke to de-stress.

examples.text: Cette promenade l'aide à déstresser.
examples.trans: This walk helps him de-stress.

examples.text: J'ai taxé une clope pour déstresser.
examples.trans: I bummed a smoke to de-stress.

meanings.note: A small individual aspect of something; plural détails.

examples.text: Ne perdons pas de temps sur les détails.
examples.trans: Let's not waste time on details.

examples.text: C'est un détail.
examples.trans: It's a detail.

examples.text: Elle vous expliquera tous les détails.
examples.trans: She will explain all the details to you.

meanings.note: Se détendre = to relax (oneself). Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Core French verb meaning 'to relax'.

examples.text: Commence par te détendre.
examples.trans: Start by relaxing.

examples.text: Détends-toi!
examples.trans: Relax!

examples.text: J'ai quelque chose pour se détendre.
examples.trans: I have something to relax.

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Je suis très calme et détendu.
examples.trans: I am very calm and relaxed.

examples.text: Une allure détendue.
examples.trans: A relaxed look.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la détermination', plural 'les déterminations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'determination'.

examples.text: Notre détermination est totale.
examples.trans: Our determination is complete.

examples.text: Ne sous-estime jamais notre détermination, Élise.
examples.trans: Never underestimate our determination, Elise.

meanings.note: To uncover something buried in the ground or hidden in archives.

examples.text: Ils ont déterré un coffret en fer-blanc sous la dalle.
examples.trans: They unearthed a tin box beneath the flagstone.

examples.text: L'archiviste a déterré une photographie centenaire du quartier.
examples.trans: The archivist dug up a century-old photograph of the neighborhood.

examples.text: Pour vous dire la vérité, je déteste le bruit du rez-de-chaussée. J'adore cet endroit!
examples.trans: To tell you the truth, I hate ground-floor noise. I love this space!

examples.text: Je déteste attendre.
examples.trans: I hate waiting.

meanings.en: trash, waste, rubbish; piece of trash (insult)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le détritus', plural 'les détritus') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'trash'.

examples.text: Un vrai détritus.
examples.trans: A true piece of trash.

examples.text: Un vrai détritus, voilà.
examples.trans: A true piece of trash.

meanings.note: Détruire trois ans de travail. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Core French verb meaning 'to destroy, ruin'.

examples.text: Ils détruisent trois ans de mon travail!
examples.trans: They destroy three years of my work!

examples.text: Le feu a détruit la maison.
examples.trans: The fire destroyed the house.

examples.text: Un scénario est fait pour être détruit!
examples.trans: A script is made to be destroyed!

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.
Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Je suis dévastée par cette nouvelle.
examples.trans: I am devastated by this news.

examples.text: Il était complètement dévasté.
examples.trans: He was completely devastated.

examples.text: Je suis dévastée.
examples.trans: I am devastated.

meanings.note: responsable du développement = head of development

examples.text: Le développement des projets.
examples.trans: Project development.

examples.text: Un projet en plein développement.
examples.trans: A project in full development.

examples.text: Tu diriges maintenant tout le développement créatif.
examples.trans: You now direct all creative development.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to develop'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'développé').

examples.text: Développer les activités de l'agence.
examples.trans: To develop the agency's activities.

examples.text: Hicham veut développer des nouvelles branches.
examples.trans: Hicham wants to develop new branches.

meanings.note: Dévorer un livre.
Dévorer un livre.

examples.text: Tu m'as dévorée comme une hyène!
examples.trans: You devoured me like a hyena!

examples.text: Elle dévore ce roman.
examples.trans: She's devouring this novel.

examples.text: J'ai besoin que tu le dévores immédiatement.
examples.trans: I need you to devour it immediately.

meanings.note: Past participle of décevoir.

examples.text: Je suis déçue.
examples.trans: I'm disappointed.

examples.text: Il est très déçu.
examples.trans: He's very disappointed.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.
Used as a masculine noun: un dîner calme.

examples.text: Madame Odette, Antoine et moi avons réservé un dîner calme près d'ici: vous venez demain?
examples.trans: Madam Odette, Antoine and I booked a quiet dinner nearby: will you join us tomorrow?

examples.text: On dîne à huit heures.
examples.trans: We have dinner at eight.

meanings.note: also called 'un mail' or 'un courriel'

examples.text: Contrat envoyé par e-mail.
examples.trans: Contract sent by email.

examples.text: Je t'envoie un e-mail.
examples.trans: I'll send you an email.

examples.text: Contrat envoyé par e-mail. Une nouvelle aventure commence.
examples.trans: Contract sent by email. A new adventure begins.

meanings.note: Un verre d'eau = a glass of water.

examples.text: Un verre d'eau, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: A glass of water, please.

examples.text: L'eau est froide.
examples.trans: The water is cold.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to erase'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'effacé').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 's'effacer: to fade away'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'effacé').

examples.text: Le monde s'efface lentement.
examples.trans: The world is slowly fading.

examples.text: Effacer le tableau.
examples.trans: To erase the board.

examples.text: Adieu, le monde s'efface lentement.
examples.trans: Farewell, the world is slowly fading.

meanings.en: effect, result, impact; effet secondaire = side effect
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le effet', plural 'les effets') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'effect'.

examples.text: Les effets secondaires.
examples.trans: The side effects.

examples.text: Quel est l'effet?
examples.trans: What is the effect?

examples.text: Regardez les effets secondaires sur Internet!
examples.trans: Look at the side effects on the Internet!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'effective'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ces pilules sont très efficaces.
examples.trans: These pills are very effective.

examples.text: Une méthode efficace.
examples.trans: An efficient method.

examples.text: Alors, j'ai ces pilules très efficaces.
examples.trans: Then, I have these very effective pills.

meanings.note: Faire un effort means make an effort.

examples.text: Fais un effort!
examples.trans: Make an effort!

examples.text: C'est un gros effort.
examples.trans: It's a big effort.

examples.text: Nous avons fait un énorme effort, Hélène.
examples.trans: We've made a huge effort, Hélène.

examples.text: C'est effrayant!
examples.trans: That's scary!

examples.text: Une histoire effrayante.
examples.trans: A scary story.

meanings.note: In eh bien, introduces a reaction or transition, like well.
Can call for attention, like hey.

examples.text: Eh bien... merci quand même.
examples.trans: Well... thanks anyway.

examples.text: Eh, Camille!
examples.trans: Hey, Camille!

examples.text: Eh bien, évidemment!
examples.trans: Well, obviously!

meanings.note: for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle
for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle

examples.text: Elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: It's full of sharks.

examples.text: Elle est actrice.
examples.trans: She's an actress.

meanings.en: to wrap, pack up (purchases or parcels); (informal) to thrill
meanings.note: At shops and markets, je vous l'emballe? means 'shall I wrap it up for you?'.

examples.text: Le potier emballe chaque tasse dans une feuille de journal.
examples.trans: The potter wraps each cup in a sheet of newspaper.

examples.text: Tout est emballé dans le panier, on peut rentrer!
examples.trans: Everything is wrapped up in the basket—we can head home!

meanings.en: to board, embark; to arrest, take in (colloquial)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'embark'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'embarqué').

examples.text: La police a fini par embarquer les deux acteurs.
examples.trans: The police ended up hauling the two actors in.

examples.text: Nous allons bientôt embarquer dans l'avion pour Cannes.
examples.trans: We are going to board the plane for Cannes soon.

examples.text: On m'embarque aussi?
examples.trans: Are you taking me in too?

meanings.note: se sentir embarrassé = to feel self-conscious

examples.text: Elle était très embarrassée.
examples.trans: She was very embarrassed.

examples.text: Un silence embarrassé.
examples.trans: An awkward silence.

examples.text: Je serais beaucoup trop embarrassée là-bas.
examples.trans: I would be much too embarrassed there.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la embauche', plural 'les embauches') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hiring'.

examples.text: La discrimination à l'embauche.
examples.trans: Hiring discrimination.

examples.text: C'est une vraie discrimination à l'embauche.
examples.trans: That is real hiring discrimination.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Si vous ne la gardez pas à plein temps, Étienne, moi je l'embauche dans ma cuisine!
examples.trans: If you do not keep her full-time, Etienne, I am hiring her in my kitchen!

examples.text: C'est facile à embaucher ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to hire, take on staff together.

meanings.en: traffic jam, congestion (often plural: les embouteillages)
meanings.note: Literally 'bottling' (a bottleneck of cars).

examples.text: Prendre le train permet d'éviter les embouteillages.
examples.trans: Taking the train lets you avoid traffic jams.

examples.text: Il est arrivé en retard à cause d'un embouteillage.
examples.trans: He arrived late because of a traffic jam.

meanings.note: Reflexive. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to fit together'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'emboîté').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to fit together'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'emboîté').

examples.text: Tout s'emboîte parfaitement ici.
examples.trans: Everything fits together perfectly here.

examples.text: Les pièces s'emboîtent bien.
examples.trans: The pieces fit together well.

meanings.note: Kiss someone; compound past uses avoir.
With se, kiss one another; compound past uses être.
Embrace or hug someone.

examples.text: On s'est embrassés.
examples.trans: We kissed.

examples.text: Je t'embrasse.
examples.trans: Love (at the end of a letter or call).

examples.text: L'envie subite de s'embrasser et de prendre une chambre? Ça arrive.
examples.trans: The sudden urge to kiss and get a room? It happens.

meanings.note: Informal/familiar. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to bother'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'embêté').

examples.text: Tu fais ça pour m'embêter.
examples.trans: You are doing this to annoy me.

examples.text: Ne l'embête pas.
examples.trans: Don't bother him.

examples.text: Tu fais ça juste pour m'embêter!
examples.trans: You're doing this just to annoy me!

meanings.note: To take a person (or pet) along with you to another place (contrast 'emporter' for objects, though colloquially used for handy gear too).

examples.text: Nous emmenons les enfants voir la fontaine du square.
examples.trans: We are taking the children to see the fountain in the square.

examples.text: Emmenez un parapluie si vous sortez en fin d'après-midi.
examples.trans: Take an umbrella along if you go out late this afternoon.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to move in'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'emménagé').

examples.text: Gabriel emménage dans le bureau.
examples.trans: Gabriel moves into the office.

examples.text: Tu vois bien, j'emménage aujourd'hui!
examples.trans: You see well, I am moving in today!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le empire', plural 'les empires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'empire'.

examples.text: Tu deviendras l'héritière de l'empire Barneville!
examples.trans: You will become the Barneville empire heiress!

examples.text: Bâtir un grand empire commercial.
examples.trans: To build a great commercial empire.

meanings.en: emploi du temps = schedule, timetable (literally 'use of time')
meanings.note: Chercher un emploi.
Chercher un emploi.

examples.text: Elle a un problème d'emploi du temps.
examples.trans: She has a schedule problem.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé un emploi.
examples.trans: I found a job.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le employé', plural 'les employés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'employee'.

examples.text: La santé de mes employés.
examples.trans: The health of my employees.

examples.text: Un employé de l'agence.
examples.trans: An employee of the agency.

examples.text: Je me soucie de la santé de mes employés.
examples.trans: I care about the health of my employees.

meanings.note: emporter un dossier = to take a file along

examples.text: Vous pourriez l'emporter à Cannes.
examples.trans: You could take it to Cannes.

examples.text: Emporter un repas.
examples.trans: To take out a meal.

examples.text: Vous pourriez l'emporter à Cannes pour moi?
examples.trans: Could you take it to Cannes for me?

meanings.note: To borrow a book or item on loan; to follow a street, bridge, or shortcut.

examples.text: J'ai emprunté cet atlas à la bibliothèque municipale.
examples.trans: I borrowed this atlas from the town library.

examples.text: Empruntons la ruelle pavée pour éviter la grande avenue.
examples.trans: Let's take the cobbled lane to avoid the main avenue.

empêcher.gloss: to prevent, to stop, to hinder

meanings.note: empêcher quelqu'un de faire = to prevent someone from doing

examples.text: On l'empêche d'être Christophe Bel.
examples.trans: We're stopping him being Christophe Bel.

examples.text: Rien ne peut l'empêcher.
examples.trans: Nothing can stop it.

examples.text: Et pourquoi travailler avec Christophe Bel si on l'empêche d'être Christophe Bel?
examples.trans: And why work with Christophe Bel if we stop him being Christophe Bel?

en.gloss: in; on; of it; about it; some

meanings.note: Preposition. En retard means late; en vacances means on holiday.
Object pronoun replacing a phrase introduced by de. The English wording depends on the expression: en parler means to talk about it; j'en ai assez means I have had enough.
Object pronoun referring to an unspecified amount or to a quantity named after the action: j'en ai deux means I have two (of them).

examples.text: Je suis en retard.
examples.trans: I'm late.

examples.text: Tu es en vacances?
examples.trans: Are you on holiday?

examples.text: Nous en parlons.
examples.trans: We're talking about it.

meanings.note: Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'live', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Nous allons régler nos comptes en direct.
examples.trans: We are going to settle our scores live.

examples.text: Le match est diffusé en direct.
examples.trans: The match is broadcast live.

meanings.note: very frequent in speech; the t of fait is pronounced

examples.text: En fait, je suis comédienne.
examples.trans: Actually, I'm an actress.

examples.text: En fait, c'est simple.
examples.trans: In fact, it's simple.

examples.text: Bonjour. En fait, vous et lui...
examples.trans: Hello. Actually, you and him...

meanings.note: A vague answer. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'sort of', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: En quelque sorte.
examples.trans: Sort of.

examples.text: C'est mon patron, en quelque sorte.
examples.trans: He's my boss, in a way.

examples.text: En quelque sorte. Ça fait trois semaines que je suis là.
examples.trans: Sort of. I've been here for three weeks.

meanings.note: To put a picture or map in a frame; to guide or mentor apprentices.

examples.text: Nous allons encadrer cette aquarelle pour le salon.
examples.trans: We are going to frame this watercolor for the lounge.

examples.text: Deux grands tilleuls encadrent le portail en fer forgé.
examples.trans: Two tall linden trees frame the wrought-iron gate.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'pregnant'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Elle est enceinte.
examples.trans: She is pregnant.

examples.text: J'étais enceinte! Pars!
examples.trans: I was pregnant! Leave!

examples.text: Je suis enceinte, Hicham.
examples.trans: I am pregnant, Hicham.

meanings.en: delighted, enchanted; nice to meet you
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'delighted'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Enchantée, Nadia. Ça sent très bon ici!
examples.trans: Nice to meet you, Nadia. It smells wonderful in here!

examples.text: Enchanté de faire votre connaissance.
examples.trans: Delighted to meet you.

enchaîner.gloss: to follow on, to chain together

meanings.en: to follow on immediately, to chain together
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to follow on immediately'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'enchaîné').

examples.text: Je ne peux pas enchaîner deux tournages.
examples.trans: I cannot do two film shoots back-to-back.

examples.text: Je peux pas enchaîner comme ça.
examples.trans: I cannot follow on like that.

examples.text: Et il doit enchaîner avec l'autre film!
examples.trans: And he has to jump straight into the next film!

meanings.en: enclosure, pen, fenced paddock for animals
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le enclos', plural 'les enclos') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'enclosure'.

examples.text: Les loups? Dans cet enclos fermé?
examples.trans: Wolves? Inside this enclosed pen?

examples.text: Les bêtes restent dans leur enclos la nuit.
examples.trans: The animals stay in their pen at night.

meanings.note: j'ai encore un agent? = do I still have an agent?

examples.text: Encore un café?
examples.trans: Another coffee?

examples.text: Ouf! Une bonne idée sauve encore le petit-déjeuner.
examples.trans: Phew! A good idea saves breakfast again.

meanings.note: spelling keeps 'e' before 'a/o' (nous encourageons)

examples.text: Il est venu m'encourager!
examples.trans: He came to encourage me!

examples.text: Je t'encourage à continuer.
examples.trans: I encourage you to keep going.

meanings.note: À l'encre = in ink.

examples.text: Merveilleux! Votre nom entre dans le grand cahier d'Henri à l'encre indélébile!
examples.trans: Wonderful! Your name goes into Henri's big notebook in permanent ink!

examples.text: Voici l'encre sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the ink on the table.

endormir.gloss: to put to sleep, fall asleep

meanings.en: to put to sleep; s'endormir = to fall asleep
meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire') meaning 'to put to sleep'; essential in everyday spoken and professional French.

examples.text: Elle s'endort paisiblement.
examples.trans: She falls asleep peacefully.

examples.text: Elle s'endort paisiblement avec toi.
examples.trans: She falls asleep peacefully with you.

examples.text: C'est un bel endroit.
examples.trans: It's a lovely place.

examples.text: Un endroit calme.
examples.trans: A quiet place.

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking elided article l'enfance; d'enfance = 'childhood (adj)'.

examples.text: Ces deux initiales datent de notre enfance.
examples.trans: Those two initials go back to our childhood.

examples.text: Il a passé toute son enfance dans ce quartier tranquille.
examples.trans: He spent his whole childhood in this quiet neighborhood.

meanings.note: Can be masculine or feminine depending on the child; the generic un enfant does not specify a sex.

examples.text: Je voulais un enfant.
examples.trans: I wanted a child.

examples.text: Ils ont deux enfants.
examples.trans: They have two children.

examples.text: Attendez une minute... Numéro douze, {STREET}, et deux initiales d'enfance écrites dans le coin!
examples.trans: Wait a moment... Number twelve, {STREET}, and two childhood initials written in the corner!

meanings.note: c'est l'enfer! = it's hell! / it's a nightmare!

examples.text: C'est l'enfer!
examples.trans: It's hell!

examples.text: La circulation est un enfer ce matin.
examples.trans: Traffic is hell this morning.

meanings.note: être enfermé = to be shut in / locked up

examples.text: Enfermer à clé.
examples.trans: To lock with a key.

examples.text: Elle reste enfermée chez elle.
examples.trans: She stays shut in at home.

examples.text: Pour l'instant, son sac reste bien enfermé à clé.
examples.trans: For now, his bag stays safely locked up.

enfiler.gloss: to slip on, put on clothing

meanings.en: to slip on, quickly put on clothes
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to slip on'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'enfilé').

examples.text: Il enfile sa veste.
examples.trans: He slips on his jacket.

examples.text: Il n'est pas question d'enfiler ça.
examples.trans: There is no question of slipping this on.

examples.text: C'est parfait, enfilons cette fausse botte!
examples.trans: It is perfect, let us slip on this fake boot!

meanings.note: Enfin prêt! = Finally ready!

examples.text: La deuxième page de la valse est enfin terminée!
examples.trans: The second page of the waltz is finally finished!

examples.text: Après la pluie, le soleil revient enfin dans la cour.
examples.trans: After the rain, the sun finally returns to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Engager un employé. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to hire'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'engagé').
S'engager. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to hire'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'engagé').

examples.text: Si vous m'engagez, je serai parfait.
examples.trans: If you hire me, I will be perfect.

examples.text: L'agence engage un nouvel agent.
examples.trans: The agency is hiring a new agent.

examples.text: Samy n'est pas encore engagé.
examples.trans: Samy is not yet hired.

meanings.note: un artiste engagé = a committed artist

examples.text: Un film très engagé.
examples.trans: A very committed film.

examples.text: Une actrice engagée.
examples.trans: A socially engaged actress.

examples.text: C'est un jeune idéaliste engagé politiquement.
examples.trans: He is a young politically committed idealist.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le engin', plural 'les engins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'machine'.

examples.text: Comment est-ce qu'on fait marcher cet engin?
examples.trans: How do you make this contraption work?

examples.text: Il conduit un drôle d'engin électrique dans Paris.
examples.trans: He drives a strange electric contraption around Paris.

meanings.en: to intoxicate, make drunk; to exhilarate
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to intoxicate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'enivré').

examples.text: Le succès l'enivre.
examples.trans: Success intoxicates him.

examples.text: Cette odeur m'enivre.
examples.trans: This scent intoxicates me.

examples.text: Le pouvoir que tu as m'enivre!
examples.trans: The power you have intoxicates me!

meanings.en: to remove, to take away, to subtract
meanings.note: Enlever cinq ans.
Enlever son manteau.

examples.text: Enlève ton manteau.
examples.trans: Take off your coat.

examples.text: Ne vous inquiétez pas! L'eau gazeuse froide enlève très bien le jus d'orange.
examples.trans: Do not worry! Cold sparkling water takes orange juice right out.

examples.text: Assieds-toi, Thibault, enlève ton manteau lourd et regarde cette valise bleue.
examples.trans: Sit down, Thibault, take off your heavy coat, and look at this blue suitcase.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le enlèvement', plural 'les enlèvements') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'abduction'.

examples.text: C'est un enlèvement d'enfant.
examples.trans: It is a child abduction.

examples.text: C'est un enlèvement d'enfant!
examples.trans: It is a child abduction!

meanings.note: Feminine: ennemie.

examples.text: Je vais avoir beaucoup d'ennemis.
examples.trans: I'll have a lot of enemies.

examples.text: Il a des ennemis.
examples.trans: He has enemies.

examples.text: Si je vais chez StarMédia maintenant, je vais avoir beaucoup d'ennemis.
examples.trans: If I go to StarMédia now, I'll have a lot of enemies.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le ennui', plural 'les ennuis') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'boredom'.
Masculine noun ('le ennui', plural 'les ennuis') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'boredom'.

examples.text: Il n'aime pas l'ennui.
examples.trans: He doesn't like boredom.

examples.text: Il y a pire que l'ennui dans une relation.
examples.trans: There are worse things than boredom in a relationship.

examples.text: Ne dites pas du mal de l'ennui.
examples.trans: Do not speak ill of boredom.

meanings.note: Je t'ennuie = I'm boring you.
Reflexive.

examples.text: Dis-le si je t'ennuie.
examples.trans: Say it if I'm boring you.

examples.text: Je m'ennuie ici.
examples.trans: I'm bored here.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Ce film est très ennuyeux.
examples.trans: This movie is very boring.

examples.text: Votre deuxième jour ne sera pas ennuyeux.
examples.trans: Your second day will not be boring.

examples.text: Sûrement un avis ennuyeux pour repeindre les volets sur la rue.
examples.trans: Probably a boring notice about repainting the street shutters.

meanings.note: enregistrer un album = to record an album

examples.text: Je n'ai jamais enregistré professionnellement.
examples.trans: I have never recorded professionally.

examples.text: Enregistrer une chanson.
examples.trans: To record a song.

meanings.note: *Enrouler X dans Y* means to wrap something up inside a cloth, towel, or paper.

examples.text: Enroulez les glaçons dans une serviette propre avant de les poser.
examples.trans: Wrap the ice cubes in a clean towel before placing them.

examples.text: Il enroule la grande feuille de papier à musique avec soin.
examples.trans: He rolls up the large sheet of music paper carefully.

related.gloss: roll (of tape, paper, or fabric); rolling pin

meanings.note: Hanging sign outside a shop or hotel.

examples.text: La boutique a une grande enseigne dehors?
examples.trans: Does the shop have a big sign outside?

examples.text: Grand, manteau gris foncé, il lève les yeux vers l'enseigne de notre hôtel!
examples.trans: Tall, dark grey coat, he is looking up at our hotel sign!

meanings.note: Together, in company or in combination.

meanings.en: as a noun: the whole, a set
meanings.note: As a masculine noun, un ensemble is a group or set.

examples.text: On travaille ensemble.
examples.trans: We work together.

examples.text: Restez ici, ouvrons la porte ensemble.
examples.trans: Stay here, let us open the door together.

examples.text: À neuf heures? Attendez, ouvrons le portail ensemble.
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

examples.text: On mange, et ensuite on part.
examples.trans: We eat, and then we leave.

examples.text: Le pont, puis la pharmacie verte à droite. Et ensuite?
examples.trans: The bridge, then the green pharmacy on the right. And next?

meanings.note: je ne veux pas l'entendre = I don't want to hear it

examples.text: Tu entends la musique?
examples.trans: Can you hear the music?

examples.text: Très généreux! Vous avez entendu la cloche du portail en bas?
examples.trans: Very generous! Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?

meanings.note: Built from en + terre ('earth').

examples.text: Ne nous enterrez pas avant d'avoir lu tout le dossier, Étienne.
examples.trans: Stop burying us before reading the whole file, Etienne.

examples.text: C'est facile à enterrer ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to bury together.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'eager'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il est très enthousiaste.
examples.trans: He is very enthusiastic.

examples.text: Je suis très heureux et enthousiaste d'être ici.
examples.trans: I am very happy and enthusiastic to be here.

meanings.note: Le monde entier = the whole world. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'whole'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Pour les enfants du monde entier.
examples.trans: For the children of the whole world.

examples.text: J'ai attendu une journée entière.
examples.trans: I waited a whole day.

examples.text: Je suis allée à cette soirée uniquement pour les enfants du monde entier.
examples.trans: I went to that party purely for the children of the whole world.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: C'est entièrement de ma faute.
examples.trans: It is entirely my fault.

examples.text: Je suis entièrement d'accord avec vous.
examples.trans: I completely agree with you.

examples.text: Pardon, c'est entièrement de ma faute.
examples.trans: Sorry, it is entirely my fault.

meanings.en: to circle (on a page or calendar); to surround
meanings.note: Built from en + tour: entourer une date au crayon means 'to circle a date in pencil'.

examples.text: Étienne a entouré le mauvais jour dans son petit carnet.
examples.trans: Étienne circled the wrong day in his little notebook.

examples.text: Un muret en pierre entoure toute la cour de l'hôtel.
examples.trans: A low stone wall surrounds the entire hotel courtyard.

entraîner.gloss: to train (s'entraîner = to practise, to train)

meanings.note: Reflexive: s’entraîner = train or practise. Compound past uses être: elle s’est entraînée.

meanings.en: entraîner = to coach, to lead to

examples.text: Je me suis entraînée pendant des mois.
examples.trans: I trained for months.

examples.text: Il s'entraîne tous les jours.
examples.trans: He trains every day.

examples.text: Il s'entraîne dans une salle de sport.
examples.trans: He works out at a gym.

meanings.note: Entre de bonnes mains = in good hands; entre nous = between us.

examples.text: La boulangerie est entre de très bonnes mains.
examples.trans: The bakery is in very good hands.

examples.text: La petite table se trouve entre le piano et la fenêtre.
examples.trans: The small table stands between the piano and the window.

examples.text: Une entreprise n'est pas une famille.
examples.trans: A company is not a family.

examples.text: Une entreprise n'est pas une famille. Il y a des lois.
examples.trans: A company is not a family. There are laws.

examples.text: L'entreprise a payé une chambre d'hôtel privée pendant dix ans.
examples.trans: The company paid for a private hotel room for ten years.

meanings.en: to come in, to go in
meanings.note: Passé composé with être.
Polite imperative.

examples.text: Attends vendredi à midi: je veux être au premier rang quand l'homme à la valise entrera!
examples.trans: Wait until Friday at noon: I want a front-row seat when Suitcase Man walks in!

examples.text: Bonsoir! Entrez vite à l'abri de la pluie, monsieur.
examples.trans: Good evening! Come quickly inside out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: Vous deux?! Laissez vos tasses, entrez tout de suite!
examples.trans: Both of you?! Leave your cups, come inside right away!

meanings.note: Un entretien d'embauche.

examples.text: Je n'ai pas commencé l'entretien.
examples.trans: I haven't started the interview.

examples.text: J'ai un entretien demain.
examples.trans: I have an interview tomorrow.

examples.text: Le fil avait besoin d'être redressé, c'est tout. Rien de sentimental dans le bon entretien.
examples.trans: The wire needed straightening, that is all. Nothing sentimental about good maintenance.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la entrée', plural 'les entrées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'entrance'.

examples.text: Je vous en prie, madame. Lundi après-midi, l'entrée était sombre.
examples.trans: Go right ahead, madam. Monday afternoon, the lobby was dark.

examples.text: Laissez vos chaussures mouillées dans l'entrée.
examples.trans: Leave your wet shoes in the hallway.

examples.text: Tu as une enveloppe?
examples.trans: Have you got an envelope?

examples.text: La lettre est dans l'enveloppe.
examples.trans: The letter is in the envelope.

meanings.note: To wrap an object protectively in paper or cloth; to surround softly.

examples.text: Le carnet était enveloppé dans une toile cirée.
examples.trans: The notebook was wrapped in waxed cloth.

examples.text: Le boulanger enveloppe la brioche tiède dans du papier.
examples.trans: The baker wraps the warm brioche in paper.

meanings.en: reverse, wrong side; upside down (à l'envers)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le envers', plural 'les envers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'reverse'.

examples.text: Je vais boire à l'envers.
examples.trans: I will drink upside down.

examples.text: Mettre un pull à l'envers.
examples.trans: To put a sweater on inside out.

meanings.note: Avoir envie de plus infinitive means feel like or want to do something.

examples.text: J'ai envie de partir.
examples.trans: I feel like leaving.

examples.text: Elle a envie d'un café.
examples.trans: She wants a coffee.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'roughly'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Environ cent cinquante kilomètres.
examples.trans: About one hundred fifty kilometers.

examples.text: Oui, environ cent cinquante kilomètres chaque semaine.
examples.trans: Yes, about one hundred fifty kilometers every week.

meanings.note: envisager un poste = consider a position

examples.text: Comment tu envisages ce poste?
examples.trans: How do you envisage this position?

examples.text: Nous envisageons plusieurs options.
examples.trans: We are considering several options.

meanings.note: Past participle envoyé; future j'enverrai. A preceding feminine direct object can give envoyée.

examples.text: Je t'envoie une carte postale de Lyon.
examples.trans: I'm sending you a postcard from Lyon.

examples.text: Qui a envoyé cette lettre officielle?
examples.trans: Who sent this official letter?

meanings.note: Une grave erreur. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'blunder, mistake'.

examples.text: Ce tournage était une erreur.
examples.trans: This shoot was a mistake.

examples.text: Quelqu'un à la gare a pris ma valise bleue par erreur!
examples.trans: Someone at the train station took my blue suitcase by mistake!

examples.text: Nous avons accidentellement mis deux réservations pour la chambre sept ce soir.
examples.trans: We accidentally booked two guests into room seven tonight.

meanings.note: Usually uncountable when naming the sport; also an ascent or an escalation in other contexts.

examples.text: J'ai fait un stage d'escalade.
examples.trans: I did a rock-climbing course.

examples.text: Elle aime l'escalade.
examples.trans: She likes rock climbing.

examples.text: J'ai fait un stage d'escalade ce week-end.
examples.trans: I did a rock-climbing course this weekend.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le escalier', plural 'les escaliers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'stairs'.

examples.text: Monter l'escalier.
examples.trans: To climb the stairs.

examples.text: Descendre par l'escalier.
examples.trans: To go down by the stairs.

examples.text: Exactement ce qu'il me faut. Où est l'escalier?
examples.trans: Just what I need. Where are the stairs?

meanings.note: same form for masculine and feminine: un/une esclave, l'esclave

examples.text: Non, Sofia joue l'esclave.
examples.trans: No, Sofia is playing the slave.

examples.text: Je joue l'esclave?
examples.trans: I'm playing the slave?

examples.text: On veut les esclaves derrière le château, d'accord?
examples.trans: We want the slaves behind the chateau, okay?

meanings.note: Open room or space; narrow gap or cavity between stones.

examples.text: Il y a un petit espace sec juste sous la pierre.
examples.trans: There is a small dry space right underneath the stone.

examples.text: La salle à manger offre un bel espace lumineux.
examples.trans: The dining room offers a lovely bright space.

meanings.note: une touriste espagnole = a Spanish tourist

examples.text: Une touriste espagnole dans le métro.
examples.trans: A Spanish tourist in the subway.

examples.text: Elle parle espagnol.
examples.trans: She speaks Spanish.

examples.text: Une touriste espagnole croisée dans le métro!
examples.trans: A Spanish tourist crossed paths with in the subway!

meanings.note: Feeling of hope or expectation ('dans l'espoir de' = in the hope of).

examples.text: Ils ont caché la boîte dans l'espoir de la rouvrir ensemble.
examples.trans: They hid the box in the hope of reopening it together.

examples.text: Gardons espoir: le soleil revient toujours après l'averse.
examples.trans: Let's keep hope: the sun always comes back after the shower.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le espresso', plural 'les espressos') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'espresso'.

examples.text: Je prends toujours un espresso bien serré le matin.
examples.trans: I always have a strong espresso in the morning.

examples.text: Voulez-vous un espresso avant la réunion?
examples.trans: Would you like an espresso before the meeting?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le esprit', plural 'les esprits') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'spirit'.

examples.text: C'est dans cet esprit.
examples.trans: It is in that spirit.

examples.text: Ce nouveau scénario ressemble à cet esprit.
examples.trans: This new script resembles that spirit.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la espèce', plural 'les espèces') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sort'.

examples.text: Payé en espèces!
examples.trans: Paid in cash!

examples.text: Payé en espèces! Gardez vos outils ouverts, je traverse le pont en courant!
examples.trans: Paid in cash! Keep your tools open, I am running back across the bridge!

meanings.note: + infinitive or + que.

examples.text: J'espère être comme vous.
examples.trans: I hope to be like you.

examples.text: On espère que oui.
examples.trans: We hope so.

meanings.note: Souvent au pluriel: les essais.

examples.text: Et maintenant, Claire: nous sommes vendredi, le dernier jour de votre semaine d'essai.
examples.trans: And now, Claire: today is Friday, the last day of your trial week.

examples.text: Aux essais, il parlait, il parlait!
examples.trans: At the screen tests, he talked and talked!

meanings.note: Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'fitting'.

examples.text: Des séances d'essayage.
examples.trans: Fitting sessions.

examples.text: Elle a des essayages.
examples.trans: She has costume fittings.

examples.text: Elle a un défilé et des essayages.
examples.trans: She has a fashion show and costume fittings.

meanings.note: Essayer de + infinitive.
Clothes.

examples.text: J'ai tout essayé.
examples.trans: I tried everything.

examples.text: Et regardez, ce gilet doux en laine est propre et neuf. Essayez-le.
examples.trans: And look, this soft wool cardigan is clean and new. Try it on.

meanings.note: L'essentiel est de participer. Masculine noun ('le essentiel', plural 'les essentiels') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'essential part'.

examples.text: Pour moi, l'essentiel reste le film.
examples.trans: For me, the essential thing remains the film.

examples.text: L'essentiel est fait.
examples.trans: The main part is done.

examples.text: Nous respectons cette règle essentielle.
examples.trans: We respect this essential rule.

meanings.note: Stem alternates essuie / essuyons.

examples.text: Essuyez la poussière sur la plaque en laiton dessus... attendez, lisez ce numéro!
examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate on top... wait, read that number!

examples.text: C'est facile à essuyer ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to wipe, dry together.

meanings.note: Cardinal point east ('à l'est de' = east of; pronounced /ɛst/, unlike verb 'est' /ɛ/).

examples.text: Les chambres de l'est reçoivent la lumière du matin.
examples.trans: The east-facing rooms catch the morning light.

examples.text: La girouette tourne doucement vers l'est.
examples.trans: The weathervane turns gently toward the east.

meanings.note: Est-ce que introduces a yes/no question.

examples.text: Est-ce que tu viens?
examples.trans: Are you coming?

examples.text: Est-ce que vous travaillez ici?
examples.trans: Do you work here?

meanings.en: turns a sentence into a yes/no question
meanings.note: est-ce que tu viens? = are you coming?

examples.text: Est-ce que j'ai fait quelque chose de mal?
examples.trans: Have I done something wrong?

examples.text: Est-ce que vous êtes prête?
examples.trans: Are you ready?

examples.text: Est-ce que Rebecca est dans mon agenda?
examples.trans: Is Rebecca in my diary?

meanings.note: aller chez l'esthéticienne = to go to the beautician

examples.text: L'adresse de mon esthéticienne.
examples.trans: The address of my aesthetician.

examples.text: Une excellente esthéticienne.
examples.trans: An excellent beautician.

examples.text: La journaliste a seulement parlé de mon esthéticienne!
examples.trans: The journalist only talked about my aesthetician!

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced.

examples.text: Et vous?
examples.trans: And you?

examples.text: Et demain?
examples.trans: And tomorrow?

examples.text: Euh… oui.
examples.trans: Er… yes.

examples.text: Frais? Euh, oui! Les vieux tuyaux du quartier se réveillent doucement le matin!
examples.trans: Chilly? Uh, yes! The old neighbourhood pipes wake up gently in the morning!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'euphoric'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est un état presque euphorisant.
examples.trans: It is an almost euphoric state.

examples.text: C'est un état presque euphorisant!
examples.trans: It is an almost euphoric state!

meanings.note: Plural takes -s: vingt mille euros.

examples.text: Voici cinquante euros de la caisse. Rapportez le ticket!
examples.trans: Here is fifty euros from the cash box. Bring back the receipt!

examples.text: Juste ici! Tout a coûté trente-huit euros, alors voici douze euros de monnaie.
examples.trans: Right here! Everything cost thirty-eight euros, so here is twelve euros in change.

examples.text: Ça coûte dix euros.
examples.trans: It costs ten euros.

meanings.note: lowercase as an adjective; capitalised as a noun (un Européen)

examples.text: Un groupe d'agences européennes.
examples.trans: A group of European agencies.

examples.text: Un film européen.
examples.trans: A European film.

examples.text: Oui. Il veut créer un groupe d'agences européennes.
examples.trans: Yes. He wants to create a group of European agencies.

meanings.en: them (stressed pronoun, masculine or mixed plural)
meanings.note: after a preposition: pour eux, avec eux
Eux, ils savent.

examples.text: Je suis là pour eux tous les jours.
examples.trans: I'm here for them every day.

examples.text: Je travaille avec eux.
examples.trans: I work with them.

examples.text: Je suis là pour eux tous les jours, mais ça ne suffit jamais.
examples.trans: I'm here for them every day, but it's never enough.

meanings.note: A former partner of either gender; the written form does not change in the plural.

examples.text: Florence, mon ex.
examples.trans: Florence, my ex.

examples.text: Il voit encore son ex.
examples.trans: He still sees his ex.

examples.text: Florence, mon ex. Mais c'était il y a longtemps.
examples.trans: Florence, my ex. But that was a long time ago.

meanings.note: Both *-c-* and *-t* are pronounced in modern French (`/ɛɡzakt/`) in masculine and feminine alike.

examples.text: Notez l'heure exacte de la cuisson sur le carnet.
examples.trans: Write down the exact baking time in the notebook.

examples.text: Voici la copie exacte de la vieille clé du jardin.
examples.trans: Here is the exact copy of the old garden key.

meanings.note: also as an answer: Exactement! = That's right!

examples.text: Oui, exactement.
examples.trans: Yes, exactly.

examples.text: C'est exactement ça.
examples.trans: That's exactly it.

meanings.en: to exaggerate, to overstate, to go too far
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to exaggerate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'exagéré').

examples.text: Tu exagères toujours.
examples.trans: You always exaggerate.

examples.text: Sans exagérer.
examples.trans: Without exaggerating.

examples.text: Tu exagères toujours tes émotions, Gabriel.
examples.trans: You always exaggerate your emotions, Gabriel.

meanings.note: Passer un examen = to take an exam. Masculine noun ('le examen', plural 'les examens') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'exam'.

examples.text: Je suis arrivée au centre d'examen.
examples.trans: I arrived at the test center.

examples.text: Elle a réussi son examen.
examples.trans: She passed her exam.

examples.text: Quand je suis arrivée au centre d'examen, j'ai coincé la portière sur la main de l'examinateur.
examples.trans: When I arrived at the test center, I caught the car door on the examiner's hand.

meanings.note: Feminine: une examinatrice.

examples.text: La main de l'examinateur.
examples.trans: The examiner's hand.

examples.text: L'examinateur attend dans la voiture.
examples.trans: The examiner is waiting in the car.

meanings.note: also alone as an exclamation: Excellent!

examples.text: C'est une excellente nouvelle pour toute l'agence!
examples.trans: That is excellent news for the whole agency!

examples.text: Tu as fait un excellent travail sur ce contrat.
examples.trans: You did an excellent job on this contract.

meanings.note: faire une exception = to make an exception

examples.text: C'est une exception.
examples.trans: It's a one-off.

examples.text: Pour toi, je fais une exception.
examples.trans: For you, I'll make an exception.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un flair exceptionnel.
examples.trans: An exceptional instinct.

examples.text: C'est Andréa qui est vraiment exceptionnelle.
examples.trans: It is Andrea who is truly exceptional.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'exciting'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est excitant.
examples.trans: It's exciting.

examples.text: Une perspective excitante, non?
examples.trans: An exciting prospect, right?

examples.text: Ici, ce n'est pas du tout excitant.
examples.trans: Here, this is not exciting at all.

meanings.note: L'excitation de la découverte. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'excitement, thrill'.

examples.text: J'aime l'excitation de la découverte.
examples.trans: I like the excitement of discovery.

examples.text: Il y a beaucoup d'excitation ici.
examples.trans: There is a lot of excitement here.

meanings.en: to exclude, to expel, to bar
meanings.note: Irregular third-group French verb inherited from core Latin roots, used across registers for 'to exclude'.

examples.text: Nous sommes exclues de la crèche.
examples.trans: We are excluded from the daycare.

examples.text: On ne peut pas exclure cette option.
examples.trans: We cannot exclude this option.

examples.text: Oui, nous sommes exclues de la crèche.
examples.trans: Yes, we are excluded from the daycare.

examples.text: Exclusif, hein?
examples.trans: Exclusive, huh?

examples.text: Un contrat exclusif.
examples.trans: An exclusive contract.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la exclusivité', plural 'les exclusivités') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'exclusivity'.

examples.text: Le contrat exige l'exclusivité.
examples.trans: The contract demands exclusivity.

examples.text: Le contrat américain exige l'exclusivité totale.
examples.trans: The American contract demands total exclusivity.

examples.text: Isabelle Huppert a signé une exclusivité stricte.
examples.trans: Isabelle Huppert signed strict exclusivity.

meanings.note: plural: présenter ses excuses = to apologise

examples.text: Je vous présente mes excuses.
examples.trans: I apologise.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas une excuse.
examples.trans: That's no excuse.

meanings.note: excusez-moi = excuse me, sorry (polite); excuse-moi (informal)

examples.text: Excusez-moi, c'est un peu improvisé.
examples.trans: Sorry, it's a bit last-minute.

examples.text: Excuse-moi, je suis en retard.
examples.trans: Sorry, I'm late.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le excès', plural 'les excès') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'excess'.

examples.text: Un excès de vitesse.
examples.trans: A speeding offense.

examples.text: M. Norman Thavaud roulait en excès de vitesse.
examples.trans: Mr. Norman Thavaud was speeding.

meanings.en: individual copy (of a book, newspaper, or printed menu)
meanings.note: Un exemplaire du menu = a copy of the menu.

examples.text: J'ai gardé un exemplaire du menu dans mon tiroir.
examples.trans: I kept a copy of the menu in my drawer.

examples.text: La libraire a commandé dix exemplaires de ce roman.
examples.trans: The bookseller ordered ten copies of this novel.

meanings.note: Par exemple = for example.

examples.text: Par exemple?
examples.trans: For example?

examples.text: C'est un bon exemple.
examples.trans: It's a good example.

meanings.note: un public exigeant = a demanding audience

examples.text: Une œuvre exigeante.
examples.trans: A demanding work.

examples.text: Un client très exigeant.
examples.trans: A very demanding client.

examples.text: Le film de Julien est une œuvre exigeante.
examples.trans: Julien's film is a demanding work.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to demand'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'exigé').

examples.text: Le contrat exige l'exclusivité totale.
examples.trans: The contract demands total exclusivity.
