examples.text: Le contrat américain exige l'exclusivité totale.
examples.trans: The American contract demands total exclusivity.

examples.text: Je dirai que tu exiges une réécriture.
examples.trans: I will say that you demand a rewrite.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to exist'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'existé').

examples.text: L'infidélité n'existe pas.
examples.trans: Infidelity does not exist.

examples.text: Ça n'existe pas.
examples.trans: That does not exist.

examples.text: L'infidélité n'existe pas vraiment.
examples.trans: Infidelity does not really exist.

examples.text: Trop exotique?
examples.trans: Too exotic?

examples.text: Une île exotique.
examples.trans: An exotic island.

examples.text: Et Sofia Leprince? Trop exotique?
examples.trans: And Sofia Leprince? Too exotic?

meanings.note: Feminine: experte.

examples.text: Samuel était l'expert.
examples.trans: Samuel was the expert.

examples.text: C'est un expert.
examples.trans: He's an expert.

examples.text: Samuel était l'expert. Une de ses anciennes amies veut voir son testament.
examples.trans: Samuel was the expert. One of his old friends wants to see his will.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'explanation'.

examples.text: Donne-moi une explication.
examples.trans: Give me an explanation.

examples.text: Camille, donne-moi une explication.
examples.trans: Camille, give me an explanation.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas une explication suffisante.
examples.trans: That is not a sufficient explanation.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'explicit'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Des scènes explicites.
examples.trans: Explicit scenes.

examples.text: Une réponse explicite.
examples.trans: An explicit answer.

examples.text: Il n'y a rien de trop explicite dans le texte.
examples.trans: There is nothing too explicit in the text.

meanings.note: expliquer quelque chose à quelqu'un

examples.text: Je vous explique maintenant.
examples.trans: I'll explain to you now.

examples.text: Peux-tu m'expliquer?
examples.trans: Can you explain to me?

examples.text: Je vous explique maintenant. C'est dans le nord, près des lacs.
examples.trans: I'll explain to you now. It's in the north, near the lakes.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le exploit', plural 'les exploits') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'feat'.

examples.text: Terminer le tournage à temps est un exploit.
examples.trans: Finishing filming on time is a feat.

examples.text: Tu as réussi un exploit incroyable.
examples.trans: You achieved an incredible feat.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to detonate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'explosé').

examples.text: La dispute a explosé.
examples.trans: The argument exploded.

examples.text: Alors après cinq mois, la tension a explosé.
examples.trans: So after five months, the tension exploded.

examples.text: Un film qui explose est mauvais pour tous.
examples.trans: A movie that collapses is bad for everyone.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Il a une présence explosive sur scène.
examples.trans: He has an explosive presence on stage.

examples.text: Il a une grande force explosive.
examples.trans: He has great explosive strength.

meanings.note: Rapid delivery or train ('courrier express'); quick café espresso ('un express').

examples.text: Le facteur vient d'apporter un pli en courrier express.
examples.trans: The mail carrier just delivered a packet by express mail.

examples.text: Le train express rejoint Lyon en moins de deux heures.
examples.trans: The express train reaches Lyon in under two hours.

meanings.note: un visage expressif = an expressive face

examples.text: Un visage unique et très expressif.
examples.trans: A unique and very expressive face.

examples.text: Des yeux très expressifs.
examples.trans: Very expressive eyes.

examples.text: Oui, un visage unique et très expressif.
examples.trans: Yes, a unique and very expressive face.

examples.text: Oui, c'est une expression française.
examples.trans: Yes, it's a French expression.

examples.text: J'aime bien cette expression.
examples.trans: I like this expression.

meanings.note: faire exprès = to do on purpose; sans faire exprès = by accident, without meaning to

examples.text: Tu l'as dit sans faire exprès.
examples.trans: You said it without meaning to.

examples.text: Il ne l'a pas fait exprès.
examples.trans: He didn't do it on purpose.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to expel'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'expulsé').

examples.text: Elle menace de faire expulser son collègue.
examples.trans: She threatens to have her colleague evicted.

examples.text: Tu veux vraiment me faire expulser?
examples.trans: Do you really want to have me expelled?

meanings.note: Person who mails a letter or parcel (feminine 'expéditrice').

examples.text: Le nom de l'expéditeur est écrit au dos de l'enveloppe.
examples.trans: The sender's name is written on the back of the envelope.

examples.text: Sans adresse d'expéditeur, la carte reste un mystère.
examples.trans: With no return address from the sender, the card remains a mystery.

meanings.note: Adventurous journey or search party; dispatch of parcels.

examples.text: Toute la famille est prête pour l'expédition du dimanche.
examples.trans: The whole family is ready for the Sunday expedition.

examples.text: Chaque bonne expédition commence par une carte bien pliée.
examples.trans: Every good expedition starts with a neatly folded map.

meanings.note: faire une expérience = to conduct an experiment
faire une expérience = to conduct an experiment

examples.text: C'est une expérience très difficile, Gabriel.
examples.trans: It is a very difficult experience, Gabriel.

examples.text: Une expérience scientifique.
examples.trans: A scientific experiment.

examples.text: Je n'ai pas d'expérience dans ce métier.
examples.trans: I have no experience in this profession.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'experimental'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un film expérimental.
examples.trans: An experimental film.

examples.text: C'est un petit film expérimental.
examples.trans: It is a small experimental film.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'exquisite'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ces pâtisseries ont un goût exquis.
examples.trans: These pastries have an exquisite taste.

examples.text: Vous avez des goûts tout à fait exquis.
examples.trans: You have truly exquisite tastes.

meanings.note: Un extrait de film = a film clip. Masculine noun ('le extrait', plural 'les extraits') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'excerpt'.

examples.text: Regardons un extrait.
examples.trans: Let's watch an excerpt.

examples.text: Regardons un extrait du film.
examples.trans: Let's watch a clip of the film.

examples.text: Regarde cet extrait vidéo sur mon écran d'ordinateur.
examples.trans: Watch this video excerpt on my computer screen.

meanings.note: une histoire extraordinaire = an extraordinary story

examples.text: C'est un chaman extraordinaire.
examples.trans: He is an extraordinary shaman.

examples.text: Une opportunité extraordinaire.
examples.trans: An extraordinary opportunity.

examples.text: Je sais que vous êtes sceptique, mais je connais un chaman extraordinaire.
examples.trans: I know you are skeptical, but I know an extraordinary shaman.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Il est extrêmement doué.
examples.trans: He is extremely talented.

examples.text: Un rôle extrêmement difficile.
examples.trans: An extremely difficult role.

examples.text: Il est charmant et extrêmement doué.
examples.trans: He is charming and extremely talented.

meanings.note: Une force extérieure. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor').

examples.text: La porte extérieure est fermée.
examples.trans: The outside door is closed.

examples.text: L'extérieur est identique, oui! Mais regardez à l'intérieur!
examples.trans: The outside is identical, yes! But look inside!

meanings.note: Invariable in the plural: les fa.

examples.text: Toujours là pour t'entendre jouer ta gamme de fa majeur lentement, Thibault!
examples.trans: Still here waiting to hear you play your F-major scale slowly, Thibault!

examples.text: Voici le fa sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the F on the table.

meanings.en: to make by hand, build, craft
meanings.note: Fabriquer un meuble en bois = build a piece of wooden furniture.

examples.text: Les deux frères fabriquent des tables en bois massif.
examples.trans: The two brothers build solid wood tables.

examples.text: Cet artisan fabrique des violons depuis quarante ans.
examples.trans: This craftsperson has been making violins for forty years.

examples.text: Le Tchekhov était fabuleux.
examples.trans: The Chekhov was fabulous.

examples.text: Une soirée fabuleuse.
examples.trans: A fabulous evening.

meanings.note: short for 'la faculté'; à la fac = at university

examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu as fait à la fac?
examples.trans: What did you study at university?

examples.text: Elle est à la fac.
examples.trans: She's at university.

related.word: short for 'la faculté'; à la fac

meanings.en: face, front; face à = facing, in the face of, confronted with
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la face', plural 'les faces') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'face'.

examples.text: Face à cette situation.
examples.trans: Faced with this situation.

examples.text: Regarder en face.
examples.trans: To look straight in the face.

examples.text: Claire, regarde par la vitre: ils sont face à face sous le tilleul!
examples.trans: Claire, look through the glass: they are face to face under the linden tree!

meanings.note: Takes *à* before an infinitive when following a noun or *être* with a concrete subject (*un panneau facile à lire*, 'an easy-to-read sign').

examples.text: Cette recette de soupe aux lentilles est simple et facile à faire.
examples.trans: This lentil soup recipe is simple and easy to make.

examples.text: Les grands chiffres noirs sont faciles à lire de loin.
examples.trans: The large black numbers are easy to read from afar.

meanings.note: Regularly formed from facile + -ment.

examples.text: Ces chaises se plient très facilement d'une seule main.
examples.trans: These chairs fold up very easily with one hand.

examples.text: Le grès épais ne se casse pas facilement.
examples.trans: Thick stoneware does not break easily.

meanings.note: Feminine: factrice.

examples.text: Le facteur vient de me faire signer un recommandé. Il y a un tampon rouge d'agence immobilière.
examples.trans: The postman just had me sign for registered mail. There is a red property-agency stamp.

examples.text: Voici le facteur sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the postman, mail carrier on the table.

meanings.note: A bill or invoice setting out what is owed for goods or services.

examples.text: Voici la facture.
examples.trans: Here's the bill.

examples.text: La facture est chère.
examples.trans: The bill is expensive.

examples.text: Oui, c'est envoyé. Voici la facture.
examples.trans: Yes, it's been sent. Here's the bill.

meanings.note: Se sentir faible = to feel weak. Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Tu crois que ça va te rendre faible?
examples.trans: Do you think that will make you look weak?

examples.text: Un signal très faible.
examples.trans: A very weak signal.

meanings.note: From 'faible' (weak).

examples.text: C'est mauvais d'être en position de faiblesse.
examples.trans: It's bad to be in a position of weakness.

examples.text: Chacun a ses faiblesses.
examples.trans: Everyone has their weaknesses.

examples.text: C'est mauvais pour l'agence d'être en position de faiblesse.
examples.trans: It's bad for the agency to be in a position of weakness.

meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire') meaning 'to weaken'; essential in everyday spoken and professional French.

examples.text: Il ne faut pas faiblir.
examples.trans: We must not falter.

examples.text: Battez-vous pour chaque contrat sans faiblir.
examples.trans: Fight for each contract without faltering.

meanings.en: to almost / nearly do something (followed by infinitive)
meanings.note: Used chiefly in the passé composé: j'ai failli tomber = I nearly fell.

examples.text: J'ai failli oublier les clés sur le comptoir!
examples.trans: I nearly forgot the keys on the counter!

examples.text: La tasse a failli glisser du plateau.
examples.trans: The cup almost slipped off the tray.

meanings.note: No article.

meanings.en: faire faillite = to go bankrupt, to go bust
meanings.note: No article.

examples.text: Et on peut faire faillite?
examples.trans: And could we go bankrupt?

examples.text: L'entreprise a fait faillite.
examples.trans: The company went bankrupt.

meanings.note: Appetite or hunger ('avoir faim' = to be hungry, literally 'to have hunger').

examples.text: La marche au grand air nous a donné faim!
examples.trans: Walking in the fresh air has made us hungry!

examples.text: Avez-vous faim? La brioche sort tout juste du four.
examples.trans: Are you hungry? The brioche is fresh out of the oven.

meanings.note: for (duration): ça fait des mois que j'attends = I've been waiting for months

meanings.en: faire la surprise à = to surprise
ça fait trois semaines que = it's been three weeks since
meanings.note: With time.

examples.text: Je peux vous faire confiance?
examples.trans: Can I trust you?

examples.text: Faites-moi confiance. Descendons l'accueillir.
examples.trans: Trust me. Let us go down and welcome him.

meanings.note: In en fait (actually), the final t is pronounced: fɛt.

examples.text: C'est un fait.
examples.trans: It's a fact.

examples.text: En fait, je travaille ici.
examples.trans: Actually, I work here.

meanings.en: to be needed, to be necessary
meanings.note: only with impersonal il: il faut + noun or infinitive

examples.text: Il faut des autorisations.
examples.trans: You need permits.

examples.text: Il faut partir.
examples.trans: We have to leave.

meanings.note: Well-known, celebrated ('le fameux...' = that famous...); delicious, splendid.

examples.text: Voici enfin la fameuse boussole dont parlait la lettre!
examples.trans: Here at last is the famous compass the letter spoke of!

examples.text: Sa tarte aux prunes est vraiment fameuse.
examples.trans: Her plum tart is truly delicious.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'family'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une fête familiale.
examples.trans: A family party.

examples.text: Le cercle familial.
examples.trans: The family circle.

examples.text: C'est trop fou pour notre comédie familiale, Andréa.
examples.trans: That is too crazy for our family comedy, Andrea.

meanings.note: Feminine: familière (/familjɛʁ/).

examples.text: Comme c'est curieux! L'écriture sur l'étiquette me semblait familière.
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on the tag seemed familiar to me.

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment familier.
examples.trans: This place is really familiar.

examples.text: Ma famille est à Paris.
examples.trans: My family is in Paris.

examples.text: C'est pour faire plaisir à ma famille.
examples.trans: It's to make my family happy.

meanings.note: Un fan de cinéma.

examples.text: Il faut penser aux vrais fans de la série.
examples.trans: We have to think of the real fans of the show.

examples.text: Elle est fan de cette actrice.
examples.trans: She's a fan of this actress.

meanings.note: Un film fantastique.
Un film fantastique.

examples.text: Ce nouveau scénario est absolument fantastique!
examples.trans: This new script is absolutely fantastic!

examples.text: C'est une actrice fantastique que tout le monde adore.
examples.trans: She is a fantastic actress whom everyone adores.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le fantôme', plural 'les fantômes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ghost'.

examples.text: C'est moi le fameux fantôme.
examples.trans: I am the famous ghost.

examples.text: Son fantôme, c'est une idée brillante!
examples.trans: Her ghost is a brilliant idea!

examples.text: Le fantôme va nous sauver.
examples.trans: The ghost is going to save us.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la farce', plural 'les farces') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'prank'.

examples.text: C'est une mauvaise farce.
examples.trans: It is a bad joke.

examples.text: Le dindon de la farce.
examples.trans: The butt of the joke.

examples.text: Et aussi de dindon de la farce!
examples.trans: And also of a fall guy!

meanings.en: flour (cereal powder for baking or cooking)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la farine', plural 'les farines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'flour'.

examples.text: Ils pétrissent de la pâte avec de la farine.
examples.trans: They knead dough with flour.

examples.text: Ajouter un kilo de farine de blé.
examples.trans: To add a kilo of wheat flour.

meanings.note: La Fashion Week = Fashion Week. Feminine noun ('la fashion', plural 'les fashions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fashion style'.

examples.text: Pendant la Fashion Week.
examples.trans: During Fashion Week.

examples.text: Le monde de la fashion.
examples.trans: The fashion world.

examples.text: Merci d'être venue pendant la Fashion Week.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming during Fashion Week.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la fatigue', plural 'les fatigues') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tiredness'.

examples.text: Écroulé de fatigue.
examples.trans: Collapsed with exhaustion.

examples.text: Je vais m'écrouler de fatigue.
examples.trans: I am going to collapse from tiredness.

examples.text: La fatigue me plonge dans une transe.
examples.trans: Exhaustion plunges me into a trance.

meanings.en: to tire, to tire out, to wear out
meanings.note: Reflexive.
Reflexive.

examples.text: Après huit ans à me fatiguer!
examples.trans: After eight years of tiring me out!

examples.text: Ce voyage m'a beaucoup fatigué.
examples.trans: This trip tired me out a lot.

meanings.note: Très fatigué = very tired.

examples.text: Je suis très fatiguée.
examples.trans: I'm very tired.

examples.text: On est tous fatigués.
examples.trans: We're all tired.

faufiler.gloss: to slip in, weave through, sneak in

meanings.en: to slip through, weave one's way
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to slip through'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'faufilé').

examples.text: Je me faufile rapidement dans la foule.
examples.trans: I slip through the crowd quickly.

examples.text: Il se faufile entre les tables.
examples.trans: He weaves between the tables.

examples.text: Pardonnez-moi, je me faufile rapidement.
examples.trans: Pardon me, I am slipping through quickly.

meanings.note: C'est ma faute = it's my fault.
Une faute d'orthographe.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas ta faute.
examples.trans: It's not your fault.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas votre faute. Mais je n'ai que le manteau sur mon dos!
examples.trans: It is not your fault. Still, I only have the coat on my back!

meanings.note: Un fauteuil d'orchestre.
Un fauteuil d'orchestre.

examples.text: C'est son fauteuil.
examples.trans: That's his armchair.

examples.text: Assieds-toi dans ce fauteuil.
examples.trans: Sit down in this armchair.

meanings.note: C'est faux = that's wrong.
Descriptive

examples.text: Non, c'est faux.
examples.trans: No, that's wrong.

examples.text: C'est une fausse excuse.
examples.trans: It's a fake excuse.

meanings.note: Figurative: juste une façade. Feminine noun ('la façade', plural 'les façades') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'facade'.
Figurative: juste une façade. Feminine noun ('la façade', plural 'les façades') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'facade'.

examples.text: Juste une façade.
examples.trans: Just a front.

examples.text: C'est une façade pour cacher la vérité.
examples.trans: It is a front to hide the truth.

examples.text: Un arrangement temporaire, juste une façade.
examples.trans: A temporary arrangement, just a facade.

meanings.note: une façon de faire = a way of doing things

examples.text: C'est une façon bizarre de faire.
examples.trans: It's a strange way of doing things.

examples.text: De toute façon, je viens.
examples.trans: Anyway, I'm coming.

meanings.note: Sa femme = his wife.
Ma femme = my wife.

examples.text: C'est une femme brillante.
examples.trans: She's a brilliant woman.

examples.text: Il parle à sa femme.
examples.trans: He's talking to his wife.

meanings.note: Regular *-re* verb (*vendre* pattern); past participle *fendu* ('cracked, split') is common for dry wood.

examples.text: Percez doucement pour ne pas fendre cette fine planche.
examples.trans: Drill gently so as not to split this thin board.

examples.text: Heureusement, le bois ancien n'est pas fendu du tout.
examples.trans: Fortunately, the old wood isn't cracked at all.

meanings.en: first element of feng shui (Chinese spatial harmony)

examples.text: Elle réorganise le bureau selon le feng shui.
examples.trans: She is reorganizing the office according to feng shui.

examples.text: C'est très feng shui.
examples.trans: It is very feng shui.

meanings.note: Ouvrir / fermer la fenêtre. Feminine noun ('la fenêtre', plural 'les fenêtres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'window'.

examples.text: Regardez, il y a une fenêtre là-haut!
examples.trans: Look, there's a window up there!

examples.text: Elle regarde par la fenêtre.
examples.trans: She looks out the window.

examples.text: Parfait. La fenêtre donne sur la rue ou sur la cour?
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

meanings.note: En fer = wrought-iron; rideau de fer = metal shutter.

examples.text: Parfait! Le rideau de fer est ouvert?
examples.trans: Great! Is the metal shutter open?

examples.text: Cette grande clé en fer? Tenez, la voilà.
examples.trans: This big iron wrench? Here you go.

examples.text: Un taxi vient de s'arrêter juste devant la grille en fer!
examples.trans: A taxi just stopped right outside the iron gate!

meanings.note: Thin sheet iron coated with tin, used for biscuit tins and keepsake boxes.

examples.text: Elle range ses boutons anciens dans une boîte en fer-blanc.
examples.trans: She keeps her vintage buttons in a tin box.

examples.text: Le coffret en fer-blanc a protégé les lettres de la pluie.
examples.trans: The tinplate box protected the letters from the rain.

meanings.note: Same form in masculine and feminine singular (ferme). Placed after the noun in physical descriptions: un tour ferme ('a firm turn'), d'un pas ferme ('with a steady step').

examples.text: Donnez un tour ferme à la clé pour ouvrir le vieux loquet.
examples.trans: Give the key a firm turn to open the old latch.

examples.text: Choisissez des citrons bien jaunes et fermes sous les doigts.
examples.trans: Choose lemons that are bright yellow and firm to the touch.

meanings.note: Fermer la porte.

examples.text: La porte est fermée.
examples.trans: The door is closed.

examples.text: Bonjour! Excusez-moi, la porte est fermée à clé?
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: Excusez-moi, la porte est fermée à clé?
examples.trans: Excuse me, is the door locked?

meanings.note: Fermeture éclair = zipper.

examples.text: Regardez la fermeture éclair... oui, ses initiales sont juste là!
examples.trans: Check the zipper... yes, her initials are right here!

examples.text: Voici la fermeture sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the closing on the table.

meanings.note: Avec fermeté = firmly. Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'firmness, resolve'.

examples.text: Parler avec fermeté.
examples.trans: To speak with firmness.

examples.text: Faire preuve de fermeté.
examples.trans: To show firmness.

examples.text: D'accord, je vais lui parler avec fermeté.
examples.trans: Alright, I will speak to him with firmness.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'closed'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: La porte est fermée!
examples.trans: The door is locked!

examples.text: Le magasin est fermé le dimanche.
examples.trans: The shop is closed on Sundays.

examples.text: La porte est fermée! Je ne veux pas rester ici.
examples.trans: The door is locked! I don't want to stay here.

meanings.note: Everyday word.

examples.text: Merci, jolies petites fesses!
examples.trans: Thank you, pretty little backside!

examples.text: Tes jolies petites fesses ont amorti le choc.
examples.trans: Your pretty little backside cushioned the shock.

meanings.note: le Festival de Cannes = the Cannes Film Festival

examples.text: Tu as travaillé au festival?
examples.trans: Did you work at the festival?

examples.text: Le festival commence demain.
examples.trans: The festival starts tomorrow.

meanings.note: Tu as du feu?.

meanings.en: du feu = a light (for a cigarette)
meanings.note: Tu as du feu?.

examples.text: Tu as du feu?
examples.trans: Have you got a light?

examples.text: Le feu est rouge.
examples.trans: The light is red.

meanings.note: le feuillage vert = the green foliage

examples.text: Des aigus comme le feuillage.
examples.trans: High notes like foliage.

examples.text: Le feuillage des arbres.
examples.trans: The foliage of the trees.

examples.text: Et des aigus comme le feuillage.
examples.trans: And highs like foliage.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la feuille', plural 'les feuilles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sheet of paper'.

examples.text: Parapher cette feuille.
examples.trans: Initial this sheet.

examples.text: Pliez cette feuille et mettez-la dans votre poche tout de suite.
examples.trans: Fold that sheet and put it in your pocket right now.

examples.text: Attendez: il y a une deuxième feuille pliée et attachée derrière cet avis...
examples.trans: Wait: there is a second folded sheet clipped behind this notice...

meanings.note: Inside a piano, compressed wool *feutre* covers the hammers and lines tiny hinge bushings to keep the action silent.

examples.text: Les marteaux du piano sont recouverts de feutre de laine.
examples.trans: The piano hammers are covered in wool felt.

examples.text: Collez un petit rond de feutre sous chaque pied de chaise.
examples.trans: Stick a small felt pad under each chair leg.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Bien chaude! Vous entendez ça, Claire? Une eau chaude moderne, fiable, cinq étoiles!
examples.trans: Nice and hot! Do you hear that, Claire? Modern, reliable, five-star hot water!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment fiable.
examples.trans: This place is really reliable, dependable.

meanings.note: Attacher avec de la ficelle = tie up with twine.

examples.text: Attachez le thym et le persil avec un bout de ficelle.
examples.trans: Tie the thyme and parsley with a piece of twine.

examples.text: Le paquet de la librairie est fermé par une ficelle blanche.
examples.trans: The parcel from the bookshop is tied with white string.

meanings.note: Catalog card, recipe card, or summary sheet.

examples.text: Chaque livre ancien possède sa fiche dans le tiroir en chêne.
examples.trans: Every old book has its catalog card in the oak drawer.

examples.text: Elle consulte sa fiche de cuisine avant de peser le beurre.
examples.trans: She checks her recipe card before weighing the butter.

meanings.en: to care, to give a damn (informal)
meanings.note: Se ficher de = not to care.
Ficher quelque part.

examples.text: Je m'en fiche!
examples.trans: I do not care!

examples.text: Il s'en fiche complètement.
examples.trans: He does not care at all.

examples.text: Je m'en fiche! Je connais le rôle par cœur.
examples.trans: I do not care! I know the role by heart.

meanings.note: A file or indexed set of records; here an agent's client records.

examples.text: Je suis dans les fichiers d'Andréa.
examples.trans: I'm in Andréa's files.

examples.text: Ouvre le fichier.
examples.trans: Open the file.

examples.text: Tu ne m'as pas vu dans les fichiers d'Andréa?
examples.trans: Haven't you seen me in Andréa's files?

meanings.note: confondre la fiction et la réalité = to confuse fiction and reality

examples.text: C'est une pure fiction.
examples.trans: It is pure fiction.

examples.text: Un roman de fiction.
examples.trans: A work of fiction.

examples.text: Tu confonds la fiction et la réalité.
examples.trans: You are confusing fiction and reality.

related.word: confondre la fiction et la réalité

meanings.note: Loyal and steadfast; accurate ('fidèle au rendez-vous' = unfailingly on time).

examples.text: Les hirondelles sont fidèles au printemps chaque année.
examples.trans: The swallows faithfully return each spring.

examples.text: Ce croquis est très fidèle à la façade d'origine.
examples.trans: This sketch is very true to the original facade.

meanings.note: la fidélité à l'agence = loyalty to the agency

examples.text: Une grande fidélité.
examples.trans: Great loyalty.

examples.text: La fidélité des clients.
examples.trans: Customer loyalty.

examples.text: Il m'a parlé de fidélité à l'agence.
examples.trans: He spoke to me about agency loyalty.

meanings.note: Final *-r* IS pronounced in masculine *fier* (`/fjɛʁ/`), just like in *cher* and *amer*.

examples.text: Il est très fier du petit café qu'ils ont ouvert ensemble.
examples.trans: He is very proud of the little café they opened together.

examples.text: Elle est fière de servir le pain chaud de son propre four.
examples.trans: She is proud to serve warm bread from her own oven.

meanings.en: pride, sense of dignity or achievement
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la fierté', plural 'les fiertés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pride'.

examples.text: C'est une grande fierté pour nous.
examples.trans: It is a great pride for us.

examples.text: Avec une immense fierté.
examples.trans: With immense pride.

examples.text: C'est avec une immense fierté que je vous accueille ici.
examples.trans: It is with immense pride that I welcome you here.

meanings.en: background acting, working as an extra
meanings.note: faire de la figuration = to work as an extra

examples.text: Je ne suis pas venue pour faire de la figuration.
examples.trans: I did not come to do background work.

examples.text: Il a commencé sa carrière par la figuration.
examples.trans: He started his career as an extra.

examples.text: Mathias, je ne fais pas de la figuration!
examples.trans: Mathias, I do not do background work!

meanings.note: Pronounced /fil/ with audible l.

examples.text: Même quand la chambre quatre est vide, le vieux fil sonne deux fois.
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire rings twice.

examples.text: Le fil avait besoin d'être redressé, c'est tout. Rien de sentimental dans le bon entretien.
examples.trans: The wire needed straightening, that is all. Nothing sentimental about good maintenance.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to hand over'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'filé').

meanings.en: to dash off, to leave quickly
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to dash off'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'filé').

examples.text: File-moi ton sac.
examples.trans: Give me your bag.

examples.text: Tu files du fric à tes amis?
examples.trans: Do you hand out cash to your friends?

examples.text: Le temps file très vite.
examples.trans: Time flies very fast.

meanings.note: The family relationship: ma fille, my daughter.
A female child or young person; context distinguishes this from daughter.

examples.text: Je veux voir ma fille.
examples.trans: I want to see my daughter.

examples.text: Je suis ta fille!
examples.trans: I'm your daughter!

examples.text: Je veux voir ma fille, voyager.
examples.trans: I want to see my daughter, to travel.

examples.text: Tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: You've got the Kechiche film.

examples.text: Voici le film sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the film, movie on the table.

meanings.note: the l is silent, the s is pronounced

examples.text: Votre fils est acteur.
examples.trans: Your son is an actor.

examples.text: C'est mon fils.
examples.trans: He's my son.

examples.text: Je ne savais pas que votre fils était acteur.
examples.trans: I didn't know your son was an actor.

meanings.en: to leak out, to seep out
meanings.note: Laisser filtrer = to let leak out.

examples.text: On ne peut pas laisser filtrer cette histoire.
examples.trans: We cannot let this story leak out.

examples.text: L'eau filtre lentement.
examples.trans: The water filters slowly.

examples.text: On ne peut pas laisser filtrer cette histoire de coup de poing.
examples.trans: We cannot let this punch story get out.

meanings.note: La fin du mois ('the end of the month'), à la fin ('in the end').
As an adjective, fin (/fɛ̃/) becomes fine (/fin/) in the feminine: de la porcelaine fine ('thin/fine china').

examples.text: Nous voulons ouvrir le salon de thé avant la fin du mois.
examples.trans: We want to open the tearoom before the end of the month.

examples.text: Ces tasses sont très fines, mais elles refroidissent vite.
examples.trans: These cups are very thin, so they cool down quickly.

meanings.note: L'accord final = the final chord (masculine plural finals or finaux).

examples.text: L'accord final résonne doucement sous les arbres.
examples.trans: The final chord rings softly under the trees.

examples.text: Voici la touche finale sur notre panneau d'accueil.
examples.trans: Here is the final touch on our welcome sign.

examples.text: Je crois que je vais bien dormir ce soir, finalement.
examples.trans: I think I will sleep well tonight after all.

examples.text: Alors tu n'as pas besoin d'argent, finalement.
examples.trans: So you don't need money, after all.

examples.text: Finalement, elle reste.
examples.trans: In the end, she's staying.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to finalize'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'finalisé').

examples.text: J'ai finalisé le contrat.
examples.trans: I finalized the contract.

examples.text: C'est bon, j'ai finalisé le contrat.
examples.trans: All good, I finalized the contract.

examples.text: Le financement du cinéma.
examples.trans: Cinema funding.

examples.text: On cherche un financement.
examples.trans: We are looking for funding.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to finance'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'financé').

examples.text: J'ai financé les rénovations.
examples.trans: I funded the renovations.

examples.text: Qui va financer ce projet?
examples.trans: Who will fund this project?

examples.text: J'ai financé les rénovations il y a cinq ans.
examples.trans: I financed the renovations five years ago.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé un partenaire financier.
examples.trans: I found a financial partner.

examples.text: C'est une aide financière.
examples.trans: It is financial aid.

meanings.note: C'est fini = it's over.

examples.text: Mais c'est fini.
examples.trans: But it's over.

examples.text: Le travail est fini.
examples.trans: The work is finished.

examples.text: Il a même fini toute sa soupe de légumes avant de monter.
examples.trans: He even finished all his vegetable soup before going up.

meanings.note: Finir par plus infinitive means eventually do something or end up doing it.

examples.text: Tout finit par passer.
examples.trans: Everything eventually passes.

examples.text: Je finis mon travail.
examples.trans: I'm finishing my work.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le fisc', plural 'les fiscs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tax authority'.

examples.text: Ils ont appelé le fisc.
examples.trans: They called the tax authorities.

examples.text: C'est vous qui avez appelé le fisc!
examples.trans: It is you who called the tax inspectors!

meanings.note: Contrôle fiscal = tax audit.

examples.text: Le contrôle fiscal.
examples.trans: The tax audit.

examples.text: Une année fiscale.
examples.trans: A fiscal year.

meanings.note: Small crack in porcelain or stone.

examples.text: Pas une seule fissure! Qui l'a rapportée?
examples.trans: Not a single crack! Who brought it back?

examples.text: Voici la fissure sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the crack, hairline fracture on the table.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le fixe', plural 'les fixes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'base salary'.

examples.text: Il demande une hausse de son fixe.
examples.trans: He asks for a raise in his base salary.

examples.text: Je peux aussi augmenter vos salaires fixes.
examples.trans: I can also increase your fixed salaries.

meanings.en: to fix, to attach, to establish, to set boundaries
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to fix'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'fixé').

examples.text: Fixer des limites.
examples.trans: To set limits.

examples.text: Fixer un rendez-vous.
examples.trans: To schedule an appointment.

examples.text: Personne ne fixe les clients. On rend le sac et on fait son travail.
examples.trans: Nobody stares at guests. We hand back the bag and do our job.

meanings.en: to whip, beat up (se flageller = beat oneself up)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to whip'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'flagellé').

examples.text: Arrête de te flageller.
examples.trans: Stop beating yourself up.

examples.text: Arrête de te flageller tout le temps.
examples.trans: Stop beating yourself up all the time.

meanings.en: flair, instinct, keen sense of smell
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le flair', plural 'les flairs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'intuition'.

examples.text: Avoir du flair.
examples.trans: To have a keen nose / intuition.

examples.text: Un chien avec du flair.
examples.trans: A dog with a keen sense of smell.

examples.text: Il a du flair, comme sa maîtresse.
examples.trans: He has a good nose, like his mistress.

meanings.note: Pilot flame in an oven or boiler.

examples.text: Et voilà la flamme bleue, bien stable, exactement comme il faut.
examples.trans: And there goes the blue flame, nice and steady, just as it should be.

examples.text: Voici la flamme sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the flame on the table.

meanings.note: Borrowed from English. Masculine noun ('le flash', plural 'les flashs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'camera flash'.

examples.text: Il y a eu un flash.
examples.trans: There was a camera flash.

examples.text: J'ai vu un flash dans la nuit.
examples.trans: I saw a flash in the night.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'flashy'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ce modèle est flashy.
examples.trans: This design is flashy.

examples.text: Voici un modèle flashy et audacieux.
examples.trans: Here is a flashy and daring design.

examples.text: Pas besoin de me flatter!
examples.trans: No need to flatter me!

examples.text: Il flatte la productrice.
examples.trans: He flatters the producer.

meanings.note: Être flatté de. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'flattered'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Merci beaucoup, je suis sincèrement flattée.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, I am genuinely flattered.

examples.text: Il était très flatté par ces compliments.
examples.trans: He was very flattered by these compliments.

meanings.note: Miel de fleurs ('wildflower/blossom honey') takes plural fleurs without an article after de.

examples.text: Claire pose un petit vase de fleurs fraîches sur le comptoir.
examples.trans: Claire puts a small vase of fresh flowers on the counter.

examples.text: Ce miel de fleurs a un parfum très doux.
examples.trans: This blossom honey has a very gentle aroma.

meanings.note: Decorated with a flower pattern or covered in blossoms.

examples.text: Oui, de charmants voyageurs très polis, et une dame calme avec une boîte à chapeau fleurie a pris la six!
examples.trans: Yes, lovely polite travellers, and a quiet lady with a floral hatbox took Room Six!

examples.text: Au mois de mai, le balcon fleuri parfume toute la cour.
examples.trans: In the month of May, the flower-filled balcony scents the whole courtyard.

meanings.note: Un/une fleuriste = florist or flower shop.

examples.text: Prenez la deuxième rue, à côté du fleuriste, pas la ruelle étroite.
examples.trans: Take the second street, beside the flower shop, not the narrow alley.

examples.text: Voici le fleuriste sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the florist, flower shop on the table.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le fleuve', plural 'les fleuves') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'river'.

examples.text: Le fleuve brise ses digues.
examples.trans: The river breaks its dikes.

examples.text: Froides comme l'eau du fleuve.
examples.trans: Cold as river water.

meanings.note: Everyday slang: les flics.

examples.text: Écoutez, ce sont les flics!
examples.trans: Listen, it's the cops!

examples.text: Écoutez, ce sont les flics! Il faut partir d'ici!
examples.trans: Listen, it's the cops! We have to get out of here!

meanings.en: to freak out, panic, get scared
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to freak out'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'flippé').

examples.text: J'ai flippé face à ta jeunesse.
examples.trans: I freaked out facing your youth.

examples.text: Il flippe avant de monter sur scène.
examples.trans: He freaks out before going on stage.

examples.text: Je flippe pour mon avenir.
examples.trans: I am terrified for my future.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le flop', plural 'les flops') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'flop'.

examples.text: Le flop du film n'est pas ma faute.
examples.trans: The film's flop is not my fault.

examples.text: Ce projet a été un véritable flop.
examples.trans: This project was a complete flop.

meanings.note: Out of focus or indistinct to the eye (for example when reading without one's glasses).

examples.text: Oh là là... à l'envers, le deux et le six se ressemblent énormément quand c'est flou!
examples.trans: Oh dear... upside down, two and six look remarkably similar when blurry!

examples.text: Sans mes lunettes de lecture, les petits chiffres restent tout flous.
examples.trans: Without my reading glasses, the small numbers stay completely blurry.

meanings.note: Borrowed from English.

examples.text: Voilà le flyer.
examples.trans: Here's the flyer.

examples.text: Je donne des flyers.
examples.trans: I'm handing out flyers.

meanings.en: arrow (drawn pointer or bow arrow); church spire
meanings.note: Used constantly on maps, signs, and blueprints for a directional arrow.

examples.text: Suivez la petite flèche bleue dessinée sur le plan.
examples.trans: Follow the little blue arrow drawn on the plan.

examples.text: Une flèche en bois indique l'entrée du jardin.
examples.trans: A wooden arrow points to the garden entrance.

meanings.note: Ma foi is a mild conversational interjection.

examples.text: Ma foi, personne ne refuse une brioche chaude à la cannelle à sept heures du matin.
examples.trans: Well now, nobody turns down a warm cinnamon roll at seven in the morning.

examples.text: Voici la foi sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the faith on the table.

meanings.note: Du foin = some hay.

examples.text: Il y a des insectes dans le foin?
examples.trans: Are there insects in the hay?

examples.text: Ils sont dans le foin.
examples.trans: They are in the hay.

meanings.note: une bête de foire = a fairground attraction

examples.text: Des bêtes de foire.
examples.trans: Fairground animals.

examples.text: Aller à la foire.
examples.trans: To go to the fair.

examples.text: Ce sont juste des bêtes de foire.
examples.trans: They are just fairground animals.

meanings.en: to blow, fail, mess up completely
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to blow'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'foiré').

examples.text: J'ai totalement foiré mon audition.
examples.trans: I totally blew my audition.

examples.text: Le projet a foiré au dernier moment.
examples.trans: The project fell through at the last moment.

examples.text: J'ai totalement foiré mon audition aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: I totally blew my audition today.

meanings.note: Une fois, deux fois = once, twice.

examples.text: Encore une fois!
examples.trans: Once more!

examples.text: Rester ici avec vous tous? Oui, cent fois oui!
examples.trans: Stay here with all of you? Yes, a hundred times yes!

meanings.note: c'est de la folie = that's crazy / madness

examples.text: C'est de la folie de changer la scène!
examples.trans: It's madness to change the scene!

examples.text: Quelle folie!
examples.trans: What madness!

examples.text: C'est de la folie! La première, c'est dans une semaine.
examples.trans: That is madness! Opening night is in a week.

foncer.gloss: to go for it, rush ahead

meanings.en: to rush boldly forward, go for it
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go for it'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'foncé').

examples.text: C'est une belle chance, fonce!
examples.trans: It's a great opportunity, go for it!

examples.text: Elle te plaît beaucoup. Fonce!
examples.trans: You like her very much. Go for it!

examples.text: Maintenant, tu dois foncer au casting.
examples.trans: Now, you must hurry to the casting.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la fonction', plural 'les fonctions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'duty'.

examples.text: C'est la vraie fonction d'une assistante.
examples.trans: That is the real job of an assistant.

examples.text: Exercer ses fonctions.
examples.trans: To carry out one's duties.

examples.text: C'est ça, la vraie fonction d'une assistante.
examples.trans: That is the true job of an assistant.

meanings.en: to work, to operate, to function
meanings.note: Synonym of marcher.

examples.text: Ça ne fonctionne pas!
examples.trans: That does not work!

examples.text: La machine fonctionne bien.
examples.trans: The machine works well.

examples.text: Non, ça ne va pas! Ça ne fonctionne pas!
examples.trans: No, that will not do! That does not work!

meanings.note: Compound colours stay invariable: bleu foncé.

examples.text: Attendez, elle est bleu foncé, exactement comme la vôtre!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

examples.text: Une autre valise bleu foncé! C'est le sac de Madame Odette?
examples.trans: Another dark-blue suitcase! Is this Madam Odette's bag?

examples.text: Attendez... bonjour, monsieur! Vous appelez pour la valise bleu foncé?
examples.trans: Wait... hello, sir! Are you calling about the dark-blue suitcase?

meanings.note: au fond du couloir = at the end of the corridor

meanings.en: à fond: fully; with all one's effort
meanings.note: Se donner à fond: give it one's all.

examples.text: Au fond, il est gentil.
examples.trans: Deep down, he's nice.

examples.text: C'est au fond à droite.
examples.trans: It's at the back on the right.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la fondation', plural 'les fondations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'foundation'.

examples.text: Elle donne de l'argent à une fondation.
examples.trans: She gives money to a foundation.

examples.text: Pour une fondation animale...
examples.trans: For an animal foundation...

fonder.gloss: to found, to establish a family

meanings.en: to found, to establish, to build (a family, an institution)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to found'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'fondé').

examples.text: Fonder une famille.
examples.trans: To start a family.

examples.text: Fonder une entreprise.
examples.trans: To found a company.

examples.text: Je veux fonder cette famille avec toi.
examples.trans: I want to build this family with you.

meanings.note: invariable plural/singular; de nouveaux fonds = new funds/capital
Masculine noun ('le fonds', plural 'les fonds') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'funds'.

examples.text: S'il n'y a pas de nouveaux fonds, ASK ne survivra pas.
examples.trans: If there are no new funds, ASK will not survive.

examples.text: Il cherche des fonds.
examples.trans: He is looking for funds.

examples.text: S'il n'y a pas de nouveaux fonds, ASK ne survivra pas à ce contrôle fiscal.
examples.trans: If there are no new funds, ASK will not survive this tax audit.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la fontaine', plural 'les fontaines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fountain'.

examples.text: Des fontaines de limonade.
examples.trans: Lemonade fountains.

examples.text: Une belle fontaine.
examples.trans: A beautiful fountain.

examples.text: Cinq sur cinq. Vous êtes devant la petite fontaine en pierre?
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you in front of the little stone fountain?

meanings.note: des forces = energy, strength (plural)

examples.text: Ça donne des forces.
examples.trans: It gives you energy.

examples.text: Je n'ai plus de force.
examples.trans: I have no strength left.

meanings.note: To apply too much force to a lock or mechanism ('sans forcer' = gently, without forcing); to compel.

examples.text: Tournez la clé doucement sans jamais forcer la serrure.
examples.trans: Turn the key gently without ever forcing the lock.

examples.text: Inutile de forcer le couvercle, il glisse sur le côté.
examples.trans: There's no need to force the lid; it slides sideways.

meanings.note: Inevitably, definitely, bound to be ('pas forcément' = not necessarily).

examples.text: Avec une telle odeur de beurre, c'est forcément délicieux.
examples.trans: With a butter aroma like that, it's bound to be delicious.

examples.text: Le plus court chemin n'est pas forcément le plus joli.
examples.trans: The shortest path isn't necessarily the prettiest.

meanings.note: Faire une formation. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'training course, education'.

examples.text: Tu as vraiment fait une formation?
examples.trans: Did you really take a training course?

examples.text: Une formation professionnelle.
examples.trans: A professional training course.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: L'assurance a formellement rejeté la demande.
examples.trans: The insurance categorically rejected the claim.

examples.text: L'assurance a formellement rejeté leur dossier.
examples.trans: The insurance formally rejected their claim.

meanings.note: To make up a shape or whole when joined together; to train an apprentice.

examples.text: Les quatre cartes réunies forment un plan du quartier.
examples.trans: Placed together, the four cards form a map of the neighborhood.

examples.text: Elle a formé plusieurs jeunes pâtissiers dans sa cuisine.
examples.trans: She has trained several young pastry chefs in her kitchen.

examples.text: Tu as fait quelque chose de formidable.
examples.trans: You did something wonderful.

examples.text: C'est une actrice formidable.
examples.trans: She's a wonderful actress.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le formulaire', plural 'les formulaires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'form'.

examples.text: Remplissez ce formulaire.
examples.trans: Fill out this form.

examples.text: On peut télécharger le formulaire maintenant?
examples.trans: Can we download the form now?

examples.text: Voyons ce formulaire sur son ordinateur.
examples.trans: Let us look for this form on his computer.

meanings.note: Describes strength or intensity.
Can mean loud; as an adverb in parler fort, does not change.

meanings.en: quelque chose de fort = something powerful
meanings.note: After quelque chose, the descriptive word is introduced by de.

examples.text: Elle est très forte.
examples.trans: She's very strong.

examples.text: Oh! Vous avez vu Étienne par la fenêtre? J'essayais pourtant de sourire deux fois plus fort!
examples.trans: Oh! Did you see Etienne through the window? Yet I was trying to smile twice as wide!

meanings.note: Coûter une fortune means 'to cost a fortune / cost an arm and a leg'.

examples.text: Refaire toute la toiture en ardoise coûte une fortune.
examples.trans: Redoing the whole slate roof costs a fortune.

examples.text: On peut meubler la salle avec goût sans dépenser une fortune.
examples.trans: We can furnish the room tastefully without spending a fortune.

meanings.note: The circumflex on *ê* marks an Old French *s* that still survives in English *forest* and French *forestier*.

examples.text: Après la pluie, le jardin sent aussi bon qu'une forêt.
examples.trans: After the rain, the garden smells as good as a forest.

examples.text: Nous marchons souvent dans la forêt le dimanche matin.
examples.trans: We often walk in the forest on Sunday mornings.

meanings.note: C'est fou! = it's crazy!.
Informal.

examples.text: C'est fou!
examples.trans: It's crazy!

examples.text: Elle est folle de joie.
examples.trans: She's wild with joy.

meanings.en: lightning; coup de foudre = love at first sight
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la foudre', plural 'les foudres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lightning'.

examples.text: Ce fut un coup de foudre.
examples.trans: It was love at first sight.

examples.text: La foudre est tombée.
examples.trans: Lightning struck.

meanings.note: Standard culinary verb for beating eggs, cream, or lemon curd (*fouetter la crème*, *des œufs fouettés*).

examples.text: Fouettez le jus de citron avec les œufs et le sucre.
examples.trans: Whisk the lemon juice with the eggs and sugar.

examples.text: Elle fouette la crème fraîche jusqu'à ce qu'elle soit légère.
examples.trans: She whips the cream until it is light.

meanings.note: To search pockets, drawers, or shelves thoroughly.

examples.text: Il fouille dans son manteau pour retrouver ses lunettes.
examples.trans: He rummages through his coat to find his glasses.

examples.text: Nous avons fouillé toutes les étagères du fond.
examples.trans: We searched all the back shelves.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la foule', plural 'les foules') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'crowd'.

examples.text: La foule sur la Croisette.
examples.trans: The crowd on the Croisette.

examples.text: Une grande foule.
examples.trans: A large crowd.

examples.text: Regarde le soleil et la foule sur la Croisette.
examples.trans: Look at the sun and the crowd on the Croisette.

meanings.note: Sorti du four = fresh out of the oven.

examples.text: Mon pain est déjà dans le four, au moins.
examples.trans: My bread is already in the oven, at least.

examples.text: Bonjour, Madame Odette! Mes brioches à la cannelle sortent tout juste du four.
examples.trans: Good morning, Madam Odette! My cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Tout droit sorti du four: le gâteau au citron du vendredi, avec les parts du coin!
examples.trans: Straight out of the oven: Friday lemon cake, with the corner pieces!

meanings.note: Plural *des fourneaux*; *être aux fourneaux* means 'to be cooking at the stove'.

examples.text: La grande casserole de soupe mijote sur le fourneau.
examples.trans: The big pot of soup simmers on the stove.

examples.text: Dès l'aube, le boulanger travaille devant ses fourneaux.
examples.trans: From dawn, the baker works in front of his ovens and stoves.

meanings.note: Une fraction de seconde. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'fraction, small part'.
Une fraction du budget. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'fraction, small part'.

examples.text: Tout a basculé en une fraction de seconde!
examples.trans: Everything flipped in a fraction of a second!

examples.text: Cela s'est produit en une fraction de seconde.
examples.trans: It happened in a fraction of a second.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la fracture', plural 'les fractures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fracture'.

examples.text: En cas de fractures.
examples.trans: In case of fractures.

examples.text: Une fracture du dos.
examples.trans: A back fracture.

examples.text: En cas de fractures du dos.
examples.trans: In case of back fractures.

examples.text: Les acteurs sont fragiles et sensibles.
examples.trans: Actors are fragile and sensitive.

examples.text: Attention, c'est fragile!
examples.trans: Careful, it's fragile!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to weaken'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'fragilisé').

examples.text: Ce départ fragilise l'agence.
examples.trans: This departure weakens the agency.

examples.text: Le départ de Mathias fragilise notre agence.
examples.trans: Mathias's departure weakens our agency.

meanings.note: argent frais = fresh funds
de l'eau fraîche = cool water

examples.text: Il nous faut de l'argent frais.
examples.trans: We need fresh funds.

examples.text: Je voudrais de l'eau fraîche.
examples.trans: I would like cool water.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la fraise', plural 'les fraises') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'strawberry'.

examples.text: Ces belles fraises sont délicieuses.
examples.trans: These lovely strawberries are delicious.

examples.text: Manger des fraises.
examples.trans: To eat strawberries.

examples.text: On peut servir du beurre salé avec de la confiture de fraises?
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with strawberry jam?

meanings.note: Feminine: franche.

examples.text: Non, Claire, soyons francs! Monsieur, nous respectons beaucoup le Guide de Lyon!
examples.trans: No, Claire, let us be frank! Sir, we deeply respect the Lyon Guide!

examples.text: Et voilà la cloche du portail. Un coup franc.
examples.trans: There goes the gate bell. One firm ring.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Franchement, c'est impossible.
examples.trans: Frankly, it is impossible.

examples.text: Franchement, il n'a pas tort.
examples.trans: Frankly, he is not wrong.

examples.text: franchement, petit frère, tu m'as manqué aussi.
examples.trans: honestly, little brother, I missed you too.

meanings.note: Regular -ir (-issant) verb.

examples.text: Regardez par la fenêtre de la cour, Étienne: quelqu'un vient de franchir le portail en courant!
examples.trans: Look through the courtyard window, Etienne: someone just ran through the gate!

examples.text: C'est facile à franchir ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to cross, step through together.

meanings.note: Parler avec franchise. Feminine noun ('la franchise', plural 'les franchises') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'frankness'.

examples.text: J'ai toujours adoré ta franchise.
examples.trans: I have always loved your frankness.

examples.text: Votre franchise me touche.
examples.trans: Your frankness touches me.

examples.text: Nous devons nous parler en toute franchise.
examples.trans: We must speak to each other frankly.

meanings.note: no capital letter for the adjective
As a noun naming a person, written with a capital: un Français, une Française; les Français means the French.

examples.text: La paperasse française!
examples.trans: French paperwork!

examples.text: Il est français.
examples.trans: He's French.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'striking'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est vraiment très frappant.
examples.trans: It is truly very striking.

examples.text: C'est vraiment très frappant, Noémie.
examples.trans: It is truly very striking, Noemie.

frapper.gloss: to knock (at a door); to strike, hit

meanings.en: to knock (on a door or gate); to strike
meanings.note: *Frapper à la porte / au portail* means 'to knock at the door/gate'; also used for piano hammers striking strings.

examples.text: Quelqu'un frappe doucement à la porte d'entrée.
examples.trans: Someone is knocking softly at the front door.

examples.text: Quand on appuie sur la touche, le marteau frappe la corde.
examples.trans: When you press the key, the hammer strikes the string.

meanings.en: to hum softly (without singing the words)
meanings.note: Takes a direct object for the tune: fredonner un air, fredonner une mélodie.

examples.text: Odette fredonne la valse en lisant la vieille partition.
examples.trans: Odette hums the waltz as she reads the old sheet music.

examples.text: Nadia fredonne toujours en préparant ses gâteaux le matin.
examples.trans: Nadia always hums while making her cakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le frein', plural 'les freins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'brake pedal'.

examples.text: N'appuie pas sur le frein.
examples.trans: Do not press on the brake.

examples.text: N'appuie pas sur le frein et l'accélérateur.
examples.trans: Do not press on the brake and the accelerator.

meanings.note: Easily crumbled into powder or grains (of mortar, stone, or shortbread pastry).

examples.text: Avec le temps, le vieux mortier est devenu sec et friable.
examples.trans: Over time, the old mortar has grown dry and crumbly.

examples.text: Une bonne pâte sablée reste fine et légèrement friable.
examples.trans: Good shortbread pastry stays delicate and slightly crumbly.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le fric', plural 'les frics') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cash'.

examples.text: Il a plein de fric.
examples.trans: He has lots of money.

examples.text: Tu files du fric à tes amis?
examples.trans: Do you hand out cash to your friends?

meanings.note: Everyday short form of réfrigérateur.

examples.text: Le camion du laitier est en panne. Regardez dans le frigo!
examples.trans: The milkman's van has broken down. Look in the fridge!

examples.text: Voici le frigo sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the fridge, refrigerator on the table.

meanings.en: shiver, chill; thrill (le grand frisson = the big thrill)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le frisson', plural 'les frissons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shiver'.

examples.text: Le grand frisson.
examples.trans: The big thrill.

examples.text: Le grand frisson. Allons-y, maintenant.
examples.trans: The big thrill. Let's go now.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la friture', plural 'les fritures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fried food'.

examples.text: Une odeur de friture.
examples.trans: A smell of fried food.

examples.text: Au fait, ton haut sent la friture.
examples.trans: By the way, your top smells like frying.

meanings.en: cold (adjective); avoir froid = to feel cold; il fait froid = it's cold

examples.text: J'ai froid.
examples.trans: I'm cold.

examples.text: J'avais les mains froides sous le choc!
examples.trans: My hands were cold from the shock!

meanings.note: Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'cheese'.

examples.text: Un plateau de fromages.
examples.trans: A cheese board.

examples.text: Du fromage de chèvre.
examples.trans: Goat cheese.

examples.text: Trois bouteilles de lait, vingt œufs, du beurre, du fromage et des pommes rouges!
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

meanings.note: Froncer les sourcils = to frown.

examples.text: Qu'est-ce qu'il dit? Pourquoi vous froncez les sourcils?
examples.trans: What is he saying? Why are you frowning?

examples.text: C'est facile à froncer ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to furrow, wrinkle together.

meanings.note: Final t is silent: /fʁɔ̃/.

examples.text: Juste là sur votre front, bien au chaud.
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, safe and sound.

examples.text: Impeccable, Étienne! Et vos lunettes sont même sur votre nez et pas sur votre front.
examples.trans: Spotless, Etienne! And your glasses are even on your nose and not on your forehead.

examples.text: Laissez-moi baisser mes lunettes de mon front... Chambre neuf?!
examples.trans: Let me pull my glasses down from my forehead... Room nine?!

meanings.note: la frontière entre vie privée et travail = the boundary between private life and work

examples.text: La frontière est floue.
examples.trans: The boundary is blurry.

examples.text: Traverser la frontière.
examples.trans: To cross the border.

examples.text: La frontière entre travail et vie privée disparaît.
examples.trans: The boundary between work and private life vanishes.

meanings.en: brother-buddy, sibling pal (playful blend of frère + pote)

examples.text: Tchin, frote!
examples.trans: Cheers, brother-buddy!

examples.text: Tu es mon meilleur frote.
examples.trans: You're my best brother-buddy.

examples.text: Tu es ma sœpote et je suis ton frote!
examples.trans: You are my sister-buddy and I am your brother-buddy!

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: {M1}, est-ce que tu accroches ces lanternes en papier pour midi?
examples.trans: {M1}, are you hanging those paper lanterns for noon?

examples.text: Quinze ans à frotter des clés en laiton et à repasser mes cravates... finis en trente jours!
examples.trans: Fifteen years polishing brass keys and ironing my ties... gone in thirty days!

meanings.note: Piece of fruit ('fruits rouges' = red summer berries); figurative reward of effort.

examples.text: Elle décore la tarte avec des fruits rouges du marché.
examples.trans: She tops the tart with red berries from the market.

examples.text: Ce jardin est le fruit de trente années de patience.
examples.trans: This garden is the fruit of thirty years of patience.

examples.text: Il joue le frère de Guillaume.
examples.trans: He plays Guillaume's brother.

examples.text: J'ai un frère.
examples.trans: I have a brother.

fréquenter.gloss: to attend, frequent, hang out with

meanings.note: Fréquenter une école. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to attend'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'fréquenté').
Fréquenter un café. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to attend'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'fréquenté').

examples.text: J'ai fréquenté l'école française à Berlin.
examples.trans: I attended the French school in Berlin.

examples.text: Il fréquente ce milieu depuis longtemps.
examples.trans: He has frequented these circles for a long time.

meanings.en: to flee, to run away from, to avoid
meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to flee, to avoid'.

examples.text: Fuir ses devoirs.
examples.trans: To flee one's duties.

examples.text: Fuir le danger.
examples.trans: To flee danger.

examples.text: {F2}, il y a un problème à l'intérieur? Est-ce que la chaudière est encore en panne?
examples.trans: {F2}, is something wrong inside? Did the boiler break again?

meanings.note: une fuite dans la presse = a press leak
Prendre la fuite. Feminine noun ('la fuite', plural 'les fuites') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'leak'.

examples.text: Ce qu'il nous faut, c'est une fuite.
examples.trans: What we need is a leak.

examples.text: Il y a une fuite d'eau.
examples.trans: There is a water leak.

examples.text: Ce qu'il nous faut, c'est une fuite, pour que les fans commencent à protester.
examples.trans: What we need is a leak, so that the fans start to protest.

meanings.en: to leak out, be leaked (news, secrets)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to leak out'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'fuité').

examples.text: Sinon, ça va fuiter.
examples.trans: Otherwise, it will leak.

examples.text: Sinon, tout cela va fuiter.
examples.trans: Otherwise, all of this will leak.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to smoke'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'fumé').

examples.text: Non, je ne fume pas.
examples.trans: No, I don't smoke.

examples.text: Il fume une cigarette.
examples.trans: He's smoking a cigarette.

examples.text: D'abord, on ouvre la fenêtre pour fumer.
examples.trans: First, we open the window to smoke.

meanings.note: Smoke produced by something burning.

meanings.en: partir en fumée = to go up in smoke
meanings.note: In partir en fumée, an image of something disappearing or being lost.

examples.text: Tout part en fumée.
examples.trans: Everything goes up in smoke.

examples.text: Il y a de la fumée.
examples.trans: There's smoke.

examples.text: Les chagrins, les hommes, tout part en fumée.
examples.trans: Sorrows, men, it all goes up in smoke.

meanings.note: ressembler à des funérailles = to look like a funeral

examples.text: Des funérailles nationales.
examples.trans: A state funeral.

examples.text: Assister aux funérailles.
examples.trans: To attend the funeral.

examples.text: Ça risque de ressembler à des funérailles!
examples.trans: It is likely to look like a funeral!

meanings.note: furieux contre quelqu'un = furious with someone

examples.text: Elle va être furieuse contre moi.
examples.trans: She's going to be furious with me.

examples.text: Il est furieux.
examples.trans: He's furious.

examples.text: Elle est furieuse contre Mathias.
examples.trans: She's furious with Mathias.

meanings.note: Artist's willow or spindle-wood charcoal stick, or a charcoal drawing ('dessin au fusain').

examples.text: Ce portrait rapide a été dessiné au fusain.
examples.trans: This quick portrait was drawn in charcoal.

examples.text: Le fusain permet de tracer des ombres très douces.
examples.trans: Charcoal lets you draw very soft shadows.

meanings.note: Faire sauter un fusible (or faire sauter les plombs) means 'to blow a fuse'.

examples.text: Le vieux grille-pain a encore fait sauter un fusible.
examples.trans: The old toaster blew a fuse again.

examples.text: Henri garde toujours une boîte de fusibles neufs à l'atelier.
examples.trans: Henri always keeps a box of spare fuses in the workshop.

meanings.note: Un projet futur = a future project. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'future'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Parlons de ta future carrière.
examples.trans: Let's talk about your future career.

examples.text: Les générations futures.
examples.trans: Future generations.

examples.text: Ensuite, parlons de ta future carrière.
examples.trans: Next, let's talk about your future career.

examples.text: Vous n'êtes pas fâchée?
examples.trans: You're not angry?

examples.text: Il est fâché contre moi.
examples.trans: He is angry with me.

examples.text: Vous n'êtes pas fâchée? C'est juste une idée.
examples.trans: You're not angry? It's just an idea.

meanings.note: Usually plural: félicitations. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'congratulations, praise'.

examples.text: Toutes nos félicitations.
examples.trans: All our congratulations.

examples.text: Félicitations pour ton film.
examples.trans: Congratulations on your movie.

examples.text: Toutes mes félicitations!
examples.trans: All my congratulations!

meanings.note: Used in the plural as an exclamation: Félicitations! = Congratulations!

examples.text: Félicitations pour l'ouverture de votre café!
examples.trans: Congratulations on the opening of your café!

examples.text: Toute l'équipe mérite nos félicitations.
examples.trans: The whole team deserves our congratulations.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'congratulate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'félicité').

examples.text: Les œufs brouillés sont délicieux, {F1}. Fais mes compliments à {F2}!
examples.trans: The scrambled eggs are delicious, {F1}. Tell {F2} my compliments!

examples.text: Félicitez votre collègue.
examples.trans: Congratulate your colleague.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'feline'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une beauté féline.
examples.trans: A feline beauty.

examples.text: Une grâce féline.
examples.trans: A feline grace.

examples.text: Il écrit que ma beauté féline le hante.
examples.trans: He writes that my feline beauty haunts him.

meanings.note: le rôle principal féminin = the female lead

examples.text: Vous êtes toujours sûr pour le rôle principal féminin?
examples.trans: Are you still sure about the female lead?

examples.text: Un prénom féminin.
examples.trans: A female first name.

examples.text: En tout cas, solidarité féminine!
examples.trans: In any case, female solidarity!

meanings.note: incarner la féminité = to embody femininity

examples.text: Ma féminité est plutôt à plat.
examples.trans: My femininity is rather flat.

examples.text: Incarner la féminité.
examples.trans: To embody femininity.

examples.text: Ma féminité est plutôt à plat aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: My femininity is rather flat today.

meanings.note: A celebration or party; faire la fête means go out or have fun partying.

examples.text: Tu as fait la fête?
examples.trans: Were you out partying?

examples.text: C'est une belle fête.
examples.trans: It's a lovely party.

examples.text: On fait la fête ce soir!
examples.trans: We're partying tonight!

meanings.note: Avoir is the helper in completed past forms.

examples.text: On fête son anniversaire.
examples.trans: We are celebrating her birthday.

examples.text: J'ai fêté mes vingt ans.
examples.trans: I celebrated my twentieth birthday.

meanings.note: faire une gaffe = to make a blunder

examples.text: Faire une gaffe.
examples.trans: To make a blunder.

examples.text: Quelle gaffe!
examples.trans: What a blunder!

examples.text: Pardon, je crois que j'ai fait une grosse gaffe.
examples.trans: Sorry, I think that I made a big blunder.

meanings.note: Feminine: gagnante. Masculine noun ('le gagnant', plural 'les gagnants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'winner'.

examples.text: C'est un gagnant.
examples.trans: He is a winner.

examples.text: Tu es un battant, un gagnant!
examples.trans: You are a fighter, a winner!

examples.text: Les gagnants sont toujours en bout!
examples.trans: The winners are always on the end!

meanings.note: For receiving income or a wage.
For winning a game, competition or prize.

examples.text: Ce que gagne chaque personne.
examples.trans: What each person earns.

examples.text: On a gagné!
examples.trans: We won!

examples.text: Réglez votre réveil, Henri. Demain matin, on gagne contre l'eau froide!
examples.trans: Set your alarm, Henri. Tomorrow morning, we beat the cold water!

examples.text: Alors je porte une gaine.
examples.trans: So I'm wearing a girdle.

examples.text: Une gaine trop serrée.
examples.trans: A girdle that's too tight.

meanings.note: Rendez-vous galant = romantic date. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'romantic'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Un homme galant. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'romantic'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est pas un rendez-vous galant.
examples.trans: This is not a romantic date.

examples.text: Il est très galant.
examples.trans: He is very gallant.

meanings.en: to frolic, to gambol, to skip about

examples.text: Des animaux qui gambadent dans les bois.
examples.trans: Animals frolicking in the woods.

examples.text: Les enfants gambadent dans le jardin.
examples.trans: The children frolic in the garden.

meanings.note: Le laser game = laser tag. Masculine noun ('le game', plural 'les games') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'game'.
Une bonne game. Masculine noun ('le game', plural 'les games') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'game'.

examples.text: Elvis aime bien le laser game.
examples.trans: Elvis likes laser tag.

examples.text: On fait un laser game ce soir.
examples.trans: We are playing laser tag tonight.

examples.text: Deux sessions de laser game.
examples.trans: Two laser game sessions.

meanings.note: informal; feminine gamine = little girl

examples.text: C'est quoi le rôle, une gamine?
examples.trans: What's the part, a little girl?

examples.text: Les gamins jouent dehors.
examples.trans: The kids are playing outside.

meanings.note: Faire ses gammes = to practise scales.

examples.text: Le grand frère était vif et bruyant, toujours pressé de finir ses gammes.
examples.trans: The older brother was lively and loud, always in a hurry to finish his scales.

examples.text: Toujours là pour t'entendre jouer ta gamme de fa majeur lentement, Thibault!
examples.trans: Still here waiting to hear you play your F-major scale slowly, Thibault!

meanings.note: Silent final -t (cf. ganterie).

examples.text: Mets toujours les gants de four avant de sortir la plaque.
examples.trans: Always put on the oven mitts before taking out the tray.
