examples.text: J'ai laissé mes gants en laine dans ma poche.
examples.trans: I left my wool gloves in my pocket.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la garantie', plural 'les garanties') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'guarantee'.

examples.text: Aucune garantie financière.
examples.trans: No financial guarantee.

examples.text: Vous n'avez donc aucune garantie financière?
examples.trans: You therefore have no financial guarantee?

meanings.note: La garde des enfants.
Mettre en garde = to warn.
Prendre garde means to take care or beware.

examples.text: Prenez garde!
examples.trans: Beware!

examples.text: Tu m'as mise en garde.
examples.trans: You warned me.

meanings.note: Garder un enfant.
Garder un enfant.

examples.text: Garde la monnaie.
examples.trans: Keep the change.

examples.text: Vous gardez un tournevis partout sur vous, Henri!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere on you, Henri!

meanings.note: Un ange gardien = a guardian angel.
Un gardien de but = a goalkeeper.

examples.text: Tu es mon ange gardien.
examples.trans: You're my guardian angel.

examples.text: Le gardien ouvre la porte.
examples.trans: The caretaker opens the door.

meanings.note: Main railway station.

examples.text: Quelqu'un à la gare a pris ma valise bleue par erreur!
examples.trans: Someone at the train station took my blue suitcase by mistake!

examples.text: Claire, appelez tout de suite le bureau des objets trouvés de la gare.
examples.trans: Claire, call the station lost-and-found office right away.

examples.text: De la soupe chaude? Après cette marche froide sous la pluie, ça a l'air merveilleux.
examples.trans: Hot soup? After that cold walk in the rain, that sounds wonderful.

meanings.en: to park (garer une voiture / se garer)
meanings.note: Used transitively with the vehicle (garer une camionnette) or reflexively for the driver (se garer devant la porte).

examples.text: Le livreur vient de garer sa camionnette devant l'entrée.
examples.trans: The deliveryman has just parked his van in front of the entrance.

examples.text: On peut facilement se garer derrière la place le matin.
examples.trans: You can easily park behind the square in the morning.

meanings.note: colloquial; singular and plural have the same form

examples.text: Le gars du site de rencontres?
examples.trans: The guy from the dating site?

examples.text: C'est un bon gars.
examples.trans: He is a good guy.

examples.text: C'est un cauchemar, les gars.
examples.trans: It is a nightmare, guys.

examples.text: Je joue un garçon qui a le cœur brisé.
examples.trans: I play a boy with a broken heart.

examples.text: C'est un garçon très gentil.
examples.trans: He's a very nice young man.

examples.text: La vie écrit de meilleurs duos que nous, mes chers garçons.
examples.trans: Life writes better duets than we do, my dear boys.

meanings.note: à gauche = on the left, to the left
La main gauche = the left hand.

examples.text: Tu as regardé en haut à gauche!
examples.trans: You looked up and to the left!

examples.text: Tournez à gauche.
examples.trans: Turn left.

related.gloss: on the left, to the left

meanings.note: Eau gazeuse = sparkling water; feminine: gazeuse.

examples.text: Ne vous inquiétez pas! L'eau gazeuse froide enlève très bien le jus d'orange.
examples.trans: Do not worry! Cold sparkling water takes orange juice right out.

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment gazeux.
examples.trans: This place is really sparkling, carbonated.

meanings.note: ressembler à une geisha = to look like a geisha

examples.text: Maquillée comme une geisha.
examples.trans: Made up like a geisha.

examples.text: Le costume de geisha.
examples.trans: The geisha costume.

examples.text: J'ai dit fantôme, pas geisha!
examples.trans: I said ghost, not geisha!

meanings.en: to freeze, to be freezing cold
meanings.note: Il gèle = it is freezing.

examples.text: Il gèle à vélo.
examples.trans: It is freezing on a bicycle.

examples.text: L'eau gèle en hiver.
examples.trans: Water freezes in winter.

examples.text: Il gèle à vélo. Je pédale comme une folle!
examples.trans: It's freezing on a bike. I pedal like crazy!

meanings.note: j'ai les pieds gelés = my feet are freezing

examples.text: J'avais les pieds gelés.
examples.trans: My feet were freezing.

examples.text: C'est différent. C'était un festival dans les Alpes, j'avais les pieds gelés!
examples.trans: That's different. It was a festival in the Alps, my feet were freezing!

meanings.note: gelée royale = royal jelly, a health food made by bees
Weather.

examples.text: Prends de la gelée royale.
examples.trans: Take some royal jelly.

examples.text: Il y a de la gelée ce matin.
examples.trans: There's frost this morning.

meanings.note: Être du genre means be the type; du is de plus le.
A category of film, book or other work.

examples.text: C'est quel genre de film?
examples.trans: What kind of film is it?

examples.text: Le genre d'hôtel qui répare une lampe sous la pluie et garde le sac d'un inconnu.
examples.trans: The kind of hotel that fixes a lamp in the rain and guards a stranger's bag.

meanings.note: A plural-only noun. Most following adjectives are masculine plural; certain preceding adjectives can be feminine.

examples.text: Des gens comptent sur ce film.
examples.trans: People are counting on this film.

examples.text: Les gens sont gentils ici.
examples.trans: People are nice here.

examples.text: Parce que le bon café et le pain chaud rendent les gens sympas!
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!

meanings.note: c'est gentil = that's kind (of you)

examples.text: C'est gentil.
examples.trans: That's kind of you.

examples.text: Elle est très gentille.
examples.trans: She's very nice.

meanings.note: An English loan for a courteous, well-mannered man. The traditional plural is gentlemen; the regularised plural gentlemans also occurs.

examples.text: Quel gentleman!
examples.trans: What a gentleman!

examples.text: C'est un vrai gentleman.
examples.trans: He's a real gentleman.

examples.text: Quel bon ami. Quel gentleman!
examples.trans: What a good friend. What a gentleman!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to sprout'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'germé').

examples.text: Vois si elle germe.
examples.trans: See if it sprouts.

examples.text: Vois tranquillement si elle germe.
examples.trans: See calmly if it sprouts.

meanings.note: Un geste de rébellion.
Un geste de rébellion.

examples.text: C'est un geste de rébellion.
examples.trans: It's a gesture of rebellion.

examples.text: Elle fait un grand geste.
examples.trans: She makes a big gesture.

examples.text: Dans le film, c'est un geste de rébellion.
examples.trans: In the film, it's a gesture of rebellion.

meanings.note: Gestion d'image = image management.

examples.text: Un pôle gestion d'image.
examples.trans: An image-management department.

examples.text: Et un pôle gestion d'image pour les acteurs.
examples.trans: And an image-management department for the actors.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la gifle', plural 'les gifles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'slap'.

examples.text: Elle lui a donné une gifle.
examples.trans: She gave him a slap.

examples.text: Donne-moi une bonne gifle.
examples.trans: Give me a good slap.

examples.text: Une gifle ne règle rien du tout.
examples.trans: A slap settles nothing at all.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to slap'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'giflé').

examples.text: Ne me gifle pas!
examples.trans: Do not slap me!

examples.text: Gifle-moi maintenant, vas-y!
examples.trans: Slap me now, go ahead!

meanings.note: Un gilet de protection. Masculine noun ('le gilet', plural 'les gilets') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'vest'.

examples.text: Mets ton gilet.
examples.trans: Put on your vest.

examples.text: Et regardez, ce gilet doux en laine est propre et neuf. Essayez-le.
examples.trans: And look, this soft wool cardigan is clean and new. Try it on.

meanings.note: Manger une glace. Feminine noun ('la glace', plural 'les glaces') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ice cream'.
Une glace. Feminine noun ('la glace', plural 'les glaces') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ice cream'.

examples.text: J'adore la glace au chocolat.
examples.trans: I love chocolate ice cream.

examples.text: Son grand-père coupait du gâteau tiède au citron avec du sucre glace dessus!
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with icing sugar on top!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'ice-cold'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Le chien est glacé.
examples.trans: The dog is ice-cold.

examples.text: D'ici demain matin, l'eau de la douche sera glacée.
examples.trans: By tomorrow morning, the shower water will be ice-cold.

meanings.note: Sweet sugar glaze on a cake.

examples.text: Oh! Le glaçage jaune au citron! On se battait pour la part du coin chaque vendredi!
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze! We fought over the corner piece every Friday!

examples.text: Voici le glaçage sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the icing, glaze on the table.

meanings.note: From 'glisser' (to slip).

examples.text: Attention, c'est glissant!
examples.trans: Careful, it's slippery!

examples.text: Le sol est glissant.
examples.trans: The floor is slippery.

examples.text: Attention, ça glisse!
examples.trans: Careful, it's slippery!

examples.text: Le pied glisse vers la tombe.
examples.trans: The foot slips towards the grave.

examples.text: J'ai senti un pied glisser vers la tombe.
examples.trans: I felt one foot slip towards the grave.

meanings.en: hinge pin, pintle (for doors and shutters)
meanings.note: Final *-d* is silent (`/ɡɔ̃/`). Traditional French shutters lift onto vertical iron *gonds* set into the stone wall (hence the idiom *sortir de ses gonds*, 'to fly off the handle').

examples.text: Versez deux gouttes d'huile sur chaque gond avant d'ouvrir.
examples.trans: Pour two drops of oil onto each hinge pin before opening.

examples.text: Nous avons reposé les quatre volets verts sur leurs gonds.
examples.trans: We hung the four green shutters back onto their hinge pins.

meanings.note: From gonfler (to blow up, inflate).

examples.text: Un canard gonflable.
examples.trans: An inflatable duck.

examples.text: Un matelas gonflable.
examples.trans: An air mattress.

examples.text: J'étais dans la piscine, avec mon canard gonflable.
examples.trans: I was in the swimming pool, with my inflatable duck.

meanings.en: swollen (wood from dampness, or a sprained ankle); puffed up
meanings.note: Past participle of *gonfler* used as an adjective (*du bois gonflé par l'eau*, *une cheville gonflée*).

examples.text: La vieille porte en bois est un peu gonflée après la pluie.
examples.trans: The old wooden door is slightly swollen after the rain.

examples.text: Mettez du froid tout de suite sur une cheville gonflée.
examples.trans: Put cold right away on a swollen ankle.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la gorge', plural 'les gorges') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'throat'.

examples.text: L'eau froide fait mal à la gorge.
examples.trans: Cold water hurts the throat.

examples.text: L'eau froide est mauvaise pour ta gorge?
examples.trans: Is cold water bad for your throat?

meanings.note: Built from gorge ('throat').

examples.text: Tenez, buvez une gorgée d'eau fraîche, Monsieur Antoine. Qu'est-ce qu'il y a sur cette feuille?
examples.trans: Here, drink a sip of cool water, Mr Antoine. What is on that sheet of paper?

examples.text: Voici la gorgée sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the sip, swallow on the table.

meanings.en: un beau gosse = a handsome guy, a hunk (colloquial)

examples.text: Tu es un beau gosse!
examples.trans: You are a handsome guy!

examples.text: C'est un beau gosse.
examples.trans: He's a good-looking guy.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la gourmandise', plural 'les gourmandises') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'delicacy'.
Feminine noun ('la gourmandise', plural 'les gourmandises') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'love of good food'.

examples.text: Les macarons sont une douce gourmandise.
examples.trans: Macarons are a sweet treat.

examples.text: C'est ma gourmandise préférée à Paris.
examples.trans: It is my favorite treat in Paris.

meanings.note: une goutte d'eau, une goutte de lait

examples.text: Avec une goutte de lait.
examples.trans: With a drop of milk.

examples.text: Pas une goutte!
examples.trans: Not a drop!

meanings.note: Circumflex marks Old French s (compare English 'gusto'); final -t is silent.

examples.text: Ce gâteau au citron a exactement le goût des dimanches d'autrefois.
examples.trans: This lemon cake tastes just like Sundays from years ago.

examples.text: Chacun ses goûts, mais moi je préfère le café bien serré.
examples.trans: To each their own taste, though I prefer my coffee nice and strong.

meanings.en: to taste, try a bite or spoonful of
meanings.note: Direct object (goûter ce miel = 'taste this honey') or goûter à quelque chose. As a masculine noun, le goûter is the afternoon snack around 4 p.m.

examples.text: Goûtez une petite cuillère de ce miel doré!
examples.trans: Taste a little spoonful of this golden honey!

examples.text: Thibault goûte toujours la pâte avant d'enfourner.
examples.trans: Thibault always tastes the batter before putting it in the oven.

meanings.note: Agent noun from *goûter* ('to taste'); feminine is *une goûteuse*.

examples.text: Les deux frères sont nos goûteurs officiels pour les tartes.
examples.trans: The two brothers are our official taste testers for the tarts.

examples.text: Un bon goûteur reconnaît tout de suite le miel de montagne.
examples.trans: A good taster recognizes mountain honey right away.

meanings.note: Manger des graines = to eat seeds.

examples.text: Elles mangent des graines.
examples.trans: They eat seeds.

examples.text: Je plante des graines dans le jardin.
examples.trans: I'm planting seeds in the garden.

meanings.note: Metric unit of weight used in French kitchens and post offices.

examples.text: Il faut peser cent vingt grammes de beurre doux.
examples.trans: You need to weigh out one hundred twenty grams of unsalted butter.

examples.text: En pâtisserie, tout se joue à quelques grammes près.
examples.trans: In baking, everything comes down to a few grams.

meanings.note: before the noun: une grande actrice = a great actress
Une grande star.

examples.text: C'est une grande star.
examples.trans: She's a big star.

examples.text: Paris est une grande ville.
examples.trans: Paris is a big city.

meanings.note: Used in negative expressions: pas grand-chose means not much.

examples.text: Vous ne perdez pas grand-chose.
examples.trans: You're not missing much.

examples.text: Il n'y a pas grand-chose.
examples.trans: There's not much.

meanings.note: Both *grands-mères* and *grand-mères* are accepted plurals in modern French.

examples.text: Ma grand-mère faisait cuire une grande brioche chaque dimanche.
examples.trans: My grandmother used to bake a big brioche every Sunday.

examples.text: Ce livre de recettes vient de la cuisine de sa grand-mère.
examples.trans: This recipe book comes from her grandmother's kitchen.

meanings.note: Plural: les grands-pères.

examples.text: Il y a trois ans, après le décès de notre grand-père, Thibault et moi nous sommes disputés au sujet de la vieille maison.
examples.trans: Three years ago, after our grandfather passed away, Thibault and I argued over the old house.

examples.text: En fait, j'ai seulement écrit: Quelque chose de Grand-Père t'attend à l'Hôtel du Tilleul vendredi à midi.
examples.trans: Actually, I only wrote: Something from Grandfather is waiting for you at Hotel du Tilleul Friday at noon.

examples.text: Son grand-père coupait du gâteau tiède au citron avec du sucre glace dessus!
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with icing sugar on top!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'grandiose'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une fête grandiose.
examples.trans: A grandiose party.

examples.text: Un spectacle grandiose.
examples.trans: A spectacular show.

examples.text: Je veux une fête grandiose, les amis!
examples.trans: I want a grandiose party, friends!

grandir.gloss: to grow up; to grow taller

meanings.en: to grow up (of a person); to grow taller/bigger
meanings.note: Regular -ir verb (-iss- in plural forms) conjugated with avoir in the passé composé: j'ai grandi ici ('I grew up here').

examples.text: Thibault et Antoine ont grandi à deux pas du marché.
examples.trans: Thibault and Antoine grew up a stone's throw from the market.

examples.text: Le tilleul de la cour a beaucoup grandi en trente ans.
examples.trans: The linden tree in the courtyard has grown a great deal in thirty years.

meanings.note: Dans la grange = in the barn.

examples.text: Il nous reste une demi-journée dans la grange.
examples.trans: We have half a day left in the barn.

examples.text: Les chevaux sont dans la grange.
examples.trans: The horses are in the barn.

meanings.en: to itch (*ça me gratte*); to scratch, scrape
meanings.note: Notice the reversal from English: *le nez me gratte* literally says 'my nose scratches me', meaning 'my nose itches'.

examples.text: J'ai les mains pleines de farine et le bout du nez me gratte!
examples.trans: My hands are covered in flour and the tip of my nose itches!

examples.text: Grattez doucement la vieille peinture sèche avec une lame.
examples.trans: Gently scrape off the old dry paint with a blade.

meanings.note: Costing nothing, complimentary.

examples.text: L'entrée du square municipal est gratuite toute l'année.
examples.trans: Admission to the municipal park square is free all year round.

examples.text: Le petit concert du dimanche après-midi est gratuit.
examples.trans: The Sunday afternoon concert is free of charge.

related.gloss: to give (as a present), to offer

meanings.note: Formed from the feminine adjective gratuite + -ment.

examples.text: Les deux frères ont poncé toutes les tables gratuitement.
examples.trans: The two brothers sanded all the tables for free.

examples.text: Le musée de la ville se visite gratuitement le premier dimanche.
examples.trans: The town museum can be visited for free on the first Sunday.

meanings.en: deep, low-pitched, resonant (of a voice, note, or instrument)
meanings.note: In music, grave means 'low-pitched / bass' (the opposite is aigu, 'high-pitched').

meanings.en: serious, grave (ce n'est pas grave = it's no big deal)
meanings.note: Everyday reassurance: Ce n'est pas grave! ('Don't worry, it's nothing serious!').

examples.text: Ce vieux piano droit a un son très chaud et un peu grave.
examples.trans: This old upright piano has a very warm, slightly deep tone.

examples.text: Une tasse ébréchée, ce n'est vraiment pas grave.
examples.trans: One chipped cup is really no big deal.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Attendez une minute... Numéro douze, {STREET}, et deux initiales d'enfance écrites dans le coin!
examples.trans: Wait a moment... Number twelve, {STREET}, and two childhood initials written in the corner!

examples.text: C'est facile à graver ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to engrave, carve together.

meanings.note: Top room under the roof beams.

examples.text: Voici la petite clé en argent pour la porte du grenier au troisième étage.
examples.trans: Here is the small silver key for the third-floor attic door.

examples.text: Donnez-nous quinze minutes et ce grenier sera mieux que la chambre sept!
examples.trans: Give us fifteen minutes and this attic will beat room seven!

examples.text: C'est pour ça que vous écoutiez la rue depuis le grenier hier soir!
examples.trans: That is why you were listening to the street from the attic last night!

meanings.note: Used for both wrought-iron gates and oven racks.

examples.text: Il refroidit sur la grille en ce moment: croûte dorée et bon parfum de citron!
examples.trans: It is cooling on the rack right now: golden crust and lovely lemon scent!

examples.text: Un taxi vient de s'arrêter juste devant la grille en fer!
examples.trans: A taxi just stopped right outside the iron gate!

meanings.note: griller un acteur = to burn out an actor

examples.text: J'ai peur qu'on finisse par le griller.
examples.trans: I am afraid we will burn him out.

examples.text: Faire griller du pain.
examples.trans: To toast bread.

meanings.note: Toasted golden in an oven or pan ('amandes grillées', 'pain grillé').

examples.text: Des amandes effilées grillées parfument tout le coin café.
examples.trans: Toasted flaked almonds scent the whole café corner.

examples.text: Elle sert le thé du matin avec deux tranches de pain grillé.
examples.trans: She serves morning tea with two slices of toast.

meanings.en: to climb, clamber over (grimper sur / grimper à)
meanings.note: Vivid everyday verb for climbing up a ladder, tree, hill, or pile of obstacles.

examples.text: Personne ne veut grimper sur des chaises pour sortir!
examples.trans: Nobody wants to clamber over chairs just to get outside!

examples.text: La vigne vierge grimpe le long du mur en brique.
examples.trans: The Virginia creeper climbs up the brick wall.

meanings.en: creak, squeak (of a hinge, pedal, or floorboard)
meanings.note: From grincer ('to creak, squeak').

examples.text: Après une goutte d'huile, on n'entend plus aucun grincement.
examples.trans: After a drop of oil, you cannot hear a single squeak anymore.

examples.text: Le vieux portail s'ouvre enfin sans grincement.
examples.trans: The old gate finally opens without a creak.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la grippe', plural 'les grippes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'flu'.

examples.text: Elle a attrapé une mauvaise grippe.
examples.trans: She caught a bad flu.

examples.text: Une simple grippe paralyse le tournage.
examples.trans: A simple flu paralyzes the shoot.

examples.text: Pourquoi devraient-elles s'inquiéter de cette grippe?
examples.trans: Why should they worry about this flu?

meanings.note: Feminine: grise (/ɡʁiz/).

examples.text: Deux paires de grandes chaussures marron pour homme et des pulls gris.
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes and grey sweaters.

examples.text: Franchement, je préfère être ici que dans mon vieux bureau gris.
examples.trans: Honestly, I like being here much better than in my old grey office.

examples.text: Mes mains tremblent... il y a un homme grand avec un manteau gris foncé?
examples.trans: My hands are shaking... is there a tall man in a dark grey coat?

meanings.note: Before the noun: un gros contrat.
About people: not polite.

examples.text: C'est un gros problème.
examples.trans: It's a big problem.

examples.text: Un gros contrat.
examples.trans: A big contract.

meanings.note: une première grossesse = a first pregnancy

examples.text: Ce n'est pas la grossesse.
examples.trans: It is not the pregnancy.

examples.text: Annoncer une grossesse.
examples.trans: To announce a pregnancy.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas plutôt la grossesse?
examples.trans: Is it not rather the pregnancy?

meanings.note: grossir pendant la grossesse = to gain weight during pregnancy

examples.text: Est-ce que j'ai beaucoup grossi?
examples.trans: Have I gained a lot of weight?

examples.text: La rivière a grossi.
examples.trans: The river has swollen.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la grotte', plural 'les grottes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cavern'.

examples.text: Tu vis dans une grotte?
examples.trans: Do you live in a cave?

examples.text: Tu vis dans une grotte, Mathias?
examples.trans: Do you live in a cave, Mathias?

meanings.note: Un groupe d'agences.

examples.text: Il veut créer un groupe d'agences européennes.
examples.trans: He wants to create a group of European agencies.

examples.text: Un groupe d'amis.
examples.trans: A group of friends.

examples.text: Oui. Il veut créer un groupe d'agences européennes.
examples.trans: Yes. He wants to create a group of European agencies.

meanings.note: Avoir de la grâce = to have grace.

examples.text: Vous avez de la grâce.
examples.trans: You have grace.

examples.text: Grâce à toi.
examples.trans: Thanks to you.

examples.text: Les chambres resteront chaudes jusqu'au matin, Claire, grâce aux murs en brique.
examples.trans: The rooms will stay warm until morning, Claire, thanks to the brick walls.

meanings.note: Invariable in the plural; final -s is silent (/ɡʁɛ/). Stoneware cups and jugs (en grès) are prized in French cafés because they hold heat well.

examples.text: Les tasses en grès gardent le café bien chaud.
examples.trans: Stoneware cups keep the coffee nice and hot.

examples.text: La potière vend des bols en grès émaillé au marché.
examples.trans: The potter sells glazed stoneware bowls at the market.

meanings.note: la Guerre de Cent Ans = the Hundred Years' War

examples.text: Il prépare un film sur la Guerre de Cent Ans.
examples.trans: He is preparing a movie about the Hundred Years' War.

examples.text: C'est un film de guerre.
examples.trans: It is a war movie.

examples.text: C'est la guerre entre ASK et StarMedia.
examples.trans: It is war between ASK and StarMedia.

meanings.note: faire le guet = to keep watch / keep a lookout Normally uncountable in this sense.

examples.text: Fais le guet devant la porte!
examples.trans: Keep watch in front of the door!

examples.text: Il est aux aguets.
examples.trans: He is on the lookout.

examples.text: Donc il récompensera ma loyauté. Fais le guet, d'accord?
examples.trans: So he will reward my loyalty. Keep watch, okay?

related.gloss: to keep watch / keep a lookout

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le guide', plural 'les guides') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'guidebook'.

examples.text: As-tu trouvé un guide intéressant?
examples.trans: Did you find an interesting guide?

examples.text: Sauf s'il écrit pour le Guide annuel de Lyon!
examples.trans: Unless he writes for the annual Lyon Guide!

examples.text: Le Guide de Lyon? Attendez: vous pensez que je suis inspecteur d'hôtels?
examples.trans: The Lyon Guide? Wait: do you think I am a hotel inspector?

guérir.gloss: to heal, to recover, to cure

meanings.en: to heal, to get well, to recover
meanings.note: To recover or heal; here recovering emotionally after the relationship.
Transitive.

examples.text: Je dois faire ça pour guérir.
examples.trans: I have to do this in order to heal.

examples.text: Il va vite guérir.
examples.trans: He'll recover quickly.

examples.text: C'est une blessure qui ne guérira jamais.
examples.trans: It is a wound that will never heal.

examples.text: Attention, il y a une guêpe sur la confiture!
examples.trans: Careful, there's a wasp on the jam!

examples.text: La guêpe est entrée par la fenêtre ouverte.
examples.trans: The wasp came in through the open window.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la gymnastique', plural 'les gymnastiques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'gymnastics'.

examples.text: Elle fait sa gymnastique du matin.
examples.trans: She does her morning gymnastics.

examples.text: Parfait, je vais commencer ma gymnastique.
examples.trans: Perfect, I will start my exercises.

meanings.note: Gâcher tout = to ruin everything. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to ruin'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'gâché').
Gâcher du temps. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to ruin'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'gâché').

examples.text: Tu gâches tout!
examples.trans: You ruin everything!

examples.text: Ne gâche pas la soirée.
examples.trans: Don't spoil the evening.

examples.text: Je suis très heureuse ici, je ne veux pas gâcher ça.
examples.trans: I am very happy here, I do not want to ruin that.

meanings.note: For wasted time, effort, talent or an opportunity.
Can also describe a botched or messy result.

examples.text: Quel gâchis!
examples.trans: What a waste!

examples.text: C'est un gâchis de talent.
examples.trans: It's a waste of talent.

examples.text: Quel gâchis.
examples.trans: What a waste.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le gâteau', plural 'les gâteaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cake'.

examples.text: Un gâteau avec des bonbons.
examples.trans: A cake with candy.

examples.text: Un gâteau au chocolat.
examples.trans: A chocolate cake.

examples.text: Onze heures vingt. Le gâteau est prêt, Nadia?
examples.trans: Eleven twenty. Is the cake ready, Nadia?

meanings.note: Un canard géant = a giant duck. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'giant'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un canard géant, quelle idée!
examples.trans: A giant duck, what an idea!

examples.text: Une statue géante.
examples.trans: A giant statue.

examples.text: Le mec est un génie? Un canard géant, de la mauvaise musique... Ouais, un vrai génie!
examples.trans: The guy is a genius? A giant duck, bad music... Yeah, a real genius!

meanings.note: Informal praise.

examples.text: C'est une idée géniale.
examples.trans: It's a brilliant idea.

examples.text: Attendez: le beurre salé est mauvais pour la confiture, mais génial pour les œufs brouillés!
examples.trans: Wait: salted butter is bad for jam, but amazing for scrambled eggs!

meanings.note: Un coup de génie = a stroke of genius.

examples.text: Garder ces chaises pliantes était un vrai coup de génie!
examples.trans: Keeping those folding chairs was a real stroke of genius!

examples.text: Il ne faut pas être un génie pour aimer cette tarte.
examples.trans: You don't have to be a genius to love this tart.

meanings.note: direction générale = executive management

examples.text: Elle prend la direction générale de l'agence.
examples.trans: She takes the general management of the agency.

examples.text: Une vue générale de la situation.
examples.trans: A general view of the situation.

examples.text: Pour la direction générale de StarMédia?
examples.trans: For the general directorship of StarMedia?

meanings.en: generally, as a general rule, usually
meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Les assurances remboursent généralement.
examples.trans: Insurances generally reimburse.

examples.text: Il arrive généralement à l'heure.
examples.trans: He generally arrives on time.

examples.text: Les assurances remboursent généralement ces frais imprévus.
examples.trans: Insurances generally reimburse these unforeseen costs.

meanings.note: Feminine in -euse.

examples.text: C'est une offre très généreuse.
examples.trans: It's a very generous offer.

examples.text: Il est très généreux.
examples.trans: He's very generous.

examples.text: Très généreux! Vous avez entendu la cloche du portail en bas?
examples.trans: Very generous! Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la générosité', plural 'les générosités') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'generosity'.

examples.text: Un geste d'une générosité immense.
examples.trans: A gesture of immense generosity.

examples.text: C'est un geste d'une générosité immense.
examples.trans: It is a gesture of immense generosity.

meanings.note: For managing a business or handling a situation; je gère can mean I have it under control.

examples.text: C'est moi qui gère!
examples.trans: I'm handling it!

examples.text: Il gère l'agence.
examples.trans: He runs the agency.

examples.text: Non, Mathias, c'est moi qui gère!
examples.trans: No, Mathias, I'm handling it!

examples.text: Ça va être gênant.
examples.trans: It's going to be embarrassing.

examples.text: C'est une situation très gênante.
examples.trans: It's a very awkward situation.

meanings.note: Stronger faux-ami trap: gêné means 'embarrassed/uncomfortable', not 'annoyed'.

examples.text: J'étais trop gêné pour redemander ma valise tout de suite.
examples.trans: I felt too embarrassed to ask for my suitcase back right away.

examples.text: Ne soyez pas gênée, entrez prendre une tasse de thé chaud.
examples.trans: Don't feel awkward, come in and have a cup of hot tea.

meanings.en: ha!, aha! (exclamation of triumph, surprise, or laughter)
meanings.note: Spelled with *h* aspiré (`h` is silent `/a/`, but blocks liaison before it).

examples.text: Ha! Je savais bien que cette clé ouvrait le tiroir!
examples.trans: Ha! I knew that key opened the drawer!

examples.text: Ha, pas une seule goutte d'eau sur ma veste propre!
examples.trans: Ha, not a single drop of water on my clean jacket!

meanings.en: s'habiller = to get dressed, to dress oneself
meanings.note: Tu t'habilles comme ça?.

examples.text: Tu t'habilles comme ça pour un dîner?
examples.trans: You dress like that for a dinner?

examples.text: Il s'habille bien.
examples.trans: He dresses well.

examples.text: Tu t'habilles comme ça pour un dîner de travail?
examples.trans: You dress like that for a work dinner?

meanings.en: to live, to reside, to inhabit
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to reside'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'habité').

examples.text: Laura Smet n'habite pas ici.
examples.trans: Laura Smet does not live here.

examples.text: Ah oui? Votre famille habitait près d'ici autrefois?
examples.trans: Oh yes? Did your family live near here once?

meanings.note: avoir l'habitude de = to be used to; comme d'habitude = as usual

examples.text: C'est juste une habitude.
examples.trans: It's just a habit.

examples.text: Comme d'habitude.
examples.trans: As usual.

examples.text: La même que d'habitude.
examples.trans: The same as usual.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas habituel.
examples.trans: It is not customary.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas habituel pour des essais.
examples.trans: That is not typical for an audition.

habituer.gloss: to accustom; to get used to (s'habituer)

meanings.en: to accustom; s'habituer à = to get used to, grow fond of
meanings.note: Reflexive s'habituer à quelque chose takes être in the passé composé: je me suis habitué(e) à...

examples.text: Je me suis vite habituée au calme de cette cour.
examples.trans: I quickly got used to the quiet of this courtyard.

examples.text: On s'habitue très facilement au pain frais du matin.
examples.trans: You get used to fresh morning bread very easily.

meanings.note: Feminine form: une habituée.

examples.text: Les habitués du quartier arrivent dès l'ouverture.
examples.trans: The neighborhood regulars arrive right at opening time.

examples.text: La boulangère connaît le prénom de chaque habitué.
examples.trans: The baker knows every regular's first name.

related.gloss: to accustom; to get used to (s'habituer)

meanings.note: éprouver de la haine = to feel hatred

examples.text: Il te transfère sa haine.
examples.trans: He transfers his hatred to you.

examples.text: Une haine profonde.
examples.trans: A deep hatred.

examples.text: Il te transfère sa haine pour Mathias.
examples.trans: He transfers his hatred for Mathias to you.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la haleine', plural 'les haleines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'breath'.

examples.text: Un tunnel de mauvaise haleine.
examples.trans: A tunnel of bad breath.

examples.text: Retenir son haleine.
examples.trans: To hold one's breath.

examples.text: Il a une mauvaise haleine terrible!
examples.trans: He has terrible bad breath!

meanings.note: Un sérieux handicap. Masculine noun ('le handicap', plural 'les handicaps') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'disadvantage'.

examples.text: Est-il un atout ou un véritable handicap?
examples.trans: Is he an asset or a real handicap?

examples.text: Ne pas parler anglais est un handicap.
examples.trans: Not speaking English is a handicap.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'disabled'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Les animaux handicapés ont besoin d'aide.
examples.trans: Disabled animals need help.

examples.text: À tous les animaux handicapés!
examples.trans: To all the handicapped animals!

meanings.note: Aspirate h: un hangar.

examples.text: Ce sera dans un hangar en banlieue.
examples.trans: It will be in a warehouse in the suburbs.

examples.text: Un grand hangar.
examples.trans: A large warehouse.

examples.text: Sauf que ce sera dans un hangar en banlieue.
examples.trans: Except it will be in a warehouse in the suburbs.

meanings.en: to haunt, to obsess, to plague
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to haunt'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'hanté').

examples.text: Cette idée me hante.
examples.trans: This idea haunts me.

examples.text: Un château hanté.
examples.trans: A haunted castle.

examples.text: Il écrit que ma beauté féline le hante.
examples.trans: He writes that my feline beauty haunts him.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le haricot', plural 'les haricots') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bean'.

examples.text: Des haricots verts.
examples.trans: Green beans.

examples.text: Un haricot blanc.
examples.trans: A white bean.

examples.text: Tu ressembles à un petit haricot sec.
examples.trans: You look like a little dried bean.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le hasard', plural 'les hasards') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'chance'.

examples.text: Nous nous sommes rencontrés dans la rue par hasard.
examples.trans: We met in the street by chance.

examples.text: Dans ce métier, il ne faut rien laisser au hasard.
examples.trans: In this profession, you must leave nothing to chance.

meanings.en: to raise, lift (hausser la voix = raise one's voice)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'raise'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'haussé').

examples.text: Ne haussez pas la voix.
examples.trans: Don't raise your voice.

examples.text: Ne haussez pas la voix!
examples.trans: Do not raise your voice!

meanings.note: Aspirate h: no liaison (les hauts).
Haut placé = high-ranking, high up.

examples.text: Une haute montagne.
examples.trans: A high mountain.

examples.text: Le papier doré sur l'étagère du haut. Pourquoi?
examples.trans: The gold wrapper on the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Vertical height or elevation (aspirate h: 'la hauteur', 'à hauteur des yeux' = at eye level).

examples.text: Le tableau est accroché exactement à hauteur des yeux.
examples.trans: The painting is hung right at eye level.

examples.text: Depuis les hauteurs de la ville, on aperçoit la rivière.
examples.trans: From the heights of the town, you can see the river.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'weekly'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Notre point hebdomadaire.
examples.trans: Our weekly check-in.

examples.text: Je viens pour notre point tutelle hebdomadaire.
examples.trans: I come for our weekly check-in.

meanings.en: huh?, right? (asking for agreement at the end of a sentence)
meanings.note: Informal.
Informal.

examples.text: Exclusif, hein?
examples.trans: Exclusive, huh?

examples.text: C'est bon, hein?
examples.trans: It's good, right?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la herbe', plural 'les herbes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'grass'.

examples.text: Bien. Mets ces herbes vertes fraîches dessus avant de servir.
examples.trans: Good. Put these fresh green herbs on top before serving.

examples.text: C'est vous qui cultivez ces herbes, Henri?
examples.trans: Do you grow these herbs yourself, Henri?

examples.text: Sentez-moi ça! Du pain chaud, des œufs chauds et des herbes fraîches.
examples.trans: Smell that! Warm bread, hot eggs, and fresh herbs.

meanings.note: Dans une heure = in an hour.
À quatorze heures = at two pm.

examples.text: À onze heures.
examples.trans: At eleven o'clock.

examples.text: Quelle heure est-il? Neuf heures trente-cinq!
examples.trans: What time is it? Nine thirty-five!

examples.text: Heureusement, tout va bien.
examples.trans: Fortunately, everything is fine.

examples.text: Mon Dieu! Pas une goutte sur la table, heureusement... tout est sur ma cravate!
examples.trans: Oh dear! Not a drop on the table, thankfully... all of it is on my tie!

meanings.note: Feminine: heureuse.

examples.text: Heureux pour toujours.
examples.trans: Happy Ever After.

examples.text: Je suis très heureux pour vous.
examples.trans: I'm very happy for you.

examples.text: Voici Marie-Sophie Garnier, chef scénariste sur Heureux pour toujours.
examples.trans: This is Marie-Sophie Garnier, head screenwriter on Happy Ever After.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to bump into
meanings.note: Aspirate h: no liaison or elision.

meanings.en: se heurter = to collide, to clash
meanings.note: Reflexive.

examples.text: Mon inconscient et celui de Julie Gayet se heurtent de partout.
examples.trans: My subconscious and Julie Gayet's clash everywhere.

examples.text: Ils se heurtent toujours.
examples.trans: They always clash.

meanings.note: Yesterday; hier soir means last night, not yesterday evening in ordinary English.

examples.text: Hier, j'ai vu Line.
examples.trans: Yesterday I saw Line.

examples.text: On a fait quoi hier soir?
examples.trans: What did we do last night?

examples.text: Regardez ce qui est arrivé au portail hier soir.
examples.trans: Look what arrived at the gate last night.

meanings.note: Danser le hip-hop.

examples.text: Elle danse le hip-hop dans le film.
examples.trans: She dances hip-hop in the film.

examples.text: J'écoute du hip-hop.
examples.trans: I listen to hip-hop.

examples.text: Une fille magnifique, pleine d'énergie... Et qui danse le hip-hop!
examples.trans: A gorgeous girl, full of energy... And who dances hip-hop!

meanings.note: A story or account; histoire de introduces what it is about.
Also history as a field or past events.

examples.text: C'est l'histoire d'un vieux couple.
examples.trans: It's the story of an old couple.

examples.text: Quelle histoire!
examples.trans: What a story!

examples.text: Nerveux pour un petit train en bois? Cette histoire devient bizarre.
examples.trans: Nervous about a little wooden train? This story is getting strange.

meanings.note: un drame historique = a historical drama

examples.text: Un film historique.
examples.trans: A historical movie.

examples.text: Un monument historique.
examples.trans: A historic monument.

examples.text: Un architecte qui travaille sur les vieilles cours historiques dans tout Lyon!
examples.trans: An architect who works on historic old courtyards all over Lyon!

meanings.note: En hiver = in winter.

examples.text: C'est l'hiver.
examples.trans: It's winter.

examples.text: En hiver, il fait froid.
examples.trans: In winter it's cold.

meanings.note: Used almost exclusively in the expression hocher la tête ('to nod one's head' in agreement or thought).
Begins with an aspirated h (le hochement, je hoche without elision).

examples.text: Puis il a hoché la tête deux fois vers Étienne et a écrit deux mots sur sa serviette: Même goût!
examples.trans: Then he nodded twice to Etienne and wrote two words on his napkin: Exact taste!

examples.text: Henri hoche la tête en écoutant le plan d'Antoine.
examples.trans: Henri nods his head while listening to Antoine's plan.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le homicide', plural 'les homicides') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'homicide'.

examples.text: On ne prépare pas un homicide!
examples.trans: We are not planning a homicide!

examples.text: Un homicide involontaire.
examples.trans: An involuntary manslaughter.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le hommage', plural 'les hommages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tribute'.

examples.text: Je veux rendre hommage aux agents.
examples.trans: I want to pay tribute to agents.

examples.text: Un bel hommage à Arlette.
examples.trans: A fine tribute to Arlette.

examples.text: Je veux surtout rendre hommage aux agents.
examples.trans: I especially want to pay tribute to agents.

meanings.note: The h is silent: l'homme.
In general statements.

examples.text: C'est un homme.
examples.trans: It's a man.

examples.text: Le rôle est pour un homme.
examples.trans: The part is for a man.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le homonyme', plural 'les homonymes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'namesake'.
Masculine noun ('le homonyme', plural 'les homonymes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'homonym'.

examples.text: Elle a trouvé une homonyme.
examples.trans: She found a namesake.

examples.text: Tu veux trouver une simple homonyme?
examples.trans: You want to find a simple namesake?

examples.text: L'homonyme peut jouer le personnage mort.
examples.trans: The namesake can play the dead character.

meanings.note: Moral integrity, privilege, or tribute ('parole d'honneur' = word of honor).

examples.text: Parole d'honneur, votre secret est bien gardé ici.
examples.trans: Word of honor, your secret is safe here.

examples.text: C'est un grand honneur de vous accueillir ce soir.
examples.trans: It is a great honor to welcome you this evening.

meanings.note: Sois honnête = be fair / be honest. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'honest'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Sois honnête, je dis la vérité!
examples.trans: Be fair, I'm telling the truth!

examples.text: C'est un homme honnête.
examples.trans: He is an honest man.

examples.text: Merci à vous deux d'avoir été honnêtes au lieu de me renvoyer sous la pluie.
examples.trans: Thank you both for being honest instead of sending me back into the rain.

meanings.note: Truthfully, frankly; in an upright, fair manner.

examples.text: Honnêtement, je ne m'attendais pas à une telle surprise.
examples.trans: Honestly, I wasn't expecting such a surprise.

examples.text: Ils ont partagé les parts de gâteau très honnêtement.
examples.trans: They shared the slices of cake very fairly.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la honnêteté', plural 'les honnêtetés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'honesty'.

examples.text: Votre honnêteté est admirable.
examples.trans: Your honesty is admirable.

examples.text: Votre honnêteté est tout à fait admirable.
examples.trans: Your honesty is entirely admirable.

meanings.note: Avoir honte de = to be ashamed of.

examples.text: Tu as honte de moi?
examples.trans: Are you ashamed of me?

examples.text: J'ai honte.
examples.trans: I'm ashamed.

meanings.en: up!, there we go!; also part of Lindy Hop / hip-hop

examples.text: Allez, hop, au travail !
examples.trans: Come on, up we go, back to work!

examples.text: Ils dansent le Lindy Hop.
examples.trans: They are dancing the Lindy Hop.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le hoquet', plural 'les hoquets') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hiccup'.

examples.text: J'ai un terrible hoquet qui commence.
examples.trans: I have terrible hiccups beginning.

examples.text: C'est seulement un petit hoquet.
examples.trans: It is only a little hiccup.

examples.text: Le hoquet est enfin parti.
examples.trans: The hiccup is finally gone.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le horaire', plural 'les horaires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'schedule'.

examples.text: C'est un chevauchement d'horaires.
examples.trans: It is a schedule overlap.

examples.text: Dix-neuf raisons?! Vous accueillez votre frère ou vous lisez un horaire de train?
examples.trans: Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a train timetable?

meanings.note: élargir ses horizons = to broaden one's horizons

examples.text: Je voulais élargir tes horizons.
examples.trans: I wanted to broaden your horizons.

examples.text: Je voulais juste élargir tes horizons.
examples.trans: I just wanted to broaden your horizons.

meanings.note: Mute h: l'horloge (/lɔʁlɔʒ/).

examples.text: Ouvrez-la après midi, patron! Regardez l'horloge: il est midi moins cinq!
examples.trans: Open it after noon, boss! Look at the clock: it is five to twelve!

examples.text: Voici l'horloge sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the wall clock on the table.

meanings.note: Proverbial in French for patient, steady-handed precision (*un travail d'horloger*, *des mains d'horloger*).

examples.text: Réparer ce petit mécanisme demande la patience d'un horloger.
examples.trans: Repairing this tiny mechanism takes a watchmaker's patience.

examples.text: L'horloger du quartier a réglé la pendule de l'entrée.
examples.trans: The neighborhood clockmaker adjusted the hall clock.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'horror'.

meanings.en: avoir horreur de = to hate, to loathe
meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'horror'.

examples.text: L'horreur absolue!
examples.trans: Total horror!

examples.text: J'ai horreur du froid.
examples.trans: I hate the cold.

examples.text: L'horreur absolue! C'était comme si elle avait treize ans.
examples.trans: Total horror! It was as if she were thirteen.

examples.text: Tout le monde le trouve horrible.
examples.trans: Everyone thinks he's horrible.

examples.text: Quel temps horrible!
examples.trans: What horrible weather!

hors.gloss: out of, off ('hors du feu' = off the heat)

meanings.note: Aspirate h in standard phrases like hors de, though hors du feu ('off the heat') is standard in cooking.

examples.text: Retirez la casserole hors du feu et mélangez.
examples.trans: Take the saucepan off the heat and stir.

examples.text: Ce vieux pont se trouve juste hors de la ville.
examples.trans: That old bridge is right outside town.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'outlaw'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Nous sommes complètement hors-la-loi.
examples.trans: We are completely outside the law.

examples.text: Nous sommes complètement hors-la-loi, Gabriel!
examples.trans: We are completely outside the law, Gabriel!

meanings.note: Être hospitalisé. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to hospitalize'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'hospitalisé').

examples.text: J'étais souvent hospitalisé.
examples.trans: I was often hospitalized.

examples.text: Il a été hospitalisé d'urgence.
examples.trans: He was hospitalized urgently.

examples.text: Enfant, j'avais les os fragiles et j'étais souvent hospitalisé.
examples.trans: As a child, I had fragile bones and I was often hospitalized.

meanings.note: une ambiance hostile = a hostile atmosphere

examples.text: L'ambiance est devenue très hostile.
examples.trans: The atmosphere became very hostile.

examples.text: Un regard hostile.
examples.trans: A hostile look.

examples.text: Mon départ s'est fait dans une ambiance hostile.
examples.trans: My departure took place in a hostile atmosphere.

meanings.en: oil (olive oil in cooking, or machine oil for hinges)
meanings.note: Mute *h* (`l'huile`, `/lɥil/`); covers both *l'huile d'olive* in the kitchen and lubricating oil in the workshop.

examples.text: Ajoutez un filet d'huile d'olive sur la soupe chaude.
examples.trans: Add a drizzle of olive oil on top of the hot soup.

examples.text: Deux gouttes d'huile suffisent pour faire tourner la charnière.
examples.trans: Two drops of oil are enough to make the hinge turn.

meanings.en: to oil (hinges, wood, or a baking pan)
meanings.note: Takes elision with mute h: j'huile, l'huiler.

examples.text: Henri a huilé les gonds du portail ce matin.
examples.trans: Henri oiled the gate hinges this morning.

examples.text: Huilez légèrement le moule à tarte avant la cuisson.
examples.trans: Lightly oil the tart pan before baking.

meanings.note: final t pronounced, except before a consonant: huit jours = ɥi ʒuʁ

examples.text: En huit ans.
examples.trans: In eight years.

examples.text: Il est huit heures.
examples.trans: It's eight o'clock.

related.word: final t pronounced, except before a consonant: huit jours

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'human'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Tu es plus humain.
examples.trans: You are more human.

examples.text: Un comportement humain.
examples.trans: A humane behavior.

examples.text: Depuis que tu t'es séparé de ta femme, tu es plus humain.
examples.trans: Since you separated from your wife, you are more human.

meanings.note: Quality of being humane. Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'humanity, humaneness'.
Quality of being humane. Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'humanity, humaneness'.

examples.text: La séparation ou l'humanité?
examples.trans: The separation or the humanity?

examples.text: Faire preuve d'humanité.
examples.trans: To show humanity.

examples.text: Si ça continue, l'humanité va s'éteindre!
examples.trans: If this continues, humanity will go extinct!

meanings.note: Slightly wet or moisture-laden (*du papier humide*, *l'air humide*), milder than *mouillé* ('wet') or *trempé* ('soaked').

examples.text: Essuyez la table avec un chiffon légèrement humide.
examples.trans: Wipe the table with a slightly damp cloth.

examples.text: L'air humide de la nuit empêche la peinture de sécher dehors.
examples.trans: The damp night air keeps the paint from drying outside.

meanings.note: Moisture in the air, ground, or stone walls.

examples.text: La toile cirée protège le papier contre l'humidité.
examples.trans: The waxed cloth protects the paper from moisture.

examples.text: Après l'averse, une douce humidité monte du jardin.
examples.trans: After the rain shower, a gentle dampness rises from the garden.

meanings.note: une humiliation publique = a public humiliation

examples.text: Ça n'atténue pas mon humiliation.
examples.trans: That does not lessen my humiliation.

examples.text: Éviter toute humiliation.
examples.trans: To avoid any humiliation.

examples.text: Ça n'atténuera pas mon humiliation publique.
examples.trans: That will not diminish my public humiliation.

meanings.en: to humiliate, to humble; s'humilier = humiliate oneself
meanings.note: Humilier quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to humble'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'humilié').

examples.text: Ne pas s'humilier devant lui.
examples.trans: Not to humiliate oneself before him.

examples.text: Je refuse de la laisser s'humilier.
examples.trans: I refuse to let her humiliate herself.

examples.text: Vous voulez vraiment m'humilier comme cela?
examples.trans: Do you really want to humiliate me like that?

meanings.note: Sense of humor. Masculine noun ('le humour', plural 'les humours') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'humor'.

examples.text: L'humour de Couchey!
examples.trans: Couchey humor!

examples.text: Il a beaucoup d'humour.
examples.trans: He has a lot of humor.

examples.text: Très bien. L'humour de Couchey!
examples.trans: Very well. Couchey humor!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to scream'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'hurlé').

examples.text: Tu n'as pas besoin de hurler.
examples.trans: You do not need to yell.

examples.text: Il hurle sur tout le monde.
examples.trans: He screams at everyone.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'extremely'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: C'est un scénario hyper intéressant.
examples.trans: It is a super interesting script.

examples.text: C'est vraiment hyper intéressant pour le film.
examples.trans: It is genuinely fascinating for the film.

meanings.en: hypochondriac, person overly anxious about health
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le hypocondriaque', plural 'les hypocondriaques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hypochondriac'.

examples.text: C'est un hypocondriaque total.
examples.trans: He is a total hypochondriac.

examples.text: François Berléand est un hypocondriaque total!
examples.trans: François Berléand is a total hypochondriac!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la hypocrisie', plural 'les hypocrisies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hypocrisy'.

examples.text: Écœuré par leur hypocrisie.
examples.trans: Sickened by their hypocrisy.

examples.text: C'est de la pure hypocrisie.
examples.trans: That is pure hypocrisy.

examples.text: Je suis profondément écœuré par leur hypocrisie.
examples.trans: I am deeply sickened by their hypocrisy.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Hypothétiquement parlant, je veux dire.
examples.trans: Hypothetically speaking, I mean.

examples.text: C'est possible, hypothétiquement.
examples.trans: It is possible, hypothetically.

examples.text: Tu m'as dévorée comme une hyène!
examples.trans: You devoured me like a hyena!

examples.text: Le cri de la hyène.
examples.trans: The cry of the hyena.

meanings.en: avoir hâte de + infinitive = can't wait to, to look forward to
meanings.note: No article after 'avoir'.

examples.text: J'ai hâte de le lire.
examples.trans: I can't wait to read it.

examples.text: J'ai hâte de te voir.
examples.trans: I can't wait to see you.

meanings.en: hey! (to get someone's attention or protest)

examples.text: Hé, arrête de me regarder comme ça!
examples.trans: Hey, stop looking at me like that!

examples.text: Hé, attends-moi!
examples.trans: Hey, wait for me!

meanings.note: Expresses regret. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'alas', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Mais c'est trop tard, hélas.
examples.trans: But it is too late, alas.

examples.text: Hélas, il est parti.
examples.trans: Alas, he has left.

meanings.note: se mettre en hérisson = to curl up defensively

examples.text: Un petit hérisson.
examples.trans: A little hedgehog.

examples.text: Un hérisson en boule.
examples.trans: A hedgehog curled in a ball.

examples.text: J'étais comme un hérisson en boule!
examples.trans: I was like a curled-up hedgehog!

meanings.note: The thing inherited can be introduced by de; uses avoir in the compound past.

examples.text: J'hérite de toutes ses parts.
examples.trans: I inherit all his shares.

examples.text: Elle a hérité de la maison.
examples.trans: She inherited the house.

examples.text: J'hérite donc de toutes ses parts.
examples.trans: So I inherit all his shares.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le héritier', plural 'les héritiers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'heir'.

examples.text: Tu deviendras l'héritière de l'empire Barneville!
examples.trans: You will become the Barneville empire heiress!

examples.text: Désigner un héritier légitime.
examples.trans: To appoint a legitimate heir.

meanings.note: aspirate h: le héros (no elision); feminine: une héroïne

examples.text: Le héros du jour!
examples.trans: The hero of the day!

examples.text: C'est le héros du film.
examples.trans: He's the hero of the film.

examples.text: Le héros du jour! Mathias, vous entrerez dans l'histoire.
examples.trans: The hero of the day! Mathias, you'll go down in history.

meanings.note: Comme une héroïne.

examples.text: Comme une héroïne.
examples.trans: Like a heroine.

examples.text: C'est la véritable héroïne de l'histoire.
examples.trans: She is the true heroine of the story.

examples.text: Tu es une héroïne, Claire! Donne-moi le lait d'abord pour la machine à café.
examples.trans: You are a hero, Claire! Give me the milk first for the coffee machine.

examples.text: Je comprends ton hésitation.
examples.trans: I understand your hesitation.

examples.text: Sans hésitation!
examples.trans: Without hesitation!

meanings.note: Hésiter à faire quelque chose.

examples.text: Et là tu hésites?
examples.trans: And now you're hesitating?

examples.text: François, il t'a invité personnellement. Et là tu hésites?
examples.trans: François, he invited you personally. And now you're hesitating?

examples.text: Il hésite à partir chez StarMedia.
examples.trans: He is hesitating about leaving for StarMedia.

meanings.note: *H* aspiré (`le hêtre`, no elision!); hard, fine-grained *bois de hêtre* is prized for piano actions and furniture.

examples.text: Les petites pièces du piano sont taillées dans du bois de hêtre.
examples.trans: The small piano parts are carved from beechwood.

examples.text: Cet établi en hêtre massif sert depuis cinquante ans.
examples.trans: This solid beech workbench has been in use for fifty years.

meanings.note: à l'hôpital = in hospital, at the hospital

examples.text: Il est à l'hôpital.
examples.trans: He's in hospital.

examples.text: L'hôpital est grand.
examples.trans: The hospital is big.

meanings.note: À l'hôtel = at the hotel.

examples.text: Il avait une chambre à l'hôtel Saint-Georges.
examples.trans: He had a room at the Hotel Saint-Georges.

examples.text: On connaît le patron de l'hôtel.
examples.trans: We know the owner of the hotel.

examples.text: Hôtel du Tilleul, bonjour! Claire à l'appareil.
examples.trans: Hotel du Tilleul, good morning! Claire speaking.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le i', plural 'les i') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'the letter i'.

examples.text: Sans le i.
examples.trans: Without the i.

examples.text: Valentin, comme Valentini sans le i.
examples.trans: Valentin, like Valentini without the i.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le iceberg', plural 'les icebergs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'iceberg'.

examples.text: Ce problème n'est que la partie visible de l'iceberg.
examples.trans: This problem is only the tip of the iceberg.

examples.text: Le navire essaie d'éviter un immense iceberg.
examples.trans: The ship is trying to avoid a huge iceberg.

examples.text: C'est sympa ici.
examples.trans: It's nice here.

examples.text: Laissez vos photos ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos here.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la icône', plural 'les icônes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'icon'.

examples.text: L'icône du cinéma français.
examples.trans: The icon of French cinema.

examples.text: Une icône de la mode.
examples.trans: A fashion icon.

examples.text: Gong Li est l'icône de L'Oréal, le partenaire principal du festival.
examples.trans: Gong Li is the icon of L'Oreal, the main partner of the festival.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: L'extérieur est identique, oui! Mais regardez à l'intérieur!
examples.trans: The outside is identical, yes! But look inside!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment identique.
examples.trans: This place is really identical.

meanings.en: identity, personal identification or identity papers
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la identité', plural 'les identités') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'identity'.

examples.text: Une pièce d'identité.
examples.trans: An identity document.

examples.text: Tu étais sans pièce d'identité?
examples.trans: You were without ID?

meanings.note: A fool; feminine idiote, also used as an adjective. Can be affectionate or insulting depending on context.

examples.text: Quel idiot!
examples.trans: What an idiot!

examples.text: Ne fais pas l'idiot.
examples.trans: Don't be silly.

examples.text: Je finis par passer pour un idiot! Tu sais ce qu'elle a fait?
examples.trans: I end up looking like an idiot! Do you know what she did?

examples.text: Tu es l'amant idéal, c'est ça?
examples.trans: You're the ideal lover, is that it?

examples.text: C'est la solution idéale.
examples.trans: It's the ideal solution.

meanings.note: un jeune idéaliste = a young idealist

examples.text: C'est un jeune idéaliste engagé.

examples.text: Les grands idéalistes.
examples.trans: Great idealists.

examples.text: C'est un jeune idéaliste engagé politiquement.
examples.trans: He is a young politically committed idealist.

examples.text: C'était mon idée.
examples.trans: It was my idea.

examples.text: J'ai une idée.
examples.trans: I have an idea.

examples.trans: Yes, that would be disgraceful.

examples.trans: Despicable behavior.
