examples.trans: Yes, that would be disgraceful. Still...

meanings.note: Il m'ignore.

meanings.en: to be unaware of, not know
meanings.note: J'ignore la vérité.

examples.text: Il m'invite et il m'ignore!
examples.trans: He invites me and he ignores me!

examples.text: Il ne me parle pas! Il m'invite, et il m'ignore!
examples.trans: He isn't talking to me! He invites me, and he ignores me!

examples.text: Il est là.
examples.trans: He is here.

examples.text: Il y a une réunion.
examples.trans: There is a meeting.

meanings.note: Never changes for plural.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
examples.trans: Is there another Clémentine?

examples.text: Il y a une réunion.
examples.trans: There's a meeting.

examples.text: Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: To decorate or clarify a book, card, or text with drawings; to exemplify.

examples.text: Elle aime illustrer ses carnets de cuisine à l'aquarelle.
examples.trans: She likes to illustrate her recipe notebooks in watercolor.

examples.text: Des cartes postales anciennes illustrent l'histoire du quartier.
examples.trans: Vintage postcards illustrate the neighborhood's history.

meanings.note: for a group of men, or a mixed group; elles for women only

examples.text: Ils n'ont rien pour l'instant, madame, je suis vraiment désolé.
examples.trans: They have nothing for now, madam, I am truly sorry.

examples.text: Et les grands frères n'arrivent jamais en avance quand ils veulent garder l'air calme.
examples.trans: And big brothers never arrive early when they want to look calm.

examples.text: Claire, regarde par la vitre: ils sont face à face sous le tilleul!
examples.trans: Claire, look through the glass: they are face to face under the linden tree!

meanings.note: Gestion d'image.
Une belle image.

examples.text: La gestion d'image pour les acteurs.
examples.trans: Image management for the actors.

examples.text: Et un pôle gestion d'image pour les acteurs.
examples.trans: And an image-management department for the actors.

meanings.note: Avoir de l'imagination.

examples.text: Les réalisateurs n'ont pas d'imagination.
examples.trans: Directors have no imagination.

examples.text: Elle a beaucoup d'imagination.
examples.trans: She has a lot of imagination.

examples.text: Audrey, les réalisateurs n'ont pas d'imagination.
examples.trans: Audrey, directors have no imagination.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to imagine'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'imaginé').

examples.text: Imaginez une plage.
examples.trans: Imagine a beach.

examples.text: J'imagine que oui.
examples.trans: I imagine so.

examples.text: Imaginez qu'il y a une ligne invisible entre nous.
examples.trans: Imagine there's an invisible line between us.

meanings.note: Formed from *in-* (spelled *im-* before *b*) + *battre* + *-able*.

examples.text: Sa tarte chaude aux citrons du marché est vraiment imbattable.
examples.trans: Her warm market-lemon tart is truly unbeatable.

examples.text: À ce prix-là, la qualité de ces tasses est imbattable.
examples.trans: At that price, the quality of these cups is unbeatable.

meanings.note: Imiter quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to imitate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'imité').

examples.text: Imiter Hicham à ton entretien?
examples.trans: Imitate Hicham at your interview?

examples.text: Il imite très bien les acteurs.
examples.trans: He imitates actors very well.

examples.text: Imiter Hicham à ton entretien? Tu ne devrais pas être toi-même?
examples.trans: Imitate Hicham at your interview? Shouldn't you be yourself?

meanings.note: Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Une immense star du cinéma.
examples.trans: An immense cinema star.

examples.text: Pourquoi? C'est une immense star du cinéma.
examples.trans: Why? She is an immense movie star.

examples.text: Il dit que tu as un talent immense.
examples.trans: He says that you have immense talent.

meanings.note: Plongé profondément dans une activité. Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Tu étais trop immergé dans ton rôle.
examples.trans: You were too immersed in your role.

examples.text: L'acteur est totalement immergé dans son personnage.
examples.trans: The actor is completely immersed in his character.

meanings.note: Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion. Standard masculine noun meaning 'apartment building, block'.

examples.text: Ils sont devant l'immeuble.
examples.trans: They are in front of the building.

examples.text: Il s'installe dans un nouvel immeuble.
examples.trans: He is moving into a new building.

examples.text: Dans les vieux immeubles en brique, l'eau met souvent longtemps à monter tout en haut.
examples.trans: In old brick buildings, water often takes a long time to reach the very top.

meanings.note: Something about to happen very soon.

examples.text: Le retour d'Audrey est imminent.
examples.trans: Audrey's return is imminent.

examples.text: Un départ imminent.
examples.trans: An imminent departure.

examples.text: Le retour d'Audrey sur un tournage est imminent.
examples.trans: Audrey's return to a film shoot is imminent.

meanings.note: des biens immobiliers = real estate properties

examples.text: Des biens immobiliers dans le centre de Paris.
examples.trans: Real estate properties in the centre of Paris.

examples.text: Une agence immobilière.
examples.trans: An estate agency.

examples.text: Le facteur vient de me faire signer un recommandé. Il y a un tampon rouge d'agence immobilière.
examples.trans: The postman just had me sign for registered mail. There is a red property-agency stamp.

meanings.note: The role in the Tarantino film.
Botany.

examples.text: Elle joue l'immortelle.
examples.trans: She plays the immortal woman.

examples.text: L'immortelle est jeune.
examples.trans: The immortal woman is young.

meanings.note: avec effet immédiat = with immediate effect

examples.text: Un effet immédiat.
examples.trans: An immediate effect.

examples.text: Une réponse immédiate.
examples.trans: An immediate reply.

examples.text: Je pars avec un effet immédiat!
examples.trans: I leave with immediate effect!

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem. Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Parle à Ramzy immédiatement.
examples.trans: Talk to Ramzy immediately.

examples.text: Je dois régler ce problème immédiatement.
examples.trans: I must settle this problem immediately.

examples.text: Venez immédiatement.
examples.trans: Come immediately.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Ce qu'elle a fait est impardonnable.
examples.trans: What she did is unforgivable.

examples.text: Une erreur impardonnable.
examples.trans: An unforgivable mistake.

examples.text: C'est totalement impardonnable, Gabriel!
examples.trans: That is totally unforgivable, Gabriel!

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Vous êtes toujours impeccable.
examples.trans: You are always flawless.

examples.text: Impeccable, Étienne! Et vos lunettes sont même sur votre nez et pas sur votre front.
examples.trans: Spotless, Etienne! And your glasses are even on your nose and not on your forehead.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'imply'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'impliqué').

examples.text: Cela implique des changements.
examples.trans: That implies changes.

examples.text: Pour nous, ça implique des changements. Changer d'agent.
examples.trans: For us, that implies changes. Changing agents.

examples.text: Diriger implique de perdre certaines batailles.
examples.trans: Leading implies losing certain battles.

meanings.note: ça n'a aucune importance = it doesn't matter at all

examples.text: Ça n'a aucune importance!
examples.trans: That doesn't matter at all!

examples.text: C'est sans importance.
examples.trans: It's unimportant.

examples.text: C'est important.
examples.trans: It's important.

examples.text: Une réunion importante.
examples.trans: An important meeting.

meanings.note: Impersonally: to matter ('peu importe' = never mind, no matter); to bring goods in from abroad.

examples.text: Peu importe la pluie, nous avons de bons parapluies!
examples.trans: Never mind the rain, we have good umbrellas!

examples.text: Ce qui importe le plus, c'est de tenir sa promesse.
examples.trans: What matters most is keeping one's promise.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to impose'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'imposé').

examples.text: Il impose des changements.
examples.trans: He imposes changes.

examples.text: Il impose des changements inacceptables.
examples.trans: He is imposing unacceptable changes.

meanings.note: same form for masculine and feminine

examples.text: C'est impossible.
examples.trans: It's impossible.

examples.text: Rien n'est impossible.
examples.trans: Nothing is impossible.

meanings.note: j'ai l'impression que = I have the feeling that

examples.text: J'ai l'impression qu'il m'évite.
examples.trans: I have the feeling he's avoiding me.

examples.text: Quelle impression!
examples.trans: What an impression!

examples.text: Son jeu sur scène est vraiment très impressionnant.
examples.trans: His acting on stage is really very impressive.

examples.text: C'est un chiffre d'affaires tout à fait impressionnant.
examples.trans: That is a thoroughly impressive turnover.

examples.text: Vos menaces ne m'impressionnent pas.
examples.trans: Your threats don't impress me.

examples.text: Elle impressionne tout le monde.
examples.trans: She impresses everyone.

meanings.note: Un menu imprimé = a printed menu.

examples.text: J'ai imprimé vingt cartes du menu en grands caractères.
examples.trans: I printed twenty menu cards in large print.

examples.text: L'imprimerie du quartier imprime nos affiches.
examples.trans: The neighborhood print shop prints our posters.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Une histoire improbable.
examples.trans: An improbable story.

examples.text: Un accident complètement improbable.
examples.trans: A completely improbable accident.

meanings.note: Faire de l'improvisation. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion. Standard feminine noun meaning 'spontaneous acting, improvisation'.

examples.text: Nous allons faire une courte improvisation.
examples.trans: We are going to do a short improvisation.

examples.text: L'improvisation demande de la créativité.
examples.trans: Improvisation requires creativity.

meanings.note: To make it up on the spot.

examples.text: Quand il oublie son texte, il préfère improviser.
examples.trans: When he forgets his lines, he prefers to improvise.

examples.text: Vas-y, improvise quelque chose de naturel devant la caméra!
examples.trans: Go on, improvise something natural in front of the camera!

meanings.note: Planned or made spontaneously rather than prepared in advance.

examples.text: C'est un peu improvisé.
examples.trans: It's a bit last-minute.

examples.text: Un dîner improvisé.
examples.trans: An impromptu dinner.

examples.text: Excusez-moi, c'est un peu improvisé.
examples.trans: Sorry, it's a bit last-minute.

meanings.note: an old-fashioned word for an artist's agent

examples.text: Elle dit imprésario, pas agent.
examples.trans: She says impresario, not agent.

examples.text: C'est un grand imprésario.
examples.trans: He's a great impresario.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le imprévu', plural 'les imprévus') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'unforeseen event'.

examples.text: J'ai eu un petit imprévu ce matin.
examples.trans: I had a minor unexpected hitch this morning.

examples.text: J'ai eu un petit imprévu.
examples.trans: I had a small unexpected issue.

examples.text: Un petit imprévu? Tu te moques de moi?
examples.trans: A small unexpected issue? Are you mocking me?

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots. Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Hicham est très impulsif.
examples.trans: Hicham is very impulsive.

examples.text: Non, surtout pas, Hicham est très impulsif.
examples.trans: No, especially not, Hicham is very impulsive.

examples.text: C'est une réaction trop impulsive, attends!
examples.trans: That is too impulsive a reaction, wait!

meanings.note: Silent final -t.

examples.text: Ce règlement se lit comme un gros manuel d'impôts.
examples.trans: This regulation reads like a thick tax textbook.

examples.text: Il range les papiers d'impôts dans un classeur vert.
examples.trans: He files the tax papers in a green binder.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.trans: That is unacceptable.

examples.text: Un comportement inacceptable.
examples.trans: Unacceptable behavior.

examples.text: C'est un chantage inacceptable, Hicham.
examples.trans: That is unacceptable blackmail, Hicham.

meanings.note: Classic word for an unfinished musical work, letter, or painting (*une valse inachevée*, *la Symphonie inachevée*).

examples.text: Ne laissez pas votre travail inachevé avant de fermer l'atelier.
examples.trans: Don't leave your work unfinished before closing the workshop.

meanings.note: Not expected; feminine inattendue.

examples.text: C'est totalement inattendu.
examples.trans: It's totally unexpected.

examples.text: Une visite inattendue.
examples.trans: An unexpected visit.

examples.text: Et surtout inattendu.
examples.trans: And above all unexpected.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to embody'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'incarné').

examples.text: Une personne incarne l'agence.
examples.trans: One person embodies the agency.

examples.text: Elle incarne ce personnage à merveille.
examples.trans: She plays this character wonderfully.

examples.text: Elle incarne un fantôme sans nom.
examples.trans: She embodies a nameless ghost.

meanings.note: Opposite of certain.

examples.text: La situation est incertaine.

meanings.note: Sortir incognito = to go out incognito. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.trans: To travel incognito.

examples.text: Elle est sortie incognito.

examples.text: Tu n'es jamais sortie incognito?
examples.trans: Have you never gone out incognito?

meanings.note: Une décision incompréhensible. Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.trans: This story with France 2 is incomprehensible.

examples.text: Sa réaction était totalement incompréhensible.
examples.trans: His reaction was completely incomprehensible.

meanings.note: feminine: une inconnue; also adjective: unknown

examples.trans: I don't leave my children with a stranger!

examples.text: Le genre d'hôtel qui répare une lampe sous la pluie et garde le sac d'un inconnu.
examples.trans: The kind of hotel that fixes a lamp in the rain and guards a stranger's bag.

meanings.note: L'inconscient.

examples.trans: My subconscious and Julie Gayet's clash.

examples.text: C'est dans l'inconscient.
examples.trans: It's in the subconscious.

meanings.note: Culinary term: to fold berries, flour, or egg whites gently into a batter.

examples.text: Incorporez doucement les fruits rouges entiers dans la pâte aux amandes.
examples.trans: Gently fold the whole berries into the almond batter.

examples.text: Il incorpore le beurre fondu à l'aide d'une cuillère en bois.
examples.trans: He folds in the melted butter with a wooden spoon.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Tu es vraiment incorrigible.
examples.trans: You are truly incorrigible.

examples.text: Tu es vraiment incorrigible et pleine d'énergie!
examples.trans: You are truly incorrigible and full of energy!

examples.text: Tu es vraiment incorrigible ce soir.
examples.trans: You are really incorrigible tonight.

meanings.note: Hard to believe, extraordinary.

examples.text: C'est incroyable que l'encre soit restée aussi nette!

examples.text: Quelle histoire incroyable derrière cette vieille porte!
examples.trans: What an unbelievable story behind this old door!

meanings.note: Clue in a mystery or treasure hunt; revealing sign.

examples.text: Le premier indice est caché dans une rime au dos de la carte.
examples.trans: The first clue is hidden in a rhyme on the back of the card.

examples.text: Chaque petit détail de ce dessin est un indice précieux.
examples.trans: Every tiny detail of this drawing is a precious clue.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to indicate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'indiqué').

examples.text: Quelle heure indique votre montre maintenant, Henri?
examples.trans: What time does your watch show now, Henri?

examples.text: J'indique sans père sur l'acte.
examples.trans: I indicate fatherless on the certificate.

examples.text: Le panneau indique la bonne direction.
examples.trans: The sign indicates the right direction.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: C'est une question particulièrement indiscrète, Gabriel!
examples.trans: That is a particularly indiscreet question, Gabriel!

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Elle est indisponible.
examples.trans: She is unavailable.

examples.text: Le numéro est indisponible.

examples.text: Comment ça, Isabelle est indisponible?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Isabelle is unavailable?

examples.text: C'est une industrie.
examples.trans: It's an industry.

examples.text: L'industrie du cinéma.
examples.trans: The film industry.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Je pourrais rouler indéfiniment.
examples.trans: I could drive indefinitely.

examples.text: Attendre indéfiniment.
examples.trans: To wait endlessly.

meanings.note: Encre indélébile = permanent ink.

examples.text: Merveilleux! Votre nom entre dans le grand cahier d'Henri à l'encre indélébile!
examples.trans: Wonderful! Your name goes into Henri's big notebook in permanent ink!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment indélébile.
examples.trans: This place is really indelible, permanent.

meanings.note: Producteur indépendant. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Un producteur indépendant.
examples.trans: An independent producer.

examples.text: Je voulais devenir un producteur indépendant.
examples.trans: I wanted to become an independent producer.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Une surprise indésirable.
examples.trans: An unwelcome surprise.

examples.text: Certaines surprises sont indésirables.
examples.trans: Some surprises are unwelcome.

examples.text: Tout médicament a des effets indésirables.
examples.trans: Every medication has undesirable effects.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le infarctus', plural 'les infarctus') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'heart attack'.

examples.text: Mathias se remet de son infarctus.
examples.trans: Mathias is recovering from his heart attack.

examples.text: Il sort tout juste d'un infarctus.
examples.trans: He just came through a heart attack.

examples.text: Tu as failli mourir d'un infarctus!
examples.trans: You almost died of a heart attack!

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard feminine noun meaning 'infidelity, unfaithfulness'.

examples.text: L'infidélité n'existe pas vraiment.
examples.trans: Infidelity does not really exist.

examples.text: Une infidélité conjugale.
examples.trans: Marital infidelity.

meanings.note: merci infiniment = thank you so much

examples.text: Merci infiniment.
examples.trans: Thank you so much.

examples.text: Elle l'aime infiniment.
examples.trans: She loves him endlessly.

meanings.note: une infirmière diplômée = a certified nurse

examples.text: Travailler comme infirmier.
examples.trans: To work as a nurse.

examples.text: Une infirmière de garde.
examples.trans: A nurse on duty.

examples.text: Faites confiance à une infirmière diplômée!
examples.trans: Trust a certified nurse!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la infirmière', plural 'les infirmières') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nurse'.

examples.trans: I am an ordinary nurse.

examples.text: Non, je suis une simple infirmière.
examples.trans: No, I am an ordinary nurse.

examples.text: Je joue le rôle d'une infirmière.
examples.trans: I play the role of a nurse.

meanings.note: Influencer quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to influence'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'influencé').

examples.text: Il a influencé Hicham pour te choisir!
examples.trans: He influenced Hicham to pick you!

examples.text: Influencer une décision.
examples.trans: To influence a decision.

meanings.note: short for information; des infos = info

examples.text: Tu as des infos sur lui?
examples.trans: Do you have info on him?

examples.text: Regarder les infos.
examples.trans: To watch the news.

examples.text: Tu as des infos sur Luchini?
examples.trans: Do you have info on Luchini?

meanings.note: Informer les gens. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to inform'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'informé').

examples.text: Informe les gens de ta nouvelle adresse.
examples.trans: Inform people of your new address.

examples.text: Je vous informe de mon arrivée.
examples.trans: I inform you of my arrival.

examples.text: J'ai d'excellentes sources bien informées.
examples.trans: I have excellent, well-informed sources.

meanings.en: to brew, to steep, to infuse (tea or herbs)

examples.text: Le thé a infusé trop longtemps.

examples.text: Laisse infuser trois minutes.
examples.trans: Let it steep for three minutes.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la infusion', plural 'les infusions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'herbal tea'.

examples.text: Tu veux une infusion?
examples.trans: Would you like an herbal tea?

examples.text: Tu veux bien une infusion?
examples.trans: Would you like an herbal tea?

examples.text: Oui, je veux bien une infusion.
examples.trans: Yes, I would love an herbal tea.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le ingénieur', plural 'les ingénieurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'engineer'.

examples.text: L'ingénieur du son règle les micros.

examples.text: L'ingénieur du son peut nettoyer ça.
examples.trans: The sound engineer can clean that.

meanings.note: Ingérence extérieure. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard feminine noun meaning 'outside meddling, intrusion'.

examples.text: Je ne veux aucune ingérence extérieure.
examples.trans: I want no outside interference.

examples.text: C'est une ingérence inacceptable.
examples.trans: It is an unacceptable intrusion.

meanings.note: Usually plural when referring to monogrammed letters.

examples.text: Pas de numéro de téléphone, malheureusement. Seulement deux initiales et un vieux nom de rue.
examples.trans: No phone number, unfortunately. Only two initials and an old street name.

examples.text: Regardez la fermeture éclair... oui, ses initiales sont juste là!
examples.trans: Check the zipper... yes, her initials are right here!

examples.text: Attendez une minute... Numéro douze, {STREET}, et deux initiales d'enfance écrites dans le coin!
examples.trans: Wait a moment... Number twelve, {STREET}, and two childhood initials written in the corner!

meanings.note: être injuste envers quelqu'un = to be unfair to someone

examples.text: Tu es vraiment injuste!
examples.trans: You're really being unfair!

examples.text: C'est une décision injuste.
examples.trans: It's an unfair decision.

examples.text: Arrête, tu es vraiment injuste! Tu as beaucoup de chance.
examples.trans: Stop it, you are being really unfair! You are very lucky.

meanings.note: Une terrible injustice. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard feminine noun meaning 'injustice, unfairness'.

examples.text: Je vis très mal toute cette terrible injustice.
examples.trans: I am coping very badly with this terrible injustice.

examples.text: Il lutte contre toutes les injustices.
examples.trans: He fights against all injustices.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis'). Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Ce sera une soirée inoubliable.
examples.trans: It will be an unforgettable evening.

examples.text: Ce sera une soirée inoubliable pour nous tous.
examples.trans: This will be an unforgettable evening for all of us.

examples.text: Elle vous donnera une allure inoubliable.
examples.trans: It will give you an unforgettable look.

meanings.note: Note the feminine 'inquiète'.

examples.text: Tu étais si fatiguée hier soir, j'étais inquiet.
examples.trans: You were so tired last night, I was worried.

examples.text: Elle est très inquiète.
examples.trans: She is very worried.

meanings.note: Ça m'inquiète = that worries me.

examples.text: Ça ne m'inquiète pas.
examples.trans: That doesn't worry me.

examples.text: Tu m'inquiètes.
examples.trans: You're worrying me.

meanings.note: irregular verb; past participle: inscrit

examples.text: J'inscris mon enfant à l'école.
examples.trans: I am enrolling my child in school.

examples.text: Tu inscris le bébé aux castings?
examples.trans: Are you signing the baby up for auditions?

examples.text: Il y a des insectes dans le foin?
examples.trans: Are there insects in the hay?

examples.text: Un insecte! Il y avait un insecte!
examples.trans: An insect! There was an insect!

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Ce détail est insignifiant.
examples.trans: This detail is insignificant.

examples.text: Nos petites erreurs semblent insignifiantes désormais.
examples.trans: Our little mistakes seem insignificant now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard feminine noun meaning 'insistence'.

examples.text: Regarder avec insistance.
examples.trans: To stare insistently.

examples.text: Parler avec insistance.
examples.trans: To speak with insistence.

examples.text: Arrêtez de me regarder avec insistance.
examples.trans: Stop looking at me insistently.

meanings.note: Insister pour entrer.

examples.text: Après avoir insisté.
examples.trans: After insisting.

examples.text: Oui, comme tu vois. Après avoir insisté.
examples.trans: Yes, as you can see. After insisting.

meanings.note: Feminine: inspectrice.

examples.text: Des douches glacées?! Avec l'inspecteur du Guide de Lyon au troisième étage?!
examples.trans: Ice-cold showers?! With the Lyon Guide inspector on the third floor?!

examples.text: Le Guide de Lyon? Attendez: vous pensez que je suis inspecteur d'hôtels?
examples.trans: The Lyon Guide? Wait: do you think I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Official visit or careful examination to verify that everything meets required standards.

examples.text: Une lettre officielle de la mairie?! Attendez, mon cœur ne survivra pas à une autre inspection!
examples.trans: An official letter from City Hall?! Hold on, my heart will not survive another inspection!

examples.text: L'inspection des poutres en chêne du salon s'est très bien passée.
examples.trans: The inspection of the oak beams in the sunroom went very well.

meanings.note: Masculine counterpart: un inspecteur.

examples.text: L'inspectrice du patrimoine a félicité toute la maison.
examples.trans: The heritage inspector congratulated the whole house.

examples.text: L'inspectrice vérifie chaque fenêtre et chaque sortie.
examples.trans: The inspector checks every window and every exit.

meanings.note: Prendre une grande inspiration = take a deep breath.

examples.text: Prenez une grande inspiration avant d'ouvrir la porte.
examples.trans: Take a deep breath before opening the door.

examples.text: Le jardin tranquille donne de l'inspiration à la musicienne.
examples.trans: The quiet garden gives inspiration to the musician.

meanings.en: s'inspirer de = to take inspiration from

examples.text: Je me suis inspiré de cette affaire.
examples.trans: I took inspiration from this case.

examples.text: Cette histoire m'inspire.
examples.trans: This story inspires me.

meanings.note: Used both for technical installation and simply setting out chairs and tables (*installer douze chaises*).

examples.text: Installons quatre petites tables près des fenêtres du jardin.
examples.trans: Let's set up four small tables near the garden windows.

examples.text: L'électricien a installé une lampe neuve au plafond.
examples.trans: The electrician installed a new lamp on the ceiling.

related.gloss: to put away, tidy up, store neatly

meanings.note: pour l'instant = for the moment, for now
Un instant, s'il vous plaît. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard masculine noun meaning 'instant, moment'.

examples.text: Attendez un instant.
examples.trans: Wait a moment.

examples.text: Un instant, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: One moment, please.

examples.text: Voilà un taxi devant le portail à l'instant.
examples.trans: Here comes a taxi in front of the gate right now.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le instinct', plural 'les instincts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'natural instinct'.

examples.text: Suivre son instinct.
examples.trans: Follow one's instinct.

examples.text: Ton instinct est à quel niveau?
examples.trans: What level is your instinct at?

meanings.note: film institutionnel = corporate film

examples.text: Un film institutionnel.
examples.trans: A corporate film.

examples.text: C'est un film institutionnel pour ASK.
examples.trans: This is a major film for ASK.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la institutrice', plural 'les institutrices') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'schoolteacher'.

examples.text: C'est le rôle principal de l'institutrice.
examples.trans: It is the leading role of the schoolteacher.

examples.text: L'institutrice lit une belle histoire aux enfants.
examples.trans: The schoolteacher reads a nice story to the children.

examples.text: Pour le rôle principal de l'institutrice?
examples.trans: For the leading role of the schoolteacher?

examples.text: Désolée de vous avoir insulté.
examples.trans: Sorry for insulting you.

examples.text: Ne m'insulte pas!
examples.trans: Don't insult me!

examples.text: Désolée de vous avoir insulté. Dîner demain?
examples.trans: Sorry for insulting you. Dinner tomorrow?

examples.text: Ma fille n'est pas insupportable!
examples.trans: My daughter is not unbearable!

examples.text: Ce bruit est insupportable.
examples.trans: This noise is unbearable.

meanings.note: Final *-ct* is pronounced `/kt/` in both masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Malgré le voyage, les douze tasses en grès sont arrivées intactes.
examples.trans: Despite the trip, the twelve stoneware cups arrived intact.

examples.text: Les touches en ivoire du vieux piano sont restées intactes.
examples.trans: The ivory keys of the old piano remained undamaged.

related.gloss: to damage, spoil (s'abîmer = get damaged, chip)

meanings.note: La propriété intellectuelle. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: La propriété intellectuelle.
examples.trans: Intellectual property.

examples.text: Un travail intellectuel.
examples.trans: An intellectual work.

examples.text: Droit, spécialisée en propriété intellectuelle.
examples.trans: Law school, specialized in intellectual property.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas très intelligent.
examples.trans: It's not very smart.

examples.text: C'est une femme très intelligente.
examples.trans: She's a very intelligent woman.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas très intelligent de sortir avec l'assistante de son agent.
examples.trans: It's not very smart to go out with his agent's assistant.

examples.text: C'était intense.
examples.trans: It was intense.

examples.text: Une journée intense.
examples.trans: An intense day.

meanings.note: jouer avec intensité = to act with intensity

examples.text: Une intensité folle.
examples.trans: A wild intensity.

examples.text: L'intensité de la scène.
examples.trans: The intensity of the scene.

examples.text: Jean Dujardin y joue avec une intensité folle.
examples.trans: Jean Dujardin acts with wild intensity in it.

meanings.note: Avoir l'intention de + infinitive = 'to intend to'.

examples.text: Je n'avais aucune intention de vendre le vieux piano du salon.
examples.trans: I had no intention at all of selling the old parlor piano.

examples.text: C'est une délicate intention de votre part.
examples.trans: That is a thoughtful gesture on your part.

examples.text: Il est très bien intentionné.
examples.trans: He is very well-meaning.

examples.text: Méfie-toi des gens mal intentionnés.
examples.trans: Watch out for ill-intentioned people.

meanings.note: Rule forbidding an action ('interdiction de...' = no ... allowed).

examples.text: Interdiction d'ouvrir l'enveloppe avant midi pile!
examples.trans: No opening the envelope before twelve sharp!

examples.text: Une pancarte rappelle l'interdiction de marcher sur les pelouses.
examples.trans: A sign reminds visitors not to walk on the lawns.

interdire.gloss: to forbid, to ban, to prohibit
interdire.governs: quelque chose à quelqu'un; de + infinitive

meanings.note: interdire à quelqu'un de faire quelque chose; past participle interdit(e) = forbidden

examples.text: Notre amour est mille fois interdit.
examples.trans: Our love is a thousand times forbidden.

examples.text: Il est interdit de fumer ici.
examples.trans: Smoking is forbidden here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: C'est interdit de fumer.
examples.trans: Smoking is forbidden.

examples.text: Une zone interdite.
examples.trans: A prohibited zone.

examples.text: C'est interdit que des femmes se parlent?
examples.trans: Is it forbidden for women to talk to each other?

meanings.note: Aucune interférence. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard feminine noun meaning 'meddling, interference'.

examples.text: Je refuse toute interférence dans mon travail.
examples.trans: I refuse any interference in my work.

examples.text: Il y a trop d'interférences extérieures.
examples.trans: There is too much outside interference.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Une carrière internationale.
examples.trans: An international career.

examples.text: Un aéroport international.
examples.trans: An international airport.

examples.text: Une carrière internationale dans James Bond.
examples.trans: An international career in James Bond.

meanings.note: Sur internet = on the internet. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard masculine noun meaning 'internet, online network'.

examples.text: Une connexion internet rapide.
examples.trans: A fast internet connection.

examples.text: Chercher sur internet.
examples.trans: To search on the internet.

examples.text: C'est vrai. Mais le cinéma, ce n'est pas Internet.
examples.trans: That's true. But cinema isn't the Internet.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le interphone', plural 'les interphones') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'intercom'.

examples.text: On sonne à l'interphone.
examples.trans: Someone is ringing the intercom.

examples.text: Attention, Oscar sonne à l'interphone!
examples.trans: Watch out, Oscar is ringing the intercom!

meanings.note: Conjugated like rompre (3rd sg il interrompt with -t).

examples.text: L'orage d'été a interrompu le concert dans la cour.
examples.trans: The summer storm interrupted the concert in the courtyard.

examples.text: Excusez-moi de vous interrompre une seconde.
examples.trans: Excuse me for interrupting you for a second.

meanings.note: Appuyer sur l'interrupteur means 'to press/flip the light switch'.

examples.text: L'interrupteur du couloir se trouve à droite de la porte.
examples.trans: The hallway light switch is to the right of the door.

examples.text: Henri remplace le vieil interrupteur par une plaque en laiton.
examples.trans: Henri replaces the old switch with a brass plate.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la interruption', plural 'les interruptions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'interruption'.

examples.text: Une interruption de tournage.
examples.trans: A production shutdown.

examples.text: Une interruption coûte des millions de dollars.
examples.trans: A shutdown costs millions of dollars.

examples.text: L'assurance va couvrir l'interruption?
examples.trans: Will the insurance cover the shutdown?

meanings.note: Uses être in compound past tenses: elle est intervenue.

examples.text: Réglez ça ou j'interviens!
examples.trans: Sort it out or I'll step in!

examples.text: La police intervient.
examples.trans: The police step in.

examples.text: Réglez ça en vingt-quatre heures ou j'interviens!
examples.trans: Sort it out in twenty-four hours or I step in!

meanings.note: Usually feminine in French. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard feminine noun meaning 'interview, press interview'.

examples.text: Les interviews pour le film.
examples.trans: The interviews for the movie.

examples.text: Donner une interview.
examples.trans: To give an interview.

examples.text: Les interviews, les photos pour le film, c'est hors de question.
examples.trans: Interviews, photos for the film, it is out of the question.

meanings.note: La pièce la plus intime. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: C'est la pièce la plus intime.
examples.trans: It is the most intimate room.

examples.text: Un dîner intime.
examples.trans: An intimate dinner.

examples.text: La plus intime. Je vous laisse entrer.
examples.trans: The most intimate. I will let you go in.

meanings.note: Intimider quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to intimidate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'intimidé').

examples.text: Elle va penser qu'elle vous intimide.
examples.trans: She will think that she intimidates you.

examples.text: Rien ne peut l'intimider.
examples.trans: Nothing can intimidate him.

examples.text: Tu intimides peut-être beaucoup de prétendants.
examples.trans: You perhaps intimidate many suitors.

meanings.note: A close private connection, or privacy, depending on context.
A close private connection, or privacy, depending on context.

examples.text: C'est de l'intimité pure.
examples.trans: It's pure intimacy.

examples.text: Un moment d'intimité.
examples.trans: A moment of intimacy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Un livre très intéressant.
examples.trans: A very interesting book.

examples.text: As-tu trouvé un guide intéressant, Monica?
examples.trans: Did you find an interesting guide, Monica?

examples.text: C'est vraiment hyper intéressant pour le film.
examples.trans: It is genuinely fascinating for the film.

meanings.note: Ça m'intéresse = that interests me.

meanings.en: s'intéresser à = to be interested in

examples.text: C'est ce qui m'intéresse.
examples.trans: That's what interests me.

examples.text: Ce rôle m'intéresse beaucoup.
examples.trans: This part interests me a lot.

meanings.note: Intéressé par = interested in.

examples.text: Vous n'êtes pas intéressé?
examples.trans: You're not interested?

examples.text: Elle est intéressée.
examples.trans: She's interested.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le intérieur', plural 'les intérieurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'interior'.

examples.text: La scène suivante est tournée à l'intérieur du château.
examples.trans: The next scene is filmed inside the castle.

examples.text: Elle cache une grande force à l'intérieur.
examples.trans: She hides a great strength on the inside.

meanings.note: Par intérim = acting, interim. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard masculine noun meaning 'interim, temporary work'.

examples.text: Ton agent par intérim.
examples.trans: Your interim agent.

examples.text: Travailler en intérim.
examples.trans: To do temporary work.

examples.text: Je serai en quelque sorte ton agent par intérim.
examples.trans: I will be your interim agent in a way.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard masculine noun meaning 'interest, self-interest'.

examples.text: L'intérêt personnel.
examples.trans: Self-interest.

examples.text: Quand on est riche, on apprend à reconnaître l'intérêt personnel.
examples.trans: When you are rich, you learn to recognize self-interest.

examples.text: Réfléchis bien à l'intérêt de l'agence.
examples.trans: Think carefully about the agency's interest.

meanings.note: Un exercice inutile. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Sans totale liberté, l'art est inutile.
examples.trans: Without total freedom, art is useless.

examples.text: C'est une dépense inutile.
examples.trans: It is an unnecessary expense.

examples.text: Nous voulions éviter les bavardages inutiles.
examples.trans: We wanted to avoid unnecessary gossip.

meanings.en: to make up a story, invent

examples.text: Elle invente une fausse excuse.
examples.trans: She invents a false excuse.

examples.text: Je n'ai pas le pouvoir d'inventer ça.
examples.trans: I do not have the power to make that up.

examples.text: Il a inventé un nouveau genre.
examples.trans: He invented a new genre.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le inverse', plural 'les inverses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'opposite'.

examples.text: Ça devrait être totalement l'inverse.
examples.trans: It should be totally the reverse.

examples.text: C'est l'inverse de ce que je voulais.
examples.trans: It is the opposite of what I wanted.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to reverse'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'inversé').

examples.text: On a juste inversé deux rôles.
examples.trans: We just switched two roles.

examples.text: Quoi? Il refuse d'inverser les rôles?
examples.trans: What? He refuses to switch the roles?

meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Core French verb meaning 'to invest'.

examples.text: Pourquoi investirait-il chez nous?
examples.trans: Why would he invest in us?

examples.text: Oui, mais pourquoi investirait-il chez nous?
examples.trans: Yes, but why would he invest in us?

examples.text: Tu n'es pas investie dans cette grossesse.
examples.trans: You are not invested in this pregnancy.

meanings.note: perdre son investissement = to lose one's investment

examples.text: Un gros investissement.
examples.trans: A major investment.

examples.text: Rentabiliser un investissement.
examples.trans: To make an investment profitable.

examples.text: Il a peur de perdre son investissement.
examples.trans: He is afraid of losing his investment.

meanings.note: Something that cannot be seen; same singular spelling for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Une ligne invisible.
examples.trans: An invisible line.

examples.text: Il est presque invisible.
examples.trans: He's almost invisible.

examples.text: Imaginez qu'il y a une ligne invisible entre nous.
examples.trans: Imagine there's an invisible line between us.

meanings.note: une invitation à / aux = an invitation to

examples.text: Une invitation aux Césars!
examples.trans: An invitation to the Césars!

examples.text: Je n'ai pas eu d'invitation.
examples.trans: I didn't get an invitation.

meanings.note: Inviter quelqu'un à prendre le thé = invite someone for tea.

examples.text: Nous avons invité tous les voisins de la rue vendredi.
examples.trans: We invited all the neighbors on the street on Friday.

examples.text: Je vous invite à boire une tasse de thé chaud.
examples.trans: I invite you to have a cup of hot tea.

meanings.en: guest (at an event, dinner, or gathering)
meanings.note: Feminine form: une invitée.

examples.text: Chaque invité trouve une chaise autour des tables.
examples.trans: Every guest finds a chair around the tables.

examples.text: Allons accueillir notre première invitée au portail!
examples.trans: Let's go welcome our first guest at the gate!

meanings.en: unpublished, never before performed or released
meanings.note: Une valse inédite = an unpublished waltz.

examples.text: Elle a retrouvé une partition inédite dans le pupitre.
examples.trans: She found an unpublished score inside the music stand.

examples.text: Ce carnet contient trois poèmes inédits.
examples.trans: This notebook contains three unpublished poems.

meanings.note: une situation irrattrapable = an unrecoverable situation

examples.text: Est-ce que la situation est irrattrapable?
examples.trans: Is the situation beyond repair?

examples.text: Une erreur irrattrapable.
examples.trans: An irreparable mistake.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: La très grande et irremplaçable Arlette.
examples.trans: The great and irreplaceable Arlette.

examples.text: Son aide est irremplaçable.
examples.trans: Her help is irreplaceable.

examples.text: La très grande et irremplaçable Arlette!
examples.trans: The very great and irreplaceable Arlette!

meanings.note: Not acting with proper care or responsibility; same singular spelling for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Tu es complètement irresponsable!
examples.trans: You're completely irresponsible!

examples.text: C'est irresponsable.
examples.trans: It's irresponsible.

examples.text: Ils vont encore dire qu'on est irresponsables.
examples.trans: They're going to say we're irresponsible again.

meanings.note: Du ruban isolant (or du chatterton) is insulating electrical tape.

examples.text: Henri entoure la connexion proprement avec du ruban isolant noir.
examples.trans: Henri wraps the connection neatly with black electrical tape.

examples.text: Ce rideau épais est aussi très isolant contre le froid.
examples.trans: This thick curtain also insulates very well against the cold.

examples.text: C'est l'isolement qui m'intéresse.
examples.trans: It's the isolation that interests me.

examples.text: Il vit dans l'isolement.
examples.trans: He lives in isolation.

meanings.note: Planned path or sequence of stops from one place to another.

examples.text: Nous avons tracé tout l'itinéraire au crayon sur le plan.
examples.trans: We traced the whole route in pencil on the map.

examples.text: Cet itinéraire passe par les plus jolies ruelles de la ville.
examples.trans: This route goes through the prettiest lanes in town.

meanings.note: Masculine noun: des touches en ivoire ('ivory piano keys'). Also used invariable as an off-white colour shade.

examples.text: Ce piano ancien a encore ses touches en ivoire d'origine.
examples.trans: This antique piano still has its original ivory keys.

examples.text: La lumière donne au mur une belle teinte ivoire.
examples.trans: The light gives the wall a lovely ivory tint.

meanings.note: Être ivre = to be drunk. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'drunk'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Tu es ivre, Mathias.
examples.trans: You are drunk, Mathias.

examples.text: Il est complètement ivre.
examples.trans: He is completely drunk.

examples.text: Tu es ivre, Mathias. Je ne t'ai jamais vu ivre!
examples.trans: You are drunk, Mathias. I have never seen you drunk!

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'formerly'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Tu voulais cela jadis.
examples.trans: You wanted that formerly.

examples.text: Tu voulais qu'il me reconnaisse jadis.
examples.trans: You wanted him to acknowledge me once.

meanings.note: La jalousie est stupide. Feminine noun ('la jalousie', plural 'les jalousies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'jealousy'.

examples.text: La jalousie, c'est tellement stupide.
examples.trans: Jealousy is so stupid.

examples.text: Une crise de jalousie.
examples.trans: A fit of jealousy.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'jealous'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je suis jaloux.
examples.trans: I am jealous.

examples.text: Une nature jalouse.
examples.trans: A jealous nature.

examples.text: Je crois que je suis jaloux!
examples.trans: I think that I am jealous!

meanings.note: With ne: je ne mens jamais.

examples.text: Je n'ai jamais vu un acteur aussi exigeant!
examples.trans: I have never seen such a demanding actor!

examples.text: Il ne répond jamais au téléphone pendant le week-end.
examples.trans: He never answers the phone during the weekend.

examples.text: Oh... oh non. Où est ma chaise? J'ai les jambes qui tremblent.
examples.trans: Oh... oh no. Where is my chair? My legs are shaking.

examples.text: Il mord les jambes des traîtres!
examples.trans: He bites traitors' legs!

examples.text: J'ai mal aux jambes.
examples.trans: My legs hurt.

meanings.note: Courtyard or backyard garden.

examples.text: Bon endroit. Deux chaises solides, tournées vers les herbes du jardin et pas vers la fenêtre.
examples.trans: Good spot. Two solid chairs, facing the garden herbs and not the window.

examples.text: Voici le jardin sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the garden on the table.

examples.text: Je jardine le dimanche.
examples.trans: I garden on Sundays.

examples.text: Elle aime jardiner.
examples.trans: She likes gardening.

meanings.note: same form in masculine and feminine

examples.text: L'un est noir et l'autre est jaune.
examples.trans: One is black and the other is yellow.

examples.text: Une fleur jaune.
examples.trans: A yellow flower.

meanings.note: Un club de jazz. Masculine noun ('le jazz', plural 'les —') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'jazz music'.

examples.text: Le club de jazz.
examples.trans: The jazz club.

examples.text: J'adore le jazz.
examples.trans: I love jazz.

examples.text: C'était à New York, au club de jazz où il jouait.
examples.trans: It was in New York, at the jazz club where he was playing.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel.

examples.text: J'ai un loft.
examples.trans: I've got a loft.

examples.text: Je n'ai jamais vu cette boîte en quinze ans!
examples.trans: I have never seen that box in fifteen years!

meanings.note: jeter un coup d'œil = to have a look / glance

examples.text: Je vais jeter un coup d'œil dans le sac.
examples.trans: I'm going to take a look inside the bag.

examples.text: Ne jette rien par terre.
examples.trans: Don't throw anything on the ground.

examples.text: jeter un coup d'œil
examples.trans: to take a quick look

meanings.note: Game or pastime ('jeu de piste' = treasure/scavenger hunt); set of cards or keys.

examples.text: Toute la matinée ressemble à un grand jeu de piste.
examples.trans: The whole morning feels like a grand treasure hunt.

examples.text: Il garde un second jeu de clés derrière le comptoir.
examples.trans: He keeps a spare set of keys behind the counter.

examples.text: Le marché est ouvert le jeudi matin.
examples.trans: The market is open on Thursday mornings.

examples.text: Jeudi, on répare enfin la chaudière.
examples.trans: On Thursday we finally fix the boiler.

meanings.note: Goes before the noun.

examples.text: C'est une jeune femme.
examples.trans: She's a young woman.

examples.text: Il est jeune.
examples.trans: He's young.

meanings.note: La jeunesse = youth / youthfulness. Feminine noun ('la jeunesse', plural 'les jeunesses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'youth'.

examples.text: La jeunesse, c'est notre avenir.
examples.trans: Youth is our future.

examples.text: Les souvenirs de jeunesse.
examples.trans: Memories of youth.

examples.text: J'ai flippé face à ta jeunesse.
examples.trans: I freaked out facing your youth.

meanings.note: A feeling of happiness; plein de joie, full of joy.

examples.text: Quelle joie!
examples.trans: What joy!

examples.text: Elle est pleine de joie.
examples.trans: She's full of joy.

examples.text: Samou était plein de joie, libre!
examples.trans: Samou was full of joy, free!

joindre.gloss: to join, to reach, to contact

meanings.en: to reach, to contact; to join, to attach
meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to join, to reach, to contact'.

examples.text: Elle essaie de vous joindre.
examples.trans: She is trying to reach you.

examples.text: Difficile à joindre.
examples.trans: Difficult to reach.

examples.text: Oui, elle essaie de vous joindre depuis deux jours.
examples.trans: Yes, she has been trying to reach you for two days.

meanings.note: Plumbing joint between two pipes.

examples.text: Tenez cette lampe de poche bien droite sur le joint du tuyau, juste ici.
examples.trans: Hold this flashlight steady on the pipe joint, right here.

examples.text: Voici le joint sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the seal, gasket, pipe joint on the table.

examples.text: C'est une jolie robe.
examples.trans: It's a pretty dress.

examples.text: Vous êtes sûre? Il a l'air joli et bien chaud!
examples.trans: Are you sure? It looks lovely and nice and warm!

examples.text: Elle a des joues roses.
examples.trans: She has pink cheeks.

examples.text: Il faut faire les joues.
examples.trans: The cheeks need doing.

meanings.note: jouer un rôle, jouer le frère de...
Je joue dans un spectacle.
Jouer au foot, jouer du piano.

examples.text: Il joue le frère de Guillaume.
examples.trans: He plays Guillaume's brother.

examples.text: Elle joue dans une pièce.
examples.trans: She's acting in a play.

meanings.note: Feminine: joueuse. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'player, gambler'.

examples.text: C'est un bon joueur.
examples.trans: He is a good player.

examples.text: Je trouve ça drôle. Vous êtes une joueuse, et c'est rare.
examples.trans: I find it funny. You are a gambler, and that is rare.

examples.text: Un jour.
examples.trans: One day.

examples.text: Chaque jour.
examples.trans: Every day.

meanings.en: that very day (used with demonstrative ce: ce jour-là)
meanings.note: Hyphenated -là points back to a specific day in the past or future.

examples.text: Depuis ce jour-là, les deux frères ne s'étaient plus parlé.
examples.trans: Since that day, the two brothers hadn't spoken to each other again.

examples.text: Il pleuvait à verse ce jour-là quand le train est arrivé.
examples.trans: It was pouring rain that day when the train pulled in.

meanings.note: Irregular -al -> -aux plural (les journaux). Du papier journal (no preposition) means 'newspaper / newsprint' used for wrapping fragile goods at market.

examples.text: La marchande emballe chaque assiette dans du papier journal.
examples.trans: The stallholder wraps each plate in newspaper.

examples.text: Odette lit le journal local en buvant son thé.
examples.trans: Odette reads the local newspaper while drinking her tea.

meanings.note: un article de journaliste = a journalist's article

examples.text: La journaliste pose des questions.
examples.trans: The journalist asks questions.

examples.text: Rencontrer une journaliste.
examples.trans: To meet a journalist.

examples.text: La journaliste a seulement parlé de mon esthéticienne!
examples.trans: The journalist only talked about my aesthetician!

meanings.note: the whole day, as time you live through; bonne journée = have a nice day

examples.text: Quelle longue journée à l'hôtel!
examples.trans: What a long day at the hotel!

examples.text: Bonne journée, madame!
examples.trans: Have a good day, madam!

meanings.note: Plural in -x: joyaux. Masculine noun ('le joyau', plural 'les joyaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'jewel'.

examples.text: Un joyau, envié de tous.
examples.trans: A jewel, envied by all.

examples.text: La vérité, c'est que mon agence... C'est une belle boîte. Un joyau, envié de tous.
examples.trans: The truth is that my agency... It's a great company. A jewel, envied by all.

examples.text: Le patron est mort l'hiver dernier, depuis, le joyau est à vendre.
examples.trans: The owner died last winter, since then, the jewel has been for sale.

meanings.note: Le professeur de judo. Masculine noun ('le judo', plural 'les judos') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'judo martial art'.

examples.text: Mon professeur de judo quand j'avais dix ans?
examples.trans: My judo teacher from when I was ten?

examples.text: Il fait du judo depuis cinq ans.
examples.trans: He has been doing judo for five years.

related.gloss: a judo martial art / judo martial arts

meanings.note: Also feminine: une juge. Masculine noun ('le juge', plural 'les juges') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'judge'.

examples.text: Le juge va décider.
examples.trans: The judge will decide.

examples.text: Le juge pourrait lui retirer le permis.
examples.trans: The judge could take away his license.

examples.text: Elle est adressée au juge familial.
examples.trans: It is addressed to the family judge.

meanings.note: Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'opinion, appraisal, judgment'.

examples.text: Des regards de jugement.
examples.trans: Judgmental looks.

examples.text: Comment ça? Des regards de jugement?
examples.trans: How so? Judgmental looks?

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to judge'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'jugé').

examples.text: Personne ne te juge ce soir.
examples.trans: Nobody is judging you tonight.

examples.text: Il juge ce projet très prometteur.
examples.trans: He considers this project very promising.

examples.text: Personne ne te juge, respire un coup.
examples.trans: Nobody is judging you, take a breath.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le juin', plural 'les juins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sixth month'.

examples.text: Le seize juin.
examples.trans: June sixteenth.

examples.text: La prochaine date est le seize juin.
examples.trans: The next date is June sixteenth.

examples.text: Alors, vous voulez le seize juin?
examples.trans: So, do you want June sixteenth?

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'twin'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il ressemble beaucoup à son frère jumeau.
examples.trans: He looks a lot like his twin brother.

examples.text: Les deux sœurs jumelles travaillent dans le cinéma.
examples.trans: The two twin sisters work in cinema.

meanings.note: Un agent junior. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'junior'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est pour quand je serai agent junior!
examples.trans: It is for when I am a junior agent!

examples.text: Il est cadre junior.
examples.trans: He is a junior executive.

examples.text: Je veux être agent junior.
examples.trans: I want to be a junior agent.

meanings.note: porter une jupe = to wear a skirt; tout ce qui porte une jupe = anything in a skirt (colloquial for women)

examples.text: Il se réfugie avec tout ce qui porte une jupe.
examples.trans: He takes refuge with anything wearing a skirt.

examples.text: Elle porte une jupe.
examples.trans: She is wearing a skirt.

meanings.note: An emphatic assurance; it need not refer to a legal oath.
Colours can clash: ces couleurs jurent.

examples.text: Je te jure, c'est vrai.
examples.trans: I swear, it's true.

examples.text: Il jure de ne rien dire.
examples.trans: He swears not to say anything.

examples.text: Je te jure, c'est un film magnifique.
examples.trans: I swear, it's a wonderful film.

meanings.note: to do with the law: le service juridique = the Legal Department

examples.text: Voici le service juridique.
examples.trans: This is the Legal Department.

examples.text: C'est un problème juridique.
examples.trans: It's a legal problem.

examples.text: Un jus d'orange.
examples.trans: An orange juice.

examples.text: Permettez-moi de servir le jus d'orange frais, madame!
examples.trans: Allow me to pour the fresh orange juice, madam!

meanings.note: Jusqu'à demain = until tomorrow.

examples.text: J'attends jusqu'à demain.
examples.trans: I'll wait until tomorrow.

examples.text: Il travaille jusqu'à huit heures.
examples.trans: He works until eight.

meanings.note: Elides to jusqu' before vowels: jusqu'à demain, jusqu'au bout.

examples.text: Je lis le mot: Désolé pour l'erreur. Gardez mon sac bleu jusqu'à vendredi, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Let me read the note: Sorry for the mistake. Please keep my blue bag until Friday.

examples.text: Jusqu'à vendredi? Pas de nom, pas de signature!
examples.trans: Until Friday? No name, no signature!

examples.text: Pourquoi laisser ses chaussures et son train en bois chez des inconnus jusqu'à vendredi?
examples.trans: Why leave one's shoes and wooden train with strangers until Friday?

meanings.en: that far, up to that point; until then, so far
meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'that far'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Il ne fallait pas aller jusque-là.
examples.trans: You shouldn't have gone that far.

examples.text: Jusque-là, tout se passait bien.
examples.trans: Until then, everything was going well.

examples.text: Non. Il ne fallait pas aller jusque-là.
examples.trans: No. You shouldn't have gone that far.

meanings.note: Adverb: je veux juste.
Adjective.

examples.text: Juste là sur votre front, bien au chaud.
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, safe and sound.

examples.text: Sur la cour, juste au-dessus du vieux tilleul. C'est très calme.
examples.trans: The courtyard, right above the old linden tree. It is very quiet.

examples.text: Juste sous cette arche. Je vais monter la valise bleue pour vous.
examples.trans: Right under this archway. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Je pensais justement à vous.
examples.trans: I was just thinking of you.

examples.text: Oh, mon carnet en cuir! Merci! Je le cherchais justement.
examples.trans: Oh, my leather notebook! Thank you! I was just looking for it.

examples.text: Je le cherchais justement.
examples.trans: I was just looking for it.

meanings.note: attaquer en justice = to take legal action, to sue

examples.text: On va attaquer en justice.
examples.trans: We are going to sue in court.

examples.text: Faire confiance à la justice.
examples.trans: To trust the justice system.

examples.text: Mais quand elle est attaquée, je la défends. On va attaquer en justice, et soyez sûrs qu'on gagnera.
examples.trans: But when it is attacked, I defend it. We will sue in court, and be sure we will win.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le karma', plural 'les karmas') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'karma'.

examples.trans: It's bad for my karma to lie to a friend.

examples.text: Avec cette bonne action, tu vas améliorer ton karma.
examples.trans: With this good deed, you're going to improve your karma.

examples.text: Mon karma est mauvais ce mois-ci.
examples.trans: My karma is bad this month.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to enjoy'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'kiffé').

examples.text: On kiffe ce joli moment.
examples.trans: We're loving this lovely moment.

examples.text: On kiffe ce joli moment ensemble.
examples.trans: We are enjoying this lovely moment together.

meanings.note: Everyday clipped form of kilogramme; followed by de without an article: trois kilos de citrons.

examples.text: Il me faut deux kilos de pommes pour la compote.
examples.trans: I need two kilos of apples for the stewed fruit.

examples.text: Ce sac de farine pèse cinq kilos.
examples.trans: This bag of flour weighs five kilos.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le kilomètre', plural 'les kilomètres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'kilometer'.

examples.trans: One hundred fifty kilometers every week.

examples.trans: Do you do many kilometers per week?

examples.text: Oui, environ cent cinquante kilomètres chaque semaine.
examples.trans: Yes, about one hundred fifty kilometers every week.

meanings.en: physiotherapist, physical therapist (colloquial short for kinésithérapeute)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le kiné', plural 'les kinés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'physiotherapist'.

examples.trans: To make an appointment with the physiotherapist.

examples.text: Mon kiné Alexandre sera là aussi.
examples.trans: My physiotherapist Alexandre will be there too.

examples.text: La mort fait partie de la vie.
examples.trans: Death is part of life.

examples.trans: I'll explain to you now. It's in the north, near the lakes.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le lacet', plural 'les lacets') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shoelace'.

examples.text: Donnez vos lacets.
examples.trans: Give your shoelaces.

examples.text: Donnez vos lacets pour le cordon!
examples.trans: Give your shoelaces for the cord!

examples.text: Voici la laine sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the wool on the table.

meanings.note: laisser quelqu'un voir = to let someone see

examples.text: Laissez vos photos ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos here.

examples.text: Laisse-moi parler!
examples.trans: Let me speak!

meanings.note: Du lait d'amande = almond milk.

examples.trans: A coffee with milk.

examples.text: Avec une goutte de lait d'amande.
examples.trans: With a drop of almond milk.

examples.trans: The milkman's van has broken down. Look in the fridge!

examples.text: Voici le laitier sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the milkman, dairy supplier on the table.

meanings.note: En laiton = made of brass.

examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.trans: There is a brass reading lamp in my workshop downstairs.

examples.text: Branche la lampe en laiton d'Henri... oh, regarde cette belle lumière jaune!
examples.trans: Plug in Henri's brass lamp... oh, look at that lovely yellow light!

lame.gloss: slat (of a shutter or floor); blade

meanings.en: wooden slat (of a louvered shutter or floorboard); blade
meanings.note: Covers thin flat strips of wood (*les lames d'un volet*, *les lames du parquet*) as well as knife blades.

examples.text: Peignez chaque petite lame du volet avec le pinceau fin.
examples.trans: Paint each little slat of the shutter with the thin brush.

examples.text: L'air passe doucement entre les lames des volets fermés.
examples.trans: Air passes gently between the slats of the closed shutters.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le lampadaire', plural 'les lampadaires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'street lamp'.

examples.text: Il prend les robes pour des lampadaires.
examples.trans: He takes dresses for lampposts.

examples.text: Il prend les robes pour des lampadaires!
examples.trans: He takes dresses for lampposts!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la lampe', plural 'les lampes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'light fixture'.

examples.text: Il m'a offert une jolie lampe.
examples.trans: He gave me a pretty lamp.

examples.text: Il y a une lampe de lecture en laiton dans mon atelier en bas.
examples.trans: There is a brass reading lamp in my workshop downstairs.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to launch'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'lancé').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to throw'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'lancé').

meanings.en: se lancer: to take the plunge, embark on
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'se lancer: to take the plunge'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'lancé').

examples.text: Tu dois te lancer maintenant, Camille.
examples.trans: You must take the plunge now, Camille.

examples.text: L'agence lance une nouvelle campagne.
examples.trans: The agency launches a new campaign.

meanings.note: Le langage corporel. Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'language, speech'.

examples.text: Adopter le même langage corporel.
examples.trans: To adopt the same body language.

examples.text: Le langage des signes.
examples.trans: Sign language.

examples.text: Je vais lui parler de la PNL et du langage corporel.
examples.trans: I will talk to her about NLP and body language.

meanings.note: Hanging courtyard or street lantern.

examples.text: {M1}, est-ce que tu accroches ces lanternes en papier pour midi?
examples.trans: {M1}, are you hanging those paper lanterns for noon?

examples.text: Regardez ces lanternes dorées sous le ciel du soir, comme c'est paisible!
examples.trans: Look at those golden lanterns against the evening sky, how peaceful!

examples.text: Le public préférerait voir des lapins.
examples.trans: The audience would prefer to see rabbits.

examples.text: Un petit lapin blanc.
examples.trans: A little white rabbit.

meanings.note: False friend: means 'wide', not 'large' (grand).

examples.trans: Careful, Etienne, the pitcher spout is wide!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment large.
examples.trans: This place is really wide, broad.

meanings.note: largement suffisant = more than enough

examples.text: C'est largement suffisant.
examples.trans: That's more than enough.

examples.text: On a largement le temps.
examples.trans: We have plenty of time.

examples.text: C'est largement suffisant. Fantastique!
examples.trans: That's more than enough. Fantastic!

meanings.note: Built from large ('wide').

examples.text: Voici la largeur sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the width on the table.

meanings.en: to dump, drop (a romantic partner); to ditch
meanings.note: Informal/familiar. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to dump'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'largué').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to dump'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'largué').

examples.text: C'est comme se faire larguer.
examples.trans: It's like getting dumped.

examples.text: Elle l'a largué hier soir.
examples.trans: She dumped him last night.

examples.text: C'est comme se faire larguer alors qu'on n'a jamais été ensemble.
examples.trans: It's like getting dumped when you were never even together.

meanings.note: Avoir les larmes aux yeux = have tears in one's eyes.

examples.text: En écoutant le violon, il avait les larmes aux yeux.
examples.trans: Listening to the violin, he had tears in his eyes.

examples.text: Couper des oignons fait toujours venir les larmes.
examples.trans: Chopping onions always brings tears.

meanings.note: Rayon laser. Masculine noun ('le laser', plural 'les lasers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'laser light'.
Jouer au laser. Masculine noun ('le laser', plural 'les lasers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'laser light'.

examples.text: Le laser game est très amusant.
examples.trans: Laser tag is very fun.

examples.text: Un rayon laser rouge.
examples.trans: A red laser beam.

examples.text: Elvis aime bien le laser game.
examples.trans: Elvis likes laser tag.

meanings.note: Jouer au laser game. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'laser tag game', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Viens jouer au laser game!
examples.trans: Come and play laser games!

examples.text: On a fait une partie de laser game.
examples.trans: We played a game of laser tag.

meanings.note: Narrow wooden slat of a park bench, crate, or bed frame.

examples.text: Les lattes du banc viennent d'être repeintes en vert sombre.
examples.trans: The slats of the bench have just been repainted dark green.

examples.text: Une inscription discrète se cache sous la troisième latte.
examples.trans: A discreet inscription hides beneath the third slat.

meanings.en: to wash (windows, dishes, clothes, or hands)
meanings.note: Transitive for objects (laver les vitres); reflexive when washing oneself or part of the body (se laver les mains).

examples.trans: We are going to wash all the tall windowpanes before Friday.

examples.text: Claire lave soigneusement les douze tasses neuves.
examples.trans: Claire carefully washes the twelve new cups.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel
As a direct-object pronoun: le is masculine, la feminine; both become l' before a vowel sound.

examples.text: Le film est fantastique.

examples.text: La pièce de Koltès.
examples.trans: The Koltès play.

meanings.note: As a noun naming the colour, masculine; as an adjective, feminine verte.

examples.text: Un très beau vert.
examples.trans: A very nice green.

examples.text: Elle aime le vert.
examples.trans: She likes green.

examples.text: Vous avez eu du vert?
examples.trans: You got green?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la lecture', plural 'les lectures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'reading'.

examples.text: Il y a une lampe de lecture en laiton dans mon atelier en bas.
examples.trans: There is a brass reading lamp in my workshop downstairs.

examples.text: Le soir, la lecture au salon est très calme.
examples.trans: In the evening, reading in the lounge is very calm.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le lendemain', plural 'les lendemains') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'following day'.

examples.text: Du jour au lendemain.
examples.trans: From one day to the next / overnight.

examples.text: Le lendemain matin.
examples.trans: The next morning.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas disparaître du jour au lendemain.
examples.trans: I do not want to disappear overnight.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'slow'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Le rythme du film est un peu lent.
examples.trans: The pace of the movie is a bit slow.

examples.text: La circulation en ville à midi est toujours lente.
examples.trans: City traffic at noon is always slow.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Le monde s'efface lentement.
examples.trans: The world fades slowly.

examples.text: Parlez plus lentement, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Speak more slowly, please.

examples.text: Toujours là pour t'entendre jouer ta gamme de fa majeur lentement, Thibault!
examples.trans: Still here waiting to hear you play your F-major scale slowly, Thibault!

meanings.note: Named from Latin *lenticula*; optical glass lenses were later named after the biconvex shape of a lentil!

examples.text: Une soupe chaude de lentilles dorées réchauffe tout l'hiver.
examples.trans: A hot soup of golden lentils warms you up all winter.

examples.text: Les lentilles cuisent vite avec une carotte et un peu de thym.
examples.trans: Lentils cook quickly with a carrot and a bit of thyme.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and number with the noun it replaces

examples.text: Il doit y avoir une solution! — Laquelle?
examples.trans: There must be a solution! — Which one?

examples.text: Lequel tu préfères?
examples.trans: Which one do you prefer?

examples.text: Laquelle? On pourrait dire qu'il y a une nouvelle taxe sur les acteurs français?
examples.trans: Which one? Could we say there's a new tax on French actors?

meanings.note: une note de frais = an expense claim
De l'eau fraîche.

examples.text: Mes notes de frais.
examples.trans: My expense claims.

examples.text: Les frais de voyage.
examples.trans: Travel expenses.

examples.text: Pour vérifier mes costumes et mes notes de frais. Bonne chance!
examples.trans: To check my suits and my expense claims. Good luck!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'washed out'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
