examples.text: Je suis lessivée ce soir.
examples.trans: I am exhausted tonight.

examples.text: Je suis lessivée mais tellement heureuse.
examples.trans: I am wiped out but so happy.

meanings.note: Envoyer une lettre.

examples.text: Étienne! Vous êtes tout pâle! Asseyez-vous: qu'est-ce que dit la lettre?
examples.trans: Etienne! You went completely pale! Sit down: what does the letter say?

examples.text: Oh! Avec les valises, la chaudière et la lettre, j'avais complètement oublié!
examples.trans: Oh! With the suitcases, the boiler, and the letter, I had completely forgotten!

meanings.note: Leurs before a plural noun.

examples.text: C'est leur spécialité.
examples.trans: It's their speciality.

examples.text: Ils aiment leurs enfants.
examples.trans: They love their children.

meanings.en: to raise, lift (se lever = to get up, stand up)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'raise'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'levé').

examples.text: Lève-toi maintenant.
examples.trans: Get up now.

examples.text: Grand, manteau gris foncé, il lève les yeux vers l'enseigne de notre hôtel!
examples.trans: Tall, dark grey coat, he is looking up at our hotel sign!

examples.text: lève les yeux
examples.trans: looks up

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le levier', plural 'les leviers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lever'.

examples.text: Il faut un levier solide pour négocier.
examples.trans: One needs solid leverage to negotiate.

examples.text: Pour négocier, il faut un levier solide.
examples.trans: To negotiate, one needs solid leverage.

meanings.en: lesson, educational instruction or piece of advice
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la leçon', plural 'les leçons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lesson'.

examples.text: Une leçon de vie.
examples.trans: A life lesson.

examples.text: Apprendre une leçon.
examples.trans: To learn a lesson.

examples.text: Rappelle-toi la leçon de Samuel Kerr.
examples.trans: Remember the lesson of Samuel Kerr.

meanings.note: Liberté conditionnelle = parole.

examples.text: Tu es en liberté conditionnelle!
examples.trans: You are on parole!

examples.text: Il aime sa liberté.
examples.trans: He loves his freedom.

meanings.note: Same form in masculine and feminine: le libraire / la libraire (false friend: librarian is bibliothécaire).

examples.text: La libraire d'à côté nous apporte souvent le courrier.
examples.trans: The bookshop owner next door often brings us the mail.

examples.text: Demandez conseil à la libraire du quartier.
examples.trans: Ask the neighborhood bookseller for advice.

meanings.note: Shop that sells books (false friend: a lending library is 'une bibliothèque').

examples.text: J'adore flâner dans la petite librairie du coin.
examples.trans: I love browsing in the little corner bookshop.

examples.text: La vitrine de la librairie présente des romans de voyage.
examples.trans: The bookshop window displays travel novels.

meanings.note: Available for an appointment or work.
At liberty; free of charge is gratuit, a different meaning.

examples.text: Elle est libre dans trois semaines.
examples.trans: She's free in three weeks.

examples.text: Tu es libre ce soir?
examples.trans: Are you free tonight?

examples.text: Henri... Claire... dites-moi que la chambre six est libre ce soir, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Henri... Claire... please tell me room six is free tonight.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Je peux bouger librement.
examples.trans: I can move freely.

examples.text: Regardez, je peux bouger librement maintenant.
examples.trans: Look, I can move freely now.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to free'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'libéré').

meanings.en: se libérer: to free oneself, break free, let oneself go
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'se liberer: to free oneself'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'libéré').

examples.text: Ensemble, on se libérait vraiment.
examples.trans: Together, we truly freed ourselves.

examples.text: La police a libéré les otages.
examples.trans: The police freed the hostages.

examples.text: Un rendez-vous s'est libéré demain.
examples.trans: An appointment opened up tomorrow.

meanings.note: lier deux personnes = to bind two people together

examples.text: Ce qui nous lie vraiment.
examples.trans: What truly binds us.

examples.text: Lier une amitié sincère.
examples.trans: To forge a sincere friendship.

examples.text: Je me demande souvent ce qui nous lie.
examples.trans: I often wonder what connects us.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (*du lierre grimpant*). Historically *l'ierre* (from Latin *hedera*) fused its definite article into the word itself!

examples.text: Le lierre vert grimpe autour de la vieille grille en fer.
examples.trans: Green ivy climbs around the old iron gate.

examples.text: Écartez doucement le lierre avant de repeindre le mur.
examples.trans: Gently move the ivy aside before repainting the wall.

meanings.note: In au lieu de, literally in the place of, it forms the expression instead of.

examples.text: Deux cachets au lieu d'un.
examples.trans: Two fees instead of one.

examples.text: Choisissons un lieu calme.
examples.trans: Let's choose a quiet place.

meanings.note: Cosmetic surgery to tighten facial skin.

examples.text: Elles ont toutes le même lifting.
examples.trans: They all have the same facelift.

examples.text: Pas de lifting pour moi!
examples.trans: No facelift for me!

examples.text: Une ligne droite.
examples.trans: A straight line.

examples.text: La ligne est occupée.
examples.trans: The line is busy.

examples.text: Imaginez qu'il y a une ligne invisible entre nous.
examples.trans: Imagine there's an invisible line between us.

meanings.note: Il y a des limites. Feminine noun ('la limite', plural 'les limites') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'limit'.

examples.text: Il y a des limites ici.
examples.trans: There are limits here.

examples.text: Il ne faut pas dépasser les limites.
examples.trans: One must not cross the limits.

examples.text: Oui, mais ce film pousse les limites assez loin.
examples.trans: Yes, but this movie pushes the boundaries quite far.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la limousine', plural 'les limousines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'limousine'.

examples.text: Elle est arrivée en limousine.
examples.trans: She arrived in a limousine.

examples.text: J'ai eu une magnifique limousine blanche.
examples.trans: I had a magnificent white limousine.

meanings.note: Flax plant or crisp woven linen fabric and thread ('fil de lin', 'nappe en lin').

examples.text: Les tables sont dressées avec des nappes en lin écru.
examples.trans: The tables are set with unbleached linen tablecloths.

examples.text: Le carnet ancien est relié avec un fil de lin solide.
examples.trans: The old notebook is bound with strong linen thread.

examples.text: On prend un cours de Lindy Hop.
examples.trans: We are taking a Lindy Hop class.

examples.text: Elle adore danser le Lindy.
examples.trans: She loves dancing the Lindy.

meanings.note: Armoire à linge = linen cupboard.

examples.text: J'apporte des draps blancs propres de l'armoire à linge!
examples.trans: I will bring clean white sheets from the linen cupboard!

examples.text: Voici le linge sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the household linen, laundry on the table.

meanings.note: Fort comme un lion.

examples.text: Toute la puissance d'un lion!
examples.trans: All the power of a lion!

examples.text: Le lion dort.
examples.trans: The lion is sleeping.

meanings.note: a cosmetic treatment that moves fat into the face

examples.text: C'est du lipofilling.
examples.trans: It's lipofilling.

examples.text: Le lipofilling, c'est simple?
examples.trans: Is lipofilling simple?

related.gloss: a fat transfer to the face / fat transfer to the faces

meanings.en: cash (payer en liquide = pay in cash); liquid
meanings.note: At French markets and cafés, payer en liquide or payer en espèces means 'to pay in cash' (as opposed to par carte).

examples.text: Au marché du samedi, il vaut mieux payer en liquide.
examples.trans: At the Saturday market, it is best to pay in cash.

examples.text: Vous préférez régler par carte ou en liquide?
examples.trans: Would you rather pay by card or in cash?

examples.text: Je dois lire le cahier de réservations, mais je ne trouve pas mes lunettes!
examples.trans: I need to read the reservation book, but I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: Je lis le mot: Désolé pour l'erreur. Gardez mon sac bleu jusqu'à vendredi, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Let me read the note: Sorry for the mistake. Please keep my blue bag until Friday.

examples.text: Dix-neuf raisons?! Vous accueillez votre frère ou vous lisez un horaire de train?
examples.trans: Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a train timetable?

meanings.note: Une pâte bien lisse = a smooth dough.

examples.text: Pétrissez jusqu'à ce que la pâte soit souple et lisse.
examples.trans: Knead until the dough is supple and smooth.

examples.text: Après le ponçage, le plateau en bois est tout lisse.
examples.trans: After sanding, the wooden tabletop is completely smooth.

meanings.note: Sur ma liste = on my list.

examples.text: Je fais une liste.
examples.trans: I'm making a list.

examples.text: Le papier marche toujours quand le courant est coupé.
examples.trans: Paper still works when the power goes out.

meanings.note: A bed, the noun; distinct from lit, a form of lire, read.

examples.text: Je suis au lit.
examples.trans: I'm in bed.

examples.text: Le lit est grand.
examples.trans: The bed is big.

examples.text: C'est fait! Et le tapis bleu va juste à côté du lit.
examples.trans: Done! And the blue rug fits right beside the bed.

meanings.note: la lividité cadavérique = post-mortem lividity

examples.text: La lividité cadavérique.
examples.trans: Post-mortem lividity.

examples.text: Une grande lividité.
examples.trans: Great pallor.

examples.text: La lividité cadavérique n'est pas blanche.
examples.trans: Post-mortem lividity is not white.

meanings.en: delivery, handover of goods or letters
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la livraison', plural 'les livraisons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'delivery'.

examples.text: Une livraison très urgente.
examples.trans: A very urgent delivery.

examples.text: Tu appelles le service de livraison?
examples.trans: Are you calling the delivery service?

examples.text: C'est une livraison très urgente.
examples.trans: It is a very urgent delivery.

meanings.note: Masculine un livre means 'a book' (and un livre d'or, literally 'book of gold', is a visitor guestbook); feminine une livre means 'a pound (half a kilo)'.

examples.text: Les clients laissent un petit mot dans le livre d'or de l'hôtel.
examples.trans: Guests leave a short note in the hotel's guestbook.

examples.text: Cette étagère est pleine de vieux livres de cuisine.
examples.trans: This shelf is full of old cookbooks.

meanings.note: Plural in -aux: les locaux.

examples.text: Ils ont loué un local clair au rez-de-chaussée.
examples.trans: They rented a bright ground-floor space.

examples.text: Les chaises pliantes sont rangées dans le petit local.
examples.trans: The folding chairs are stored in the small utility room.

meanings.note: A person who rents rather than owns the home; une locataire for a woman, un locataire for a man.

examples.text: Je suis locataire.
examples.trans: I rent my flat.

examples.text: Le locataire paie le loyer.
examples.trans: The tenant pays the rent.

examples.text: Moi, je n'ai rien. Je suis locataire.
examples.trans: Me, I have nothing. I rent my flat.

meanings.note: Engine at the front of a train.

examples.text: Ouvre le papier blanc... non! La locomotive en bois sculptée par Grand-Père!
examples.trans: Open the white paper... no! The wooden locomotive carved by Grandfather!

examples.text: Voici la locomotive sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the locomotive, train engine on the table.

meanings.note: Borrowed from English.

examples.text: J'ai un petit loft.
examples.trans: I've got a little loft.

examples.text: Un loft à Paris.
examples.trans: A loft in Paris.

meanings.note: être dans sa loge = to be in one's dressing room

meanings.en: box at the theatre or opera
meanings.note: Une loge à l'Opéra.

examples.text: Elle est dans sa loge.
examples.trans: She is in her dressing room.

examples.text: Il attend dans sa loge avant le tournage.
examples.trans: He waits in his dressing room before filming.

related.gloss: to be in one's dressing room

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le logement', plural 'les logements') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'housing'.

examples.text: C'est difficile de trouver un logement pas cher à Paris.
examples.trans: It is hard to find affordable housing in Paris.

examples.text: Elle cherche un nouveau logement près de l'agence.
examples.trans: She is looking for a new flat near the agency.

meanings.note: Takes e before a/o: nous logeons.

examples.text: Je n'arrive pas à croire que vous logez dans le même hôtel, Madame Odette.
examples.trans: I cannot believe you are staying in the exact same hotel, Madam Odette.

examples.text: C'est facile à loger ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to stay, lodge together.

examples.text: Désolée, on a ce nouveau logiciel.
examples.trans: Sorry, we have this new software.

examples.text: Ce logiciel est très simple.
examples.trans: This software is very simple.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la loi.

examples.text: La loi municipale protège le bail des petits cafés de quartier.
examples.trans: Municipal law protects the lease of small neighborhood cafés.

examples.text: Ici, la première loi de la maison, c'est un bon café chaud.
examples.trans: Around here, the first law of the house is a good hot coffee.

meanings.note: Loin de: far from.

examples.text: C'est loin?
examples.trans: Is it far?

examples.text: Et la théière est bien chaude! Tout le monde recule loin de la fenêtre!
examples.trans: And the teapot is piping hot! Everybody step back from the window!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'distant'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un quartier lointain.
examples.trans: A distant neighborhood.

examples.text: Des souvenirs lointains.
examples.trans: Distant memories.

examples.text: Je n'aime pas les arrondissements trop lointains.
examples.trans: I do not like distant arrondissements.

meanings.note: Longue vie! = long life!.

examples.text: Longue vie!
examples.trans: Long life!

examples.text: C'est une longue histoire.
examples.trans: It's a long story.

meanings.note: Il y a longtemps means a long time ago; longtemps alone describes a long duration.

examples.text: C'était il y a longtemps.
examples.trans: It was a long time ago.

examples.text: Tu restes longtemps?
examples.trans: Are you staying long?

examples.text: Dans les vieux immeubles en brique, l'eau met souvent longtemps à monter tout en haut.
examples.trans: In old brick buildings, water often takes a long time to reach the very top.

longuement.gloss: at length, for a long time

meanings.en: at length, for a long time
meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: On en a discuté longuement.
examples.trans: We discussed it at length.

examples.text: On en a longuement discuté.
examples.trans: We discussed it at length.

examples.text: J'en ai longuement discuté avec Colette.
examples.trans: I discussed it at great length with Colette.

meanings.note: Informal, borrowed from English.

examples.text: Elle aime mon look?
examples.trans: Does she like my look?

examples.text: Il a un nouveau look.
examples.trans: He has a new look.

meanings.en: latch, catch (on a door, window, or folding chair)
meanings.note: Final -t is silent (/lɔkɛ/). Refers to a mechanical catch or latch that clicks shut or releases.

examples.text: Appuyez sur le petit loquet pour plier la chaise.
examples.trans: Press the little catch to fold the chair.

examples.text: Le loquet de la fenêtre ferme très bien maintenant.
examples.trans: The window latch closes very smoothly now.

meanings.note: Feminine: loseuse. Masculine noun ('le loser', plural 'les losers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'underdog'.

examples.text: Je suis un loser.
examples.trans: I am a loser.

examples.text: Il pense déjà que je suis un loser.
examples.trans: He already thinks that I am a loser.

meanings.note: Deep long-handled kitchen ladle for serving soup, punch, or broth.

examples.text: Étienne a versé deux grandes louches de jus de citron au lieu de deux cuillères!
examples.trans: Étienne poured in two big ladles of lemon juice instead of two spoons!

examples.text: Elle sert la soupe chaude à l'aide d'une louche en argent.
examples.trans: She serves the hot soup with a silver ladle.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to rent'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'loué').

examples.text: Nous louons un bureau.
examples.trans: We rent an office.

examples.text: Alors pourquoi on ne la loue jamais aux clients?
examples.trans: Then why do we never rent it to guests?

meanings.note: A wolf; the final p is silent.

meanings.en: quand on parle du loup: speak of the devil
meanings.note: In quand on parle du loup, used when the person being discussed appears.

examples.text: Quand on parle du loup!
examples.trans: Speak of the devil!

examples.text: Le loup est dans la forêt.
examples.trans: The wolf is in the forest.

examples.text: Quand on parle du loup… Papa!
examples.trans: Speak of the devil… Dad!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'heavy'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Calme et agréable, merci, mais cette valise semble très lourde aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Quiet and pleasant, thank you, though this suitcase feels very heavy today.

examples.text: Pas étonnant qu'elle soit si lourde. Du bois et du cuir!
examples.trans: No wonder it is so heavy. Wood and leather!

examples.text: Assieds-toi, Thibault, enlève ton manteau lourd et regarde cette valise bleue.
examples.trans: Sit down, Thibault, take off your heavy coat, and look at this blue suitcase.

examples.text: Je parle de dignité et de loyauté.
examples.trans: I'm talking about dignity and loyalty.

examples.text: Sa loyauté est admirable.
examples.trans: Her loyalty is admirable.

meanings.note: Payer le loyer = to pay the rent. Masculine noun ('le loyer', plural 'les loyers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'rent'.

examples.text: Le loyer est cher.
examples.trans: The rent is expensive.

examples.text: Du cabinet du propriétaire de l'immeuble? Étrange, notre loyer est payé jusqu'à l'été prochain.
examples.trans: From the building landlord's office? Strange, our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: Indirect object.
Stressed form: avec lui.

examples.text: Dis-lui merci.
examples.trans: Say thank you to him.

examples.text: Pour lui donner rendez-vous ici vendredi à midi?
examples.trans: Asking him to meet you here Friday at noon?

meanings.note: High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'himself'; clitic forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Il le fait lui-même.
examples.trans: He does it himself.

examples.text: Il peut faire ses cascades lui-même.
examples.trans: He can do his own stunts.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.
French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Cet endroit est tellement lumineux.
examples.trans: This place is so bright.

examples.text: Une idée lumineuse.
examples.trans: A brilliant idea.

examples.text: Oh, j'adore cette immense pièce lumineuse!
examples.trans: Oh, I love this huge, luminous room!

examples.text: Elle attrape bien la lumière.
examples.trans: She catches the light well.

examples.text: Il y a de la lumière.
examples.trans: There's light.

meanings.note: Lundi prochain = next Monday.

examples.text: Lundi prochain?
examples.trans: Next Monday?

examples.text: À lundi!
examples.trans: See you on Monday!

examples.text: Oh, c'est la valise jumelle du train de lundi?
examples.trans: Oh, is that the twin suitcase from Monday's train?

meanings.note: La lune de miel = honeymoon. Feminine noun ('la lune', plural 'les lunes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'moon'.

examples.text: Notre lune de miel commence.
examples.trans: Our honeymoon begins.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas gâcher notre lune de miel.
examples.trans: I do not want to ruin our honeymoon.

examples.text: La lune de miel est terminée.
examples.trans: The honeymoon is over.

meanings.note: Always plural for eyeglasses: des/mes lunettes.

examples.text: Je dois lire le cahier de réservations, mais je ne trouve pas mes lunettes!
examples.trans: I need to read the reservation book, but I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: Pourquoi mes lunettes seraient... oh! Elles sont sur ma tête!
examples.trans: Why would my glasses be... oh! They are on my head!

examples.text: Mon Dieu, quelle confusion! Laissez-moi regarder l'étiquette avec mes lunettes.
examples.trans: Dear me, what a mix-up! Let me look at the tag with my glasses.

meanings.en: making and repair of violins and stringed instruments
meanings.note: Un atelier de lutherie = a luthier's / violin-maker's workshop (from luth, 'lute').

examples.text: L'atelier de lutherie se trouve au numéro dix de la rue.
examples.trans: The violin workshop is at number ten on the street.

examples.text: La lutherie demande du bois sec et beaucoup de patience.
examples.trans: Violin-making requires seasoned wood and great patience.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la lutte', plural 'les luttes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'struggle'.

examples.text: La lutte continue.
examples.trans: The struggle continues.

examples.text: Pourtant, Mathias adore cette lutte acharnée.
examples.trans: Yet, Mathias loves this fierce struggle.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un hôtel luxueux.
examples.trans: A luxurious hotel.

examples.text: Une villa luxueuse.
examples.trans: A luxurious villa.

examples.text: Qui a envoyé ce berceau luxueux?
examples.trans: Who sent this luxurious crib?

meanings.note: masculine despite ending in -ée: le lycée

examples.text: On était au lycée ensemble.
examples.trans: We were in high school together.

examples.text: Nous étions de très bons amis au lycée.
examples.trans: We were very good friends in high school.

examples.text: Personne n'attendait grand-chose de nous au lycée.
examples.trans: Nobody expected much of us in high school.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le lys', plural 'les lys') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lily'.

examples.text: Voici des lys blancs pour toi.
examples.trans: Here are some white lilies for you.

examples.text: Les lys sont magnifiques.
examples.trans: The lilies are magnificent.

meanings.note: être là = to be here, to be present

examples.text: Juste là sur votre front, bien au chaud.
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, safe and sound.

examples.text: Regardez la fermeture éclair... oui, ses initiales sont juste là!
examples.trans: Check the zipper... yes, her initials are right here!

examples.text: À droite, près du bureau, là où la lumière est bonne.
examples.trans: On the right, near the desk, where the light is good.

examples.text: Donc je veux vraiment tourner là-bas.
examples.trans: So I really want to shoot over there.

examples.text: Qui est là-bas?
examples.trans: Who is over there?

examples.text: Comment on va parler avec eux là-bas?
examples.trans: How are we going to talk with them in there?

meanings.note: Inside that box, room, or bag.

examples.text: Qu'est-ce qui peut bien se cacher là-dedans?
examples.trans: What on earth could be hiding in there?

examples.text: Rangez les cartes là-dedans pour qu'elles restent bien plates.
examples.trans: Put the maps in there so they stay nice and flat.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'on that'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Nous sommes tout à fait d'accord là-dessus.
examples.trans: We completely agree on that point.

examples.text: Tu peux compter sur moi là-dessus.
examples.trans: You can count on me on that score.

meanings.note: Spoken French lao expression meaning 'up there', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Regardez, il y a une fenêtre là-haut!
examples.trans: Look, there's a window up there!

examples.text: Qui habite là-haut?
examples.trans: Who lives up there?

examples.text: Il y a même un vrai lit là-haut?
examples.trans: Is there even a proper bed up there?

meanings.note: Un plan lâche = a cowardly plan.
Same form in masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Tu es un lâche.
examples.trans: You're a coward.

examples.text: Ne sois pas lâche!
examples.trans: Don't be a coward!

examples.text: Tu es un menteur et un lâche. Je sais que c'est à cause de mon âge.
examples.trans: You're a liar and a coward. I know it's because of my age.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Ils nous trahissent lâchement.
examples.trans: They betray us cowardly.

examples.text: Tes associés te trahissent lâchement.
examples.trans: Your partners betray you cowardly.

meanings.en: to let go of, to drop
meanings.note: Informal.
Informal.

examples.text: Lâche le contrat!
examples.trans: Let go of the contract!

examples.text: Ne lâche pas!
examples.trans: Don't give up!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la lèvre', plural 'les lèvres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lip'.

examples.text: J'ai trop froid, mes lèvres se bloquent.
examples.trans: I am too cold, my lips are locking up.

examples.text: Un sourire sur les lèvres.
examples.trans: A smile on the lips.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'statutory'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est mon droit légal le plus strict.
examples.trans: It is my strictest legal right.

examples.text: Peut-être, mais c'est mon droit légal.
examples.trans: Maybe, but it is my legal right.

examples.text: Quels sont les risques légaux?
examples.trans: What are the legal risks?

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'legendary'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Des couples légendaires travaillaient ensemble.
examples.trans: Legendary couples worked together.

examples.text: Une créature légendaire.
examples.trans: A legendary creature.

examples.text: C'est ridicule. Une actrice légendaire!
examples.trans: It is ridiculous. A legendary actress!

meanings.note: Explanatory caption under a drawing or key on a map; traditional legend.

examples.text: Une courte légende à l'encre précise la date du croquis.
examples.trans: A brief ink caption notes the date of the sketch.

examples.text: Regardez la légende en bas de la carte pour lire les symboles.
examples.trans: Check the key at the bottom of the map to read the symbols.

meanings.note: Masculine léger (/leʒe/) has a silent -r; feminine légère (/leʒɛʁ/) adds a grave accent and pronounces the final -r.

examples.text: Sans les livres dessus, le meuble devient beaucoup plus léger.
examples.trans: Without the books on it, the piece of furniture becomes much lighter.

examples.text: Ces chaises pliantes sont solides mais très légères à porter.
examples.trans: These folding chairs are sturdy yet very light to carry.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le légume', plural 'les légumes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'vegetable'.

examples.text: Il mange beaucoup de légumes.
examples.trans: He eats a lot of vegetables.

examples.text: On peut encore commander des légumes!
examples.trans: We can still order vegetables!

examples.text: Il a même fini toute sa soupe de légumes avant de monter.
examples.trans: He even finished all his vegetable soup before going up.

meanings.note: To a slight degree, gently, or lightly.

examples.text: Penchez légèrement la fiche vers la lumière de la fenêtre.
examples.trans: Tilt the card slightly toward the window light.

examples.text: Les amandes sont légèrement dorées au four.
examples.trans: The almonds are lightly browned in the oven.

meanings.en: macaron, a small round almond biscuit

examples.text: Un macaron à la pistache.
examples.trans: A pistachio macaron.

examples.text: J'adore les macarons.
examples.trans: I love macarons.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le machin', plural 'les machins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'thing'.

examples.text: Passe-moi ce machin.
examples.trans: Pass me that thingy.

examples.text: Un drôle de machin.
examples.trans: A strange gizmo.

examples.text: La scène où la femme coupe le machin de l'homme.
examples.trans: The scene where the woman cuts off the man's thing.

meanings.note: Une machine de sport. Feminine noun ('la machine', plural 'les machines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'machine'.

examples.text: Une machine à laver.
examples.trans: A washing machine.

examples.text: Donne-moi le lait d'abord pour la machine à café.
examples.trans: Give me the milk first for the coffee machine.

examples.text: Tu es une héroïne, Claire! Donne-moi le lait d'abord pour la machine à café.
examples.trans: You are a hero, Claire! Give me the milk first for the coffee machine.

meanings.note: Bonjour, madame.
Abbreviated Mme.

examples.text: Merci, madame.
examples.trans: Thank you, madam.

examples.text: Madame Odette, tout va bien? Vous avez sonné!
examples.trans: Madam Odette, is everything alright? You rang the bell!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la mademoiselle', plural 'les mesdemoiselles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'Miss'.

examples.text: Bonjour, mademoiselle.
examples.trans: Hello, Miss.

examples.text: Faites entrer mademoiselle Schneck.
examples.trans: Show Miss Schneck in.

examples.text: Par ici, mademoiselle, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: This way, miss, please.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la mafia', plural 'les mafias') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mafia'.
Feminine noun ('la mafia', plural 'les mafias') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'organized crime syndicate'.

examples.text: Les nounous à Paris, c'est une mafia!
examples.trans: Nannies in Paris are a mafia!

examples.text: Une véritable mafia contrôle ce secteur.
examples.trans: A real mafia controls this sector.

meanings.note: Note the false friend: un magasin is a retail store, whereas an English 'magazine' is un magazine (/maɡazin/) or une revue.

examples.text: Le magasin de meubles livre gratuitement dans le quartier.
examples.trans: The furniture shop delivers free of charge in the neighbourhood.

examples.text: Tous les petits magasins de la place ouvrent à neuf heures.
examples.trans: All the small shops on the square open at nine o'clock.

examples.text: La couverture d'un grand magazine.
examples.trans: The cover of a big magazine.

examples.text: Je lis un magazine.
examples.trans: I'm reading a magazine.

examples.text: Elle fera la couverture d'un grand magazine!
examples.trans: She'll be on the cover of a big magazine!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le magicien', plural 'les magiciens') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'magician'.
Masculine noun ('le magicien', plural 'les magiciens') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'miracle worker'.

examples.text: J'avais l'impression d'être une magicienne.
examples.trans: I felt like I was a magician.

examples.text: Le magicien a fait disparaître la carte.
examples.trans: The magician made the card disappear.

examples.text: J'étais assistant pour un magicien!
examples.trans: I was assistant to a magician!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la magie', plural 'les magies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'magic'.

examples.text: La magie du cinéma opère toujours.
examples.trans: Cinema magic always works.

examples.text: Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Une ambiance magique.
examples.trans: A magical atmosphere.

examples.text: Un moment magique.
examples.trans: A magical moment.

examples.text: Dans quel hôtel magique es-tu tombé par hasard, petit frère?
examples.trans: What kind of magical hotel did you stumble into, little brother?

meanings.note: Splendid, breathtaking, wonderful.

examples.text: Quelle vue magnifique sur les toits de la vieille ville!
examples.trans: What a magnificent view over the rooftops of the old town!

examples.text: Le tilleul en fleurs offre un spectacle magnifique.
examples.trans: The blooming linden tree is a magnificent sight.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Une actrice tellement magnétique.
examples.trans: An actress so magnetic.

examples.text: Cette actrice est tellement magnétique et élégante.
examples.trans: That actress is so magnetic and elegant.

meanings.note: Months are masculine and never capitalised in French: en mai ('in May'), le dix mai ('on the tenth of May', using cardinal dix).

examples.text: Le tilleul de la cour commence à fleurir fin mai.
examples.trans: The linden tree in the courtyard begins to bloom in late May.

examples.text: La carte postale est datée du dix mai.
examples.trans: The postcard is dated the tenth of May.

meanings.note: En maillot de bain = in a swimsuit.

examples.text: Des maillots de bain autour de la piscine.
examples.trans: Swimsuits around the swimming pool.

examples.text: Il porte un maillot bleu.
examples.trans: He is wearing a blue jersey.

examples.text: Une ambiance sexy, des maillots de bain... La petite Mathurine est superbe!
examples.trans: A sexy atmosphere, swimsuits... Little Mathurine is gorgeous!

meanings.en: a hand, help (un coup de main)

examples.text: Lave-toi les mains.
examples.trans: Wash your hands.

examples.text: Elle a un stylo à la main.
examples.trans: She has a pen in her hand.

examples.text: Tu peux commencer maintenant?
examples.trans: Can you start now?

examples.text: Je pars maintenant.
examples.trans: I'm leaving now.

maintenir.gloss: to hold, to keep in place

meanings.en: to hold, to keep (in a position)
meanings.note: conjugated like 'tenir': maintenez la porte fermée

examples.text: Maintenez la porte fermée.
examples.trans: Hold the door closed.

examples.text: Il maintient sa décision.
examples.trans: He stands by his decision.

examples.text: Maintenez la porte fermée et tirez les rideaux.
examples.trans: Hold the door closed and draw the curtains.

meanings.note: Head of a municipality. Masculine noun ('le maire', plural 'les maires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mayor'.

examples.text: Je dois parler au maire.
examples.trans: I have to speak to the mayor.

examples.text: Monsieur le maire est occupé.
examples.trans: Mr. Mayor is busy.

examples.text: Je dois y aller, je dois parler au maire.
examples.trans: I have to go, I have to speak to the mayor.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la mairie', plural 'les mairies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'town hall'.

examples.text: On va à la mairie demain.
examples.trans: We are going to town hall tomorrow.

examples.text: Attends, Thibault: tu travailles toujours au service des contrats de la mairie?!
examples.trans: Wait, Thibault: you still work at City Hall's contract office?!

meanings.note: Mais oui! = of course!.

examples.text: L'extérieur est identique, oui! Mais regardez à l'intérieur!
examples.trans: The outside is identical, yes! But look inside!

examples.text: Ce n'est pas votre faute. Mais je n'ai que le manteau sur mon dos!
examples.trans: It is not your fault. Still, I only have the coat on my back!

meanings.note: À la maison = at home. Feminine noun ('la maison', plural 'les maisons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'house'.

examples.text: Une belle maison.
examples.trans: A beautiful house.

examples.text: Il y a vingt-cinq ans? Dans cette même maison?
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago? In that same house?

examples.text: Alors la maison dit bonjour toute seule?
examples.trans: So the house says hello on its own?

meanings.note: Fa majeur = F major.

examples.text: Toujours là pour t'entendre jouer ta gamme de fa majeur lentement, Thibault!
examples.trans: Still here waiting to hear you play your F-major scale slowly, Thibault!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment majeur.
examples.trans: This place is really major.

meanings.note: L'actionnaire majoritaire. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'dominant'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: L'actionnaire majoritaire.
examples.trans: The majority shareholder.

examples.text: Monsieur Janowski, vous êtes actionnaire majoritaire d'ASK avec soixante pour cent.
examples.trans: Mr. Janowski, you are majority shareholder of ASK with sixty percent.

examples.text: Je suis l'actionnaire majoritaire.
examples.trans: I am the majority shareholder.

meanings.note: Used after an action: mal réagir means to react badly.
As a masculine noun: le mal, les maux.

examples.text: J'ai mal à la tête.
examples.trans: I have a headache.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas te faire de mal.
examples.trans: I don't want to hurt you.

meanings.note: same form in masculine and feminine

examples.text: Dis que je suis malade.
examples.trans: Say that I'm ill.

examples.text: Il est tombé malade.
examples.trans: He fell ill.

examples.text: Avoir des enfants, ce n'est pas une maladie!
examples.trans: Having children isn't an illness!

examples.text: C'est une maladie rare.
examples.trans: It's a rare disease.

examples.text: Mathias, avoir des enfants, ce n'est pas une maladie!
examples.trans: Mathias, having children isn't an illness!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la malchance', plural 'les malchances') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bad luck'.

examples.text: C'est une terrible malchance.
examples.trans: It is terrible bad luck.

examples.text: C'est vraiment une terrible malchance.
examples.trans: It is really terrible bad luck.

examples.text: C'était juste un malentendu.
examples.trans: It was just a misunderstanding.

examples.text: Il y a un malentendu.
examples.trans: There is a misunderstanding.

meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'despite', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Malgré l'ordre d'arrêter.
examples.trans: Despite the order to stop.

examples.text: Réussir malgré les difficultés.
examples.trans: To succeed despite the difficulties.

examples.text: Jean continue de jouer malgré l'ordre d'arrêter.
examples.trans: Jean continues to act despite the order to stop.

meanings.note: Porter malheur means bring bad luck, as in a superstition.
A misfortune or unfortunate event; plural malheurs.

examples.text: Ça porte malheur.
examples.trans: It brings bad luck.

examples.text: Quel malheur!
examples.trans: How awful!

examples.text: On n'offre pas du vert à une actrice. Ça porte malheur.
examples.trans: You don't give green to an actress. It brings bad luck.

meanings.note: Opposite: heureusement.

examples.text: Pas de numéro de téléphone, malheureusement. Seulement deux initiales et un vieux nom de rue.
examples.trans: No phone number, unfortunately. Only two initials and an old street name.

examples.text: Pas de numéro de téléphone, malheureusement.
examples.trans: No phone number, unfortunately.

meanings.note: The opposite of honnête, honest; here Andréa accuses Françoise of being unfair or dishonest.

examples.text: C'est tellement malhonnête!
examples.trans: That's so dishonest!

examples.text: Un homme malhonnête.
examples.trans: A dishonest man.

examples.text: C'est tellement malhonnête! Elle avait déjà pris sa décision.
examples.trans: That's so dishonest! She'd already made her decision.

meanings.note: Feminine is *maligne* (`/maliɲ/`). Exclaimed alone (*Malin!*), it praises a neat, practical trick.

examples.text: C'est très malin d'ajouter une goutte de vinaigre dans l'eau!
examples.trans: It's very smart to add a drop of vinegar to the water!

examples.text: Elle a trouvé une astuce maligne pour plier toutes les chaises.
examples.trans: She found a clever trick to fold all the chairs.

meanings.note: Describes something unhealthy or an unhealthy atmosphere.

examples.text: C'est malsain.
examples.trans: It's unhealthy.

examples.text: Une ambiance malsaine.
examples.trans: An unhealthy atmosphere.

examples.text: Trois mois, Camille! C'est malsain.
examples.trans: Three months, Camille! It's unhealthy.

meanings.note: Used without an article when speaking of one's own mother inside the family (*Maman nous faisait laver les vitres*).

examples.text: Maman préparait toujours une grande tarte le dimanche midi.
examples.trans: Mom always made a big tart for Sunday lunch.

examples.text: J'appelle maman ce soir pour lui raconter la nouvelle.
examples.trans: I'm calling Mom tonight to tell her the news.

examples.text: Merci, Mamie.
examples.trans: Thank you, Gran.

examples.text: Je vais chez ma mamie.
examples.trans: I'm going to my grandma's.

meanings.note: Gender pair to remember: feminine *la manche* is a clothing sleeve; masculine *le manche* is a tool/pan handle.

examples.text: Retroussons nos manches avant de laver les grandes vitres.
examples.trans: Let's roll up our sleeves before washing the tall windows.

examples.text: Attention à ne pas mettre de peinture sur ta manche blanche!
examples.trans: Be careful not to get paint on your white sleeve!

meanings.note: nous mangeons keeps the 'e' for the soft g sound

examples.text: Elles mangent des graines.
examples.trans: They eat seeds.

examples.text: On mange ensemble à midi?
examples.trans: Shall we eat together at noon?

meanings.note: Une manifestation culturelle.
Une manifestation culturelle.

examples.text: Elle va organiser des manifestations!
examples.trans: She's going to organize protests!

examples.text: Il y a une manifestation dans la rue.
examples.trans: There is a protest in the street.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la manigance', plural 'les manigances') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'underhand scheme'.

examples.text: Des manigances en coulisses.
examples.trans: Underhand scheming behind the scenes.

examples.text: Déjouer une manigance.
examples.trans: To foil a scheme.

examples.text: Et vous avec vos petites manigances?
examples.trans: And what about you with your little schemes?

meanings.en: to plot, scheme behind someone's back
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to scheme'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'manigancé').

examples.text: Il a tout manigancé.
examples.trans: He engineered everything.

examples.text: C'est Andréa qui a tout manigancé.
examples.trans: It is Andréa who engineered everything.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le manipulateur', plural 'les manipulateurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'manipulator'.

examples.text: Tu es un manipulateur.
examples.trans: You are a manipulator.

examples.text: Tu es devenu un simple manipulateur.
examples.trans: You have become a mere manipulator.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to manipulate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'manipulé').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to manipulate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'manipulé').

examples.text: Il manipule tout le monde.
examples.trans: He manipulates everyone.

examples.text: Manipuler avec soin.
examples.trans: Handle with care.

examples.text: C'est Mathias. Il manipule tout le monde.
examples.trans: That's Mathias. He manipulates everyone.

meanings.note: De manière + adj = in a ... manner. Feminine noun ('la manière', plural 'les manières') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'way'.

examples.text: Agissez de manière responsable!
examples.trans: Act in a responsible manner!

examples.text: Une étrange manière d'agir.
examples.trans: A strange way of acting.

examples.text: Si, mais pas de cette manière.
examples.trans: Yes, but not this way.

meanings.note: Un grand mannequin = a top model. Masculine noun ('le mannequin', plural 'les mannequins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fashion model'.

examples.text: Je pensais que tu étais mannequin.
examples.trans: I thought you were a model.

examples.text: Travailler comme mannequin.
examples.trans: To work as a model.

examples.text: C'est le mannequin Aymeline Val.
examples.trans: That is the model Aymeline Val.

meanings.note: Absent from its expected place ('la pièce manquante' = the missing piece).

examples.text: Voici enfin la carte manquante de la collection!
examples.trans: Here at last is the missing card from the collection!

examples.text: Il a retrouvé le bouton manquant au fond du tiroir.
examples.trans: He found the missing button at the back of the drawer.

related.gloss: to get back, recover, find again

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le manque', plural 'les manques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lack'.

examples.text: C'est un manque de respect total.
examples.trans: It is a complete lack of respect.

examples.text: Un manque d'attention peut coûter cher.
examples.trans: A lack of attention can be costly.

examples.text: Il nous manque 6 millions.
examples.trans: We are missing 6 millions.

meanings.en: to be missed by (tu me manques = I miss you)
meanings.note: back to front: the person missed is the subject

examples.text: Tu me manques.
examples.trans: I miss you.

examples.text: Paris me manque.
examples.trans: I miss Paris.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le manteau', plural 'les manteaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'coat'.

examples.text: Elles sont dans la poche de votre manteau?
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

examples.text: Ce n'est pas votre faute. Mais je n'ai que le manteau sur mon dos!
examples.trans: It is not your fault. Still, I only have the coat on my back!

examples.text: Voici une serviette sèche pour votre manteau et un bol de soupe chaude, monsieur.
examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat and a bowl of hot soup, sir.

meanings.note: Un manuel scolaire / un manuel d'impôts.

examples.text: Ne lisez pas votre accueil comme un vieux manuel!
examples.trans: Don't read your welcome like an old textbook!

examples.text: Le manuel explique comment régler le minuteur du four.
examples.trans: The manual explains how to set the oven timer.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le maquillage', plural 'les maquillages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'makeup'.

examples.text: Venez au maquillage.
examples.trans: Come to makeup.

examples.text: Pascal a demandé un maquillage complet.
examples.trans: Pascal asked for full-body makeup.

examples.text: Venez vous installer au maquillage.
examples.trans: Come and sit down in makeup.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to apply makeup to'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'maquillé').

examples.text: Nous devons maquiller l'actrice.
examples.trans: We must apply makeup to the actress.

examples.text: Nous devons maquiller tout votre corps.
examples.trans: We have to do your whole body with makeup.

examples.text: Pourquoi maquiller mon corps entier?
examples.trans: Why put makeup on my entire body?

meanings.note: monter les marches = to climb the stairs

examples.text: Monter les marches du festival.
examples.trans: To climb the steps of the festival.

examples.text: Une marche d'escalier.
examples.trans: A staircase step.

examples.text: Attendez. Regardez en bas sur la marche en pierre.
examples.trans: Wait. Look down on the stone step.

meanings.note: Travel on foot.
For a machine or plan, function or work; ça marche can also signal agreement.

examples.text: Il marche très bien.
examples.trans: It's working fine.

examples.text: Je marche jusqu'à l'agence.
examples.trans: I walk to the agency.

examples.text: Ça marche!
examples.trans: Okay, deal!

meanings.note: Le marché local. Masculine noun ('le marché', plural 'les marchés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'market'.
Marché conclu = deal / agreed. Masculine noun ('le marché', plural 'les marchés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'market'.

examples.text: Marché conclu!
examples.trans: Deal!

examples.text: Je vais au marché.
examples.trans: I am going to the market.

examples.text: Le café de mes rêves — juste ici dans notre propre cour! Attendez que je le dise à toute la rue!
examples.trans: My dream café—right here in our own courtyard! Wait until I tell the whole street!

meanings.note: No article for 'on Tuesday': mardi.

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday.

examples.text: Mardi, j'ai une réunion.
examples.trans: On Tuesday I have a meeting.

meanings.note: Blank border around the edge of a page or map; leeway ('marge de manœuvre').

examples.text: Une note au crayon est inscrite dans la marge du livre.
examples.trans: A penciled note is written in the margin of the book.

examples.text: Laissez une petite marge blanche tout autour du dessin.
examples.trans: Leave a narrow white margin all around the drawing.

meanings.note: A man in relation to the person he is married to.

examples.text: Mon mari travaille avec Samuel.
examples.trans: My husband works with Samuel.

examples.text: Voici son mari.
examples.trans: This is her husband.

meanings.note: demander quelqu'un en mariage = to propose to someone

examples.text: Alors il te demandera en mariage.
examples.trans: Then he'll ask you to marry him.

examples.text: Un beau mariage à l'église.
examples.trans: A beautiful church wedding.

examples.text: Alors, notre mariage est bien terminé.
examples.trans: So, our marriage is truly over.

meanings.note: Marier quelqu’un = marry someone to another person; se marier avec = get married to someone.

meanings.en: marier = to marry off, to perform a wedding

examples.text: Il veut peut-être se marier avec elle!
examples.trans: Maybe he wants to marry her!

examples.text: Ils vont se marier en juin.
examples.trans: They're getting married in June.

examples.text: J'aimais la vie et les artistes, lui voulait se marier.
examples.trans: I loved life and artists, he wanted to get married.

meanings.en: sea, marine (*du sel marin* = sea salt)
meanings.note: Also gives the invariable color phrase *bleu marine* ('navy blue').

examples.text: Une pincée de sel marin relève même les gâteaux au chocolat.
examples.trans: A pinch of sea salt brightens even chocolate cakes.

examples.text: L'air marin donne faim après une longue promenade.
examples.trans: Sea air gives you an appetite after a long walk.

meanings.note: Être marié(e) avec quelqu'un.

examples.text: Mathias est marié.
examples.trans: Mathias is married.

examples.text: Elle est mariée.
examples.trans: She is married.

meanings.note: Une grande marmite de soupe = a big pot of soup.

examples.text: La soupe de lentilles mijote dans la grande marmite.
examples.trans: The lentil soup is simmering in the big pot.

examples.text: Chauffez un filet d'huile d'olive au fond de la marmite.
examples.trans: Warm a drizzle of olive oil at the bottom of the pot.

meanings.note: Engraved or drawn mark, token, or bookmark ('marque-page'); maker's brand.

examples.text: Le tailleur de pierre a laissé sa marque sur l'arche.
examples.trans: The stonemason left his mark on the arch.

examples.text: Une discrète marque à la craie indique le bon tiroir.
examples.trans: A discreet chalk mark shows the right drawer.

meanings.note: Marqué en rouge = marked in red. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to mark'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'marqué').
Marquer un but. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to mark'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'marqué').

examples.text: Les jours sont marqués en rouge.
examples.trans: The days are marked in red.

examples.text: Marquer un point.
examples.trans: To score a point.

examples.text: Les jours de tournage sont marqués en rouge.
examples.trans: The shooting days are marked in red.

meanings.note: A feminine noble title; masculine marquis.

examples.text: Elle joue la marquise.
examples.trans: She plays the marchioness.

examples.text: La marquise entre dans le salon.
examples.trans: The marchioness enters the drawing room.

meanings.en: en avoir marre (de) = to be fed up (with), to be sick of
meanings.note: Casual everyday idiom.

examples.text: J'en ai marre.
examples.trans: I'm fed up.

examples.text: Elle en a marre d'attendre.
examples.trans: She is sick of waiting.

meanings.note: Invariable adjective: des chaussures marron.

examples.text: Deux paires de grandes chaussures marron pour homme et des pulls gris.
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes and grey sweaters.

examples.text: Attendez: à qui est ce petit carnet en cuir marron sur le comptoir?
examples.trans: Wait: whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le mars', plural 'les mars') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'March'.

examples.text: Elle joue au théâtre en mars.
examples.trans: She performs at the theater in March.

examples.text: Tu joues Hamlet en mars prochain?
examples.trans: You are playing Hamlet next March?

meanings.en: hammer (workshop tool, or felt hammer inside a piano)
meanings.note: Plural *des marteaux*; in an upright or grand piano, each key drives a small wooden *marteau* padded with wool felt.

examples.text: Chaque touche du piano soulève un petit marteau en bois.
examples.trans: Each piano key lifts a small wooden hammer.

examples.text: Passez-moi le petit marteau et deux clous fins.
examples.trans: Hand me the small hammer and two thin nails.

related.gloss: string (of a piano or violin); rope
key (of a piano or keyboard), button

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le masque', plural 'les masques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mask'.

examples.text: Garde ton visage comme un masque.
examples.trans: Keep your face like a mask.

examples.text: L'acteur porte un masque de comédie.
examples.trans: The actor wears a comedy mask.

examples.text: Garde le visage calme comme un masque.
examples.trans: Keep your face calm like a mask.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to mask'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'masqué').

examples.text: Le maquillage masque les traits de la doublure.
examples.trans: The makeup conceals the features of the stand-in.

examples.text: L'éclairage masque tous les traits.
examples.trans: The lighting conceals all features.

meanings.note: A physical treatment or massage; a masculine noun.

examples.text: Réservez-moi un massage.
examples.trans: Book me a massage.

examples.text: Un massage, ça fait du bien.
examples.trans: A massage does you good.

examples.text: Réservez-moi un massage, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Book me a massage, please.

meanings.note: Bois / chêne massif = solid wood / oak; f. massive.

examples.text: Du chêne massif, quatre-vingts ans d'âge. Pas une seule fuite.
examples.trans: Solid oak, eighty years old. Not a single leak.

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment massif.
examples.trans: This place is really solid, massive.

meanings.note: Un match de football. Masculine noun ('le match', plural 'les matchs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'match'.

examples.text: J'ai des billets pour le match.
examples.trans: I have tickets for the match.

examples.text: Regarder le match.
examples.trans: To watch the match.

examples.text: J'ai des billets pour le match du PSG!
examples.trans: I have tickets for the PSG match!

meanings.note: être à la maternité = to be in the maternity ward

examples.text: Elle est à la maternité.
examples.trans: She is at the maternity clinic.

examples.text: Le congé de maternité.
examples.trans: Maternity leave.

examples.text: Mais si, tu es à la maternité!
examples.trans: Oh yes, you are in the maternity ward!

meanings.note: Du matin = a.m., in the morning.

examples.text: À quatre heures du matin.
examples.trans: At four in the morning.

examples.text: Je travaille le matin.
examples.trans: I work in the mornings.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'morning'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Votre visite matinale me touche.
examples.trans: Your morning visit touches me.

examples.text: Il fait une promenade matinale.
examples.trans: He goes for a morning walk.

examples.text: Votre visite matinale me touche sincèrement.
examples.trans: Your morning visit touches me sincerely.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la matinée', plural 'les matinées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'morning duration'.

examples.text: J'ai travaillé toute la matinée.
examples.trans: I worked all morning.

examples.text: Une belle matinée.
examples.trans: A lovely morning.

examples.text: Avec plaisir! Bonne matinée, madame.
examples.trans: Gladly! Enjoy your morning, madam.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la matière', plural 'les matières') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'material'.
Feminine noun ('la matière', plural 'les matières') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'subject matter'.

examples.text: Le réalisateur manque encore de matière.
examples.trans: The director still lacks footage.

examples.text: Il n'y a pas matière à s'inquiéter.
examples.trans: There is no reason to worry.

examples.text: Le réalisateur manque encore de matière pour monter.
examples.trans: The director still lacks footage for editing.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'grown-up'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un texte mature.
examples.trans: A mature text.

examples.text: Un comportement mature.
examples.trans: Mature behavior.

examples.text: Je trouve son écriture particulièrement mature.
examples.trans: I find his writing particularly mature.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le matériel', plural 'les matériels') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'equipment'.

examples.text: Vous pouvez décharger le matériel.
examples.trans: You can unload the equipment.

examples.text: Le matériel pour la fête est arrivé.
examples.trans: The equipment for the party has arrived.

examples.text: Vous pouvez déposer le matériel dans la rue.
examples.trans: You can drop off the equipment in the street.

meanings.note: usually before the noun: une mauvaise nouvelle
Être mauvais en sport.

examples.text: C'est une mauvaise idée.
examples.trans: It's a bad idea.

examples.text: Je suis mauvaise en maths.
examples.trans: I'm bad at maths.

meanings.note: Highest possible level, temperature, or amount; au maximum means 'at full heat/power' or 'at most'.

examples.text: Trois heures de l'après-midi?! Thibault, allume les deux fours au maximum cette seconde!
examples.trans: Three in the afternoon?! Thibault, turn both ovens up to full heat this second!

examples.text: La salle peut accueillir trente personnes au maximum.
examples.trans: The room can hold thirty people at most.

meanings.en: master, ruler; maître à bord = in charge
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le maître', plural 'les maîtres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'master'.

examples.text: Tu seras maître à bord.
examples.trans: You will be in charge.

examples.text: Tu vas être maître à bord ici.
examples.trans: You are going to be in charge here.

meanings.note: For a dog: voilà ta maîtresse.

examples.text: Regarde, voilà ta maîtresse.
examples.trans: Look, here's your owner.

examples.text: La maîtresse est gentille.
examples.trans: The teacher is nice.

meanings.note: Before the verb; m' before a vowel.

examples.text: Vous me sauvez tout mon séjour, tous les deux.
examples.trans: You two are saving my whole stay.

examples.text: Exactement ce qu'il me faut. Où est l'escalier?
examples.trans: Just what I need. Where are the stairs?

meanings.note: Un mec bien = a good guy. Masculine noun ('le mec', plural 'les mecs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'guy'.

examples.text: Le mec est un génie?
examples.trans: The guy is a genius?

examples.text: C'est un mec sympa.
examples.trans: He's a nice guy.

examples.text: Le mec est un génie? Un canard géant, de la mauvaise musique... Ouais, un vrai génie!
examples.trans: The guy is a genius? A giant duck, bad music... Yeah, a real genius!

examples.text: C'est ma meilleure amie.
examples.trans: She's my best friend.

examples.text: La vie écrit de meilleurs duos que nous, mes chers garçons.
examples.trans: Life writes better duets than we do, my dear boys.

examples.text: Vos menaces ne m'impressionnent pas.
examples.trans: Your threats don't impress me.

examples.text: C'est une menace sérieuse.
examples.trans: It's a serious threat.

meanings.note: Menacer de = to threaten to.

examples.text: Tu me menaces?
examples.trans: Are you threatening me?

examples.text: Il menace de partir.
examples.trans: He threatens to leave.

examples.text: La production menace de faire un procès.
examples.trans: The production threatens a lawsuit.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'threatened'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ces animaux sont menacés.
examples.trans: These animals are endangered.

examples.text: Elle défend les espèces menacées.
examples.trans: She defends endangered species.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le mendiant', plural 'les mendiants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'beggar'.

examples.text: Nous ne sommes pas des mendiants.
examples.trans: We are not beggars.

examples.text: Nous ne sommes pas des mendiants, Mathias.
examples.trans: We are not beggars, Mathias.

meanings.note: For a path or clue to lead somewhere ('mener à'); to guide or conduct.

examples.text: Ce petit escalier en pierre mène directement au jardin.
examples.trans: This little stone staircase leads straight to the garden.

examples.text: Menez la marche, nous vous suivons de près!
examples.trans: Lead the way, we're right behind you!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le mensonge', plural 'les mensonges') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lie'.

examples.text: Trop de mensonges.
examples.trans: Too many lies.

examples.text: Parlons du mensonge dans le couple.
examples.trans: Let us talk about lies in a relationship.

examples.text: Mathias, il y a eu beaucoup de mensonges.
examples.trans: Mathias, there were many lies.

meanings.note: Feminine: menteuse.

examples.text: Tu es un menteur!
examples.trans: You're a liar!

examples.text: C'est une menteuse.
examples.trans: She's a liar.

meanings.note: Thé à la menthe = mint tea.

examples.text: Voilà pour vous, madame: du thé chaud à la menthe et du miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea and honey.

examples.text: Voici la menthe sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the mint on the table.

meanings.note: Mentir à quelqu'un.

examples.text: Je ne te mens jamais.
examples.trans: I never lie to you.

examples.text: Tu mens!
examples.trans: You're lying!

meanings.note: Chin of the face.

examples.text: Il se frotte le menton d'un air pensif devant la carte.
examples.trans: He rubs his chin thoughtfully in front of the map.

examples.text: Elle relève son écharpe en laine jusqu'au menton.
examples.trans: She pulls her wool scarf up to her chin.

meanings.note: In a French café or bistro, *le menu* often means a fixed-price combination (e.g. soup + tart + tea), while the full list is *la carte*.

examples.text: Le menu de midi propose une soupe chaude et une part de tarte.
examples.trans: The lunch menu offers a hot soup and a slice of tart.

examples.text: Elle écrit le menu du jour à l'encre noire sur un carton.
examples.trans: She writes today's menu in black ink on a card.

meanings.note: Craftsman who makes wooden furniture and doors.

examples.text: Un menuisier vivait là avec ses deux petits-fils: l'aîné jouait du piano, et le petit adorait les trains!
examples.trans: A carpenter lived there with his two grandsons: the older boy played piano, and the little one loved trains!

examples.text: Un menuisier... et un petit train en bois à l'intérieur du sac!
examples.trans: A carpenter... and a little wooden train inside the bag!

meanings.note: Salé comme la mer = salty as the sea.

examples.text: Ce bouillon est beaucoup trop salé, comme l'eau de mer!
examples.trans: This broth is way too salty, like seawater!

examples.text: Ils passent deux semaines au bord de la mer en août.
examples.trans: They spend two weeks by the sea in August.

meanings.note: merci beaucoup = thank you very much

examples.text: Merci beaucoup pour votre aide précieuse aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your valuable help today.

examples.text: Je te dis mille fois merci pour ce beau rôle!
examples.trans: I thank you a thousand times for this great role!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le mercredi', plural 'les mercredis') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'day of the week'.

examples.text: La séance de mercredi.
examples.trans: Wednesday's screening.

examples.text: À mercredi prochain.
examples.trans: See you next Wednesday.

examples.text: Attends: et mercredi soir, tu as réservé ici sous ton vrai nom?
examples.trans: Wait: and Wednesday night, you booked in here under your real name?

meanings.note: exclamation of anger or frustration; also used informally to wish good luck before a show

examples.text: Oh merde, j'ai complètement oublié mon rendez-vous!
examples.trans: Oh damn, I completely forgot my appointment!

examples.text: On lui a dit merde pour lui souhaiter bonne chance.
examples.trans: We told her break a leg to wish her good luck.

examples.text: Oh merde, j'ai oublié mes clés.
examples.trans: Oh damn, I forgot my keys.

examples.text: Ça te va à merveille.
examples.trans: It suits you perfectly.

examples.text: C'est une merveille!
examples.trans: It's a marvel!

meanings.note: Wonderful or marvellous; feminine merveilleuse pronounces the final z sound.

examples.text: C'est merveilleux!
examples.trans: That's wonderful!

examples.text: Une soirée merveilleuse.
examples.trans: A wonderful evening.

examples.text: De la soupe chaude? Après cette marche froide sous la pluie, ça a l'air merveilleux.
examples.trans: Hot soup? After that cold walk in the rain, that sounds wonderful.

meanings.note: Laisser un message vocal means 'to leave a voicemail / voice message'.

examples.text: La mairie a laissé un message vocal sur le répondeur.
examples.trans: City Hall left a voicemail on the answering machine.

examples.text: Claire note chaque message avec l'heure de l'appel.
examples.trans: Claire writes down every message along with the time of the call.

meanings.note: La messagerie vocale. Feminine noun ('la messagerie', plural 'les messageries') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'voicemail'.

examples.text: Vous êtes sur la messagerie de Mathias.
examples.trans: You have reached Mathias's voicemail.

examples.text: Laissez un mot sur ma messagerie.
examples.trans: Leave a note on my voicemail.

examples.text: Oui, je suis tombé sur sa messagerie.
examples.trans: Yes, I reached his voicemail.

meanings.note: In sheet music, une mesure is a musical bar; sur mesure means 'made to measure, custom-made'.

examples.text: Les huit premières mesures de cette valse sont très douces.
examples.trans: The first eight bars of this waltz are very gentle.

examples.text: Antoine note toutes les mesures de la pièce dans son carnet.
examples.trans: Antoine writes all the room's measurements in his notebook.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Neuf sur dix?! Personne ne mesure les cours à moins que...
examples.trans: Nine out of ten?! Nobody measures courtyards unless...

examples.text: Il vient de mesurer avec l'ancienne: il lui en reste deux sur l'étagère!
examples.trans: He just measured it against the old one: he has two left on the shelf!

examples.text: Regardez bien cette page: elle mesure les décibels et le calme, pas les étoiles d'hôtel!
examples.trans: Look closely at this page: it measures decibels and quietness, not hotel stars!

meanings.note: metteur en scène = stage/theatre director

examples.text: Le metteur en scène.
examples.trans: The director.

examples.text: Le jeune metteur en scène avec l'acteur âgé.
examples.trans: The young director with the older actor.

examples.text: En tant que metteur en scène.
examples.trans: As a director.

meanings.note: Place something somewhere. Mettre un pied dans la tombe evokes being close to death.

examples.text: Je mets les documents sur la table.
examples.trans: I put the documents on the table.

examples.text: Mets ces herbes vertes fraîches dessus avant de servir.
examples.trans: Put these fresh green herbs on top before serving.

meanings.en: piece of furniture; (in plural les meubles) furniture
meanings.note: Countable in French! English uncountable 'furniture' translates to plural des meubles, and 'a piece of furniture' is simply un meuble.

examples.text: Nous avons trouvé de beaux meubles anciens à la brocante.
examples.trans: We found lovely antique furniture at the flea market.

examples.text: Ce meuble en noyer vient de la maison de mon oncle.
examples.trans: This walnut piece of furniture comes from my uncle's house.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le micro', plural 'les micros') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'microphone'.

examples.text: Elle parle devant le micro.
examples.trans: She speaks in front of the microphone.

examples.text: Le micro de la radio fonctionne bien.
examples.trans: The radio microphone is working well.

examples.text: J'étais bien au micro ce soir?
examples.trans: Was I good on the microphone tonight?

meanings.note: À midi = at noon.

meanings.en: le Midi = the south of France
meanings.note: Capitalised.

examples.text: L'un à midi.
examples.trans: One at noon.

examples.text: On déjeune à midi.
examples.trans: We have lunch at noon.

meanings.note: La lune de miel = honeymoon. Masculine noun ('le miel', plural 'les miels') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sweet honey'.

examples.text: Du miel doux.
examples.trans: Sweet honey.

examples.text: Voilà pour vous, madame: du thé chaud à la menthe et du miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea and honey.

examples.text: Excellent choix! Vous voulez du miel ou de la confiture de pommes à côté?
examples.trans: Wonderful choice! Would you like honey or apple jam on the side?

meanings.en: le mien / la mienne / les miens / les miennes = mine
meanings.note: replaces 'mon/ma/mes + noun' and agrees with the noun

examples.text: C'est ton verre ou le mien?
examples.trans: Is that your glass or mine?

examples.text: Dites-leur que la mienne a un ruban rouge dans la poche du haut!
examples.trans: Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!

meanings.note: Ne pas laisser une miette = not leave a single crumb.

examples.text: Les invités n'ont pas laissé une seule miette de tarte!
examples.trans: The guests didn't leave a single crumb of tart!

examples.text: Les oiseaux picorent les miettes de pain dans la cour.
examples.trans: The birds peck at the bread crumbs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Comparative of bien.

examples.text: C'est mieux.
examples.trans: It's better.

examples.text: Ce serait mieux avec un homme.
examples.trans: It would be better with a man.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'attractive'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Elle est très mignonne.
examples.trans: She is very cute.

examples.text: Elle est mignonne et elle couche pour réussir.
examples.trans: She is cute and sleeps her way to success.

examples.text: Et en plus elle est mignonne, Hicham va adorer.
examples.trans: And plus she is pretty, Hicham is going to love her.

meanings.en: to simmer gently over low heat
meanings.note: Laisser mijoter à feu doux = let simmer over low heat.

examples.text: Laissez mijoter la soupe vingt minutes à feu doux.
examples.trans: Let the soup simmer twenty minutes over low heat.

examples.text: Un bon plat mijote sur le fourneau depuis midi.
examples.trans: A good dish has been simmering on the stove since noon.

meanings.note: Au milieu = in the middle.
ce milieu = this world, this business

examples.text: C'est un milieu difficile.
examples.trans: It's a tough world.

examples.text: Au milieu de la table.
examples.trans: In the middle of the table.

meanings.note: Des militants politiques. Masculine noun ('le militant', plural 'les militants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'activist'.

examples.text: Des militants sont devant le studio.
examples.trans: Activists are in front of the studio.

examples.text: Un militant engagé.
examples.trans: A dedicated activist.

examples.text: Camille? Des militants sont devant le studio.
examples.trans: Camille? Activists are in front of the studio.

meanings.note: Never takes an s.

examples.text: Trois cent mille.
examples.trans: Three hundred thousand.

examples.text: Mille mercis!
examples.trans: Thanks a million!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le millier', plural 'les milliers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'thousand'.

examples.text: Des milliers de spectateurs attendent devant le cinéma.
examples.trans: Thousands of spectators are waiting in front of the cinema.

examples.text: Le festival attire plusieurs milliers de visiteurs.
examples.trans: The festival attracts several thousand visitors.

meanings.note: 1/1000 of a metre.

examples.text: Vingt millimètres, en laiton, vanne de chaudière: je vais répéter ça tout le long!
examples.trans: Twenty millimetres, brass, boiler valve: I am going to repeat that all the way!

examples.text: Vérifiez bien que la bague à l'intérieur fait vingt millimètres.
examples.trans: Make sure the ring inside is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Noun of quantity. Masculine noun ('le million', plural 'les millions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'one million'.

examples.text: Deux cents millions d'euros!
examples.trans: Two hundred million euros!

examples.text: Un million de spectateurs.
examples.trans: One million spectators.

examples.text: Hicham a vendu son site pour deux cents millions d'euros!
examples.trans: Hicham sold his site for two hundred million euros!

examples.text: Mince, j'ai oublié mon téléphone !
examples.trans: Shoot, I forgot my phone!

examples.text: Oh mince, il est déjà midi.
examples.trans: Oh darn, it's already noon.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la mine', plural 'les mines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'look'.

examples.text: Tu as bonne mine ce matin.
examples.trans: You look well this morning.

examples.text: Bonjour Gabriel, tu as bonne mine!
examples.trans: Hello Gabriel, you look well!

meanings.note: Feminine: mineure. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'minor, under-age person'.

examples.text: Interdit aux mineurs.
examples.trans: Forbidden to minors.

examples.text: Protéger les mineurs.
examples.trans: To protect minors.

examples.text: Vous ne craignez pas une interdiction aux mineurs?
examples.trans: Are you not afraid of an age restriction?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la miniature', plural 'les miniatures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'miniature'.

examples.text: J'ai acheté des petites miniatures.
examples.trans: I bought small miniatures.

examples.text: Oui, j'ai des petites miniatures.
examples.trans: Yes, I have small miniatures.

meanings.note: au minimum = at a minimum, at the very least (pronounced -ɔm)

examples.text: Un César, au minimum!
examples.trans: A César, at the very least!

examples.text: C'est le strict minimum.
examples.trans: That's the bare minimum.

related.gloss: at a minimum, at the very least (pronounced -ɔm)

meanings.note: The noun can describe a woman or a man: la ministre or le ministre.

examples.text: La ministre arrive.
examples.trans: The minister is arriving.

examples.text: Il connaît le ministre.
examples.trans: He knows the minister.

examples.text: Le rapport du ministère.
examples.trans: The ministry report.

examples.text: Le ministère de la Culture.
examples.trans: The Ministry of Culture.

meanings.note: Used without an article after prepositions (*à minuit*, *avant minuit*), just like *midi* ('noon').
