examples.text: Toutes les fenêtres de la rue sont éteintes à minuit.
examples.trans: All the street windows are dark at midnight.

examples.text: L'orage a commencé quelques minutes avant minuit.
examples.trans: The storm started a few minutes before midnight.

meanings.note: Stronger and more vivid than *petit* (*une minuscule vis*, 'a tiny screw').

examples.text: Il faut une pince fine pour tenir cette minuscule pièce en laiton.
examples.trans: You need thin tweezers to hold this tiny brass part.

examples.text: Écrivez les détails en lettres minuscules tout en bas.
examples.trans: Write the details in tiny letters right at the bottom.

meanings.note: Cinq minutes = five minutes.

examples.text: Attendez cinq minutes.
examples.trans: Wait five minutes.

examples.text: J'arrive dans une minute.
examples.trans: I'll be there in a minute.

meanings.note: Derived from *minute*; essential in baking (*régler / surveiller le minuteur*).

examples.text: Réglez le minuteur sur vingt-cinq minutes pour les tartes.
examples.trans: Set the timer for twenty-five minutes for the tarts.

examples.text: Dès que le minuteur sonne, sortez le pain du four.
examples.trans: As soon as the timer rings, take the bread out of the oven.

meanings.note: Faire des miracles = work wonders / miracles.

examples.text: Une bonne nuit de sommeil fait toujours des miracles.
examples.trans: A good night's sleep always works wonders.

examples.text: C'est un petit miracle que le vieux piano sonne si juste!
examples.trans: It is a small miracle that the old piano sounds so in tune!

meanings.note: Wall or bathroom mirror.

examples.text: Regardez dans le miroir derrière le comptoir, patron.
examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the counter, boss.

examples.text: Et pas de miroir au mur, et le sol semble nu sans tapis.
examples.trans: And no mirror on the wall, and the floor feels bare without a rug.

examples.text: Où est-ce que j'accroche ce miroir rond? À gauche de la fenêtre ou à droite?
examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?

mise.gloss: putting, placing; mise à jour = update

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la mise', plural 'les mises') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'putting'.

examples.text: Une petite mise à jour du dossier.
examples.trans: A quick update of the file.

examples.text: Il lui faut une petite mise à jour.
examples.trans: It just needs a small update.

examples.text: Sauver la mise.
examples.trans: To save the day.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to bet on'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'misé').

examples.text: Nous devons miser sur les séries.
examples.trans: We must bet on series.

examples.text: Nous devons aussi miser sur les séries.
examples.trans: We must also bet on television series.

meanings.note: Remplir une mission. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'mission, assignment'.

examples.text: Mission accomplie, Andréa!
examples.trans: Mission accomplished, Andrea!

examples.text: Une mission délicate pour l'agence.
examples.trans: A delicate mission for the agency.

examples.text: Mission accomplie, Andréa.
examples.trans: Mission accomplished, Andrea.

meanings.note: en mode silencieux = on silent mode
À la mode. Masculine noun ('le mode', plural 'les modes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mode'.

examples.text: Il était en mode silencieux.
examples.trans: It was on silent mode.

examples.text: Change le mode du téléphone.
examples.trans: Change the phone setting.

examples.text: Il était en mode silencieux. Tu veux une coupe? On a sorti le champagne.
examples.trans: It was on silent mode. Do you want a glass? We brought out the champagne.

meanings.note: Modern or contemporary; same singular spelling for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Ça devient moderne.
examples.trans: It becomes modern.

examples.text: Un film moderne.
examples.trans: A modern film.

examples.text: Bien chaude! Vous entendez ça, Claire? Une eau chaude moderne, fiable, cinq étoiles!
examples.trans: Nice and hot! Do you hear that, Claire? Modern, reliable, five-star hot water!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'modest'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un rôle modeste mais marquant.
examples.trans: A modest but memorable role.

examples.text: Le rôle prévu était très modeste.
examples.trans: The intended role was very modest.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la modification', plural 'les modifications') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'modification'.

examples.text: Cette modification n'était pas prévue.
examples.trans: This modification was not planned.

examples.text: Cette modification n'était pas convenue.
examples.trans: This modification was not agreed upon.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to modify'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'modifié').

examples.text: Il veut modifier la scène.
examples.trans: He wants to modify the scene.

examples.text: Pascal veut modifier la scène prévue.
examples.trans: Pascal wants to change the planned scene.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le modèle', plural 'les modèles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'design'.

examples.text: Voici un modèle audacieux.
examples.trans: Here is a bold design.

examples.text: Voici un modèle flashy et audacieux.
examples.trans: Here is a flashy and daring design.

meanings.note: Stressed form: pour moi, avec moi.

examples.text: Et moi?
examples.trans: And me?

examples.text: Moi, c'est Henri. Vous êtes en avance de dix minutes.
examples.trans: I am Henri. You are ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Stressed emphatic pronoun, used independently or to reinforce a subject.

examples.text: Moi-même, je ne sais pas.
examples.trans: Even I don't know.

examples.text: Je l'ai fait moi-même.
examples.trans: I did it myself.

examples.text: Passez-moi le téléphone, je vais lui demander moi-même!
examples.trans: Pass me the phone, I will ask him myself!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'slightest'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Au moindre doute.
examples.trans: At the slightest doubt.

examples.text: Ni leur accorder la moindre attention.
examples.trans: Nor give them the slightest attention.

examples.text: Au moindre doute, elle dégage.
examples.trans: At the slightest doubt, she is out.

meanings.note: House sparrow common in French courtyards, parks, and café terraces.

examples.text: Deux moineaux picorent des miettes près du banc.
examples.trans: Two sparrows peck at crumbs near the bench.

examples.text: Les moineaux chantent dès l'aube dans les branches du tilleul.
examples.trans: The sparrows sing at dawn in the branches of the linden tree.

meanings.note: Moins de trente ans = under thirty.

examples.text: Il est moins grand que moi.
examples.trans: He's shorter than me.

examples.text: Attends au moins une heure.
examples.trans: Wait at least an hour.

meanings.note: Same form in the plural.

examples.text: Ça fait des mois.
examples.trans: It's been months.

examples.text: Je pars dans un mois.
examples.trans: I'm leaving in a month.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'moldy'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Les pages sont complètement moisies.
examples.trans: The pages are completely moldy.

examples.text: Une odeur de moisi.
examples.trans: A smell of mold.

examples.text: Les pages sont complètement moisies et sales.
examples.trans: The pages are completely moldy and dirty.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la moitié', plural 'les moitiés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'half'.

examples.text: C'est la moitié du travail.
examples.trans: It is half of the work.

examples.text: Couper en deux moitiés.
examples.trans: To cut into two halves.

examples.text: Moitié prix pour ce soir, et le petit-déjeuner offert toute la semaine!
examples.trans: Half price for tonight, and free breakfast all week!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le mojito', plural 'les mojitos') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mojito cocktail'.

examples.text: Veux-tu boire un bon mojito?
examples.trans: Do you want to drink a nice mojito?

examples.text: Deux mojitos, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Two mojitos, please.

examples.text: Veux-tu boire un bon mojito avec moi?
examples.trans: Do you want to drink a nice mojito with me?

meanings.en: en ce moment = at the moment, currently

examples.text: Je joue en ce moment.
examples.trans: I'm acting at the moment.

examples.text: Un moment, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: One moment, please.

meanings.note: Ma before a feminine noun; mon before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel sound or mute h.

examples.text: Je suis à mon cours.
examples.trans: I'm at my lesson.

examples.text: C'est ma place.
examples.trans: It's my seat.

meanings.note: un dîner mondain = a high-society dinner party

examples.text: Allez à vos dîners mondains!
examples.trans: Go to your high-society dinners!

examples.text: La vie mondaine à Paris.
examples.trans: High-society life in Paris.

examples.text: Il y a du monde.
examples.trans: There are people here.

examples.text: Nadia parle à tout le monde dans notre rue comme à de vieux amis.
examples.trans: Nadia talks to everyone on our street like old friends.

meanings.note: la Première Guerre mondiale = the First World War

examples.text: Une crise mondiale.
examples.trans: A global crisis.

examples.text: Le marché mondial.
examples.trans: The world market.

examples.text: Pendant la Première Guerre mondiale, c'est ça?
examples.trans: During the First World War, is that it?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le moniteur', plural 'les moniteurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'monitor'.

examples.text: Le réalisateur regarde la scène sur son moniteur.
examples.trans: The director watches the scene on his monitor.

examples.text: L'infirmière vérifie le moniteur à l'hôpital.
examples.trans: The nurse checks the monitor at the hospital.

meanings.note: Voici la monnaie = here is the change.

examples.text: Juste ici! Tout a coûté trente-huit euros, alors voici douze euros de monnaie.
examples.trans: Right here! Everything cost thirty-eight euros, so here is twelve euros in change.

examples.text: Voici la monnaie sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the change, small coins on the table.

meanings.note: the practice of having only one partner/spouse

examples.text: Tout est permis, sauf la norme de la monogamie.
examples.trans: Everything is allowed, except the norm of monogamy.

examples.text: La monogamie est une norme sociale.
examples.trans: Monogamy is a social norm.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le monologue', plural 'les monologues') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'monologue'.

examples.text: L'actrice a répété son grand monologue.
examples.trans: The actress rehearsed her big monologue.

examples.text: Le réalisateur a coupé son monologue.
examples.trans: The director cut her monologue.

examples.text: Il a supprimé tout mon grand monologue.
examples.trans: He deleted my entire big monologue.

meanings.note: Polite address: merci, monsieur.
Un monsieur.

examples.text: Bonjour, monsieur! Oui, le bureau est propre et les clés sont prêtes.
examples.trans: Good morning, sir! Yes, the desk is clean and the keys are ready.

examples.text: Oh, comme c'est aimable, monsieur. Juste un demi-verre.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind, sir. Just half a glass.

examples.text: Attendez... bonjour, monsieur! Vous appelez pour la valise bleu foncé?
examples.trans: Wait... hello, sir! Are you calling about the dark-blue suitcase?

meanings.en: un monstre sacré = a legendary star

examples.text: Tu es un monstre de séduction.
examples.trans: You're a monster of seduction.

examples.text: Un film de monstres.
examples.trans: A monster movie.

examples.text: Cette fille avait raison. Tu es un monstre.
examples.trans: That girl was right. You're a monster.

examples.text: Tu es ma mère. C'est monstrueux!
examples.trans: You're my mother. It's monstrous!

examples.text: Une erreur monstrueuse.
examples.trans: A monstrous mistake.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le montage', plural 'les montages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'film editing'.
Masculine noun ('le montage', plural 'les montages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'assembly'.

examples.text: Nous devons assurer le montage du film.
examples.trans: We must secure the editing of the film.

examples.text: Le montage prend plusieurs semaines.
examples.trans: Editing takes several weeks.

examples.text: Je sais bien, mais nous devons assurer le montage.
examples.trans: I know well, but we must secure the editing.

meanings.note: De montagne describes mountain produce such as miel de montagne ('mountain honey') or fromage de montagne.

examples.text: Ce miel de montagne est récolté à la fin de l'été.
examples.trans: This mountain honey is harvested at the end of summer.

examples.text: On voit le sommet de la montagne par temps clair.
examples.trans: You can see the top of the mountain in clear weather.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le montant', plural 'les montants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'financial amount'.

examples.text: Ajoutez un zéro à ces montants.
examples.trans: Add a zero to these amounts.

examples.text: Ajoute un zéro à tous ces montants.
examples.trans: Add a zero to all these amounts.

meanings.en: to go up, to get on
meanings.note: Monter à cheval; often just monter.
Monter à cheval; often just monter.

examples.text: Elle monte à cheval.
examples.trans: She rides a horse.

examples.text: Vous savez monter?
examples.trans: Can you ride?

meanings.note: À ma montre = by my watch.

examples.text: Sept heures vingt-neuf à ma montre. Les clients descendent l'escalier.
examples.trans: Seven twenty-nine on my watch. Guests are coming down the stairs.

examples.text: Juste un peu de beurre, merci. Pourquoi regardez-vous votre montre, monsieur?
examples.trans: Just a little butter, thank you. Why are you looking at your watch, sir?

examples.text: Quelle heure indique votre montre maintenant, Henri?
examples.trans: What time does your watch show now, Henri?

meanings.note: Montrer quelque chose à quelqu'un.

examples.text: Je vous montre l'agence.
examples.trans: I'll show you the agency.

examples.text: Montre-moi ta photo!
examples.trans: Show me your photo!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la montée', plural 'les montées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'rise'.

examples.text: La montée des marches à Cannes est un moment magique.
examples.trans: Walking up the steps at Cannes is a magical moment.

examples.text: La petite montée vers le village est assez raide.
examples.trans: The climb up to the village is quite steep.

meanings.note: Often reflexive: se moquer de. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to tease'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'moqué').

examples.text: Il se moque de ses amis.
examples.trans: He makes fun of his friends.

examples.text: Tu veux juste te moquer de moi.
examples.trans: You just want to make fun of me.

examples.text: Un petit imprévu? Tu te moques de moi?
examples.trans: A small unexpected issue? Are you mocking me?

meanings.note: remonter le moral = to cheer up, to boost morale

examples.text: Pour vous remonter le moral.
examples.trans: To cheer you up.

examples.text: Garder le moral.
examples.trans: To keep one's spirits up.

examples.text: Je peux faire quelque chose pour vous remonter le moral?
examples.trans: Can I do anything to cheer you up?

related.gloss: to cheer up, to boost morale

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le morceau', plural 'les morceaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'piece'.

examples.text: Un morceau de pain.
examples.trans: A piece of bread.

examples.text: Couper en morceaux.
examples.trans: To cut into pieces.

examples.text: Elle fait cuire le morceau sur un barbecue.
examples.trans: She cooks the piece on a barbecue.

examples.text: Il mord les jambes des traîtres!
examples.trans: He bites traitors' legs!

examples.text: Ce chien ne mord pas.
examples.trans: This dog doesn't bite.

examples.text: Jean Gabin, arrête! Il mord les jambes des traîtres!
examples.trans: Jean Gabin, stop it! He bites traitors' legs!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la morgue', plural 'les morgues') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'morgue'.

examples.text: La scène se passe dans une morgue.
examples.trans: The scene takes place in a morgue.

examples.text: Le médecin entre dans la morgue.
examples.trans: The doctor enters the morgue.

examples.text: Or votre scène se passe à la morgue.
examples.trans: Yet your scene takes place in the morgue.

meanings.note: past participle of mourir, used as an adjective
As a feminine noun. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'dead'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Samuel est mort.
examples.trans: Samuel is dead.

examples.text: Ce film n'est pas mort.
examples.trans: This film isn't dead.

examples.text: Mais ce film est mort.
examples.trans: But this film is dead.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.
c'est mortel d'ennui = it is terribly boring

examples.text: C'est mortel d'ennui pour moi.
examples.trans: It is terribly boring for me.

examples.text: Une blessure mortelle.
examples.trans: A fatal wound.

examples.text: C'est petit-bourgeois et mortel d'ennui pour moi.
examples.trans: It is petty-bourgeois and deadly boring for me.

meanings.note: Lime-and-sand masonry mortar binding bricks or flagstones; kitchen mortar bowl.

examples.text: Le vieux mortier à la chaux laisse respirer les pierres.
examples.trans: The old lime mortar lets the stones breathe.

examples.text: Un peu de mortier sec s'effrite autour de la dalle.
examples.trans: A bit of dry mortar crumbles around the flagstone.

meanings.note: Note the silent final t.

examples.text: Je ne comprends pas un mot.
examples.trans: I don't understand a word.

examples.text: Dis-moi un mot.
examples.trans: Say a word to me.

meanings.note: Car or machine engine.

examples.text: Ne bougez plus, tous les deux. Vous entendez ce moteur s'arrêter au bord du trottoir?
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Do you hear that engine stopping at the kerb?

examples.text: Voici le moteur sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the engine, motor on the table.

meanings.note: From the verb 'motiver'.

examples.text: Elle est jeune et motivée.
examples.trans: She's young and keen.

examples.text: Il est très motivé.
examples.trans: He's very motivated.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la moto', plural 'les motos') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'motorcycle'.

examples.text: Rouler en moto.
examples.trans: To ride a motorcycle.

examples.text: Une belle moto.
examples.trans: A nice motorcycle.

examples.text: Parce que je roule toujours en moto!
examples.trans: Because I always ride a motorcycle!

meanings.note: Playful exclamation pledging secrecy ('motus!' or 'motus et bouche cousue!' = my lips are sealed!).

examples.text: Personne ne doit savoir avant ce soir: motus!
examples.trans: Nobody must find out before tonight: mum's the word!

examples.text: Motus et bouche cousue jusqu'à l'ouverture du coffret!
examples.trans: Mum's the word and lips sealed until we open the box!

meanings.note: Soft to the touch (e.g., softened butter 'beurre mou', damp ground); gentle or slack (note 'mol' before masculine vowel/mute h).

examples.text: Sortez le beurre à l'avance pour qu'il soit bien mou.
examples.trans: Take the butter out ahead of time so it gets nice and soft.

examples.text: Après la pluie, la terre du jardin reste un peu molle.
examples.trans: After the rain, the garden soil stays a bit soft.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le mouchoir', plural 'les mouchoirs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'paper handkerchief'.

examples.text: Elle prend des mouchoirs.
examples.trans: She takes some tissues.

examples.text: J'ai juste un pyjama et des mouchoirs. Merci!
examples.trans: I just have pajamas and tissues. Thank you!

meanings.note: La Mouette = Chekhov's play The Seagull

examples.text: Je suis la mouette.
examples.trans: I am the seagull.

examples.text: Les mouettes sur la plage.
examples.trans: The seagulls on the beach.

meanings.note: From mouiller. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'wet'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: J'ai déjà les pieds mouillés!
examples.trans: My feet are already wet!

examples.text: L'herbe est mouillée.
examples.trans: The grass is wet.

examples.text: Parce que les volets en bois mouillés adoucissent l'écho des pavés...
examples.trans: Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the cobblestones...

meanings.note: Masculine noun: baking tin, cake pan, or mold ('moule à gâteau').

examples.text: Nadia répartit la pâte dans trois petits moules ronds.
examples.trans: Nadia divides the batter into three small round baking tins.

examples.text: Beurrez légèrement le moule avant d'y verser la préparation.
examples.trans: Lightly butter the cake pan before pouring in the batter.

meanings.note: With être in the past: il est mort.
Mourir de faim = to be starving.

examples.text: Il est mort à l'hôpital.
examples.trans: He died in hospital.

examples.text: Je meurs de faim!
examples.trans: I'm starving!

meanings.note: porter la moustache = to wear a mustache

examples.text: Il a une belle moustache.
examples.trans: He has a nice mustache.

examples.text: Se raser la moustache.
examples.trans: To shave one's mustache.

examples.text: C'est comme dans le film La Moustache.
examples.trans: It is like in the movie The Mustache.

meanings.note: Movement or motion; here Line wants an energetic role.

examples.text: Je veux du mouvement!
examples.trans: I want movement!

examples.text: Un petit mouvement de la main.
examples.trans: A little movement of the hand.

examples.text: Je veux du mouvement, de l'action, de l'énergie!
examples.trans: I want movement, action, energy!

meanings.note: trouver un moyen de = find a way to
Avoir des moyens. Masculine noun ('le moyen', plural 'les moyens') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'way'.

examples.text: Je dois trouver un moyen d'éloigner Hartman.
examples.trans: I must find a way to get Hartman away.

examples.text: Il n'y a aucun moyen de refuser.
examples.trans: There is no way to refuse.

examples.text: C'est le moyen parfait pour rentrer.
examples.trans: It is the perfect way to get home.

meanings.note: Doubles the -t in the feminine: muet (/mɥɛ/) -> muette (/mɥɛt/). Also used for silent letters in French spelling (un e muet, un h muet).

examples.text: Henri a réparé le marteau de la touche muette.
examples.trans: Henri repaired the hammer of the silent piano key.

examples.text: Devant la surprise, Étienne est resté muet pendant dix secondes.
examples.trans: Faced with the surprise, Étienne stood speechless for ten seconds.

examples.text: Amour et Muffins.
examples.trans: Love and Muffins.

examples.text: Un muffin au chocolat.
examples.trans: A chocolate muffin.

meanings.note: Borrowed from English for a tall straight-sided coffee/tea mug without a saucer, distinct from une tasse (traditional teacup/coffee cup) and un bol (breakfast bowl).

examples.text: Thibault boit son café noir dans un grand mug bleu.
examples.trans: Thibault drinks his black coffee out of a big blue mug.

examples.text: Pour le salon de thé, Nadia préfère des tasses plutôt que des mugs.
examples.trans: For the tearoom, Nadia prefers teacups rather than mugs.

meanings.note: Belonging to or run by the town or city ('bibliothèque municipale', 'square municipal').

examples.text: La bibliothèque municipale conserve les archives du quartier.
examples.trans: The municipal library holds the neighborhood archives.

examples.text: L'orchestre joue chaque été dans le jardin municipal.
examples.trans: The orchestra plays every summer in the town park.

meanings.note: Exterior or interior structural wall.

examples.text: Et pas de miroir au mur, et le sol semble nu sans tapis.
examples.trans: And no mirror on the wall, and the floor feels bare without a rug.

examples.text: Attention dans le virage, ne cognez pas le mur!
examples.trans: Careful on the turn, do not bump the wall!

examples.text: Les chambres resteront chaudes jusqu'au matin, Claire, grâce aux murs en brique.
examples.trans: The rooms will stay warm until morning, Claire, thanks to the brick walls.

meanings.note: To speak softly in a low, gentle voice, or to rustle/murmur (of wind or water).

examples.text: Il a murmuré que sa voix était fatiguée d'avoir parlé pendant tout le voyage en train.
examples.trans: He whispered that his voice was tired from talking during the whole train trip.

examples.text: La fontaine en pierre murmure doucement au fond de la cour.
examples.trans: The stone fountain murmurs softly at the back of the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used humorously in the plural (*les muscles*) to contrast brute force with technique or oil.

examples.text: Un peu d'huile aide plus que tous les muscles du monde.
examples.trans: A little oil helps more than all the muscle in the world.

examples.text: Pétrir la pâte à pain à la main fait travailler les muscles.
examples.trans: Kneading bread dough by hand works your muscles.

meanings.note: une comédie musicale = a musical comedy

examples.text: C'est une comédie musicale érotique.
examples.trans: It is an erotic musical.

examples.text: Un talent musical.
examples.trans: A musical talent.

examples.text: Elle conviendrait bien pour ta comédie musicale.
examples.trans: She would be a great fit for your musical.

meanings.note: Person who plays a musical instrument or composes music.
Feminine form: une musicienne.

examples.text: Vous avez joué comme un vrai musicien, Antoine, et regardez qui se lève à la table numéro un!
examples.trans: You played like a true musician, Antoine, and look who is standing up at table number one!

examples.text: Voici six nouvelles parts pour la table trois; garde deux gros coins pour les musiciens!
examples.trans: Here go six more slices for table three; save two big corners for the musicians!

meanings.note: Jouer de la musique ('play music'), écouter de la musique ('listen to music'), de la musique écrite à la main ('handwritten music').

examples.text: La musique du piano traverse doucement la cour.
examples.trans: The piano music drifts gently across the courtyard.

examples.text: J'aime travailler le matin avec un peu de musique classique.
examples.trans: I like working in the morning with a bit of classical music.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: C'est un baiser de respect mutuel.
examples.trans: It is a kiss of mutual respect.

examples.text: Ils ont un respect mutuel profond.
examples.trans: They have a deep mutual respect.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la mutuelle', plural 'les mutuelles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'health insurance'.

examples.text: Une mutuelle santé.
examples.trans: A health insurance fund.

examples.text: Avez-vous une mutuelle?
examples.trans: Do you have health insurance?

examples.text: Tu as une bonne mutuelle santé?
examples.trans: Do you have good health insurance?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le mystère', plural 'les mystères') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mystery'.

examples.text: Ce film garde tout son mystère.
examples.trans: This movie keeps all its mystery.

examples.text: Regarde, tu as survécu au coup de feu du matin et à l'appel mystère!
examples.trans: Look, you survived the morning rush and the mystery phone call!

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un client mystérieux.
examples.trans: A mysterious client.

examples.text: Bien sûr que je suis venu. Pourquoi tu t'es caché derrière un mot mystérieux?
examples.trans: Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?

meanings.note: Standard word for 'mother' (more affectionate everyday family address is maman).

examples.text: Ma mère faisait toujours une tarte au citron le dimanche.
examples.trans: My mother always used to make a lemon tart on Sundays.

examples.text: Ce carnet de recettes appartient à la mère de Nadia.
examples.trans: This recipe notebook belongs to Nadia's mother.

meanings.note: un mètre soixante-quinze = one meter seventy-five

examples.text: Attendez: qui est assis à dix mètres d'ici dans notre cour en ce moment?
examples.trans: Wait: who is sitting ten metres from here in our courtyard right now?

examples.text: Il mesure un mètre quatre-vingts.
examples.trans: He measures one meter eighty.

examples.text: À quelques mètres d'ici.
examples.trans: A few meters from here.

meanings.note: Descriptive

examples.text: C'est méchant!
examples.trans: That's mean!

examples.text: Ne sois pas méchant.
examples.trans: Don't be mean.

meanings.note: Un client mécontent. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'unhappy'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Quand ma mère a un client mécontent, elle fait un geste.
examples.trans: When my mother has an unhappy customer, she makes a concession.

examples.text: Le directeur est mécontent.
examples.trans: The director is displeased.

examples.text: Quand ma mère a un client mécontent, elle fait un geste pour ses amis.
examples.trans: When my mother has an unhappy customer, she gives her friends a discount.

meanings.en: patron, sponsor, benefactor of the arts
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le mécène', plural 'les mécènes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'patron'.

examples.text: Un puissant mécène.
examples.trans: A powerful patron.

examples.text: Le mécène des artistes.
examples.trans: The patron of artists.

examples.text: Attention, cet homme est un puissant mécène.
examples.trans: Careful, this man is a powerful patron.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la médaille', plural 'les médailles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'medal'.

examples.text: Ma mère reçoit la médaille de la ville.
examples.trans: My mother receives the medal of the city.

examples.text: Une médaille d'or.
examples.trans: A gold medal.

meanings.note: aller chez le médecin = to go to the doctor's

examples.text: Tu as besoin d'un nouveau médecin!
examples.trans: You need a new doctor!

examples.text: Elle est médecin.
examples.trans: She's a doctor.

examples.text: Tu as besoin d'un nouveau médecin, tu es folle!
examples.trans: You need a new doctor, you're crazy!

examples.text: Les médias peuvent être cruels.
examples.trans: The media can be cruel.

examples.text: Il parle aux médias.
examples.trans: He's speaking to the media.

meanings.note: irregular masculine plural: médicaux

examples.text: Ce sont vos résultats médicaux.
examples.trans: It's your medical results.

examples.text: Une visite médicale.
examples.trans: A medical check-up.

meanings.note: prendre un médicament = to take medicine

examples.text: Tu as un médicament?
examples.trans: Do you have any medicine?

examples.text: Je prends un médicament pour le dos.
examples.trans: I'm taking medicine for my back.

examples.text: Oui, un médicament. J'ai mal au dos.
examples.trans: Yes, some medicine. My back hurts.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la méditation', plural 'les méditations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'meditation'.

examples.text: Je fais de la méditation tous les matins.
examples.trans: I meditate every morning.

examples.text: Je fais de la méditation et du yoga.
examples.trans: I do meditation and yoga.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to ponder'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'médité').

examples.text: Je te laisse méditer.
examples.trans: I leave you to ponder.

examples.text: Je te laisse méditer là-dessus.
examples.trans: I leave you to ponder that.

meanings.note: From se méfier. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'suspicious'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il savait que je serais moins méfiant.
examples.trans: He knew I would be less suspicious.

examples.text: Elle reste méfiante.
examples.trans: She remains wary.

examples.text: Bien sûr, il savait que je serais moins méfiant.
examples.trans: Of course, he knew I would be less suspicious.

meanings.note: Describes a wistful or gloomy mood; same singular spelling for either gender.

examples.text: Vous n'êtes pas du genre mélancolique.
examples.trans: You're not the melancholy type.

examples.text: Une chanson mélancolique.
examples.trans: A melancholy song.

examples.text: Mélancolique? Non, non!
examples.trans: Melancholy? No, no!

meanings.note: mélanger le travail et la vie privée = to mix work and private life

examples.text: Je ne mélange pas le travail et la vie privée.
examples.trans: I don't mix work and private life.

examples.text: On mélange tout.
examples.trans: We mix everything together.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a musical tune or air that can be hummed or played on an instrument.

examples.text: Cette mélodie au piano reste facilement en tête.
examples.trans: This piano melody stays in your head easily.

examples.text: Odette reconnaît la mélodie dès les premières notes.
examples.trans: Odette recognises the tune from the very first notes.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la mémoire', plural 'les mémoires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'memory'.

examples.text: Avoir une bonne mémoire.
examples.trans: To have a good memory.

examples.text: Des trous de mémoire.
examples.trans: Memory blanks.

examples.text: Les gens me posent des questions sur ma mémoire.
examples.trans: People are asking me questions about my memory.

meanings.note: faire le ménage = to do the cleaning / housework

examples.text: Oui, elle fait le ménage pour la duchesse.
examples.trans: Yes, she does the cleaning for the duchess.

examples.text: Je fais le ménage le samedi.
examples.trans: I do the cleaning on Saturdays.

examples.text: Les femmes de ménage et les vacances étaient payées avec l'argent de l'agence.
examples.trans: The cleaners and the vacations were paid for with the agency's money.

meanings.en: to deserve, to merit, to be worth

examples.text: Il le mérite après huit ans!
examples.trans: He deserves it after eight years!

examples.text: Tu mérites des vacances.
examples.trans: You deserve a holiday.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'deserved'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un succès mérité.
examples.trans: A well-deserved success.

examples.text: Des vacances bien méritées.
examples.trans: Well-deserved vacations.

examples.text: Il prend simplement quelques jours de repos mérité.
examples.trans: He is simply taking a few days of well-deserved rest.

meanings.note: Plural: les métaux.

examples.text: Écoutez quand je penche le coffre: un objet en métal vient de glisser dedans.
examples.trans: Listen when I tilt the chest: a metal object just slid inside.

examples.text: Voici le métal sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the metal on the table.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Vite, refermez-le! Montons-le tout de suite... attendez, c'est quoi ce grand bruit métallique?
examples.trans: Quick, close it! Let us take it upstairs right away... wait, what is that loud metallic noise?

examples.text: Très paisible! Mais vous avez entendu un drôle de choc métallique à l'instant?
examples.trans: Very peaceful! Though did you hear a funny metallic knock just now?

meanings.note: une métaphore filée = an extended metaphor

examples.text: Utiliser une métaphore.
examples.trans: To use a metaphor.

examples.text: Une belle métaphore.
examples.trans: A beautiful metaphor.

examples.text: Il est très métaphore animalière, non?
examples.trans: He is very into animal metaphors, isn't he?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la méthode', plural 'les méthodes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'acting technique or method'.

examples.text: La méthode de l'Actor Studio.
examples.trans: The Actor Studio method.

examples.text: C'est la méthode de l'Actor Studio.
examples.trans: It is the Actor Studio method.

examples.text: Vos méthodes sont révoltantes.
examples.trans: Your methods are revolting.

meanings.note: A job, trade or profession.

examples.text: J'arrêterais ce métier.
examples.trans: I'd quit this job.

examples.text: Quel est ton métier?
examples.trans: What do you do for a living?

examples.text: Sans toi, je crois que j'arrêterais ce métier.
examples.trans: Without you, I think I'd quit this job.

meanings.note: prendre le métro = to take the metro

examples.text: Non, je prends le métro.
examples.trans: No, I'm taking the metro.

examples.text: La station de métro est là.
examples.trans: The metro station is right there.

meanings.note: Short for météorologie (feminine).

examples.trans: I am checking the weather, Nadia! Who left this thick envelope near the bell?

examples.text: Voici la météo sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the weather forecast, weather on the table.

meanings.en: to mix, to meddle in affairs
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to mix'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'mêlé').

examples.trans: What business is it of yours?

examples.text: De quoi tu te mêles, Hicham?
examples.trans: What business is it of yours, Hicham?

meanings.note: Before a noun, means the same; can take a plural s in this use.
As an adverb meaning even, it does not change.

examples.text: Elles ont le même lifting.
examples.trans: They have the same facelift.

examples.text: C'est la même chose.
examples.trans: It's the same thing.

examples.text: Il y a vingt-cinq ans? Dans cette même maison?
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago? In that same house?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le môme', plural 'les mômes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'kid'.

examples.trans: Do not deprive this kid.

examples.text: Je ne peux pas priver ce môme.
examples.trans: I cannot deprive this kid.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'mature'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: After careful consideration, I accept this role.

examples.trans: These fruits from the garden are nice and ripe.

dire n'importe quoi = to talk nonsense

examples.trans: Stop talking nonsense!

related.gloss: to know how to swim; nous nageons

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la naissance', plural 'les naissances') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'birth'.

examples.text: Nous fêtons la naissance de Flora.
examples.trans: We celebrate the birth of Flora.

examples.text: Il vient pour la déclaration de naissance?
examples.trans: Is he coming for the birth declaration?

examples.trans: Here is a clean white tablecloth and two blue cups.

examples.text: Voici la nappe sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the tablecloth on the table.

meanings.note: le conservatoire national = the national conservatory

examples.text: Le théâtre national.
examples.trans: The national theater.

examples.text: Une fête nationale.
examples.trans: A national holiday.

examples.trans: I must definitely go to the national conservatoire.

meanings.note: la protection de la nature = nature conservation

examples.trans: Nature is important in his project.

examples.trans: In the heart of nature.

examples.text: Elle est très naturelle.
examples.trans: She is very natural.

examples.text: Ne t'inquiète pas, sois naturelle.
examples.trans: Don't worry, be natural.

examples.trans: In our hotel, five-star service comes naturally... whoops!

examples.text: La seconde moitié de la mélodie coule naturellement.
examples.trans: The second half of the melody flows naturally.

examples.text: Naturellement, votre table est réservée pour vendredi.
examples.trans: Of course, your table is reserved for Friday.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le naufrage', plural 'les naufrages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shipwreck'.

examples.text: Sans un naufrage inattendu.
examples.trans: Without an unexpected disaster.

examples.text: Elle aurait été excellente sans un naufrage.
examples.trans: It could have been excellent without a disaster.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le navet', plural 'les navets') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cinematic flop'.

examples.text: Ce film est un navet.
examples.trans: This movie is a dud.

examples.text: Elle ne peut pas tourner ce navet!
examples.trans: She cannot shoot this dud!

examples.text: Ce film de science-fiction sera un navet.
examples.trans: This science fiction movie will be a dud.

meanings.note: To travel by boat; here sailing with her father.
Naviguer sur Internet.

examples.trans: Yes, I sail a lot with my father.

examples.text: Il aime naviguer en été.
examples.trans: He likes sailing in summer.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le navire', plural 'les navires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ship'.

examples.text: Il a abandonné le navire.
examples.trans: He abandoned ship.

examples.text: Mathias a abandonné le navire.
examples.trans: Mathias abandoned ship.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'deeply sorry'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je suis vraiment navré.
examples.trans: I am truly sorry.

examples.text: Je suis vraiment navré, Hicham.
examples.trans: I am truly sorry, Hicham.

meanings.note: Idiom for not being naive. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be born, to arise'.

meanings.en: ne pas être né de la dernière pluie = not born yesterday
meanings.note: Idiom for not being naive. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be born, to arise'.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas né de la dernière pluie.
examples.trans: I was not born yesterday.

examples.text: Elle est née à Paris.
examples.trans: She was born in Paris.

examples.text: Notre petite fille n'est pas encore née!
examples.trans: Our little girl is not born yet!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'naive'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: J'ai été bien trop naïve ce soir.
examples.trans: I was much too naive tonight.

examples.text: Ne soyez pas si naïf avec eux.
examples.trans: Do not be so naive with them.

examples.text: J'ai été bien trop naïve, apparemment.
examples.trans: I was much too naive, apparently.

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

examples.text: Rien n'est signé.
examples.trans: Nothing is signed.

examples.text: Attention dans le virage, ne cognez pas le mur!
examples.trans: Careful on the turn, do not bump the wall!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le nerf', plural 'les nerfs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nerve'.

examples.text: Cette situation me met les nerfs!
examples.trans: This situation gets on my nerves!

examples.text: Il faut garder son calme et ses nerfs.
examples.trans: One must keep calm and maintain one's nerves.

examples.text: Cette histoire me met vraiment les nerfs!
examples.trans: This situation really gets on my nerves!

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Les acteurs sont toujours un peu nerveux avant la première.
examples.trans: The actors are always a bit nervous before opening night.

examples.text: Le café fort le rend beaucoup trop nerveux.
examples.trans: Strong coffee makes him far too jittery.

meanings.note: Unlike most short adjectives in -et, the final -t IS pronounced even in the masculine (/nɛt/); feminine doubles it to nette (/nɛt/).

examples.text: L'interrupteur neuf fait un petit clic bien net.
examples.trans: The new switch gives a crisp, clean little click.

examples.text: Les lettres sur cette vieille carte sont encore très nettes.
examples.trans: The letters on this old card are still very sharp.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to clean'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'nettoyé').

examples.text: Je nettoie le sol.
examples.trans: I am cleaning the floor.

examples.text: Tu vois bien, je nettoie.
examples.trans: You can see, I am cleaning.

examples.text: Oui s'il te plaît, nettoie son visage.
examples.trans: Yes please, clean her face.

meanings.note: Final f sounds like /v/ before ans and heures.
Un gilet neuf, une ampoule neuve.

examples.text: C'est à neuf heures.

examples.text: J'ai neuf pages à lire.
examples.trans: I have nine pages to read.

examples.text: Vous pouvez? C'est à neuf heures.
examples.trans: Can you make it? It's at nine o'clock.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.trans: A serious neurodegenerative disease.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas une maladie neurodégénérative grave.
examples.trans: It is not a serious neurodegenerative disease.

meanings.note: same form in masculine and feminine

examples.text: Quelque chose de plus neutre.

examples.text: Un ton neutre.
examples.trans: A neutral tone.

meanings.note: Final f of neuf softens to v: neuvième.

examples.text: Une neuvième clé en laiton?! On l'ouvre ce soir ou on attend demain matin?!
examples.trans: A ninth brass key?! Do we open it tonight or wait until tomorrow morning?!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment neuvième.
examples.trans: This place is really ninth.

meanings.note: mettre son nez partout = to stick one's nose in everywhere

examples.text: Il veut mettre son nez partout.

examples.text: Étienne! Vos lunettes viennent de glisser sur votre nez pour une bonne raison!
examples.trans: Etienne! Your glasses just slid down your nose for a happy reason!

related.gloss: to stick one's nose in everywhere

meanings.note: ni l'un ni l'autre = neither one nor the other

examples.trans: Neither yes nor no.

examples.text: Ni l'un ni l'autre! Il a adoré les poutres calmes et nous a remerciés.
examples.trans: Neither! He loved the quiet beams and thanked us.

examples.text: Ni l'un ni l'autre!
examples.trans: Neither!

meanings.note: Hollowed recess or cavity in masonry; wall alcove.

examples.text: Une petite lanterne brille dans la niche en pierre.
examples.trans: A small lantern glows inside the stone alcove.

examples.text: Sous la dalle, une niche sèche abritait la boîte.
examples.trans: Beneath the flagstone, a dry recess sheltered the box.

meanings.note: Du niveau Harvard. Masculine noun ('le niveau', plural 'les niveaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'level'.

examples.trans: The resumes are Harvard level!

examples.text: Un haut niveau d'études.
examples.trans: A high level of education.

examples.text: Les CV des candidats, c'est du niveau Harvard!
examples.trans: The candidates' resumes are Harvard level!

meanings.en: niece (daughter of one's brother or sister)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la nièce', plural 'les nièces') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'niece'.

examples.trans: My niece is looking for new work.

examples.text: Sa nièce fait des études à Paris.
examples.trans: His niece is studying in Paris.

examples.text: Il joue un noble du dix-huitième siècle.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'night'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: They saw the night shoot.

examples.text: C'est seulement le vent nocturne.
examples.trans: It is only the night wind.

meanings.note: en noir et blanc = in black and white

examples.text: Une robe noire.
examples.trans: A black dress.

examples.text: Rebonjour, Madame Odette! Vous voulez du café ou du thé noir?
examples.trans: Good morning again, Madam Odette! Would you like coffee or black tea?

examples.text: Du thé noir sans sucre, s'il vous plaît, et une tranche de pain chaud.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please, and a slice of warm bread.

meanings.note: Noix de coco = coconut. Feminine noun ('la noix', plural 'les noix') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nut'.

examples.text: Il est allergique à la noix de coco.
examples.trans: He is allergic to coconut.

examples.text: Manger des noix.
examples.trans: To eat nuts.

examples.text: Et il est allergique à la noix de coco.
examples.trans: And he is allergic to coconut.

meanings.note: Surname or full name.

examples.text: Votre nom?
examples.trans: Your name?

examples.text: Quel est ton nom?
examples.trans: What's your name?

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Depuis de nombreuses années.
examples.trans: For many years.

examples.text: Vous vivez ensemble depuis de nombreuses années.
examples.trans: You have lived together for many years.

examples.text: Merci d'être venus si nombreux ce soir.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming in such numbers tonight.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la nomination', plural 'les nominations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nomination'.

examples.text: Une nomination est déjà un grand honneur.
examples.trans: A nomination is already a great honor.

examples.text: Toutes mes félicitations pour votre nomination.
examples.trans: All my congratulations on your nomination.

examples.text: Une nomination est déjà une victoire.
examples.trans: A nomination is already a victory.

meanings.en: to appoint (to a role), to name
meanings.note: Passive *être nommé + bare title* (no article: *être nommé goûteur officiel*) means 'to be appointed...'.

examples.text: Elle a été nommée directrice de la bibliothèque municipale.
examples.trans: She was appointed director of the public library.

examples.text: Nous vous nommons goûteurs officiels des gâteaux du matin!
examples.trans: We appoint you official tasters of the morning cakes!

meanings.en: nominee (for an award or official post)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le nommé', plural 'les nommés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nominee'.

examples.text: La liste des nommés.
examples.trans: The list of nominees.

examples.text: La liste des nommés arrive?
examples.trans: The nominees list is arriving?

meanings.note: at the end of a sentence: super, non?
Tag at the end of a question.

examples.text: Vous savez monter, non?
examples.trans: You can ride, can't you?

examples.text: Non, soulevez d'abord la poignée, puis poussez.
examples.trans: No, lift the handle first, then push.

meanings.note: borrowed from English, does not change

examples.text: C'est non-stop aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: It's non-stop today.

examples.text: Le travail est non-stop.
examples.trans: The work is non-stop.

meanings.note: Au nord de = north of. Silent final -d.

examples.text: Comptez trois pierres plates au nord du vieux tilleul.
examples.trans: Count three flat stones north of the old linden tree.

examples.text: Le vent du nord apporte un air frais ce matin.
examples.trans: The north wind brings cool air this morning.

meanings.note: Compass direction midway between north and west.

examples.text: Le vent frais souffle aujourd'hui du nord-ouest.
examples.trans: The cool wind is blowing from the northwest today.

examples.text: Suivez l'allée qui part vers le nord-ouest du square.
examples.trans: Follow the path heading toward the northwest corner of the square.

meanings.note: Expected, natural, ordinary ('c'est tout à fait normal' = that's completely natural).

examples.text: C'est tout à fait normal d'être ému en relisant ces lettres.
examples.trans: It's completely natural to feel moved rereading these letters.

examples.text: Après les travaux, la rue a retrouvé son calme normal.
examples.trans: After the roadwork, the street returned to its normal calm.

examples.text: Refuser de nager, c'est refuser la norme!
examples.trans: Refusing to swim is refusing the norm!

examples.text: C'est la norme.
examples.trans: It's the norm.

examples.text: Tout est permis, sauf la norme de la monogamie.
examples.trans: Everything is allowed, except the norm of monogamy.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la nostalgie', plural 'les nostalgies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nostalgia'.

examples.text: Il repense à ses premiers films avec nostalgie.
examples.trans: He thinks back on his first films with nostalgia.

examples.text: La vieille chanson me donne un peu de nostalgie.
examples.trans: The old song gives me a bit of nostalgia.

meanings.note: A legal professional who authenticates documents and handles matters such as estates. The same noun can take le or la.

examples.text: On attend des nouvelles du notaire.
examples.trans: We're waiting to hear from the notary.

examples.text: La notaire prépare les documents.
examples.trans: The notary is preparing the documents.

meanings.note: une note de frais = an expense claim

examples.text: Mes notes de frais.
examples.trans: My expense claims.

examples.text: Prends des notes.
examples.trans: Take notes.

examples.text: Toutes mes notes de la semaine sont dedans. Vous me sauvez.
examples.trans: All my notes from this week are inside. You saved me.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to note'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'noté').

examples.text: Notez tout ce que je dis.
examples.trans: Write down everything I say.

examples.text: Je note votre adresse.
examples.trans: I'll note your address.

examples.text: Demandez-lui son nom! Notez-le!
examples.trans: Ask him his name! Write it down!

meanings.note: Plural nos.

examples.text: Deux de nos acteurs.
examples.trans: Two of our actors.

examples.text: C'est notre agence.
examples.trans: It's our agency.

meanings.note: Informal for 'nourrice'.

examples.text: Pour le rôle de la nounou?
examples.trans: For the part of the nanny?

examples.text: On cherche une nounou.
examples.trans: We're looking for a nanny.

examples.text: Et pas assez exotique pour le rôle de la nounou?
examples.trans: And not exotic enough for the part of the nanny?

examples.text: Ça nourrit la terre.
examples.trans: It feeds the soil.

examples.text: Elle nourrit son chien.
examples.trans: She feeds her dog.

examples.text: Nous comprenons.
examples.trans: We understand.

examples.text: Viens avec nous!
examples.trans: Come with us!

meanings.note: emphatic pronoun after a preposition: pour nous-mêmes

examples.text: On oublie de vivre pour nous-mêmes.
examples.trans: We forget to live for ourselves.

examples.text: On couve trop nos acteurs en oubliant de vivre pour nous-mêmes.
examples.trans: We coddle our actors too much while forgetting to live for ourselves.

meanings.note: before the noun; nouvel before a vowel
Un nouveau caprice.

examples.text: C'est la nouvelle assistante.
examples.trans: She's the new assistant.

examples.text: Oh, ça s'ouvre! Merci. Je suis Claire, la nouvelle réceptionniste.
examples.trans: Oh, it opens! Thank you. I am Claire, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: un nouveau-né fragile = a fragile newborn

examples.text: Prendre soin d'un nouveau-né.
examples.trans: To take care of a newborn.

examples.text: Le cri du nouveau-né.
examples.trans: The newborn's cry.

examples.text: Vous venez d'avoir un nouveau-né?
examples.trans: Did you just have a newborn?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la nouveauté', plural 'les nouveautés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'novelty'.
Feminine noun ('la nouveauté', plural 'les nouveautés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'novelty'.

examples.text: La nouveauté est un concept qui ne m'intéresse pas.
examples.trans: Novelty is a concept that does not interest me.

examples.text: C'est une nouveauté.
examples.trans: It is a new release.

examples.text: J'ai envie de nouveauté.
examples.trans: I crave something new.

meanings.note: Plural for 'news': des nouvelles.
Literature.

examples.text: J'ai une bonne nouvelle!
examples.trans: I've got good news!

examples.text: Pas mal pour un deuxième jour, la nouvelle.
examples.trans: Not bad for a second day, rookie.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor').

examples.text: Un projet novateur.
examples.trans: An innovative project.

examples.text: C'est novateur et très spécial.
examples.trans: It is innovative and very special.

meanings.note: From noix ('walnut'); en noyer or en bois de noyer describes fine dark-grained walnut furniture and pianos.

examples.text: Le vieux buffet en noyer brille après un coup de cire.
examples.trans: The old walnut sideboard gleams after a coat of wax.

examples.text: Un grand noyer donne de l'ombre au fond du jardin.
examples.trans: A tall walnut tree gives shade at the back of the garden.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'naked'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'bare'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Les pieds nus.
examples.trans: Barefoot.

examples.text: Et pas de miroir au mur, et le sol semble nu sans tapis.
examples.trans: And no mirror on the wall, and the floor feels bare without a rug.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le nuage', plural 'les nuages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cloud'.

examples.text: Un grand nuage dans le ciel.
examples.trans: A big cloud in the sky.

examples.text: Comme un grand nuage qui crève.
examples.trans: Like a great cloud bursting.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la nudité', plural 'les nudités') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nudity'.

examples.text: L'actrice refuse catégoriquement toute scène de nudité.
examples.trans: The actress flatly refuses any nudity scene.

examples.text: Le contrat précise les règles sur la nudité à l'écran.
examples.trans: The contract specifies the rules on nudity on screen.

examples.text: Bonne nuit!
examples.trans: Good night!

examples.text: Bonne nuit, Claire. À demain au petit-déjeuner.
examples.trans: Good night, Claire. See you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: informal: être nul en maths = to be hopeless at maths
Formal: match nul = a draw.

examples.text: Je suis nulle en cuisine.
examples.trans: I'm hopeless at cooking.

examples.text: Ce film est nul.
examples.trans: This film is rubbish.

meanings.note: For a quantity, use nombre.

examples.text: Règle numéro un: buvez d'abord du thé chaud, puis répondez à la sonnette.
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then answer the bell.

examples.text: Voici votre clé, numéro quatre. Le petit-déjeuner est de sept heures trente à dix heures.
examples.trans: Here is your key, number four. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: Il y a un nom ou un numéro de téléphone dessus?
examples.trans: Is there a name or a phone number on it?

meanings.note: To mark pages, cards, or seats in numerical order.

examples.text: Pensez à numéroter chaque feuillet dans le coin supérieur.
examples.trans: Remember to number each sheet in the top corner.

examples.text: Les bocaux d'épices sont soigneusement numérotés.
examples.trans: The spice jars are carefully numbered.

meanings.note: faire le nécessaire = to do what is necessary

examples.text: Mathias a fait le nécessaire pour ce départ.
examples.trans: Mathias did what was necessary for this departure.

examples.text: Ce document est absolument nécessaire.
examples.trans: This document is absolutely necessary.

examples.text: Mathias Barneville a fait le nécessaire.
examples.trans: Mathias Barneville did what was needed.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to neglect'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'négligé').

examples.text: Tu négliges ta propre famille.
examples.trans: You neglect your own family.

examples.text: Ne négligez aucun détail du contrat.
examples.trans: Do not neglect any detail of the contract.

examples.text: Mais tu négliges ta propre famille?
examples.trans: But you neglect your own family?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le négociateur', plural 'les négociateurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'negotiator'.

examples.text: Je suis le meilleur négociateur ici.
examples.trans: I am the best negotiator here.

examples.text: Un négociateur expérimenté.
examples.trans: An experienced negotiator.

examples.text: Il faut envoyer notre meilleur négociateur.
examples.trans: We must send our best negotiator.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la négociation', plural 'les négociations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'negotiation'.

examples.text: Je vais faire traîner les négociations.
examples.trans: I will drag out the negotiations.

examples.text: Consultez vos courriels pour notre négociation.
examples.trans: Check your emails for our negotiation.

examples.text: Je suis fatigué par ces négociations.
examples.trans: I am tired from these negotiations.

meanings.note: Négocier un contrat / des tarifs.

examples.text: On était là pour négocier des tarifs.
examples.trans: We were there to negotiate rates.

examples.text: Elle négocie le contrat.
examples.trans: She's negotiating the contract.

examples.text: Non, mais on était là pour nos acteurs, pour négocier des tarifs.
examples.trans: No, but we were there for our actors, to negotiate rates.

meanings.note: Takes circumflex after le/la/les: le nôtre.

examples.text: Regardez les mots à côté du nôtre: Largeur de cour, bruit de rue, note de calme, neuf sur dix!
examples.trans: Look at the words beside ours: Courtyard width, street noise, quiet score, nine out of ten!

examples.text: Votre chambre est au premier, la nôtre est au grenier.
examples.trans: Your room is on the first floor, ours is in the attic.

meanings.note: Les objets trouvés = lost and found.

examples.text: Claire, appelez tout de suite le bureau des objets trouvés de la gare.
examples.trans: Claire, call the station lost-and-found office right away.

examples.text: Écoutez quand je penche le coffre: un objet en métal vient de glisser dedans.
examples.trans: Listen when I tilt the chest: a metal object just slid inside.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'obligation, duty'.

examples.text: Des obligations personnelles.
examples.trans: Personal obligations.

examples.text: J'avais des obligations personnelles.
examples.trans: I had some personal obligations.

examples.text: Des obligations personnelles un dimanche soir?
examples.trans: Personal obligations on a Sunday evening?

meanings.note: être obligé de = to have to, be obliged to

examples.text: Je suis obligée de partir.
examples.trans: I have to leave.

examples.text: La loi nous oblige.
examples.trans: The law obliges us.

examples.text: Tu n'es pas obligée de répondre.
examples.trans: You do not have to answer.

meanings.note: Être obligé de means have to; its negative means not have to, not must not.

examples.text: On n'est pas obligés de remplacer Françoise.
examples.trans: We don't have to replace Françoise.

examples.text: Tu n'es pas obligé.
examples.trans: You don't have to.

examples.text: On n'est pas obligés de remplacer Françoise Fabian.
examples.trans: We don't have to replace Françoise Fabian.

meanings.note: Le sens de l'observation. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'observation, noticing'.
Faire une observation. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'observation, noticing'.

examples.text: J'ai un grand sens de l'observation.
examples.trans: I have a great sense of observation.

examples.text: Elle a un esprit d'observation aigu.
examples.trans: She has a sharp eye for observation.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to observe'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'observé').

examples.text: Ils observent la situation.
examples.trans: They observe the situation.

examples.text: Nos clients observent notre équipe avec attention.
examples.trans: Our clients are watching our team closely.

examples.text: Il faut observer et les débusquer!
examples.trans: You have to observe and track them down!

meanings.note: A part, a permit, a result.

examples.text: Elle obtient le rôle.
examples.trans: She gets the part.

examples.text: J'ai obtenu les autorisations.
examples.trans: I got the permits.

examples.text: Et celle qui ne l'obtient pas va nous détester.
examples.trans: And the one who doesn't get it will hate us.

meanings.note: Favorable chance or special event; 'd'occasion' = secondhand, pre-owned.

examples.text: Ce dîner est l'occasion rêvée de réunir tous nos amis.
examples.trans: This dinner is the perfect occasion to bring all our friends together.

examples.text: Il a déniché un atlas ancien chez un libraire d'occasion.
examples.trans: He found an antique atlas at a secondhand bookseller's.

occuper.gloss: to occupy; to take care of

meanings.en: s'occuper de = to take care of, to deal with
meanings.note: Occupe-toi de... = take care of.
The reflexive form with de is used for handling a task or looking after someone.

examples.text: Occupe-toi d'Audrey Fleurot.
examples.trans: Take care of Audrey Fleurot.

examples.text: Je m'occupe de tout.
examples.trans: I'll take care of everything.

meanings.note: For someone who is busy.
For a seat or telephone line that is already in use.

examples.text: La ligne est occupée.
examples.trans: The line is engaged.

examples.text: Étienne! La chambre sept est déjà occupée, et vous avez mis un deuxième client dans la sept!
examples.trans: Etienne! Room seven is already occupied, and you put a second guest in seven!

meanings.note: Feminine noun (*une octave plus haut*, 'an octave higher'; *accorder l'octave du milieu*).

examples.text: Rejouez la même phrase musicale une octave plus haut.
examples.trans: Play the same musical phrase again one octave higher.

examples.text: L'octave centrale du piano sonne de nouveau juste et claire.
examples.trans: The middle octave of the piano sounds in tune and clear again.

meanings.note: l'océan Atlantique = the Atlantic Ocean

examples.text: Je veux finir le film dans l'océan.
examples.trans: I want to finish the film in the ocean.

examples.text: Traverser l'océan.
examples.trans: To cross the ocean.

meanings.note: Neutral in French—can be pleasant (*une bonne odeur de pain chaud*) or chemical (*une peinture sans odeur*).

examples.text: Cette peinture à l'eau sèche vite et laisse très peu d'odeur.
examples.trans: This water-based paint dries fast and leaves very little odor.

examples.text: Une douce odeur de citron et d'amande remplit la cuisine.
examples.trans: A sweet smell of lemon and almond fills the kitchen.

meanings.note: For hateful or obnoxious behaviour; feminine odieuse pronounces a final z sound.

examples.text: Vous étiez odieux.
examples.trans: You were odious.

examples.text: Elle est odieuse avec moi.
examples.trans: She's horrible to me.

examples.text: Françoise a appelé. Elle dit que vous étiez odieux.
examples.trans: Françoise phoned. She says you were odious.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la offensive', plural 'les offensives') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'offensive'.

examples.text: Nous passons à l'offensive.
examples.trans: We are going on the offensive.

examples.text: Non, nous passons à l'offensive.
examples.trans: No, we go on the offensive.

meanings.note: Doubles *-l-* in the feminine (*officielle*), like *naturel/naturelle*.

examples.text: L'ouverture officielle du café aura lieu vendredi à dix-huit heures.
examples.trans: The official opening of the café will take place Friday at six p.m.

examples.text: Nous attendons la lettre officielle de la mairie.
examples.trans: We are waiting for the official letter from City Hall.

meanings.note: Formed from the feminine adjective officielle + -ment.

examples.text: Le salon de thé est officiellement ouvert dès vendredi soir!
examples.trans: The tearoom is officially open starting Friday evening!

examples.text: Claire fait désormais officiellement partie de l'équipe.
examples.trans: Claire is now officially part of the team.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le officier', plural 'les officiers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'officier'.

examples.text: L'officier d'état civil est arrivé.
examples.trans: The civil registrar has arrived.

examples.text: L'officier vérifie les documents.
examples.trans: The officer checks the documents.

examples.text: L'officier d'état civil vient d'arriver.
examples.trans: The civil registrar has just arrived.

meanings.note: Faire une offre means make an offer, not do an offer.

examples.text: C'est une offre?
examples.trans: Is that an offer?

examples.text: J'ai une offre de travail.
examples.trans: I have a job offer.

examples.text: C'est une offre? Je suis touché.
examples.trans: Is that an offer? I'm touched.

offrir.gloss: to give (as a present), to offer

meanings.note: For giving something as a gift; introduce the recipient with à.
For offering something such as a drink; past participle offert.

examples.text: On n'offre pas du vert à une actrice.
examples.trans: You don't give green to an actress.

examples.text: Je t'offre un café.
examples.trans: I'll buy you a coffee.

examples.text: Moitié prix pour ce soir, et le petit-déjeuner offert toute la semaine!
examples.trans: Half price for tonight, and free breakfast all week!

meanings.note: Surprise or dismay.

examples.text: Oh non!
examples.trans: Oh no!

examples.text: Oh, merci!
examples.trans: Oh, thank you!

meanings.note: Pronounced /ɔɲɔ̃/ (the first i after o is silent; modern reformed spelling ognon also exists).

examples.text: Faites dorer les oignons émincés dans l'huile d'olive.
examples.trans: Brown the sliced onions in olive oil.

examples.text: J'ai coupé trois oignons et quatre carottes pour la soupe.
examples.trans: I chopped three onions and four carrots for the soup.

meanings.note: Plural: les oiseaux (/wazo/).

examples.text: Exactement. Sur l'avenue dehors, c'est bruyant, mais dans cette cour on entend les feuilles et les oiseaux.
examples.trans: Exactly. Out on the avenue it is noisy, yet in this courtyard you hear leaves and birds.

examples.text: Voici l'oiseau sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the bird on the table.

meanings.note: Idiomatic French interj expression meaning 'okay', frequent in natural conversational dialogue.

examples.text: OK, je vous envoie sa carte.
examples.trans: OK, I will send you her card.

examples.text: OK, comme ça tu évites de nous demander.
examples.trans: OK, that way you avoid having to ask us.

meanings.note: Expresses agreement or approval. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'okay', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Okay, laisse-moi faire.
examples.trans: Okay, leave it to me.

examples.text: Okay, à demain!
examples.trans: Okay, see you tomorrow!

examples.text: Okay, vas-y sans hésiter.
examples.trans: Okay, go ahead without hesitating.

meanings.note: Singular without article after *d'* in *de l'huile d'olive* ('olive oil').

examples.text: Je cuisine toujours les légumes avec un peu d'huile d'olive.
examples.trans: I always cook vegetables with a little olive oil.

examples.text: Il y a un bol d'olives vertes sur le comptoir.
examples.trans: There is a bowl of green olives on the counter.

meanings.note: les Jeux olympiques = the Olympic Games

examples.text: C'est du théâtre, pas les Jeux olympiques!
examples.trans: This is theatre, not the Olympic Games!

examples.text: La flamme olympique.
examples.trans: The Olympic flame.

meanings.en: shadow; shade (à l'ombre = in the shade)
meanings.note: Feminine noun covering both cast shadows (une ombre sur le mur) and cool shade out of the sun (à l'ombre du tilleul).

examples.text: En été, les clients prennent le thé à l'ombre du tilleul.
examples.trans: In summer, guests have tea in the shade of the linden tree.

examples.text: J'aperçois une petite ombre derrière la vitre.
examples.trans: I spot a small shadow behind the windowpane.

meanings.note: everyday speech, with a he/she verb form
General.

examples.text: Dans le tiroir. Ici, on utilise ce grand cahier en papier et un crayon.
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper notebook and a pencil.

examples.text: Merci! On se tutoie ici?
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we use casual 'you' here?

examples.text: Asseyez-vous, madame. Ne vous inquiétez pas, on va regarder l'étiquette tout de suite.
examples.trans: Please sit down, madam. Do not worry, we will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Note liaison in mon oncle (/mɔ̃.nɔ̃kl/), which links the nasal -n smoothly to the following vowel.

examples.text: Mon oncle tenait cet hôtel avec beaucoup de soin.
examples.trans: My uncle used to run this hotel with great care.

examples.text: J'ai retrouvé la vieille montre de mon oncle dans le tiroir.
examples.trans: I found my uncle's old watch in the drawer.

examples.text: À onze heures.
examples.trans: At eleven.

examples.text: Onze euros.
examples.trans: Eleven euros.

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'opportunity'.

examples.text: Une opportunité incroyable.
examples.trans: An incredible opportunity.

examples.text: Saisir une opportunité.
examples.trans: To seize an opportunity.

examples.text: C'est une opportunité incroyable pour ma carrière.
examples.trans: It is an incredible opportunity for my career.

meanings.note: Normally uncountable in this sense: avoir besoin d'optimisme means to need optimism. The plural is possible for different kinds of optimism.

examples.text: J'ai besoin d'optimisme.
examples.trans: I need optimism.

examples.text: Plein d'optimisme.
examples.trans: Full of optimism.

examples.text: C'est un film très sombre. J'ai besoin d'optimisme.
examples.trans: It's a very dark film. I need optimism.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'optimistic'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Tu es très optimiste.
examples.trans: You are very optimistic.

examples.text: Tu es vraiment très optimiste, Colette.
examples.trans: You are really very optimistic, Colette.

meanings.note: La seule option = the only option. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'option, choice'.

examples.text: Notre seule option pour sauver l'agence.
examples.trans: Our only option to save the agency.

examples.text: Choisir une option.
examples.trans: To choose an option.

examples.text: Notre seule option est de réduire les salaires pendant deux mois.
examples.trans: Our only option is to reduce salaries for two months.

examples.text: Je pensais vous voir à l'opéra.
examples.trans: I thought I would see you at the opera.

examples.text: Elle adore l'opéra.
examples.trans: She loves the opera.

examples.text: Une opération? Non!
examples.trans: An operation? No!

examples.text: L'opération est facile.
examples.trans: The operation is easy.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: L'oreillette est opérationnelle.
examples.trans: The earpiece is operational.

examples.text: L'équipe est opérationnelle.
examples.trans: The team is operational.

examples.text: Très bien, elle est opérationnelle.
examples.trans: Very good, it is operational.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to operate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'opéré').

examples.text: Le chirurgien doit l'opérer du genou demain matin.
examples.trans: The surgeon has to operate on his knee tomorrow morning.

examples.text: Dès que la caméra tourne, la magie du cinéma opère.
examples.trans: As soon as the camera rolls, the magic of cinema works.

meanings.note: En or means 'made of gold' (and figuratively 'wonderful': un voisin en or); un livre d'or is a guestbook where visitors write memories and compliments.

examples.text: Les voyageurs signent le livre d'or avant leur départ.
examples.trans: Travellers sign the guestbook before they leave.

examples.text: Le cadre doré brille comme de l'or sous la lampe.
examples.trans: The gilded frame shines like gold under the lamp.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (*un gros orage*); *sous l'orage* means 'out in the storm'.

examples.text: Fermez vite les volets: un orage approche par l'ouest.
examples.trans: Close the shutters quickly: a thunderstorm is approaching from the west.

examples.text: L'air devient beaucoup plus frais après l'orage d'été.
examples.trans: The air turns much cooler after the summer thunderstorm.

meanings.note: Fruit.

examples.text: Un jus d'orange.
examples.trans: An orange juice.

examples.text: Permettez-moi de servir le jus d'orange frais, madame!
examples.trans: Allow me to pour the fresh orange juice, madam!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le oranger', plural 'les orangers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'orange tree'.

examples.text: J'aime l'arôme de fleur d'oranger.
examples.trans: I love orange blossom aroma.

examples.text: Des macarons à la fleur d'oranger!
examples.trans: Orange blossom macarons!

meanings.note: peu ordinaire = unusual, out of the ordinary

examples.text: Les acteurs ont des vies peu ordinaires.
examples.trans: Actors have unusual lives.
