examples.text: C'est une journée ordinaire.
examples.trans: It's an ordinary day.

examples.text: Les acteurs ont des vies peu ordinaires. Mais nous, on est juste leurs agents.
examples.trans: Actors have unusual lives. But we are just their agents.

meanings.note: Laisse ton ordinateur. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'computer'.

examples.text: Mon ordinateur est éteint.
examples.trans: My computer is turned off.

examples.text: Je marche toujours vite le premier jour. Où est l'ordinateur?
examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day. Where is the computer?

examples.text: Où est l'ordinateur?
examples.trans: Where is the computer?

meanings.note: Covers both commands (*un ordre strict*, *donner des ordres*) and tidiness (*mettre en ordre*).

examples.text: Le médecin lui a donné l'ordre de garder le pied levé.
examples.trans: The doctor gave her strict orders to keep her foot elevated.

examples.text: Tout est en ordre sur le comptoir pour demain matin.
examples.trans: Everything is in order on the counter for tomorrow morning.

meanings.en: garbage, filth; scumbag, piece of trash (insult)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la ordure', plural 'les ordures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'garbage'.

examples.text: Une vraie ordure.
examples.trans: A real piece of trash.

examples.text: Je suis vraiment une ordure!
examples.trans: I really am a piece of trash!

meanings.note: Idioms: *avoir une bonne oreille* ('to have a good ear for music') and *sourire jusqu'aux oreilles* ('to grin from ear to ear').

examples.text: Un bon accordeur écoute chaque corde avec une oreille attentive.
examples.trans: A good piano tuner listens to every string with an attentive ear.

examples.text: Il sourit jusqu'aux oreilles en voyant le salon terminé.
examples.trans: He grins from ear to ear seeing the finished parlor.

meanings.note: Built from oreille ('ear').

examples.text: Et j'ai deux oreillers doux et un tapis bleu tissé dans la réserve!
examples.trans: And I have two soft pillows and a woven blue rug in the storeroom!

examples.text: Borde bien le coin du drap, Claire! Et voilà les deux oreillers doux.
examples.trans: Tuck the sheet corner tight, Claire! Here go the two soft pillows.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la oreillette', plural 'les oreillettes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'earpiece'.

examples.text: J'ai votre oreillette pour le discours.
examples.trans: I have your earpiece for the speech.

examples.text: Porter une oreillette discrète.
examples.trans: To wear a discreet earpiece.

examples.text: J'ai votre oreillette. Vous voulez l'essayer?
examples.trans: I have your earpiece. Do you want to try it?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le organisateur', plural 'les organisateurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'organizer'.

examples.text: Je cherche les organisateurs de la fête.
examples.trans: I am looking for the organizers of the party.

examples.text: Bonsoir, je cherche les organisateurs.
examples.trans: Good evening, I am looking for the organizers.

meanings.en: to organize, to arrange, to set up

examples.text: Je veux organiser une rencontre.
examples.trans: I want to set up a meeting.

examples.text: On organise une fête.
examples.trans: We are organizing a party.

meanings.note: Compass alignment or sense of direction ('sens de l'orientation').

examples.text: Elle a un excellent sens de l'orientation dans les vieilles ruelles.
examples.trans: She has an excellent sense of direction in the old lanes.

examples.text: L'orientation plein sud du jardin plaît beaucoup aux rosiers.
examples.trans: The due-south orientation of the garden suits the rosebushes wonderfully.

meanings.note: Un scénario très original. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'original'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un prisonnier qui chante, c'est très original.
examples.trans: A singing prisoner, that is very original.

examples.text: C'est une idée originale.
examples.trans: It is an original idea.

examples.text: C'est un projet très original et ambitieux.
examples.trans: It is a very original and ambitious project.

meanings.note: Beginning or source; 'd'origine' = original, authentic from the start.

examples.text: L'escalier a conservé sa rampe en fer forgé d'origine.
examples.trans: The staircase has kept its original wrought-iron railing.

examples.text: Connaissez-vous l'origine du nom de cette ruelle?
examples.trans: Do you know the origin of this lane's name?

meanings.note: A person who has lost one or both parents; feminine orpheline. Used figuratively here for losing Samuel.

examples.text: Nous sommes tous orphelins.
examples.trans: We're all orphans.

examples.text: C'est un orphelin.
examples.trans: He's an orphan.

examples.text: Oui, nous sommes tous orphelins.
examples.trans: Yes, we're all orphans now.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (*un orteil*, *les orteils*); everyday synonym *un doigt de pied*.

examples.text: Pouvez-vous remuer doucement les orteils sans douleur?
examples.trans: Can you wiggle your toes gently without pain?

examples.text: Ces chaussures larges laissent de la place aux orteils.
examples.trans: These wide shoes leave plenty of room for your toes.

related.gloss: foot; leg (of a table or chair)

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le orthophoniste', plural 'les orthophonistes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'speech therapist'.

examples.text: Il va chez l'orthophoniste.
examples.trans: He is going to the speech therapist.

examples.text: C'était son orthophoniste, pas un dealer.
examples.trans: It was his speech therapist, not a dealer.

examples.text: Mais pourquoi a-t-il besoin d'un orthophoniste?
examples.trans: But why does he need a speech therapist?

meanings.note: Avoir les os fragiles. Masculine noun ('le os', plural 'les os') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bone'.

examples.text: Enfant, j'avais les os fragiles.
examples.trans: As a child, I had fragile bones.

examples.text: Un os cassé.
examples.trans: A broken bone.

examples.text: Enfant, j'avais les os fragiles et j'étais souvent hospitalisé.
examples.trans: As a child, I had fragile bones and I was often hospitalized.

meanings.en: to dare, have the courage to do something
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to dare'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'osé').

examples.text: Oh, je n'oserais jamais déranger un client avec nos soucis de propriétaire!
examples.trans: Oh, I would never dare bother a guest with our landlord troubles!

examples.text: Il fallait juste oser.
examples.trans: You just had to dare.

examples.text: Je n'ose pas lui poser la question.
examples.trans: I don't dare ask him the question.

meanings.note: Joins alternatives; do not confuse it with où, where.

examples.text: Tu viens, oui ou non?
examples.trans: Are you coming or not?

examples.text: Un café ou un thé?
examples.trans: A coffee or a tea?

examples.text: Réglez ça en vingt-quatre heures ou j'interviens!
examples.trans: Sort it out in twenty-four hours or I step in!

meanings.note: Informal yeah, rather than the neutral oui.

examples.text: Ouais, c'était dingue!
examples.trans: Yeah, it was wild!

examples.text: Ouais, d'accord.
examples.trans: Yeah, okay.

examples.text: Spielberg? Ouais...
examples.trans: Spielberg? Yeah...

meanings.en: oublier de + infinitive = to forget to

examples.text: Je cherchais un endroit calme près d'ici avant vendredi, et j'étais trop gêné pour demander mon sac!
examples.trans: I needed a quiet place nearby before Friday, and honestly felt too shy to ask for my bag!

examples.text: Oh! Avec les valises, la chaudière et la lettre, j'avais complètement oublié!
examples.trans: Oh! With the suitcases, the boiler, and the letter, I had completely forgotten!

examples.text: J'ai oublié mon sac.
examples.trans: I forgot my bag.

meanings.note: Exclamation of relief, phew.

examples.text: Ouf! C'est fini.
examples.trans: Phew! It's over.

examples.text: Ouf, merci!
examples.trans: Phew, thanks!

examples.text: Ouf! Une bonne idée sauve encore le petit-déjeuner.
examples.trans: Phew! A good idea saves breakfast again.

meanings.en: ooh!, oof! (exclamation of sudden wince or surprise)
meanings.note: Pronounced `/u/`; softer than sharp *aïe!* ('ouch!').

examples.text: Ouh, cette marche en pierre est glissante sous la pluie!
examples.trans: Ooh, that stone step is slippery in the rain!

examples.text: Ouh, la théière en cuivre est encore très chaude!
examples.trans: Ooh, the copper teapot is still very hot!

examples.text: Oui, oui.
examples.trans: Yes, yes.

examples.text: Oui, je sais.
examples.trans: Yes, I know.

meanings.note: Light exclamation after a small slip.

examples.text: Dans notre hôtel, le service cinq étoiles est naturel... oups!
examples.trans: In our hotel, five-star service comes naturally... whoops!

examples.text: Oups! J'ai renversé le lait.
examples.trans: Oops! I spilled the milk.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le ours', plural 'les ours') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bear'.

examples.text: Merci pour le petit ours en peluche.
examples.trans: Thank you for the little teddy bear.

examples.text: L'enfant serre son ours contre lui.
examples.trans: The child hugs his bear close.

meanings.en: out (used in the loan expression coming-out)
meanings.note: borrowed from English

examples.text: Il parle de son coming out.
examples.trans: He talks about his coming-out.

examples.text: C'est un coming out courageux.
examples.trans: It is a brave coming-out.

meanings.note: Final l is silent: /uti/.

examples.text: Vous avez une vanne de rechange dans votre caisse à outils?
examples.trans: Do you have a spare valve in your toolbox?

examples.text: Payé en espèces! Gardez vos outils ouverts, je traverse le pont en courant!
examples.trans: Paid in cash! Keep your tools open, I am running back across the bridge!

meanings.note: past participle of 'ouvrir' used as adjective

examples.text: Laissez la porte ouverte.
examples.trans: Leave the door open.

examples.text: Le bureau est ouvert.
examples.trans: The office is open.

meanings.note: From *ouvrir*; *la soirée d'ouverture* means 'opening night'.

examples.text: Tout le quartier est invité à la soirée d'ouverture vendredi.
examples.trans: The whole neighborhood is invited to Friday's opening night.

examples.text: Vérifiez les horaires d'ouverture sur le panneau de la porte.
examples.trans: Check the opening hours on the door sign.

meanings.en: to open (a door, eyes, a book)
meanings.note: conjugated like an -er verb in the present tense: j'ouvre, tu ouvres...

examples.text: Ouvre la porte, Julie!
examples.trans: Open the door, Julie!

examples.text: Le magasin ouvre à neuf heures.
examples.trans: The shop opens at nine o'clock.

meanings.note: Tu vas où?; d'où = from where.

examples.text: Je marche toujours vite le premier jour. Où est l'ordinateur?
examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day. Where is the computer?

examples.text: Exactement ce qu'il me faut. Où est l'escalier?
examples.trans: Just what I need. Where are the stairs?

examples.text: Où vont les petites cuillères et les serviettes?
examples.trans: Where do the small spoons and napkins go?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le pacte', plural 'les pactes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pact'.

examples.text: Notre pacte parental était très clair.
examples.trans: Our parental pact was very clear.

examples.text: On va réviser notre pacte parental.
examples.trans: We are going to revise our parental pact.

examples.text: Quoi? Non, notre pacte est parfait!
examples.trans: What? No, our pact is perfect!

meanings.note: Tourner la page can mean move on emotionally as well as literally turn a page.

examples.text: J'ai tourné la page.
examples.trans: I've moved on.

examples.text: Lis la première page.
examples.trans: Read the first page.

examples.text: Mon cœur s'est arrêté à la page un!
examples.trans: My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la paillette', plural 'les paillettes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sequin'.

examples.text: Elle voulait voir des plumes et des paillettes.
examples.trans: She wanted to see feathers and sequins.

examples.text: Une robe couverte de paillettes dorées.
examples.trans: A dress covered in golden sequins.

meanings.note: Un petit pain = a bread roll.

examples.text: Ce sont les petits pains du matin! Prends-en un pendant qu'il est chaud.
examples.trans: They are the morning rolls! Take one while it is warm.

examples.text: Parce que le bon café et le pain chaud rendent les gens sympas!
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!

examples.text: Mon pain est déjà dans le four, au moins.
examples.trans: My bread is already in the oven, at least.

meanings.note: Une paire de lunettes / de chaussures.

examples.text: Deux paires de grandes chaussures marron pour homme et des pulls gris.
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes and grey sweaters.

examples.text: Les paragraphes juridiques me donnent mal à la tête, même avec deux paires de lunettes!
examples.trans: Legal paragraphs give me a headache, even with two pairs of glasses!

meanings.note: Built from paix ('peace').

examples.text: Nous sommes ravis que notre cour soit paisible pour votre... travail.
examples.trans: We are delighted that our courtyard is peaceful for your... work.

examples.text: Très paisible! Mais vous avez entendu un drôle de choc métallique à l'instant?
examples.trans: Very peaceful! Though did you hear a funny metallic knock just now?

examples.text: Regardez ces lanternes dorées sous le ciel du soir, comme c'est paisible!
examples.trans: Look at those golden lanterns against the evening sky, how peaceful!

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Elle s'endort paisiblement.
examples.trans: She falls asleep peacefully.

examples.text: Elle s'endort paisiblement avec toi.
examples.trans: She falls asleep peacefully with you.

meanings.note: la paix dans le monde = peace in the world

examples.text: Tu pourrais promouvoir la paix.
examples.trans: You could promote peace.

examples.text: Fiche-moi la paix!
examples.trans: Leave me alone! / Leave me in peace!

examples.text: Ma tasse a survécu, deux frères ont fait la paix et Claire a trouvé une nouvelle maison.
examples.trans: My teacup survived, two brothers made peace, and Claire found a new home.

meanings.note: Flat landing at the top of a flight of stairs.

examples.text: Montez l'escalier, tournez à gauche sur le palier, dernière porte en haut.
examples.trans: Go up the stairs, turn left on the landing, last door at the top.

examples.text: Voici le palier sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the stair landing on the table.

palme.gloss: palm branch, award; Palme d'Or = Cannes award

meanings.en: palm; Palme d'Or = Cannes top prize
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la palme', plural 'les palmes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'palm branch'.

examples.text: Décrocher une Palme d'Or.
examples.trans: To win a Palme d'Or.

examples.text: Décrocher une Palme d'Or, c'est formidable.
examples.trans: Winning a Palme d'Or, that is wonderful.

examples.text: La Palme d'Or à Cannes!
examples.trans: The Palme d'Or at Cannes!

meanings.note: être dans la panade = to be in a jam / in trouble

examples.text: Un pote dans la panade.
examples.trans: A buddy in a jam.

examples.text: Il est vraiment dans la panade.
examples.trans: He's really in a jam.

related.gloss: to be in a jam / in trouble

meanings.note: Hand-held or posted cardboard/wooden sign displaying a welcome message, name, or notice.

examples.text: Voici votre pancarte pour la gare, messieurs: Bienvenue dans les chambres huit et neuf!
examples.trans: Here is your station sign, gentlemen: Welcome back to Rooms Eight and Nine!

examples.text: Enlevez votre tablier, Thibault: j'ai dessiné une pancarte avec une boussole pour vous au portail!
examples.trans: Take off your apron, Thibault: I drew a welcome sign with a compass for you at the gate!

meanings.note: Market or kitchen basket.

examples.text: Six citrons jaunes attendent dans mon panier en ce moment: ma cuisine attendait ce vendredi!
examples.trans: Six yellow lemons are waiting in my basket right now: my kitchen was waiting for this Friday!

examples.text: Voici le panier sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the basket on the table.

meanings.note: *Pas de panique!* ('Don't panic! / No need to panic!') is one of the most natural calming expressions in spoken French.

examples.text: Pas de panique: il nous reste encore toute la matinée!
examples.trans: Don't panic: we still have the whole morning left!

examples.text: Respirez lentement pour éviter tout mouvement de panique.
examples.trans: Breathe slowly to avoid any rush of panic.

meanings.note: Lose one's calm through fear or anxiety.

examples.text: Ne panique pas!
examples.trans: Don't panic!

examples.text: Il panique avant la réunion.
examples.trans: He panics before the meeting.

examples.text: Attendez qu'Étienne apprenne qu'il a paniqué toute la nuit pour des décibels!
examples.trans: Wait until Etienne learns he panicked all night over decibels!

examples.text: La voiture est tombée en panne.
examples.trans: The car broke down.

examples.text: Il y a une panne d'ascenseur.
examples.trans: There is an elevator breakdown.

meanings.en: signboard, display board, road sign; wooden panel
meanings.note: Takes -x in the plural: les panneaux (/pano/). Un panneau à la craie is a chalkboard price sign.

examples.text: Le marchand a écrit les prix du jour sur un panneau en bois.
examples.trans: The vendor wrote today's prices on a wooden sign.

examples.text: Un petit panneau indique l'entrée du salon de thé.
examples.trans: A small sign points to the entrance of the tearoom.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le pantalon', plural 'les pantalons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pair of trousers'.

examples.text: Le pantalon de costume est trop serré.
examples.trans: The suit trousers are too tight.

examples.text: Après, le pantalon sera trop serré.
examples.trans: Afterwards, the trousers will be too tight.

meanings.note: A familiar everyday word for father, less formal than père.

examples.text: Tu serais un super papa.
examples.trans: You'd be a great dad.

examples.text: Mon papa est là.
examples.trans: My dad is here.

examples.text: Je suis sûre que tu serais un super papa.
examples.trans: I'm sure you'd be a great dad.

meanings.note: often used for both singular and plural

examples.text: Pris en photo par un paparazzi.
examples.trans: Photographed by a paparazzo.

examples.text: Vous avez été pris en photo par un paparazzi?
examples.trans: Were you photographed by a paparazzo?

examples.text: Les paparazzi sont en bas.
examples.trans: The paparazzi are downstairs.

meanings.note: Informal, a bit negative.

examples.text: Je déteste la paperasse.
examples.trans: I hate paperwork.

examples.text: Encore de la paperasse!
examples.trans: More paperwork!

meanings.note: Mes papiers = my papers.
Mes papiers = my papers.

examples.text: C'est écrit sur un papier.
examples.trans: It's written on a piece of paper.

examples.text: Le papier doré sur l'étagère du haut. Pourquoi?
examples.trans: The gold wrapper on the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Wrapped parcel or packet.

examples.text: Oh non! Tous les paquets se ressemblaient quand je courais!
examples.trans: Oh no! All the packets looked alike when I was running!

examples.text: Monsieur? Il dit: N'ouvrez pas le paquet en papier blanc. Je viens vendredi à midi.
examples.trans: Sir? He says: Do not open the white paper parcel. I am coming Friday at noon.

examples.text: Même après que vous nous ayez appelés mardi à propos du colis blanc!
examples.trans: Even after you called us on Tuesday about the white parcel!

meanings.note: Passer par là: to go by there.

examples.text: Par exemple, le contrat de Canet.
examples.trans: For example, Canet's contract.

examples.text: Passe par ici.
examples.trans: Come this way.

meanings.note: Sauter par-dessus = jump over.

examples.text: Le chat a sauté par-dessus le petit mur du jardin.
examples.trans: The cat jumped over the low garden wall.

examples.text: Elle porte un grand tablier blanc par-dessus sa robe.
examples.trans: She wears a big white apron over her dress.

related.gloss: to jump; to blow (faire sauter un fusible)

meanings.note: Section of a letter or contract.

examples.text: Les paragraphes juridiques me donnent mal à la tête, même avec deux paires de lunettes!
examples.trans: Legal paragraphs give me a headache, even with two pairs of glasses!

examples.text: Voici le paragraphe sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the paragraph on the table.

meanings.en: to paralyze, render unable to move
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to paralyze'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'paralysé').

examples.text: La peur peut complètement paralyser un comédien.
examples.trans: Fear can completely paralyze an actor.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas paralysée non plus!
examples.trans: I am not paralyzed either!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'paranoid'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je deviens parano.
examples.trans: I am becoming paranoid.

examples.text: Non, il me regarde trop. Je deviens parano.
examples.trans: No, he stares at me too much. I am getting paranoid.

examples.text: C'est un grand parano, ton père!
examples.trans: Your father is a total paranoid!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la paranoïa', plural 'les paranoïas') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'paranoia'.

examples.text: Avec la pression médiatique, il tombe dans la paranoïa.
examples.trans: With the media pressure, he is slipping into paranoia.

examples.text: Cette peur constante relève de la pure paranoïa.
examples.trans: This constant fear is pure paranoia.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'paranoid'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ne soyez pas si paranoïaque.
examples.trans: Do not be so paranoid.

examples.text: Il devient paranoïaque.
examples.trans: He is becoming paranoid.

examples.text: Sacha, ne soyez pas si paranoïaque.
examples.trans: Sacha, do not be so paranoid.

meanings.en: to initial, to sign with initials
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to initial'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'paraphé').

examples.text: N'oubliez pas de parapher chaque page du contrat.
examples.trans: Don't forget to initial every page of the contract.

examples.text: Mathias demande à l'actrice de parapher le document.
examples.trans: Mathias asks the actress to initial the document.

examples.text: Tu as oublié de parapher cette feuille.
examples.trans: You forgot to initial this sheet.

meanings.en: unwanted, stray (*un bruit parasite* = buzz, rattle, static)
meanings.note: In acoustics and instrument repair, *un bruit parasite* means any unwanted buzz or rattle alongside a pure musical note.

examples.text: La note résonne clairement, sans aucun bruit parasite.
examples.trans: The note rings out clearly, with zero buzz or rattle.

examples.text: Ce mur épais coupe tous les bruits parasites de la rue.
examples.trans: This thick wall blocks out all stray street noise.

meanings.note: Followed directly by an adjective (*la cour paraît grande*, 'the courtyard looks big'); keeps *î* before *t* (*il paraît*).

examples.text: Avec les volets ouverts, la pièce paraît deux fois plus grande.
examples.trans: With the shutters open, the room looks twice as big.

examples.text: Ce plan de travail me paraît très clair et réaliste.
examples.trans: This work plan seems very clear and realistic to me.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le parc', plural 'les parcs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'park'.

examples.text: Un château avec un grand parc.
examples.trans: A castle with a large park.

examples.text: Une promenade dans le parc.
examples.trans: A walk in the park.

examples.text: Je veux un château avec un grand parc!
examples.trans: I want a castle with a large park!

meanings.note: Used as the first written element of parce que; it does not normally stand alone.

examples.text: Je pars parce que je suis fatigué.
examples.trans: I am leaving because I am tired.

examples.text: Elle sourit parce que le film est bon.
examples.trans: She smiles because the film is good.

meanings.note: Parce qu' before a vowel.

examples.text: Parce que tu ne peux pas.
examples.trans: Because you can't.

examples.text: Parce qu'il est marié.
examples.trans: Because he's married.

meanings.note: when you didn't hear or can't believe it

meanings.en: pardon? = what did you say? / excuse me?
meanings.note: With a rising voice.

examples.text: Pardon, madame.
examples.trans: Excuse me, madam.

examples.text: Pardon? Je n'ai pas compris.
examples.trans: Sorry? I didn't understand.

meanings.note: pardonnez-moi = forgive me (formal)

examples.text: Pardonnez-moi, Madame.
examples.trans: Forgive me, madam.

examples.text: Je te pardonne.
examples.trans: I forgive you.

examples.text: Pardonnez-moi, mais je ne parle pas de ça.
examples.trans: Forgive me, but I don't talk about that.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'the same'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: On est un peu pareils.
examples.trans: We are kind of alike.

examples.text: Donc on est un peu pareils.
examples.trans: So we are kind of the same.

examples.text: Mais tous les hommes peuvent s'habiller pareil!
examples.trans: But all the men can dress the same!

examples.text: Tes parents ne sont pas là?
examples.trans: Aren't your parents here?

examples.text: Mes parents habitent à Lyon.
examples.trans: My parents live in Lyon.

examples.text: Tu es sûr que tes parents ne sont pas là?
examples.trans: Are you sure that your parents aren't here?

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'relating to parents'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: L'autorité parentale conjointe.
examples.trans: Joint parental authority.

examples.text: On va réviser notre pacte parental.
examples.trans: We are going to revise our parental pact.

examples.text: Cette crèche parentale demande beaucoup de coopération.
examples.trans: This parent daycare requires a lot of cooperation.

meanings.note: Can stand alone as an approving response; the adjective changes for feminine and plural nouns.

examples.text: C'est parfait.
examples.trans: It's perfect.

examples.text: Personne n'est parfait.
examples.trans: Nobody's perfect.

examples.text: Parfait. La fenêtre donne sur la rue ou sur la cour?
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

meanings.note: Parler parfaitement. Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.
C'est parfaitement vrai. Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Elle parle parfaitement anglais.
examples.trans: She speaks English perfectly.

examples.text: C'est parfaitement clair.
examples.trans: It is perfectly clear.

examples.text: Elle parle parfaitement anglais avec l'accent.
examples.trans: She speaks English perfectly with the accent.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'sometimes'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: C'est parfois difficile.
examples.trans: It is sometimes difficult.

examples.text: Parfois, il arrive en retard.
examples.trans: Sometimes, he arrives late.

examples.text: Oh! Parfois les vieux tuyaux ont une petite bulle d'air la nuit.
examples.trans: Oh! Sometimes old pipes have a little air bubble at night.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le parfum', plural 'les parfums') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'scent'.

examples.text: Elle porte toujours un parfum très léger et élégant.
examples.trans: She always wears a very light and elegant perfume.

examples.text: J'adore le parfum des fleurs dans ce jardin.
examples.trans: I love the scent of the flowers in this garden.

examples.text: Il refroidit sur la grille en ce moment: croûte dorée et bon parfum de citron!
examples.trans: It is cooling on the rack right now: golden crust and lovely lemon scent!

parfumer.gloss: to scent, fill with fragrance, flavor

meanings.en: to scent (a room); to flavor (a dish)
meanings.note: Parfumer toute la maison = fill the whole house with a wonderful scent.

examples.text: La cannelle chaude parfume toute la cour de l'hôtel.
examples.trans: Warm cinnamon scents the whole hotel courtyard.

examples.text: Quelques feuilles de menthe parfument le thé vert.
examples.trans: A few mint leaves flavor the green tea.

meanings.en: Parisian, of or relating to the city of Paris
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'Parisian'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un taxi parisien.
examples.trans: A Parisian taxi.

examples.text: La vie parisienne.
examples.trans: Parisian life.

examples.text: Je suis dans un taxi parisien.
examples.trans: I am in a Parisian taxi.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le parking', plural 'les parkings') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'parking space'.

examples.text: Il n'y a pas de parking privé ici.
examples.trans: There is no private parking here.

examples.text: Le camion cherche un parking.
examples.trans: The truck is looking for parking.

examples.text: Il n'y a pas de parking privé.
examples.trans: There is no private parking.

meanings.note: parler à quelqu'un = to talk to someone

examples.text: Je parle de sa carrière.
examples.trans: I'm talking about his career.

examples.text: Tu parles français?
examples.trans: Do you speak French?

meanings.en: among, in the middle of, included in
meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'among', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Flora sera très heureuse parmi eux.
examples.trans: Flora will be very happy among them.

examples.text: Un grand talent parmi tant d'autres.
examples.trans: A great talent among so many others.

examples.text: Merci, Flora sera très heureuse parmi eux.
examples.trans: Thank you, Flora will be very happy among them.

meanings.note: Spoken word or pledge ('parole d'honneur' = word of honor; 'tenir parole' = keep one's word); song lyrics ('les paroles').

examples.text: Quand il donne sa parole, on peut compter sur lui.
examples.trans: When he gives his word, you can count on him.

examples.text: Elle connaît encore toutes les paroles de cette vieille chanson.
examples.trans: She still knows all the words to that old song.

meanings.note: In à part, the combination means apart from or separately.

examples.text: J'ai payé ma part.
examples.trans: I paid my share.

examples.text: Tout le monde est ici, à part lui.
examples.trans: Everyone is here except him.

meanings.note: To share food, stories, or joy with others; to divide into portions.

examples.text: Nous allons partager cette grande brioche autour du thé.
examples.trans: We are going to share this big brioche over tea.

examples.text: Merci de partager ce beau souvenir avec nous.
examples.trans: Thank you for sharing this lovely memory with us.

meanings.en: willing, ready, on board to participate
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'willing'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je suis partant.
examples.trans: I am on board.

examples.text: Je suis totalement partant pour le film!
examples.trans: I am totally on board for the film!

meanings.en: partner (acting co-star, business partner, romantic partner; same form m/f)
meanings.note: same form for masculine and feminine

examples.text: Il veut choisir ses partenaires.
examples.trans: He wants to choose his partners.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé un partenaire financier.
examples.trans: I found a financial partner.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la participation', plural 'les participations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'guest appearance'.
Feminine noun ('la participation', plural 'les participations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'participation'.

examples.text: Ajoute une participation exceptionnelle de Balasko.
examples.trans: Add a special appearance by Balasko.

examples.text: Merci pour votre participation active.
examples.trans: Thank you for your active participation.

examples.text: Ajoute une participation de Balasko et j'accepte.
examples.trans: Add an appearance by Balasko and I accept.

meanings.note: To take part in an event, contest, or festival; always followed by the preposition à ('participer à').

examples.text: Trempez la plume dans l'encre, Claire: l'Hôtel du Tilleul participe au Festival des Cours Historiques!
examples.trans: Dip the pen in ink, Claire: the Hotel du Tilleul is entering the Historic Courtyards Festival!

examples.text: Tous les voisins participent à la fête de samedi dans la cour.
examples.trans: All the neighbours are taking part in Saturday's celebration in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Très particulier = very strange.
Très particulier = very strange.

examples.text: Une journée très particulière.
examples.trans: A very strange day.

examples.text: C'est un cas particulier.
examples.trans: It's a special case.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: C'est particulièrement difficile.
examples.trans: It is particularly difficult.

examples.text: Particulièrement réussi.
examples.trans: Particularly successful.

examples.text: Je trouve son écriture particulièrement mature.
examples.trans: I find his writing particularly mature.

meanings.note: A portion or section: une partie du film = part of the film.

meanings.en: faire partie de = to be part of
meanings.note: No article.
Une partie de cartes.

examples.text: Je fais partie de ta famille.
examples.trans: I'm part of your family.

examples.text: Une partie du film.
examples.trans: Part of the film.

examples.text: Je fais partie de ta famille, moi aussi!
examples.trans: I'm part of your family too!

meanings.note: No object: je pars = I'm leaving.
partir en vacances = to go on holiday

examples.text: Je pars demain.
examples.trans: I'm leaving tomorrow.

examples.text: Elle part en vacances.
examples.trans: She's going on holiday.

meanings.note: Printed music pages.

examples.text: Seulement des robes, des partitions et ma tasse préférée!
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite cup!

examples.text: Complètement par accident! Chez mon cousin, je l'ai ouverte et j'ai vu des partitions et un ruban rouge.
examples.trans: By complete accident! At my cousin's flat, I opened it and saw sheet music and a red ribbon.

examples.text: C'est impossible de travailler avec un bébé partout.
examples.trans: It's impossible to work with a baby everywhere.

examples.text: Je t'ai cherché partout.
examples.trans: I looked for you everywhere.

examples.text: Vous gardez un tournevis partout sur vous, Henri!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere on you, Henri!

meanings.note: Main negation word; alone in short phrases like Pas encore!
Entendre des pas = hear footsteps; le pas de vis = screw thread.

examples.text: Pas maintenant.
examples.trans: Not now.

examples.text: Pas de numéro de téléphone, malheureusement.
examples.trans: No phone number, unfortunately.

meanings.note: Le passage vers la deuxième page = the transition into the second page.

examples.text: Écoutez ce doux passage entre les deux thèmes.
examples.trans: Listen to this gentle transition between the two themes.

examples.text: Laissez le passage libre devant la porte de la cuisine.
examples.trans: Keep the walkway clear in front of the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'fleeting'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est une douleur passagère.
examples.trans: It is a fleeting pain.

examples.text: C'est juste une petite contraction passagère.
examples.trans: It is just a minor passing contraction.

meanings.note: Feminine form: une passante.

examples.text: Les passants s'arrêtent sur le trottoir pour écouter le piano.
examples.trans: Passersby stop on the sidewalk to listen to the piano.

examples.text: Un passant a lu le menu affiché sur le portail.
examples.trans: A passerby read the menu posted on the gate.

meanings.note: The reflexive expression se passer means to happen.

examples.text: Je passe demain.
examples.trans: I'll stop by tomorrow.

examples.text: Passez-moi la grosse clé anglaise à votre gauche.
examples.trans: Pass me the heavy wrench on your left.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la passerelle', plural 'les passerelles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'footbridge'.

examples.text: Ce court-métrage est une bonne passerelle vers le cinéma.
examples.trans: This short film is a good stepping stone into cinema.

examples.text: Les passagers traversent la passerelle pour monter à bord.
examples.trans: The passengers cross the footbridge to get on board.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'love affair, passion'.

examples.text: La nouvelle passion d'une actrice.
examples.trans: The new passion of an actress.

examples.text: La nouvelle passion de Virginie Efira?
examples.trans: Virginie Efira's new passion?

examples.text: Nous avons vécu deux mois de passion.
examples.trans: We lived two months of passion.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Il l'aime passionnément.
examples.trans: He loves her passionately.

examples.text: C'est toi que j'aime passionnément.
examples.trans: It is you that I love passionately.

meanings.note: C'est du passé = it's in the past.
Adjectival use describing a time already passed.

examples.text: C'est du passé.
examples.trans: It's in the past.

examples.text: Il parle de son passé.
examples.trans: He talks about his past.

meanings.note: une pastille à la menthe = a mint lozenge

examples.text: Prendre une pastille.
examples.trans: To take a mint.

examples.text: Une pastille pour la gorge.
examples.trans: A throat lozenge.

examples.text: Tenez, prenez cette petite pastille douce.
examples.trans: Here, take this sweet little mint.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le pastis', plural 'les pastis') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pastis'.

examples.text: Un pastis, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: A pastis, please.

examples.text: Un pastis, s'il vous plaît!
examples.trans: A pastis, please!

meanings.note: informal for pomme de terre; une patate chaude = a hot potato

examples.text: Il me refile une patate chaude!
examples.trans: He is passing me a hot potato!

examples.text: J'ai la patate.
examples.trans: I am full of energy.

related.word: informal for pomme de terre; une patate chaude

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la paternité', plural 'les paternités') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'paternity'.

examples.text: La procédure de reconnaissance de paternité de Mathias.
examples.trans: Mathias's paternity recognition procedure.

examples.text: Assumer pleinement sa paternité.
examples.trans: To fully embrace one's fatherhood.

examples.text: Cette histoire de paternité te tracasse?
examples.trans: Is this paternity business bothering you?

examples.text: C'est pathétique.
examples.trans: It's pathetic.

examples.text: Une excuse pathétique.
examples.trans: A pathetic excuse.

meanings.note: With calm patience (pronounced /pasjamɑ̃/, formed on 'patient').

examples.text: La pâte doit lever patiemment dans un endroit tiède.
examples.trans: The dough must rise patiently in a warm spot.

examples.text: Il a attendu patiemment la fin de l'averse sous le porche.
examples.trans: He waited patiently under the archway for the shower to end.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la patience', plural 'les patiences') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'patience'.

examples.text: Il faut avoir beaucoup de patience.
examples.trans: One must have a lot of patience.

examples.text: Le réalisateur commence à perdre patience.
examples.trans: The director is starting to lose patience.

examples.text: Merci pour votre patience! Henri va vérifier la cave tout de suite.
examples.trans: Thank you for your patience! Henri is going to check the cellar right away.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le patient', plural 'les patients') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'patient'.

examples.text: Vous avez soigné un vieux patient?
examples.trans: You cared for an elderly patient?

examples.text: Les patients à l'hôpital sont importants aussi!
examples.trans: Patients at the hospital are important too!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to wait patiently'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'patienté').

examples.text: Faire patienter quelqu'un.
examples.trans: To keep someone waiting.

examples.text: Patienter dans la salle d'attente.
examples.trans: To wait in the waiting room.

examples.text: Je vais la faire patienter dans mon bureau.
examples.trans: I am going to keep her waiting in my office.

meanings.note: Cultural and architectural heritage.

examples.text: Un courrier immobilier? Montrez-le-nous: je travaille aux contrats de la mairie, et Antoine connaît le patrimoine!
examples.trans: A property letter? Show it to us: I work in City Hall contracts, and Antoine knows heritage law!

examples.text: Voici le patrimoine sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the heritage, historic buildings on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine: patronne.

examples.text: C'est le patron.
examples.trans: He's the boss.

examples.text: La patronne est là.
examples.trans: The boss (woman) is here.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la patronne', plural 'les patronnes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'female boss'.

examples.text: Andréa est une excellente patronne.
examples.trans: Andrea is an excellent boss.

examples.text: Et quand arrive votre patronne Andréa?
examples.trans: And when is your boss Andrea arriving?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la patte', plural 'les pattes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'paw'.

examples.text: Ne mettez pas vos grosses pattes partout.
examples.trans: Do not put your big paws everywhere.

examples.text: La patte du chien.
examples.trans: The dog's paw.

meanings.note: Pousser la pâte avec la paume de la main = push the dough with the palm of your hand.

examples.text: Appuyez sur la pâte avec la paume de la main.
examples.trans: Press on the dough with the palm of your hand.

examples.text: Elle tient la petite clé en laiton dans sa paume.
examples.trans: She holds the little brass key in her palm.

meanings.note: Faire une pause = to take a break. Feminine noun ('la pause', plural 'les pauses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'break'.

examples.text: Je veux faire une pause.
examples.trans: I want to take a break.

examples.text: Elle ne fait pas de pause!
examples.trans: She does not take a break!

examples.text: L'avenir... Je veux faire une pause avec tout ça.
examples.trans: The future... I want to take a break from all that.

meanings.note: Le pauvre homme. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'poor'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Une famille pauvre. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'poor'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Pauvre Ryan!
examples.trans: Poor Ryan!

examples.text: Le pauvre garçon est fatigué.
examples.trans: The poor boy is tired.

examples.text: Alors dis-moi pourquoi le pauvre monsieur derrière le comptoir a l'air prêt à pleurer.
examples.trans: Then tell me why the poor gentleman behind the counter looks ready to cry.

meanings.note: Les pavés = cobbled street.

examples.text: Parce que les volets en bois mouillés adoucissent l'écho des pavés...
examples.trans: Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the cobblestones...

examples.text: Voici le pavé sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the cobblestone, paving stone on the table.

meanings.note: no 'pour' needed: payer un café, payer une assistante

examples.text: Je paie l'addition.
examples.trans: I'm paying the bill.

examples.text: Payé en espèces!
examples.trans: Paid in cash!

meanings.note: un pays étranger = a foreign country

examples.text: C'est le plus grand festival du pays.
examples.trans: It's the biggest festival in the country.

examples.text: Voyager dans un autre pays.
examples.trans: To travel to another country.

examples.text: Où va ce pays?
examples.trans: What is this country coming to?

examples.text: Le paysage est magnifique!
examples.trans: The landscape is magnificent!

examples.text: Un beau paysage d'hiver.
examples.trans: A beautiful winter landscape.

meanings.note: Feminine: paysanne.

examples.text: Un documentaire sur les paysans sans terre.
examples.trans: A documentary about landless farmers.

examples.text: Les paysans travaillent la terre.
examples.trans: The farmers work the land.

examples.text: Il tourne un documentaire sur les paysans sans terre au Honduras.
examples.trans: He's filming a documentary about landless farmers in Honduras.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la peau', plural 'les peaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'human skin or complexion'.

examples.text: Prendre soin de sa peau.
examples.trans: To take care of one's skin.

examples.text: Une peau très pâle.
examples.trans: Very pale skin.

examples.text: La peau devient plutôt rose bleutée.
examples.trans: The skin turns rather bluish pink.

meanings.note: Irregular: je peins, nous peignons, j'ai peint.

examples.text: Seulement une clé dorée peinte au-dessus de la porte. Montrez cette vanne au vendeur.
examples.trans: Only a painted golden key above the door. Show this valve to the clerk.

examples.text: C'est facile à peindre ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to paint together.

meanings.en: trouble, effort (valoir la peine = to be worth it)
meanings.note: Valoir la peine = to be worth it. Feminine noun ('la peine', plural 'les peines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'trouble'.
Feminine noun ('la peine', plural 'les peines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'trouble'.

examples.text: Ça en vaut la peine.
examples.trans: It's worth it.

examples.text: Oui, ça en vaut la peine.
examples.trans: Yes, it's worth it.

examples.text: Il a de la peine.
examples.trans: He is sad.

meanings.note: La peinture est fraîche = wet paint.

examples.text: Toutes les clés de un à sept sont prises, et la peinture de la huit est fraîche.
examples.trans: Every key from one to seven is taken, and room eight has wet paint.

examples.text: Voici la peinture sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the paint on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la peluche', plural 'les peluches') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'stuffed animal'.

examples.text: Nous avions une peluche de blaireau.
examples.trans: We had a stuffed badger toy.

examples.text: Merci pour le petit ours en peluche.
examples.trans: Thank you for the little teddy bear.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Écoutez quand je penche le coffre: un objet en métal vient de glisser dedans.
examples.trans: Listen when I tilt the chest: a metal object just slid inside.

examples.text: C'est facile à pencher ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to tilt, lean together.

examples.text: C'est notre pendaison de crémaillère.
examples.trans: It is our housewarming party.

examples.text: Tout est prêt pour la pendaison de crémaillère.
examples.trans: Everything is ready for the housewarming.

meanings.note: Pendant le film.
Pendant quinze ans.

examples.text: Pendant quinze ans.
examples.trans: For fifteen years.

examples.text: Je dors pendant le film.
examples.trans: I sleep during the film.

meanings.note: Penser que... = to think that.
Penser à.

examples.text: Ils ont pensé que c'était mieux.
examples.trans: They thought it was better.

examples.text: Je pense à toi.
examples.trans: I'm thinking of you.

meanings.note: école de pensée = school of thought
Feminine noun ('la pensée', plural 'les pensées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'thought'.

examples.text: Quelle école de pensée?
examples.trans: What school of thought?

examples.text: Une pensée positive.
examples.trans: A positive thought.

examples.text: Ça dépend de ton école de pensée.
examples.trans: That depends on your school of thought.

meanings.note: Uphill or downhill slope of a street, roof, or hillside ('en pente' = sloping).

examples.text: La ruelle descend en pente douce vers le square.
examples.trans: The lane slopes gently down toward the park square.

examples.text: Les cyclistes ralentissent dans la pente pavée.
examples.trans: Cyclists slow down on the cobbled slope.

meanings.en: to break through, pierce; make a breakthrough in one's career
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to break through'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'percé').

examples.text: Nous allons percer ensemble.
examples.trans: We are going to break through together.

examples.text: Percez sans hésiter!
examples.trans: Break through without hesitation!

examples.text: Oui, nous allons percer ensemble.
examples.trans: Yes, we are going to break through together.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la percée', plural 'les percées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'breakthrough'.

examples.text: Une percée décisive.
examples.trans: A decisive breakthrough.

examples.text: C'est le signe de la percée.
examples.trans: It is the sign of the breakthrough.

examples.text: Une percée après tant de tensions?
examples.trans: A breakthrough after so much tension?

meanings.note: Past participle perdu; compound tenses use avoir.

examples.text: J'ai perdu un ami.
examples.trans: I have lost a friend.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas perdre ça.
examples.trans: I do not want to lose that.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'perfectionist'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il est perfectionniste.
examples.trans: He is a perfectionist.

examples.text: Ben est un véritable perfectionniste.
examples.trans: Ben is a true perfectionist.

meanings.note: figuratively, a wonderful helpful person

examples.text: Vous êtes une vraie perle.
examples.trans: You are a real gem.

examples.text: Merci Noémie, vous êtes une vraie perle.
examples.trans: Thank you Noemie, you are a real gem.

meanings.note: permettre à quelqu'un de faire = to allow someone to do

examples.text: Permettez-moi de vous aider.
examples.trans: Allow me to help you.

examples.text: Permettez-moi de servir le jus d'orange frais, madame!
examples.trans: Allow me to pour the fresh orange juice, madam!

examples.text: Permettez-moi. Mon Dieu, vous avez mis des pierres dedans?
examples.trans: Allow me. Goodness, did you pack stones inside?

meanings.en: permit, license (permis de conduire = driver's license)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le permis', plural 'les permis') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'permit'.

examples.text: Le permis de conduire.
examples.trans: The driver's license.

examples.text: Bonne chance pour ton permis de conduire.
examples.trans: Good luck for your driving license.

examples.text: J'ai peur qu'il rate son permis.
examples.trans: I am afraid he will fail his driving test.

meanings.note: Polite formula: *avec votre permission* ('with your permission, if you allow me').

examples.text: Avec votre permission, j'aimerais ouvrir la fenêtre un instant.
examples.trans: With your permission, I would like to open the window for a moment.

examples.text: Elle a demandé la permission d'emprunter le vieux carnet.
examples.trans: She asked permission to borrow the old notebook.

meanings.note: Final -l is traditionally silent (/pɛʁsi/).

examples.text: Cueillez deux brins de persil frais dans le bac de la cour.
examples.trans: Pick two sprigs of fresh parsley from the courtyard planter.

examples.text: Un peu de persil haché donne de la couleur à la soupe.
examples.trans: A little chopped parsley adds color to the soup.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to persist'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'persisté').

examples.text: Le sexisme persiste dans ce milieu.
examples.trans: Sexism persists in this industry.

examples.text: Le froid persiste depuis plusieurs jours.
examples.trans: The cold has persisted for several days.

examples.text: Le sexisme dans ce milieu persiste.
examples.trans: Sexism in this industry persists.

meanings.note: Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'fictional figure, character'.

examples.text: Le personnage principal.
examples.trans: The main character.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas sûre du personnage.
examples.trans: I am not sure about the character.

examples.text: Le personnage n'est pas compliqué.
examples.trans: The character is not complicated.

meanings.note: With ne: il ne voit personne.
As a noun: une personne (feminine).

examples.text: Il n'y a personne.
examples.trans: There's nobody here.

examples.text: Je ne connais personne.
examples.trans: I don't know anyone.

meanings.note: rien de personnel = nothing personal

examples.text: Ce n'est rien de personnel.
examples.trans: It's nothing personal.

examples.text: C'est une question personnelle.
examples.trans: It's a personal question.

examples.text: Ce n'est rien de personnel. L'agence ne peut pas continuer comme ça.
examples.trans: It's nothing personal. The agency can't go on like this.

meanings.note: Invité personnellement. mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Il t'a invité personnellement.
examples.trans: He invited you personally.

examples.text: François, il t'a invité personnellement. Et là tu hésites?
examples.trans: François, he invited you personally. And now you're hesitating?

examples.text: Est-ce que Fabrice la connaît personnellement?
examples.trans: Does Fabrice know her personally?

examples.text: Une belle perspective.
examples.trans: A fine prospect.

examples.text: Une perspective excitante, non?
examples.trans: An exciting prospect, right?

meanings.note: Une ambiance pesante. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'heavy'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Tu as eu raison, l'ambiance est pesante.
examples.trans: You were right, the atmosphere is heavy.

examples.text: Il régnait un silence très pesant.
examples.trans: A very heavy silence reigned.

meanings.en: to be heavy, weigh heavily on someone's mind
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to weigh down'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'pesé').

examples.text: Cette situation me pèse.
examples.trans: This situation weighs on me.

examples.text: Ça me pèse de lui faire du mal.
examples.trans: It weighs on me to hurt him.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'pessimistic'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ne soyez pas si pessimiste.
examples.trans: Do not be so pessimistic.

examples.text: Une vision pessimiste.
examples.trans: A pessimistic outlook.

examples.text: Ton père avait tort d'être aussi pessimiste.
examples.trans: Your father was wrong to be so pessimistic.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la peste', plural 'les pestes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pest'.
Feminine noun ('la peste', plural 'les pestes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'plague'.

examples.text: Je vais surveiller cette peste.
examples.trans: I will keep an eye on that pest.

examples.text: Cette fille est une vraie peste.
examples.trans: That girl is a real pest.

meanings.note: Affectionate, a bit condescending.
Un petit cours.

examples.text: J'ai un petit loft.
examples.trans: I've got a little loft.

examples.text: C'est une petite agence.
examples.trans: It's a small agency.

meanings.note: un mode de vie petit-bourgeois = a conventional middle-class lifestyle

examples.text: C'est petit-bourgeois pour moi.
examples.trans: It is petty-bourgeois for me.

examples.text: Une mentalité petite-bourgeoise.
examples.trans: A petty-bourgeois mindset.

examples.text: C'est petit-bourgeois et mortel d'ennui pour moi.
examples.trans: It is petty-bourgeois and deadly boring for me.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le petit-déjeuner', plural 'les petits-déjeuners') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'morning meal'.

examples.text: Je prends toujours un café au petit-déjeuner.
examples.trans: I always have a coffee at breakfast.

examples.text: On a organisé un petit-déjeuner avec le réalisateur.
examples.trans: We organized a breakfast meeting with the director.

examples.text: Bonne nuit, Claire. À demain au petit-déjeuner.
examples.trans: Good night, Claire. See you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le petit-fils', plural 'les petits-fils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'grandson'.

examples.text: Son petit-fils habite à Lyon.
examples.trans: Her grandson lives in Lyon.

examples.text: Un menuisier vivait là avec ses deux petits-fils: l'aîné jouait du piano, et le petit adorait les trains!
examples.trans: A carpenter lived there with his two grandsons: the older boy played piano, and the little one loved trains!

meanings.en: un peu = a little, a bit
meanings.note: Peu de temps = little time.
Peu de temps = little time.

examples.text: Un peu de café?
examples.trans: A little coffee?

examples.text: Je suis un peu fatigué.
examples.trans: I'm a bit tired.

meanings.note: Avoir peur de = to be afraid of.

examples.text: J'ai peur!
examples.trans: I'm scared!

examples.text: Parce que j'avais peur que tu sois encore en colère.
examples.trans: Because I was afraid you were still angry.

examples.text: Peut-être demain.
examples.trans: Maybe tomorrow.

examples.text: Seulement trois petits cartons! Peut-être quatre!
examples.trans: Only three small boxes! Maybe four!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la pharmacie', plural 'les pharmacies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pharmacy'.

examples.text: Aller à la pharmacie.
examples.trans: Go to the pharmacy.

examples.text: Le pont, puis la pharmacie verte à droite. Et ensuite?
examples.trans: The bridge, then the green pharmacy on the right. And next?

examples.text: Henri, vous m'entendez? Je viens de dépasser la pharmacie verte!
examples.trans: Henri, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Feminine form: une pharmacienne; shop: la pharmacie.

examples.text: Le pharmacien du coin est venu boire un thé à six heures.
examples.trans: The corner pharmacist came for tea at six o'clock.

examples.text: Demandez une bande souple au pharmacien pour votre cheville.
examples.trans: Ask the pharmacist for an elastic wrap for your ankle.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (clipped from la photographie): une vieille photo en noir et blanc ('an old black-and-white photo').

examples.text: Cette photo en noir et blanc montre la cour autrefois.
examples.trans: This black-and-white photo shows the courtyard in the old days.

examples.text: Claire encadre la photo et l'accroche près de la réception.
examples.trans: Claire frames the photo and hangs it near the front desk.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to photocopy'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'photocopié').

examples.text: J'ai photocopié le document.
examples.trans: I photocopied the document.

examples.text: Le contrat secret a été photocopié ici.
examples.trans: The secret contract was photocopied here.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la photocopieuse', plural 'les photocopieuses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'photocopier'.

examples.text: La photocopieuse est en panne.
examples.trans: The photocopier is out of order.

examples.text: Tout le monde connaît l'historique d'une photocopieuse!
examples.trans: Everyone knows the log of a photocopier!

examples.text: Merde, je l'ai oubliée à la photocopieuse!
examples.trans: Damn, I forgot her at the photocopier!

meanings.note: un artiste photographe = a photographic artist

examples.text: Je travaille avec des artistes photographes.
examples.trans: I work with photographic artists.

examples.text: Un photographe professionnel.
examples.trans: A professional photographer.

examples.text: Les photographes attendent votre arrivée!
examples.trans: The photographers are waiting for your arrival!

examples.text: Tu es photogénique.
examples.trans: You're photogenic.

examples.text: Elle est très photogénique.
examples.trans: She's very photogenic.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la phrase', plural 'les phrases') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sentence'.

examples.text: Une deuxième phrase.
examples.trans: A second sentence.

examples.text: Répétez cette phrase.
examples.trans: Repeat this sentence.

examples.text: Quand j'ai le trac, mes phrases deviennent très longues et compliquées!
examples.trans: When I get stage fright, my sentences become very long and complicated!

meanings.note: Note gender contrast: la physique = physics (science), whereas le physique = physical appearance / build.

examples.text: La chaleur dans un four, c'est tout simplement de la physique!
examples.trans: Heat inside an oven is simply physics!

examples.text: Il étudie la physique et l'acoustique des salles.
examples.trans: He studies physics and room acoustics.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le phénomène', plural 'les phénomènes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'rare phenomenon'.

examples.text: C'est un véritable phénomène d'énergie.
examples.trans: He is a true phenomenon of energy.

examples.text: Mais c'est qui ce phénomène?
examples.trans: Who is this character, anyway?

meanings.note: Jouer du piano = to play the piano.

examples.text: Il y a vingt-cinq ans, je donnais des cours de piano près d'ici.
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago, I taught piano lessons near here.

examples.text: Si je connais?! Chaque vendredi pendant six ans, j'ai monté cet escalier en bois pour donner cours de piano!
examples.trans: Do I know it?! Every Friday for six years, I climbed those wooden stairs to teach piano!

examples.text: Un menuisier vivait là avec ses deux petits-fils: l'aîné jouait du piano, et le petit adorait les trains!
examples.trans: A carpenter lived there with his two grandsons: the older boy played piano, and the little one loved trains!

meanings.note: Sharp mountain peak; idiom 'tomber à pic' = to arrive right on cue, at the exact right moment.

examples.text: Tu tombes à pic, je sors justement les tasses!
examples.trans: Your timing is perfect — I'm just getting out the cups!

examples.text: Au loin, la neige brille encore sur le plus haut pic.
examples.trans: In the distance, snow still gleams on the highest peak.

pied.gloss: foot; leg (of a table or chair)

meanings.note: Final *-d* is silent (`/pje/`). Covers both human feet (*poser le pied par terre*) and furniture legs (*les pieds de la table*).

examples.text: Gardez le pied posé sur ce coussin toute la soirée.
examples.trans: Keep your foot resting on this cushion all evening.

examples.text: On peut aller au marché à pied en cinq minutes.
examples.trans: You can walk to the market on foot in five minutes.

meanings.note: En pierre = made of stone.

examples.text: Permettez-moi. Mon Dieu, vous avez mis des pierres dedans?
examples.trans: Allow me. Goodness, did you pack stones inside?

examples.text: Attendez. Regardez en bas sur la marche en pierre.
examples.trans: Wait. Look down on the stone step.

examples.text: Tournez à gauche devant notre portail et marchez tout droit jusqu'au pont en pierre.
examples.trans: Turn left outside our gate and walk straight ahead to the stone bridge.

meanings.note: Neuf heures pile. Invariable French adverb meaning 'sharp'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Il est arrivé à midi pile.
examples.trans: He arrived at noon sharp.

examples.text: Huit heures pile! Notre client est là!
examples.trans: Eight o'clock on the dot! Our guest is here!

examples.text: À sept heures pile, trente minutes avant le petit-déjeuner.
examples.trans: At seven sharp, thirty minutes before breakfast.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la pilule', plural 'les pilules') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pill'.

examples.text: Prendre une pilule.
examples.trans: To take a pill.

examples.text: J'ai ces pilules très efficaces.
examples.trans: I have these very effective pills.

examples.text: Alors, j'ai ces pilules très efficaces.
examples.trans: Then, I have these very effective pills.

meanings.note: une histoire pimentée = a spicy story

examples.text: C'est une nouvelle pimentée!
examples.trans: It's spicy news!

examples.text: Un plat bien pimenté.
examples.trans: A very spicy dish.

examples.text: Au contraire, ça va faire le buzz! C'est pimenté!
examples.trans: On the contrary, it will create buzz! It is spicy!

meanings.note: Singular in French where English uses a plural pair (*une pince fine* = 'a pair of thin tweezers / fine-nose pliers').

examples.text: Il saisit la petite tige en laiton avec une pince fine.
examples.trans: He grips the tiny brass pin with thin tweezers.

examples.text: Rangez la pince et le tournevis dans la boîte à outils.
examples.trans: Put the pliers and the screwdriver back in the toolbox.

meanings.note: Plural *des pinceaux*; *un coup de pinceau* means 'a brushstroke'.

examples.text: Rincez bien les pinceaux à l'eau tiède après la peinture.
examples.trans: Rinse the paintbrushes thoroughly in warm water after painting.

examples.text: Prenez un pinceau plat et large pour les grandes planches.
examples.trans: Use a wide flat brush for the large boards.

meanings.en: pinch (small amount held between thumb and finger)
meanings.note: Formed from *pincer* ('to pinch') + *-ée* ('amount contained in'), just like *une cuillerée* or *une gorgée*.

examples.text: Ajoutez toujours une petite pincée de sel dans la pâte à tarte.
examples.trans: Always add a tiny pinch of salt to tart dough.

examples.text: Goûtez une pincée du pot blanc pour vérifier si c'est du sucre.
examples.trans: Taste a pinch from the white jar to check whether it's sugar.

meanings.note: A familiar or child-directed word; faire pipi means pee, often used with children or pets.

examples.text: Tu veux faire pipi?
examples.trans: Do you need to pee?

examples.text: Le chien fait pipi.
examples.trans: The dog is peeing.

examples.text: Tu veux faire pipi, Jean Gabin?
examples.trans: Do you need to pee, Jean Gabin?

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'worse'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est pire que tout.
examples.trans: It's worse than everything.

examples.text: Pire qu'un tuyau...
examples.trans: Worse than a pipe...

examples.text: Pire qu'un tuyau... une lettre recommandée du propriétaire de l'immeuble est arrivée à midi.
examples.trans: Worse than a pipe... a registered letter from the building owner arrived at noon.

meanings.note: aller à la piscine = to go to the swimming pool

examples.text: La piscine est grande.
examples.trans: The swimming pool is large.

examples.text: C'est ridicule, la piscine et le canard!
examples.trans: It's ridiculous, the pool and the duck!

examples.text: Il n'y aura pas de piscine sur scène.
examples.trans: There will be no swimming pool on stage.

related.gloss: to go to the swimming pool

meanings.note: Trail of clues ('jeu de piste' = treasure hunt; 'être sur la bonne piste' = be on the right track); bike lane or ski run.

examples.text: Ce nouveau détail nous met sur la bonne piste!
examples.trans: This new detail puts us on the right track!

examples.text: Les cousins ont préparé un jeu de piste dans tout le jardin.
examples.trans: The cousins set up a treasure hunt across the whole garden.

pistonner.gloss: to pull strings for, to recommend

meanings.en: to pull strings for, use connections for (informal)
meanings.note: Pistonner quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to pull strings for'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'pistonné').

examples.text: Mathias a pistonné sa fille!
examples.trans: Mathias pulled strings for his daughter!

examples.text: Il s'est fait pistonner.
examples.trans: He got recommended through connections.

examples.text: Si! Mathias a pistonné sa fille!
examples.trans: Yes! Mathias pulled strings for his daughter!

meanings.en: pistou, Provençal cold sauce made from basil, garlic, and olive oil
meanings.note: similar to pesto, without pine nuts

examples.text: Une recette de pistou.
examples.trans: A recipe for pistou.

examples.text: La soupe au pistou.
examples.trans: Vegetable soup with pistou.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le pitbull', plural 'les pitbulls') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pitbull terrier'.

examples.text: Comme agent, elle défend ses acteurs comme un pitbull.
examples.trans: As an agent, she defends her actors like a pitbull.

examples.text: Le voisin promène son pitbull en laisse.
examples.trans: The neighbour walks his pitbull on a leash.

meanings.note: avoir pitié de = to take pity on; par pitié = for pity's sake

examples.text: Non, pitié!
examples.trans: No, please have mercy!

examples.text: Ayez pitié de nous.
examples.trans: Have mercy on us.

examples.text: Oui, elle nous a tout soufflé sans pitié!
examples.trans: Yes, she snatched everything from us without mercy!

related.gloss: to take pity on; par pitié = for pity's sake

meanings.note: Can express contempt, pathetic, or evoke pity, pitiful; context and tone distinguish them.

examples.text: C'est pitoyable!
examples.trans: It's pathetic!

examples.text: Un film pitoyable.
examples.trans: A pitiful film.

examples.text: Tu peux être tellement snob, Andréa. C'est pitoyable!
examples.trans: You can be such a snob, Andréa. It's pathetic!

meanings.note: La pièce de Koltès.
In a flat.

examples.text: Je dois voir la pièce.
examples.trans: I have to see the play.

examples.text: Un appartement de trois pièces.
examples.trans: A three-room flat.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le piège', plural 'les pièges') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'trap'.

examples.text: Je suis tombée dans un piège.
examples.trans: I fell into a trap.

examples.text: Je vous avais dit que cette tablette est un piège.
examples.trans: I told you that tablet is a trap.

meanings.note: Feminine: piétonne. Masculine noun ('le piéton', plural 'les piétons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pedestrian'.

examples.text: Attention aux piétons.
examples.trans: Watch out for pedestrians.

examples.text: Passage pour piétons.
examples.trans: Pedestrian crossing.

examples.text: Attention au passage pour piétons.
examples.trans: Watch out for the pedestrian crossing.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le placard', plural 'les placards') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cupboard'.

examples.text: Les dossiers sont dans le placard.
examples.trans: The files are in the cupboard.

examples.text: J'ai enfermé l'autre valise bleue à clé dans notre placard à bagages.
examples.trans: I locked the other blue suitcase in our luggage closet.

examples.text: Je pose cette valise bleue ici cinq minutes pendant que je balaie le placard.
examples.trans: Let me set this blue suitcase here for five minutes while I sweep the closet.

meanings.note: Deux places = two tickets.

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday.

examples.text: Il y a de la place.
examples.trans: There's room.

meanings.note: Le placement de produit = product placement in a film or programme.

examples.text: Le placement de produit est dans le film.
examples.trans: The product placement is in the film.

examples.text: Ce placement est visible.
examples.trans: This placement is visible.

meanings.en: to place, to put, to seat
meanings.note: Past participle used as adjective.

meanings.en: haut placé = high up, in a senior position
meanings.note: Past participle used as adjective.

examples.text: Il est haut placé aux impôts.
examples.trans: He's high up at the tax office.

examples.text: Elle place les invités.
examples.trans: She seats the guests.

meanings.note: Final -d is silent (/plafɔ̃/). Contrast le plafond (indoor ceiling), le toit (outer roof), and le sol (floor).

examples.text: Henri suspend la lampe en verre au milieu du plafond.
examples.trans: Henri hangs the glass lamp in the middle of the ceiling.

examples.text: Le plafond en bois donne une acoustique très douce à la pièce.
examples.trans: The wooden ceiling gives the room very soft acoustics.

meanings.note: Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard feminine noun meaning 'beach, seaside'.

examples.text: Aller à la plage.
examples.trans: To go to the beach.

examples.text: Une plage de sable.
examples.trans: A sandy beach.

examples.text: On ira ensemble à la plage.
examples.trans: We will go together to the beach.

meanings.en: to plead, defend (plaider sa cause = plead someone's case)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'plead'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'plaidé').

examples.text: Il a plaidé sa cause.
examples.trans: He pleaded her case.

examples.text: C'est Mathias qui a plaidé ta cause.
examples.trans: Mathias is the one who pleaded your case.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la plaie', plural 'les plaies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'wound'.

examples.text: C'est une vraie plaie.
examples.trans: It is a real pain.

examples.text: Une vraie plaie, ces peaux de banane!
examples.trans: A real nuisance, these banana peels!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la plainte', plural 'les plaintes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'legal complaint'.
Feminine noun ('la plainte', plural 'les plaintes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'groan'.

examples.text: Il a déposé une plainte.
examples.trans: He filed a complaint.

examples.text: S'il te plaît, retire ta plainte.
examples.trans: Please, withdraw your complaint.

meanings.en: to please, to be liked by
meanings.note: Ça me plaît = I like it.

meanings.en: s'il vous plaît / s'il te plaît = please
meanings.note: Formal / informal.

examples.text: Paris me plaît beaucoup.
examples.trans: I like Paris a lot.

examples.text: Gardez mon sac bleu jusqu'à vendredi, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Please keep my blue bag until Friday.

meanings.note: Tu plaisantes? = are you kidding?.

examples.text: Tu plaisantes?
examples.trans: Are you kidding?

examples.text: Je ne plaisante pas.
examples.trans: I'm not joking.

meanings.note: Avec plaisir = with pleasure.

meanings.en: faire plaisir à = to please, to make happy

examples.text: Avec plaisir!
examples.trans: With pleasure!

examples.text: Ça fait plaisir à ma famille.
examples.trans: It makes my family happy.

meanings.note: Le plan a marché = the plan worked. Masculine noun ('le plan', plural 'les plans') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'plan'.
Un plan de la ville. Masculine noun ('le plan', plural 'les plans') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'plan'.

examples.text: Le plan a marché!
examples.trans: The plan worked!

examples.text: Quel est le plan?
examples.trans: What is the plan?

examples.text: C'était mon plan lâche de lundi... avant de vous rencontrer tous.
examples.trans: That was my cowardly Monday plan... before meeting all of you.

meanings.en: wooden board; chopping board ('planche à découper')
meanings.note: Sur la planche en bois = on the wooden cutting board.

examples.text: Posez les carottes lavées sur la grande planche en bois.
examples.trans: Place the washed carrots on the big wooden cutting board.

examples.text: Il scie une planche de chêne pour réparer l'étagère.
examples.trans: He saws an oak plank to repair the shelf.

meanings.note: Built from planche ('plank').

examples.text: Va lui parler, Claire, avant qu'il use le plancher!
examples.trans: Go talk to him, Claire, before he wears out the floorboards!

examples.text: Voici le plancher sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the wooden floor, floorboards on the table.

meanings.note: Le planning de tournage.

examples.text: J'ai dû réécrire le planning.
examples.trans: I had to rewrite the schedule.

examples.text: Le planning est très serré.
examples.trans: The schedule is very tight.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la plante', plural 'les plantes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'plant'.

examples.text: Voici une plante pour le bureau.
