examples.trans: Here is a plant for the office.

examples.text: Il faut bien quelqu'un pour s'occuper des plantes de la cour.
examples.trans: Somebody has to take care of the courtyard plants.

meanings.en: to plant; to abandon, ditch, leave in the lurch (planter quelqu'un)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to plant'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'planté').

examples.text: On plante Mathias?
examples.trans: Are we ditching Mathias?

examples.text: Et on plante Mathias tout seul?
examples.trans: And we leave Mathias completely behind?

examples.text: Il va se planter complètement!
examples.trans: He is going to crash and burn completely!

meanings.note: Engraved brass or door plate.

examples.text: Essuyez la poussière sur la plaque en laiton dessus... attendez, lisez ce numéro!
examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate on top... wait, read that number!

examples.text: Voici la plaque sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the plate, metal plaque on the table.

meanings.note: Standard French block of butter.

examples.text: Attends une seconde, Claire... tu as pris quelle plaquette de beurre?
examples.trans: Wait a second, Claire... which packet of butter did you grab?

examples.text: Voici la plaquette sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the block, slab on the table.

meanings.en: to laminate, coat in protective plastic
meanings.note: Une carte plastifiée = a laminated card.

examples.text: Nous avons plastifié les menus pour les tables du jardin.
examples.trans: We laminated the menus for the garden tables.

examples.text: Une feuille plastifiée ne craint pas les gouttes de pluie.
examples.trans: A laminated sheet is not afraid of raindrops.

meanings.note: Masculine plat (/pla/) has a silent -t; feminine plate (/plat/) pronounces it. Note de l'eau plate ('still water', as opposed to eau gazeuse).

examples.text: Une fois pliée, la chaise devient toute plate contre le mur.
examples.trans: Once folded, the chair becomes completely flat against the wall.

examples.text: Posez le carton bien à plat sur la grande table.
examples.trans: Set the cardboard box nice and flat on the big table.

meanings.note: Plural *des plateaux* (`/plato/`).

examples.text: Elle apporte le thé à la menthe et les tasses sur un grand plateau.
examples.trans: She brings the mint tea and cups on a big tray.

examples.text: Six plateaux de citrons jaunes parfument toute la cuisine.
examples.trans: Six trays of yellow lemons scent the whole kitchen.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: C'était fou et platonique.
examples.trans: It was crazy and platonic.

examples.text: Une relation platonique.
examples.trans: A platonic relationship.

examples.text: Non... c'était fou et platonique.
examples.trans: No... it was wild and platonic.

meanings.note: Plein de = full of.

examples.text: Elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: It's full of sharks.

examples.text: Le café est plein.
examples.trans: The café is full.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Tu mérites pleinement ce rôle.
examples.trans: You fully deserve this role.

examples.text: Profiter pleinement.
examples.trans: To enjoy fully.

examples.text: Tu mérites pleinement ce premier rôle.
examples.trans: You fully deserve this lead role.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le pleur', plural 'les pleurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'crying'.

examples.text: Ce sont des pleurs de décharge.
examples.trans: These are release crying episodes.

examples.text: Ce sont des pleurs de soulagement.
examples.trans: These are tears of relief.

meanings.note: Ne pleurez pas = don't cry.

examples.text: Ne pleurez pas.
examples.trans: Don't cry.

examples.text: Le bébé pleure.
examples.trans: The baby is crying.

meanings.note: Impersonal verb: il pleut, il a plu.

examples.text: Le papier marche toujours quand le courant est coupé.
examples.trans: Paper still works when the power goes out.

examples.text: Il pleut dehors et tous les hôtels de la rue sont complets! Qu'est-ce qu'on fait?
examples.trans: It is raining outside and every hotel on the street is full! What do we do?

meanings.note: Fold or crease in paper or fabric; formal sealed envelope ('sous pli').

examples.text: Lissez doucement le pli central de la vieille carte.
examples.trans: Smooth the center crease of the old map gently.

examples.text: La nappe repassée ne présente pas un seul faux pli.
examples.trans: The ironed tablecloth doesn't have a single wrinkle.

meanings.note: Chaise pliante = folding chair.

examples.text: Vous avez trouvé les trois chaises pliantes derrière la chaufferie, Henri?
examples.trans: Did you find the three folding chairs behind the boiler room, Henri?

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment pliant.
examples.trans: This place is really folding.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Tenez, il y a une enveloppe blanche pliée sur la poignée.
examples.trans: Look, there is a folded white envelope on the handle.

examples.text: Pliez cette feuille et mettez-la dans votre poche tout de suite.
examples.trans: Fold that sheet and put it in your pocket right now.

examples.text: Attendez: il y a une deuxième feuille pliée et attachée derrière cet avis...
examples.trans: Wait: there is a second folded sheet clipped behind this notice...

plisser.gloss: to squint ('plisser les yeux'); to crease, pleat

meanings.en: to squint (*plisser les yeux*); to wrinkle, pleat
meanings.note: *Plisser les yeux* ('to crease/narrow one's eyes') is the exact idiomatic French equivalent of English 'to squint'.

examples.text: Sans ses lunettes, il plisse les yeux pour lire le menu.
examples.trans: Without his glasses, he squints to read the menu.

examples.text: La grande lumière du jardin nous fait plisser les yeux.
examples.trans: The bright garden sunlight makes us squint.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to plunge'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'plongé').

examples.text: La fatigue me plonge dans une transe.
examples.trans: Fatigue plunges me into a trance.

examples.text: Il plongeait jusqu'au bout de sa passion.
examples.trans: He dived to the very end of his passion.

meanings.note: Sous la pluie = in the rain. Feminine noun ('la pluie', plural 'les pluies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'rain'.

examples.text: Sous la pluie?
examples.trans: In the rain?

examples.text: La pluie tombe fort.
examples.trans: The rain is falling hard.

examples.text: Seulement le tilleul de la cour et la pluie.
examples.trans: Only the linden tree in the courtyard and the rain.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la plume', plural 'les plumes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'feather'.
Feminine noun ('la plume', plural 'les plumes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'quill'.

examples.text: Elle voulait voir des plumes!
examples.trans: She wanted to see feathers!

examples.text: Un oiseau aux jolies plumes colorées.
examples.trans: A bird with pretty colored feathers.

examples.text: Elle voulait voir des plumes et des paillettes.
examples.trans: She wanted to see feathers and glitter.

meanings.note: With ne: je n'en peux plus.
pronounced plys at the end of a sentence in this sense

examples.text: Il n'est plus là.
examples.trans: He's not here any more.

examples.text: Henri est deux fois plus curieux que nous!
examples.trans: Henri is twice as curious as we are!

meanings.note: Plusieurs choses = several things. Spoken French det expression meaning 'several', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Je peux faire plusieurs choses ensemble.
examples.trans: I can do several things together.

examples.text: Il a plusieurs amis à Paris.
examples.trans: He has several friends in Paris.

examples.text: Pas depuis plusieurs jours, pour te protéger.
examples.trans: Not for several days, to protect you.

meanings.note: Rather or quite, qualifying a description.
In a choice, instead or rather than; context distinguishes it.

examples.text: Ça va plutôt bien.
examples.trans: It's going pretty well.

examples.text: Je prends plutôt un thé.
examples.trans: I'll have a tea instead.

examples.text: À vrai dire, plutôt bien. Vraiment bien, même.
examples.trans: To tell the truth, rather well. Really well, in fact.

meanings.en: rainy, wet (of weather or a season)
meanings.note: Adjectives in -eux stay unchanged in the masculine plural (pluvieux) and form the feminine in -euse (pluvieuse /plyvjøz/).

examples.text: Après un printemps pluvieux, le jardin est tout vert.
examples.trans: After a rainy spring, the garden is bright green.

examples.text: Par temps pluvieux, tout le monde préfère le salon de thé.
examples.trans: In rainy weather, everyone prefers the tearoom.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le plâtre', plural 'les plâtres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'plaster'.

examples.text: Elle porte un plâtre.
examples.trans: She is wearing a cast.

examples.text: Voici un faux plâtre très élégant.
examples.trans: Here is a very elegant fake cast.

examples.text: Elle porte un plâtre à la jambe.
examples.trans: She wears a cast on her leg.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'full'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: L'adoption plénière est irrévocable.
examples.trans: Full adoption is irrevocable.

examples.text: L'adoption plénière ne sera plus possible.
examples.trans: Full adoption will no longer be possible.

meanings.note: Lampe de poche = pocket flashlight.

examples.text: Elles sont dans la poche de votre manteau?
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

examples.text: Dites-leur que la mienne a un ruban rouge dans la poche du haut!
examples.trans: Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!

examples.text: Ma valise! J'ouvre la poche du haut... oui, mon ruban rouge!
examples.trans: My suitcase! Let me open the top pocket... yes, my red ribbon!

meanings.note: Protective cloth pouch, paper sleeve, or small clutch bag.

examples.text: La boussole se range dans une petite pochette en velours.
examples.trans: The compass slips into a small velvet pouch.

examples.text: J'ai glissé les photographies dans une pochette cartonnée.
examples.trans: I tucked the photographs into a cardboard folder.

meanings.note: Both *-d-* and *-s* are silent (`/pwa/`), and singular and plural are spelled identically (*un poids, des poids*).

examples.text: Appuyez sur la touche de tout le poids de votre main.
examples.trans: Press the key with the full weight of your hand.

examples.text: L'étagère en bois massif supporte facilement ce poids.
examples.trans: The solid wood shelf easily supports that weight.

meanings.en: dagger (coup de poignard = stab in the back)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le poignard', plural 'les poignards') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'dagger'.

examples.text: C'est un coup de poignard.
examples.trans: It is a stab in the back.

examples.text: C'est un véritable coup de poignard!
examples.trans: That is a real stab in the back!

meanings.note: La poignée de la porte = the door handle.

examples.text: Bonjour. Non, soulevez d'abord la poignée, puis poussez.
examples.trans: Good morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.

examples.text: Il y a une petite carte en papier attachée à la poignée.
examples.trans: There is a small paper card tied to the handle.

examples.text: Tenez, il y a une enveloppe blanche pliée sur la poignée.
examples.trans: Look, there is a folded white envelope on the handle.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le poil', plural 'les poils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hair'.
Masculine noun ('le poil', plural 'les poils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'a poil = completely naked'.

examples.text: Je suis à poil tout le temps dans ce film!
examples.trans: I am naked the whole time in this film!

examples.text: Le chien a les poils longs.
examples.trans: The dog has long hair.

examples.text: Je suis à poil tout le temps!
examples.trans: I am naked the entire time!

meanings.note: Des bras poilus = hairy arms. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'hairy'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il est plutôt poilu.
examples.trans: He is quite hairy.

examples.text: Un chien très poilu.
examples.trans: A very hairy dog.

examples.text: Un mètre soixante-quinze, plutôt poilu, beau postérieur... C'est toi, Gabriel?
examples.trans: Five feet nine, quite hairy, nice rear... Is it you, Gabriel?

meanings.note: Coup de poing = punch.

examples.text: Qui a donné le coup de poing?
examples.trans: Who threw the punch?

examples.text: Serrer les poings.
examples.trans: To clench one's fists.

examples.text: Attendez. Qui a donné le coup de poing?
examples.trans: Wait. Who threw the punch?

examples.text: Bon, faisons le point sur les réservations.
examples.trans: Right, let's go over the bookings.

examples.text: C'est un point important pour la réunion.
examples.trans: That's an important point for the meeting.

meanings.note: Sharp tip of a needle, star, or pen; culinary pinch ('une pointe de sel'); 'sur la pointe des pieds' = on tiptoe.

examples.text: La pointe de l'étoile gravée montre le nord.
examples.trans: The tip of the carved star points north.

examples.text: Il traverse le couloir sur la pointe des pieds.
examples.trans: He crosses the hallway on tiptoe.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Regardez où Antoine pointe son crayon, Étienne!
examples.trans: Look where Antoine is pointing his pencil, Etienne!

examples.text: C'est facile à pointer ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to point together.

meanings.note: Faire du 38 de pointure. Feminine noun ('la pointure', plural 'les pointures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shoe size'.
Une grosse pointure. Feminine noun ('la pointure', plural 'les pointures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shoe size'.

examples.text: Prends les miennes, nous faisons la même pointure.
examples.trans: Take mine, we wear the same shoe size.

examples.text: Quelle est votre pointure de chaussures?
examples.trans: What is your shoe size?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le poivre', plural 'les poivres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pepper'.

examples.text: Le sel et le poivre.
examples.trans: Salt and pepper.

examples.text: Ajouter du poivre.
examples.trans: To add pepper.

examples.text: Je confonds le poivre et le sel aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: I confuse the pepper and the salt today.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le poker', plural 'les pokers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'poker'.

examples.text: Et je joue au poker tous les mardis.
examples.trans: And I play poker every Tuesday.

examples.text: Une partie de poker entre amis.
examples.trans: A poker game between friends.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'polite'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il faut rester polis.
examples.trans: We must stay polite.

examples.text: Calme, polie, trente-cinq ans peut-être.
examples.trans: Quiet, polite, maybe thirty-five.

meanings.note: une série policière, un film policier

examples.text: Une série policière.
examples.trans: A detective series.

examples.text: Elle lit un roman policier.
examples.trans: She's reading a crime novel.

examples.text: Entrez. Il a été choisi pour une série policière.
examples.trans: Come in. He has been chosen for a detective series.

meanings.note: engagé politiquement = politically committed

examples.text: Engagé politiquement depuis toujours.
examples.trans: Politically committed all along.

examples.text: C'est correct politiquement.
examples.trans: It's politically correct.

examples.text: C'est un jeune idéaliste engagé politiquement.
examples.trans: He is a young politically committed idealist.

meanings.note: Confiture de pommes = apple jam.

examples.text: Trois bouteilles de lait, vingt œufs, du beurre, du fromage et des pommes rouges!
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

examples.text: Neuf minutes! Voici le lait, les œufs et les pommes!
examples.trans: Nine minutes! Here are the milk, the eggs, and the apples!

examples.text: Excellent choix! Vous voulez du miel ou de la confiture de pommes à côté?
examples.trans: Wonderful choice! Would you like honey or apple jam on the side?

meanings.note: Rounded ornamental knob at the top of a walking stick, umbrella handle, or saddle.

examples.text: Et marchant à côté d'Antoine avec une élégante canne à pommeau d'argent et un chapeau clair...
examples.trans: And walking beside Antoine with an elegant silver-topped walking stick and a light hat...

examples.text: Le pommeau en argent de sa canne brille au soleil de l'après-midi.
examples.trans: The silver knob of his walking stick gleams in the afternoon sun.

meanings.note: La pompe de la piscine.

examples.text: Mais un jour, la pompe a bloqué mon maillot.
examples.trans: But one day, the pump trapped my swimsuit.

examples.text: La pompe fonctionne bien.
examples.trans: The pump works well.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le pompier', plural 'les pompiers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'firefighter'.

examples.text: Appelez les pompiers!
examples.trans: Call the firefighters!

examples.text: J'ai appelé tous les hôpitaux, puis les pompiers.
examples.trans: I called all the hospitals, then the firefighters.

examples.text: Appelez vite les pompiers immédiatement!
examples.trans: Quickly call the fire department immediately!

meanings.note: Takes a cedilla (ç) before a/o to keep the /s/ sound: nous ponçons, je ponçais. From la pierre ponce ('pumice stone').

examples.text: Antoine propose de poncer les vieilles tables en bois dans la cour.
examples.trans: Antoine offers to sand down the old wooden tables in the courtyard.

examples.text: Il faut poncer légèrement le volet avant de le repeindre.
examples.trans: You need to sand the shutter lightly before repainting it.

meanings.note: Being right on time.

examples.text: Moi? Oh, j'adore simplement la ponctualité! Sept heures quatorze, quelle belle minute!
examples.trans: Me? Oh, I simply love punctuality! Seven fourteen, what a lovely minute!

examples.text: Voici la ponctualité sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the punctuality on the table.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le pont', plural 'les ponts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bridge'.

examples.text: Le pont, puis la pharmacie verte à droite. Et ensuite?
examples.trans: The bridge, then the green pharmacy on the right. And next?

examples.text: À gauche au portail, tout droit jusqu'au pont. Je traverse le fleuve?
examples.trans: Left at the gate, straight ahead to the bridge. Do I cross the river?

meanings.en: pop (sudden soft snapping or popping sound)
meanings.note: Onomatopoeic noun; used in spoken French for the small pop of a blown bulb, fuse, or cork.

examples.text: On a entendu un petit pop quand le fusible a sauté.
examples.trans: We heard a little pop when the fuse blew.

examples.text: La lampe s'allume enfin en silence, sans aucun pop.
examples.trans: The lamp finally turns on silently, without a single pop.

meanings.note: Liked or known by a broad public.
In other contexts, of ordinary people or working-class.

examples.text: Elle est très populaire.
examples.trans: She's very popular.

examples.text: C'est une chanson populaire.
examples.trans: It's a popular song.

examples.text: Line Renaud est belle, du bon âge, et très populaire.
examples.trans: Line Renaud is beautiful, the right age, and very popular.

meanings.note: Used both for delicate tableware (des tasses en porcelaine) and for classic ceramic electrical fuses and insulators.

examples.text: Les vieilles tasses en porcelaine blanche sont rangées dans le buffet.
examples.trans: The old white china cups are stored in the sideboard.

examples.text: Henri installe un fusible neuf en porcelaine dans le boîtier.
examples.trans: Henri fits a new porcelain fuse inside the fuse box.

meanings.note: Covered stone entranceway or vaulted carriage porch leading into a courtyard.

examples.text: Abritez-vous sous le porche le temps que la pluie passe.
examples.trans: Take shelter under the arched doorway while the rain passes.

examples.text: Le vieux porche voûté ouvre sur une cour fleurie.
examples.trans: The old vaulted porch opens onto a flower-filled courtyard.

meanings.en: portable, mobile; téléphone portable = mobile phone
meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Mon téléphone portable.
examples.trans: My mobile phone.

examples.text: Un appareil portable.
examples.trans: A portable device.

examples.text: Attendez, j'ai oublié mon téléphone portable!
examples.trans: Wait, I forgot my mobile phone!

meanings.note: Regular plural: les portails.

examples.text: Voilà un taxi devant le portail à l'instant.
examples.trans: Here comes a taxi in front of the gate right now.

examples.text: Vous avez entendu ça, Henri? Quelqu'un vient de sonner au portail!
examples.trans: Did you hear that, Henri? Someone just rang the gate bell!

examples.text: Bonjour, Madame Odette! Regardez ce qui est arrivé au portail hier soir.
examples.trans: Good morning, Madam Odette! Look what arrived at the gate last night.

meanings.note: Laisser la porte ouverte means leave the door open.

examples.text: La porte est ouverte.
examples.trans: The door is open.

examples.text: Ferme la porte.
examples.trans: Close the door.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le porte-bonheur', plural 'les porte-bonheur') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'lucky charm'.

examples.text: Tu es mon porte-bonheur.
examples.trans: You are my lucky charm.

examples.text: Vous êtes un porte-bonheur pour moi.
examples.trans: You are a lucky charm for me.

meanings.note: Pocket wallet for bills and cards; artist's or minister's portfolio.

examples.text: Il garde une vieille photo pliée dans son portefeuille.
examples.trans: He keeps an old folded photo in his wallet.

examples.text: Avez-vous pensé à prendre votre portefeuille avant de sortir?
examples.trans: Did you remember to grab your wallet before heading out?

meanings.en: to carry (heavy items); to wear (clothing or glasses)
meanings.note: Covers both carrying objects (porter les tables, porter un panier) and wearing clothes or accessories (porter des lunettes).

examples.text: Les deux frères portent facilement la grande table de la cave.
examples.trans: The two brothers easily carry the big table up from the cellar.

examples.text: Thibault m'aide à porter les pots de miel jusqu'à l'hôtel.
examples.trans: Thibault helps me carry the honey jars back to the hotel.

examples.text: J'ai coincé la portière.
examples.trans: I jammed the car door.

examples.text: Ferme la portière.
examples.trans: Close the car door.

meanings.note: Fortified wine from Portugal.

examples.text: J'ai du porto.
examples.trans: I have some port.

examples.text: Tu veux un verre de porto?
examples.trans: Do you want a glass of port?

examples.text: J'adore le porto.
examples.trans: I love port.

meanings.note: Drawn, painted, or photographed likeness of a person.

examples.text: Un portrait au fusain est accroché au-dessus de la cheminée.
examples.trans: A charcoal portrait hangs above the fireplace.

examples.text: Elle ressemble trait pour trait au portrait de sa grand-mère.
examples.trans: She looks feature for feature like her grandmother's portrait.

meanings.note: Poser une question.
Poser une question.

examples.text: Pose ton sac ici.
examples.trans: Put your bag here.

examples.text: Je peux poser une question?
examples.trans: Can I ask a question?

examples.text: Il y a un côté positif.
examples.trans: There's a bright side.

examples.text: Elle est positive.
examples.trans: She's positive.

meanings.note: en position de faiblesse = in a position of weakness

examples.text: Être en position de faiblesse.
examples.trans: To be in a position of weakness.

examples.text: Quelle est votre position?
examples.trans: What is your position?

examples.text: C'est mauvais pour l'agence d'être en position de faiblesse.
examples.trans: It's bad for the agency to be in a position of weakness.

meanings.note: Pas possible! = No way! / You're kidding!

examples.text: Pas possible! Tu as trouvé un atelier dans notre rue?!
examples.trans: No way! You found a studio on our street?!

examples.text: Venez dès que possible pour goûter les tartes chaudes.
examples.trans: Come as soon as possible to taste the warm tarts.

meanings.note: stem change é -> è in present singular

examples.text: On ne possède pas quelqu'un.
examples.trans: You do not own someone.

examples.text: Il possède une maison.
examples.trans: He owns a house.

examples.text: Ton corps t'appartient. On ne possède pas quelqu'un.
examples.trans: Your body belongs to you. You do not own someone.

meanings.note: Carte postale = postcard; m.pl. postaux.

examples.text: Nous ne nous sommes pas parlé depuis ce jour-là. La semaine dernière, je lui ai envoyé une courte carte postale.
examples.trans: We have not spoken since that day. Last week I sent him one short postcard.

examples.text: Regardez, il est déjà midi quatre. Peut-être qu'il a jeté ma carte postale à la poubelle.
examples.trans: Look, it is already twelve-oh-four. Maybe he threw my postcard in the bin.

examples.text: J'ai reconnu ton écriture carrée sur cette carte postale en deux secondes.
examples.trans: I recognized your neat block handwriting on that postcard in two seconds.

meanings.note: Gender pair: masculine *un poste* is a job/position or station; feminine *la poste* is the post office.

examples.text: Goûter les tartes chaudes est le meilleur poste de la maison!
examples.trans: Tasting warm tarts is the best job in the house!

examples.text: Chacun connaît son poste en cuisine pour demain matin.
examples.trans: Everyone knows their kitchen station for tomorrow morning.

meanings.en: to apply for (a job or position)
meanings.note: Postuler à / pour un poste. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to apply'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'postulé').

examples.trans: You do not want me to apply?

examples.trans: To apply for a job.

meanings.note: Un beau postérieur = a nice rear. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'rear, backside'.

examples.trans: A nice rear in the photo.

examples.trans: He sits on his backside.

examples.trans: Five feet nine, quite hairy, nice rear... Is it you, Gabriel?

pot.gloss: jar, pot, jug (pot à lait = milk jug)

meanings.en: jar (of jam or honey), flower pot, small jug
meanings.note: Final -t is silent in both singular and plural (/po/). Un pot de miel = a jar of honey; un arbre en pot = a potted tree; un pot à lait = a milk jug.

examples.trans: Nadia lines up six jars of jam on the shelf.

examples.text: J'apporte une théière chaude et un petit pot à lait.
examples.trans: I am bringing a hot teapot and a small milk jug.

meanings.note: Un bon pote.

examples.trans: A buddy in a jam.

examples.text: C'est mon meilleur pote.
examples.trans: He's my best buddy.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le potentiel', plural 'les potentiels') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'potential'.

examples.text: Ce jeune comédien a vraiment un grand potentiel.
examples.trans: This young actor really has great potential.

examples.text: Nous cherchons des acheteurs potentiels pour l'agence.
examples.trans: We are looking for potential buyers for the agency.

meanings.note: Feminine noun derived from potier ('potter').

examples.text: Le stand de poterie vend de très beaux bols faits à la main.
examples.trans: The pottery stall sells lovely handmade bowls.

examples.text: J'adore la poterie artisanale de notre région.
examples.trans: I love the handcrafted pottery from our region.

meanings.note: jeter à la poubelle = to throw in the trash

examples.text: Vider la poubelle.
examples.trans: To empty the trash.

examples.trans: To throw in the trash.

meanings.note: Finely ground culinary ingredient ('poudre d'amandes' = almond flour/ground almonds; 'sucre en poudre' = caster sugar).

examples.trans: This guy is the golden goose.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le poème', plural 'les poèmes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'poem'.

examples.text: Écrire un poème.
examples.trans: To write a poem.

examples.text: Lire un poème.

Prendre quelqu'un dans un film.
