examples.text: Avec un discours pareil, tout le monde va s'endormir!
examples.trans: With a speech like that, everyone is going to fall asleep!

examples.text: Le chat s'est endormi sur le coussin tiède.
examples.trans: The cat fell asleep on the warm cushion.

meanings.note: Bien s'entendre = to get on well.

examples.text: Nous nous entendons bien.
examples.trans: We get along well.

examples.text: Elle s'entend bien avec Hervé.
examples.trans: She gets on well with Hervé.

s'envoler.gloss: to soar, take flight, float away

meanings.en: to take wing, fly off, soar (of birds, sheets of paper, or musical notes)
meanings.note: Les notes s'envolent dans la cour = the notes soar out into the courtyard.

cells: il s'est envolé / elle s'est envolée
ils se sont envolés / elles se sont envolées

examples.text: Les premières notes du violon s'envolent sous le tilleul.
examples.trans: The first notes of the violin soar out under the linden tree.

examples.text: Fermez le dossier avant que vos feuilles s'envolent!
examples.trans: Close the folder before your pages blow away!

meanings.note: Apologise with pour or de introducing what one is sorry for; pronominal verb uses être in the past.

examples.text: Je voudrais m'excuser pour hier.
examples.trans: I'd like to apologise for yesterday.

examples.text: Il s'excuse toujours.
examples.trans: He's always apologising.

examples.text: Il doit s'excuser d'abord!
examples.trans: He must apologise first!

meanings.en: to humiliate oneself, to lose face
meanings.note: Humiliate oneself or lose face; pronominal verb uses être in the compound past.

examples.text: Je ne vais pas m'humilier.
examples.trans: I'm not going to humiliate myself.

examples.text: Il ne veut pas s'humilier devant elle.
examples.trans: He doesn't want to lose face in front of her.

examples.text: Je ne vais pas m'humilier. Je sais qu'il dira non.
examples.trans: I'm not going to humiliate myself. I know he'll say no.

meanings.en: please (to one person you say 'tu' to)
meanings.note: literally 'if it pleases you'; formal/plural is 's'il vous plaît'

examples.text: Hervé, s'il te plaît!
examples.trans: Hervé, please!

examples.text: Viens m'aider, s'il te plaît.
examples.trans: Come and help me, please.

examples.text: Hervé, s'il te plaît! Je veux mon thé.
examples.trans: Hervé, please! I want my tea.

meanings.note: formal or plural; casual: s'il te plaît

examples.text: Un café, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: A coffee, please.

examples.text: Asseyez-vous, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Have a seat, please.

examples.text: Réservez-moi un massage, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Book me a massage, please.

s'occuper.gloss: to take care of, to deal with

meanings.en: to look after, to take care of
meanings.note: S'occuper de quelqu'un.
Je m'en occupe = I'll handle it.

examples.text: Tu t'occupes de lui?
examples.trans: Do you look after him?

examples.text: Je m'occupe de tout.
examples.trans: I'll take care of everything.

meanings.note: Fine sand of garden paths, beaches, or bedding beneath flagstones.

examples.text: La dalle repose sur un lit de sable bien sec.
examples.trans: The flagstone rests on a bed of dry sand.

examples.text: Les allées de sable blond crissent doucement sous nos pas.
examples.trans: The pale sand paths crunch softly beneath our footsteps.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le sac', plural 'les sacs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'handbag'.

examples.text: Pose ton sac sur la table.
examples.trans: Put your bag on the table.

examples.text: Pour l'instant, son sac reste bien enfermé à clé.
examples.trans: For now, his bag stays safely locked up.

examples.text: Gardez mon sac bleu jusqu'à vendredi, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Please keep my blue bag until Friday.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le sacrifice', plural 'les sacrifices') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sacrifice'.

examples.text: Ce métier demande parfois de grands sacrifices personnels.
examples.trans: This profession sometimes requires great personal sacrifices.

examples.text: Ses parents ont fait beaucoup de sacrifices pour ses études.
examples.trans: Her parents made many sacrifices for her studies.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to sacrifice'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'sacrifié').

examples.text: Je ne vais pas sacrifier notre relation pour un film.
examples.trans: I'm not going to sacrifice our relationship for a film.

examples.text: Il a tout sacrifié.
examples.trans: He sacrificed everything.

examples.text: Jamais plus! Je ne vais pas sacrifier notre relation pour un film.
examples.trans: Never again! I'm not going to sacrifice our relationship for a film.

meanings.note: After noun: un dossier sacré. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sacred'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Before noun: un sacré menteur. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sacred'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Chaque dossier est sacré ici.
examples.trans: Every file is sacred here.

examples.text: Un lieu sacré.
examples.trans: A sacred place.

examples.text: Chaque dossier est sacré ici. Toujours.
examples.trans: Every file is sacred here. Always.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'well-behaved'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Le chien est très sage.
examples.trans: The dog is very well-behaved.

examples.text: Écoutez: même la sonnette de la chambre quatre est restée sage toute la soirée!
examples.trans: Listen: even room four's buzzer has behaved itself all evening!

examples.text: sage
examples.trans: well-behaved

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la sage-femme', plural 'les sages-femmes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'midwife'.

examples.text: Elle appelle la sage-femme.
examples.trans: She calls the midwife.

examples.text: Qu'est-ce qu'elle dit, la sage-femme?
examples.trans: What is the midwife saying?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la sagesse', plural 'les sagesses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'wisdom'.

examples.text: Merci pour ta sagesse.
examples.trans: Thank you for your wisdom.

examples.text: Merci pour ta sagesse, Arlette.
examples.trans: Thank you for your wisdom, Arlette.

meanings.en: to bleed, drain dry, squeeze financially
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to bleed'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'saigné').

examples.text: Elle est en train de nous saigner.
examples.trans: She is bleeding us dry.

examples.text: Élise est en train de nous saigner.
examples.trans: Élise is bleeding us dry.

examples.text: Tu veux saigner notre agence?
examples.trans: Do you want to bleed our agency dry?

meanings.note: Saisir l'instant. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to grasp, seize'.
Saisir le sens. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to grasp, seize'.

examples.text: C'est beaucoup mieux, nous saisissons cet instant!
examples.trans: It is much better, we grasp this moment!

examples.text: Il a saisi cette belle occasion.
examples.trans: He seized this fine opportunity.

meanings.en: season (of a TV show or year)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la saison', plural 'les saisons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'calendar season'.

examples.text: La prochaine saison de la série.
examples.trans: The next season of the series.

examples.text: Peux-tu trouver la prochaine saison?
examples.trans: Can you find the next season?

examples.text: C'est maintenant la saison des présentations d'atelier.
examples.trans: It is now theater workshop showcase season.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la salade', plural 'les salades') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'salad'.

examples.text: Une salade verte.
examples.trans: A green salad.

examples.text: Manger de la salade.
examples.trans: To eat salad.

examples.text: Je mange une salade de quinoa.
examples.trans: I am eating a quinoa salad.

meanings.note: réduire les salaires = to reduce salaries

examples.text: L'égalité des salaires est importante.
examples.trans: Equal pay is important.

examples.text: L'égalité des salaires est importante dans tous les métiers.
examples.trans: Equal pay is important in every profession.

examples.text: Nos salaires sont versés à la fin du mois.
examples.trans: Our salaries are paid at the end of the month.

meanings.note: Un torchon sale.
Une sale histoire.

examples.text: Elle le prend comme un torchon sale!
examples.trans: She takes it like a dirty rag!

examples.text: Tes mains sont sales.
examples.trans: Your hands are dirty.

meanings.note: se salir les mains = to get one's hands dirty

examples.text: Se salir les mains.
examples.trans: To get one's hands dirty.

examples.text: Salir un vêtement.
examples.trans: To dirty a piece of clothing.

examples.text: Il faut parfois se salir les mains.
examples.trans: One must sometimes get one's hands dirty.

meanings.note: a large or shared room: salle de presse, salle de réunion

examples.text: Voilà la salle de presse.
examples.trans: Here's the press room.

examples.text: La salle est pleine.
examples.trans: The room is full.

salon.gloss: lounge, drawing room (salon de thé = tearoom)

meanings.en: living room, lounge; tearoom (salon de thé)
meanings.note: Un salon de thé is a traditional French tearoom serving hot tea, pastries, and tarts in the afternoon.

examples.text: Le salon de thé accueille les voisins chaque vendredi après-midi.
examples.trans: The tearoom welcomes neighbours every Friday afternoon.

examples.text: Les voyageurs lisent tranquillement dans le petit salon.
examples.trans: The guests read quietly in the small lounge.

saluer.gloss: to greet; to take a bow

meanings.en: to greet, say hello to; to bow to an audience
meanings.note: Saluer les voisins = greet the neighbors; saluer le public = take a bow.

examples.text: La pianiste et le violoniste saluent le public ensemble.
examples.trans: The pianist and the violinist take a bow together.

examples.text: Elle sort sur le pas de la porte pour saluer les habitués.
examples.trans: She steps out to the doorway to greet the regulars.

meanings.note: Casual.
Casual.

examples.text: Salut! Tu dois être Claire. Moi, c'est Nadia, de la cuisine.
examples.trans: Hi! You must be Claire. I am Nadia, from the kitchen.

examples.text: Salut, à demain!
examples.trans: Bye, see you tomorrow!

meanings.note: Beurre salé = salted butter; opposite of doux / sucré.

examples.text: On peut servir du beurre salé avec de la confiture de fraises?
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with strawberry jam?

examples.text: Attendez: le beurre salé est mauvais pour la confiture, mais génial pour les œufs brouillés!
examples.trans: Wait: salted butter is bad for jam, but amazing for scrambled eggs!

examples.text: Claire a acheté du beurre salé, alors ce matin on fait de bons œufs brouillés!
examples.trans: Claire bought salted butter, so this morning we are making good scrambled eggs!

meanings.note: Medial -e- is usually dropped in speech (/samdi/). Samedi = 'on Saturday' (this Saturday); le samedi = 'on Saturdays' (habitually).

examples.text: Le grand marché a lieu sur la place chaque samedi matin.
examples.trans: The big market takes place on the square every Saturday morning.

examples.text: La livraison des chaises arrive samedi à quatorze heures.
examples.trans: The delivery of the chairs arrives on Saturday at two p.m.

meanings.en: SAMU, emergency medical response service in France
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le samu', plural 'les samus') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'SAMU'.

examples.text: Appelez vite le SAMU, cet homme a fait un malaise!
examples.trans: Call the paramedics quickly, this man has fainted!

examples.text: Les médecins du SAMU sont arrivés en cinq minutes.
examples.trans: The emergency medical team arrived in five minutes.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'vascular'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un vaisseau sanguin s'est bouché.
examples.trans: A blood vessel got blocked.

examples.text: Un petit vaisseau sanguin s'est bouché.
examples.trans: A small blood vessel got blocked.

examples.text: Sans rendez-vous?
examples.trans: Without an appointment?

examples.text: Un café sans sucre.
examples.trans: A coffee without sugar.

meanings.note: Santé! = Cheers! (to your health). Normally uncountable in this sense.

examples.text: Levons nos verres et buvons à votre bonne santé!
examples.trans: Let's raise our glasses and drink to your good health!

examples.text: Le médecin dit qu'il est en parfaite santé.
examples.trans: The doctor says that he is in perfect health.

examples.text: À votre santé!
examples.trans: To your health! / Cheers!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le sashimi', plural 'les sashimis') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sashimi'.

examples.text: Nous avons partagé une assiette de sashimis au restaurant japonais.
examples.trans: We shared a plate of sashimi at the Japanese restaurant.

examples.text: Le chef coupe le poisson frais pour préparer les sashimis.
examples.trans: The chef slices the fresh fish to prepare the sashimi.

meanings.note: Satisfait de = pleased with.

examples.text: Je suis satisfait.
examples.trans: I'm satisfied.

examples.text: Tu as l'air satisfait de toi.
examples.trans: You look pleased with yourself.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la saucisse', plural 'les saucisses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cooked sausage'.

examples.text: Une saucisse délicieuse.
examples.trans: A delicious sausage.

examples.text: La saucisse de Morteau est spectaculaire.
examples.trans: The Morteau sausage is spectacular.

meanings.note: Sauf que = except that.

examples.text: Sauf que ce sera dans un hangar.
examples.trans: Except that it will be in a warehouse.

examples.text: Tout le monde est là sauf lui.
examples.trans: Everyone is here except him.

examples.text: Sauf s'il écrit pour le Guide annuel de Lyon!
examples.trans: Unless he writes for the annual Lyon Guide!

sauter.gloss: to jump; to blow (faire sauter un fusible)

meanings.en: to jump, leap; (electrical) to blow or trip
meanings.note: Faire sauter le fusible / les plombs means 'to blow the fuse / trip the breaker'.

examples.text: Le vieux câble en tissu a fait sauter le fusible de l'entrée.
examples.trans: The old cloth-covered wire blew the entrance fuse.

examples.text: Le chat saute légèrement sur le muret du jardin.
examples.trans: The cat leaps lightly onto the low garden wall.

meanings.note: Se comporter comme un sauvage.
Un animal sauvage.

examples.text: Tu m'appelles une sauvage?
examples.trans: Are you calling me a savage?

examples.text: Donc je suis soit une esclave, soit une danseuse de hip-hop, soit une sauvage?
examples.trans: So I'm either a slave, or a hip-hop dancer, or a savage?

examples.text: Pourquoi se cache-t-il dans les bois sauvages?
examples.trans: Why is he hiding in the wild woods?

examples.text: Il a sauvé le contrat.
examples.trans: He saved the contract.

examples.text: Tu m'as sauvé!
examples.trans: You saved me!

meanings.note: Tu es mon sauveur. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'savior, rescuer'.

examples.text: Tu es mon sauveur, Noémie!
examples.trans: You are my savior, Noémie!

examples.text: Notre sauveur est arrivé.
examples.trans: Our savior has arrived.

examples.text: Oh, voilà enfin mon sauveur adoré!
examples.trans: Oh, here is finally my beloved savior!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la saveur', plural 'les saveurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'flavor'.

examples.text: Elle veut goûter chaque saveur.
examples.trans: She wants to taste each flavor.

examples.text: Je veux goûter toutes les saveurs.
examples.trans: I want to taste every flavor.

savoir.gloss: to know; to know how to

meanings.note: Je ne sais pas = I don't know.
+ infinitive: savoir monter.

examples.text: Vous savez monter?
examples.trans: Can you ride?

examples.text: Super. Dites-moi tout ce qu'il faut savoir.
examples.trans: Great. Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: passer un savon = to give an earful, scold

examples.text: Un morceau de savon.
examples.trans: A bar of soap.

examples.text: Ampoule neuve la semaine dernière, savon propre et beaucoup d'eau chaude.
examples.trans: New bulb last week, clean soap, and plenty of hot water.

meanings.note: From *le savon* ('soap'); masculine singular and plural are identical (*savonneux*), feminine *-euse* (`/savɔnøz/`).

examples.text: Lavez d'abord les carreaux avec une éponge et de l'eau savonneuse.
examples.trans: First wash the windowpanes with a sponge and soapy water.

examples.text: Attention, le sol mouillé est un peu savonneux.
examples.trans: Careful, the wet floor is a little soapy.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to savor'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'savouré').

examples.text: Laisse-moi savourer mon verre.
examples.trans: Let me savor my drink.

examples.text: Il savoure sa victoire.
examples.trans: He savors his victory.

examples.text: Excusez-moi un instant, madame, savourez votre thé chaud!
examples.trans: Excuse me one moment, madam, enjoy your hot tea!

meanings.note: Un grand scandale. Masculine noun ('le scandale', plural 'les scandales') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'scandal'.

examples.text: Élisabeth prétend qu'il y a un scandale.
examples.trans: Elisabeth claims that there is a scandal.

examples.text: Cette affaire a causé un scandale.
examples.trans: This affair caused a scandal.

examples.text: Mais de quel scandale parles-tu donc?
examples.trans: But what scandal are you talking about?

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Ce comportement est tout à fait scandaleux.
examples.trans: This behavior is completely scandalous.

examples.text: Une décision scandaleuse.
examples.trans: A scandalous decision.

examples.text: C'est scandaleux, elle a eu raison.
examples.trans: That is outrageous, she was right.

meanings.note: Stamped wax or official emblem seal ('sceau de cire' = wax seal; homophone of 'seau' = bucket).

examples.text: Le sceau de cire porte les initiales des trois amis.
examples.trans: The wax seal bears the initials of the three friends.

examples.text: Elle brise délicatement le sceau avec le coupe-papier.
examples.trans: She delicately breaks the seal with the letter opener.

meanings.note: To seal an envelope with wax or seal a stone box shut; figuratively to seal a pact.

examples.text: L'enveloppe était scellée à la cire rouge depuis trente ans.
examples.trans: The envelope had been sealed with red wax for thirty years.

examples.text: Une poignée de main chaleureuse vient sceller leur accord.
examples.trans: A warm handshake seals their agreement.

meanings.note: rester sceptique = to remain skeptical

examples.text: Je sais que vous êtes sceptique.
examples.trans: I know you are skeptical.

examples.text: Un regard sceptique.
examples.trans: A skeptical look.

examples.text: Je sais que vous êtes sceptique, mais je connais un chaman extraordinaire.
examples.trans: I know you are skeptical, but I know an extraordinary shaman.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la science-fiction', plural 'les science-fictions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'science fiction'.

examples.text: C'est un film de science-fiction.
examples.trans: It is a science fiction film.

examples.text: Ce film de science-fiction sera un navet.
examples.trans: This science fiction movie will be a dud.

meanings.note: Sur mon scooter = on my scooter.

examples.text: On y va sur mon scooter.
examples.trans: We're going on my scooter.

examples.text: Il vient en scooter.
examples.trans: He comes by scooter.

examples.text: On y va sur mon scooter. Tu n'as pas peur?
examples.trans: We're going on my scooter. You're not afraid?

meanings.note: of a film or play; also le scénario

examples.text: Voici les scripts.
examples.trans: Here are the scripts.

examples.text: Elle lit un script.
examples.trans: She's reading a script.

meanings.note: sans scrupules = ruthless, without scruples

examples.text: Cette femme est sans scrupules.
examples.trans: This woman is without scruples.

examples.text: Avoir des scrupules.
examples.trans: To have qualms.

examples.text: Cette femme est un monstre sans scrupules!
examples.trans: This woman is a monster without scruples!

meanings.note: Note silent p in pronunciation: /skylte/.

examples.text: Ouvre le papier blanc... non! La locomotive en bois sculptée par Grand-Père!
examples.trans: Open the white paper... no! The wooden locomotive carved by Grandfather!

examples.text: C'est facile à sculpter ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to carve, sculpt together.

meanings.note: A scene in a film or play; scène d’amour, love scene.
The stage: sur scène, on stage.

examples.text: C'est une belle scène.
examples.trans: It's a beautiful scene.

examples.text: Elle monte sur scène.
examples.trans: She goes on stage.

examples.text: Quand vous regardez des films, des scènes d'amour...
examples.trans: When you watch films, love scenes...

meanings.note: The written story and dialogue of a film.
A possible situation.

examples.text: Sans scénario, pas de film.
examples.trans: No script, no film.

examples.text: C'est un bon scénario.
examples.trans: It's a good script.

meanings.note: From 'scénario' (screenplay).

examples.text: Elle est chef scénariste sur la série.
examples.trans: She is head screenwriter on the series.

examples.text: Un grand scénariste.
examples.trans: A great screenwriter.

meanings.note: La scénographie du spectacle.

examples.text: Toute la scénographie est construite autour.
examples.trans: The entire set design is built around it.

examples.text: La scénographie est magnifique.
examples.trans: The set design is magnificent.

examples.text: Pas de piscine? Toute la scénographie est construite autour.
examples.trans: No pool? The entire set design is built around it.

meanings.note: Reflexive clitic used with third-person subjects; s' before a suitable vowel sound.

examples.text: Il se réveille.
examples.trans: He wakes up.

examples.text: Elle se prépare.
examples.trans: She gets ready.

meanings.note: Fight or struggle; contre introduces what one opposes, pour what one supports.

examples.text: Il faut se battre.
examples.trans: We have to fight.

examples.text: Ils se battent pour le rôle.
examples.trans: They're fighting for the part.

examples.text: Oui, il faut se battre contre le chagrin.
examples.trans: Yes, we must fight against sorrow.

examples.text: Je n'arrive pas à me concentrer.
examples.trans: I can't concentrate.

examples.text: Concentre-toi!
examples.trans: Concentrate!

meanings.note: On your own, without help.
débrouille-toi! = sort it out yourself!

examples.text: Je me débrouille seule.
examples.trans: I manage on my own.

examples.text: Il se débrouille bien en français.
examples.trans: He gets by well in French.

se méfier.gloss: to distrust; to be wary of

meanings.en: to distrust; to be wary of

examples.text: Méfie-toi de lui.
examples.trans: Be wary of him.

examples.text: Je me méfie de cette promesse.
examples.trans: I distrust that promise.

se passer.governs: mostly used with ça or il as subject

meanings.note: qu'est-ce qui se passe? = what's happening?
Ça se passe bien = it's going well.

examples.text: Ça se passe bien?
examples.trans: Is it going well?

examples.text: Qu'est-ce qui se passe?
examples.trans: What's going on?

examples.text: Ça ne se passe pas du tout.
examples.trans: It's not happening at all.

meanings.note: Remember something: se souvenir de plus what is remembered.

examples.text: Vous vous souvenez encore de ça après toutes ces années?
examples.trans: Do you still remember that after all these years?

examples.text: Je ne me souviens pas.
examples.trans: I don't remember.

examples.text: Je ne me souviens pas vraiment.
examples.trans: I don't really remember.

se tromper.gloss: to be wrong, to make a mistake

meanings.en: to be wrong, to be mistaken
meanings.note: Reflexive.

meanings.en: se tromper de: to get the wrong...
meanings.note: Se tromper de porte.

examples.text: Je me suis trompée.
examples.trans: I was wrong.

examples.text: Tu te trompes.
examples.trans: You're wrong.

meanings.note: Pronounced `/so/` (plural *des seaux*, also `/so/`).

examples.text: Remplissez le seau d'eau tiède avant de monter sur l'échelle.
examples.trans: Fill the bucket with warm water before climbing the ladder.

examples.text: Elle pose deux seaux propres à côté de la porte du jardin.
examples.trans: She sets two clean buckets beside the garden door.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'dry'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Du pain sec.
examples.trans: Dry bread.

examples.text: Une feuille sèche.
examples.trans: A dry leaf.

examples.text: Antoine l'a posé quand il a pris la serviette sèche!
examples.trans: Antoine set it down when he took the dry towel!

meanings.note: le second rôle = the supporting role

examples.text: Elle joue le second rôle.
examples.trans: She plays the supporting role.

examples.text: La seconde fois.
examples.trans: The second time.

examples.text: Oui! Le second rôle, avec un cachet formidable!
examples.trans: Yes! The supporting role, with a huge paycheck!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'secondary'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Les effets secondaires.
examples.trans: The side effects.

examples.text: Une question secondaire.
examples.trans: A secondary issue.

examples.text: Regardez les effets secondaires sur Internet!
examples.trans: Look at the side effects on the Internet!

meanings.note: A second, the unit of time; the c sounds like g.
As an adjective, feminine form of second.

examples.text: En deux secondes.
examples.trans: In two seconds.

examples.text: Une seconde, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: One second, please.

examples.text: Écouter le son de la pièce... attendez une seconde!
examples.trans: Listening to the sound of the room... wait a second!

meanings.note: Au secours! = help!.

examples.text: Au secours!
examples.trans: Help!

examples.text: Appeler les secours.
examples.trans: To call emergency services.

examples.text: Au secours! François?
examples.trans: Help! François?

meanings.note: En secret = in secret, secretly.

examples.text: Ça restera notre petit secret.
examples.trans: It will stay our little secret.

examples.text: Tu travailles en secret?
examples.trans: Are you working in secret?

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Ils créent secrètement une agence.
examples.trans: They are secretly creating an agency.

examples.text: Elle prépare secrètement son départ.
examples.trans: She is secretly preparing her departure.

examples.text: Ils créent secrètement leur propre agence concurrente.
examples.trans: They are secretly creating their own rival agency.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la secrétaire', plural 'les secrétaires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'office assistant'.

examples.text: Une jeune secrétaire au bureau.
examples.trans: A young secretary at the office.

examples.text: C'est une jeune secrétaire jolie et sexy.
examples.trans: She is a young, pretty, and sexy secretary.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'section, division'.

examples.text: Une section du festival.
examples.trans: A section of the festival.

examples.text: La section officielle.
examples.trans: The official section.

examples.text: Il y a aussi une section appelée ACID.
examples.trans: There is also a section called ACID.

meanings.note: les seins d'une femme = a woman's breasts

examples.text: Mes seins ont changé.
examples.trans: My breasts have changed.

examples.text: Nourrir au sein.
examples.trans: To breastfeed.

examples.text: Mes seins ne sont pas très rayonnants!
examples.trans: My breasts are not very radiant!

meanings.note: Last of the single-word French teens before hyphenated *dix-sept, dix-huit, dix-neuf*.

examples.text: Il manque exactement seize mesures à la fin de cette valse.
examples.trans: Exactly sixteen bars are missing at the end of this waltz.

examples.text: Le train de seize heures arrive toujours à l'heure.
examples.trans: The four p.m. (16:00) train always arrives on time.

meanings.note: Final *-l* is pronounced (`/sɛl/`); *du sel fin* is fine table/baking salt, *du gros sel* is coarse cooking salt.

examples.text: Passez-moi le pot de sel pour la soupe de légumes, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Pass me the salt jar for the vegetable soup, please.

examples.text: Ne confondez surtout pas le sel fin et le sucre en poudre!
examples.trans: Above all, don't mix up the fine salt and the caster sugar!

meanings.note: From English.

examples.text: On fait un selfie?
examples.trans: Shall we take a selfie?

examples.text: Elle veut un selfie avec la star.
examples.trans: She wants a selfie with the star.

meanings.note: Figurative.

meanings.en: se remettre en selle = to get back in the saddle
meanings.note: Figurative.

examples.text: Elle peut se remettre en selle.
examples.trans: She can get back in the saddle.

examples.text: La selle du cheval.
examples.trans: The horse's saddle.

meanings.note: Cette semaine = this week.

examples.text: Je dois voir la pièce cette semaine.
examples.trans: I have to see the play this week.

examples.text: Trois semaines.
examples.trans: Three weeks.

examples.text: Bon, on faisait semblant.
examples.trans: All right, we were pretending.

examples.text: Elle fait semblant de dormir.
examples.trans: She's pretending to sleep.

examples.text: Bon, on faisait semblant. On était là pour voir le directeur.
examples.trans: All right, we were pretending. We were there to see the manager.

examples.text: Vous semblez souffrir.
examples.trans: You seem to be suffering.

examples.text: Il semble fatigué ce matin.
examples.trans: He seems tired this morning.

meanings.en: meaning, reason (avoir du sens = to make sense)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le sens', plural 'les sens') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'meaning'.

examples.text: Ça n'a aucun sens.
examples.trans: That makes no sense.

examples.text: Claire, vous avez le sens de l'accueil!
examples.trans: Claire, you have a gift for hospitality!

examples.text: Claire, vous avez le sens de l'accueil! Vous me sauvez la vie!
examples.trans: Claire, you have a gift for hospitality! You are saving my life!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la sensation', plural 'les sensations') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sensation'.

examples.text: C'est une sensation divine.
examples.trans: It is a divine feeling.

examples.text: C'est une sensation artistique absolument divine.
examples.trans: It is an absolutely divine artistic feeling.

examples.text: Je vais faire sensation.
examples.trans: I am going to make a splash.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la sensibilité', plural 'les sensibilités') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sensitivity'.

examples.text: Il a une grande sensibilité artistique.
examples.trans: He has a great artistic sensitivity.

examples.text: Et il a aussi beaucoup de sensibilité.
examples.trans: And he also has a lot of sensitivity.

meanings.note: false friend: English 'sensible' is 'raisonnable'

examples.text: Les acteurs sont fragiles et sensibles.
examples.trans: Actors are fragile and sensitive.

examples.text: C'est un sujet sensible.
examples.trans: It's a sensitive subject.

meanings.note: une voix sensuelle = a sensual voice

examples.text: Je cherche une voix sensuelle et végétale.
examples.trans: I am looking for a sensual and vegetal voice.

examples.text: Une danse sensuelle.
examples.trans: A sensual dance.

examples.text: Elle est tellement belle et sensuelle.
examples.trans: She is so beautiful and sensual.

meanings.note: Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum').

meanings.en: avoir des sentiments pour quelqu'un = to have feelings for someone
meanings.note: Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum').

examples.text: J'avais des sentiments pour toi.
examples.trans: I had feelings for you.

examples.text: C'est un sentiment bizarre.
examples.trans: It's a strange feeling.

examples.text: Je parle de sentiments! J'avais des sentiments pour toi.
examples.trans: I'm talking about feelings! I had feelings for you.

meanings.en: romantic, sentimental, related to love life
meanings.note: Vie sentimentale = love life. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'romantic'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Mélanger travail et vie sentimentale.
examples.trans: Mixing work and love life.

examples.text: Ce cadeau a une valeur sentimentale.
examples.trans: This gift has sentimental value.

examples.text: Le fil avait besoin d'être redressé, c'est tout. Rien de sentimental dans le bon entretien.
examples.trans: The wire needed straightening, that is all. Nothing sentimental about good maintenance.

meanings.note: Can describe perceiving a sensation or movement; se sentir describes how one feels.
Also used for smelling: ça sent bon, it smells good.

examples.text: J'ai senti un pied glisser.
examples.trans: I felt a foot slip.

examples.text: Ça sent bon ici.
examples.trans: It smells good in here.

examples.text: J'ai senti un pied glisser vers la tombe.
examples.trans: I felt one foot slip towards the grave.

meanings.note: the p is silent, the t is pronounced

examples.text: Voici votre clé, numéro quatre. Le petit-déjeuner est de sept heures trente à dix heures.
examples.trans: Here is your key, number four. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: Huit clients affamés descendent à sept heures et demie!
examples.trans: Eight hungry guests come down at half past seven!

examples.text: Donnez-moi un sac et de l'argent! L'épicerie du coin ouvre à sept heures.
examples.trans: Give me a bag and some cash! The corner grocery shop opens at seven.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'seventh'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'le septieme art: cinema'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: J'en suis à ma septième agonie!
examples.trans: I am on my seventh death scene!

examples.text: Au septième étage.
examples.trans: On the seventh floor.

examples.text: Oh non, j'en suis à ma septième agonie!
examples.trans: Oh no, I am already on my seventh death scene!

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Travailler sereinement.
examples.trans: To work peacefully.

examples.text: Envisager l'avenir sereinement.
examples.trans: To face the future serenely.

examples.text: Maintenant, je peux retourner tourner sereinement.
examples.trans: Now, I can return to filming peacefully.

meanings.note: Serrer sa ceinture.
serrer la main, serrer dans ses bras

examples.text: Serre un peu ta ceinture.
examples.trans: Tighten your belt a bit.

examples.text: Il me serre la main.
examples.trans: He shakes my hand.

meanings.note: changer les serrures = to change the locks

examples.text: La clé est dans la serrure.
examples.trans: The key is in the lock.

examples.text: Le vendeur est en train de l'ouvrir! Reste au téléphone une seconde.
examples.trans: The clerk is unlocking it right now! Stay on the phone one second.

examples.text: Il y a une petite serrure devant, et regardez collée en dessous: une vieille clé en laiton!
examples.trans: There is a tiny lock on the front, and look taped underneath: an old brass key!

meanings.note: From *serrer* ('to tighten'); *tenir bien serré* means 'to fit snugly / hold tight' (and *un café serré* is a short espresso!).

examples.text: La vis neuve tient bien serrée dans le bois sec.
examples.trans: The new screw holds nice and tight in the dry wood.

examples.text: Ne faites pas un nœud trop serré sur le tablier.
examples.trans: Don't tie too tight a knot on the apron.

meanings.note: masculine: un servant / un domestique

examples.text: Je joue une servante, comme toi.
examples.trans: I'm playing a servant, like you.

examples.text: La servante ouvre la porte.
examples.trans: The maidservant opens the door.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le serveur', plural 'les serveurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'waiter'.

examples.text: Je ne suis qu'un simple serveur.
examples.trans: I am only a simple waiter.

examples.text: Le serveur apporte les cafés.
examples.trans: The waiter brings the coffees.

meanings.note: In a company: le service juridique.
Rendre un service = to do a favour.

examples.text: Voici le service juridique.
examples.trans: This is the Legal Department.

examples.text: Tu me rends un service?
examples.trans: Can you do me a favour?

meanings.note: Means bath towel in a room and napkin at the table.

examples.text: Calmez-vous, Étienne. La chambre est propre et les serviettes sont fraîches.
examples.trans: Relax, Etienne. The room is clean and the towels are fresh.

examples.text: Où vont les petites cuillères et les serviettes?
examples.trans: Where do the small spoons and napkins go?

examples.text: Mets une serviette et une petite cuillère à côté de chaque tasse bleue.
examples.trans: Put one napkin and one teaspoon beside every blue cup.

meanings.note: à quoi ça sert? = what's the point?

meanings.en: servir à = to be useful for, to be the point of
meanings.note: à quoi ça sert? = what's the point?

examples.text: Ça ne sert à rien.
examples.trans: It's no use.

examples.text: Permettez-moi de servir le jus d'orange frais, madame!
examples.trans: Allow me to pour the fresh orange juice, madam!

meanings.note: Feminine: servante.

examples.text: Il est serviteur.
examples.trans: He is a servant.

examples.text: Un fidèle serviteur.
examples.trans: A loyal servant.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'session, round'.

examples.text: Deux sessions de laser game.
examples.trans: Two sessions of laser game.

examples.text: La session d'examen.
examples.trans: The exam session.

examples.text: On a réservé deux sessions de laser game.
examples.trans: We booked two laser game sessions.

meanings.note: Before a noun it can mean only; after a person it often means alone.

examples.text: Il est seul.
examples.trans: He is alone.

examples.text: C'est notre seul allié.
examples.trans: He is our only ally.

examples.text: J'ai seulement vingt ans.
examples.trans: I'm only twenty.

examples.text: Seulement un café.
examples.trans: Just a coffee.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le sexisme', plural 'les sexismes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sexism'.

examples.text: Le sexisme dans ce milieu est insupportable.
examples.trans: Sexism in this industry is unbearable.

examples.text: Il faut lutter contre tout sexisme.
examples.trans: We must fight against all sexism.

examples.text: Le sexisme dans ce milieu persiste.
examples.trans: Sexism in this industry persists.

meanings.note: Une ambiance sexy. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sexy'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une ambiance sexy avec des maillots de bain.
examples.trans: A sexy atmosphere with swimsuits.

examples.text: Elle est très sexy.
examples.trans: She is very sexy.

examples.text: Une ambiance sexy, des maillots de bain... La petite Mathurine est superbe!
examples.trans: A sexy atmosphere, swimsuits... Little Mathurine is gorgeous!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le shooting', plural 'les shootings') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'photo shoot'.

examples.text: On ne reporte jamais un tel shooting!
examples.trans: One never postpones such a shoot!

examples.text: Un shooting de mode.
examples.trans: A fashion shoot.

examples.text: D'accord, je vais assurer ce beau shooting.
examples.trans: All right, I will deliver on this fine shoot.

meanings.note: le monde du showbiz = the world of showbiz

examples.text: Dans le monde du showbiz.
examples.trans: In the world of showbiz.

examples.text: Les vedettes du showbiz.
examples.trans: The stars of showbiz.

examples.text: Dans ton merveilleux monde du showbiz!
examples.trans: In your wonderful world of showbiz!

meanings.en: second element of feng shui (Chinese spatial harmony)

examples.text: Ce bureau respecte le feng shui.
examples.trans: This office follows feng shui.

examples.text: Elle adore le feng shui.
examples.trans: She loves feng shui.

meanings.note: Si tu veux = if you want.
answering a negative question: Aucune nouvelle? - Si!

examples.text: Si tu veux, on peut en parler demain matin.
examples.trans: If you want, we can talk about it tomorrow morning.

examples.text: Dis-moi tout de suite si le rôle t'intéresse.
examples.trans: Tell me right away if the role interests you.

meanings.note: le sien, la sienne, les siens, les siennes

examples.text: Mon cœur ira rejoindre le sien.
examples.trans: My heart will go join his.

examples.text: Chacun le sien.
examples.trans: To each his own.

examples.text: Noémie a déjà rendu les siennes ce matin.
examples.trans: Noemie already gave back hers this morning.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la sieste', plural 'les siestes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nap'.

examples.text: Faire une sieste.
examples.trans: To take a nap.

examples.text: Une courte sieste.
examples.trans: A short nap.

examples.text: Je fais des siestes dans la journée.
examples.trans: I take naps during the day.

meanings.note: Agreed-upon sound, gesture, or light that gives notice to act.
Irregular plural in -aux: les signaux.

examples.text: Quelqu'un vient de sonner deux fois à la cloche en laiton: c'est le signal des deux frères!
examples.trans: Someone just rang the brass bell twice: that is the signal from the two brothers!

examples.text: Dès qu'Odette donne le signal, Antoine commence le premier accord.
examples.trans: As soon as Odette gives the signal, Antoine begins the first chord.

meanings.note: Signaler un objet perdu = to report a lost item.

examples.text: Je compose le numéro... Allô? Quelqu'un a signalé une valise bleue échangée?
examples.trans: I am dialling the number... Hello? Did anyone report a swapped blue suitcase?

examples.text: C'est facile à signaler ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to report, point out together.

examples.text: Plus de dix mille signatures en une nuit!
examples.trans: More than ten thousand signatures in one night!

examples.text: Il manque votre signature.
examples.trans: Your signature is missing.

meanings.note: C'est un signe = it's a sign. Masculine noun ('le signe', plural 'les signes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sign'.

examples.text: Un instant, Nadia vient de me faire signe depuis le café avec une idée!
examples.trans: One moment, Nadia just waved to me from the cafe with an idea!

examples.text: C'est un bon signe pour la semaine.
examples.trans: That's a good sign for the week.

meanings.note: a contract, a document; signer avec une agence = join an agency
rien n'est signé = nothing is signed

examples.text: Rien n'est signé.
examples.trans: Nothing is signed.

examples.text: Signez ici, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Sign here, please.

meanings.note: que signifie ce mot? = what does this word mean?

examples.text: NOW signifie maintenant.
examples.trans: NOW means right now.

examples.text: Cela ne signifie rien.
examples.trans: That means nothing.

examples.text: NOW signifie maintenant, c'est le présent immédiat!
examples.trans: NOW means right now, it is the immediate present!

meanings.note: Masculine noun (*le silence*, *trente ans de silence*), unlike most *-ence* nouns in French!

examples.text: On entend résonner chaque note dans le silence du matin.
examples.trans: You can hear every note ring out in the morning silence.

examples.text: Après une seconde de silence, toute la salle applaudit.
examples.trans: After a second of silence, the whole room applauds.

meanings.note: en mode silencieux = on silent mode

examples.text: Il était en mode silencieux.
examples.trans: It was on silent mode.

examples.text: La rue est silencieuse.
examples.trans: The street is quiet.

examples.text: Ça te fait une belle silhouette.
examples.trans: It gives you a lovely figure.

examples.text: On voit sa silhouette dans la nuit.
examples.trans: You can see her silhouette in the night.

examples.text: C'est simple.
examples.trans: It's simple.

examples.text: Une question simple.
examples.trans: A simple question.

meanings.note: Simply or just; here, without needing to do anything else.

examples.text: C'est simplement parfait.
examples.trans: It's simply perfect.

examples.text: Dis simplement oui.
examples.trans: Just say yes.

examples.text: Je vérifie simplement la sécurité. C'est mon métier.
examples.trans: I am simply checking security. That is my job.

examples.text: Je suis sincère.
examples.trans: I mean it / I'm sincere.

examples.text: Elle est toujours sincère.
examples.trans: She is always sincere.

meanings.note: Être sincèrement touché. Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Merci beaucoup, je suis sincèrement flattée.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, I am genuinely flattered.

examples.text: Je vous remercie sincèrement pour votre aide.
examples.trans: I thank you sincerely for your help.

examples.text: Votre visite matinale me touche sincèrement.
examples.trans: Your morning visit touches me sincerely.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la sincérité', plural 'les sincérités') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sincerity'.

examples.text: Ta grande sincérité est touchante.
examples.trans: Your great sincerity is moving.

examples.text: Ta grande sincérité est très touchante.
examples.trans: Your great sincerity is very moving.

examples.text: Absolument, la sincérité est essentielle.
examples.trans: Absolutely, sincerity is essential.

meanings.note: Compound of *si* + *non*; links a practical instruction to what happens if you forget (*fermez la porte, sinon l'air froid entre*).

examples.text: Gardez une part de tarte, sinon il n'en restera plus ce soir!
examples.trans: Save a slice of tart, or else there won't be any left tonight!

examples.text: Notez le nom sur le pot, sinon on va oublier ce qu'il contient.
examples.trans: Write the name on the jar, otherwise we'll forget what's inside.

meanings.note: A website in an online context.
A physical site or place in other contexts.

examples.text: Je suis sur le site.
examples.trans: I'm on the website.

examples.text: C'est un site de rencontre.
examples.trans: It's a dating site.

examples.text: J'ai passé la nuit sur le site de ma banque.
examples.trans: I spent the night on my bank's website.

meanings.note: La situation à l'agence.

examples.text: Où la situation est incertaine.
examples.trans: Where the situation is uncertain.

examples.text: Pour rester à ASK, où la situation est incertaine.
examples.trans: To stay at ASK, where the situation is uncertain.

meanings.note: pronounced si before a consonant: six jours = si ʒuʁ

examples.text: Six mois.
examples.trans: Six months.

examples.text: Non, Étienne, le couple du sud est arrivé dans la chambre six il y a une heure.
examples.trans: No, Etienne, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

related.word: pronounced si before a consonant: six jours

meanings.note: au dix-huitième siècle = in the 18th century

examples.text: Elle vit encore au dix-huitième siècle!
examples.trans: She's still living in the eighteenth century!

examples.text: C'est un château du dix-septième siècle.
examples.trans: It's a seventeenth-century chateau.

siège.gloss: seat (of a chair, car, or hall)

meanings.en: seat (part you sit on, or a chair/seat in general)
meanings.note: Refers specifically to the seat panel of a chair (soulever le siège) as well as formal seating or a company's head office.

examples.text: Soulevez légèrement le siège en bois pour replier la chaise.
examples.trans: Lift the wooden seat slightly to fold the chair up.

examples.text: Il reste deux sièges libres tout près du piano.
examples.trans: There are two seats free right near the piano.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le smoking', plural 'les smokings') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tuxedo'.

examples.text: Elle porte un smoking Armani.
examples.trans: She wears an Armani tuxedo.

examples.text: Je préfère porter le smoking Armani.
examples.trans: I prefer to wear the Armani tuxedo.

examples.text: Tu te sens mieux en smoking?
examples.trans: Do you feel better in a tuxedo?

meanings.note: written SMS in capitals; also called 'un texto'

examples.text: Tu m'as quitté avec un SMS!
examples.trans: You broke up with me by text!

examples.text: Envoie-moi un SMS.
examples.trans: Send me a text.

meanings.note: A snobbish person; also an adjective with the same singular spelling for either gender.

examples.text: Tu es tellement snob!
examples.trans: You're such a snob!

examples.text: Ce sont des snobs.
examples.trans: They're snobs.

examples.text: Tu peux être tellement snob, Andréa. C'est pitoyable!
examples.trans: You can be such a snob, Andréa. It's pathetic!

meanings.en: to snub, to look down upon
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to snub'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'snobé').

examples.text: Elle me séduit puis me snobe.
examples.trans: She charms me then snubs me.

examples.text: Ne me snobe pas.
examples.trans: Do not snub me.

examples.text: Elle me séduit, puis elle me snobe.
examples.trans: She charms me, then she snubs me.

examples.text: Les filles à Paris sont plus sobres.
examples.trans: Girls in Paris are more understated.

examples.text: Une robe très sobre.
examples.trans: A very simple dress.

examples.text: J'ai fait un an de socio, puis j'ai arrêté.
examples.trans: I did a year of sociology, then I stopped.

examples.text: Il étudie la socio.
examples.trans: He studies sociology.

meanings.note: argent de la société = company's money

examples.text: C'est l'argent de la société.
examples.trans: It's the company's money.

examples.text: Certains ont même acheté des chaussettes avec l'argent de la société!
examples.trans: Some people even bought socks with the company's money!

examples.text: De quelle société provient ce courrier?
examples.trans: Which company does this mail come from?

meanings.note: Un soda frais = a cold soda. Masculine noun ('le soda', plural 'les sodas') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'soda'.

examples.text: Un soda zéro sucre.
examples.trans: A zero-sugar soda.

examples.text: Boire un soda.
examples.trans: To drink a soda.

examples.text: Oui, un soda zéro sucre.
examples.trans: Yes, a zero-sugar soda.

soi.gloss: oneself ('chez soi' = home, one's own place)

meanings.en: oneself (*rentrer chez soi* = to go home / come home)
meanings.note: Indefinite stressed pronoun corresponding to *on* or infinitives without a specific subject (*rentrer chez soi*, 'to come home').

examples.text: Cette mélodie douce donne l'impression de rentrer chez soi.
examples.trans: This gentle melody feels like coming home.

examples.text: Il fait bon boire une tisane chaude chez soi quand il pleut.
examples.trans: It feels good to drink hot herbal tea at home when it rains.

related.gloss: to go home, to come back

meanings.note: Silk fabric or ribbon; 'papier de soie' = delicate tissue paper used to wrap fragile items.

examples.text: Les aquarelles sont protégées par des feuilles de papier de soie.
examples.trans: The watercolors are protected by sheets of tissue paper.

examples.text: Un ruban de soie verte entoure le petit carnet.
examples.trans: A green silk ribbon ties the small notebook.

meanings.note: Thirst; avoir soif, be thirsty.

examples.text: J'ai soif.
examples.trans: I'm thirsty.

examples.text: Tu as soif?
examples.trans: Are you thirsty?

examples.text: Rien, j'avais un peu soif.
examples.trans: Nothing, I was a bit thirsty.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to care for'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'soigné').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to take care of'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'soigné').

examples.text: Vous avez soigné un patient?
examples.trans: You cared for a patient?

examples.text: Vous avez soigné un vieux patient?
examples.trans: You cared for an elderly patient?

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Je le note soigneusement.
examples.trans: I note it down carefully.

examples.text: Très bien, je le note soigneusement.
examples.trans: Very good, I note it down carefully.

meanings.note: Describes neat handwriting, a tidy ledger page (*une page soignée*), or careful craftsmanship.

examples.text: Son écriture ronde et soignée reste très facile à lire.
examples.trans: Her round, neat handwriting is still very easy to read.

examples.text: Il fait toujours un travail propre et soigné à l'atelier.
examples.trans: He always does clean, careful work in the workshop.

meanings.note: Prendre soin de = to take care of.

meanings.en: prendre soin de = to take care of

examples.text: Prends soin de toi.
examples.trans: Take care of yourself.

examples.text: Prends soin de toi, Andréa.
examples.trans: Take care of yourself, Andréa.

examples.text: Avec beaucoup de soin.
examples.trans: With great care.

meanings.note: Ce soir = tonight.

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: I can't come tonight.

examples.text: À ce soir!
examples.trans: See you tonight!

meanings.note: Bonne soirée = have a nice evening.
Une soirée = an evening party.

examples.text: La soirée est finie.
examples.trans: The evening is over.

examples.text: Écoutez: même la sonnette de la chambre quatre est restée sage toute la soirée!
examples.trans: Listen: even room four's buzzer has behaved itself all evening!

meanings.note: Soit jeudi, soit vendredi.

examples.text: Soit jeudi, soit vendredi.
examples.trans: Either Thursday or Friday.

examples.text: Soit tu viens, soit tu restes.
examples.trans: Either you come or you stay.

meanings.note: the x is pronounced like s: swasɑ̃t

examples.text: La scène soixante est coupée.
examples.trans: Scene sixty is cut.

examples.text: Il a soixante ans.
examples.trans: He is sixty.

meanings.note: Invariable French cardinal numeral meaning 'seventy', used before plural nouns and in time/date expressions.

examples.text: C'est soixante-dix films.
examples.trans: That is seventy films.

examples.text: J'ai soixante-dix cafés à servir.
examples.trans: I have seventy coffees to serve.

examples.text: Non, en réalité, c'est soixante-dix films!
examples.trans: No, in reality, it is seventy films!

meanings.note: La séquence soixante-neuf. Spoken French num expression meaning 'sixty-nine', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: La séquence soixante-neuf.
examples.trans: Sequence sixty-nine.

examples.text: Il a soixante-neuf ans.
examples.trans: He is sixty-nine years old.

meanings.note: soixante-quinze ans = seventy-five years

examples.text: Un mètre soixante-quinze.
examples.trans: Five feet nine (1.75 meters).

examples.text: Page soixante-quinze.
examples.trans: Page seventy-five.

examples.text: Un mètre soixante-quinze, plutôt poilu, beau postérieur... C'est toi, Gabriel?
examples.trans: Five feet nine, quite hairy, nice rear... Is it you, Gabriel?

meanings.note: Walking surface indoors or outdoors.

examples.text: Et pas de miroir au mur, et le sol semble nu sans tapis.
examples.trans: And no mirror on the wall, and the floor feels bare without a rug.

examples.text: Bonsoir. Pardon pour l'eau sur votre sol propre.
examples.trans: Good evening. Sorry for the water on your clean floor.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le soldat', plural 'les soldats') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'soldier'.

examples.text: L'histoire d'un soldat.
examples.trans: The story of a soldier.

examples.text: Les soldats au front.
examples.trans: The soldiers at the front.

examples.text: C'est l'histoire d'un brave soldat blessé.
examples.trans: It is the story of a brave wounded soldier.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le soleil', plural 'les soleils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sun'.

examples.text: Asseyez-vous près de la fenêtre au soleil, madame! Rien ne presse là-haut!
examples.trans: Sit down near the sunny window, madam! Nothing is urgent upstairs!

examples.text: Je peux revoir l'étiquette en papier ici, en plein soleil?
examples.trans: May I look at the paper tag again here, in bright sunlight?

examples.text: Sous le soleil.
examples.trans: Under the sun.

meanings.note: être solidaire de = to stand in solidarity with

examples.text: Faut qu'on reste solidaires.
examples.trans: We have to stick together.

examples.text: Mais nous devons rester tous solidaires!
examples.trans: But we must all stick together!

meanings.note: Solidarité féminine. Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'solidarity, mutual support'.

examples.text: La solidarité féminine est importante.
examples.trans: Female solidarity is important.

examples.text: Faire preuve de solidarité.
examples.trans: To show solidarity.

examples.text: En tout cas, solidarité féminine!
examples.trans: In any case, female solidarity!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'solid'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Nous formons un couple solide.
examples.trans: We make a solid couple.

examples.text: Une maison solide.
examples.trans: A sturdy house.

examples.text: Bon endroit. Deux chaises solides, tournées vers les herbes du jardin et pas vers la fenêtre.
examples.trans: Good spot. Two solid chairs, facing the garden herbs and not the window.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'solitary'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Tu as joué en solitaire.
examples.trans: You played solo.

examples.text: Une promenade solitaire le soir.
examples.trans: A solitary walk in the evening.

examples.text: Tu as joué en solitaire et tu as perdu.
examples.trans: You played solo and you lost.

meanings.note: La solitude d'un enfant. Feminine noun ('la solitude', plural 'les solitudes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'loneliness'.

examples.text: Vous connaissez la solitude d'un enfant malade?
examples.trans: Do you know the loneliness of a sick child?

examples.text: Aimer la solitude.
examples.trans: To like solitude.

examples.text: Non, je connais la solitude d'un enfant qui s'ennuie.
examples.trans: No, I know the loneliness of a bored child.

meanings.en: to solicit, to ask for (roles or favors)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to ask for'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'sollicité').

examples.text: Je ne sollicite jamais les rôles.
examples.trans: I never solicit roles.

examples.text: Vraiment? Mais je ne sollicite jamais les rôles.
examples.trans: Really? But I never solicit roles.

meanings.note: An answer to a problem; feminine noun.

examples.text: On va trouver une solution.
examples.trans: We'll find a solution.

examples.text: Il y a une solution.
examples.trans: There's a solution.

examples.text: Une solution? Une grande actrice de quatre-vingts ans, libre dans trois semaines?
examples.trans: A solution? A great eighty-year-old actress, free in three weeks?

meanings.en: solvent, capable of meeting financial debts
meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: L'actrice affirme qu'elle n'est pas solvable.
examples.trans: The actress claims that she is not solvent.

examples.text: Cette entreprise est parfaitement solvable.
examples.trans: This company is perfectly solvent.

examples.text: Je n'ai rien, je ne suis pas solvable.
examples.trans: I have nothing, I am not solvent.

meanings.note: A room or colour can be dark.
A film or story can be gloomy or bleak.

examples.text: C'est un film très sombre.
examples.trans: It's a very dark film.

examples.text: La pièce est sombre.
examples.trans: The room is dark.

examples.text: Je vous en prie, madame. Lundi après-midi, l'entrée était sombre.
examples.trans: Go right ahead, madam. Monday afternoon, the lobby was dark.

meanings.note: Une grosse somme. Feminine noun ('la somme', plural 'les sommes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sum'.

examples.text: Je donne toute la somme à l'UNICEF.
examples.trans: I'm giving the whole sum to UNICEF.

examples.text: C'est une belle somme.
examples.trans: It's a tidy sum.

examples.text: J'ai le plaisir de donner toute la somme de monsieur Kadropov à l'UNICEF.
examples.trans: I have the pleasure of giving the whole sum from Mr Kadropov to UNICEF.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le sommeil', plural 'les sommeils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sleep'.

examples.text: J'ai tellement sommeil que je vais me coucher tôt.
examples.trans: I am so sleepy that I am going to bed early.

examples.text: Le manque de sommeil se voit sur son visage.
examples.trans: The lack of sleep shows on her face.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun owned (son sac, sa valise, ses clés); used before feminine vowel-initial nouns too.
Masculine noun: le son du piano.

examples.text: Ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: His twenty years of career.

examples.text: C'est son agent.
examples.trans: It's her agent.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le sondage', plural 'les sondages') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'survey'.

examples.text: Surtout pas de sondage!
examples.trans: Absolutely no testing!

examples.text: Non, surtout pas de sondage!
examples.trans: No, absolutely no testing!

meanings.note: Sonder les intentions de qqn. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to sound out'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'sondé').
Sonder les profondeurs. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to sound out'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'sondé').

examples.text: Juste pour le sonder un peu.
examples.trans: Just to sound him out a little.

examples.text: Je vais sonder le réalisateur.
examples.trans: I will sound out the director.

meanings.note: A telephone or bell rings.
For how something sounds to the ear, including an appealing name or idea.

examples.text: Ça sonne vraiment bien.
examples.trans: That sounds really good.

examples.text: Le téléphone sonne.
examples.trans: The phone is ringing.

examples.text: Madame Odette, tout va bien? Vous avez sonné!
examples.trans: Madam Odette, is everything alright? You rang the bell!

meanings.note: Sound of a bell or telephone.

examples.text: Ne lui donnez pas d'idées, Madame Odette! Je me suis presque attachée à ces deux sonneries.
examples.trans: Do not give it ideas, Madam Odette! I have grown almost fond of those two rings.

examples.text: Voici la sonnerie sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the ring, ringing tone on the table.

meanings.note: Diminutive built from sonner.

examples.text: Règle numéro un: buvez d'abord du thé chaud, puis répondez à la sonnette.
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then answer the bell.

examples.text: Il n'y a personne. C'est la sonnette de la chambre quatre.
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

examples.text: Écoutez: même la sonnette de la chambre quatre est restée sage toute la soirée!
examples.trans: Listen: even room four's buzzer has behaved itself all evening!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sophisticated'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est une robe très sophistiquée.
examples.trans: It is a very sophisticated dress.

examples.text: C'est beaucoup trop sophistiqué pour moi.
examples.trans: It is much too sophisticated for me.

meanings.note: Toutes sortes de = all kinds of.

meanings.en: faire en sorte que + subjunctive = to make sure that, to see to it that

examples.text: Tu peux faire en sorte qu'elle refuse.
examples.trans: You can make sure that she refuses.

examples.text: C'est une sorte de jeu.
examples.trans: It's a kind of game.

meanings.note: la sortie du film = the release of the film

examples.text: Une rupture pendant la sortie du film.
examples.trans: A breakup during the release of the film.

examples.text: Vers la sortie de secours.
examples.trans: Towards the emergency exit.

examples.text: Une rupture pendant la sortie du film, c'est mauvais pour nous.
examples.trans: A breakup during the film release is bad for us.

meanings.note: Sortir de introduces the place or event being left. With this meaning, compound past uses être.

examples.text: Elle sort du bureau.
examples.trans: She's leaving the office.

examples.text: Mes brioches à la cannelle sortent tout juste du four.
examples.trans: My cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le souci', plural 'les soucis') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'worry'.

examples.text: On a trop de soucis.
examples.trans: We have too many worries.

examples.text: Oh, je n'oserais jamais déranger un client avec nos soucis de propriétaire!
examples.trans: Oh, I would never dare bother a guest with our landlord troubles!

meanings.en: to care about, worry about, pay heed to (usually pronominal se soucier de)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to care about'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'soucié').

examples.text: Je me soucie de mes employés.
examples.trans: I care about my employees.

examples.text: Il ne se soucie de rien.
examples.trans: He does not care about anything.

examples.text: Je me soucie de la santé de mes employés.
examples.trans: I care about the health of my employees.

meanings.en: saucer (small plate under a teacup or coffee cup)
meanings.note: Built historically from sous ('under') + coupe ('cup'): the little dish that sits under the cup.

examples.text: Claire pose une petite cuillère sur chaque soucoupe blanche.
examples.trans: Claire sets a teaspoon on every white saucer.

examples.text: La tasse en grès ne glisse pas sur sa soucoupe.
examples.trans: The stoneware cup does not slip on its saucer.

meanings.note: Feminine: soudaine. Describes an event or feeling that happens unexpectedly.

examples.text: Une idée soudaine.
examples.trans: A sudden idea.

examples.text: C'était une envie soudaine.
examples.trans: It was a sudden urge.

examples.text: Il a soudainement fait froid.
examples.trans: It suddenly got cold.

examples.text: Le vent s'est levé soudainement.
examples.trans: The wind picked up suddenly.

examples.text: Il a soudainement fait froid. C'est l'enfer en scooter.
examples.trans: It suddenly got cold. It is hell on a scooter.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'united'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: On reste soudés.
examples.trans: We stick together.

examples.text: On reste toujours soudés, d'accord?
examples.trans: We always stick together, right?

examples.text: Nous formons une vraie équipe soudée maintenant.
examples.trans: We form a real tight team now.

meanings.note: Reprendre son souffle = to catch one's breath.

examples.text: Voici les deux valves en laiton, {M1}! Reprendre mon souffle? Jamais!
examples.trans: Here are both brass valves, {M1}! Catch my breath? Never!

examples.text: Voici le souffle sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the breath on the table.

souffler.gloss: to blow; to catch one's breath

meanings.en: to blow (air or wind); to take a breather
meanings.note: Transitive (*souffler l'air sec vers la fenêtre*) or intransitive (*le vent souffle*).

examples.text: Le petit ventilateur souffle de l'air tiède le long du couloir.
examples.trans: The small fan blows warm air down the hallway.

examples.text: Soufflez sur votre thé à la menthe avant de boire.
examples.trans: Blow on your mint tea before drinking.

meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire') meaning 'to suffer'; essential in everyday spoken and professional French.

examples.text: Vous semblez souffrir beaucoup.
examples.trans: You seem to be suffering a lot.

examples.text: Il souffre du dos depuis des jours.
examples.trans: He has been suffering from back pain for days.

examples.text: Asseyez-vous Mathias, vous semblez souffrir.
examples.trans: Sit down Mathias, you seem to be suffering.

meanings.en: to wish (souhaiter bonne chance à quelqu'un)
meanings.note: Intervocalic -h- is silent (/swɛte/). Used in warm wishes: souhaiter la bienvenue, souhaiter bonne chance, souhaiter bon courage.

examples.text: Toute l'équipe nous souhaite bonne chance pour l'ouverture.
examples.trans: The whole team wishes us good luck for the opening.

examples.text: Je vous souhaite une très belle soirée à l'hôtel.
examples.trans: I wish you a lovely evening at the hotel.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le soulagement', plural 'les soulagements') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'relief'.

examples.text: Quel soulagement d'en avoir fini!
examples.trans: What a relief to be done with it!

examples.text: Quel soulagement! Voici votre clé en argent, Monsieur Antoine.
examples.trans: What a relief! Here is your silver key, Mr Antoine.

examples.text: Quel soulagement!
examples.trans: What a relief!

meanings.note: Être soulagé = to be relieved.

examples.text: Vous pouvez être soulagés.
examples.trans: You can be relieved.

examples.text: Je suis très soulagé.
examples.trans: I am very relieved.

meanings.note: Stem alternates soulève / soulevons.

examples.text: Bonjour. Non, soulevez d'abord la poignée, puis poussez.
examples.trans: Good morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.

examples.text: C'est facile à soulever ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to lift, raise together.

meanings.en: soup, hot vegetable or meat broth
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la soupe', plural 'les soupes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'soup'.

examples.text: Voici une serviette sèche pour votre manteau et un bol de soupe chaude, monsieur.
examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat and a bowl of hot soup, sir.

examples.text: De la soupe chaude? Après cette marche froide sous la pluie, ça a l'air merveilleux.
examples.trans: Hot soup? After that cold walk in the rain, that sounds wonderful.

examples.text: Il a même fini toute sa soupe de légumes avant de monter.
examples.trans: He even finished all his vegetable soup before going up.

meanings.note: Une pâte souple = supple, elastic dough.

examples.text: Après dix minutes, la pâte à pain devient bien souple.
examples.trans: After ten minutes, the bread dough turns nice and supple.

examples.text: Ce cuir souple protège le carnet dans la poche.
examples.trans: This supple leather protects the notebook in the pocket.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to suspect'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'soupçonné').

examples.text: Je commence à soupçonner un piège derrière cette offre.
examples.trans: I am starting to suspect a trap behind this offer.

examples.text: Personne ne soupçonne la vérité au bureau.
examples.trans: Nobody suspects the truth at the office.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la source', plural 'les sources') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'source'.

examples.text: J'ai d'excellentes sources.
examples.trans: I have excellent sources.

examples.text: J'ai d'excellentes sources bien informées.
examples.trans: I have excellent, well-informed sources.

meanings.note: Final l is silent: /suʁsi/; froncer les sourcils = frown.

examples.text: Qu'est-ce qu'il dit? Pourquoi vous froncez les sourcils?
examples.trans: What is he saying? Why are you frowning?

examples.text: Voici le sourcil sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the eyebrow on the table.

meanings.note: Être sourd. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'deaf'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Parce qu'elle est sourde.
examples.trans: Because she is deaf.

examples.text: Il est sourd comme un pot.
examples.trans: He is deaf as a post.

examples.text: Mais Arlette n'est pas sourde du tout!
examples.trans: But Arlette is not deaf at all!

meanings.note: Wearing a warm, welcoming smile.

examples.text: Sur la photo, les trois amis apparaissent jeunes et souriants.
examples.trans: In the photo, the three friends look young and smiling.

examples.text: La boulangère accueille chaque client d'un air souriant.
examples.trans: The baker greets every customer with a cheerful smile.

meanings.note: also the infinitive verb 'to smile'

examples.text: J'aime le regard et le sourire.
examples.trans: I like the look and the smile.

examples.text: Elle a un beau sourire.
examples.trans: She has a lovely smile.

examples.text: Comment faisiez-vous pour lui redonner le sourire, Madame Odette?
examples.trans: How did you bring his smile back, Madam Odette?

meanings.note: Invariable plural: une souris, des souris.

examples.text: Discret comme une souris! Il s'asseyait sur la troisième marche pour écouter chaque note.
examples.trans: Quiet as a mouse! He sat on the third step to listen to every note.

examples.text: Voici la souris sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the mouse on the table.

meanings.note: Sous la pluie = in the rain. Core French preposition meaning 'under', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Le chat dort sous la table.
examples.trans: The cat sleeps under the table.

examples.text: J'avais les mains froides sous le choc!
examples.trans: My hands were cold from the shock!

examples.text: Une chambre sous les toits? Je peux la voir d'abord?
examples.trans: An attic room? May I see it first?

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to underestimate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'sous-estimé').

examples.text: Tu as sous-estimé tes collègues.
examples.trans: You underestimated your colleagues.

examples.text: Ne sous-estimez jamais vos adversaires.
examples.trans: Never underestimate your opponents.

examples.text: Tu as sous-estimé tes propres collègues, Mathias.
examples.trans: You underestimated your own colleagues, Mathias.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to sublet'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'sous-loué').

examples.text: L'agence a dû sous-louer cet étage entier.
examples.trans: The agency had to sublet this entire floor.

examples.text: Sous-louer son appartement pendant l'été.
examples.trans: To sublet one's apartment during the summer.

meanings.note: Usually plural sous-vêtements for underwear as a whole.

examples.text: Les sous-vêtements des stars.
examples.trans: The stars' underwear.

examples.text: J'achète des sous-vêtements.
examples.trans: I'm buying underwear.

meanings.note: Soutenir un projet. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to support, to back'.

examples.text: Tu ne la soutiens pas.
examples.trans: You do not support her.

examples.text: Soutenir ses enfants.
examples.trans: To support one's children.

examples.text: C'est dingue! Tu ne la soutiens pas.
examples.trans: This is crazy! You do not support her.

meanings.note: Apporter son soutien. Masculine noun ('le soutien', plural 'les soutiens') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'support'.

examples.text: Merci pour ton soutien.
examples.trans: Thank you for your support.

examples.text: Merci pour ton soutien, Gabriel.
examples.trans: Thank you for your support, Gabriel.

examples.text: Un soutien précieux.
examples.trans: Valuable support.

meanings.en: se souvenir de = to remember, to recall
meanings.note: Conjugated like venir. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to remember (se souvenir)'.

examples.text: Les maisons de famille et les vieux souvenirs, ces disputes-là font mal.
examples.trans: Family houses and old memories, arguments like those hurt deeply.

examples.text: Alors quelqu'un avec un souvenir de Grand-Père, c'était toi depuis le début, Antoine.
examples.trans: So someone with a keepsake from Grandfather was you from the start, Antoine.

examples.text: Je suis souvent seule.
examples.trans: I'm often alone.

examples.text: On se voit souvent.
examples.trans: We see each other often.

examples.text: C'est faux. Je suis souvent seule.
examples.trans: That's false. I'm often alone.

meanings.note: A play, a concert, a show on stage.

examples.text: Je joue dans un spectacle.
examples.trans: I'm in a show.

examples.text: Le spectacle est à huit heures.
examples.trans: The show is at eight.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'impressive'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une vue spectaculaire.
examples.trans: A spectacular view.

examples.text: La saucisse de Morteau est spectaculaire.
examples.trans: The Morteau sausage is spectacular.

examples.text: Cette scène intime doit rester très spectaculaire.
