examples.trans: This intimate scene must remain very spectacular.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le spectateur', plural 'les spectateurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'viewer'.

examples.text: Les spectateurs vont admirer ton grand courage.
examples.trans: The viewers will admire your great courage.

examples.text: La salle est pleine de spectateurs.
examples.trans: The hall is full of spectators.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'spectral'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Cette pâleur spectrale est saisissante.
examples.trans: This spectral pallor is striking.

examples.text: Une voix spectrale dans la nuit.
examples.trans: A ghostly voice in the night.

examples.text: Cette pâleur spectrale est vraiment magnifique.
examples.trans: This spectral pallor is really magnificent.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Ce sujet spirituel m'intéresse.
examples.trans: This spiritual subject interests me.

examples.text: Ce sujet spirituel m'intéresse beaucoup.
examples.trans: This spiritual subject interests me very much.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'splendid'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Tu étais splendide ce soir.
examples.trans: You were splendid tonight.

examples.text: Tu étais splendide sur le tapis.
examples.trans: You were splendid on the red carpet.

examples.text: Voici votre splendide suite au Crillon.
examples.trans: Here is your splendid suite at the Crillon.

meanings.note: Une salle de sport = a gym.

examples.text: Tu paies une salle de sport très chère.
examples.trans: You pay for a very expensive gym.

examples.text: Tu fais du sport?
examples.trans: Do you do any sport?

examples.text: Tu paies une salle de sport très chère, mais tu n'y vas jamais.
examples.trans: You pay for a very expensive gym, but you never go there.

meanings.note: quelque chose de spécial = something special

examples.text: Je sens quelque chose de spécial.
examples.trans: I feel something special.

examples.text: C'est une occasion spéciale.
examples.trans: It's a special occasion.

meanings.note: Spécialisé en = specialized in. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to specialize'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'spécialisé').

examples.text: Elle est spécialisée en propriété intellectuelle.
examples.trans: She is specialized in intellectual property.

examples.text: Se spécialiser dans le droit.
examples.trans: To specialize in law.

examples.text: Droit, spécialisée en propriété intellectuelle.
examples.trans: Law school, specialized in intellectual property.

examples.text: C'est la spécialité de la maison.
examples.trans: It's the house speciality.

examples.text: Quelle est votre spécialité?
examples.trans: What's your speciality?

meanings.note: Fenced neighborhood garden square with trees, benches, and gravel paths (pronounced /skwaʁ/).

examples.text: Nous traversons le square fleuri pour rejoindre la bibliothèque.
examples.trans: We cross the flower-filled park square to reach the library.

examples.text: À midi, les lecteurs s'installent sur les bancs du square.
examples.trans: At noon, readers settle onto the benches of the park square.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Et voilà la flamme bleue, bien stable, exactement comme il faut.
examples.trans: And there goes the blue flame, nice and steady, just as it should be.

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment stable.
examples.trans: This place is really steady, stable.

meanings.note: faire un stage = to do an internship

examples.text: Je peux vous offrir un stage.
examples.trans: I can offer you an internship.

examples.text: Elle fait un stage dans une agence.
examples.trans: She's doing an internship at an agency.

meanings.note: Un stagiaire chez ASK. Masculine noun ('le stagiaire', plural 'les stagiaires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'intern'.

examples.text: J'étais stagiaire et j'ai jeté ce scénario.
examples.trans: I was an intern and I threw away this script.

examples.text: Le stagiaire prépare le café.
examples.trans: The intern is making coffee.

meanings.note: Pronounced the French way with a nasal vowel and audible final -d (/stɑ̃d/): un stand de bricolage ('a hardware stall').

examples.text: Henri trouve toujours des vis en laiton au stand de bricolage.
examples.trans: Henri always finds brass screws at the hardware stall.

examples.text: Le stand de miel attire tout le quartier le samedi.
examples.trans: The honey stall draws the whole neighbourhood on Saturdays.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le stand-up', plural 'les stand-ups') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'stand-up comedy performance'.

examples.text: Elle rêve de faire du stand-up.
examples.trans: She dreams of doing stand-up comedy.

examples.text: Elle rêve maintenant de faire du stand-up.
examples.trans: She now dreams of doing stand-up comedy.

examples.text: Elle veut faire du stand-up maintenant!
examples.trans: She wants to do stand-up now!

meanings.note: Always feminine, even for a man.

examples.text: Des stars.
examples.trans: Stars.

examples.text: C'est une grande star.
examples.trans: He's a big star.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le statut', plural 'les statuts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'status'.

examples.text: Les statuts de l'entreprise doivent être signés demain.
examples.trans: The company bylaws must be signed tomorrow.

examples.text: Son nouveau statut d'associé lui donne plus de responsabilités.
examples.trans: His new partner status gives him more responsibilities.

meanings.note: steak tartare = seasoned raw beef dish

examples.text: Un steak tartare, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: A steak tartare, please.

examples.text: Un steak frites.
examples.trans: A steak and fries.

examples.text: J'ai besoin de manger un steak tartare.
examples.trans: I need to eat a steak tartare.

meanings.note: An order, borrowed from English.

examples.text: Stop! Arrête!
examples.trans: Stop! Stop it!

examples.text: Stop, c'est assez.
examples.trans: Stop, that's enough.

meanings.en: to stop, halt an action or process
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to stop'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'stoppé').

examples.text: Pour stopper un dossier important.
examples.trans: To stop an important file.

examples.text: Il faut stopper l'hémorragie.
examples.trans: We must stop the bleeding.

examples.text: Oui, pour stopper un dossier très important.
examples.trans: Yes, to stop a very important file.

meanings.note: Un grand stratège.

examples.text: C'est un stratège.
examples.trans: He's a strategist.

examples.text: Elle est une bonne stratège.
examples.trans: She's a good strategist.

examples.text: Peut-être pas généreux, mais c'est un stratège.
examples.trans: Maybe not generous, but he's a strategist.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le stress', plural 'les stress') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'physical or mental stress'.

examples.text: Il a beaucoup de stress au travail.
examples.trans: He has a lot of stress at work.

examples.text: Tes problèmes de stress ne s'arrangent pas.
examples.trans: Your stress problems are not getting better.

examples.text: Le bébé évacue tout son stress.
examples.trans: The baby releases all its stress.

meanings.en: to stress out, to feel anxious
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to stress out'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'stressé').

examples.text: Vous stressez un peu aujourd'hui?
examples.trans: Are you stressing out a bit today?

examples.text: Est-ce que vous stressez un peu aujourd'hui?
examples.trans: Are you stressing out a bit today?

examples.text: Là, je stresse beaucoup!
examples.trans: Now, I am stressing a lot!

meanings.note: From 'stresser'.

examples.text: Vous êtes stressée par l'audit?
examples.trans: Are you stressed about the audit?

examples.text: Il est très stressé aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: He's very stressed today.

meanings.note: Final *-ct* is pronounced `/kt/` in both masculine and feminine (*un ordre strict*, *une règle stricte*).

examples.text: La boulangère est très stricte sur la température du four.
examples.trans: The baker is very strict about the oven temperature.

examples.text: Repos complet ce soir: c'est un ordre strict!
examples.trans: Complete rest tonight: those are strict orders!

meanings.note: strictement professionnel = strictly professional

examples.text: C'était strictement professionnel.
examples.trans: It was strictly professional.

examples.text: C'est strictement interdit.
examples.trans: It is strictly forbidden.

examples.text: C'était strictement professionnel, tu le sais.
examples.trans: It was strictly professional, you know that.

meanings.note: Masculine: un strip-teaseur.

examples.text: C'est l'histoire d'une strip-teaseuse écolo.
examples.trans: It's the story of an ecologist stripper.

examples.text: Elle joue une strip-teaseuse.
examples.trans: She plays a stripper.

examples.text: C'est l'histoire d'une strip-teaseuse écolo. Très drôle, très moderne.
examples.trans: It's the story of an ecologist stripper. Very funny, very modern.

meanings.note: au studio radio = at the radio studio
Un petit studio à Paris. Masculine noun ('le studio', plural 'les studios') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'studio'.

examples.text: Des militants sont devant le studio.
examples.trans: Activists are in front of the studio.

examples.text: Elle travaille dans un studio de cinéma.
examples.trans: She works in a cinema studio.

examples.text: Voilà, c'est la pièce la plus importante du studio.
examples.trans: Here we are, this is the most important room in the studio.

examples.text: C'est tellement stupide!
examples.trans: It's so stupid!

examples.text: Une question stupide.
examples.trans: A silly question.

meanings.note: Feminine: stupéfaite (/stypefɛt/).

examples.text: Madame Odette, vous avez l'air stupéfaite! Vous connaissez le douze, rue des Tilleuls?
examples.trans: Madam Odette, you look amazed! Do you know number twelve, Rue des Tilleuls?

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment stupéfait.
examples.trans: This place is really astonished, stunned.

meanings.note: Artistic, architectural, or writing style.

examples.text: On reconnaît tout de suite le style élégant de son écriture.
examples.trans: You immediately recognize the elegant style of her handwriting.

examples.text: La maison mêle le style ancien et le confort d'aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: The house blends historic style with modern comfort.

examples.text: Mon stylo ne marche pas.
examples.trans: My pen isn't working.

examples.text: Prête-moi ton stylo, s'il te plaît.
examples.trans: Lend me your pen, please.

meanings.note: Refillable nibbed fountain pen.

examples.text: Elle écrit toutes ses lettres avec un vieux stylo-plume.
examples.trans: She writes all her letters with an old fountain pen.

examples.text: Le stylo-plume glisse sans effort sur le papier épais.
examples.trans: The fountain pen glides effortlessly across the thick paper.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le stéréotype', plural 'les stéréotypes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'stereotype'.

examples.text: C'est un stéréotype courant.
examples.trans: That is a common stereotype.

examples.text: C'est un beau stéréotype ridicule.
examples.trans: That is a nice ridiculous stereotype.

meanings.note: Une envie subite = a sudden urge.

examples.text: L'envie subite de prendre une chambre?
examples.trans: The sudden urge to get a room?

examples.text: Un départ subit.
examples.trans: A sudden departure.

examples.text: L'envie subite de s'embrasser et de prendre une chambre? Ça arrive.
examples.trans: The sudden urge to kiss and get a room? It happens.

examples.text: Elle est sublime!
examples.trans: She's sublime!

examples.text: Une robe sublime.
examples.trans: A gorgeous dress.

examples.text: Audrey Fleurot? Pourquoi pas? Elle est sublime!
examples.trans: Audrey Fleurot? Why not? She's sublime!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la substance', plural 'les substances') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'substance'.

examples.text: Cette scène est vide de substance.
examples.trans: This scene is empty of substance.

examples.text: Ce texte a une grande substance artistique.
examples.trans: This text has great artistic substance.

examples.text: Cette séquence est maintenant vide de substance.
examples.trans: This sequence is now empty of substance.

meanings.note: Un grand succès. Masculine noun ('le succès', plural 'les succès') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'success'.

examples.text: C'est le début d'un grand succès.
examples.trans: It is the beginning of a great success.

examples.text: Le film a eu un immense succès.
examples.trans: The film was a huge success.

examples.text: C'est un grand succès pour toi.
examples.trans: It is a great success for you.

examples.text: Des sucettes gratuites!
examples.trans: Free lollipops!

examples.text: Une sucette pour toi.
examples.trans: A lollipop for you.

meanings.note: Du sucre = some sugar.

examples.text: Sans sucre, merci.
examples.trans: No sugar, thanks.

examples.text: Volontiers! Avec du lait et un peu de sucre, s'il te plaît.
examples.trans: Gladly! With milk and a little sugar, please.

meanings.note: Built from sucre ('sugar').

examples.text: C'est du beurre demi-sel! Mes petits pains sucrés ont besoin de beurre doux!
examples.trans: That is salted butter! My sweet rolls need unsalted butter!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment sucré.
examples.trans: This place is really sweet, sugared.

meanings.note: Le sud = the south (of France).

examples.text: Non, Étienne, le couple du sud est arrivé dans la chambre six il y a une heure.
examples.trans: No, Etienne, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

examples.text: Voici le sud sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the south on the table.

meanings.note: Ça suffit = that's enough; un sourire suffit = a smile is enough (invariable past participle suffi).

examples.text: Un accueil simple et sincère suffit largement.
examples.trans: A simple, sincere welcome is more than enough.

examples.text: Deux cuillères de miel suffisent pour toute la théière.
examples.trans: Two spoons of honey are enough for the whole teapot.

examples.text: C'est largement suffisant.
examples.trans: That's more than enough.

examples.text: Trois jours, c'est suffisant.
examples.trans: Three days is enough.

examples.text: C'est largement suffisant. Fantastique!
examples.trans: That's more than enough. Fantastic!

meanings.note: Suggérer symboliquement.

examples.text: Ce serait plus fort de le suggérer.
examples.trans: It would be stronger to suggest it.

examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu suggères?
examples.trans: What do you suggest?

meanings.note: A set of connected rooms in a hotel.
Very common.
La suite de l'histoire.

examples.text: Une suite au Carlton.
examples.trans: A suite at the Carlton.

examples.text: Je réserve une suite.
examples.trans: I'm booking a suite.

meanings.note: Always follows its noun when pointing to the next item in a series: la page suivante, la carte suivante (whereas prochain often refers to upcoming calendar time from 'now': vendredi prochain).

examples.text: Tournez à la page suivante pour lire la fin de la lettre.
examples.trans: Turn to the next page to read the end of the letter.

examples.text: La carte postale suivante montre le salon en été.
examples.trans: The next postcard shows the lounge in summer.

meanings.note: For following a person or route.
Figuratively, for following and understanding what someone is saying.

examples.text: Tu me suis?
examples.trans: Do you follow me?

examples.text: Suivez-moi, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Follow me, please.

examples.text: Le vieux bureau clair sous les toits... suivez-moi, vite!
examples.trans: The old bright attic study... follow me, quickly!

examples.text: J'adore le sujet.
examples.trans: I love the subject.

examples.text: On change de sujet.
examples.trans: Let's change the subject.

meanings.note: Informal, does not change.

examples.text: Super. Dites-moi tout ce qu'il faut savoir.
examples.trans: Great. Tell me everything I need to know.

examples.text: La chambre est super calme.
examples.trans: The room is really quiet.

meanings.note: une femme superbe = a stunning woman

examples.text: La petite Mathurine est superbe!
examples.trans: Little Mathurine is gorgeous!

examples.text: C'est un spectacle superbe.
examples.trans: It's a superb show.

examples.text: Une ambiance sexy, des maillots de bain... La petite Mathurine est superbe!
examples.trans: A sexy atmosphere, swimsuits... Little Mathurine is gorgeous!

meanings.note: Je vous en supplie = I beg you.

examples.text: Solveig, je vous en supplie.
examples.trans: Solveig, I beg you.

examples.text: Elle le supplie de rester.
examples.trans: She begs him to stay.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'extra'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Les heures supplémentaires ne s'arrangent jamais.
examples.trans: Overtime hours never get any better.

examples.text: Nous avons commandé une part supplémentaire.
examples.trans: We ordered an extra portion.

examples.text: Oui, un jour de tournage supplémentaire!
examples.trans: Yes, an extra day of shooting!

supporter.gloss: to stand, to put up with; to support

meanings.en: to stand, to bear, to put up with
meanings.note: Je ne peux pas supporter ça.

examples.text: Je ne peux pas supporter ça.
examples.trans: I can't stand that.

examples.text: Elle ne supporte pas le froid.
examples.trans: She can't stand the cold.

meanings.en: to delete, to take down, to cancel

examples.text: Je le supprime?
examples.trans: Should I delete it?

examples.text: Il a supprimé le message.
examples.trans: He deleted the message.

meanings.note: Sur la table, sur la route.
Sur haut-parleur = on speaker.

examples.text: Le livre est sur la table.
examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: Tu es sur haut-parleur.
examples.trans: You're on speaker.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la surface', plural 'les surfaces') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'exterior'.

examples.text: Sous la surface.
examples.trans: Beneath the surface.

examples.text: Audiard veut ce qu'il y a sous la surface.
examples.trans: Audiard wants what lies beneath the surface.

examples.text: Un beau couple, c'est seulement la surface.
examples.trans: A beautiful couple is only the surface.

meanings.en: to overcome, to conquer, to surmount
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to overcome'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'surmonté').

examples.text: Surmonter une épreuve.
examples.trans: To overcome an ordeal.

examples.text: Surmonter ses peurs.
examples.trans: To overcome one's fears.

examples.text: Tu es courageux, tu vas surmonter cette épreuve.
examples.trans: You are brave, you will overcome this trial.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le surnom', plural 'les surnoms') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'moniker'.

examples.text: Un vieux surnom d'enfance.
examples.trans: An old childhood nickname.

examples.text: Non, c'est juste un vieux surnom.
examples.trans: No, it is just an old nickname.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'surprising'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un nom surprenant.
examples.trans: A surprising name.

examples.text: Une nouvelle surprenante.
examples.trans: Surprising news.

examples.text: C'est un nom assez surprenant pour un festival!
examples.trans: That is quite a surprising name for a festival!

meanings.en: to surprise, catch off guard, astonish
meanings.note: Irregular third-group French verb inherited from core Latin roots, used across registers for 'to surprise'.

examples.text: Il va nous surprendre.
examples.trans: He is going to surprise us.

examples.text: Moi, je pense qu'il va surprendre.
examples.trans: I think he will surprise everyone.

meanings.note: The feminine surprise ends in a pronounced z sound.

examples.text: Je suis surpris.
examples.trans: I'm surprised.

examples.text: Elle n'est pas surprise.
examples.trans: She isn't surprised.

meanings.note: faire la surprise à = to surprise someone

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
examples.trans: I wanted to surprise you.

examples.text: Quelle surprise!
examples.trans: What a surprise!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'surrealist'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Cette conversation devient complètement surréaliste!
examples.trans: This conversation is becoming completely surreal!

examples.text: Le décor du film a un côté très surréaliste.
examples.trans: The film set has a very surreal feel.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le sursaut', plural 'les sursauts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'start'.

examples.text: Le bébé se réveille en sursaut.
examples.trans: The baby wakes up with a start.

examples.text: Flora s'est réveillée en sursaut.
examples.trans: Flora woke up with a start.

examples.text: Surtout, ne dis rien!
examples.trans: Above all, don't say anything!

examples.text: J'aime surtout le cinéma.
examples.trans: I especially like cinema.

surveiller.gloss: to watch over, to look after

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to watch over'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'surveillé').

examples.text: Je vais surveiller les bureaux.
examples.trans: I will watch over the offices.

examples.text: Je surveille la météo, Nadia! Qui a posé cette grosse enveloppe près de la cloche?
examples.trans: I am checking the weather, Nadia! Who left this thick envelope near the bell?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la survie', plural 'les survies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'survival'.

examples.text: C'est notre chance de survie.
examples.trans: It is our chance of survival.

examples.text: C'est notre dernière chance de survie.
examples.trans: It is our last chance of survival.

meanings.note: Survivre à quelque chose; past participle survécu.

examples.text: Regarde, tu as survécu au coup de feu du matin et à l'appel mystère!
examples.trans: Look, you survived the morning rush and the mystery phone call!

examples.text: Cette maison a survécu à quatre-vingts hivers et à une vanne cassée hier matin.
examples.trans: This house survived eighty winters and one broken valve yesterday morning.

examples.text: Ma tasse a survécu, deux frères ont fait la paix et Claire a trouvé une nouvelle maison.
examples.trans: My teacup survived, two brothers made peace, and Claire found a new home.

suspendre.gloss: to suspend, put on hold, hang

meanings.note: Irregular third-group French verb inherited from core Latin roots, used across registers for 'to suspend'.

examples.text: {M1}, est-ce que tu accroches ces lanternes en papier pour midi?
examples.trans: {M1}, are you hanging those paper lanterns for noon?

examples.text: Le tournage du film est suspendu.
examples.trans: The filming of the movie is suspended.

examples.text: Ils suspendent les négociations.
examples.trans: They suspend negotiations.

meanings.note: En suspens = on hold, unresolved. Masculine noun ('le suspens', plural 'les suspens') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'suspense'.

examples.text: Des contrats en suspens.
examples.trans: Contracts on hold.

examples.text: Laisser l'affaire en suspens.
examples.trans: To leave the matter on hold.

examples.text: Monter des films est compliqué, et on a des contrats en suspens.
examples.trans: Setting up films is complicated, and we have contracts on hold.

meanings.note: Map symbol, carved emblem, or meaningful token.

examples.text: Chaque symbole de la légende correspond à un monument.
examples.trans: Every symbol in the map key corresponds to a landmark.

examples.text: Le vieux tilleul est devenu le symbole de l'hôtel.
examples.trans: The old linden tree has become the symbol of the hotel.

examples.text: Le suggérer symboliquement.
examples.trans: To suggest it symbolically.

examples.text: C'est très important symboliquement.
examples.trans: It is very important symbolically.

meanings.note: Short for sympathique; informal.

examples.text: C'est sympa ici.
examples.trans: It's nice here.

examples.text: Parce que le bon café et le pain chaud rendent les gens sympas!
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Des amis très sympathiques.
examples.trans: Very nice friends.

examples.text: Un accueil fort sympathique.
examples.trans: A very friendly welcome.

examples.text: Oui, avec quelques amis très sympathiques.
examples.trans: Yes, with a few very nice friends.

meanings.note: une séance de travail = a work session

examples.text: La séance a été difficile.
examples.trans: The session was difficult.

examples.text: Une séance de cinéma.
examples.trans: A film screening.

examples.text: La séance a été très difficile?
examples.trans: Was the session very difficult?

meanings.note: Accent switches *é -> è* before silent endings in the present (*la peinture sèche*), while the future keeps *é* (*elle séchera*).

examples.text: Avec l'air chaud qui circule, la peinture va sécher avant ce soir.
examples.trans: With warm air circulating, the paint will dry before tonight.

examples.text: Laissez sécher les pinceaux propres sur un torchon.
examples.trans: Let the clean paintbrushes dry on a kitchen towel.

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'stability, emotional security'.

examples.text: Ce travail est ma sécurité.
examples.trans: This job is my security.

examples.text: Je vérifie simplement la sécurité. C'est mon métier.
examples.trans: I am simply checking security. That is my job.

examples.text: Tu es un monstre de séduction.
examples.trans: You're a monster of seduction.

examples.text: Une opération de séduction.
examples.trans: A charm offensive.

examples.text: Pour moi, c'est une question de séduction.
examples.trans: For me, it is a matter of seduction.

meanings.en: to charm, to win over, to seduce

examples.text: Tu es très douée pour séduire les gens.
examples.trans: You're very good at charming people.

examples.text: Ce rôle la séduit.
examples.trans: This part appeals to her.

examples.text: Elle croise son patron et décide de le séduire.
examples.trans: She runs into her boss and decides to seduce him.

meanings.note: Bon séjour! = Enjoy your stay!

examples.text: Vous me sauvez tout mon séjour, tous les deux.
examples.trans: You two are saving my whole stay.

examples.text: Voici le séjour sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the stay, visit on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'selection'.

examples.text: La sélection officielle.
examples.trans: The official selection.

examples.text: Une belle sélection.
examples.trans: A fine selection.

examples.text: C'est la sélection pour les premiers films?
examples.trans: Is that the selection for first films?

meanings.note: From se séparer. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'separation'.

examples.text: La séparation ou l'humanité?
examples.trans: The separation or the humanity?

examples.text: Une séparation difficile.
examples.trans: A difficult separation.

meanings.note: se séparer = to break up, to split up

examples.text: Des acteurs qui se séparent.
examples.trans: Actors who are splitting up.

examples.text: Il sépare les deux enfants.
examples.trans: He separates the two children.

examples.text: Des acteurs qui se séparent, c'est un désastre. Le film va faire un bide.
examples.trans: Actors splitting up is a disaster. The movie is going to flop.

meanings.en: sequence, scene (in a script or film)
meanings.note: Tourner une séquence. Feminine noun ('la séquence', plural 'les séquences') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sequence'.

examples.text: Voyons voir, quelle séquence?
examples.trans: Let us see, which sequence?

examples.text: C'est la séquence finale.
examples.trans: It is the final sequence.

examples.text: La séquence soixante-neuf.
examples.trans: Sequence sixty-nine.

meanings.note: une série policière = a detective series

examples.text: Il joue dans une série policière.
examples.trans: He acts in a detective series.

examples.text: J'adore cette série.
examples.trans: I love this series.

examples.text: Entrez. Il a été choisi pour une série policière.
examples.trans: Come in. He has been chosen for a detective series.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Parlons sérieusement de ce projet.
examples.trans: Let's speak seriously about this project.

examples.text: Sérieusement Hicham, tout avance très bien.
examples.trans: Seriously Hicham, everything is progressing very well.

examples.text: Je dois vous parler très sérieusement.
examples.trans: I must talk to you very seriously.

meanings.note: Je suis sérieuse = I mean it.

examples.text: Je suis sérieuse.
examples.trans: I'm serious. (a woman speaking)

examples.text: C'est sérieux?
examples.trans: Is it serious?

meanings.note: Bien sûr = of course.

examples.text: Tu es sûr?
examples.trans: Are you sure?

examples.text: Bien sûr!
examples.trans: Of course!

meanings.note: mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Ils ont sûrement tout.
examples.trans: They surely have everything.

examples.text: Il va sûrement venir.
examples.trans: He will surely come.

examples.text: Son propriétaire va sûrement le chercher bientôt.
examples.trans: Its owner will surely look for it soon.

meanings.en: sister-buddy, sibling pal (playful blend of sœur + pote)

examples.text: Tu es ma sœpote!
examples.trans: You are my sister-buddy!

examples.text: Ma sœpote habite à Paris.
examples.trans: My sister-buddy lives in Paris.

examples.text: Tu es ma sœpote et je suis ton frote!
examples.trans: You are my sister-buddy and I am your brother-buddy!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la sœur', plural 'les sœurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sister'.

examples.text: Je suis chez ma sœur.
examples.trans: I am at my sister's place.

examples.text: Je suis chez ma sœur, c'est l'horreur!
examples.trans: I am at my sister's, it is horrible!

examples.text: Ma sœur est complètement bouleversée.
examples.trans: My sister is completely overwhelmed.

meanings.note: A piece of furniture.
In à table, it is a call to come and eat, not a name for the meal itself.

examples.text: À table!
examples.trans: Dinner's ready!

examples.text: Nous avons déjeuné à cette table.
examples.trans: We had lunch at this table.

examples.text: Il y a deux mois, lui et moi avons déjeuné à cette table.
examples.trans: Two months ago, he and I had lunch at this table.

meanings.note: A table or chart, including a spreadsheet when Excel is specified.
A painting, a different sense of the same word.
A board used for displaying or writing on.

examples.text: Un tableau Excel.
examples.trans: A spreadsheet.

examples.text: Un beau tableau.
examples.trans: A beautiful painting.

examples.text: Henri, regardez le tableau des clés derrière nous: un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept, huit!
examples.trans: Henri, look at the key board behind us: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight!

meanings.en: tablet computer; small shelf; bar of chocolate
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la tablette', plural 'les tablettes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tablet computer'.

examples.text: Je l'ai sur ma tablette.
examples.trans: I have it on my tablet.

examples.text: Une tablette tactile.
examples.trans: A touchscreen tablet.

examples.text: Je vous avais dit que cette tablette est un piège.
examples.trans: I told you that tablet is a trap.

meanings.note: Mettre / enlever son tablier = put on / take off one's apron.

examples.text: Les boulangers enlèvent leurs tabliers blancs à six heures.
examples.trans: The bakers take off their white aprons at six o'clock.

examples.text: Elle noue son tablier avant de fouetter les œufs.
examples.trans: She ties her apron before whisking the eggs.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'forbidden'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ce sujet est complètement tabou entre nous.
examples.trans: This subject is completely taboo between us.

examples.text: Je suis archi-flatté, mais c'est tabou.
examples.trans: I am extremely flattered, but it is taboo.

meanings.note: Final *-t* is silent (`/tabuʁɛ/`); covers kitchen step stools, bar stools, and piano stools.

examples.text: Tenez bien le petit tabouret en bois avant de monter dessus.
examples.trans: Hold the little wooden stool steady before stepping onto it.

examples.text: Il s'assied sur un tabouret bas pour réparer la serrure.
examples.trans: He sits on a low stool to repair the lock.

related.gloss: rung (of a stool or ladder); bar

meanings.note: Classic French minimal pair: *une tache* (no circumflex) = a stain or spot; *une tâche* (with circumflex *â*) = a task or job!

examples.text: De l'eau tiède enlève tout de suite une tache de peinture à l'eau.
examples.trans: Warm water immediately removes a smudge of water-based paint.

examples.text: Il porte un tablier pour éviter les taches sur sa chemise.
examples.trans: He wears an apron to avoid stains on his shirt.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la taille', plural 'les tailles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'size'.
Feminine noun ('la taille', plural 'les tailles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'height'.
Feminine noun ('la taille', plural 'les tailles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'waist'.

examples.text: Quelle est votre taille de pantalon?
examples.trans: What is your trouser size?

examples.text: Une personne de grande taille.
examples.trans: A tall person.

examples.text: J'ai utilisé la dernière cet hiver. Seule la vieille quincaillerie après le pont vend cette taille.
examples.trans: I used the last one this winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge sells this size.

taire.gloss: to keep quiet, silence; se taire = to remain silent

meanings.note: Irregular third-group French verb inherited from core Latin roots, used across registers for 'to keep quiet'.

examples.text: Je ne peux pas me taire.
examples.trans: I cannot stay silent.

examples.text: Tais-toi, ne parle pas ici!
examples.trans: Be quiet, do not speak here!

meanings.note: Avoir du talent = to be talented.

examples.text: Elle a du talent.
examples.trans: She's talented.

examples.text: Quel talent!
examples.trans: What talent!

examples.text: Il est jeune, mais très talentueux.
examples.trans: He's young, but very talented.

examples.text: Une actrice talentueuse.
examples.trans: A talented actress.

examples.text: Il est jeune, mais très talentueux. Comme Xavier Dolan.
examples.trans: He's young, but very talented. Like Xavier Dolan.

meanings.en: heel (foot, sock, or shoe); end crust of bread
meanings.note: Also used affectionately in French bakeries for the crusty end piece of a baguette (*le talon du pain*)!

examples.text: Glissez un oreiller souple sous votre talon pour reposer la cheville.
examples.trans: Slip a soft pillow under your heel to rest your ankle.

examples.text: Ses talons résonnent doucement sur les pierres de la cour.
examples.trans: Her heels click softly on the courtyard stones.

related.gloss: foot; leg (of a table or chair)

meanings.note: Official postmark or agency stamp.

examples.text: Le facteur vient de me faire signer un recommandé. Il y a un tampon rouge d'agence immobilière.
examples.trans: The postman just had me sign for registered mail. There is a red property-agency stamp.

examples.text: Voici le tampon sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the ink stamp, rubber stamp on the table.

meanings.note: faire du tango = to dance the tango

examples.text: Vous faites du tango.
examples.trans: You dance the tango.

examples.text: J'adore le tango.
examples.trans: I love the tango.

examples.text: Pour la danse à la barre, je sais que vous faites du tango.
examples.trans: For the pole dancing, I know that you do the tango.

meanings.note: tant de + noun (no article): tant de tragédie

meanings.en: tant mieux = so much the better

examples.text: Sans tant de tragédie.
examples.trans: Without so much tragedy.

examples.text: Il a tant de travail.
examples.trans: He has so much work.

meanings.note: Standard word for 'aunt' (informal family nickname: tata or tatie).

examples.text: La tante d'Étienne jouait merveilleusement bien du piano.
examples.trans: Étienne's aunt used to play the piano wonderfully.

examples.text: Ma tante a écrit toutes ses recettes à l'encre bleue.
examples.trans: My aunt wrote all her recipes in blue ink.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'flashy'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Elle déteste les bijoux trop tape-à-l'œil.
examples.trans: She hates overly flashy jewellery.

examples.text: Ce costume brillant est un peu tape-à-l'œil pour la scène.
examples.trans: This shiny costume is a bit gaudy for the scene.

taper.gloss: to clap (taper dans les mains), tap, knock; to type

meanings.en: to clap (taper dans les mains), tap, knock; to type
meanings.note: Taper dans les mains is a classic acoustics test—and everyday French for clapping hands.

examples.text: Antoine tape une fois dans ses mains pour écouter l'écho.
examples.trans: Antoine claps his hands once to listen for an echo.

examples.text: Quelqu'un tape doucement au carreau de la cuisine.
examples.trans: Someone taps gently on the kitchen windowpane.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le tapis', plural 'les tapis') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'carpet'.

examples.text: Elle marche sur le tapis rouge.
examples.trans: She walks on the red carpet.

examples.text: C'est fait! Et le tapis bleu va juste à côté du lit.
examples.trans: Done! And the blue rug fits right beside the bed.

examples.text: Et pas de miroir au mur, et le sol semble nu sans tapis.
examples.trans: And no mirror on the wall, and the floor feels bare without a rug.

meanings.note: To pat or tap gently and repeatedly with the fingers or hand.
Diminutive/frequentative of taper ('to tap, strike').

examples.text: Pas étonnant qu'il ait tapoté la poche de son manteau: il a apporté une carte de toast pour nous!
examples.trans: No wonder he patted his coat pocket: he brought a toast card for us!

examples.text: Elle tapote doucement le coussin du banc près du piano.
examples.trans: She gently pats the bench cushion beside the piano.

meanings.note: For a late time or doing something late.

meanings.en: à plus tard = see you later
meanings.note: With plus, later; à plus tard is the farewell see you later.

examples.text: Il est tard.
examples.trans: It's late.

examples.text: Je rentre tard.
examples.trans: I'm getting home late.

examples.text: Trop tard! Il a dit merci et il a raccroché!
examples.trans: Too late! He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.en: to delay, take long, tarry (ne pas tarder = be soon, arrive shortly)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to delay'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'tardé').

examples.text: Il ne va pas tarder.
examples.trans: He will not be long.

examples.text: Le SAMU ne va pas tarder.
examples.trans: The ambulance will not be long.

meanings.note: une répétition tardive = a late rehearsal

examples.text: Une heure tardive.
examples.trans: A late hour.

examples.text: Des regrets tardifs.
examples.trans: Belated regrets.

examples.text: Et les répétitions tardives à deux heures?
examples.trans: And the late rehearsals until two in the morning?

meanings.note: Négocier des tarifs.

examples.text: On était là pour négocier des tarifs.
examples.trans: We were there to negotiate rates.

examples.text: Quel est le tarif?
examples.trans: What is the rate?

examples.text: Non, mais on était là pour nos acteurs, pour négocier des tarifs.
examples.trans: No, but we were there for our actors, to negotiate rates.

meanings.note: often used with steak: steak tartare

examples.text: J'ai besoin d'un steak tartare.
examples.trans: I need a steak tartare.

examples.text: Un tartare de saumon.
examples.trans: A salmon tartare.

examples.text: J'ai besoin de manger un steak tartare.
examples.trans: I need to eat a steak tartare.

meanings.note: Named with au/à la/aux before the filling: une tarte au citron ('a lemon tart'), une tarte aux pommes ('an apple tart').

examples.text: Nadia sort deux belles tartes au citron du four.
examples.trans: Nadia takes two lovely lemon tarts out of the oven.

examples.text: Une part de tarte tiède accompagne parfaitement le thé.
examples.trans: A slice of warm tart goes perfectly with tea.

tartine.gloss: buttered slice of bread with spread, open-faced toast

meanings.en: slice of bread spread with butter, jam, or honey
meanings.note: A classic French breakfast staple: une tartine de beurre et de confiture, often dipped in coffee or hot chocolate.

examples.text: Thibault mange sa tartine de confiture en lisant le plan.
examples.trans: Thibault eats his slice of bread and jam while reading the plan.

examples.text: Je prépare des tartines beurrées avec le pain frais du matin.
examples.trans: I am making buttered bread slices with the morning's fresh bread.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le tas', plural 'les tas') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pile'.

examples.text: Un tas de pierres.
examples.trans: A heap of stones.

examples.text: Un tas de viande.
examples.trans: A slab of meat.

examples.text: Je refuse d'être un tas de viande!
examples.trans: I refuse to be a slab of meat!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la tasse', plural 'les tasses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'drinking cup'.

examples.text: Prends une tasse de café.
examples.trans: Take a cup of coffee.

examples.text: Voici une nappe blanche propre et deux tasses bleues.
examples.trans: Here is a clean white tablecloth and two blue cups.

examples.text: Vous deux?! Laissez vos tasses, entrez tout de suite!
examples.trans: Both of you?! Leave your cups, come inside right away!

meanings.note: Animal that lives underground.
Informal.

examples.text: Il y a une taupe à l'agence.
examples.trans: There's a mole at the agency.

examples.text: La taupe vit sous la terre.
examples.trans: The mole lives underground.

examples.text: Une nouvelle taxe sur les acteurs français.
examples.trans: A new tax on French actors.

examples.text: Les taxes sont élevées.
examples.trans: The taxes are high.

examples.text: Laquelle? On pourrait dire qu'il y a une nouvelle taxe sur les acteurs français?
examples.trans: Which one? Could we say there's a new tax on French actors?

meanings.en: to bum, borrow something without paying
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to bum'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'taxé').

examples.text: J'ai taxé une clope au guichet.
examples.trans: I bummed a smoke at the ticket counter.

examples.text: Il taxe toujours des cigarettes.
examples.trans: He always bums cigarettes.

examples.text: J'ai taxé une clope pour déstresser.
examples.trans: I bummed a smoke to de-stress.

meanings.note: prendre un taxi / monter dans le taxi

examples.text: Voilà un taxi devant le portail à l'instant.
examples.trans: Here comes a taxi in front of the gate right now.

examples.text: Un taxi vient de s'arrêter juste devant la grille en fer!
examples.trans: A taxi just stopped right outside the iron gate!

examples.text: Ne prends pas ce taxi!
examples.trans: Don't take that taxi!

meanings.en: cheers!, here's to you! (toast when clinking glasses)
meanings.note: Often doubled: tchin-tchin.

examples.text: Tchin, frote!
examples.trans: Cheers, brother-buddy!

examples.text: Tchin-tchin à votre santé!
examples.trans: Cheers to your health!

meanings.note: casual object pronoun, before the verb

examples.text: Volontiers! Avec du lait et un peu de sucre, s'il te plaît.
examples.trans: Gladly! With milk and a little sugar, please.

examples.text: Laisse-moi bien te regarder, Antoine! Tu es devenu plus grand que le piano!
examples.trans: Let me look at you properly, Antoine! You grew taller than the piano!

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: De telles douleurs physiques.
examples.trans: Such physical pains.

examples.text: Tu as souvent de telles douleurs?
examples.trans: Do you often have such pains?

examples.text: Ne dis pas de telles bêtises.
examples.trans: Do not say such silly things.

meanings.note: c'est tellement stupide = it's so stupid

examples.text: C'est tellement stupide!
examples.trans: It's so stupid!

examples.text: Je l'aime tellement.
examples.trans: I love her so much.

meanings.note: Not permanent. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'temporary'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un arrangement temporaire.
examples.trans: A temporary arrangement.

examples.text: Un travail temporaire.
examples.trans: A temporary job.

examples.text: Un arrangement temporaire, juste une façade.
examples.trans: A temporary arrangement, just a facade.

meanings.note: Une capsule temporelle = a time capsule.

examples.text: Cette petite boîte en fer est une vraie capsule temporelle.
examples.trans: This small tin box is a real time capsule.

examples.text: Trente ans séparent ces deux repères temporels.
examples.trans: Thirty years separate those two points in time.

meanings.note: Tout le temps = all the time.
Quel temps fait-il?.

examples.text: Tout le temps.
examples.trans: All the time.

examples.text: Je n'ai pas le temps.
examples.trans: I don't have time.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le tempérament', plural 'les tempéraments') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'temperament'.

examples.text: Chacun son tempérament.
examples.trans: To each their own temperament.

examples.text: Un tempérament d'artiste.
examples.trans: An artistic temperament.

examples.text: On a chacun notre tempérament, c'est humain.
examples.trans: We each have our temperament, it is human.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la température', plural 'les températures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'temperature'.

examples.text: De l'eau à température ambiante.
examples.trans: Room-temperature water.

examples.text: Je voudrais de l'eau à température ambiante.
examples.trans: I would like room-temperature water.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la tempête', plural 'les tempêtes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'storm'.

examples.text: Une grosse tempête bloque tous les bateaux au port.
examples.trans: A big storm is keeping all the boats in port.

examples.text: Calme-toi, ce n'est qu'une tempête dans un verre d'eau.
examples.trans: Calm down, it is just a tempest in a teacup.

meanings.note: To hold out one's hand or an object ('tendre la main'); to stretch a cloth or string taut.

examples.text: Elle lui tend la boussole avec un grand sourire.
examples.trans: She holds the compass out to him with a big smile.

examples.text: Tendez l'oreille: on entend la cloche de midi!
examples.trans: Listen closely: you can hear the noon bell!

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Il l'embrasse tendrement.
examples.trans: He kisses her tenderly.

examples.text: Embrasse-moi tendrement dans ce taxi.
examples.trans: Kiss me tenderly in this taxi.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la tendresse', plural 'les tendresses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tenderness'.

examples.text: Elle parle avec tendresse.
examples.trans: She speaks with tenderness.

examples.text: Souviens-toi du passé avec tendresse.
examples.trans: Remember the past with tenderness.

examples.text: Merci pour ta tendresse et ton écoute.
examples.trans: Thank you for your tenderness and listening.

meanings.note: Une corde tendue. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'tense'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Une corde tendue. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'tense'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est très tendu.
examples.trans: It is very tense.

examples.text: Une situation tendue.
examples.trans: A tense situation.

examples.text: La comédie n'est pas forcément drôle. C'est très tendu.
examples.trans: Comedy is not necessarily funny. It is very tense.

meanings.note: Imperative: tiens! / tenez!.
Imperative: tiens! / tenez!.

examples.text: Tenez, les voilà.
examples.trans: Here, there they are.

examples.text: Il tient un livre.
examples.trans: He's holding a book.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'nervous strain, emotional tension'.

examples.text: La tension monte vite.
examples.trans: Tension rises quickly.

examples.text: Alors après cinq mois, la tension a explosé.
examples.trans: So after five months, the tension exploded.

examples.text: Laisse-moi éliminer toute cette tension.
examples.trans: Let me eliminate all this tension.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'tempting'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est très tentant.
examples.trans: It is very tempting.

examples.text: C'est une opportunité très tentante.
examples.trans: It is a very tempting opportunity.

meanings.note: To attempt something challenging ('tenter de + infinitive'); to tempt with a treat.

examples.text: Tentons de résoudre la première énigme avant le déjeuner.
examples.trans: Let's try to solve the first riddle before lunch.

examples.text: Laissez-vous tenter par une part de tarte tiède!
examples.trans: Let yourself be tempted by a slice of warm tart!

meanings.note: tenue de sport = sports kit; tenue de soirée = evening wear

examples.text: Je n'ai pas eu le temps d'acheter une tenue.
examples.trans: I didn't have time to buy an outfit.

examples.text: C'est une jolie tenue.
examples.trans: That's a nice outfit.

examples.text: On ne peut pas avoir deux femmes dans la même tenue en même temps.
examples.trans: We cannot have two women in the same outfit at the same time.

related.gloss: sports kit; tenue de soirée = evening wear

meanings.note: Enfin terminé(e)! = Finally finished!

examples.text: Odette a enfin terminé la valse commencée il y a trente ans.
examples.trans: Odette has finally finished the waltz started thirty years ago.

examples.text: Nous terminons le service du soir vers neuf heures.
examples.trans: We finish evening service around nine o'clock.

meanings.en: ground, plot, field (tâter le terrain = sound out the situation)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le terrain', plural 'les terrains') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ground'.

examples.text: Tâter le terrain.
examples.trans: Testing the waters.

examples.text: Il faut d'abord tâter le terrain.
examples.trans: We must test the waters first.

meanings.note: At a café, the outdoor seating area; en terrasse locates someone at those tables.

examples.text: Un café en terrasse?
examples.trans: A coffee on the terrace?

examples.text: La terrasse est pleine.
examples.trans: The terrace is full.

examples.text: Tu viens prendre un café en terrasse?
examples.trans: Will you come for a coffee on the terrace?

meanings.en: ground, floor (*par terre* = on the floor / ground); soil
meanings.note: *Poser le pied par terre* ('to put one's foot down on the floor') is the everyday idiom for touching the ground indoors or outdoors.

examples.text: Ne posez rien par terre dans le couloir pendant qu'on peint.
examples.trans: Don't put anything on the floor in the hallway while we paint.

examples.text: La terre des pots de fleurs est encore fraîche ce matin.
examples.trans: The soil in the flowerpots is still cool and moist this morning.

meanings.note: same form in masculine and feminine

examples.text: C'est une nouvelle terrible.
examples.trans: It's terrible news.

examples.text: Il va écrire un avis terrible d'une étoile!
examples.trans: He is going to write a terrible one-star review!

meanings.note: Very much or terribly, intensifying the feeling of loss here.

examples.text: Tu nous manques terriblement.
examples.trans: We miss you terribly.

examples.text: C'est terriblement triste.
examples.trans: It's terribly sad.

examples.text: Samuel, tu nous manques terriblement.
examples.trans: Samuel, we miss you terribly.

meanings.note: Both consonants in -st are pronounced (/tɛst/); faire un test means 'to run a test / test it out'.

examples.text: Faisons un premier test avant de refermer le boîtier.
examples.trans: Let's do a first test before closing the casing back up.

examples.text: Le test d'éclairage dans le jardin d'hiver est réussi!
examples.trans: The lighting test in the winter garden is a success!

meanings.note: A will setting out someone's wishes for their property after death.

examples.text: Il n'a pas laissé de testament.
examples.trans: He didn't leave a will.

examples.text: Où est le testament?
examples.trans: Where is the will?

examples.text: Merci. Samuel n'a pas laissé de testament.
examples.trans: Thank you. Samuel didn't leave a will.

meanings.en: to test, try out (equipment, a recipe, or lighting)
meanings.note: Everyday verb from le test; allons tester la lampe means 'let's go test the lamp'.

examples.text: Allons tester la nouvelle lampe du plafond avant la nuit.
examples.trans: Let's go test the new ceiling lamp before nightfall.

examples.text: Nadia teste une nouvelle recette de biscuits aux amandes.
examples.trans: Nadia is testing out a new almond biscuit recipe.

texte.gloss: text; lines (of a play or film)

meanings.note: apprendre un texte = to learn lines
apprendre un texte = to learn lines

examples.text: Ce n'est pas facile d'apprendre un texte.
examples.trans: It's not easy to learn lines.

examples.text: Tu connais ton texte?
examples.trans: Do you know your lines?

meanings.note: Pronounced /tɛ̃/ (like teint).

examples.text: Le thym frais pousse au soleil dans un pot en terre.
examples.trans: Fresh thyme grows in the sun in a clay pot.

examples.text: Un brin de thym parfume doucement le bouillon.
examples.trans: A sprig of thyme gently flavors the broth.

examples.text: Un thé?
examples.trans: Tea?

examples.text: Je prends un thé.
examples.trans: I'll have a tea.

meanings.note: Built from thé ('tea').

examples.text: Verse l'eau chaude dans la théière, Claire, les voilà!
examples.trans: Pour the hot water into the teapot, Claire, here they come!

examples.text: Et la théière est bien chaude! Tout le monde recule loin de la fenêtre!
examples.trans: And the teapot is piping hot! Everybody step back from the window!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la théorie', plural 'les théories') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'theory'.

examples.text: Elle lit des théories sur les bébés.
examples.trans: She reads theories about babies.

examples.text: Où as-tu appris toutes ces théories?
examples.trans: Where did you learn all these theories?

examples.text: C'est une belle théorie du complot.
examples.trans: That is a fine conspiracy theory.

meanings.note: une thérapie de couple = couples therapy

examples.text: Faire une thérapie de couple.
examples.trans: To do couples therapy.

examples.text: Suivre une thérapie.
examples.trans: To undergo therapy.

examples.text: Nous faisons actuellement une thérapie de couple.
examples.trans: We are currently doing couples therapy.

meanings.note: Faire du théâtre = to act on stage.

examples.text: Elle a fait un peu de théâtre.
examples.trans: She's done a bit of theatre.

examples.text: On va au théâtre.
examples.trans: We're going to the theatre.

meanings.note: Ticket de caisse = shop receipt.

examples.text: Non, seulement mon stylo et trois vieux tickets!
examples.trans: No, only my pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: Voici cinquante euros de la caisse. Rapportez le ticket!
examples.trans: Here is fifty euros from the cash box. Bring back the receipt!

examples.text: Quelle vitesse! L'épicier vous a donné un ticket?
examples.trans: What speed! Did the grocer give you a receipt?

meanings.en: le tien / la tienne / les tiens / les tiennes = yours (informal 'tu')
meanings.note: agrees in gender and number with the thing owned

examples.text: Tu veux un autographe? — Le tien?
examples.trans: Do you want an autograph? — Yours?

examples.text: C'est mon verre ou le tien?
examples.trans: Is this my glass or yours?

examples.text: Le tien?
examples.trans: Yours?

tige.gloss: stem, stalk (of a plant); thin rod

meanings.en: plant stem, vine stalk; slender metal rod
meanings.note: Used for flower/ivy stems (*la tige du lierre*) as well as slender metal pins or shafts.

examples.text: Attachez doucement la tige verte au treillis sans la casser.
examples.trans: Gently tie the green stem to the trellis without snapping it.

examples.text: Coupez le bout des tiges avant de mettre les fleurs dans l'eau.
examples.trans: Trim the ends of the stems before putting the flowers in water.

meanings.note: Fragrant courtyard shade tree; also herbal tea.

examples.text: Sur la cour, juste au-dessus du vieux tilleul. C'est très calme.
examples.trans: The courtyard, right above the old linden tree. It is very quiet.

examples.text: Bienvenue à l'Hôtel du Tilleul, Claire. Votre deuxième jour ne sera pas ennuyeux.
examples.trans: Welcome to the Hotel du Tilleul, Claire. Your second day will not be boring.

examples.text: Hôtel du Tilleul, bonjour! Claire à l'appareil.
examples.trans: Hotel du Tilleul, good morning! Claire speaking.

meanings.note: Un timbre unique. Masculine noun ('le timbre', plural 'les timbres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tone'.

examples.text: Oui, elle a un timbre unique.
examples.trans: Yes, she has a unique timbre.

examples.text: Il a un timbre de voix chaleureux.
examples.trans: He has a warm vocal timbre.

examples.text: Un petit chat timide.
examples.trans: A shy little cat.

examples.text: Il est très timide.
examples.trans: He is very shy.

tirer.gloss: to pull, slide out; to draw

meanings.note: Seen on doors all over France: Tirez ('Pull') vs Poussez ('Push').

examples.text: Tirez doucement le meuble vers vous pendant que je soulève.
examples.trans: Pull the piece of furniture gently towards you while I lift.

examples.text: Claire tire les rideaux pour laisser entrer le soleil.
examples.trans: Claire draws back the curtains to let the sunlight in.

meanings.note: Built from tirer ('to pull').

examples.text: Dans le tiroir. Ici, on utilise ce grand cahier en papier et un crayon.
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper notebook and a pencil.

examples.text: Voici le tiroir sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the drawer on the table.

meanings.note: French distinguishes *le thé* (made from tea leaves, with caffeine) from *une tisane* (caffeine-free herbal infusion of chamomile, linden blossom, or verbena).

examples.text: Le soir, elle boit une tisane chaude aux fleurs de tilleul.
examples.trans: In the evening, she drinks a hot linden-blossom herbal tea.

examples.text: Cette tisane à la camomille sent le miel et le jardin.
examples.trans: This chamomile herbal tea smells of honey and the garden.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb: un tapis tissé = a woven rug.

examples.text: Et j'ai deux oreillers doux et un tapis bleu tissé dans la réserve!
examples.trans: And I have two soft pillows and a woven blue rug in the storeroom!

examples.text: C'est facile à tisser ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to weave together.

meanings.note: En tissu describes cloth-covered items, including old mid-century braided cloth-insulated electrical wire (du fil en tissu).

examples.text: Les vieux fils électriques entourés de tissu doivent être changés.
examples.trans: Old cloth-wrapped electrical wires must be replaced.

examples.text: Claire choisit un tissu vert doux pour les coussins du salon.
examples.trans: Claire chooses a soft green fabric for the lounge cushions.

meanings.en: title (of a piece of music, book, or document), heading
meanings.note: Masculine noun for the title written at the top of a page, score, or book cover.

examples.text: Le titre de la valse est écrit à la plume en haut de la feuille.
examples.trans: The title of the waltz is written in fountain pen at the top of the sheet.

examples.text: Vous vous souvenez du titre de ce vieux livre?
examples.trans: Do you remember the title of that old book?

meanings.note: Between chaud and froid.

examples.text: Touche le radiateur — le bas est chaud, alors que le haut devient froid.
examples.trans: Feel the radiator—the bottom is warm, while the top is turning cool.

examples.text: Son grand-père coupait du gâteau tiède au citron avec du sucre glace dessus!
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with icing sugar on top!

examples.text: Excusez-moi, messieurs: voici le thé chaud, et le gâteau tiède au citron arrive.
examples.trans: Excuse me, gentlemen: here is hot tea, and warm lemon cake is on the way.

meanings.en: toast (drink to someone's health or honor)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le toast', plural 'les toasts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'toast'.
Masculine noun ('le toast', plural 'les toasts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'toast'.

examples.text: Je porte un toast très clair.
examples.trans: I propose a very clear toast.

examples.text: Nous levons nos verres pour un toast.
examples.trans: We raise our glasses for a toast.

examples.text: Je voudrais porter un grand toast!
examples.trans: I would like to propose a big toast!

meanings.note: Stressed form: et toi? = and you?.

examples.text: Et toi?
examples.trans: And you?

examples.text: C'est pour toi.
examples.trans: It's for you.

meanings.note: Formal/plural: vous-même(s).

examples.text: Dis-lui toi-même pourquoi!
examples.trans: Tell him why yourself!

examples.text: Fais-le toi-même.
examples.trans: Do it yourself.

examples.text: Je rêve! Dis-lui toi-même pourquoi!
examples.trans: I'm dreaming! Tell him why yourself!

meanings.note: Sturdy woven linen or cotton cloth ('toile cirée' = waxed waterproof cloth); painter's canvas.

examples.text: Le coffret était protégé par un carré de toile cirée.
examples.trans: The box was protected by a square of waxed cloth.

examples.text: Le peintre installe sa toile à l'ombre du porche.
examples.trans: The painter sets up his canvas in the shade of the porch.

meanings.note: usually plural: les toilettes = the restroom
Faire sa toilette. Feminine noun ('la toilette', plural 'les toilettes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'restroom'.

examples.text: Je vais aux toilettes.
examples.trans: I am going to the restroom.

examples.text: Où sont les toilettes?
examples.trans: Where is the restroom?

examples.text: Non, je vais juste aux toilettes.
examples.trans: No, I am just going to the restroom.

meanings.note: Bound in woven bookcloth ('carnet toilé') or mounted on linen ('carte toilée').

examples.text: Il ouvre un carnet toilé bleu marine aux coins dorés.
examples.trans: He opens a navy cloth-bound notebook with gilt corners.

examples.text: Les vieilles cartes routières étaient souvent toilées pour durer.
examples.trans: Old road maps were often linen-backed to last.

meanings.note: Sous les toits = up under the eaves.

examples.text: Le vieux bureau clair sous les toits... suivez-moi, vite!
examples.trans: The old bright attic study... follow me, quickly!

examples.text: Écoutez la pluie sur le toit, c'est tellement chaleureux ici!
examples.trans: Listen to the rain on the roof, it feels so cosy up here!

examples.text: Rassurez-vous! Nous avons préparé notre chambre calme sous les toits juste pour vous.
examples.trans: Rest assured! We prepared our quiet attic room just for you.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (*une soupe de tomates rôties*).

examples.text: En été, nous préparons une grande soupe de tomates aux herbes.
examples.trans: In summer, we make a big pot of herb tomato soup.

examples.text: Choisissez des tomates bien mûres et parfumées au marché.
examples.trans: Pick ripe, fragrant tomatoes at the market.

meanings.note: The place where someone is buried; a feminine noun.

examples.text: Un pied glisse vers la tombe.
examples.trans: A foot slips towards the grave.

examples.text: Il y a des fleurs sur la tombe.
examples.trans: There are flowers on the grave.

examples.text: J'ai senti un pied glisser vers la tombe.
examples.trans: I felt one foot slip towards the grave.

meanings.note: Passé composé with 'être'.

meanings.en: laisser tomber = to drop it, to forget it
meanings.note: Laisse tomber! = forget it!.

examples.text: Il est tombé dans la rue.
examples.trans: He fell in the street.

examples.text: Laisse tomber, mon chéri.
examples.trans: Leave it, darling.

examples.text: Dans quel hôtel magique es-tu tombé par hasard, petit frère?
examples.trans: What kind of magical hotel did you stumble into, little brother?

meanings.note: Informal, one owner; ton, ta, tes.

examples.text: Tes premières vacances!
examples.trans: Your first holiday!

examples.text: C'est ton vélo?
examples.trans: Is it your bike?

meanings.note: Avoids ambiguity with *la touche* (piano key) and *la clé* (door key / clef): 'in the same key' in music is *dans la même tonalité*.

examples.text: Elle écrit la fin de la valse dans la même tonalité douce.
examples.trans: She writes the ending of the waltz in the same gentle key.

examples.text: La tonalité de sol majeur donne une couleur claire au morceau.
examples.trans: The key of G major gives the piece a bright color.

meanings.note: Être en tongs. Feminine noun ('la tong', plural 'les tongs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'flip-flop'.

examples.text: C'est magnifique, mais je suis en tongs!
examples.trans: It is magnificent, but I am in flip-flops!

examples.text: Il marche sur la plage en tongs.
examples.trans: He walks on the beach in flip-flops.

examples.text: C'est comme faire une randonnée en tongs!
examples.trans: It is like hiking in flip-flops!

meanings.note: Couvrir un bol avec un torchon propre = cover a bowl with a clean kitchen towel.

examples.text: Couvrez la pâte tiède avec un torchon légèrement humide.
examples.trans: Cover the warm dough with a slightly damp kitchen towel.

examples.text: Il essuie les tasses blanches avec un torchon sec.
examples.trans: He dries the white cups with a dry tea towel.

meanings.note: To twist or bend metal out of shape; to wring out a wet cloth.

examples.text: Soulevez bien droit pour ne pas tordre la charnière.
examples.trans: Lift straight up so you don't bend the hinge.

examples.text: Elle tord le torchon humide avant de l'étendre.
examples.trans: She wrings out the damp kitchen towel before hanging it up.

meanings.en: twist, mild sprain (of an ankle or wrist)
meanings.note: Related to *tordre* ('to twist'); *une torsion de la cheville* describes twisting one's ankle without a fracture.

examples.text: Ce n'est rien de cassé, juste une légère torsion de la cheville.
examples.trans: Nothing is broken, just a slight twist of the ankle.

examples.text: Un peu de glace calme vite la douleur après une torsion.
examples.trans: A little ice quickly calms the ache after a twist.

meanings.note: avoir tort = to be wrong; n'avoir pas tort = to not be wrong
Faire du tort à quelqu'un. Masculine noun ('le tort', plural 'les torts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'wrong'.

examples.text: Un discours de cinq minutes avec dix-neuf raisons pour lesquelles nous avions tort tous les deux.
examples.trans: A five-minute speech with nineteen reasons why we were both wrong.

examples.text: Il n'a pas tort.
examples.trans: He is not wrong.

examples.text: Tu as tort.
examples.trans: You are wrong.

meanings.en: to torture, to torment; se torturer = to torment oneself
meanings.note: Se torturer l'esprit. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to torture'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'torturé').

examples.text: Arrête de te torturer.
examples.trans: Stop torturing yourself.

examples.text: Torturer son esprit.
examples.trans: To torment one's mind.

examples.text: C'est du passé, arrête de te torturer.
examples.trans: It is in the past, stop torturing yourself.

meanings.note: Au total = in total, all together. Masculine noun ('le total', plural 'les totaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'total'.

examples.text: Nous avons dix candidats au total.
examples.trans: We have ten candidates in total.

examples.text: Calculer le total.
examples.trans: To calculate the total.

examples.text: Sans totale liberté, l'art est inutile.
examples.trans: Without total freedom, art is useless.

meanings.note: Entirely, wholly.

examples.text: L'intérieur de la boîte est resté totalement sec.
examples.trans: The inside of the box stayed completely dry.

examples.text: J'avais totalement oublié l'existence de ce passage!
examples.trans: I had completely forgotten that this passageway existed!

meanings.note: Un animal totem = a totem animal. Masculine noun ('le totem', plural 'les totems') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'totem'.

examples.text: J'ai découvert mon animal totem.
examples.trans: I discovered my totem animal.

examples.text: Un mât totem.
examples.trans: A totem pole.

examples.text: Grâce à lui, j'ai découvert mon animal totem.
examples.trans: Thanks to him, I discovered my totem animal.

meanings.note: Emotionally moving, heartwarming.

examples.text: Ce mot laissé pour la génération suivante est très touchant.
examples.trans: This note left for the next generation is deeply touching.

examples.text: Leur fidélité après tant d'années est vraiment touchante.
examples.trans: Their loyalty after so many years is truly moving.

touche.gloss: key (of a piano or keyboard), button

meanings.en: key (of a piano, organ, or keyboard)
meanings.note: Keep distinct from une clé (a door lock key or a musical clef symbol on a staff): the physical black and white keys you press on a piano are les touches.

examples.text: Une seule touche du vieux piano reste encore muette.
examples.trans: Only one key on the old piano is still silent.

examples.text: Odette essuie délicatement les quatre-vingt-huit touches.
examples.trans: Odette gently wipes the eighty-eight piano keys.

meanings.note: Je ne touche pas à mon visage.

meanings.en: toucher à: to touch, to tamper with
meanings.note: Je ne touche pas à mon visage.

examples.text: Ne touche pas!
examples.trans: Don't touch!

examples.text: Je ne touche pas à mon visage.
examples.trans: I'm not touching my face.

meanings.note: Moved emotionally by someone's words or gesture.
Also physically hit or affected, depending on context.

examples.text: Je suis touché.
examples.trans: I'm touched.

examples.text: Elle est très touchée.
examples.trans: She's very moved.

examples.text: C'est une offre? Je suis touché.
examples.trans: Is that an offer? I'm touched.

meanings.note: toujours aucune nouvelle? = still no news?

examples.text: Il est toujours là.
examples.trans: He's still here.

examples.text: La circulation en ville à midi est toujours lente.
examples.trans: City traffic at noon is always slow.

meanings.note: C'est mon tour = it's my turn. Masculine noun ('le tour', plural 'les tours') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'turn'.

examples.text: À ton tour!
examples.trans: Your turn!

examples.text: Un tour, deux tours... regardez comme le nouveau pas de vis rentre bien.
examples.trans: One turn, two turns... look how smoothly the new screw thread fits.

examples.text: Lisez la première ligne pour moi, Claire. Dites-moi que mes lunettes me jouent un tour!
examples.trans: Read the top line for me, Claire. Tell me my glasses are playing a trick on me!

meanings.note: une touriste étrangère = a foreign tourist

examples.text: Une touriste espagnole croisée dans le métro.
examples.trans: A Spanish tourist crossed paths with in the subway.

examples.text: Les touristes visitent Paris.
examples.trans: Tourists visit Paris.

examples.text: Une touriste espagnole croisée dans le métro!
examples.trans: A Spanish tourist crossed paths with in the subway!

meanings.en: to torment, to plague, to trouble deeply
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to torment'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'tourmenté').

examples.text: Cette idée me tourmente.
examples.trans: This idea torments me.

examples.text: Tourmenter son esprit.
examples.trans: To plague one's mind.

examples.text: Cette histoire me tourmente sans cesse.
examples.trans: This story torments me endlessly.

meanings.note: The process or period of making a film; tourner un film means shoot a film.

examples.text: Le tournage commence dans trois semaines.
examples.trans: The shoot starts in three weeks.

examples.text: Le tournage est fini.
examples.trans: Filming is over.

examples.text: Elle est en tournage.
examples.trans: She's on a shoot.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le tournant', plural 'les tournants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'turning point'.
Masculine noun ('le tournant', plural 'les tournants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bend'.

examples.text: C'est un grand tournant dans sa carrière.
examples.trans: It is a big turning point in his career.

examples.text: Ce film est ton grand tournant dramatique.
examples.trans: This movie is your big dramatic turning point.

meanings.note: Tournez le visage = turn your face.
Cinema.

examples.text: Elle tourne un film.
examples.trans: She's shooting a film.

examples.text: Tournez à gauche.
examples.trans: Turn left.

meanings.note: Compound of tourne + vis; invariable plural.

examples.text: Déjà fini? Vous gardez un tournevis partout sur vous, Henri!
examples.trans: Done already? You carry a screwdriver everywhere on you, Henri!

examples.text: Voici le tournevis sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the screwdriver on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la tournée', plural 'les tournées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'theatrical tour'.

examples.text: La fin de tournée approche.
examples.trans: The end of the tour approaches.

examples.text: La fin de tournée approche déjà.
examples.trans: The end of the tour is already approaching.

examples.text: On reprend à la tournée.
examples.trans: Let's pick back up at the tour.

examples.text: Tout va bien.
examples.trans: Everything is going well.

examples.text: Madame Odette, tout va bien? Vous avez sonné!
examples.trans: Madam Odette, is everything alright? You rang the bell!

meanings.note: Spoken French tudəsɥit expression meaning 'right away', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Oui, tout de suite.
examples.trans: Yes, right away.

examples.text: J'arrive tout de suite.
examples.trans: I'll be right there.

examples.text: D'accord, j'arrive tout de suite.
examples.trans: All right, I am coming right away.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: Everyone is here.

examples.text: Bonjour tout le monde!
examples.trans: Hello everyone!

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

meanings.en: toxic, harmful (of a relationship or person)
meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Cet homme est toxique pour toi.
examples.trans: This man is toxic for you.

examples.text: C'est une relation toxique.
examples.trans: It is a toxic relationship.

examples.text: Noémie, cet homme est toxique pour toi.
examples.trans: Noemie, this man is toxic for you.

meanings.note: avoir le trac = to have stage fright (final c is pronounced)

examples.text: J'ai toujours le trac avant d'entrer en scène.
examples.trans: I always get stage fright before going on stage.

examples.text: Quand j'ai le trac, mes phrases deviennent très longues et compliquées!
examples.trans: When I get stage fright, my sentences become very long and complicated!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to worry'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'tracassé').

examples.text: Cette histoire te tracasse?
examples.trans: Is this story bothering you?

examples.text: Cette histoire de paternité te tracasse?
examples.trans: Is this paternity business bothering you?

meanings.note: When cleaning windows or mirrors, *sans traces / zéro trace* means 'streak-free'.

examples.text: Une goutte de vinaigre dans l'eau tiède ne laisse aucune trace sur la vitre.
examples.trans: A drop of vinegar in warm water leaves zero streaks on the glass.

examples.text: Essuyez la table pour enlever toute trace de farine.
examples.trans: Wipe the table to remove every trace of flour.

meanings.note: To draw crisp lines, letters, or a route; for sunlight to cast shadows.
