examples.text: À midi, les aiguilles tracent une ligne verticale parfaite.
examples.trans: At noon, the clock hands form a perfect vertical line.

examples.text: Elle a tracé le plan du jardin à l'encre de Chine.
examples.trans: She drew the garden plan in India ink.

examples.text: C'est une tradition chez les comédiens.
examples.trans: It's a tradition among actors.

examples.text: C'est une vieille tradition.
examples.trans: It's an old tradition.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: C'est une fin tragique.
examples.trans: It is a tragic ending.

examples.text: Un accident tragique.
examples.trans: A tragic accident.

examples.text: C'est une histoire tragique et très sombre.
examples.trans: It is a tragic and very dark story.

examples.text: Sans tant de tragédie!
examples.trans: Without so much tragedy!

examples.text: C'est une tragédie grecque.
examples.trans: It's a Greek tragedy.

meanings.note: Trahir ses amis. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to betray'.

examples.text: Tu as trahi tes amis.
examples.trans: You betrayed your friends.

examples.text: Trahir un secret.
examples.trans: To betray a secret.

examples.text: Laisse-moi finir! Tu as trahi tes amis.
examples.trans: Let me finish! You betrayed your friends.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la trahison', plural 'les trahisons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'betrayal'.

examples.text: C'est une trahison inattendue.
examples.trans: It is an unexpected betrayal.

examples.text: C'est une trahison totalement inattendue!
examples.trans: It is a totally unexpected betrayal!

examples.text: Andréa et Gabriel préparent une trahison totale!
examples.trans: Andrea and Gabriel are preparing a total betrayal!

meanings.note: prendre le train = to take the train
être en train de faire = to be in the middle of doing

examples.text: Oui, la chambre quatre au deuxième étage! Comment était votre voyage en train?
examples.trans: Yes, room four on the second floor! How was your train trip?

examples.text: Et qu'est-ce que c'est, dans ce papier blanc? Un petit train en bois!
examples.trans: And what is this, in this white paper? A little wooden train!

examples.text: Comme c'est étrange! Nous avons pris le même train ce matin pour le même quartier.
examples.trans: How strange! We rode the same train this morning to the same district.

meanings.note: Pen or pencil stroke; facial features ('les traits').

examples.text: Les traits au fusain sont restés d'une grande finesse.
examples.trans: The charcoal strokes have remained remarkably delicate.

examples.text: Tirez un trait léger au crayon pour relier les deux points.
examples.trans: Draw a light pencil line to connect the two points.

meanings.note: traiter avec respect = to treat with respect

examples.text: Il a une drôle de façon de traiter les acteurs.
examples.trans: He has a strange way of treating actors.

examples.text: Traiter un sujet important.
examples.trans: To deal with an important topic.

examples.text: Vous me traitez comme un voleur maintenant?
examples.trans: Are you treating me like a thief now?

meanings.note: The way from one place to another.
Merci pour le trajet.

examples.text: Le trajet est long.
examples.trans: The journey is long.

examples.text: Merci pour le trajet.
examples.trans: Thanks for the lift.

meanings.note: Une tranche de pain / de gâteau.

examples.text: Du thé noir sans sucre, s'il vous plaît, et une tranche de pain chaud.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please, and a slice of warm bread.

examples.text: Voici la tranche sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the slice on the table.

meanings.note: Notice pronunciation `/tʁɑ̃kil/` (NOT `/ij/`—one of the rare *-ille* words pronounced `/il/`, alongside *ville* and *mille*!).

examples.text: J'aime le rythme tranquille de la cour en fin d'après-midi.
examples.trans: I love the unhurried pace of the courtyard in the late afternoon.

examples.text: Prenez un thé chaud dans un coin tranquille près du piano.
examples.trans: Have a hot tea in a quiet corner near the piano.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Nous allons en parler tranquillement ensemble.
examples.trans: We are going to talk about it calmly together.

examples.text: Il marche tranquillement dans la rue.
examples.trans: He walks quietly down the street.

examples.text: Elle dort tranquillement dans son berceau.
examples.trans: She is sleeping peacefully in her crib.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la transe', plural 'les transes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'trance'.

examples.text: Elle entre dans une transe.
examples.trans: She enters into a trance.

examples.text: La fatigue me plonge dans une transe.
examples.trans: Exhaustion plunges me into a trance.

meanings.note: Converting a building to a new use.

examples.text: Regardez la page un, Monsieur Antoine: transformation en bureaux le mois prochain. Nous sommes finis!
examples.trans: Look at page one, Mr Antoine: conversion into offices next month. We are finished!

examples.text: Voici la transformation sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the conversion, transformation on the table.

meanings.note: se transformer complètement = to transform completely

examples.text: Des bureaux commerciaux?! Transformer notre hôtel et ma cuisine en bureaux gris?!
examples.trans: Commercial offices?! Turn our hotel and my kitchen into grey offices?!

examples.text: Transformer une idée en projet.
examples.trans: To transform an idea into a project.

meanings.note: transférer sa haine = to transfer one's hatred

examples.text: Il te transfère sa haine.
examples.trans: He transfers his hatred to you.

examples.text: Transférer un dossier.
examples.trans: To transfer a file.

examples.text: Il te transfère sa haine pour Mathias.
examples.trans: He transfers his hatred for Mathias to you.

meanings.en: to transmit, pass along, convey, forward
meanings.note: Irregular third-group French verb inherited from core Latin roots, used across registers for 'to transmit'.

examples.text: Transmets-lui mes amitiés.
examples.trans: Pass along my regards to her.

examples.text: Transmettre un message important.
examples.trans: To convey an important message.

examples.text: J'en suis ravi. Transmets-lui mes amitiés.
examples.trans: I am delighted. Pass along my warm regards to her.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to sweat'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'transpiré').

examples.text: Transpirez ou ça ne sera pas crédible.
examples.trans: Sweat or it will not look credible.

examples.text: Je transpire beaucoup.
examples.trans: I sweat a lot.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le transport', plural 'les transports') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'transportation'.

examples.text: J'ai besoin d'un transport.
examples.trans: I need a ride.

examples.text: As-tu prévu un bon transport?
examples.trans: Did you arrange good transportation?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le traquenard', plural 'les traquenards') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'trap'.

examples.text: Ce dîner d'affaires était un vrai traquenard.
examples.trans: That business dinner was a total trap.

examples.text: Ce dîner était un vrai traquenard!
examples.trans: That dinner was a total trap!

meanings.note: Un travail = a job.

meanings.en: au travail! = let's get to work!

examples.text: Allez, au travail!
examples.trans: Come on, back to work!

examples.text: Je cherche du travail.
examples.trans: I'm looking for work.

meanings.note: travailler à Paris, travailler le dimanche

examples.text: Tu travailles le dimanche?
examples.trans: Do you work on Sundays?

examples.text: J'ai travaillé au festival.
examples.trans: I worked at the festival.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor').

examples.text: Un homme simple et travailleur.
examples.trans: A simple and hardworking man.

examples.text: Un homme simple, travailleur et attentionné.
examples.trans: A simple, hardworking, and caring man.

meanings.note: plural of travail in the building context

examples.text: L'appartement est en plein travaux.
examples.trans: The apartment is undergoing renovations.

examples.text: Mon appartement est en plein travaux.
examples.trans: My apartment is under renovation.

meanings.en: across, through (*à travers le verre* = through the glass)
meanings.note: Almost always met in the prepositional phrase *à travers* ('through', for light, glass, trees, or windows).

examples.text: La lumière dorée passe à travers les grandes vitres propres.
examples.trans: Golden light shines through the tall clean windows.

examples.text: On aperçoit le tilleul à travers la porte vitrée.
examples.trans: You can see the linden tree through the glass door.

meanings.note: No preposition: traverser Paris.

examples.text: Attention en traversant la rue.
examples.trans: Be careful crossing the street.

examples.text: À gauche au portail, tout droit jusqu'au pont. Je traverse le fleuve?
examples.trans: Left at the gate, straight ahead to the bridge. Do I cross the river?

examples.text: Payé en espèces! Gardez vos outils ouverts, je traverse le pont en courant!
examples.trans: Paid in cash! Keep your tools open, I am running back across the bridge!

traîner.gloss: to drag out, linger, hang around

meanings.en: to drag out, take too long
meanings.note: ça commence à traîner = it is dragging on
Traîner dans la rue. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to drag out'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'traîné').

examples.text: Ça commence à traîner.
examples.trans: Things are starting to drag out.

examples.text: Ne traîne pas en route.
examples.trans: Do not dawdle on the way.

examples.text: Je vais faire traîner les négociations.
examples.trans: I will drag out the negotiations.

meanings.note: Feminine traîtresse.

examples.text: Où est le traître?
examples.trans: Where's the traitor?

examples.text: Tu es un traître!
examples.trans: You're a traitor!

meanings.en: wooden or iron garden trellis, lattice
meanings.note: Final *-s* is silent (`/tʁeji/`), and singular and plural are identical (*un treillis, des treillis*).

examples.text: Posez les branches du lierre sur le treillis en bois contre le mur.
examples.trans: Rest the ivy branches on the wooden trellis against the wall.

examples.text: Les rosiers grimpent tout autour du treillis du jardin.
examples.trans: The rosebushes climb all around the garden trellis.

examples.text: C'était comme si elle avait treize ans.
examples.trans: It was as if she were thirteen.

examples.text: Chapitre treize.
examples.trans: Chapter thirteen.

examples.text: L'horreur absolue! C'était comme si elle avait treize ans.
examples.trans: Total horror! It was as if she were thirteen.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Mes mains tremblent... il y a un homme grand avec un manteau gris foncé?
examples.trans: My hands are shaking... is there a tall man in a dark grey coat?

examples.text: Oh... oh non. Où est ma chaise? J'ai les jambes qui tremblent.
examples.trans: Oh... oh no. Where is my chair? My legs are shaking.

meanings.en: to dip (a sponge or biscuit in liquid); to soak, drench
meanings.note: Past participle *trempé(e)* is the everyday word for being drenched by rain (*mes manches sont trempées!*).

examples.text: Trempez l'éponge propre dans le seau d'eau tiède.
examples.trans: Dip the clean sponge into the bucket of warm water.

examples.text: Rentrez vite sous le porche avant d'être complètement trempés!
examples.trans: Come quickly under the archway before getting soaked through!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la trentaine', plural 'les trentaines') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'about thirty'.

examples.text: Il y avait une trentaine de personnes dans la salle.
examples.trans: There were about thirty people in the room.

examples.text: Elle a commencé à réaliser des films vers la trentaine.
examples.trans: She started directing films around the age of thirty.

examples.text: Elle a trente ans.
examples.trans: She's thirty.

examples.text: Trente euros, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Thirty euros, please.

meanings.note: Spoken French num expression meaning 'number 35', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Trente-cinq ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Thirty-five years of career.

examples.text: Depuis trente-cinq ans.
examples.trans: For thirty-five years.

examples.text: Quelle heure est-il? Neuf heures trente-cinq!
examples.trans: What time is it? Nine thirty-five!

meanings.note: Compound number 30 + 8.

examples.text: Juste ici! Tout a coûté trente-huit euros, alors voici douze euros de monnaie.
examples.trans: Right here! Everything cost thirty-eight euros, so here is twelve euros in change.

examples.text: Tout a coûté trente-huit euros, alors voici douze euros de monnaie.
examples.trans: Everything cost thirty-eight euros, so here is twelve euros in change.

examples.text: J'ai trente-quatre ans.
examples.trans: I'm thirty-four.

examples.text: La chambre trente-quatre.
examples.trans: Room thirty-four.

meanings.note: Ordinal number thirtieth (30e).

examples.text: C'est aujourd'hui le trentième été de notre maison d'hôtes.
examples.trans: Today marks the thirtieth summer of our guesthouse.

examples.text: L'indice se trouve à la trentième page du registre.
examples.trans: The clue is on the thirtieth page of the ledger.

meanings.note: Aller au tribunal = to go to court.

examples.text: On va au tribunal!
examples.trans: We're going to court!

examples.text: Le tribunal est fermé.
examples.trans: The court is closed.

examples.text: Si tu pars avec tes acteurs, on va au tribunal!
examples.trans: If you leave with your actors, we're going to court!

meanings.note: offrir une tribune = give a platform
La tribune du stade. Feminine noun ('la tribune', plural 'les tribunes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'platform'.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas leur offrir une tribune.
examples.trans: I do not want to give them a platform.

examples.text: Une tribune dans le journal.
examples.trans: An op-ed column in the newspaper.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to cheat'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'triché').

examples.text: Ils pensent qu'elle a triché?
examples.trans: They think that she cheated?

examples.text: Ils pensent qu'Isabelle a triché?
examples.trans: Do they think that Isabelle cheated?

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to sort'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'trié').

examples.text: Je dois trier tous mes courriels avant midi.
examples.trans: I have to sort through all my emails before noon.

examples.text: Elle trie les photos de casting sur son bureau.
examples.trans: She is sorting the casting photos on her desk.

meanings.en: to clink glasses, to drink a toast
meanings.note: Trinquer à quelque chose.

examples.text: On trinque?
examples.trans: Shall we clink glasses?

examples.text: On trinque à l'agence!
examples.trans: Let's drink to the agency!

examples.text: Quel rabat-joie! On trinque?
examples.trans: What a killjoy! Shall we clink glasses?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le triomphe', plural 'les triomphes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'triumph'.

examples.text: C'est un triomphe absolu.
examples.trans: It is an absolute triumph.

examples.text: Le film est un grand triomphe.
examples.trans: The movie is a great triumph.

examples.text: C'est un triomphe absolu, bravo!
examples.trans: It is an absolute triumph, bravo!

examples.text: Elle est triste.
examples.trans: She's sad.

examples.text: C'est une triste histoire.
examples.trans: It's a sad story.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la tristesse', plural 'les tristesses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sadness'.

examples.text: Comprendre sa tristesse.
examples.trans: To understand her sadness.

examples.text: Éprouver de la tristesse.
examples.trans: To feel sadness.

examples.text: Je comprends ta tristesse face à ce changement.
examples.trans: I understand your sadness about this change.

examples.text: Trois semaines.
examples.trans: Three weeks.

examples.text: Trois cafés.
examples.trans: Three coffees.

meanings.note: Au troisième étage = on the third floor.

examples.text: Attendez, qu'est-ce qu'il y a au troisième étage, en haut de l'escalier?
examples.trans: Wait, what is on the third floor, at the top of the stairs?

examples.text: Voici la petite clé en argent pour la porte du grenier au troisième étage.
examples.trans: Here is the small silver key for the third-floor attic door.

examples.text: Allez, le premier arrivé au troisième étage!
examples.trans: Come on, race you to the third floor!

meanings.note: Deceive someone.
Be unfaithful to a partner; tromper quelqu’un takes a direct object.

examples.text: Il trompe sa femme.
examples.trans: He cheats on his wife.

examples.text: Les apparences peuvent tromper.
examples.trans: Appearances can be deceptive.

examples.text: Avez-vous déjà trompé votre femme, Mathias?
examples.trans: Have you ever cheated on your wife, Mathias?

meanings.note: Trop vieille = too old.
Trop de travail.

examples.text: C'est trop difficile.
examples.trans: It's too difficult.

examples.text: Trop tard! Il a dit merci et il a raccroché!
examples.trans: Too late! He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le trophée', plural 'les trophées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'trophy'.

examples.text: Ils me voient comme un trophée.
examples.trans: They see me as a trophy.

examples.text: Les hommes me voient seulement comme un trophée.
examples.trans: Men see me only as a trophy.

examples.text: Une autre actrice a remporté le trophée!
examples.trans: Another actress won the trophy!

meanings.note: trottinette électrique = electric scooter

examples.text: Regarde ces trottinettes électriques!
examples.trans: Look at those electric scooters!

examples.text: Regarde ces trottinettes électriques là-bas!
examples.trans: Look at those electric scooters over there!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le trottoir', plural 'les trottoirs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sidewalk'.

examples.text: Le long du trottoir.
examples.trans: Along the sidewalk.

examples.text: Marcher sur le trottoir.
examples.trans: To walk on the sidewalk.

examples.text: trottoir!
examples.trans: pavement / sidewalk!

meanings.note: Un petit trou de vis = a tiny screw hole.

examples.text: On voit encore deux petits trous de vis sous le vernis.
examples.trans: You can still see two tiny screw holes under the varnish.

examples.text: Il perce un trou propre dans la planche en chêne.
examples.trans: He drills a clean hole in the oak board.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to fluster'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'troublé').

examples.text: Tout homme serait troublé devant toi.
examples.trans: Any man would be flustered in front of you.

examples.text: Le vendeur était tellement timide et troublé!
examples.trans: The clerk was so shy and flustered!

examples.text: N'importe quel homme serait troublé devant toi.
examples.trans: Any man would be flustered in front of you.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la trouille', plural 'les trouilles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fear'.

examples.text: J'ai toujours une trouille bleue avant d'entrer en scène.
examples.trans: I always have terrible stage fright before going on stage.

examples.text: Ce film d'horreur m'a donné une sacrée trouille!
examples.trans: That horror movie gave me a real fright!

meanings.note: A ring or bunch of keys carried together ('un trousseau de clés').
Plural takes -x: les trousseaux.

examples.text: Prenez le trousseau, Claire; vous prenez la boîte à chapeau, et moi j'ai les deux sacs à dos.
examples.trans: Grab the keyring, Claire; you take the hatbox, and I have the two backpacks.

examples.text: Henri garde toujours son lourd trousseau de clés accroché à sa ceinture.
examples.trans: Henri always keeps his heavy bunch of keys clipped to his belt.

meanings.note: trouver quelqu'un sympa = to find someone nice

meanings.en: trouve quelque chose = think of something
meanings.note: In context.

examples.text: Trouve quelque chose.
examples.trans: Think of something.

examples.text: Tu as trouvé un appartement?
examples.trans: Have you found a flat?

meanings.note: Informal.

examples.text: C'est quoi, ce truc?
examples.trans: What's this thing?

examples.text: J'ai un truc à te dire.
examples.trans: I've got something to tell you.

meanings.note: trèfle à quatre feuilles = four-leaf clover

examples.text: Voici un trèfle à quatre feuilles.
examples.trans: Here is a four-leaf clover.

examples.text: Sinon, il y a un joli trèfle.
examples.trans: Otherwise, there is a pretty clover.

examples.text: Très bien.
examples.trans: Very well.

examples.text: C'est très important.
examples.trans: It's very important.

meanings.note: To catch one's foot on an uneven stone or step ('trébucher sur').

examples.text: Attention à ne pas trébucher sur le pavé soulevé!
examples.trans: Careful not to trip on the raised cobblestone!

examples.text: Remettons la dalle bien à plat avant que quelqu'un ne trébuche.
examples.trans: Let's set the flagstone flat again before someone stumbles.

meanings.note: Hidden treasure ('chasse au trésor', 'chasseurs de trésor'); cherished person or keepsake.

examples.text: Ce carnet de recettes familiales est un vrai trésor.
examples.trans: This family recipe notebook is a true treasure.

examples.text: Les meilleurs trésors sont souvent faits de papier et de souvenirs.
examples.trans: The best treasures are often made of paper and memories.

meanings.note: trésorerie disponible = available cash reserves

examples.text: Je n'ai plus aucune trésorerie disponible.
examples.trans: I have no cash reserves left.

examples.text: Gérer la trésorerie.
examples.trans: To manage cash flow.

examples.text: Je sais! Notre trésorerie est sous l'eau!
examples.trans: I know! Our cash flow is underwater!

meanings.note: one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues

examples.text: Tu es pénible.
examples.trans: You're a pain.

examples.text: Tu es en vacances?
examples.trans: Are you on holiday?

meanings.en: se tuer = to kill each other (or oneself)

examples.text: Elles vont se tuer!
examples.trans: They're going to kill each other!

examples.text: Ce travail me tue.
examples.trans: This work is killing me.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'Turkish'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ce film turc.
examples.trans: That Turkish film.

examples.text: La langue turque.
examples.trans: The Turkish language.

examples.text: Ce film turc est en compétition officielle?
examples.trans: Is that Turkish film in the official competition?

meanings.en: supervision, guardianship; point tutelle = supervisory check-in
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la tutelle', plural 'les tutelles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'supervision'.

examples.text: Notre point tutelle hebdomadaire.
examples.trans: Our weekly supervisory check-in.

examples.text: Je viens pour notre point tutelle hebdomadaire.
examples.trans: I come for our weekly check-in.

meanings.note: Use the familiar singular you with someone; the opposite is vouvoyer.

examples.text: Ne me tutoyez pas.
examples.trans: Don't call me tu.

examples.text: On peut se tutoyer?
examples.trans: Can we say tu to each other?

examples.text: Vous me tutoyez moins, maintenant.
examples.trans: You're using 'tu' with me less now.

meanings.note: Plural: les tuyaux.

examples.text: Oui! On dirait que ça vient du tuyau de chauffage dans le coin.
examples.trans: Yes! It sounds like it comes from the heating pipe in the corner.

examples.text: Oh! Parfois les vieux tuyaux ont une petite bulle d'air la nuit.
examples.trans: Oh! Sometimes old pipes have a little air bubble at night.

examples.text: Frais? Euh, oui! Les vieux tuyaux du quartier se réveillent doucement le matin!
examples.trans: Chilly? Uh, yes! The old neighbourhood pipes wake up gently in the morning!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le tweet', plural 'les tweets') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tweet'.

examples.text: J'ai lu tous les tweets.
examples.trans: I read all the tweets.

examples.text: Avez-vous vu tous les tweets?
examples.trans: Did you see all the tweets?

meanings.note: Un type bien = a good guy. Masculine noun ('le type', plural 'les types') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'guy'.

examples.text: On sait qui est le type sur la photo?
examples.trans: Do we know who the guy in the photo is?

examples.text: C'est un drôle de type.
examples.trans: He's a strange guy.

examples.text: Ce type ne compte pas.
examples.trans: That guy does not count.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Une demande typique de star.
examples.trans: A typical star request.

examples.text: Voilà une demande typique de grande star!
examples.trans: There is a typical request of a big star!

meanings.note: The circumflex *â* (from Old French *tasche*) distinguishes *une tâche* ('a task') from *une tache* ('a stain').

examples.text: Écrivons les trois tâches de la journée sur le tableau blanc.
examples.trans: Let's write the day's three tasks on the whiteboard.

examples.text: Quand chacun prend une tâche simple, tout avance vite.
examples.trans: When everyone takes one simple task, everything moves fast.

meanings.en: to feel, probe (tâter le terrain = test the waters / sound out)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to feel'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'tâté').

examples.text: Il faut tâter le terrain.
examples.trans: We must test the waters.

examples.text: Il faut d'abord tâter le terrain.
examples.trans: We must test the waters first.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to download'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'téléchargé').

examples.text: On peut télécharger le formulaire.
examples.trans: We can download the form.

examples.text: On peut télécharger le formulaire maintenant?
examples.trans: Can we download the form now?

meanings.en: telekinesis (ability to move objects with the mind)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la télékinésie', plural 'les télékinésies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'telekinesis'.

examples.text: Il a un pouvoir de télékinésie.
examples.trans: He has telekinesis powers.

examples.text: Ton personnage aura un pouvoir de télékinésie!
examples.trans: Your character will have telekinesis powers!

meanings.note: Au téléphone = on the phone.

examples.text: Elle est au téléphone.
examples.trans: She's on the phone.

examples.text: Où est mon téléphone?
examples.trans: Where's my phone?

meanings.en: to telephone, call on the phone
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to telephone'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'téléphoné').

examples.text: Je téléphone au coursier.
examples.trans: I am phoning the courier.

examples.text: Oui, je téléphone au coursier maintenant.
examples.trans: Yes, I am phoning the courier now.

examples.text: Tu as essayé de lui téléphoner?
examples.trans: Did you try phoning her?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la télévision', plural 'les télévisions') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'television'.

examples.text: Elle regarde souvent des séries à la télévision le soir.
examples.trans: She often watches series on television in the evening.

examples.text: Il a commencé sa carrière à la télévision.
examples.trans: He started his career in television.

examples.text: Il faut de la ténacité.
examples.trans: You need tenacity.

examples.text: Samuel a oublié de vous apprendre la ténacité.
examples.trans: Samuel forgot to teach you tenacity.

meanings.note: ne fais pas cette tête = don't look like that; faire la tête = to sulk

meanings.en: c'est dans ma tête = it's all in my head

examples.text: J'ai mal à la tête.
examples.trans: I have a headache.

examples.text: Pourquoi mes lunettes seraient... oh! Elles sont sur ma tête!
examples.trans: Why would my glasses be... oh! They are on my head!

meanings.note: Built from tête ('head'); f. têtue.

examples.text: Aha! Vous aviez peur qu'en signant votre nom, le grand frère têtu reste chez lui!
examples.trans: Aha! You feared that if you signed your name, the stubborn big brother would stay home!

examples.text: Trois années têtues... franchement, petit frère, tu m'as manqué aussi.
examples.trans: Three stubborn years... honestly, little brother, I missed you too.

meanings.note: Early relative to the usual or expected time.
In si tôt, so soon or so early.

examples.text: Pourquoi si tôt?
examples.trans: Why so soon?

examples.text: Je me lève tôt.
examples.trans: I get up early.

examples.text: Trois semaines? Pourquoi si tôt?
examples.trans: Three weeks? Why so soon?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le ukulélé', plural 'les ukulélés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'ukulele'.

examples.text: Je me mets au ukulélé.
examples.trans: I am taking up the ukulele.

examples.text: Jouer du ukulélé.
examples.trans: To play the ukulele.

examples.text: Je disais que je me mets au ukulélé.
examples.trans: I was saying that I am taking up the ukulele.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'ultra'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Cette mission est ultra confidentielle.
examples.trans: This mission is strictly confidential.

examples.text: Cette affaire reste ultra confidentielle?
examples.trans: Does this matter stay strictly confidential?

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them.

examples.text: Et voilà la cloche du portail. Un coup franc.
examples.trans: There goes the gate bell. One firm ring.

examples.text: Voilà un taxi devant le portail à l'instant.
examples.trans: Here comes a taxi in front of the gate right now.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'united'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'plain'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Nous devons rester unis.
examples.trans: We must remain united.

examples.text: Nous devons rester unis aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: We must remain united today.

examples.text: Nous formons une grande famille unie.
examples.trans: We form a large united family.

meanings.note: Un talent unique. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Oui, elle a un timbre unique.
examples.trans: Yes, she has a unique timbre.

examples.text: C'est une opportunité unique.
examples.trans: It is a unique opportunity.

examples.text: Pourtant, Samy a un talent unique!
examples.trans: Yet, Samy has a unique talent!

examples.text: Uniquement pour les enfants.
examples.trans: Purely for the children.

examples.text: Je travaille uniquement le matin.
examples.trans: I only work in the morning.

examples.text: Je suis allée à cette soirée uniquement pour les enfants du monde entier.
examples.trans: I went to that party purely for the children of the whole world.

meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire') meaning 'to unite'; essential in everyday spoken and professional French.

examples.text: Nous nous sommes unis pour sauver l'agence.
examples.trans: We united to save the agency.

examples.text: Le projet unit toute l'équipe.
examples.trans: The project unites the entire team.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le univers', plural 'les univers') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'universe'.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas mon univers.
examples.trans: It's not my world.

examples.text: Il n'est pas de mon monde, pas mon univers.
examples.trans: He is not from my world, not my universe.

meanings.note: Institution of higher education ('à l'université' = at university, in college).

examples.text: Les trois amis se sont connus sur les bancs de l'université.
examples.trans: The three friends met during their university days.

examples.text: Le quartier de l'université regorge de petites librairies.
examples.trans: The university district is full of small bookshops.

meanings.note: Règlement d'urbanisme = municipal building code.

examples.text: Bien vu, Claire. Antoine lit des règlements d'urbanisme chaque semaine.
examples.trans: Good catch, Claire. Antoine reads city building rules every week.

examples.text: Voici l'urbanisme sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the city planning, urban zoning on the table.

meanings.note: c'est une urgence = it's an emergency

examples.text: C'est une urgence!
examples.trans: It's an emergency!

examples.text: Appelez les urgences!
examples.trans: Call emergency services!

examples.text: C'est urgent.
examples.trans: It's urgent.

examples.text: Un appel urgent.
examples.trans: An urgent call.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb: user le plancher.

examples.text: Va lui parler, Claire, avant qu'il use le plancher!
examples.trans: Go talk to him, Claire, before he wears out the floorboards!

examples.text: C'est facile à user ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to wear out together.

meanings.note: same form in masculine and feminine

examples.text: Oui, elle n'est pas utile.
examples.trans: Yes, it isn't needed.

examples.text: C'est très utile.
examples.trans: It's very useful.

meanings.note: That can be used. Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Pas une seule photo utilisable!
examples.trans: Not a single usable photo!

examples.text: Ce document est utilisable.
examples.trans: This document is usable.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to use'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'utilisé').

examples.text: Ici, on utilise ce grand cahier en papier et un crayon.
examples.trans: Here we use this big paper notebook and a pencil.

examples.text: Dans le tiroir. Ici, on utilise ce grand cahier en papier et un crayon.
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper notebook and a pencil.

examples.text: J'ai utilisé la dernière cet hiver. Seule la vieille quincaillerie après le pont vend cette taille.
examples.trans: I used the last one this winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge sells this size.

meanings.en: coming and going, bustle, movement to and fro
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le va-et-vient', plural 'les va-et-vient') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'coming and going'.

examples.text: C'est quoi tout ce va-et-vient ici?
examples.trans: What is all this coming and going here?

examples.text: Il y a beaucoup de va-et-vient dans ce couloir.
examples.trans: There is a lot of coming and going in this hallway.

meanings.note: always plural: en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Tu es en vacances?
examples.trans: Are you on holiday?

examples.text: Bonnes vacances!
examples.trans: Have a good holiday!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la vache', plural 'les vaches') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cow'.

examples.text: Une vache dans le pré.
examples.trans: A cow in the meadow.

examples.text: C'est une vraie vache à lait.
examples.trans: It is a real cash cow.

examples.text: Il a parlé de vache à lait!
examples.trans: He spoke of a cash cow!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le vaisseau', plural 'les vaisseaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'blood vessel'.

examples.text: Un petit vaisseau sanguin.
examples.trans: A small blood vessel.

examples.text: Un petit vaisseau sanguin s'est bouché.
examples.trans: A small blood vessel got blocked.

meanings.note: perdre de la valeur = to lose value

examples.text: L'agence va perdre trop de valeur.
examples.trans: The agency is going to lose too much value.

examples.text: Ce tableau a une grande valeur.
examples.trans: This painting has great value.

examples.text: Il dit que sans lui, l'agence va perdre trop de valeur.
examples.trans: He says that without him, the agency is going to lose too much value.

meanings.note: faire sa valise = to pack one's bags

examples.text: Porter une valise.
examples.trans: To carry a suitcase.

examples.text: Oh, c'est la valise jumelle du train de lundi?
examples.trans: Oh, is that the twin suitcase from Monday's train?

valoir.gloss: to be worth ('valoir mieux' = be better)

meanings.en: to be worth; valoir mieux = to be better, beat
meanings.note: Il vaut mieux attendre = it is better to wait; ça vaut mieux que... = that beats...

examples.text: Le calme de cette cour vaut mieux que le bruit de la ville.
examples.trans: The quiet of this courtyard beats city noise.

examples.text: Il vaut mieux vérifier l'étiquette deux fois avant de sucrer.
examples.trans: It is better to check the label twice before sweetening.

meanings.en: waltz (piece of music or dance in 3/4 time)
meanings.note: Feminine noun covering both the dance and an instrumental piece written in three-quarter time.

examples.text: Odette joue une petite valse douce pour l'heure du thé.
examples.trans: Odette plays a gentle little waltz for teatime.

examples.text: Cette valse compte trois temps par mesure.
examples.trans: This waltz has three beats to a bar.

meanings.en: valve (on a pipe, radiator, or boiler)
meanings.note: Feminine noun: la valve.

examples.text: Tourne doucement la valve en laiton pour couper l'eau chaude.
examples.trans: Turn the brass valve gently to shut off the hot water.

examples.text: Nous avons remplacé la vieille valve de la chaudière ce matin.
examples.trans: We replaced the old boiler valve this morning.

meanings.note: Plumbing or boiler valve.

examples.text: Mauvaise nouvelle. La vanne en laiton de la vieille chaudière vient de lâcher.
examples.trans: Bad news. The brass valve on the old boiler just gave out.

examples.text: Vous avez une vanne de rechange dans votre caisse à outils?
examples.trans: Do you have a spare valve in your toolbox?

examples.text: Froides comme l'eau du fleuve. Mettez cette vieille vanne cassée dans la poche de votre manteau.
examples.trans: Cold as river water. Put this broken old valve in your coat pocket.

meanings.note: Se vanter de = to brag about. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to praise'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'vanté').
Se vanter de = to brag about. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to praise'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'vanté').

examples.text: Je ne veux pas me vanter.
examples.trans: I don't want to boast.

examples.text: Il ne cesse de vanter son succès.
examples.trans: He doesn't stop bragging about his success.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas me vanter mais je crois qu'il m'aime bien aussi.
examples.trans: I don't want to brag but I think he likes me too.

meanings.note: Cuire à la vapeur = steam-cook; une vapeur de citron = lemon-scented steam.

examples.text: Une douce vapeur de citron monte de la casserole.
examples.trans: Sweet lemon steam rises from the saucepan.

examples.text: La vapeur de la bouilloire réchauffe la petite cuisine.
examples.trans: Steam from the kettle warms the small kitchen.

meanings.en: go ahead, go on (informal imperative phrase)
meanings.note: Idiomatic French interj expression meaning 'go ahead', frequent in natural conversational dialogue.

examples.text: Bien sûr, vas-y.
examples.trans: Of course, go ahead.

examples.text: Vas-y, fais ce que tu veux!
examples.trans: Go ahead, do what you want!

examples.text: Okay, vas-y sans hésiter.
examples.trans: Okay, go ahead without hesitating.

meanings.note: Note gender: un vase (m) = a vase; la vase (f) = river silt/mud.

examples.text: Elle glisse une feuille verte dans chaque petit vase en verre.
examples.trans: She slips a green leaf into each small glass vase.

examples.text: Posez le vase bleu au centre de la nappe blanche.
examples.trans: Set the blue vase in the center of the white tablecloth.

meanings.note: une vedette de cinéma = a movie star
partager la vedette = to share the spotlight

examples.text: Ça ne vous dérange pas de partager la vedette?
examples.trans: You do not mind sharing the spotlight?

examples.text: Elle est la vedette du spectacle.
examples.trans: She is the star of the show.

examples.text: C'est toi la vedette, Gérard.
examples.trans: You are the star, Gerard.

meanings.en: the day before, eve; standby mode (en veille)

examples.text: Elle a annulé la veille du tournage.
examples.trans: She canceled the day before the shoot.

examples.text: Le téléphone est en veille.
examples.trans: The phone is on standby.

veiller.gloss: to watch over, to look after

meanings.en: to watch over, to look after, to ensure
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to watch over'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'veillé').

examples.text: Veiller sur quelqu'un.
examples.trans: To watch over someone.

examples.text: Veiller au grain.
examples.trans: To keep a sharp lookout.

examples.text: Je serai toujours là pour veiller sur toi.
examples.trans: I will always be there to watch over you.

meanings.note: avoir de la veine = to be lucky, c'est ma veine = just my luck

examples.text: Des histoires de couple, c'est ma veine.
examples.trans: Couple dramas are just my luck.

examples.text: Quelle veine!
examples.trans: What luck!

examples.text: Elle le quitte? Des histoires de couple, c'est ma veine.
examples.trans: She is leaving him? Couple dramas are just my luck.

related.gloss: to be lucky, c'est ma veine = just my luck

meanings.note: Soft pile velvet fabric (silent final -s: 'du velours'); smooth texture on the palate.

examples.text: L'étui du violon est doublé de velours vert profond.
examples.trans: The violin case is lined with deep green velvet.

examples.text: La boussole repose dans une pochette en velours doux.
examples.trans: The compass rests inside a soft velvet pouch.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le vendeur', plural 'les vendeurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shop clerk'.

examples.text: Le vendeur était très timide.
examples.trans: The clerk was very shy.

examples.text: Seulement une clé dorée peinte au-dessus de la porte. Montrez cette vanne au vendeur.
examples.trans: Only a painted golden key above the door. Show this valve to the clerk.

meanings.note: Sell; past participle vendu, with avoir in compound tenses.

examples.text: Je veux vendre.
examples.trans: I want to sell.

examples.text: Il vend des fleurs.
examples.trans: He sells flowers.

examples.text: Avec grand plaisir, Thibault, tant que personne ne parle de vendre de vieux pianos!
examples.trans: With great pleasure, Thibault, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

examples.text: Vendredi à onze heures.
examples.trans: Friday at eleven.

examples.text: À vendredi!
examples.trans: See you on Friday!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la vengeance', plural 'les vengeances') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'retaliation'.

examples.text: Une vengeance inutile.
examples.trans: A useless revenge.

examples.text: C'est une vengeance ridicule!
examples.trans: It is a ridiculous revenge!

meanings.note: Often reflexive. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to retaliate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'vengé').

examples.text: Elle veut se venger de son rival.
examples.trans: She wants to take revenge on her rival.

examples.text: Elle voulait se venger de notre agence.
examples.trans: She wanted to get revenge on our agency.

meanings.note: venir de + infinitive: je viens d'arriver = I've just arrived

meanings.en: venir de + infinitive = to have just
meanings.note: Je viens d'arriver.

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: I can't come tonight.

examples.text: Tu viens?
examples.trans: Are you coming?

related.word: venir de + infinitive: je viens d'arriver

meanings.note: Final -t is silent (/vɑ̃/); il y a du vent means 'it is windy'.

examples.text: Les fenêtres en verre protègent la terrasse du vent froid.
examples.trans: The glass windows shelter the terrace from the cold wind.

examples.text: Un léger vent fait danser les feuilles du tilleul.
examples.trans: A light breeze makes the linden leaves dance.

meanings.note: En vente = for sale, on sale.

examples.text: L'agence est en vente.
examples.trans: The agency is for sale.

examples.text: La maison est en vente.
examples.trans: The house is for sale.

examples.text: Tout le monde est au courant que l'agence est en vente.
examples.trans: Everyone knows that the agency is for sale.

meanings.note: False friend alert: a sports/music 'fan' is *un(e) fan*, whereas *un ventilateur* is exclusively a mechanical air fan!

examples.text: Allumez le petit ventilateur pour faire circuler l'air sec.
examples.trans: Turn on the small fan to keep the dry air moving.

examples.text: En été, un ventilateur silencieux rafraîchit toute la pièce.
examples.trans: In summer, a quiet fan cools the whole room.

related.gloss: to blow; to catch one's breath

meanings.note: avoir mal au ventre = to have a stomach ache

examples.text: J'ai encore un peu de ventre.
examples.trans: I still have a bit of a tummy.

examples.text: J'ai mal au ventre.
examples.trans: My stomach hurts.

examples.text: Non, j'ai encore un peu de ventre.
examples.trans: No, I still have a bit of a tummy.

meanings.note: Silent final -s; same spelling in singular and plural.

examples.text: Le vernis doré du violon brille sous la lampe.
examples.trans: The golden varnish of the violin shines under the lamp.

examples.text: Henri passe une fine couche de vernis sur le panneau.
examples.trans: Henri brushes a thin coat of varnish onto the sign.

meanings.en: glass (material: en verre); drinking glass (un verre d'eau)
meanings.note: Pronounced /vɛʁ/, identical in sound to vert ('green') and vers ('towards'); context and articles keep them clear.

examples.text: Le toit en verre laisse entrer toute la lumière du matin.
examples.trans: The glass roof lets in all the morning light.

examples.text: Je vous sers un grand verre d'eau fraîche?
examples.trans: Shall I pour you a tall glass of cool water?

meanings.note: Direction. Core French preposition meaning 'towards', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: vers midi. Core French preposition meaning 'towards', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Un pied vers la tombe.
examples.trans: A foot towards the grave.

examples.text: On arrive vers midi.
examples.trans: We'll arrive around noon.

examples.text: J'ai senti un pied glisser vers la tombe.
examples.trans: I felt one foot slip towards the grave.

meanings.note: Verser de l'eau / du thé.

examples.text: Verse l'eau chaude dans la théière, Claire, les voilà!
examples.trans: Pour the hot water into the teapot, Claire, here they come!

examples.text: C'est facile à verser ensemble.
examples.trans: It is easy to pour together.

meanings.en: version, draft (of a script or text)

examples.text: J'adore cette version finale.
examples.trans: I love this final version.

examples.text: La première version du scénario.
examples.trans: The first draft of the script.

examples.text: Merci, Noémie. J'adore cette version finale.
examples.trans: Thank you, Noémie. I love this final version.

meanings.note: feminine verte
un vin un peu vert

examples.text: La porte est verte.
examples.trans: The door is green.

examples.text: Le vin est encore un peu vert.
examples.trans: The wine is still a little unripe.

meanings.note: Dans la poche de votre veste = in your jacket pocket.

examples.text: Vos lunettes sont rangées dans la poche de votre veste.
examples.trans: Your glasses are tucked in your jacket pocket.

examples.text: Il boutonne sa veste propre avant d'aller au portail.
examples.trans: He buttons his clean jacket before going to the gate.

meanings.en: cloakroom, coat check; also used informally for coat check attendant
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le vestiaire', plural 'les vestiaires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cloakroom'.

examples.text: La vestiaire a pris nos affaires.
examples.trans: The coat check took our belongings.

examples.text: La vestiaire a déplacé nos affaires.
examples.trans: The coat check girl moved our things.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la viande', plural 'les viandes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'animal meat or flesh'.

examples.text: De la viande rouge.
examples.trans: Red meat.

examples.text: Un tas de viande.
examples.trans: A slab of meat.

examples.text: Je refuse d'être un tas de viande!
examples.trans: I refuse to be a slab of meat!

meanings.note: Idiom: *Ne criez pas victoire trop vite!* ('Don't declare victory / celebrate too soon!').

examples.text: Ne crions pas victoire avant d'avoir goûté la dernière fournée!
examples.trans: Let's not celebrate before tasting the final batch from the oven!

examples.text: Ouvrir cette vieille porte coincée était déjà une petite victoire.
examples.trans: Opening that stuck old door was already a small victory.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'vacant'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un regard vide.
examples.trans: A blank look.

examples.text: Douze coups... et la rue devant le portail est complètement vide.
examples.trans: Twelve chimes... and the street outside the gate is completely empty.

examples.text: Même quand la chambre quatre est vide, le vieux fil sonne deux fois.
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire rings twice.

meanings.note: Vider un verre. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to empty'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'vidé').

meanings.en: vider l'abcès = clear the air, settle a dispute
meanings.note: Vider l'abcès. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to empty'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'vidé').

examples.text: Elle vide son sac de voyage.
examples.trans: She empties her travel bag.

examples.text: Coupée et vidée. Passez-moi la grosse clé anglaise à votre gauche.
examples.trans: Turned off and drained. Pass me the heavy wrench on your left.

meanings.note: Vidéo en ligne = online video.

examples.text: Dans mes vidéos en ligne, il n'y a pas de stars.
examples.trans: In my online videos, there are no stars.

examples.text: Elle aime vos vidéos.
examples.trans: She likes your videos.

examples.text: Elle attire le public, et elle aime vos vidéos.
examples.trans: She draws the public, and she likes your videos.

examples.text: La vie est belle.
examples.trans: Life is beautiful.

examples.text: C'est la plus belle première semaine de toute ma vie!
examples.trans: It is the best first week of my whole life!

meanings.note: before the noun; vieil before a vowel: un vieil ami

examples.text: C'est un vieux film.
examples.trans: It's an old film.

examples.text: Non, seulement mon stylo et trois vieux tickets!
examples.trans: No, only my pen and three old receipts!

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Je vous adresse mes plus vifs remerciements.
examples.trans: I send you my warmest thanks.

examples.text: Une vive émotion traverse la pièce.
examples.trans: A keen emotion runs through the room.

examples.text: Le grand frère était vif et bruyant, toujours pressé de finir ses gammes.
examples.trans: The older brother was lively and loud, always in a hurry to finish his scales.

meanings.note: Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'village, small town'.

examples.text: Le village de mes parents.
examples.trans: My parents' village.

examples.text: Un petit village.
examples.trans: A small village.

examples.text: À Couchey. Le village de mes parents.
examples.trans: To Couchey. The village of my parents.

meanings.note: En ville = in town, downtown.

examples.text: Je suis une fille de la ville.
examples.trans: I'm a city girl.

examples.text: Paris est une grande ville.
examples.trans: Paris is a big city.

examples.text: Oui, beaucoup! Mais je suis une fille de la ville.
examples.trans: Yes, a lot! But I'm a city girl.

meanings.note: Wine; rouge, blanc and rosé specify common types.

examples.text: Ce vin est bon.
examples.trans: This wine is good.

examples.text: Un verre de vin, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: A glass of wine, please.

examples.text: Ce vin est incroyablement bon!
examples.trans: This wine is incredibly good!

meanings.note: Literally *vin + aigre* ('sour wine')! Beyond salad dressings, *le vinaigre blanc* is a classic French household cleaner for streak-free glass.

examples.text: Un peu de vinaigre blanc fait briller les vieilles vitres.
examples.trans: A splash of white vinegar makes old windowpanes sparkle.

examples.text: Elle range l'huile d'olive et le vinaigre près du fourneau.
examples.trans: She keeps the olive oil and vinegar near the stove.

examples.text: Vingt ans.
examples.trans: Twenty years.

examples.text: Vingt jours de tournage.
examples.trans: Twenty days of filming.

examples.text: La jeune actrice a seulement vingt-cinq ans.
examples.trans: The young actress is only twenty-five years old.

examples.text: J'ai attendu vingt-cinq minutes dans le couloir.
examples.trans: I waited twenty-five minutes in the corridor.

examples.text: Il est vingt-cinq.
examples.trans: It's twenty-five.

meanings.note: On the 24-hour clock, vingt-deux heures is 10 pm.

examples.text: Jusqu'à vingt-deux heures.
examples.trans: Until ten at night.

examples.text: Elle a vingt-deux ans.
examples.trans: She's twenty-two.

examples.text: Je travaille tous les jours jusqu'à vingt-deux heures. C'est dingue.
examples.trans: I work until ten at night every day. It's crazy.

meanings.note: Notice the pronounced `/t/` in *vingt-huit* (`/vɛ̃tɥit/`), as in all numbers from *vingt-deux* through *vingt-neuf*.

examples.text: Écoutez bien le passage doux à la mesure vingt-huit.
examples.trans: Listen closely to the gentle passage at bar twenty-eight.

examples.text: Le mois de février compte vingt-huit jours cette année.
examples.trans: February has twenty-eight days this year.

meanings.note: Notice t in vingt is pronounced in 21..29: /vɛ̃tnœf/.

examples.text: Sept heures vingt-neuf à ma montre. Les clients descendent l'escalier.
examples.trans: Seven twenty-nine on my watch. Guests are coming down the stairs.

examples.text: Sept heures vingt-neuf à ma montre.
examples.trans: Seven twenty-nine on my watch.

meanings.note: In numbers 21 through 29 (vingt et un ... vingt-neuf), the final -t of vingt IS pronounced (/vɛ̃tkatʁ/), unlike standalone vingt (/vɛ̃/).

examples.text: Deux douzaines, cela fait exactement vingt-quatre chaises!
examples.trans: Two dozen makes twenty-four chairs altogether!

examples.text: La partition compte seulement vingt-quatre mesures.
examples.trans: The musical score has only twenty-four bars.

meanings.note: Invariable French cardinal numeral meaning 'twenty-seven', used before plural nouns and in time/date expressions.

examples.text: Elle a fait vingt-sept prises.
examples.trans: She did twenty-seven takes.

examples.text: Vous avez fait vingt-sept prises difficiles.
examples.trans: You did twenty-seven difficult takes.

examples.text: J'ai défoncé cette porte vingt-sept fois!
examples.trans: I smashed through that door twenty-seven times!

meanings.note: the t in vingt is pronounced before trois

examples.text: Vous avez vingt-trois mois de retard.
examples.trans: You are twenty-three months late.

examples.text: Elle a vingt-trois ans.
examples.trans: She is twenty-three.

examples.text: Madame, vous avez vingt-trois mois de retard.
examples.trans: Madam, you are twenty-three months late.

meanings.note: le vingtième siècle = the twentieth century

examples.text: Le vingtième arrondissement.
examples.trans: The twentieth arrondissement.

examples.text: Pour la vingtième fois.
examples.trans: For the twentieth time.

examples.text: Non, cet atelier est dans le vingtième!
examples.trans: No, that workshop is in the twentieth!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la violence', plural 'les violences') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'violence'.

examples.text: Sa propre violence.
examples.trans: His own violence.

examples.text: Tu as ta propre folie, ta propre violence.
examples.trans: You have your own madness, your own violence.

examples.text: Mais cette violence a un sens profond.
examples.trans: But this violence has a deep meaning.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'violent'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ce scénario est trop violent.
examples.trans: This script is too violent.

examples.text: Il est beaucoup trop violent et sombre.
examples.trans: It is much too violent and dark.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to violate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'violé').

examples.text: Je ne peux pas violer le secret.
examples.trans: I cannot violate secrecy.

examples.text: Elle s'appelle Violaine.
examples.trans: Her name is Violaine.

meanings.note: Jouer du violon = play the violin; accompagner au violon = accompany on the violin.

examples.text: Notre voisin apporte son violon chaque vendredi soir.
examples.trans: Our neighbor brings his violin every Friday evening.

examples.text: Le violon et le piano se répondent dans la cour.
examples.trans: The violin and the piano answer each other in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Turn on a staircase or road.

examples.text: Attention dans le virage, ne cognez pas le mur!
examples.trans: Careful on the turn, do not bump the wall!

examples.text: Voici le virage sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the bend, turn, corner on the table.

meanings.note: informal: tu es virée = you're fired
Virer de l'argent.

examples.text: Tu es virée!
examples.trans: You're fired!

examples.text: Le patron vire son assistant.
examples.trans: The boss fires his assistant.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la virée', plural 'les virées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'night out'.

examples.text: Pour notre virée en ville.
examples.trans: For our night out in town.

examples.text: Ils ont fait une virée à la mer.
examples.trans: They went on a trip to the sea.

meanings.note: Pronounced /vis/; invariable plural: des vis.

examples.text: Attention à cette chaise du coin, attendez dix secondes, je resserre cette vis.
examples.trans: Watch that corner chair, wait ten seconds while I tighten this screw.

examples.text: Les vieilles maisons perdent une vis chaque mardi. Maintenant, asseyez-vous.
examples.trans: Old houses lose one screw every Tuesday. Now sit down.

examples.text: Un tour, deux tours... regardez comme le nouveau pas de vis rentre bien.
examples.trans: One turn, two turns... look how smoothly the new screw thread fits.

examples.text: Je ne touche pas à mon visage.
examples.trans: I'm not touching my face.

examples.text: Elle a un beau visage.
examples.trans: She has a beautiful face.

meanings.note: To sight or point toward a target landmark; to aim for a goal.

examples.text: La flèche gravée vise directement le centre du bassin.
examples.trans: The carved arrow points straight at the center of the basin.

examples.text: En pâtisserie, nous visons toujours la simplicité et le goût.
examples.trans: In baking, we always aim for simplicity and flavor.

meanings.note: Une vision de la vie.

examples.text: Tu as une vision horrible de la vie.
examples.trans: You have a horrible view of life.

examples.text: Il a une bonne vision.
examples.trans: He has good eyesight.

examples.text: Tu as une vision horrible de la vie. Elle m'a touchée.
examples.trans: You have a horrible view of life. She moved me.

meanings.en: visit, call (carte de visite = business card)
meanings.note: Une carte de visite. Feminine noun ('la visite', plural 'les visites') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'visit'.

examples.text: Merci pour votre visite.
examples.trans: Thank you for your visit.

examples.text: Ils nous donnent trente jours avant la visite des nouveaux acheteurs!
examples.trans: They give us thirty days before the new buyers inspect it!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to visit'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'visité').

examples.text: Un guide pour visiter Paris.
examples.trans: A guide to visit Paris.

examples.text: C'est un guide original pour visiter Paris.
examples.trans: It is an original guide for visiting Paris.

examples.text: Oui, je visitais un petit appartement.
examples.trans: Yes, I was visiting a small apartment.

meanings.note: Person who comes to visit a place, exhibition, or friend.
Feminine form: une visiteuse.

examples.text: Attendez: des centaines de visiteurs dans la rue des Tilleuls pour notre piano et le pain de Nadia?!
examples.trans: Wait: hundreds of visitors walking down Rue des Tilleuls for our piano and the bread from Nadia?!

examples.text: Les visiteurs admirent le vieux tilleul au milieu de la cour.
examples.trans: The visitors admire the old linden tree in the middle of the courtyard.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la vitalité', plural 'les vitalités') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'vitality'.

examples.text: J'adore sa vitalité.
examples.trans: I love his energy.

examples.text: Non, j'adore l'expérience face à la vitalité.
examples.trans: No, I love experience facing fresh energy.

examples.text: Je l'ai vite retiré.
examples.trans: I quickly pulled it back.

examples.text: Viens vite!
examples.trans: Come quickly!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la vitesse', plural 'les vitesses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'speed'.

examples.text: Quelle vitesse! L'épicier vous a donné un ticket?
examples.trans: What speed! Did the grocer give you a receipt?

examples.text: Il roulait à grande vitesse.
examples.trans: He was driving at high speed.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la vitre', plural 'les vitres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'pane of glass'.

examples.text: Les lettres sur la vitre.
examples.trans: The letters on the glass.

examples.text: Claire, regarde par la vitre: ils sont face à face sous le tilleul!
examples.trans: Claire, look through the glass: they are face to face under the linden tree!

meanings.en: glass-walled, glazed (*une porte vitrée*, *une pièce vitrée*)
meanings.note: From *la vitre* ('windowpane'); describes doors, verandas, or sunrooms enclosed with panes of glass.

examples.text: Le soleil du matin inonde toute la petite pièce vitrée.
examples.trans: Morning sunlight floods the whole little glass-walled room.

examples.text: Fermez doucement la porte vitrée qui donne sur la cour.
examples.trans: Gently close the glass door leading out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'alive'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je me sens libre et vivant.
examples.trans: I feel free and alive.

examples.text: Une langue vivante.
examples.trans: A living language.

examples.text: À l'Hôtel du Tilleul, l'endroit calme le plus vivant de Lyon!
examples.trans: Here is to the Hotel du Tilleul, the liveliest quiet place in Lyon!

meanings.note: Vivre à Paris = to live in Paris.

examples.text: Je vis à Paris.
examples.trans: I live in Paris.

examples.text: Il a vécu à Nice.
examples.trans: He lived in Nice.

meanings.en: voice, vocal (un message vocal = a voicemail)
meanings.note: Irregular masculine plural in -aux (des messages vocaux), while feminine plural is regular (vocales).

examples.text: Vous avez reçu un nouveau message vocal à dix-huit heures.
examples.trans: You received a new voicemail at six p.m.

examples.text: Écoutons vite le message vocal sur le téléphone de l'accueil.
examples.trans: Let's quickly listen to the voicemail on the front-desk phone.

meanings.note: to present something or someone near you

examples.text: C'est vrai! Et voici les clés?
examples.trans: Fair enough! And here are the keys?

examples.text: Voici votre clé, numéro quatre. Le petit-déjeuner est de sept heures trente à dix heures.
examples.trans: Here is your key, number four. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: Voici cinquante euros de la caisse. Rapportez le ticket!
examples.trans: Here is fifty euros from the cash box. Bring back the receipt!

voilà.gloss: there is; here's; there you go

meanings.note: To present something.

examples.text: Voilà exactement le contrat que je cherchais depuis ce matin!
examples.trans: Here is the exact contract I have been looking for since this morning!

examples.text: Nous voilà enfin arrivés devant le grand hôtel.
examples.trans: Here we are at last in front of the grand hotel.

meanings.note: n'avoir rien à voir avec = to have nothing to do with
Voir quelqu'un.

examples.text: On peut déplacer quatre cartons en cinq minutes. Allons voir tout de suite!
examples.trans: We can move four boxes in five minutes. Let us go look right now!

examples.text: Une chambre sous les toits? Je peux la voir d'abord?
examples.trans: An attic room? May I see it first?

examples.text: J'avance... oh, je vois la clé dorée et la porte bleue!
examples.trans: I am walking forward... oh, I see the golden key and the blue door!

meanings.note: masculine: voisin; feminine: voisine

examples.text: Et si c'est ta voisine?
examples.trans: What if she's your neighbour?

examples.text: Nos voisins sont sympas.
examples.trans: Our neighbours are nice.

meanings.note: En voiture = by car.

examples.text: Arrête la voiture!
examples.trans: Stop the car!

examples.text: Je n'ai pas de voiture, je suis à pied!
examples.trans: I don't have a car, I'm on foot!

meanings.note: same form in singular and plural; à voix basse = in a low voice

examples.text: Une voix polie? Jeune ou âgée?
examples.trans: A polite voice? Young or old?

examples.text: Excusez-moi, madame... attendez. Cette voix! Madame Odette, ma professeure de piano?!
examples.trans: Excuse me, madam... wait. That voice! Madam Odette, my piano teacher?!

examples.text: Tu perds la voix?
examples.trans: Are you losing your voice?

related.word: same form in singular and plural; à voix basse

meanings.note: Réserver un vol. Masculine noun ('le vol', plural 'les vols') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'flight'.
Masculine noun ('le vol', plural 'les vols') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'flight'.

examples.text: Tous les vols sont complets.
examples.trans: All flights are fully booked.

examples.text: Prendre un vol.
examples.trans: To take a flight.

examples.text: Vous pourriez me réserver un vol?
examples.trans: Could you book a flight for me?

meanings.note: Round valve wheel or car steering wheel.

examples.text: Tournez le volant bleu doucement vers la gauche, pas trop vite.
examples.trans: Turn the blue wheel slowly to the left, not too fast.

examples.text: Voici le volant sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the handwheel on the table.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Un couple volcanique.
examples.trans: A volcanic couple.

examples.text: Quel couple volcanique!
examples.trans: What a volcanic couple!

meanings.note: Voler quelque chose à quelqu'un.

examples.text: Il a volé mon idée!
examples.trans: He stole my idea!

examples.text: L'oiseau vole.
examples.trans: The bird is flying.

meanings.note: Wooden exterior shutters on French windows.

examples.text: Parce que les volets en bois mouillés adoucissent l'écho des pavés...
examples.trans: Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the cobblestones...

examples.text: Sûrement un avis ennuyeux pour repeindre les volets sur la rue.
examples.trans: Probably a boring notice about repainting the street shutters.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le voleur', plural 'les voleurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'thief'.

examples.text: Vous me traitez comme un voleur maintenant?
examples.trans: Are you treating me like a thief now?

examples.text: Arrêter un voleur en fuite.
examples.trans: To stop a fleeing thief.

meanings.note: oui, volontiers = yes, gladly / with pleasure

examples.text: Je viendrai volontiers.
examples.trans: I will gladly come.

examples.text: Volontiers! Avec du lait et un peu de sucre, s'il te plaît.
examples.trans: Gladly! With milk and a little sugar, please.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le vote', plural 'les votes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'vote'.

examples.text: Le conseil d'administration va passer au vote maintenant.
examples.trans: The board of directors is going to proceed to the vote now.

examples.text: Le vote pour les César reste secret jusqu'à la cérémonie.
examples.trans: The vote for the César awards remains secret until the ceremony.

meanings.note: voter pour ou contre = to vote for or against

examples.text: Il faut voter entre associés maintenant.
examples.trans: We must vote between partners now.

examples.text: Voter pour une décision.
examples.trans: To vote for a decision.

examples.text: Qui vote pour sauver nos emplois?
examples.trans: Who votes to save our jobs?

meanings.note: Polite or plural 'you'.

examples.text: Votre nom?
examples.trans: Your name?

examples.text: Laissez vos photos ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos here.

meanings.note: + noun or infinitive.
Imparfait, softer.

examples.text: Rebonjour, Madame Odette! Vous voulez du café ou du thé noir?
examples.trans: Good morning again, Madam Odette! Would you like coffee or black tea?

examples.text: Attends vendredi à midi: je veux être au premier rang quand l'homme à la valise entrera!
examples.trans: Wait until Friday at noon: I want a front-row seat when Suitcase Man walks in!

examples.text: Ça veut dire pas de chauffage cette nuit, ou pas d'eau chaude non plus?
examples.trans: Does that mean no heating tonight, or no hot water either?

meanings.note: One person, formal.
Several people.
je vous rappelle = I'll call you back

examples.text: Vous êtes où?
examples.trans: Where are you?

examples.text: Madame Odette, tout va bien? Vous avez sonné!
examples.trans: Madam Odette, is everything alright? You rang the bell!

meanings.note: Emphatic pronoun ('vous-même' for polite singular 'yourself'; 'vous-mêmes' for plural 'yourselves').

examples.text: Goûtez vous-même cette confiture d'abricots maison!
examples.trans: Taste this homemade apricot jam for yourself!

examples.text: Regardez vous-mêmes: les quatre traits forment une étoile.
examples.trans: See for yourselves: the four lines form a star.

examples.text: Vous me vouvoyez.
examples.trans: You address me formally.

examples.text: Je vouvoie mon professeur.
examples.trans: I address my teacher formally.

meanings.note: Bon voyage. Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'trip, journey'.

examples.text: Oui, la chambre quatre au deuxième étage! Comment était votre voyage en train?
examples.trans: Yes, room four on the second floor! How was your train trip?

examples.text: Voici le voyage sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the trip, journey on the table.

meanings.note: To travel from place to place; figuratively for a letter, song, or recipe to travel through time.

examples.text: J'adore voyager en train à travers la campagne française.
examples.trans: I love traveling by train across the French countryside.

examples.text: Cette petite boîte a voyagé à travers trente étés.
examples.trans: This little box has traveled across thirty summers.

meanings.note: Feminine: voyageuse.

examples.text: Une voyageuse ne peut pas rester triste là-haut pour son premier soir à Lyon!
examples.trans: A traveller cannot sit sad upstairs on her first evening in Lyon!

examples.text: Voici le voyageur sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the traveller, passenger on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la voyante', plural 'les voyantes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fortune-teller'.

examples.text: Elle consulte une voyante avant de signer chaque contrat.
examples.trans: She consults a clairvoyant before signing every contract.

examples.text: La voyante lui a prédit un grand succès au cinéma.
examples.trans: The fortune-teller predicted great film success for her.

meanings.en: come on, now then (exclamation urging sense)
meanings.note: C'est évident, voyons!. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'come on', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: C'est évident, voyons!
examples.trans: It is obvious, come on!

examples.text: Voyons ce qui se passe.
examples.trans: Let's see what happens.

meanings.note: Built with a curved stone arch or vault ('porche voûté', 'cave voûtée').

examples.text: La cave voûtée garde une fraîcheur idéale toute l'année.
examples.trans: The vaulted cellar keeps an ideal coolness all year round.

examples.text: Passez sous le porche voûté pour entrer dans la cour.
examples.trans: Walk under the arched gateway to enter the courtyard.

examples.text: C'est vrai?
examples.trans: Is that true?

examples.text: Une vraie amie.
examples.trans: A real friend.

examples.text: Tu crois vraiment qu'il va accepter ce rôle?
examples.trans: Do you really think he is going to accept this role?

examples.text: Je suis vraiment désolée pour ce petit retard.
examples.trans: I am truly sorry for this slight delay.

meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'given', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Vu l'heure tardive, nous ferions mieux de rentrer.
examples.trans: Given the late hour, we had better go home.

examples.text: C'est une excellente idée, vu la situation actuelle.
examples.trans: It is an excellent idea, considering the current situation.

meanings.note: Une belle vue.

examples.text: La chambre a une vue sur la mer.
examples.trans: The room has a view of the sea.

examples.text: Oui, un bon lit en bois, un bureau propre et la meilleure vue de la maison.
examples.trans: Yes, a good wooden bed, a clean desk, and the best view in the house.

examples.text: Comment est ma cravate aujourd'hui, Claire? Zéro goutte de jus d'orange en vue!
examples.trans: How is my tie today, Claire? Zero drops of orange juice in sight!

meanings.note: same form in masculine and feminine

examples.text: C'est trop vulgaire?
examples.trans: Is it too flashy?

examples.text: Ce n'est jamais vulgaire.
examples.trans: It's never trashy.

meanings.note: Le monde végétal = the plant world. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'plant'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Une voix sensuelle et végétale.
examples.trans: A sensual and vegetal voice.

examples.text: Le règne végétal.
examples.trans: The plant kingdom.

examples.text: Je cherche une voix sensuelle et végétale.
examples.trans: I am looking for a sensual and vegetal voice.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le véhicule', plural 'les véhicules') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'vehicle'.

examples.text: Sortez du véhicule.
examples.trans: Exit the vehicle.

examples.text: Un véhicule électrique.
examples.trans: An electric vehicle.

examples.text: Maintenant, sortez du véhicule.
examples.trans: Now, exit the vehicle.

meanings.note: faire du vélo = to cycle; à vélo = by bike

examples.text: Fais du vélo!
examples.trans: Ride a bike!

examples.text: Je vais au travail à vélo.
examples.trans: I go to work by bike.

related.gloss: to cycle; à vélo = by bike

meanings.note: Act of checking or double-checking that everything is in order.

examples.text: Vérification rapide avant trois heures: veste boutonnée, chaussures propres... où sont mes lunettes?!
examples.trans: Quick check before three strikes: jacket buttoned, clean shoes... where are my glasses?!

examples.text: Après une dernière vérification du cahier, toutes les chambres sont prêtes.
examples.trans: After one final check of the ledger, all the rooms are ready.

examples.text: Pour vérifier mes costumes et mes notes de frais.
examples.trans: To check my suits and my expense claims.

examples.text: Je vérifie l'adresse.
examples.trans: I'm checking the address.

examples.text: Je vérifie simplement la sécurité. C'est mon métier.
examples.trans: I am simply checking security. That is my job.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Un véritable ami.
examples.trans: A true friend.

examples.text: C'est un véritable enfer!
examples.trans: It is a real hell!

examples.text: À l'agence, c'est un véritable enfer!
examples.trans: At the agency, it is a real hell!

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: C'est véritablement un grand honneur.
examples.trans: It is truly a great honor.

examples.text: Il est véritablement passionné par son métier.
examples.trans: He is genuinely passionate about his craft.

examples.text: Une personne incarne véritablement notre belle agence.
